items.name: David Njoku
items.headline: David Njoku (fibula) is questionable for Week 10 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Njoku logged a week of limited sessions before drawing the questionable tag for Monday Night Football. He will need to be activated from injured reserve prior to Monday to play. Fantasy managers are likely better off making alternate plans considering the Chargers don’t play until Monday.

items.name: Ladd McConkey
items.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) is questionable for Week 10 against the Ravens.

items.name: Chris Brooks
items.headline: Packers activated RB Chris Brooks and WR Skyy Moore from injured reserve.
items.analysis: Brooks returns to a backfield once again without Josh Jacobs, appearing likely to serve as the preferred passing down back while Kaleb Johnson handles early-down duties. Moore remains unlikely to be consistently involved in the offense but brings a sizable boost to the special teams unit. The top duo of Christian Watson and Matthew Golden should continue to dominate targets through the air for one of the most pass-heavy offenses in the league.

items.name: TreVeyon Henderson
items.headline: Patriots placed RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: Henderson will now miss the coming four games, at minimum, after missing the previous two, with what the team is calling neurological symptoms. Whatever it is that Henderson is currently going through is clearly bigger than football. Rhamondre Stevenson is currently listed as questionable for Week 10 but is not expected to play, leaving the backfield in the hands of Corey Kiner in the immediate future. Here’s hoping for a speedy recovery for the electric running back.

items.name: Xavier Legette
items.headline: Panthers activated WR Xavier Legette (knee) from injured reserve.
items.analysis: Legette will make his return to a passing offense currently dominated by Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, and tight end Darren Waller, unlikely to return a usable fantasy score in his first game since Week 2. He is not on the fantasy radar despite the plus matchup against the Saints.

items.name: Jonathon Brooks
items.headline: Panthers downgraded Jonathon Brooks (core) to out for Week 10 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Brooks will miss his seventh consecutive game as he attempts to return from a core muscle injury. He managed a week of limited sessions before initially being listed as doubtful, ultimately ruled out. Chuba Hubbard will again serve as a legitimate workhorse in a plus matchup against the Saints and can be treated as a back-end RB1 in Week 10.

items.name: Tyler Goodson
items.headline: Cowboys placed RB Tyler Goodson (ankle/knee) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: It’s yet another blow to the depth of a backfield devastated by injuries this season, leaving lead back Javonte Williams again positioned well to see a workhorse role against the 49ers. The team elevated running back Israel Abanikanda in an associated move, who is likely to serve as the primary change of pace option in Week 10.

items.name: David Montgomery
items.headline: Texans ruled out David Montgomery (groin) for Week 10 against the Browns.
items.analysis: Montgomery entered the weekend listed as questionable after missing the previous three games plus the team’s Week 8 bye. Fantasy managers will have to wait another week for his return, while Woody Marks retains viable FLEX status playing as the top option alongside recent signee Emari Demercado.

items.name: Pat Freiermuth
items.headline: Pat Freiermuth (illness) is questionable for Week 10 against the Bengals.
items.analysis: Freiermuth was added to the injury report Saturday as questionable with an illness. A mid-range TE2 when healthy, Freiermuth’s potential absence likely wouldn’t change much for Darnell Washington’s fantasy outlook. Fantasy managers counting on Freiermuth will need to be proactive about alternative options as the Steelers play the Bengals on Sunday Night Football, which airs on NBC and Peacock.

items.name: Omar Cooper
items.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Omar Cooper (ankle) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Cooper seemed to be trending in the right direction this week as he got in a full practice on Friday. Now he’s expected to play against the Bills, according to Zenitz. Cooper led the Jets in targets last week and will be in the WR3 mix against Buffalo this week.

items.name: Adonai Mitchell
items.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Adonai Mitchell (knee) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Mitchell remains questionable with a knee injury that put him on the injury report after getting in a full practice Friday. However concerning Mitchell’s new injury seemed, he’s expected to play, according to Zenitz. With Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) also expected to play, Mitchell is a boom-or-bust dart throw at best in Week 10.

items.name: Kenneth Walker
items.headline: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker (groin) is out for Week 10’s game against the Falcons.
items.analysis: Walker sat out Friday’s practice with a tight groin and was officially listed as questionable for Week 10’s game against the Falcons. Now Schultz is reporting the 26-year-old running back has been ruled out. Once that becomes official, Emmett Johnson moves into the low-end RB1 mix in a plus matchup against Atlanta.

items.name: Travis Etienne
items.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Saints plan to activate Travis Etienne (hamstring) from injured reserve ahead of Week 10’s game against the Panthers.
items.analysis: Etienne practiced in full this week and now Pelissero reports he’s in line to return against the Panthers in Week 10. The 27-year-old running back deserves FLEX consideration in a plus matchup against Carolina, though he could be on a snap count in his first game in over a month.

items.name: Josh Jacobs
items.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Packers RB Josh Jacobs (finger) underwent successful surgery on Friday.
items.analysis: Jacobs had surgery on his fractured right ring finger Friday in Los Angeles, according to Pelissero. The 28-year-old running back is expected to return in the next few weeks. In the meantime, Kaleb Johnson is the only usable Packers running back for fantasy purposes. He’s an RB3/FLEX play against the Vikings in Week 10.

items.name: Jordyn Tyson
items.headline: New Orleans Football’s Mike Triplett reports that the Saints had Jordyn Tyson work with doctors at the University of Wisconsin to address his recurring hamstring issues.
items.analysis: Tyson has dealt with recurring hamstring injuries since October 2025, and was most recently sidelined by a hamstring strain suffered on August 13th. According to Triplett, the Saints sent Tyson to be evaluated by Dr. Heiderscheit and his team, which received a $4 million research grant from the NFL in 2021 to study hamstring issues, twice during his three-month rehab program. Dr. Heiderscheit successfully treated Packers WR Christian Watson’s recurring hamstring injuries in 2024. According to Triplett, the specialists “determined that something was a little small” in Tyson’s hamstring fascia, which allowed the Saints’ training staff to update Tyson’s exercise regimen with needed alterations. Per Tyson, the changes have allowed the tissue “to fire better.” Given Dr. Heiderscheit’s track record, Tyson’s odds of remaining healthy for the rest of the season are trending upward. He warrants WR3/FLEX treatment at this time.

items.name: Leonard Williams
items.headline: Seahawks ruled out Leonard Williams (stinger) for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: The Seahawks’ defense should be fine without him against a Raiders offense now led by rookie QB Fernando Mendoza. The Seahawks will have LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) and OG Anthony Bradford (knee) on the field this week, though.

items.name: Sione Vaki
items.headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Vaki sat out on Wednesday and Thursday before practicing in a limited capacity on Friday. He remains a worthwhile stash as the Lions’ No. 2 running back. His backup, Jacob Saylors (neck/hamstring), is good to go.

items.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
items.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: St. Brown was listed as questionable in Week 9 after practicing in a limited capacity all week. He managed to suit up on game day, posting an 8/86 receiving line. He was limited in all three practices this week and once again got hit with the questionable tag. We expect him to play. He should be treated as a WR1, as usual, assuming he is active.

items.name: Dont'e Thornton
items.headline: Dont’e Thornton (back) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Thornton’s injury woes continue. The young wide receiver spent much of the year on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. He had a back injury last week, and now another back injury threatens his availability. Thornton does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats, though he provides the team with a downfield element when active.

items.name: Vega Ioane
items.headline: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) practiced in full on Friday.
items.analysis: Ioane should have no issue playing against the Chargers on Monday night, nor should S Kyle Hamilton (hip), who has practiced in full in each of the last two days. Having Ioane on the field will be a big help for Jacoby Brissett in his first start for Baltimore.

items.name: Rashod Bateman
items.headline: Rashod Bateman (calf) practiced in full on Friday.
items.analysis: Bateman is firmly on track to play in the Ravens’ Monday Night Football game against the Chargers. Bateman will provide new QB Jacoby Brissett with a downfield option, but the veteran wide receiver is almost entirely reliant in ripping off one or two big plays, which has proven to be a difficult proposition for him on a weekly basis.

items.name: Keaton Mitchell
items.headline: Keaton Mitchell (hip) was limited on Friday.
items.analysis: Mitchell is trending in the right direction for the Chargers’ Week 10 game against the Ravens. The two teams play in this week’s Monday Night Football game. Mitchell is worth stashing in 12-team leagues, but he likely lacks RB2 upside.

items.name: David Njoku
items.headline: David Njoku (fibula) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Njoku is still within his 21-day practice window and has remained limited for five straight practices. He could end up playing on Monday night, but he does not need to be rostered.

items.name: Tre' Harris
items.headline: Tre’ Harris (shoulder) practiced in full on Friday.
items.analysis: Harris led the team in targets last week, but somehow managed just six yards on three catches. With Ladd McConkey (back) ailing, Harris could lead the team in targets again. He would only be a boom-bust FLEX in this case, though.

items.name: Ladd McConkey
items.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) did not practice on Friday.
items.analysis: This is unfortunate. McConkey is no stranger to playing through injury, but his availability for Week 10’s Monday Night Football game appears to be in jeopardy. If active, McConkey would be a WR2, but backup plans should be made at this time.

items.name: Joey Porter
items.headline: Joey Porter (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Porter got in a limited practice on Friday. He described himself as being at 70 percent health this week. The Cowboys listed DaRon Bland (ankle) and backup S Alijah Clark (illness) as questionable, and ruled out LB Donovan Ezeiruaku (ankle) and S P.J. Locke (concussion). Cowboys LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back) will play.

items.name: Jake Ferguson
items.headline: Cowboys ruled out Jake Ferguson (knee/ankle) for Week 10 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: This was the expected outcome. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters on Monday that Ferguson will likely be out for “multiple weeks” after suffering a knee injury. He was already dealing with an ankle injury when it happened. Ferguson does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

items.name: Tyler Goodson
items.headline: Cowboys ruled out Tyler Goodson (ankle/knee) for Week 10 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: The Cowboys will be without their No. 2 running back, removing what little threat there was to Javonte Williams’ workload. Goodson should remain stashed on 12-team benches if possible, though he could miss next week as well.

items.name: George Pickens
items.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) is not on the Cowboys’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Pickens makes his return after sitting out in Week 9. He played through the injury in Week 8, which may have been the wrong decision. The Cowboys’ No. 2 wide receiver encouragingly upgraded from limited to full participation today and can be treated as a WR2 in what should be a high-scoring game against the 49ers.

items.name: Trent Williams
items.headline: Trent Williams (shoulder) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Williams evidently injured his shoulder during the 49ers’ practice on Thursday, as did LB Dre Greenlaw (knee). 49ers OT Vederian Lowe would be Williams’ replacement if he cannot play. 49ers starting perimeter CBs Renardo Green (back) and Deommodore Lenoir (foot), and slot DB Upton Stout (shoulder) are also questionable.

items.name: Deebo Samuel
items.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) is not on the 49ers’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: The 49ers could end up limiting Samuel’s snaps in his first game back, but when he is on the field, he will likely be treated as the team’s No. 1 wide receiver. Samuel should be in fantasy football lineups as a WR3 with decent upside in what is expected to be a high-scoring game.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: 49ers ruled out Mike Evans (Achilles) for Week 10 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Losing Evans for this one is a bummer. The 49ers’ and Cowboys’ offenses should facilitate a high-scoring game environment. Regardless, the 49ers are smartly prioritizing Evans’ long-term health. Whenever he returns, he is likely to be full-go. Keep him stashed on fantasy football benches.

items.name: Chris Rodriguez
items.headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 10 injury report.
items.analysis: Rodriguez had three limited sessions ahead of this week and, should the Jaguars bludgeon the Titans, would profile to get some between-the-tackles work with Bhayshul Tuten dealing with ankle and foot injuries and not getting in much practice time. He’ll be a reasonable FLEX play against Tennessee.

items.name: Hjalte Froholdt
items.headline: Cardinals ruled out Hjalte Froholdt (concussion) for Week 10 against the Rams.
items.analysis: The Cardinals will be without Froholdt, their starting center, against a Rams team that is likely to rely on its ground game and ascending defense while navigating pass-catcher injuries. This makes life a little harder for rookie QB Carson Beck, who will make his first NFL start this week.

items.name: Chris Brooks
items.headline: Chris Brooks (ankle) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 10 game against the Vikings.
items.analysis: Brooks would have a chance to assume passing-down duties if he is activated off injured reserve. That would probably quash Pierre Strong’s value more than Marshawn Lloyd or Kaleb Johnson’s, but Brooks would probably be the favorite to see the most snaps among Green Bay’s runners if active. It would be a rough FLEX play against a good Vikings defense.

items.name: Micah Parsons
items.headline: Micah Parsons (knee/illness) will not play in Green Bay’s Week 10 game against the Vikings.
items.analysis: Parsons got in limited sessions all week and seems to be in line to play in Week 11 assuming he can upgrade to full work. The Packers have slowplayed his return and have been rewarded as their defense has been able to play quite well without him.

items.name: Colby Parkinson
items.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is not on the Rams’ final injury report for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Parkinson upgraded to full participation today. Tyler Higbee (illness) was limited. Both players were cleared to play. Davis Allen (oblique) is questionable, sandwiching a Thursday absence between two limited sessions. The Rams must be smart with their skill position players’ health, while asking as much as they can from their available players.

items.name: Charles Cross
items.headline: Charles Cross (ankle) won’t play in Seattle’s Week 10 game against the Raiders.
items.analysis: He did resume practicing on Thursday, but it was a quick hook and a Friday DNP. Still, it’s an encouraging sign for his status for Week 12 — after the Week 11 bye — that he was able to get on the practice field at all.

items.name: Rashid Shaheed
items.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) is not on Seattle’s final Week 10 injury report.
items.analysis: He’ll return to his boom/bust fantasy role as Seattle’s field-stretcher and punt returner after missing a few weeks due to this knee injury. Shaheed practiced in full all week and should not have any real limitations.

items.name: Drew Lock
items.headline: Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) is not on Seattle’s final Week 10 injury report.
items.analysis: Lock will step in as the starter again as Seattle takes on the Raiders, and he should profile as a reasonable superflex QB2. He was limited in all three practices this week, ceding some practice snaps to let Jalen Milroe run the show. The re-injury risk here does not quite appear to be zero.

items.name: Omar Cooper
items.headline: Omar Cooper (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Cooper was limited on Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full participation on Friday. The team listed him as questionable for a reason, but he is likely on the right side of questionable at this time. With Adonai Mitchell (knee) suddenly ailing, Cooper could warrant WR3 treatment against the Bills.

items.name: Adonai Mitchell
items.headline: Adonai Mitchell (knee) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Mitchell practiced in full today, but was added to the injury report with a new knee issue. This is a little concerning. The team could be trying to collect more info right now. We expect to hear more later today or at some point tomorrow. At this point, Mitchell must be viewed as firmly in the questionable column.

items.name: Chris Bell
items.headline: Chris Bell (knee) is doubtful for Miami’s Week 10 game against the Colts.
items.analysis: He did not practice Thursday or Friday after aggravating his surgically repaired knee in practice on Wednesday. The Dolphins have no reason to push Bell, so we’d be stunned if he played. Not that you were looking for reasons to lean into a Kyle McCord start, but Bell’s injury should free up targets for Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas on the FLEX line.

items.name: Garrett Wilson
items.headline: Garrett Wilson (concussion) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
items.analysis: All three of the Jets’ starting wide receivers are questionable to play, though Wilson practiced in full practice and is expected to play. Wilson could handle a hefty workload if he is indeed cleared to play, as expected, and one or two of the others are limited or ruled out. Wilson is a WR2 this week.

items.name: Carson Wentz
items.headline: Carson Wentz (ankle) is not on Minnesota’s final Week 10 injury report.
items.analysis: He’ll be Kirk Cousins’ QB2 on Sunday. Those of us who watched Monday’s game against the Bills are very grateful for that.

items.name: Kyler Murray
items.headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) won’t play in Minnesota’s Week 10 game against the Packers.
items.analysis: He wouldn’t have played anyway with Kirk Cousins coming over. Murray will reclaim QB2 duties when healthy, but dealing with a grade 2 strain on his hamstring, that may not be for a few weeks.

items.name: T.J. Hockenson
items.headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 10 game against the Packers.
items.analysis: Hockenson didn’t practice at any point this week and his status for Week 11 is likely in question as well. Gavin Bartholomew has picked up the slack this year when Hockenson has sat and will be a reasonable low-end TE2 play.

items.name: Dalton Kincaid
items.headline: Dalton Kincaid (ankle) is not on the Bills’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Jets.
items.analysis: With Kincaid’s multi-year knee injury behind him, the Bills’ tight end put together a great offseason and has proven to be a reliable player even when banged up this season. Kincaid is firmly in the TE1 ranks for this divisional showdown against the Jets in Week 10.

items.name: Danielle Hunter
items.headline: Danielle Hunter (hamstring) will not play in Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
items.analysis: Hunter popped up on the report with this injury on Thursday as limited and wound up ruled out after a DNP on Friday. Rough scenes for the $40 million-a-year edge rusher. This will be the first game he has missed since the 2021 season. Houston’s pass rush looks tenuous against the Browns with Will Anderson Jr. also on the questionable line.

items.name: Will Anderson
items.headline: Will Anderson (ankle) is questionable for Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
items.analysis: Anderson was added to the report as limited on Thursday and did not practice on Friday, throwing his status into major doubt ahead of Houston’s game in Cleveland. He has been listed with an ankle before this year, and with Danielle Hunter suddenly out, Cleveland’s pass offense could see some efficiency boosts against the Texans without their star rushers.

items.name: Marvin Harrison
items.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) won’t play in Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
items.analysis: Harrison did not practice on Thursday or Friday and it’s possible this develops into a longer-term injury. Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson will step in as reasonable FLEX plays with Harrison’s snaps off the table. The Texans probably won’t score 40 points again, but they have struggled to move the ball on the ground and should throw plenty against the Browns.

items.name: Tank Dell
items.headline: Tank Dell (hand/shoulder) is not on Houston’s final Week 10 injury report.
items.analysis: The diminutive speedster got in back-to-back full practices and should see a reasonable workload against the Browns. He’s a low-end WR3 or high-end FLEX play at this point, with more upside possible if he’s able to repeat last week’s target share.

items.name: David Montgomery
items.headline: David Montgomery (groin) is questionable for Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
items.analysis: Montgomery got in a full practice for the first time since returning from his groin injury. It’s certainly possible he’s back, but given a likely snap count in his return, it’d be hard to trust him as more than a what-the-heck FLEX.

items.name: Woody Marks
items.headline: Woody Marks (knee) is not on Houston’s final Week 10 injury report.
items.analysis: Marks was cleared after a full practice on Friday. Unfortunately, David Montgomery also got in a full practice and is questionable. Marks will retain RB2 status if Montgomery sits, but would probably go back in the FLEX bin if both are active.

items.name: Peter Skoronski
items.headline: Peter Skoronski (hamstring) won’t play in Tennessee’s Week 10 game against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Not exactly what the Titans needed, losing their best offensive lineman ahead of hosting the division leaders, but it’s what they’ll get. Skoronski should be considered questionable for Week 11 as well after not practicing at any point this week following Tennessee’s Week 9 bye.

items.name: Andrei Iosivas
items.headline: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is doubtful to play in Week 10 against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Iosivas is still technically on injured reserve, although the team designated him to return this week. Fellow injured reserve players, CB Jalen Davis (hamstring) and OG Brian Parker (knee), are also listed as doubtful. Bengals S Kyle Dugger (quad) has been ruled out.

items.name: Tony Pollard
items.headline: Tony Pollard (finger/rest) is not on Tennessee’s final Week 10 injury report.
items.analysis: A Friday tradition unlike any other. Pollard, somehow still a Titan, will suit up as an fringe RB2 against the Jaguars on Sunday.

items.name: Tyjae Spears
items.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 10 game against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: If Spears can play, this is theoretically the kind of blowout game script that sets him up for FLEX value via PPR scam. We wouldn’t advise chasing it, but we wouldn’t be surprised if it happened. Spears got in a full practice today, which would seem to leave him on the optimistic side of questionable.

items.name: Jaylon Moore
items.headline: Chiefs ruled out RT Jaylon Moore (concussion) for Week 10 against the Falcons.
items.analysis: Moore will unfortunately miss this weekend’s game against the Falcons, who field a capable defensive tackle unit. Atlanta has not defended the run well, though, so the Chiefs should be able to get by without him. Chiefs CB Mansoor Delane (shoulder) is questionable to play.

items.name: Xavier Worthy
items.headline: Xavier Worthy (hamstring) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Falcons.
items.analysis: Patrick Mahomes will have his speedy wide receiver on the field this weekend. Unfortunately for Worthy, he may be operating in a reduced role with Josh Downs now in Kansas City. Worthy can still be rostered in 12-team formats, but his play could be even more volatile.

items.name: Kenneth Walker
items.headline: Kenneth Walker (groin) is questionable for Kansas City’s Week 10 game against the Falcons.
items.analysis: Not much of a surprise after he sat out Friday with what Andy Reid called a “tight groin.” This has officially waded into “we’ll see” territory over the weekend. Emmett Johnson would be a low-end RB1 with a good workload if Walker is ruled out ahead of Sunday’s games.

items.name: Blake Corum
items.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes Blake Corum’s development as a pass catcher has helped the Rams deal with increasing blitz rates.
items.analysis: Leaning on Corum and No. 1 RB Kyren Williams has helped the Rams achieve a three-game winning streak, and Atkins notes that the Rams are 4-0 this season when Corum plays at least 30 percent of the offensive snaps. His development as a receiver and pass protector has erased run-pass tells pre-snap. Corum’s development as a weapon in the screen game, specifically, has allowed the Rams to beat the increasing blitz rates they have faced since Davante Adams (hamstring) was lost as a downfield receiving weapon. Corum belongs in starting lineups on a weekly basis at this point, as he establishes himself as a reliable RB2 in both real life and fantasy football.

items.name: Alvin Kamara
items.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 10 injury report.
items.analysis: As usual, Kamara’s back listing has not prevented him in any real way from playing. A potential Travis Etienne activation off injured reserve could cut into his FLEX value in Week 10, but if Etienne stays on IR, Kamara will be a reasonable play against a rough Panthers run defense.

items.name: Derrick Harmon
items.headline: Derrick Harmon (foot) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 10 game against the Bengals.
items.analysis: He got in a full practice on Friday and spoke with reporters as well. Based on that, we’d guess he’s got a good chance to be activated off injured reserve and play against the Bengals in the first week of his 21-day window.

items.name: Ben Skowronek
items.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) is not on Pittsburgh’s final Week 10 injury report.
items.analysis: We’ll see if he goes back to being a thorn in the ceiling cases for the remainder of the Steelers’ offensive players against the Bengals. Skowronek has no standalone value.

items.name: Jakobi Meyers
items.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 10 injury report.
items.analysis: Meyers will be in line for a FLEX-worthy workload against the Titans. The good news is that the over/under has climbed to 46.5 after last week’s date with Joey Fagnano, leaving Meyers as a more viable touchdown threat in Week 10 than he was in a limited passing workload against the Ravens.

items.name: Bhayshul Tuten
items.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 10 injury report.
items.analysis: He practiced on Friday and, as it was last week, the Jaguars cleared him with just one practice. He’ll be an upside RB2 against the Titans.

items.name: Fred Johnson
items.headline: Eagles released OT Fred Johnson.
items.analysis: Johnson is a decent bet to receive interest via the waiver wire. He has played for the Eagles since 2023, logging 1,589 offensive and special teams snaps combined. While he primarily contributed as a traditional tackle, the Eagles would at times line him up as an extra blocker at tight end. He is not a reliable starter, but can still contribute in the right situation.

items.name: Terrance Ferguson
items.headline: Rams ruled out Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Ferguson is expected to be out for a couple of weeks, though the Rams are fortuitously on bye in Week 11. The rest of the Rams’ tight ends are in varying states of health. Colby Parkinson (ribs) will likely play through his injury again. Tyler Higbee (illness) and Davis Allen (oblique) did not practice on Thursday. Their game status has not been revealed.

items.name: Trent McDuffie
items.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) is questionable for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: The Rams were optimistic about McDuffie practicing on Thursday and playing on Sunday. The former did not happen. It sounds like he has a chance to play this weekend, but his recovery appears to be going slightly slower than expected. Rams S Kam Curl (toe) is also questionable to play, though LG Steve Avila (hamstring) has been ruled out.

items.name: Myles Garrett
items.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) is questionable for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters that he expects Garrett to play. This is unfortunate news for the Cardinals, who will be led by rookie Carson Beck in his first NFL start. Garrett played very well last week against the Commanders, but his preseason knee issue is apparently still bothering him. Hopefully, he can get healthy before the season’s end.

items.name: Puka Nacua
items.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua’s (knee/toe) return timeline has not changed.
items.analysis: A few days ago, McVay told reporters that Nacua would not be placed on injured reserve due to transaction limitations, so it was a bit surprising to see him land there yesterday. The move prompted some concern. He was initially expected to return in Week 14 or 15, and he will officially be eligible to return on the latter date against the Cowboys. As of today, he is on track to do so, just in time for the fantasy football playoffs. Nacua should not be dropped in any format. He will be a WR1 upon returning.

items.name: Travis Etienne
items.headline: Travis Etienne (hamstring) is questionable for New Orleans’ Week 10 game against the Panthers.
items.analysis: He did practice again today, finally hitting a full session, so he at least has cleared a full week of practices if nothing else. If Etienne does play he could be a reasonable FLEX option. There are reports that he could be on a snap count if he does play, and that mixes with the early-season usage to create a situation that isn’t necessarily guaranteed to smash. That said, the Panthers are an enticing matchup.

items.name: Kenneth Walker
items.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Kenneth Walker sat out Friday’s practice with a tight groin.
items.analysis: Reid added “we’ll see how he feels through this afternoon, with rehab, and through tomorrow.” Not exactly a glowing endorsement for Walker playing, though we expect the injury report later today to at least read questionable. If Walker were unable to go, Emmett Johnson would probably find himself with a low-end RB1 workload against the Falcons.

items.name: Taliese Fuaga
items.headline: Tailese Fuaga (knee) won’t play in New Orleans’ Week 10 game against the Panthers.
items.analysis: Fuaga has a knee sprain, per Kellen Moore. It sounds like a short-term thing and Moore has said he won’t need to go on injured reserve. Asim Richards and Mason Murphy are the backup tackles and Richards played left tackle while Kelvin Banks was sidelined earlier this season.

items.name: CJ Donaldson
items.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) won’t play in New Orleans’ Week 10 game against the Panthers.
items.analysis: The passing-down blocking back’s absence should create more opportunities for Alvin Kamara and, possibly, Travis Etienne in the passing game.

items.name: Harold Fannin
items.headline: Harold Fannin (groin) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 10 injury report against the Texans.
items.analysis: He’ll start and be a useful TE1 against a Texans defense that has had it’s share of downs in 2026. Fannin practiced every day this week and never seemed to be in real danger of missing time with the groin injury — he picked it up in practice ahead of last week’s game against the Saints.

items.name: Denzel Boston
items.headline: Denzel Boston (toe) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 10 game against the Texans.
items.analysis: He made it back on to the practice field on Friday, so he’s probably on the optimistic side of questionable at this point. Todd Monken did say at his Friday presser that Boston is “trending in the right direction.” Boston did miss the first two sessions of the week but has been no stranger to the injury report this year and has tended to gut it out. Boston was seen wearing a walking boot as he left the locker room. He still has a chance to play, but his status is worth monitoring closely.

items.name: Zachariah Branch
items.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will not play in Atlanta’s Week 10 game against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: He didn’t practice all week and enters Atlanta’s Week 11 bye off two completely lost weeks. The rookie hasn’t made much of an impact so far and doesn’t necessarily need to be kept on rosters in non-dynasty leagues at this point.

items.name: James Pearce
items.headline: James Pearce Jr. (back) is questionable for Atlanta’s Week 10 game against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Pearce got in two limited sessions on Thursday and Friday after missing Wednesday’s practice. He would appear to be on the optimistic side of questionable.

items.name: Marquise Brown
items.headline: Jordan Schultz reports the Eagles are waiving WR Hollywood Brown.
items.analysis: The trade market did not materialize for Mr. Brown, who has eight targets in four active games with the Eagles this year. He’ll look to catch on elsewhere down the stretch.

items.name: Elijah Higgins
items.headline: Cardinals signed TE Elijah Higgins to a three-year, extension.
items.analysis: Just weeks after earning a rare blurb from us here at Rotoworld, Higgins followed up his blurb-worthy performance with a three-year extension. The 26-year-old tight end has caught 18 passes for 162 yards and one touchdown this season, and is a year removed from the 30-301-0 line he posted last year. With the Cardinals hurting at receiver, it’s possible Higgins could see an expanded role going forward, especially after signing this deal, which can net him up to $26.8 million.

items.name: Zonovan Knight
items.headline: Bam Knight will play in Week 10 against the Rams after clearing concussion protocol.
items.analysis: After being upgraded to a full participant on Thursday, Knight is officially off of the injury report and good to go for Sunday’s game against the Rams. Both Knight and Tyler Allgeier are expected to factor heavily into the Cardinals’ running game this weekend, especially with Carson Beck making his first career start with a depleted receiving corps. Both Knight and Allgeier will be fringe RB3/Flex plays in a game that could prove tough for the Cardinals’ banged-up offense.

items.name: Jaelan Phillips
items.headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) is questionable for Week 10 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Despite the questionable designation, it’s safe to say Phillips is trending in the right direction after being upgraded to a full participant for Friday’s practice. Barring any unexpected setbacks, we would assume Phillips will be good to go against the Saints. The Saints also listed CB Will Lee (hamstring) and OL Brady Christensen (hamstring) as questionable, and CB Mike Jackson (groin) as doubtful.

items.name: Xavier Legette
items.headline: Xavier Legette (knee) is questionable to play in Week 10 vs. the Saints.

items.name: Xavier Legette
items.headline: Xavier Legette (knee) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Legette has missed the past six games but could join the active squad for the first time since Week 2. Even if he returns this week, the third-year wideout may have trouble carving out a fantasy-relevant receiving role every week behind Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble, and running back Chuba Hubbard. However, even in this crowded picture, the 25-year-old could warrant a stash in some deep leagues for those craving anyone with upside at wide receiver. His added presence could help Bryce Young’s fantasy value as the season goes on.

items.name: Jonathon Brooks
items.headline: Jonathon Brooks (core) is doubtful for Week 10 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Brooks was previously listed as a full participant in Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices, only for head coach Dave Canales to announce on Friday that Brooks was working with the scout team, not the 53-man roster, meaning he was actually limited throughout the week. After logging three limited practices, Brooks appears unlikely to play in Week 10 given the doubtful designation. With his return window opened earlier this week, the Panthers could delay his return by two more weeks before having to either rule him out for the season or activate him from injured reserve. We will see how things go for him next week ahead of Week 11’s game against the Ravens.

items.name: Hunter Henry
items.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) will play in Week 10 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Despite his listing with a limited practice on all three days this week, Henry was cleared from the injury report and is set for a normal role versus Detroit in Munich, Germany. Though he typically jostles each week for snaps and target share with promising rookie Eli Raridon, Henry remains one of New England’s most logical aerial threats in the red zone. Fantasy managers desperate for tight end help could do worse than throwing a dart with Henry.

items.name: Israel Abanikanda
items.headline: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Israel Abanikanda will serve as the team’s RB2 in Week 10 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Abanikanda will get the practice squad elevation over Kendre Miller, who recently signed with the team after being released by the Saints. Abanikanda has spent part of the last two seasons with the Cowboys and had a solid preseason, rushing for 91 scoreless yards on 22 carries while adding three receptions for 16 yards. We wouldn’t expect Abanikanda to see enough meaningful work to be fantasy relevant this week but he could be worth a stash in deeper leagues as insurance for Javonte Williams.

items.name: A.J. Brown
items.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) is listed as questionable for Week 10 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Despite his uncertain status, Brown, who was limited in all three practices during the week, will make the trip across the Atlantic Ocean with the Pats before their game in Munich, Germany. The veteran has missed two straight contests, and New England may decide to rest him once again before the team’s Week 11 bye. Should Brown suit up, he would sit in the WR2/WR3 tiers against a Detroit secondary that’s improved lately but has been generally friendly to receivers most of the season. If Brown can’t go, DeMario Douglas would take that baton as the top target; Mack Hollins, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams would see a boost into stronger Flex territory, and tight end Hunter Henry would slot into a more stream-worthy status.

items.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
items.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is questionable for Week 10 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Despite some belief that Stevenson could miss a short period of time due to a knee injury he suffered late in Week 9’s loss to the Packers, the 28-year-old back will have an outside chance at suiting up against the Lions after logging back-to-back limited practices to close out the week. Backup Corey Kiner is expected to step into an expanded role if Stevenson is unable to go, but will be hard to trust as anything more than an RB3/FLEX play if Stevenson does suit up. With the Pats and Lions set to face off at 9:30 AM EST in Germany, fantasy managers will want to check early inactives before setting their lineups if they either player on their roster.

items.name: Carnell Tate
items.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) will not play in Week 10 against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Head coach Robert Saleh said he is hopeful Tate will be able to return in Week 11 when the Titans visit the Cowboys, but his availability for that game will be determined once the Titans begin prepping for Dallas. In the meantime, the Titans will likely go with Wan’Dale Robinson and Chimere Dike as their top two wideouts after the pair led the team in routes run in Week 8 against the Bengals, with Elic Ayomanor also seeing some work (30 routes). Playing against a stout Jaguars defense will make all of the Titans’ receivers hard to trust as anything more than WR3/WR4 plays, while TE Gunnar Helm could also see more work after earning a season-high eight targets vs. the Bengals.

items.name: Omar Cooper
items.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Omar Cooper (ankle) will be a full participant in Friday’s practice.
items.analysis: Assuming all goes well, Cooper will likely be removed from the injury report before the end of the day, meaning he will be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Bills. Cooper caught eight passes for 58 yards in Week 9’s loss to the Chiefs, but that was with Garrett Wilson (concussion) sidelined. While we wouldn’t expect another 11-target outing from Cooper with Wilson expected to be active for Week 10, he could have some FLEX appeal after yet another strong showing. We will check back in with a final status update on Cooper when the team announces it later in the day.

items.name: Garrett Wilson
items.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said he is “confident” that Garrett Wilson (concussion) will play in Week 10 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Glenn said Wilson has one more step to clear before he is out of the league’s concussion protocol. Wilson missed last week’s game against the Chiefs due to his brain injury, but has practiced in a limited capacity twice this week and is trending toward a return. We will get a final update on Wilson once he has officially cleared the protocol, but fantasy managers can start him as a mid-to-high-end WR2 in a game that could feature plenty of points against a high-powered Bills offense.

items.name: Jordan Davis
items.headline: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Jordan Davis will not play in Week 10 against the Titans.
items.analysis: Neither Davis nor recently acquired safety Jessie Bates had bye weeks with their previous teams, which Coen noted when announcing that the two players would be sidelined for Week 10. The decision to sit both players will essentially give them a “bye week,” and it conveniently comes in a week when the Jaguars face an inferior opponent in Tennessee. Both players should be good to go in Week 11 when the Jaguars visit the Giants.

items.name: Lamar Jackson
items.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter released a statement saying Lamar Jackson (thumb) will be out for the next 6-10 weeks.
items.analysis: On the short end of this timeline, Jackson could return in Week 16 against the Browns. On the long end, Jackson would be looking at returning around the Wild Card or Divisional Round of the playoffs if the Ravens make the postseason. This timeline closely aligns with the 6-9 week absence NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported earlier in the week. If this isn’t a season-ender for Lamar, it will be close, and how the Ravens perform over the next several weeks with Jacoby Brissett under center will likely determine whether the Ravens dress him for the final few weeks of the season, even if he is ready to go. Minter said that Jackson is “doing well” after suffering his injury in Week 8 against the Bills, which is encouraging, but we’re a long way from knowing if a return for Jackson is truly in the cards. The 4-5 Ravens have lost their last four games but hope to turn things around on Monday night when they play host to the Chargers.

items.name: C.J. Henderson
items.headline: Falcons signed CB C.J. Henderson to a two-year extension.
items.analysis: The former 2020 first-rounder can earn up to $20 million on his new deal, per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, with $11 million being guaranteed. Henderson was drafted No. 9 overall by the Jaguars in 2020, but has since bounced around to the Panthers, Texans, and Steelers, and was actually cut by the Falcons in August 2025 during final roster cutdowns after camp. Since then, Henderson has played his way not only onto the 53-man roster, but into a starting role. He has started six of the eight games he has appeared in for Atlanta this season, totaling 41 tackles, nine pass breakups, and one fumble recovery while earning a PFF coverage grade of 65.3. Playing almost exclusively on the outside, he has allowed opposing receivers to go for 252 yards and three touchdowns on 44 targets.

items.name: Cameron Thomas
items.headline: Falcons signed DE Cameron Thomas to a three-year contract extension.
items.analysis: Thomas has started all nine games he has appeared in for the Falcons this season. The 26-year-old lineman spent the previous two seasons in Cleveland with head coach Kevin Stefanski, and then joined Stefanski in Atlanta on a one-year deal this offseason. Thomas has totaled 25 tackles, two sacks, and one TFL this season for the Falcons, earning a PFF grade of 77.2. His deal is worth up to $33 million and he will now be under contract through the 2029 season.

items.name: Malik Nabers
items.headline: Malik Nabers caught 5-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders.
items.analysis: Nabers was clearly not a point of emphasis in a game expected to carry significant weather impacts. Despite the weather subsiding in the second half, McCarthy remained fixed on Isaiah Likely, feeding the veteran tight end 11 targets. The matchup also played a role in the game plan, with the Commanders missing numerous key linebackers while blitzing at an above average rate. Nabers is in a good spot to bounce back against the Jaguars in Week 11, where he’ll return to WR1 status in fantasy circles.

items.name: Malachi Fields
items.headline: Malachi Fields caught 3-of-4 targets for 62 yards in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders.
items.analysis: The New York wide receivers were clearly limited by a game plan to feature tight end Isaiah Likely, with the starting trio of Malik Nabers, Fields, and Darnell Mooney combining for just 10 receptions, one more than the nine of Likely. Even so, Fields continued to demonstrate a strong connection with quarterback J.J. McCarthy as the rookie finished second on the team in receiving despite seeing only four targets. The highlight of the game came in the second half when McCarthy threaded a ball over one defender and underneath two more down the left sideline for a 25-yard gain to Fields. Although his weekly volume likely won’t be vast enough to return consistent fantasy production without an injury to Nabers or Likely, Fields continues to show the growth dynasty managers were hoping for.

items.name: Isaiah Likely
items.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 9-of-11 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders.
items.analysis: Likely as clearly the going-in game plan in a game expected to be heavily influenced by weather. The rain cleared in the first half but Likely remained the featured option through the air, likely influenced by heavy blitz rates and unrelenting pressure from the Washington defense. The 11-target game was the fifth time this season that the veteran tight end hit double-digit targets but the first time doing so with J.J. McCarthy under center. Likely remains a surefire TE1 ahead of a difficult matchup against the Jaguars in Week 11.

items.name: Cam Skattebo
items.headline: Cam Skattebo rushed 18 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders, adding 44 yards on three receptions.
items.analysis: Skattebo immediately returned to a workhorse role following the shortcomings of Devin Singletary in Week 10, the latter of whom saw but one opportunity to the 22 of Skattebo. The Skatt-man bookended halftime with a score from one yard out on the team’s final possession of the first half and a score from 13 yards out on the team’s first possession of the second half, earning two backflips in the process. The second-year back also escaped down the sideline for a 34-yard reception in the first quarter to pad his counting stats. Despite the resurgence in workload, Skattebo will be a borderline FLEX option in a difficult matchup against the pass-funnel Jaguars in Week 11.

items.name: J.J. McCarthy
items.headline: J.J. McCarthy completed 23-of-36 passes for 293 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Giants’ 24-21, Week 10 loss to the Commanders, adding 34 yards on six carries.
items.analysis: McCarthy appeared to be in complete control throughout before a game-sealing interception with under a minute to play in a three-point game. He demonstrated plus pocket presence and made numerous dime-worthy throws, the most impressive of which was a 25-yard dart to rookie Malachi Fields that was put in the only place where Fields could come down with the ball, over one defender and underneath two more down the left sideline. McCarthy leaned heavily on Isaiah Likely, feeding the veteran tight end 11 targets in what appeared to be a matchup-based game plan in the face of an aggressive pass rush. The Giants fall to 5-3-1 with the loss and pass the first tie-breaker to the Commanders after the two teams’ tie earlier this season. The Giants get a difficult matchup against arguably the most well-rounded roster in the AFC when they host the Jaguars in Week 11, where McCarthy falls to a mid-range QB2 in fantasy circles.

items.name: Treylon Burks
items.headline: Treylon Burks caught 2-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
items.analysis: Burks fought through clear discomfort after coming into the game listed questionable following a Wednesday downgrade on the practice report, catching two early passes for 27 yards before succumbing to the inside-funnel nature of the New York defense. Quarterback Jayden Daniels directed 22 of his 33 pass attempts to the trio of Stefon Diggs, Chig Okonkwo, and Ben Sinnott over the middle of the field. Burks’ situation is unlikely to improve in Week 11 with lockdown perimeter corner DJ Turner on deck.

items.name: Ben Sinnott
items.headline: Ben Sinnott caught all four targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
items.analysis: Sinnott entered the game with just one reception this season while playing as the primary blocking tight end alongside Chig Okonkwo. Okonkwo departed in the second quarter with a back injury and returned to start the second half, with the time off the field paving the way for Sinnott to triple his year-to-date reception total and score his first touchdown of the season. He would add one reception in the second half to push his total to four. The touchdown reception also came with a bit of intrigue as the pass appeared to be targeting Stefon Diggs in the end zone. Sinnott was on a crossing route at the goal line and happened to cross paths at the perfect time. He will not be fantasy viable for as long as Okonkwo remains healthy.

items.name: Antonio Williams
items.headline: Antonio Williams caught both targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
items.analysis: Williams cashed in on his first target of the game for a 31-yard score in the third quarter, adding one additional grab for 11 yards in the final frame. The electric rookie continues to play starters snaps and challenge for the team lead in route rate but had yet to get completely on the same page with quarterback Jayden Daniels, the latter of whom leaned heavily on Stefon Diggs and tight end Chig Okonkwo in this one. The talent is undeniable for Williams, but fantasy managers would love to see a bump in targets before feeling comfortable entering him into starting lineups. Williams’ next chance to return a usable fantasy outing comes in Week 11 against the inside-funnel Bengals, where he should avoid the primary coverage of lockdown corner DJ Turner.

items.name: Stefon Diggs
items.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 6-of-10 targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
items.analysis: Diggs and the Washington pass offense went as Jayden Daniels went, with the dual threat quarterback mixing perfectly thrown passes with completely errant ones, two of which were directed toward Diggs. A third incompletion bounced off Diggs’ helmet as the veteran receiver should have drawn a defensive pass interference penalty, with the ball eventually ruled an incompletion upon further review after Treylon Burks appeared to come down with what would have been one of the wilder receptions of the season. Daniels’ best pass of the game came on the game-winning touchdown to Diggs in the flat on a crosser, threaded between two defenders. Diggs made a third miss as he took it into the end zone from 32 yards out to send the team to a 3-5-1 record, now two games behind the Giants with the first tie-breaker in hand. He will remain a volatile WR3 on capped routes against the Bengals in Week 11.

items.name: Austin Ekeler
items.headline: Austin Ekeler rushed nine times for 26 yards in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants, adding 26 yards on four receptions.
items.analysis: The veteran in-season addition’s 13 opportunities matched that of starter Rachaad White, the latter of whom played the team’s first two drives before splitting the workload the rest of the way. Ekeler also split red zone work, although it was White that nearly missed a touchdown on a seven-yard run that was tackled at the one in the second quarter. Either way, the near-even split between the two caps the fantasy upside of both backs in the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt, with neither on the fantasy radar ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Bengals.

items.name: Rachaad White
items.headline: Rachaad White rushed 11 times for 47 yards in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants, adding five yards on one reception.
items.analysis: White started in name only, playing the first two drives before splitting backfield duties with fellow veteran Austin Ekeler for the remainder of the game. The two backs ended with the same number of opportunities while also splitting red zone work, with White narrowly missing a touchdown in the second quarter on his second longest run of the evening, a seven-yard scamper up the gut that was stopped at the one. His lone explosive run went for 18 yards, with those two carries accounting for more than 50 percent of his yardage total on the ground. White has fallen into a strict timeshare in the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt and brings little fantasy upside ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Bengals.

items.name: Jayden Daniels
items.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 23-of-33 passes for 249 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Commanders’ 24-21, Week 10 win over the Giants, adding 28 yards on 10 carries.
items.analysis: A late second quarter touchdown drive that was sparked by a long reception by veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs was capped off by tight end Ben Sinnott’s first touchdown of the season to send the Commanders into the half with a three-point lead. The two sides would trade touchdowns in the third quarter before the wheels appeared to fall off for Washington, with their first three possessions of the final frame going turnover on downs, interception, and interception, allowing the Giants to nurse a four-point lead inside the two-minute warning. Daniels drove the field in 49 seconds on just three plays, connecting with Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown with under a minute remaining. The Commanders would escape on the backs of a Rasul Douglas interception to send the team to a 3-5-1 record, now two games back of the Giants and with the first tie-breaker in hand following the previous tie. Daniels will look to keep the momentum going in a Week 11 meeting with the surging Bengals, where he will be an upside QB1 in another must-win game.

items.name: Jayden Daniels
items.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 23-of-33 passes for 249 yards, three touchdown, and two interceptions in the Commanders’ 24-21, Week 10 win over the Giants, adding 28 yards on 10 carries.

items.name: Chig Okonkwo
items.headline: Chig Okonkwo (back) is questionable to return to Week 10 against the Giants.
items.analysis: Okonkwo was accompanied by trainers to the locker room after failing to play on a three-and-out possession in the second quarter against the Giants. The team deemed him questionable to return before the subsequent possession. Okonkwo caught both targets for 17 yards prior to departing.

items.name: Puka Nacua
items.headline: Rams placed Puka Nacua on injured reserve with knee and toe injuries.
items.analysis: Nacua will be eligible to return for the Rams’ Week 15 game against the Cowboys. The Rams are on bye in Week 11, and he is required to miss at least four games. It was previously reported that Nacua was expected to return in Week 14 or 15. Shortly before the team made this announcement, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said that the team was “confident” Nacua would return in that timeframe. Rams coach Sean McVay previously said that the Rams would not place him on injured reserve due to transaction limitations. It is unclear whether anything has changed. Nacua suffered PCL and MCL sprains, along with a turf toe injury in Week 10 against the Commanders. ESPN’s Adam Schefter specifically cited Nacua’s MCL sprain after the move was made, adding that McVay said Nacua will miss “extended time.” Nacua should be stashed on fantasy football benches at this time.

items.name: Colby Parkinson
items.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Parkinson should play through his injury again this week. Unfortunately, Tyler Higbee (illness) did not practice, as a new addition to the injury report, and Davis Allen (oblique) was downgraded to being a non-participant. The running backs are going to get all the work they can handle this week.

items.name: Trent McDuffie
items.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Earlier today, we were told that McDuffie would resume practicing today. It turns out that report was wrong. McDuffie is on the wrong side of questionable. Myles Garrett (knee) was limited. Steve Avila (hamstring) and Kam Curl (toe) did not practice.

items.name: Rashod Bateman
items.headline: Rashod Bateman (calf) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Ravens face the Chargers in Week 10’s Monday Night Football game, theoretically giving Bateman decent odds of suiting up. He does not need to be in starting lineups as a touchdown-dependent FLEX, though.

items.name: Vega Ioane
items.headline: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Ravens’ stud rookie guard is on track to play this week, albeit with a new shoulder issue. Running backs Rasheen Ali (ankle) and Adam Randall (neck/hamstring) are practicing in full. They should play as well.

items.name: Zonovan Knight
items.headline: Bam Knight (concussion) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: Knight is on track to resume his lead rushing role this week. Unfortunately, the Cardinals face the Seahawks, potentially rendering Knight a touchdown-dependent FLEX starter against their elite defense. Hopefully, Knight remains setback-free for the rest of the week.

items.name: Deebo Samuel
items.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Samuel is still stuck in the questionable column, but his continued participation tentatively puts him on track to play in a fantasy-friendly matchup against the Cowboys in Week 10. If active, Samuel could end up serving as the 49ers’ No. 1 wide receiver. He would warrant WR3 treatment in this scenario.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) will not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: At this point, Evans seems like a long shot to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys. The 49ers allowed Christian McCaffrey to try to play through his Achilles tendinitis and it did not go well. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan indicated they learned from the experience and will let Evans get fully healthy before allowing him to retake the field.

items.name: Charles Cross
items.headline: Charles Cross (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
items.analysis: Cross and LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) were both limited at today’s practice, giving them a chance to play on Sunday against the Cardinals. Seahawks stud DT Leonard Williams (stinger) remains sidelined.

items.name: Drew Lock
items.headline: Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Lock reportedly resumed throwing today, which is good to hear. He told reporters that the oblique injury is on the right side of his body, on the back of the muscle, which he thinks makes it easier to throw the football than when he had an oblique injury on the left side of his body two years ago. Lock is a QB2 this week against the Cardinals.

items.name: Paulson Adebo
items.headline: Giants declared CB Paulson Adebo, OT J.C. Davis, OL Josh Sills, CB Nikko Reed, DT C.J. Okoye, TE Thomas Fidone and OLB Malik Harrison inactive for Week 10 against the Commanders.
items.analysis: The Giants are seemingly demoting Adebo, who entered the season as one of the team’s top-three cornerbacks. Colton Hood will take his place. Aside from that, Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and J.J. McCarthy (hip) are good to go tonight, in what is expected to be a rainy Thursday Night Football game.

items.name: Isaac Yiadom
items.headline: Commanders declared QB Athan Kaliakmanis, CB Isaac Yiadom, DT Ricky Barber, G Tanoa Togiai, C Lucas Patrick and TE Colson Yankoff inactive for Week 10 against the Giants.
items.analysis: Among the Commanders’ players who are currently healthy enough to practice, most of them will play. Treylon Burks (foot) could end up being a decoy, but Chig Okonkwo (hip) should be good to go. Only Yiadom and a few others are unable to go on Thursday night, though tonight’s kickoff could be delayed by weather.

items.name: Keaton Mitchell
items.headline: Keaton Mitchell (hip) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Mitchell should be good to go for Week 10’s Monday Night Football game against the Ravens. He and Omarion Hampton seemingly put a little distance between Kimani Vidal in the second half last week, though Mitchell only makes for a shaky bench stash.

items.name: David Njoku
items.headline: David Njoku (fibula) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Njoku is not worth rostering whenever he officially returns to the active roster, but he theoretically can contribute offensively. He will likely be a mildly productive member of the Chargers’ three-player tight end rotation.

items.name: Tre' Harris
items.headline: Tre’ Harris (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Harris led the team with seven targets last week, catching just three of them for six yards. Although he is not fantasy-relevant on his own, his presence theoretically helps Justin Herbert and Harris is on track to play in this week’s Monday Night Football game.

items.name: Ladd McConkey
items.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: The back spasms that sidelined McConkey in Week 9 against the Texans evidently remain an issue. The Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver should be viewed as questionable to play in Week 10’s Thursday Night Football game. The rest of the receiving corps is too unreliable for a WR3-level pivot if he is unable to play.

items.name: Carson Wentz
items.headline: Carson Wentz (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Wentz is tentatively on track to be available for backup duties. Kyler Murray (hamstring) remains sidelined. Neither Vikings quarterback needs to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

items.name: T.J. Hockenson
items.headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Hockenson still has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Packers, but at this point, it seems likely that he will miss at least one game. Hockenson’s potential absence would likely allow Jordan Addison to earn a little more work than he has in recent weeks. Stay tuned.

items.name: George Pickens
items.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Pickens is still stuck in the questionable column, though his continued participation is a good sign. The team allowed him to play through the injury in Week 8 against the Cardinals, which was probably the wrong call. He sat out last week despite practicing in a limited capacity. Hopefully, he upgrades to full participation tomorrow. Stay tuned.

items.name: Joey Porter
items.headline: Joey Porter (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Porter reportedly told reporters that his “whole foot is jacked up.” That sounds bad. He was able to run today, and hadn’t in a while, but declined to say whether he will play in Week 10 against the 49ers. We suspect he will sit out this weekend’s contest.

items.name: Marvin Harrison
items.headline: Marvin Harrison (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Harrison was limited yesterday and sat out today. That series of events typically suggests that the player was injured in practice. Harrison is firmly on the wrong side of questionable at this time. He can be stashed in 12-team leagues, but it may take him a while to get back into form.

items.name: Tank Dell
items.headline: Tank Dell (hand/shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: Dell is firmly on track to play in Week 10 against the Browns. He led the team with nine targets last week, catching four passes for 105 yards and one touchdown. The coaching staff reportedly drew up a play just to get him over the century mark. He is a FLEX starter this week.

items.name: Denzel Boston
items.headline: Denzel Boston (toe) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: This morning, Boston told reporters that he was hoping to resume practicing today. Unfortunately, he was unable to do so. That said, Boston’s toe injury is feeling better and things are “trending up” at the moment. It sounds like the rookie wide receiver has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Texans and would be a WR3/FLEX if so.

items.name: Harold Fannin
items.headline: Harold Fannin (groin) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Fannin is on track to play in Week 10 against the Texans. Houston’s nominally elite defense struggled for much of the season, but got back on track against the Chargers last week. It remains to be seen if they can keep the solid play going. Fannin is a TE1 regardless.

items.name: Micah Parsons
items.headline: Micah Parsons (knee/illness) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Parsons seemingly has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Vikings, but he remains in the questionable column at this time. Packers DC Jonathan Gannon has done well with Parsons sidelined. Getting him back will only improve the unit.

items.name: Xavier Worthy
items.headline: Xavier Worthy (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: We got word early on Wednesday that Worthy would suit up for practice. He ended up being a full participant and remained full today, putting him firmly on track to play in Week 10 against the Falcons. Worthy is down to being a touchdown-dependent FLEX with Josh Downs now on the roster, but his presence helps out Patrick Mahomes.

items.name: Chris Bell
items.headline: Chris Bell (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Dolphins were regularly limiting Bell’s practice reps earlier this season, so this may just be routine maintenance. The rookie wide receiver was limited yesterday. Bell has not yet established himself as a fantasy-relevant player, and he is unlikely to do so in Kyle McCord’s first start, especially if his surgically repaired knee is bothering him.

items.name: Trent McDuffie
items.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
items.analysis: Yesterday, The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reported that the Rams were hopeful that McDuffie would play in Week 10 against the Cardinals. He is tentatively on track to do so with today’s return to practice. The Rams will potentially morph into a run-heavy team that relies on the defense to generate turnovers with their top-two wide receivers and top tight end sidelined. McDuffie can help them accomplish that.

items.name: Taliese Fuaga
items.headline: Taliese Fuaga (knee) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Saints’ right tackle was added to the injury report today, which is extremely unfortunate. The team is already without center Erik McCoy (biceps). Hopefully, this is only a minor issue for Fuaga.

items.name: Omar Cooper
items.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Back-to-back limited sessions have us believing Cooper has a good chance to play in Week 10 against the Bills. The role has been up-and-down as the Jets struggle to work in all their weapons. Cooper qualifies as a FLEX play against what has been a shaky Bills defense when not facing Carson Wentz this season.

items.name: Travis Etienne
items.headline: Travis Etienne (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Etienne is firmly in the questionable camp for the Saints’ Week 10 game against the Panthers. New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill believes that the Saints would keep Etienne on a snap count if he makes his return this weekend, noting “they took it easy” on Jordyn Tyson, who returned from a lengthy hamstring injury last week. If active, Etienne likely warrants low-end RB2 treatment.

items.name: Garrett Wilson
items.headline: Garrett Wilson (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Wilson still needs to be officially cleared from concussion protocol to play, but two limited sessions have him with a real chance to be active in Week 10 after missing Week 9. If he can play, Wilson will likely be an upside fantasy WR2 against the Bills.

items.name: Jakobi Meyers
items.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
items.analysis: Meyers was limited at today’s practice. He is on track to play through the injury this week after doing so successfully last week, along with a hamstring injury. The Jaguars’ dominance has rendered Meyers somewhat of a touchdown-reliant FLEX starter, though this is a soft matchup against the Titans.

items.name: Dalton Kincaid
items.headline: Dalton Kincaid (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: After two limited sessions we don’t have a lot of doubt that Kincaid will be ready to play in Week 10’s game against the Jets. He may be managed a bit, though, as he toughs it out. He’ll remain a TE1 play regardless.

items.name: Chris Rodriguez
items.headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Rodriguez played through the hand injury without issue last week, totaling 10 carries and two receptions on Thursday night. He should again handle a FLEX-worthy workload against the Titans in Week 10, with Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) managing something.

items.name: Jared Goff
items.headline: Jared Goff (chest) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: That should alleviate any concern that he’d miss Sunday morning’s Munich kickoff against the Patriots. Goff will be a low-end QB1 for that one assuming no major negative news hits on Friday.

items.name: Bhayshul Tuten
items.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Tuten sat out all three practices before playing in last week’s Thursday Night Football game, totaling 12 carries in the process. We tentatively expect him to play in Week 10 against the Titans, and he should be in fantasy football lineups even if he sits out or is limited on Friday. Stay tuned.

items.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
items.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: He played through this last week, managing an 8/86 line against the Dolphins. We’d be surprised if he wasn’t removed from the injury report tomorrow after getting in two limited sessions on Wednesday and Thursday.

items.name: Cade Mays
items.headline: Cade Mays (ankle) will not play in Detroit’s Week 10 game against the Patriots.
items.analysis: He did not travel to Munich with the team and has not practiced since injuring his ankle in Week 8. Juice Scruggs will continue to fill in at center.

items.name: D.J. Reed
items.headline: D.J. Reed (hip) won’t play in Detroit’s Week 10 game against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Reed has not practiced since injuring his hip in Week 8. The Lions’ secondary remains a patchwork effort against Drake Maye and the Patriots.

items.name: Kerby Joseph
items.headline: Kerby Joseph (knee) won’t play in Detroit’s Week 10 game against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Joseph got in a full practice session with the Lions on Thursday, but will not travel to Munich with the club. It sounds like he’ll have a real chance to play in Week 11 when the Lions head back to the states.

items.name: Peter Skoronski
items.headline: Peter Skoronski (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Titans’ starting left guard is very unlikely to play in Week 10 against the Jaguars, who field a top-tier defense. Skoronski has been sidelined since injuring his hamstring in Week 8 against the Bengals.

items.name: Tony Pollard
items.headline: Tony Pollard (finger/rest) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Pollard practiced in full yesterday, despite the finger injury. The Titans added the rest label to his listing today, indicating his absence is simply load management. We do not expect his snaps to be impacted by the finger injury this weekend. Tyjae Spears (knee) resumed practicing, though, which could hurt Pollard’s snap share. Stay tuned.

items.name: Hunter Henry
items.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: He played off a questionable tag last week with a more checked practice report, so we’d be surprised if Henry didn’t go on Sunday. He has a real chance of being cleared off the injury report altogether on Friday after a pair of limited sessions to open the week.

items.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
items.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday DNP. Post-Week 9 reports had Stevenson with a chance to miss a short period of time, but a limited session at least points to the idea that he could play in Munich on Sunday morning. Fantasy managers reliant on Stevenson or dabbling with Corey Kiner will want to keep an eye on Friday’s injury report.

items.name: Tyjae Spears
items.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) resumed practicing on Thursday.
items.analysis: Spears was listed as a limited participant on today’s injury report, theoretically giving him a chance to play in Week 10 against the Jaguars’ elite run defense. Spears’ potential return could lower Tony Pollard’s snap share a tad, though Spears does not need to be rostered in 10-team leagues.

items.name: A.J. Brown
items.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Two limited practices would seem to have him with a real chance to play in Munich, and the fact that he made the trip at all makes it seem likely he’ll have a real chance to go. We’d consider him on the optimistic side of questionable heading into Friday’s practice report.

items.name: Alvin Kamara
items.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Saints’ veteran running back is just having his reps managed. With Audric Estime playing well and Travis Etienne (hamstring) potentially returning, Kamara does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats at this time. Kamara will continue to chip in on passing downs, though. Backup RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder) remains sidelined.

items.name: James Pearce
items.headline: James Pearce Jr. (back) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday DNP for the 23-year-old. Pearce Jr. will probably at least hit the questionable line on Friday and has a chance to be cleared off altogether if things trend in the right direction. Kevin Stefanski did not seem overly concerned about his status when asked about it, saying the Falcons “also want him to get healthy and feel good.”

items.name: Zachariah Branch
items.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: He was instantly ruled out ahead of Atlanta’s date in Madrid last Monday and has not practiced since. With the bye on tap in Week 11, we’d expect Branch to sit against the Chiefs.

items.name: Jaelan Phillips
items.headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Phillips practiced in full yesterday. Today, he was only limited. Hm. Today’s lightened workload could be a planned load management decision, but tomorrow’s practice participation will be worth watching for the Panthers’ top pass rusher. The Panthers’ stud LG Damien Lewis (knee) was also downgraded today, while starting perimeter CB Mike Jackson (groin) remained a full participant.

items.name: Carnell Tate
items.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) worked out with trainers on the side during Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: He did not elevate beyond an official DNP today, but this is an actual step after Tate missed four consecutive practices and Week 8 sandwiched around their Week 9 bye.
