Watson saw four of his seven receptions go for 20-plus yards, and found the end zone on a 39-yard touchdown in the third quarter, one play after the Packers’ defense forced a turnover. Watson has now gone for 100-plus yards in back-to-back weeks and has four games of 100-plus-yard performances on his resumé this season. He draws a tough Week 10 matchup against the Vikings and will be in the mix as a high-end WR2.

items.name: Quinshon Judkins
items.headline: Quinshon Judkins rushed 15 times for 43 yards in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints.
items.analysis: Judkins was hit at or behind the line of scrimmage constantly, resulting in a dreadful yards per carry of 2.9. This was particularly painful for fantasy managers when he got near the end zone. Judkins was stuffed from the one- and three-yard line on separate drives. He also ceded receiving work to Dylan Sampson. Judkins was targeted once while Sampson saw six opportunities through the air. Without receiving work to buoy his poor rushing days, Judkins is tumbling down the RB2 ranks. He’ll be on the RB2/3 border for his Week 10 matchup with the Texans.

items.name: Drew Lock
items.headline: Drew Lock completed 19-of-28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ 17-3, Week 9 win over the Cardinals, adding 16 yards on five carries.
items.analysis: Lock appeared to suffer discomfort in the third quarter following an incomplete pass attempt, holding his side or oblique and grimacing in pain as he made his way to sideline. He would get checked in the medical tent but returned without missing a down. Lock looked poised in the pocket and in control of the offense throughout, leaning on his alpha wide receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba early before the team went into preservation mode with a sizable lead in the second half. Lock could be looking at another start or two, pending the length of recovery from a cracked rib for Sam Darnold. The team passed an update on Lock’s oblique injury following the game, indicating that the veteran journeyman would undergo follow-on testing but that his status for Week 10 could be in doubt. He’ll be nothing more than a deep-league potential streamer against the Raiders, if active.

items.name: Drake Maye
items.headline: Drake Maye completed 21-of-38 passes for 299 yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions in the Patriots’ 45-27, Week 9 loss to the Packers.
items.analysis: Maye’s three first-half interceptions but the Patriots in the hole early, but the defenses’ inability to limit explosive plays also didn’t do them any favors. The Patriots saw three of their first six drives end in interceptions, but Maye did what he could to keep the game within reach. He completed his first touchdown pass of the day to Rhamondre Stevenson, who broke free down field for the 30-yard score in the second quarter. and on the following drive, Maye would complete passes of 19 and 28 yards to set up Efton Chism for an eight-yard touchdown with less than three minutes to go in the half. His third and final touchdown would come on a 22-yard pass to Mack Hollins, but Maye and the Patriots were under duress all afternoon and struggled to keep up with a Packers offense that didn’t slow down until it pulled it’s starters late in the fourth quarter. Maye also took four sacks in this one and has now been sacked nine times in his last three games. He’ll look to bounce back next week against the Lions in Munich.

items.name: Jordan Love
items.headline: Jordan Love completed 23-of-29 passes for 372 yards and three touchdowns in the Packers’ 45-27, Week 9 win over the Patriots.
items.analysis: As has been the case for much of the season, big plays were the name of the game for Love. Love aired the ball out at will against a helpless Patriots defense, going 6-for-9 on passes of 20-plus air yards for 235 yards and a touchdown. Love connected with Matthew Golden on multiple long plays in the first quarter, completing passes of 43 and 49 yards, and found him in the end zone for a five-yard score. Love’s longest touchdown pass of the day came in the third quarter when he connected with Christian Watson for a 39-yard-score immediately after the Packers recovered a fumble by Rhamondre Stevenson. Love and the Packers boast arguably the most explosive passing attack in the league, and both Watson and Golden continue to look like premier threats while also being versatile in other areas of the field. Love and the Vikings will have their work cut out for them next week at home against the Vikings, but he will remain in the QB1 mix.

items.name: Trey McBride
items.headline: Trey McBride caught 7-of-8 targets for 54 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 9 loss to the Seahawks.
items.analysis: The lone incompletion directed toward McBride came on the team’s final play of the game when the veteran tight end was unable to corral an end zone target that was thrown slightly behind him on fourth and goal. McBride combined with alpha wide receiver Michael Wilson to account for 15 targets on 30 Minshew pass attempts, something we’d expect to continue forward give the current state of the team. The Cardinals get another difficult matchup against the Rams in Week 10, where McBride will remain a surefire TE1 in fantasy circles.

items.name: Michael Wilson
items.headline: Michael Wilson caught 6-of-7 targets for 60 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 9 loss to the Seahawks.
items.analysis: The lone Gardner Minshew incompletion directed toward Wilson was an end zone target late in the fourth quarter, a miss that would have salvaged a usable fantasy outing for the veteran receiver. Wilson was responsible for nearly one third of the total offensive output from a Cardinals offense that was held to under 200 yards by the stingy Seattle defense, finishing second on the team in targets behind the eight of tight end Trey McBride. He remains an upside WR2 ahead of another difficult test against the Rams in Week 10.

items.name: Tyler Allgeier
items.headline: Tyler Allgeier rushed 17 times for 46 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 9 loss to the Seahawks, gaining zero additional yards on two receptions.
items.analysis: In what was the first game as the clear starter for the Cardinals in the absence of both Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight, Allgeier was contained to only 2.7 yards per carry as the offense managed under 200 yards of total offense against the stingy Seattle defense. Fantasy managers that were quick to scoop Allgeier off of waivers heading into Week 9 are surely to be disappointed with the returns, particularly considering Knight had largely outperformed the former prior to missing Week 9 with a concussion. Expect a near-even split backfield once Knight returns, which appears likely to be in Week 10 when the Cardinals face another difficult test in the Rams.

items.name: Gardner Minshew
items.headline: Gardner Minshew completed 21-of-30 passes for 166 yards in the Cardinals’ 17-3, Week 9 loss to the Seahawks, adding four yards on one carry.
items.analysis: To be fair, the matchup in Week 9 was far different than the one Minshew erupted in last week, with the Seattle defense placing the clamps on the Cardinals from the first kick, holding them to just 198 total yards of offense on the down night. The only points mustered came on the team’s first possession, with three of their five first half possessions resulting in three-and-outs. The Cardinals saw the football only thrice following the break, getting stopped after achieving first and goal from the four on their final possession of the game. It was an outing to forget for all parties. Minshew remains likely to be the starting quarterback, at least in the immediate future, but the looking presence of rookie Carson Beck could be accelerated if the former returns more games like this one. Up next for the Cardinals are the Rams in Week 10, where Minshew will be nothing more than a streamer in two-quarterback leagues.

items.name: Greg Dulcich
items.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 2-of-4 targets for 14 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Despite the quiet fantasy outing, Dulcich finished second on the team in catches and yards. If you couldn’t tell, it was not a productive day for Miami’s passing attack. Dulcich had stacked a few usable weeks over the past month, but Week 9 was his breakout spot against a dreadful Detroit defense. Having missed his big opportunity, he’ll return to the back of the TE2 ranks for Week 10 against the Colts.

items.name: Ashton Jeanty
items.headline: Ashton Jeanty had six rushes for 25 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers, adding five catches for -5 yards.
items.analysis: Jeanty and Mike Washington were scripted out in the second half, with the Raiders — as usual — falling behind by multiple scores. Jeanty was swallowed up by Niners defenders almost every time he caught the ball in the backfield. The plodding Jeanty couldn’t get anything going against a swarming 49ers defense. This was Jenaty’s sixth game of the season with at least four catches. It’s a role that has made him playable in 12-team leagues this season. Washington, meanwhile, had six carries for -3 yards. Jeanty might have some flex value in Week 10 against the Seahawks.

items.name: Eli Stowers
items.headline: Eli Stowers was held without a catch in the Eagles’ Week 9 loss to the Giants.
items.analysis: Stowers was targeted once. He’s now drawn five looks in three games since making his NFL debut in Week 7. With the Eagles now headed on bye, an adjustment upon their return could be more looks for their rookie seam man, especially/obviously if Dallas Goedert is traded ahead of Tuesday’s deadline. It is something to file away, but Stowers is still not a strong 12-team league stash ahead of the open date.

items.name: Tommy Tremble
items.headline: Tommy Tremble caught 4-of-6 targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos.
items.analysis: The Panthers liked something in their middle of the field matchups with the Broncos’ defense, targeting Tremble and Darren Waller 16 combined times. Both seam stretchers scored, with Tremble’s TD his first since Week 6. Tremble’s name has come up in the box score more than expected this year, but he has yet to have a 50-yard day and has three total touchdowns. He remains waiver-wire fodder in 12-team leagues.

items.name: Brock Bowers
items.headline: Brock Bowers caught 7-of-8 targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
items.analysis: Bowers led the Raiders in routes and tied Tre Tucker for the team lead with eight targets. Though Bowers had the ball punched out on a first half reception, he played well against a stingy San Francisco coverage unit that regularly shifted coverage his way. This marked the fifth time in 2026 Bowers has exceeded 80 receiving yards, and the sixth time he’s had at least six receptions in the game. It’s incredible production for a tight end — exactly what Bowers drafters expected when they took him in August drafts. He’ll take on the Seahawks in Week 10.

items.name: Darius Cooper
items.headline: Darius Cooper caught 2-of-8 targets for 25 yards in the Eagles’ Week 9 loss to the Giants.
items.analysis: One of Cooper’s missed connections in an inefficient performance was a drop on a potentially long score. So it goes when backup-level pass catchers are playing with No. 3 quarterbacks. Cooper has provided the Eagles with some desperately needed snaps and down-field ability, but there is extremely little chance his real life “value” translates to fantasy points in the second half of the season.

items.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
items.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) will not return in the Patriots’ Week 9 game against the Packers.
items.analysis: Stevenson suffered his knee injury late in the third quarter, but was eventually able to make it to the field under his own power. After spending a few moments in the blue medical tent, Stevenson went to the locker room and was ruled out soon after by the team. The 28-year-old back managed just 32 scoreless yards on six carries, but hauled in a 30-yard reception from Drake Maye in the second quarter, finishing the day with a 3-46-1 line on four targets. With TreVeyon Henderson (illness) sidelined with neurological concerns, the Patriots could be looking at using Corey Kiner as their top back entering Week 10 against the Lions.

items.name: Dallas Goedert
items.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 5-of-6 targets for 50 yards in the Eagles’ Week 9 loss to the Giants.
items.analysis: With No. 3 QB Joe Milton making his starting debut, Goedert padded the box score with some empty PPR production. Excellent, though there figures to be distressingly little difference between Goedert’s floor and ceiling for the time being. With the Eagles headed on bye for Week 10, how Goedert is valued upon the team’s return will depend on whether DeVonta Smith or Dontayvion Wicks finally get back in the lineup.

items.name: Brock Purdy
items.headline: Brock Purdy completed 17-of-25 attempts for 232 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders, adding seven rushes for 40 yards and a touchdown.
items.analysis: Purdy made quick work of a Raiders defense that has ranked as one of the NFL’s worst over the past month. The Niners tormented the Vegas defense with well-timed screens and quick hits to the middle of the field. Purdy used his legs in a couple high leverage situations in the first half and scored his second rushing touchdown of the season. He connected with Christian McCaffrey and Jordan Watkins for his throwing scores. The ultra-efficient Purdy will take on the generationally bad Dallas defense in Week 10.

items.name: Chris Bell
items.headline: Chris Bell failed to catch his only target in the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: With nine targets over his previous two games, Bell looked to be building some momentum headed into Week 9. Instead, he posted the dreaded goose egg. The good news is that Bell ran a route on 77 percent of Malik Willis’s dropbacks. He’s running as the team’s WR3, but there’s barely enough passing volume to keep the WR1 in the FLEX mix. Bell remains an interesting dynasty stash, but he is not on the redraft radar headed into Week 10.

items.name: Makai Lemon
items.headline: Makai Lemon caught 6-of-9 targets for 61 yards in the Eagles’ Week 9 loss to the Giants.
items.analysis: Lemon again led this limited offense in receiving as Joe Milton made his first start under center, but he hurt the cause with a handful of drops, including a particularly brutal one with the Eagles desperately trying to tie the game late. Lemon now has at least six catches in three straight games but has not reached 70 yards in the process. In other words, he is posting empty PPR volume. That will remain the “thesis of the play” when the Eagles come off bye in Week 11, though the return of either DeVonta Smith or Dontayvion Wicks would take a major bite out of Lemon’s WR3 appeal.

items.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
items.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (undisclosed) exited in the third quarter of Week 9’s game against the Patriots and went to the locker room.
items.analysis: Stevenson was slow to get up after a play late in the third quarter and was seen going to the locker room shortly after leaving the field. He spent some time in the blue medical tent, but the team has not disclosed what he is dealing with. Stevenson has rushed six times for 32 yards so far and has caught another three passes for 46 yards and a touchdown.

items.name: Malik Washington
items.headline: Malik Washington caught 2-of-3 targets for 21 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Washington wasn’t awfully involved in this game, even if you account for the Dolphins’ low-volume passing approach. He earned a 12 percent target share and added one carry for zero yards. Caleb Douglas, on the other hand, was the runaway WR1 for Miami. He earned eight targets and led the team with six grabs for 70 yards. Already completely out of the playoff race, the Dolphins are in evaluation mode with their young receiver corps. That could mean increasing workloads for Douglas, Chris Bell, and Kevin Coleman. Washington will get another week in the WR4 ranks, but he could be waiver wire fodder if he posts another quiet game against the Colts next week.

items.name: Courtland Sutton
items.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 5-of-9 targets for 45 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 9 win over the Panthers.
items.analysis: Even with Pat Bryant (ankle) returning, Sutton posted new season highs for receptions and targets as Jaylen Waddle departed early with a concussion. He did get out-gained by Bryant, who also found the end zone. Sutton is a perfectly fine role player, but it is the bitter truth that he is no longer a featured option. With Waddle now having the Broncos’ bye week to get healthy, Sutton could be returning as the team’s No. 3 option. He’s a borderline WR4/5 hold in leagues with shallower benches.

items.name: Pat Bryant
items.headline: Pat Bryant caught 4-of-5 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 9 win over the Panthers.
items.analysis: Active for the first time since Week 4, a returning Bryant (ankle) ended up leading the Broncos in receiving. Jaylen Waddle was forced to depart after only one target with a concussion. Bryant’s score, his second of the season, was a 26-yarder against broken coverage. Although his snaps were somewhat rationed following his month-long layoff, Bryant avoided setbacks and continues to look like a dark horse contender for No. 1 receiver duties in Denver. He’s a solid bench option heading into the Broncos’ Week 10 bye before their Week 11 return against the Raiders.

items.name: Ollie Gordon
items.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed 16 times for 55 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Gordon caught his only target for nine yards. Jaylen Wright was out this week. Kaytron Allen was active but entered the weekend with a quad injury. He saw one touch. Gordon earned another bell-cow workload but failed to do much with it for the second week in a row. Things should turn around for him when Miami takes on the equally down-bad Colts in Week 10. Gordon will remain in the RB2 mix despite the consecutive bust weeks.

items.name: Kyle Monangai
items.headline: Bears declared QB Case Keenum, CB Malik Muhammad, RB Kyle Monangai, LB Keyshaun Elliott and DT Jayden Loving inactive for Week 9 against the Buccaneers.
items.analysis: Monangai will miss one more week with the expectation being that the 24-year-old tailback will be good to go after the bye in Week 10. Keenum will be the emergency third quarterback.

items.name: Justin Herbert
items.headline: Justin Herbert entered the blue medical tent in Week 9 against the Texans after suffering an apparent left hand injury.
items.analysis: Herbert appeared to injure his left hand, and specifically his left middle finger, while fending off a pass rusher in the fourth quarter. He fractured the same hand, and seemingly the same digit, last year and underwent surgery to stabilize it in-season. We tentatively expect him to return after getting it taped up, but he will be playing hurt.

items.name: Jalen Coker
items.headline: Jalen Coker caught 4-of-5 targets for 29 yards in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos.
items.analysis: Coker is now really going through it over his past three games, managing just seven total catches for 74 yards and a touchdown. If there’s “good” news, it’s that it has been an offensive-wide slump in Carolina, not just Coker. He and everyone else has a premium Week 10 get-right spot in the Saints, though Coker is starting to look more like a WR3 than the WR2 he was showing out as earlier in the year.

items.name: Emeka Egbuka
items.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) is active for Week 9 against the Bears.
items.analysis: As expected, Egbuka is back after missing two games with his foot injury. The wideout has been heavily targeted when healthy, but hasn’t been particularly effective with those opportunities with zero games over 65 yards in 2026. The Bucs’ inactives for Week 9 will be OLB Yaya Diaby, G Trevor Keegan, G Billy Schrauth, CB Ayden Garnes and DL DeMonte Capehart.

items.name: Tetairoa McMillan
items.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 4-of-6 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos.
items.analysis: McMillan’s four-yard touchdown with the Panthers attempting to complete a fourth quarter comeback was his first since Week 4 and only his third of the season. He has also now been held below 60 yards receiving in three straight games as Bryce Young has been mired in a slump. If there’s good news, it’s that McMillan has maintained a decent floor, and we know the next spiked week can’t be far away. It could come as early as Week 10 against the Saints’ soft defense.

items.name: Malik Willis
items.headline: Malik Willis completed 13-of-25 passes for 128 yards and an interception in the Dolphins’ 19-9, Week 9 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Willis only added seven yards on two carries. He was on the injury report with a groin injury this week. Despite practicing in full three times, Willis appeared to be severely limited by the issue. He turned down several opportunities to scramble, instead opting to throw the ball away when the Lions’ pass-rush got close. Without the rushing production to bail him out of tough spots, the offense collapsed despite facing one of the league’s worst defenses. His passing output was already weak, but a lack of rush attempts will pull him out of the QB2 ranks entirely. He will be downgraded to a low-end QB2 for his Week 10 matchup with the Colts.

items.name: Malachi Fields
items.headline: Malachi Fields caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles.
items.analysis: Although this was a step back on Fields’ pre-bye performance of 4/83, it was actually only the second time all season he caught more than two passes. He continues to head in the right direction as J.J. McCarthy provides some upside hope for this offense. That being said, McCarthy’s (hip) status is questionable for Thursday against the Commanders, while Fields has still not proven his WR4 bonafides. He mostly remains an end-of-bench stash in conventional 12-team leagues.

items.name: Malik Nabers
items.headline: Malik Nabers caught 5-of-8 targets for 43 yards in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles.
items.analysis: Entering the game with four straight 100-yard performances, Nabers had a day of what ifs. Banged up early but no worse for the wear, Nabers played snaps with two different QBs as J.J. McCarthy missed part of the third quarter with a hip issue. McCarthy returned only for Nabers to drop a should-have-been 20-yard touchdown in the end zone. Frustrating, but 9.43 PPR points on a “down” day is not the worst outcome. Nabers and McCarthy have only four days to heal up for Thursdays short-week date with the Commanders, but Nabers’ status is not in doubt, while he will remain a high-end WR1 even if Jameis Winston returns under center for the G-Men.

items.name: Isaiah Likely
items.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 5-of-6 targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles.
items.analysis: Although it was another down day in the yardage department by his recent standards, Likely got the fantasy job done with his score and five receptions. It also wasn’t a bad outcome in a contest where J.J. McCarthy missed time with a hip injury and the Giants attempted only 27 throws vs. a reeling Eagles team. Likely’s touchdown was a five-yarder where he took advantage of mass defensive confusion at the goal line. It is unclear if McCarthy will be ready for Thursday’s short-week date with the Commanders, but Likely will remain a high-end QB1 even if Jameis Winston returns under center.

items.name: Jared Goff
items.headline: Jared Goff completed 17-of-25 passes for 170 yards and an interception in the Lions’ 19-9, Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: The Lions undoubtedly played down to their opponents in this game, putting up six points in the first half before finding slightly more success after the break. Things got off to a rocky start with an easy interception for Dolphins defensive back Chris Johnson. Goff was hit as he threw the ball and it wobbled right into Johnson’s arms. The Lions had one drive go for more than 50 yards. Jahmyr Gibbs punched in the score at the end of the drive, taking home the only Lions touchdown of the day. Goff should have no issues turning things around against the Patriots next week. He will remain near the top of the QB1 ranks for Week 10.

items.name: Emmett Johnson
items.headline: Emmett Johnson had six rushes for 34 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets.
items.analysis: Johnson, fresh off a big receiving day in Week 8 against the Broncos, didn’t see much involvement until the Chiefs were up multiple scores in the fourth quarter. He ran in his first NFL touchdown on a goal line carry after Ken Walker — who had three touchdowns on the day — was resting on the sideline. Johnson remains one of the game’s most important and upside backup running backs and should be rostered in every league in case Walker misses time.

items.name: Mason Taylor
items.headline: Mason Taylor caught 1-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Taylor ran a route on 22 of the team’s 39 drop backs while Kenyon Sadiq has 21 routes and caught all four of his targets. Splitting the TE1 role with Sadiq, Taylor won’t be fantasy viable in most formats next week against the Bills. He has four receptions over his past two games.

items.name: Sam LaPorta
items.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 4-of-5 targets for 32 yards in the Lions’ Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: LaPorta was the only Lion outside of Amon-Ra St. Brown to catch more than two passes. He accounted for a fifth of Jared Goff’s targets, but the team’s low-volume passing approach meant there wasn’t much volume to go around. LaPorta has gone cold in recent weeks with three straight games under 40 yards. He’ll look to get back on track as a mid-range TE1 versus the Patriots next week.

items.name: Kenyon Sadiq
items.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Sadiq logged 21 pass routes on the day to Mason Taylor’s 22 routes. The two tight ends have largely split the TE1 role in the New York offense in recent weeks. Taylor had just one catch on two targets against Kansas City, while Sadiq got open down the seam a couple times and found himself wide open for Geno Smith. Sadiq, who had five receptions over his previous four outings, won’t be usable in most fantasy formats next week against the Bills.

items.name: Saquon Barkley
items.headline: Saquon Barkley rushed 13 times for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 9 loss to the Giants.
items.analysis: It was a horribly inefficient day for the Eagles’ superstar back, but there was not a whole lot he could do with the Giants understandably not respecting the “threat” presented by No. 3 Philly quarterback Joe Milton. Barkley at least saved face with his three-yard scoring plunge in the first quarter. Having his snaps and touches rationed for this injury-ruined and tanking team, Barkley will probably have a hard time getting back into the RB1 ranks when Philly comes off bye in Week 11 against the Steelers.

items.name: Xavier Worthy
items.headline: Xavier Worthy sustained a hamstring injury in Week 9 against the Jets.
items.analysis: Worthy hobbled off the field after a fourth quarter reception in the KC victory. It appeared to be the serious kind of hamstring injury but we won’t know the extent of it until the team tests the speedy receiver. Worthy had caught all six of his targets for 48 yards before exiting the game. An absence of Worthy would likely free up more targets for Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice. The team’s running backs could also see an uptick in targets if Worthy misses time.

items.name: Jameson Williams
items.headline: Jameson Williams caught 1-of-2 targets for 31 yards in the Lions’ Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: We’re not sure if a player can be due for a catastrophic bust of a fantasy week, but “Jamo” was probably due for a catastrophic bust. He came into this game red hot, with 208 yards and five touchdowns over his past three games. Given Williams boom/bust nature, a flop was always right around the corner. He also dropped one of his two targets, which didn’t help his cause. The Lions get a potential shootout with the Patriots next week, meaning fantasy managers can safely keep Williams in their lineups as a WR3 despite today’s quiet outing.

items.name: Chuba Hubbard
items.headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed 16 times for 79 yards in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos, adding four receptions for 17 yards.
items.analysis: Hubbard’s 16 totes were his second fewest since Week 2, though fantasy managers will at least take the 96 yards from scrimmage. Handling huge workloads and snap counts, Hubbard hasn’t always maintained his efficiency under such voluminous usage, though we have yet to see any red flags in 2026. He will remain a strong option on the RB1/2 borderline for Week 10 against the Saints.

items.name: J.K. Dobbins
items.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed four times for 18 yards in the Broncos’ Week 9 win over the Panthers, adding a four-yard reception.
items.analysis: Dobbins operated as a pure breather back for this one, getting out-touched 21-5 by Jonah Coleman and out-snapped 58-11. Dobbins did receive two touches inside the Panthers’ 20-yard line — one of which was nullified by penalty — but none inside the 10. It sure looks as if the Broncos are ready to ride rookie Coleman, making Dobbins a shaky 12-team league hold since the Broncos are now headed on bye. They return in Week 11 against the Raiders. The odds are strong Dobbins will not be in your starting lineup for that one.

items.name: Jonah Coleman
items.headline: Jonah Coleman rushed 17 times for 57 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 9 win over the Panthers, adding four receptions for 31 yards.
items.analysis: Coleman also put the ball on the ground near his own goal line on a Bo Nix pitch, but the Broncos were thankfully able to recover. Also thankfully for fantasy managers, coach Sean Payton continued to look Coleman’s way late after the miscue, including the very next play. Coleman experienced really strong usage in Charlotte, playing 58-of-75 snaps per PFF’s initial count while easily setting a new career high with his 21 touches. He has also now cleared 80 yards from scrimmage in back-to-back contests. It must be noted that today’s score was not a goal-line carry — it came from nine yards out — but he did receive a first quarter carry from the Panthers’ four-yard line. Coleman’s role continues to grow, thus far without setback. Hopefully that does not change when the Broncos come off bye in Week 11 against the Raiders’ soft defense. We will be ranking Coleman as a strong RB2 for that one.

items.name: Gregory Desrosiers
items.headline: Greg Desrosiers rushed three times for 20 yards in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles.
items.analysis: The Giants’ “No. 2 running back” with Cam Skattebo (hamstring) on the shelf, Desrosiers was charted as playing only five snaps, but his 20 yards on three touches were just 19 fewer than Devin Singletary generated on 23 handles. Translation, if Skattebo can’t go for Thursday evening’s short-week date with the Commanders, UDFA Desrosiers might be in line for more work following Singletary’s stink bomb against the Eagles. That’s a 14-team league waivers dart calling your name.

items.name: Ashton Dulin
items.headline: Ashton Dulin caught 1-of-2 targets for 55 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Dulin’s lone reception went for a 55-yard touchdown on a simple screen late in the third quarter to bring the Colts within three, but it likely came with the veteran journeyman sitting on waiver wires. Dulin is a name to keep an eye on ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline as his role could be growing, pending what the team does with Josh Downs.

items.name: Josh Downs
items.headline: Josh Downs caught 3-of-6 targets for 24 yards in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Downs saw numerous snaps in coverage by his younger brother, Caleb Downs, and was unable to return a usable fantasy outing for the seventh time in nine appearances for the Colts this season. The subject of significant trade speculation ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, Downs appears likely to be headed for a change of scenery in a contract year, with the Colts reportedly already holding an offer in hand. More to come from one of fantasy’s most disappointing mid-round selections.

items.name: Devin Singletary
items.headline: Devin Singletary rushed 21 times for 31 yards in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles, adding two receptions for eight yards.
items.analysis: Charted by Pro Football Focus as playing 62-of-67 snaps with Cam Skattebo (hamstring) on the shelf, Singletary was an every-down player, but a predictably ineffective one. In fact, his performance was just the third time this decade a player generated fewer than 40 yards from scrimmage on 20-plus touches. The 29-year-old lost what little remained of his explosiveness several years ago, and should never end up in a position where he is “forced” to be an every-down back. With Skattebo supposedly “pushing to play” this afternoon, hopefully he will be ready for Thursday evening’s short-week date with the Commanders. If not, Singletary will be a low-upside FLEX who might cede more snaps and touches to rookie UDFA Greg Desrosiers.

items.name: Puka Nacua
items.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Puka Nacua (knee) will undergo an MRI on Monday.
items.analysis: Rams fans and fantasy managers will be holding their collective breath as they await the results of tomorrow’s MRI. According to Garafolo, Nacua suffered a knee injury on the Rams’ final offensive snap of the game when he took a rush attempt for five yards before the Rams punted the ball away. Nacua took a low hit from Commanders safety Jeremy Reaves, but didn’t appear to suffer a serious injury in real time. Garafolo reports, “the team does not believe [Nacua] suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging Monday will tell more.” It goes without saying that the Rams can ill-afford to lose another receiver, especially one of Nacua’s caliber. We will be sure to check back in with any updates on his injury as they come.

items.name: Geno Smith
items.headline: Geno Smith completed 18-of-32 attempts for 162 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs, adding one rush for eight yards.
items.analysis: The 36-year-old Smith was as immobile as ever, taking five sacks on the day and narrowly avoiding a half dozen others. Some of that was the Jets offensive line being overwhelmed against an elite KC pass rush; some of it was Smith refusing to get rid of the ball as the pocket collapsed. Smith playing without Garrett Wilson (concussion) was irate on the sideline in the fourth quarter with the Jets down multiple scores, barking at coaches and teammates alike. He had a negative EPA per drop back on the day. Smith should be seen as a matchup-dependent fantasy play. He will be streamable in Week 10 against a vulnerable Buffalo secondary.

items.name: Keenan Allen
items.headline: Keenan Allen caught 4-of-8 targets for 26 yards in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Allen wasn’t targeted until late in the second quarter but picked up two receptions on back-to-back plays to tease fantasy managers in an otherwise poor outing. Things can’t get much worse in Indianapolis, with their decisions in the coming days ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline potentially allowing Allen to step into a more featured role in the second half of the season. Stay tuned as the Colts limp into a Week 10 matchup against the Dolphins.

items.name: KC Concepcion
items.headline: KC Concepcion caught 4-of-6 targets for 85 yards and a touchdown in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints.
items.analysis: Concepcion’s day appeared to be over late in the third quarter when he limped off the field with a non-contact injury. Concepcion was unable to put any weight on his leg and needed to be helped off the field by trainers. He was then on the field to return a punt ahead of Cleveland’s next drive. The rookie made it stunningly clear that he was fine in the fourth quarter with a 64-yard receiving touchdown. Sanders hit him for a long gain and Concepcion outran two Saints defenders for his first career touchdown. With 221 receiving yards over his past three games, Concepcion is heating up just in time for the fantasy playoff hunt. He will be in the WR3 mix versus the Texans next week.

items.name: Tyler Warren
items.headline: Tyler Warren caught 4-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Warren wasn’t targeted in the first half as the team struggled to move the football consistently, catching his first ball on the team’s second possession of the third quarter. The Colts limp toward Tuesday’s trade deadline with numerous key players the subject of trade speculation, of which quarterback Daniel Jones, wide receiver Josh Downs, and running back Jonathan Taylor are amongst. Which is to say, Warren’s fantasy expectations could be heavily influenced by the team’s actions in the coming days, potentially setting the second-year tight end up to be the team’s top option during the second half of the season. Warren would appear to be in a solid spot on paper against the Dolphins in Week 10, where his fantasy value will be dependent on who remains with the team through Tuesday.

items.name: Braelon Allen
items.headline: Braelon Allen had eight rushes for 23 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs, adding two catches for 21 yards.
items.analysis: Breece Hall, returning from his quad injury, led the New York backfield with 15 carries while adding three grabs out of the backfield. It was Allen, however, who led the Jets backfield in pass routes, 21 to 10. That sort of pass game usage could keep Allen viable in deeper formats since the Jets are going to be chasing points more weeks than not. Both Jets running backs average 4.1 yards per carry against an elite KC front seven. Allen plays the Bills in Week 10.

items.name: Stefon Diggs
items.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 3-of-5 targets for 51 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams.
items.analysis: With the Commanders down three receivers, Diggs appeared prime for a decent day against a Rams secondary that was down two corners. Instead, the 32-year-old receiver was outshone by journeyman Van Jefferson for most of the day until the final drive of the game. With the Commanders looking to mount a game-tying drive, Diggs broke free into the secondary to make a 42-yard reception, which accounted for nearly all of his receiving production. In two games without Terry McLaurin, Diggs has averaged just 5.5 targets per game and totaled 89 yards and a touchdown. He’s far from the target hog he was in his prime, and shouldn’t be treated as anything more than a WR3/WR4 on Thursday night against the Giants.

items.name: Seth McGowan
items.headline: Seth McGowan rushed six times for 45 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, losing three yards on one reception.
items.analysis: McGowan came on in relief of Jonathan Taylor on third-and-goal from the two late in the first quarter, cashing in on the opportunity for his first touchdown this season. a 36-yard scamper in the fourth quarter pushed his yards per carry mark to a healthy 7.5, dwarfing the 3.5 of Taylor. McGowan should not be on waiver wires ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, with the looming possibility that Taylor has played his final snap for the Colts.

items.name: Antonio Williams
items.headline: Antonio Williams caught 3-of-6 targets for 25 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams.
items.analysis: Fantasy managers hoping for a breakout performance from Williams, with Terry McLaurin (knee), Treylon Burks (foot), and Dyami Brown (calf) all sidelined, will be left wanting more. Instead, veteran journeyman Van Jefferson stepped up, catching five passes for 58 yards and a touchdown on a team-high seven targets, while Williams was largely an afterthought. Of the six targets Williams saw on Sunday, three came in the fourth quarter with the Commanders trailing 20-13. The rookie has caught 8-of-13 targets for 79 scoreless yards over the last two weeks and will be hard to trust as anything more than a WR3/WR4 in Week 10 against the Giants.

items.name: Bo Nix
items.headline: Bo Nix completed 25-of-37 passes for 237 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in the Broncos’ 26-21, Week 9 win over the Panthers.
items.analysis: Today was only Nix’s third multi-score start of the season through the air, though it was also his second in as many weeks. It came as No. 1 wideout Jaylen Waddle left with a first half concussion. Nix’s touchdowns were a three-yard precision dart to Courtland Sutton and 31-yard busted coverage strike to a returning Pat Bryant. He also extended a few key plays with his scrambling ability, most notably avoiding a massive third down sack on the Broncos’ opening drive. It was not a perfect day, but Nix has inarguably been playing better since his dismal Thursday Night Football outing three weeks ago. Now he must wait and see on Waddle’s Week 10 status against the Raiders’ awful defense, but Bryant’s healthy return could be a massive development. Nix will be a solid QB2 streamer next Sunday.

items.name: Rachaad White
items.headline: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 28 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams, adding two receptions for 41 additional yards.
items.analysis: White’s 28 rushing yards led all Commanders running backs, but his biggest play of the game came through the air. In the second quarter, White turned a short screen pass upfield for a 45-yard gain, positioning the Commanders for a touchdown, which came on the following play when Van Jefferson found the end zone for a seven-yard score. White’s only other catch went for a four-yard loss, but the 41 receiving yards still set a new season-high for him. The 27-year-old free agent signee has three touchdowns this season and hasn’t totaled more than 80 yards from scrimmage in any game this season. He will be a fringe RB2/RB3 against the Giants, with Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) still sidelined for a few more weeks.

items.name: Jonathan Taylor
items.headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed 13 times for 46 yards in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, adding 18 yards on five receptions.
items.analysis: Taylor also lost a key fumble in the fourth quarter following the team’s second takeaway of the game, leaving fantasy managers wanting more in what could have been his final game in Indianapolis. Taylor has been the subject of significant trade speculation and rumor as we head toward Tuesday’s trade deadline, although teams will need to take on his recently-signed contract extension that ties him to the Colts through the 2028 season. Things started off rough as Taylor was subbed out on third-and-goal from the two, watching from the sideline as Seth McGowan punched it in for the team’s only rushing score of the game. It did not get better from their for Taylor’s fantasy managers as the Colts played through consistently negative game script, limiting his volume in the process. Taylor’s next opponent remains uncertain, although he currently lines up to take on the reeling Dolphins in Week 10, at least as long as he remains with the Colts.

items.name: Kyren Williams
items.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 15 times for 45 yards in the Rams’ Week 9 win over the Commanders, adding three receptions for 16 additional yards.

items.name: Bryce Young
items.headline: Bryce Young completed 28-of-39 passes for 276 yards, three touchdowns and an interception in the Panthers’ 26-21, Week 9 loss to the Broncos, also losing a fumble.
items.analysis: Young’s three-score start was his first since Week 2, though the two turnovers really put a damper on things. Young’s fourth quarter fumble short-circuited a potential game-winning drive, while his interception came in the end zone. Now, it was one of the more unlucky plays we have ever seen in the NFL — a ball seemingly everyone thought bounced off the ground actually bounced off a player into Devon Key’s arms — but Young put too much on the negative side of the ledger for the Panthers to pull this one out. They’ve now lost three straight games to fall to 3-5 on the season. Young at least snapped a streak of three straight starts with a sub-60 completion percentage. He also converted a late 4th-and-18 with an amazing throw. Young remains a frustrating option on the QB1/2 borderline heading into a golden Week 10 matchup with the Saints.

items.name: Omar Cooper
items.headline: Omar Cooper, Jr. caught 8-of-11 targets for 58 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Cooper, fresh off a Week 8 zero, led the Jets in all receiving categories with Garrett Wilson (concussion) sidelined for this one. Operating primarily from the slot, Cooper got open on a few first half dump offs and gained decent yardage after the catch. Adonai Mitchell, meanwhile, was held without a catch on seven targets. As long as he’s running a decent route rate, Cooper should be flex worthy in most formats. He’ll face the pass-funnel Buffalo defense in Week 10.

items.name: Daniel Jones
items.headline: Daniel Jones completed 20-of-34 passes for 180 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Colts’ 27-23, Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, adding 11 yards on three carries.
items.analysis: The final score would have been much more lopsided if not for 14 accepted penalties from an undisciplined Cowboys team, something that allowed the Colts to surge back in the second half and take the lead with under two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. The efforts would prove fruitless as they immediately let Dak Prescott connect with Ryan Flournoy on a 46-yard gain on the first play of the following possession, resulting in a Javonte Williams touchdown. A Jones pick on the next possession sealed the game and sent the Colts to a 2-7 record ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, with questions abound regarding the future of the franchise. Jones has been a name linked to numerous teams this week, the most of which is the Vikings following the hamstring injury sustained by Kyler Murray. More to come as the Colts enter a tear-it-down rebuild.

items.name: Rashee Rice
items.headline: Rashee Rice caught 5-of-7 targets for 49 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets.
items.analysis: Rice, as usual, led the Chiefs in targets. It was an unusually run-heavy game plan for the Chiefs against a Jets defense that showed no real interest in stopping Ken Walker. This performance comes off last week’s 56-yard, one-touchdown outing for Rice, who missed significant time with a hamstring injury. Rice profiles as a high-floor WR2/3 in most formats. He’ll face the run-funnel Falcons defense in Week 10.

items.name: Joe Milton
items.headline: Joe Milton completed 18-of-34 passes for 169 yards in the Eagles’ 19-11, Week 9 loss to the Giants, adding nine carries for 64 yards.
items.analysis: Making the first official regular season start of his career, third-year pro Milton also took a whopping seven sacks for 41 yards and a lost fumble. He never felt Arvell Reese’s pressure when he was obliterated in the second quarter and put the ball on the ground. It was, unsurprisingly, a somewhat ugly day, though Milton was also victimized by drops, including a really awful muff late in the fourth quarter by Makai Lemon. Elijah Mitchell also scrambled a potential game-scoring drive when he failed to get out of bounds to stop the clock. All in all, today would not be surprising to anyone familiar with Milton’s game. He flashed arm strength, running ability, and highly questionable game management skills. Now headed on bye before a Week 11 date against the Steelers, Milton is not a must hold in superflex leagues where other QBs actually find themselves on the wire.

items.name: Harold Fannin
items.headline: Harold Fannin caught both of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints.
items.analysis: Fannin didn’t even have a target, let alone a catch, headed into overtime. He then nearly won the game on his own with a 39-yard touchdown grab. Fannin caught a short check-down from Shedeur Sanders and stiff-armed not one, but two defenders en route to the end zone. Fannin’s target total was more than concerning, but it came in Sanders’ first and likely only start of the year. Fantasy managers shouldn’t read into it too much. With Watson returning next week against the Texans, Fannin will remain a mid-range TE1 in Week 10.

items.name: Brevyn Spann-Ford
items.headline: Brevyn Spann-Ford caught 2-of-3 targets for 20 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 9 win over the Colts.
items.analysis: Spann-Ford played much of the game in the absence of Jake Ferguson, the latter of whom departed with a scary looking knee injury in the third quarter, and still managed only three targets in a game that saw alpha wide receiver CeeDee Lamb amass 16 targets on 34 Dak Prescott pass attempts. The secondary options in this offense are not worthy of weekly fantasy considering, of which Spann-Ford is one. He is not a streaming option ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the 49ers.

items.name: Ryan Flournoy
items.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 2-of-3 targets for 53 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 9 win over the Colts.
items.analysis: Flournoy had just one catch for seven yards until the final drive of the game, where he caught a 46-yard pass on the first play of the drive to instantly place the Cowboys into the red zone while trailing by three points. A Javonte Williams touchdown and Caleb Downs interception on the subsequent possession would be enough to send the Cowboys to 4-5 with a win. Fantasy managers must be left disappointed with the outing considering George Pickens was unable to go with a hamstring injury. Flournoy will be a shaky FLEX option in Week 10 against the 49ers, regardless of the status of Pickens.

items.name: Josh Jacobs
items.headline: Josh Jacobs (hand) is questionable to return in Week 9 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: This news comes from the official team account. It was hard to tell when Jacobs suffered the injury, but star running back could be seen jogging to the locker room with trainers late in the first quarter. Jacobs leaves the game with five rushing yards on four carries and will be replaced by Pierre Strong with MarShawn Lloyd (knee) being inactive.

items.name: J.J. McCarthy
items.headline: J.J. McCarthy completed 12-of-19 passes for 127 yards in the Giants’ 19-11, Week 9 win over the Eagles, adding four carries for 22 yards.
items.analysis: Taking a beating before his third quarter hip injury, McCarthy had a much more “Minnesota day” against the Eagles, with the huge exception he again avoided turnovers. Although McCarthy’s third down decision-making was leaving a little something to be desired, his ability to avoid the big mistake was paramount in a contest where the G-Men simply had to outlast a team starting its No. 3 quarterback. He did that, finding Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely for a handful of down-field completions along the way. That does not included a dropped 20-yard touchdown from Nabers. This was McCarthy’s “worst” showing in three appearances as a Giant, but it was still promising on the whole. Now McCarthy needs to find out how sore he is going to be on Monday after really taking a walloping. He could end up highly questionable for Thursday’s short-week date with the Commanders. Stay tuned.

items.name: CeeDee Lamb
items.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 10-of-16 targets for 195 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 9 win over the Colts.
items.analysis: Lamb’s day was inches from being one of the top fantasy outings for any player this season, with the talented veteran unable to get his second foot down in the end zone in the third quarter, forcing the Cowboys to settle for a field goal. Even so, Lamb has now seen double-digit targets in each of his previous four games and five of his last six, averaging 13.8 targets per game in that span. His production in Week 9 also marked the third time this season in which Lamb has gone for more than 150 yards, handily leading the league in targets while trailing only Jaxon Smith-Njigba in yardage. Lamb and the Cowboys get a more difficult matchup against the 49ers in Week 10, where Lamb will remain an elite WR1 at home.

items.name: Shedeur Sanders
items.headline: Shedeur Sanders completed 19-of-31 passes for 297 yards and two touchdowns in the Browns’ 23-22, Week 9 overtime loss to the Saints.
items.analysis: Sanders added 10 carries for 28 yards. He struggled to get much of anything going for three quarters before finding the big one in the fourth. Sanders threw a bomb to KC Concepcion, who tracked the ball well and then outran two defenders for a 64-yard score. Sanders’ second touchdown came in overtime on a grown-man catch-and-run from Harold Fannin. Cleveland opted for a two-point conversion to go for the win, but Sanders couldn’t connect with Denzel Boston after being flushed out of the pocket. It took a while, but Sanders at least looked like a viable backup in this contest, which wasn’t the case at any point last year. He’ll return to his QB2 gig in Week 10, keeping him off the fantasy radar for now.

items.name: Javonte Williams
items.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 20 times for 101 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 9 win over the Colts, adding 23 yards on four receptions.
items.analysis: Williams notched his second 100-yard game of the season, tacking on a fourth quarter score with less than two minutes remaining to push his fantasy production into RB1 territory. Week 9 also marks the third straight week in which the Cowboys utilized a new-look, run-heavy game plan, this time utilizing Tyler Goodson to soak up carries behind Williams. Williams has now seen 20 or more carries in three straight and will remain a volume-based RB1 in a difficult matchup against the 49ers at home in Week 10.

items.name: Dak Prescott
items.headline: Dak Prescott completed 21-of-34 passes for 335 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys’ 27-23, Week 9 win over the Colts, adding one yard on two carries.
items.analysis: The two teams played to a maddening field position battle through the first three quarters in what was one of the least disciplined games in recent memory, including a multitude of penalties on key downs, two turnovers, and a missed field goal from the Cowboys. A poor fourth quarter saw the Colts snatch the lead with a late field goal, but a 46-yard deep connection with Ryan Flournoy on the the play of the subsequent possession allowed the Cowboys to take the lead with just over a minute remaining in the fourth quarter. A Caleb Down interception ended the game, allowing Prescott and the Cowboys to escape with a win to send them to 4-5 as they chase the Giants in the NFC East. Up next is a home test against the 49ers in Week 10, where Prescott will remain a back end QB1.

items.name: Caleb Douglas
items.headline: Caleb Douglas caught 6-of-8 targets for 70 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Douglas made several big plays, including a highlight-reel grab in the first quarter that saw him high-point the ball for a 20-yard gain. He also had his fair share of rookie blunders. Douglas dropped a pass on fourth down late in the fourth quarter. Detroit was able to run out the clock after getting the ball back. Douglas was also the intended target on Malik Willis’s lone interception of the day. Willis told reporters after the game that it was the result of a miscommunication between the two. The good news for Douglas is that the Dolphins are in development mode. Growing pains are part of the process and Douglas’s errors shouldn’t cost him playing time going forward. He will be in the WR3 mix when Miami takes on the Colts.

items.name: Travis Kelce
items.headline: Travis Kelce caught 4-of-6 targets for 72 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets, adding a rush for one yard and a touchdown.
items.analysis: Kelce scored on a goal line tush push in the first half. It was a nice little treat for fantasy managers starting the old guy in Week 9. Kelce was second among KC pass catchers in targets, trailing Rashee Rice, who saw seven targets on the day. Kelce remains a reliable floor option in PPR formats. He’s had at least four receptions in five games this season, though his after the catch production has (predictably) cratered. Kelce should be in 12-team league lineups against the Falcons.

items.name: Breece Hall
items.headline: Breece Hall had 15 rushes for 61 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs, adding three catches for 26 yards.
items.analysis: Finally returning from his multi-month quad injury, Hall took over as the Jets’ lead back even after Braelon Allen had a nice run as the team’s RB1. Allen ended up with 10 touches on the day, including eight carries. Hall looked spry, dodging would-be tacklers and creating yards after first contact on a handful of his touches. It seems Jets coaches were serious when they said Hall would resume lead back duties upon his return. Hall’s role in the Jets offense should make him a locked-in top-24 option, including next week against the Bills.

items.name: Ladd McConkey
items.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Chargers.
items.analysis: Immediately after the Chargers’ second play from scrimmage, the broadcast booth announced that McConkey experienced back spasms during pre-game warmups, describing the announcement as a “developing” story. It is unclear why this wasn’t announced pre-game, but here we are. Hopefully, McConkey can take the field at some point, but he could end up missing the contest. Stay tuned.

items.name: Kenneth Walker
items.headline: Ken Walker had 18 rushes for 102 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets, adding four catches for 41 yards and two touchdowns.
items.analysis: Walker sliced through a low-energy Jets defense time and again in the first half. He was more involved than usual in the pass game, taking over as KC’s primary pass catcher out of the backfield after Emmett Johnson’s big PPR performance in Week 8 against Denver. Walker would have likely had a bigger day if the Chiefs hadn’t benched their starters in the fourth quarter, up my multiple scores. This was Walker’s third multi-touchdown performance of the 2026 season, and it marks the fourth time this season he’s had at least four receptions in a game. Walker will remain a high-end fantasy play in Week 10 against the Falcons.

items.name: Blake Corum
items.headline: Blake Corum rushed 11 times for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 9 win over the Commanders.

items.name: Van Jefferson
items.headline: Van Jefferson caught 5-of-7 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams.

items.name: Puka Nacua
items.headline: Puka Nacua caught 14-of-19 targets for 150 yards and one touchdown in the Rams’ Week 9 win over the Commanders.
items.analysis: Nacua was targeted early and often by Matthew Stafford in this one. He caught three-of-four targets for 29 yards on the Rams’ first offensive drive and entered halftime with a 9-86-0 line on 11 targets. Coming out of the half, Nacua immediately caught back-to-back passes of 12 and 15 yards on a drive that ended with a Blake Corum touchdown run, and in the fourth quarter he made an impressive leaping grab for a seven-yard score to put the Rams up 20-13. Nacua has now scored in each of his last three games and has topped 100 yards three times this season. He’s the only reliable target in the Rams’ passing game and will, as usual, profile as a high-end WR1 next week against the Cardinals.

items.name: Jayden Daniels
items.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 24-of-35 passes for 273 yards and one touchdown in the Commanders’ 20-13, Week 9 loss to the Rams, adding four runs for 16 additional yards.
items.analysis: Daniels played mostly mistake-free football in this one, but a lost fumble on a strip-sack by Myles Garrett near the end of the first half proved costly as the Commanders had a chance to add to their 10-3 lead before halftime. His lone touchdown pass of the day came on a seven-yard pass to Van Jefferson, who surprisingly ended up leading the Commanders with 58 receiving yards on the day, but Daniels and the offense struggled to generate much offense in the second half against a defensive front that featured both Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett together for the first time. Daniels saw 115 of his passing yards come on his final two drives of the game as he attempted to mount a comeback, but some off-target throws and two sacks on the game’s final drive all but buried any hopes of a comeback. Daniels’ disappointing showing on the ground marks the third straight week in which he has rushed for 23 or fewer yards, and he has managed only 10 rush attempts over that stretch. Now sitting at 2-5-1 on the season, Daniels and the Commanders will look to turn things around on a short week as they prepare to face the Giants on Thursday Night Football. He profiles more as a low-end QB1 until he begins to add more value in the rushing game.

items.name: Matthew Stafford
items.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 26-of-43 passes for 228 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Rams’ 20-13, Week 9 win over the Commanders.
items.analysis: It was an uneven day for Stafford and the Rams, who managed just six points in the first half of this one. Stafford threw 19 of his 43 targets to Puka Nacua, who was unsurprisingly his most reliable receiver of the day, as the two connected 14 times for 150 yards and a touchdown. Stafford’s lone touchdown pass of the day came on a seven-yard pass to Nacua in the back of the end zone, which gave the Rams a 20-13 lead early in the fourth quarter. This marks back-to-back pedestrian outings for Stafford, who has thrown for 385 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions in his last two games. Stafford will be a fringe QB1/QB2 next week on the road against the Cardinals.

items.name: Adonai Mitchell
items.headline: Adonai Mitchell didn’t catch any of his seven targets in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs.
items.analysis: A week after going ballistic against the Raiders, the high-variance Mitchell couldn’t come up with a grab in an embarrassing effort for a Jets offense that was without Garrett Wilson (concussion). If your fantasy league awards points for air yards, Mitchell would have been a week winner against Kansas City. Alas, he could not convert any of that opportunity into real-life production, though he came awfully close on a couple well-thrown Geno Smith downfield balls. He was second on the team in targets, trailing Omar Cooper (11). Mitchell next week against the Bills will remain a boom-bust WR3 option. Buffalo has struggled against boundary receivers all season.

items.name: Patrick Mahomes
items.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 23-of-41 attempts for 242 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets, adding two rushes for eight yards.
items.analysis: Mahomes was pulled with a few minutes to go in the fourth quarter with the Chiefs up multiple scores and the Jets not all that interested in staging a comeback. Mahomes overcame an injury to his right forearm in this one. He sustained the injury on a hard hit from a blitzing New York defender who bent Mahomes’ arm back awkwardly. After getting some treatment on the sideline, Mahomes re-entered the game and seemed fine, though he was seen grimacing and shaking his arm at times. This marked Mahomes’ sixth multi-touchdown game of the season. He should remain in starting lineups as a top-12 option in Week 10 against the pass-funnel Atlanta defense.

items.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
items.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 20 times for 74 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: This was easily Gibbs’ worst fantasy outing of the year, though that largely speaks to just how incredible he has been in 2026. The big difference today was a lack of receiving usage. Gibbs was only targeted once and failed to catch a pass for the first time since Week 4 of the 2024 season. Jared Goff only attempted 25 passes, but that would still result in more than one target for Gibbs on a normal day. We’re willing to write this off as the product of a low-scoring rock fight with the Dolphins. Gibbs will be back at the top of the RB1 ranks for his Week 10 date game against the Patriots.

items.name: Thomas Booker
items.headline: Raiders declared DT Thomas Booker, WR Malik Benson, WR Dont’e Thornton, G Bryce Cabeldue, SAF Dalton Johnson, and QB Aidan O’Connell inactive for Week 9 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: The struggling Vegas defense will be without Booker against the ultra-efficient 49ers offense. The Raiders since Week 4 has allowed the NFL’s third highest EPA per rush and the fifth highest rushing success rate. That should be good news for both Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black.

items.name: Jake Ferguson
items.headline: Jake Ferguson (knee) is questionable to return to Week 9 against the Colts.
items.analysis: The term “questionable” is a vast understatement based on the replay, although the veteran tight end did walk off the field under his own power. The replay and initial reaction from Ferguson did not look good. Expect an update from the team following the game. Ferguson caught both targets for 21 yards and a touchdown prior to departing.

items.name: J.J. McCarthy
items.headline: J.J. McCarthy (hip, questionable) returned before the end of the third quarter in the Giants’ Week 9 game against the Eagles.
items.analysis: McCarthy, who presumably received some sort of pain-killing injection after twice collapsing in the third quarter, returned for the final play of the frame. He screamed at his offensive linemen to pump them up before doing so. Never a dull moment.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: 49ers declared WR Mike Evans, WR Deebo Samuel, QB Kurtis Rourke, OT Enrique Cruz, LB Tatum, Bethune, and DL Khalid Kareem inactive for Week 9 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Evans will miss at least one game with his lingering Achilles injury. Look for the Niners to be careful with their WR1 in the coming weeks. Demarcus Robinson, coming off an injury, will return to the lineup against Vegas and likely operate as the Niners’ top wideout. Robinson will be flex-viable against a porous Vegas secondary.

items.name: J.J. McCarthy
items.headline: J.J. McCarthy suffered a hip injury in the Giants’ Week 9 game against the Eagles and is questionable to return.
items.analysis: Jameis Winston, of course, is now in the game. McCarthy took a thunderclap third quarter hit from Eagles LB Zack Baun and struggled to his feet. He attempted to warm back up on the sideline before literally collapsing while trying to throw. He then headed to the blue tent before making his way to the locker room. We suppose he is genuinely questionable, but on the wrong side of the tag. McCarthy had been taking an absolute beating before going down, absorbing five sacks, many of which were of the spine-rattling variety.

items.name: Riley Moss
items.headline: Broncos CB Riley Moss suffered a concussion in Denver’s Week 9 game against the Panthers and will not return.
items.analysis: Attempting to help out in run defense, Moss took a second quarter knee to the hit and went down in extremely concerning fashion. He was ruled out after the break. The Broncos’ thinned out pass defense has been struggling since Moss’ departure.

items.name: Sam Darnold
items.headline: Seahawks declared QB Sam Darnold, WR Rashid Shaheed, T Charles Cross, G Quenton Nelson, LB Uchenna Nwosu, DT Brandon Pili, and DT Leonard Williams inactive for Week 9 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Darnold was ruled out earlier in the week while Shaheed misses his second consecutive game with a knee injury. Drew Lock gets the start under center for the second time this season while veteran receiver Cooper Kupp could see a slight uptick in usage with Shaheed sidelined. Injury trouble along the offensive line could lead to a more ball-out-quick offensive game plan as the Seahawks look to keep pace in the NFC West.

items.name: Hunter Henry
items.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) is active for Week 9 against the Packers.
items.analysis: It was reported earlier in the day that Henry had a “realistic” shot at suiting up this week after he managed to log a limited practice on Friday. Henry will profile as a high-end TE2 with A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) out this week. In addition to Brown being out, the Patriots also declared RB TreVeyon Henderson, CB Charles Woods, OT Dametrious Crownover, and QB Behren Morton inactive for Week 9.

items.name: MarShawn Lloyd
items.headline: Packers declared RB MarShawn Lloyd (knee), LB Zaire Franklin, OL Donovan Jennings, OL Sean Rhyan, OL Travis Glover, and TE Josh Whyle inactive for Week 9 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Pierre Strong and Kaleb Johnson will serve as the backups to Josh Jacobs with Lloyd sidelined. DB Keisean Nixon, who was listed as questionable entering the weekend, is active after being slowed by a groin injury earlier in the week.

items.name: Zonovan Knight
items.headline: Cardinals declared RB Bam Knight, CB Starling Thomas V, LB Eku Leota, OL Jayden Williams, OL Jon Gaines III, and OL Albert Reese IV inactive for Week 9 against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Knight’s absence due to a concussion leaves Tyler Allgeier alone atop the running back depth chart with rookie Jeremiyah Love on injured reserve. The matchup is far from ideal against the Seahawks on the road, but Allgeier appears to be in line for a legitimate workhorse role and can be started as a viable RB2. The Cardinals press forward with veteran journeyman Gardner Minshew under center following the trade of Jacoby Brissett this week.

items.name: David Njoku
items.headline: Chargers did not activate David Njoku (fibula) from injured reserve for Week 9 against the Texans.
items.analysis: Njoku entered the contest listed as doubtful, although he practiced in a limited capacity all week. He might be able to return next week, but he does not need to be added in 12-team leagues. The Chargers declared LG Kayode Awosika (fibula), S Kendall Williamson (calf), CB Deane Leonard (concussion), WR Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) and WR Theo Wease inactive for Week 9 against the Texans.

items.name: Jaylen Waddle
items.headline: Jaylen Waddle suffered a concussion in the Broncos’ Week 9 game against the Panthers and will not return.
items.analysis: Waddle was listed as questionable in the first half but then ruled out to begin the third. It’s another nightmare development for Waddle in his first Broncos season, as he has struggled for both 100 percent health and productive box scores. Today’s injury came as Waddle skied for a target over the middle of the field and got high/lowed. He had just one grab for 22 yards before departing. The only good news is the Broncos are on bye for Week 10, meaning Waddle might not miss any game time beyond this afternoon.

items.name: David Montgomery
items.headline: Texans declared David Montgomery, S Reed Blankenship, TE Cade Stover, OG Febechi Nwaiwu, OT Braden Smith and OT Nate Thomas inactive for Week 9 against the Chargers.
items.analysis: Montgomery will miss another week with his groin injury, allowing Woody Marks to qualify as a low-end, volume-based RB2. Montgomery did not practice at all this week. His status for the Texans’ Week 10 game against the Browns is up in the air. Fortunately for the Texans, S Jalen Pitre (shoulder) is making his return this week. Rookie TE Marlin Klein will also play.

items.name: Tyler Goodson
items.headline: Tyler Goodson (knee) is questionable to return to Week 9 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Goodson saw solid work early against the Colts, effectively rotating drives with starter Javonte Williams before injuring his knee in the second quarter. He was deemed questionable to return by the team after amassing 44 yards on seven carries. Expect Williams to operate as a workhorse for the remainder of the game.

items.name: Jake Ferguson
items.headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle) is ankle for Week 9 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Ferguson entered the weekend listed as questionable after being unable to practice until Friday, where he logged a limited appearance. That was apparently enough for the veteran tight end to play through the ailment, although Brevyn Spann-Ford could be more involved than normal.

items.name: Mike Gesicki
items.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 2-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Bengals’ Week 9 victory over the Falcons.
items.analysis: Gesicki had caught a touchdown in each of his last six games, but was essentially a non-factor in the win over the Falcons in Madrid. The Bengals scored three times in the red zone, but those touchdowns went to Tee Higgins (twice) and Joe Burrow. Gesicki needs those scores to be fantasy-relevant. He’ll be a touchdown-dependent TE2 heading into Week 10’s matchup with the Steelers.

items.name: Jahan Dotson
items.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-2 targets for 16 yards in the Falcons’ Week 9 loss to the Bengals.
items.analysis: The Falcons passing attack was a mess against the Bengals in Week 9. Michael Penix threw 31 times, but for just 162 yards. Dotson was a non-factor by product, totaling just 16 yards on two receptions. He’s Atlanta’s WR2, but is merely a WR5/6 heading into Week 10 against the Chiefs.

items.name: Kyle Pitts
items.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 3-of-5 targets for 23 yards in the Falcons’ Week 9 loss to the Bengals.
items.analysis: Three receptions for 23 yards is a disappointing line and unfortunately it represents the most receiving yards Pitts has had in his last three games. Pitts has four touchdowns on the season, but is unusable in fantasy unless he finds the end zone. The definition of touchdown-dependent, Pitts is a low-end TE2 in Week 10 against the Chiefs.

items.name: Drake London
items.headline: Drake London caught 5-of-5 targets for 68 yards in the Falcons’ Week 9 loss to the Bengals.
items.analysis: London bounced back after being held to one reception and eight yards in the loss to the Buccaneers in Week 8. He caught all five of his targets for 68 yards, but still has only one touchdown on the year after being held scoreless again. After dominating with Michael Penix in the lineup last season, London has just been okay with Penix under center this year. Likely facing a pass-heavy game script in Week 10 against the Chiefs, London will be a low-end WR1 again.

items.name: Bijan Robinson
items.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 19 times for 100 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 9 loss to the Bengals, adding six receptions for 47 yards.
items.analysis: Robinson bounced back nicely after posting 76 scoreless yards in the loss to the Buccaneers in Week 8. The 24-year-old running back had 100 rushing yards and score while adding six catches for 47 yards through the air. Robinson’s touchdown gives him six in nine games this year after scoring 11 times in 17 games last season. Still an elite fantasy option despite the offense around him, Robinson is a locked in RB1 against the Chiefs in Week 10.

items.name: Michael Penix
items.headline: Michael Penix completed 20-of-31 passes for 162 yards, one touchdown and one interception in the Falcons’ 34-17, Week 9 loss to the Bengals.
items.analysis: Penix has now gone back-to-back weeks without eclipsing 200 yards. He found Charlie Woerner for a one-yard touchdown in the first quarter, but couldn’t get much going for the rest of the game. Wide receiver Drake London dominated in a small sample with Penix healthy last year, but he’s had just two games with at least 100 yards and only one touchdown this season. Penix is a low-end QB2 heading into Week 10’s home matchup against the Chiefs.

items.name: Samaje Perine
items.headline: Samaje Perine rushed 11 times for 43 yards in the Bengals’ Week 9 win over the Falcons.
items.analysis: Perine had 43 yards on 11 carries, which was notable because he had two more rushing attempts than starter Chase Brown. While Brown continues to underwhelm, Perine is cutting into Brown’s ceiling (or lack thereof) more than he’s carving out a legitimate role for himself. Perine is one of the better handcuffs to stash, but he shouldn’t be in starting lineups in Week 10 against the Steelers.

items.name: Chase Brown
items.headline: Chase Brown rushed nine times for 57 yards in the Bengals’ Week 9 win over the Falcons, adding three receptions for 18 yards.
items.analysis: While Brown struggled in Week 8, the silver lining was that he out-touched Samaje Perine 20-to-5. After fumbling against the Titans last week, Perine actually had more carries than Brown (11-to-9) in Madrid. Brown saw all three targets that went to running backs against the Falcons, but there’s no way to spin this positively for the 26-year-old who had a preseason ADP in the teens. Brown still hasn’t scored since Week 1 and he’ll be an RB2 at best against the Steelers in Week 10.

items.name: Tee Higgins
items.headline: Tee Higgins caught 5-of-6 targets for 32 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals’ Week 9 victory over the Falcons.
items.analysis: Higgins had recorded at least 148 receiving yards in three of his last four games. His 32 yards were a far cry from those gaudy totals, but he was able to save the day from a fantasy perspective by catching a four-yard touchdown and an eight-yard touchdown. Higgins still has 758 receiving yards on the season to Ja’Marr Chase’s 647, so he has that going for him. Higgins is technically the WR2 on the Bengals, but he’s a top-10 WR in fantasy heading into a matchup with the Steelers in Week 10.

items.name: Ja'Marr Chase
items.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 10-of-12 targets for 155 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 9 win over the Falcons.
items.analysis: Chase hadn’t had a game with 100 yards receiving until two weeks ago. Since then, he’s had at least 10 receptions, at least 141 yards and a touchdown in back-to-back games. Ho-hum. Chase absolutely toasted Falcons cornerback AJ Terrell for a 47-yard touchdown in the first quarter on a play that looked eerily similar to a touchdown he had against Terrell when the two were in college. Chase is up to 647 yards and seven touchdowns on the season. He’s a WR1 heading into Week 10’s matchup against the Steelers.

items.name: Joe Burrow
items.headline: Joe Burrow completed 24-of-29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in the Bengals’ 34-17 Week 9 win over the Falcons, adding three carries for seven yards and a touchdown.
items.analysis: Burrow’s excellent run of play continued against the Falcons defense in Madrid in Week 9. The 29-year-old signal caller has amassed 16 passing touchdowns in the last four weeks and added two more touchdowns on the ground.
