Burrow’s production is unsurprisingly coming from playing through his top wide receivers as Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins combined for 187 yards receiving and all three receiving touchdowns against Atlanta. Burrow is likely to find himself on the shortlist for the MVP award the way things are going. He’s a locked in QB1 heading into a Week 10 matchup with the Steelers on Sunday Night Football, which airs on NBC and Peacock.

items.name: Colby Parkinson
items.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is active for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders.
items.analysis: Parkinson managed to draw a questionable tag entering the weekend after logging a limited practice on Friday. Despite being a DNP for two of the Rams’ three practices this week, he should be available to play his normal role in the Rams’ TE-heavy scheme. Parkinson has caught 14 passes for 103 yards and one touchdown this season and will not be on the fantasy radar this week. The Rams declared QB Ty Simpson, LS Joe Cardona, LB Darryl Peterson III, OL Bill Murray, OL Keagan Trost, and LB Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 9.

items.name: Jordyn Tyson
items.headline: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is active for Week 9 against the Browns.
items.analysis: Tyson will make his NFL debut after missing the first two months of the year with a hamstring injury. We’re expecting a snap count for him this week, making him an extremely risky FLEX play. Inactive for the Saints are QB Zach Wilson, S Mike Reid, RB C.J. Donaldson, DT Christen Miller, LB Jaylan Ford, OL Mason Murphy, and DL John Ridgeway III.

items.name: Mansoor Delane
items.headline: Chiefs declared CB Mansoor Delane, QB Garrett Nussmeier, FB Ben VanSumeren, DE Jack Pyburn, OT Diego Pounds, and DT Peter Woods inactive for Week 9 against the Jets.
items.analysis: The Kansas City defense will be without Delane against a Geno Smith-led Jets passing attack that showed out last week against the Raiders. The Chiefs this season are allowing the NFL’s 13th lowest EPA per drop back and rank 15th in drop back success rate allowed.

items.name: Trent McDuffie
items.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) is inactive for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders.
items.analysis: McDuffie was a DNP in practice all week but still managed to get a questionable designation entering the weekend. That said, the team’s decision doesn’t come as much of a surprise given the fact that he was unable to get on the field last week. Fortunately for the Rams, they faced a depleted Commanders receiving corps, and they will have both Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald on the field for the first time together.

items.name: Deshaun Watson
items.headline: Browns declared QB Deshaun Watson, QB Taylen Green, C Parker Brailsford, DT Maliek Collins, LB Justin Jefferson, and CB Noah Igninoghene inactive for Week 9 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Watson cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend but was not prepared as the starter throughout the week. Shedeur Sanders will get his first start of the season and Dillon Gabriel will back him up.

items.name: Justin Walley
items.headline: Colts declared TE Pharaoh Brown, LB Akeem Davis-Gaither, S AJ Haulcy, OT Charlie Heck, QB Riley Leonard, TE Will Mallory, and CB Justin Walley in active for Week 9 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: No real surprises here as the Colts limp into their final game before the league’s trade deadline. That said there remains legitimate uncertainty surrounding the usages of Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs, amongst others, in what could be their final game with the franchise.

items.name: Sam Ehlinger
items.headline: Broncos declared S Talanoa Hufanga, CB Kris Abrams-Draine, S Brandon Jones, WR Lil’Jordan Humphrey, OG Kage Casey, TE Dallen Bentley, and QB Sam Ehlinger inactive for Week 9 against the Panthers.
items.analysis: Hufanga was questionable entering the weekend due to an ankle injury, but will officially be sidelined for this one. The 28-year-old safety hasn’t played since Week 5 but was limited in back-to-back practices to close out the week, so there’s a chance he could return after the Broncos’ Week 10 bye.

items.name: Cam Skattebo
items.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is inactive for Week 9 against the Eagles.
items.analysis: With Skattebo down, the G-Men have been forced into a Devin Singletary start. Someone named “Gregory Desrosiers” appears to be the RB2. Expect a pass-focused game plan vs. Philly’s crumbling defense. Also inactive for the Giants are CB Colton Hood, CB Nikko Reed, OL Josh Sills, OL Marcus Mbow, TE Thomas Fidone II and DL C.J. Okoye.

items.name: Jaelan Phillips
items.headline: Panthers declared LB Jaelan Phillips, QB Haynes King, CB Will Lee III, RB AJ Dillon, LB Bobby Okereke, OG Damien Lewis, and DT TeRah Edwards inactive for Week 9 against the Broncos.
items.analysis: Phillips and Lewis were both ruled out before the weekend, so there’s nothing too surprising to see here. The Panthers hope to end a two-game losing streak this week at home against a stout Broncos defense.

items.name: Jaylen Wright
items.headline: Dolphins declared RB Jaylen Wright, WR Jalen Tolbert, TE Justin Joly, G Christian Haynes, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick, CB Marcellas Dial Jr., and CB Reese Taylor inactive for Week 9 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Both Wright and Kaytron Allen were questionable because of quad injuries. Allen is active and will serve as Ollie Gordon’s backup.

items.name: Treylon Burks
items.headline: Commanders declared WR Treylon Burks, QB Athan Kaliakmanis, CB Fabian Moreau, CB Isaac Yiadom, and OG Tanoa Togiai inactive for Week 9 against the Rams.
items.analysis: The Commanders find themselves incredibly thin at receiver with Burks (foot), Terry McLaurin (knee), and Dyami Brown (calf) all sidelined for this one. Stefon Diggs, along with rookie Antonio Williams could both be in line for busy days against a Rams secondary that will be without CB Trent McDuffie.

items.name: Garrett Wilson
items.headline: Jets declared Garrett Wilson, Tim Patrick, Nahshon Wright, Joseph Ossai, Trevin Wallace, Kohl Levao, and Blake Freeland inactive for Week 9 against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Wilson suffered a head injury last week and did not practice this week as he remained in the NFL’s concussion protocol. Look for Omar Cooper, Jr. and Adonai Mitchell to see more routes and targets against a tough KC secondary. Mitchell is likely to function as the team’s top wideout with Wilson sidelined.

items.name: DeVonta Smith
items.headline: Eagles declared WR DeVonta Smith, WR Dontayvion Wicks, LB Jihaad Campbell, CB Jonathan Jones, S Michael Carter II and WR Britain Covey inactive for Week 9 against the Giants.
items.analysis: Smith has now been active just one time since Week 3. With the Eagles no longer particularly interested in the 2026 season, we would consider Smith no better than 50-50 to return following the team’s Week 10 bye.

items.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
items.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is active for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: No surprises here as this was reported earlier today. St. Brown remains a top-flight WR1 for his matchup with the Phins. Sione Vaki is also active and will serve as the team’s RB2. Inactive for the Lions are CB D.J. Reed, EDGE DJ Wonnum, C Cade Mays, RB Jacob Saylors, TE Jordan Meeks, DL Mekhi Wingo, and EDGE Ahmed Hassanein.

items.name: George Pickens
items.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) is inactive for Week 9 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Pickens played through the issue last week but will ultimately be held out in Week 9. Tight end Jake Ferguson is active after failing to practice until a limited showing Friday. Ryan Flournoy steps into a featured role for the Cowboys against the inside-funnel Colts defense. Fantasy managers can insert Flournoy into rosters as a viable FLEX considering he leads the team in slot rate through the first half of the season. Also inactive for the Cowboys are LB DeMarvion Overshown, WR KaVontae Turpin, CB Joey Porter Jr., LB Tyrus Wheat, OL Ajani Cornelius, and TE Luke Schoonmaker.

items.name: Odell Beckham
items.headline: Vikings signed WR Odell Beckham from their practice squad to the active roster.
items.analysis: Beckham landed on the Vikings’ practice squad after being released by the Giants. He appeared in three games for New York and did not record any stats. Beckham hasn’t appeared in any games for Minnesota this year, but he’ll now be a member of their 53-man roster going forward.

items.name: Brian Thomas
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that it “sounds like” the Jaguars are going to listen to trade offers for Brian Thomas Jr.
items.analysis: The Jags have shot down all offers so far, but it’s hard to justify his current usage when the team could instead recoup some draft capital by moving him. Thomas hasn’t caught more than two passes in a game since Week 2. He has three games with zero catches this year and played just 19 snaps on Thursday versus the Ravens. The Chiefs are reportedly interested, though that would require the Jags to send BTJ to one of their biggest competitors in the AFC. The Steelers and 49ers are also reportedly interested.

items.name: Cam Skattebo
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is “pushing to play” in Week 9 against the Eagles.
items.analysis: Skattebo was listed as doubtful for Week 9 after getting in a single limited practice this week. Players rarely suit up after getting the doubtful tag, but it’s not out of the question. Even if he is ruled out with inactives, the fact that Skattebo is pushing to play means he should be good to go for Week 10. Devin Singletary will handle the bulk of the backfield touches if he can’t go this week.

items.name: Talanoa Hufanga
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Broncos are hopeful Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) will play in Week 9 against the Panthers.
items.analysis: Per Fowler, he remains a game-time decision. Hufanga logged two limited practices this week before receiving a questionable designation. Before going down with the injury, Hufanga had one forced fumble and two interceptions, one of which he took to the end zone. Getting him back would be a big win for the Denver defense.

items.name: Hunter Henry
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Hunter Henry (foot) has a “realistic chance to play” in Week 9 against the Packers.
items.analysis: Henry only practiced once this week but still received a questionable designation on Friday. Eli Raridon would have taken his spot in the lineup, but it sounds like Henry will give it a go. He will be a high-end TE2 for his matchup with the Packers.

items.name: Christian Kirk
items.headline: 49ers placed Christian Kirk (knee) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: Kirk missed the start of the year with a calf issue and immediately injured his knee in Week 7. The 49ers have already burned several injured reserve return designations this year, including one on Kirk himself. He could ultimately be stuck on IR for the remainder of the year, even if he’s not dealing with a catastrophic knee injury.

items.name: Jaylen Wright
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jaylen Wright (quad) will not play in Week 9 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Wright had been backing up Ollie Gordon before going down with the quad injury. Kaytron Allen is the next man up for RB2 duties, though he’s also dealing with a quad issue. Needless to say, we’re expecting a large workload for Gordon this week.

items.name: Tanner McKee
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Tanner McKee (rib) will serve as the Eagles’ backup quarterback in Week 9 against the Giants.
items.analysis: McKee was demoted to QB2 after Week 8. He suffered a rib injury in that game, but is healthy enough to hold a clipboard. Joe Milton will make his first career start versus the Giants today.

items.name: Sam Darnold
items.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Sam Darnold (quad) could “potentially” miss Week 10 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Garafolo added that Darnold is dealing with a cracked rib, though it sounds like the quad issue is what’s preventing him from playing. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald called Darnold “week to week” on Wednesday. They get their bye in Week 11, so holding him out for one more game to get an extended break makes the most sense. Fantasy managers should plan on Darnold missing Week 10 in addition to today’s game against Arizona. Drew Lock will start today. As long as his elbow issue doesn’t flare up, he will be in line to start next week as well.

items.name: Daniel Jones
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport believes the Vikings are “a team to watch” for Daniel Jones.
items.analysis: Per Rapoport, the Ravens called Indy about Jones after Lamar Jackson went down with a potentially season-ending thumb injury. They eventually traded for Jacoby Brissett. With Kyler Murray hurt and playing poorly even when healthy, the Vikings are at least going to explore some outside options at quarterback. Jones was on the team’s practice squad in 2024 before joining the Colts last year.

items.name: Jadeveon Clowney
items.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports teams have “checked in on” Jadeveon Clowney.
items.analysis: Garafolo noted that the Texans’ game against the Chargers today will go a long way in determining whether the team wants to buy or sell at the trade deadline. Even at 2-5, the team thinks they can make a run at the playoffs. Clowney has been a hired-gun pass-rusher for most of his career. He isn’t starting for Houston and has just 1.5 sacks while playing a career-low 37 percent of the snaps on defense. If the Texans feel that their season is over, he will be one of the easiest players to move on from.

items.name: Christian McCaffrey
items.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) will have a “full workload” in Week 9 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: McCaffrey went down with the hamstring injury in Week 7, but then got a well-timed bye week to recover. He was a full participant in Friday’s practice before being removed from the injury report entirely. Per usual, he will be near the top of the RB1 ranks for his date with the Raiders.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Mike Evans (Achilles) is “questionable at best” for Week 10 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: The 49ers bungled Christian McCaffrey’s Achilles tendinitis in 2024 and are determined to get it right this time around with Evans. That means taking an extra cautious approach with his return to the field. He’s already been ruled out for Week 9 and now Week 10 sounds like a long-shot. Demarcus Robinson, who returned from injured reserve earlier this week, is somehow the team’s WR1 for today’s game against the Raiders.

items.name: Jonathan Taylor
items.headline: NFL insider Josina Anderson reports the Giants “cooled on acquiring Colts RB Jonathan Taylor because of price.”
items.analysis: She added that the Giants have resolved to move on from the trade talks ahead of their Week 9 date with the Eagles. Things change quickly in the NFL and this report doesn’t guarantee that Taylor won’t be a Giant. On the other hand, Anderson’s reporting doesn’t leave much room error. With the Colts’ asking price reportedly being through the roof, the Giants are content with Cam Skattebo as their top back. Devin Singletary is expected to start this week with Skattebo banged up.

items.name: Deshaun Watson
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Deshaun Watson cleared the league’s concussion protocol but will be inactive for Week 9 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Watson returned to practice on Friday for a limited session and cleared the league’s protocol over the weekend. Still, after preparing Shedeur Sanders to start throughout the week, head coach Todd Monken decided not to throw a curveball at his own team on game day. Sanders will start and Dillon Gabriel will back him up. Watson has rebounded this year, but the lows are still staggeringly low. He took eight sacks in a blowout loss to the Steelers last week. If Sanders plays well today, Monken will at least have something to think about ahead of Week 10.

items.name: Kyle Monangai
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) will not play in Week 9 against the Bucs.
items.analysis: Per Rapoport, Monangai is expected to return after Chicago’s Week 10 bye. Monangai has been out since Week 4. He finally returned to practice earlier this week, but it was for a single, limited session on Friday. He should be back in a 1B role when the Bears take on the Saints in two weeks.

items.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is expected to play in Week 9 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: St. Brown was limited in practice throughout the week. He has a knack for getting it out through injuries and will do so again today. Even at less than full strength, St. Brown shouldn’t face much resistance from Miami’s weak secondary. He remains a top-end WR1 for his Week 9 game in South Beach.

items.name: Emeka Egbuka
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Emeka Egbuka (foot) will play in Week 9 against the Bears.
items.analysis: Egbuka missed two games with the foot injury, though a concussion also kept him out for one of them. He practiced in full on Friday, so we’re not expecting much of a pitch count for the second-year wideout. Without anyone emerging as a viable replacement for Egbuka over the past two weeks, he should reclaim the No. 1 receiver role in Tampa Bay without much of a fight. Egbuka will be on the WR2/3 border for his first game back.

items.name: Kyle Dugger
items.headline: Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 9 against the Falcons.
items.analysis: The Bengals are surprisingly healthy headed into their date with the Falcons in Madrid, Spain. Dugger is the only one of their inactives who is out with an injury. The rest are healthy scratches.

items.name: James Pearce
items.headline: Falcons EDGE James Pearce Jr. (back) is active for Week 9 against the Bengals.
items.analysis: Pearce Jr. just finished serving his eight-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy. A back issue then flared up in practice, but he’s good to go for his 2026 debut. Inactive for the Falcons are QB Andy Dalton, QB Jack Strand, WR Zachariach Branch, DB Billy Bowman, DB Robert Longerbeam, and DE Drake Jackson.

items.name: Lamar Jackson
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Lamar Jackson is out for 6-9 weeks with a fractured and dislocated thumb.
items.analysis: Per Rapoport, Jackson has already told his teammates he plans to return this season. While even the short end of that timeline would only have Jackson back in Week 15, it’s an optimistic turn of events for a quarterback who was previously expected to miss the rest of the season. At a nine-week return, Jackson would need Baltimore to make the playoffs to have a shot at returning this year. Jacoby Brissett will likely close out the fantasy season as Baltimore’s starting quarterback, but there’s a chance we get Jackson back for a final game or two in the regular season.

items.name: Mack Hollins
items.headline: Patriots activated WR Mack Hollins (calf) from injured reserve.
items.analysis: Hollins misses the minimum four games with a calf injury and returns to a pass catching corps without A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson, while tight end Hunter Henry is also listed as questionable for Week 9. There is opportunity for him to lead the team in receiving with the bulk of the remaining healthy players largely operating in the short-to-intermediate areas of the field. Fantasy managers in a bid could do worse as a FLEX option against the Packers.

items.name: Brian Robinson
items.headline: Falcons placed RB Brian Robinson (hamstring) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: The timing of the transaction is curious after Robinson missed the previous two games with the injury, potentially signaling a setback in his recovery. Either way, Robinson will now miss the coming four games, at minimum, leaving Bijan Robinson in a clear workhorse role in the immediate future.

items.name: Pat Bryant
items.headline: Broncos activated WR Pat Bryant (ankle) from injured reserve.
items.analysis: The young receiver will make his return to the active game-day roster after missing the minimum four games after injuring his ankle in Week 4. He returns to a passing attack with no clear direction or upside, with no receiver other than Courtland Sutton playing in a near every-down role of late. Perhaps he can carve out a featured role, but it is more likely this team simply doesn’t have viable weekly fantasy assets through the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) is questionable for Week 10 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku logged a week of limited sessions before drawing the questionable tag for Monday Night Football. He will need to be activated from injured reserve prior to Monday to play. Fantasy managers are likely better off making alternate plans considering the Chargers don’t play until Monday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku is still within his 21-day practice window and has remained limited for five straight practices. He could end up playing on Monday night, but he does not need to be rostered.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku is not worth rostering whenever he officially returns to the active roster, but he theoretically can contribute offensively. He will likely be a mildly productive member of the Chargers’ three-player tight end rotation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: Chargers did not activate David Njoku (fibula) from injured reserve for Week 9 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku entered the contest listed as doubtful, although he practiced in a limited capacity all week. He might be able to return next week, but he does not need to be added in 12-team leagues. The Chargers declared LG Kayode Awosika (fibula), S Kendall Williamson (calf), CB Deane Leonard (concussion), WR Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) and WR Theo Wease inactive for Week 9 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) is doubtful to play in Week 9 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku was limited all week, though he apparently is not ready to return from injured reserve. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats. The Chargers will likely employ a three-player rotation whenever he returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku’s return is probably a good thing for the offense as a whole, but the Chargers’ tight end rotation makes for a fantasy-unfriendly situation. Njoku does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats. Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku had his practice window opened this week, giving the Chargers 21 days to activate him off injured reserve. He has been out since Week 3 and is now nearing a return, getting in limited work with a fibula injury on Wednesday. WR Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) was a DNP on Wednesday. Neither Njoku nor Thompson need to be on fantasy rosters just yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: Jim Harbaugh said the team will open the 21-day practice window for David Njoku this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku has been on the shelf since being placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 3, with the potential to return following five missed games plus the team’s Week 7 bye. The team will have 21 days to activate him from short-term injured reserve, meaning Njoku is not guaranteed to be activated in time for Week 9 against the Texans. Fantasy managers that have held Njoku through his time on injured reserve can continue patiently waiting for his return while those in shallower leagues can consider adding him from waivers before he is activated.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: Chargers placed TE David Njoku (fibula) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku was unable to put any weight on his right leg and was carted from the field in Sunday’s loss to the Raiders. Njoku has caught six passes for 67 scoreless yards for the Chargers in his first two games with the team and led all tight ends on the roster with 25 routes run. He’ll have to miss at least the next four games now that he’s landed on IR, but we should have a better sense of his return timeline in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku suffered an apparent leg injury in the second quarter of Week 2 against the Raiders and was carted off the field.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: The team officially called it a knee injury and listed him as questionable to return. Njoku was unable to put weight on his right leg and had to be helped onto the cart. Several Chargers players came to the cart to see him off the field. It looks like his day is done, even if the team is calling him questionable. Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will see an uptick in routes going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) is questionable for Week 10 against the Ravens.
Ladd McConkey (back) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: This is unfortunate. McConkey is no stranger to playing through injury, but his availability for Week 10’s Monday Night Football game appears to be in jeopardy. If active, McConkey would be a WR2, but backup plans should be made at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: The back spasms that sidelined McConkey in Week 9 against the Texans evidently remain an issue. The Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver should be viewed as questionable to play in Week 10’s Thursday Night Football game. The rest of the receiving corps is too unreliable for a WR3-level pivot if he is unable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) did not play in Week 9 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey reportedly experienced back spasms during pre-game warmups. The Chargers kept that info under wraps until their first drive was underway, following an opening-drive touchdown by the Texans. We aren’t exactly sure how the Chargers were allowed to do this, but they did it, and fantasy managers who started him are stuck with 0.0 points in the box score. If he can face the Ravens next week, he will be a WR3/FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: Immediately after the Chargers’ second play from scrimmage, the broadcast booth announced that McConkey experienced back spasms during pre-game warmups, describing the announcement as a “developing” story. It is unclear why this wasn’t announced pre-game, but here we are. Hopefully, McConkey can take the field at some point, but he could end up missing the contest. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey caught 4-of-6 targets for 86 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey was fully back from various injuries that kept him sidelined for much of the season’s first month and a half. He led the Chargers in all receiving categories, and had the team’s biggest play of the game — a 54-yard gain on a nicely thrown ball from Justin Herbert. McConkey will have a solid matchup in Week 9 against a struggling Houston secondary and should remain in 12-team league lineups. It remains to be seen whether he has any sort of ceiling in a pitiful LA offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (concussion) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 8 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey’s concussion was always unlikely to hold him out for Week 8 with the team coming off their bye, with Friday’s injury report confirming that notion. The Chargers have under-performed offensive expectations more than any team through their first six games, leaving McConkey in the FLEX range for Week 8, a far cry from the WR2 range he was drafted in this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: Harris missed Week 6 before the team’s Week 7 bye but could be held out for an additional week given the nature of his injury. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status on the team’s final injury report Friday to gauge the viability of entering him back into lineups for Week 8. Fellow wide receiver Ladd McConkey (concussion) got in his second consecutive full session and should be good to go for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (concussion) will practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: The Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver could resume practicing in full today, after recovering during the team’s Week 7 bye. If McConkey is limited, an update will be provided. Exactly one week ago, The Athletic’s Noah Furtado reported that the Chargers will try to “simplify” the team’s offense in the coming weeks. They face an underperforming Rams defense in Week 8 and could (maybe) generate a bounce-back performance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: The Athletic’s Noah Furtado reports the Chargers will try to “simplify” the team’s offense in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: Justin Herbert and the flailing Chargers skill position players have appeared almost comically confused about all the pre-snap motion OC Mike McDaniel uses. That came through in the team’s embarrassing Week 6 loss to the Chiefs when players were bumping into each other during pre-snap motion calls from Herbert. Head coach Jim Harbaugh acknowledged the team is considering narrowing the offensive playbook during their bye week. “Definitely looking at volume and where you can make it to where the players can understand,” Harbaugh said when asked about how Chargers players were adjusting to McDaniel’s complex offense. The Chargers have used pre-snap motion on 74 percent of their snaps, the fourth highest rate in the NFL. Last year they used motion on 56 percent of their snaps. Hopefully these adjustments lead to some production for the NFL’s worst offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Packers activated RB Chris Brooks and WR Skyy Moore from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Brooks returns to a backfield once again without Josh Jacobs, appearing likely to serve as the preferred passing down back while Kaleb Johnson handles early-down duties. Moore remains unlikely to be consistently involved in the offense but brings a sizable boost to the special teams unit. The top duo of Christian Watson and Matthew Golden should continue to dominate targets through the air for one of the most pass-heavy offenses in the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Chris Brooks (ankle) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 10 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Brooks would have a chance to assume passing-down duties if he is activated off injured reserve. That would probably quash Pierre Strong’s value more than Marshawn Lloyd or Kaleb Johnson’s, but Brooks would probably be the favorite to see the most snaps among Green Bay’s runners if active. It would be a rough FLEX play against a good Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman believes Kaleb Johnson could have a chance to be the Packers’ lead rusher in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: With Josh Jacobs out with a broken finger, Johnson led the Packers with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown in the team’s Week 9 drubbing of the Patriots. Forty-four of those yards came on explosive rushes. Pierre Strong, meanwhile had eight carries on the day. MarShawn Lloyd was sidelined with a knee issue but could be back in the Green Bay lineup soon. Lloyd’s shocking lack of production this season could, according to Schneidman, give Johnson a real chance to seize lead back duties. Head coach Matt LaFleur after the team’s Week 9 win seemed to imply there are some pass protection concerns for Johnson. That would probably mean Chris Brooks, who’s expected to return from an ankle injury in Week 10, gets the third-down role while Jacobs is sidelined. The Packers this week take on an elite Minnesota offense that teams have run on in recent weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: MarShawn Lloyd (knee) is questionable for Week 9 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Lloyd popped up on Thursday’s injury report with the knee issue, and now appears to be a game-time decision. Chris Brooks (ankle) is also questionable for the Week 9 tilt, so there could be depth issues for the Pack behind Josh Jacobs, who has struggled in his return to action as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: MarShawn Lloyd was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday’s practice due to a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Lloyd was good to go for Wednesday’s session, so this appears to be a new issue. Chris Brooks was also limited by his ankle injury for a second-straight practice. Lloyd and Brooks — if healthy — will be the backups to Josh Jacobs for Week 9, and don’t offer much fantasy upside, if any.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Packers designated Chris Brooks (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Brooks is back at practice and could be officially activated from IR ahead of the Packers’ Week 9 matchup with the Patriots. He would likely take Pierre Strong’s spot in the lineup as Green Bay’s RB3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Packers placed RB Chris Brooks (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Brooks had been the most consistent contributor to a Green Bay backfield working to find their way in the absence of Josh Jacobs. The team appears likely to utilize journeyman Pierre Strong as the preferred passing down specialist, likely keeping the backfield in a maddening timeshare without Brooks. None are worthy of legitimate fantasy interest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Chris Brooks (ankle) will not play in Green Bay’s Week 5 game against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: This was foreshadowed a bit by the appearance of Pierre Strong Jr. on the roster. It’s unclear how the Packers will handle third-down reps between Strong, Kaleb Johnson, and MarShawn Lloyd on Sunday. Strong was on the field for 138 passes of his 192 snaps in 2024 with the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Chris Brooks (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Matt LaFleur said earlier this morning that they were going to “give him another day and see where he’s at tomorrow and make a decision after that.” It sounds like there’s still a chance Brooks could play in Week 5, but he’ll likely be on the questionable line on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Chris Brooks (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Brooks suffered the ankle injury in Week 4. He went down in the first half and did not return. Brooks underwent testing on his ankle after the game, though the exact nature of his injury has yet to be reported. He does appear to be on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5. If he can’t go, MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson will split the backfield. Johnson led the team in carries last week but also gave up a goal line fumble. We expect Lloyd to get the start versus Chicago on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: Patriots placed RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson will now miss the coming four games, at minimum, after missing the previous two, with what the team is calling neurological symptoms. Whatever it is that Henderson is currently going through is clearly bigger than football. Rhamondre Stevenson is currently listed as questionable for Week 10 but is not expected to play, leaving the backfield in the hands of Corey Kiner in the immediate future. Here’s hoping for a speedy recovery for the electric running back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) will not play in Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson is dealing with an unexpected medical emergency right now. We would imagine he did not travel to Germany with the team. It’s unclear when he will return. With Rhamondre Stevenson also expected to miss Week 10, Corey Kiner is in line to see the bulk of the team’s backfield touches this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: It seemed pretty obvious that Henderson wasn’t going to play Sunday after it was announced the second-year runner was dealing with “neurological symptoms” but it’s now official. There are much bigger things than football going on in his life. While he gets better, Corey Kiner should be the backup running back behind Rhamondre Stevenson going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson released a statement saying that he was dealing with an “unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: This certainly sounds like a scary situation for Henderson, whose absence has been the subject of speculation for nearly two weeks. Henderson said that the results of “comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, but he continues to work with specialists and physical therapists. Henderson said these issues have affected his “strength, coordination, and some of [his] physical functions,” while adding that he is working to return to full health. While we don’t want to speculate too much, it doesn’t sound like Henderson will be back anytime soon. Hopefully we will get more clarity on his situation soon, but our thoughts are with him and his continued recovery.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss believes TreVeyon Henderson’s illness might be related to the “adversity” he has faced this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Reiss was asked about Henderson’s status during his weekly appearance on the local radio show, Toucher & Hardy. According to Reiss, Henderson has faced a lot of new challenges this season, including recurring ankle issues and limited playing time, and the adversity has been tough for Henderson to deal with. Some might remember that similar reports surfaced regarding Bucky Irving, beset by multiple injuries, last season. Henderson might need more time before he resumes playing. Stay tuned. He was officially listed as a non-participant on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: It’s rare for a player to miss even one game with an illness. It’s even more unheard of for them to miss the next practice. It’s possible Henderson is dealing with something more severe than the flu or a stomach bug. If he isn’t able to play in Week 9, Rhamondre Stevenson will handle the bulk of the backfield touches once again. He touched the ball 22 times on Sunday and would be in line for a similar workload against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson first popped on the injury report with a missed practice Thursday before maintaining that status to end the week, ultimately unable to play through the ailment while being ruled out Saturday. Rhamondre Stevenson steps into a potential workhorse role against the downtrodden Dolphins, where he will be an upside RB2 in Week 8. Expect the team to elevate another back from their practice squad ahead of Sunday’s game to play behind Stevenson and Corey Kiner, the latter of whom is expected to serve as the primary change of pace option with Henderson out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is questionable for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson missed practice Thursday with an illness, ultimately drawing the questionable tag for the team’s Week 8 divisional clash with the Dolphins. That places fantasy managers in a precarious position considering the team plays in the afternoon portion of the Sunday slate. It would be prudent to make alternate plans at FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Illnesses typically don’t hold back NFL players, so we’d be surprised if Henderson missed time, but it is worth noting that it was a Thursday addition to the report. Because of that, if he missed Friday, it wouldn’t be surprising if he was listed as questionable. We’d still expect him to play either way.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson rushed three times for nine yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 14 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson continues to play second, or third, fiddle behind Rhamondre Stevenson when the Patriots are forced into “gotta have it” mode, with Stevenson the back most trusted in key situations. The Patriots fell into an early hole and were playing catch-up throughout against the Bears, something that could help to explain the lowly opportunity total for the back widely considered the more explosive of the two. Furthermore, the team continued to rotate Corey Kiner through the opportunity pecking order, placing another sizable dent in the weekly floor of Henderson. Although he could find more opportunities in a softer matchup in Week 8, he’ll be a difficult click to insert into fantasy lineups against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Panthers activated WR Xavier Legette (knee) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Legette will make his return to a passing offense currently dominated by Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, and tight end Darren Waller, unlikely to return a usable fantasy score in his first game since Week 2. He is not on the fantasy radar despite the plus matchup against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Xavier Legette (knee) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Legette has missed the past six games but could join the active squad for the first time since Week 2. Even if he returns this week, the third-year wideout may have trouble carving out a fantasy-relevant receiving role every week behind Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble, and running back Chuba Hubbard. However, even in this crowded picture, the 25-year-old could warrant a stash in some deep leagues for those craving anyone with upside at wide receiver. His added presence could help Bryce Young’s fantasy value as the season goes on.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Panthers designated Xavier Leggette (knee) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Legette practiced in full, so he could be back on the field as soon as Sunday. He would only return to a part-time role, so there isn’t any fantasy value to be had here. Jonathon Brooks is also practicing, meaning the Panthers’ offense could be getting reinforcements at multiple positions soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said the team is weighing whether or not to open Jonathon Brooks (core) return window this week
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Canales said the oft-injured Brooks still has “some things to clear recovery-wise” but noted that he could still have his practice window opened this week. Brooks suffered a core muscle injury in Week 2 against the Falcons and handled just 11 touches in his first two games of the year. Given his injury history, it’s hard to know how close he could truly be to dressing on game day, but even when he does return, we would still expect Chuba Hubbard to handle the majority of touches given how efficient he has been this season. In addition to Brooks, Canales said the team is also weighing when to open the return window for Xavier Legette, who has been sidelined since Week 2 with a knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Panthers placed WR Xavier Legette (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Legette was already ruled out for Week 4, which marks his second straight absence. He will now be forced to miss the next four games while on injured reserve, making his absence a total of five games, at minimum. John Metchie and Brycen Tremaine will continue to operate as the WR3 in the interim.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Xavier Legette (knee) will not play in Week 4 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Legette will miss a second straight game with his knee injury. He has caught just two passes for 64 yards on six targets this season and wouldn’t be on the fantasy radar even if he were active. In addition to Legette, the Panthers also ruled out OG Damien Lewis (elbow) for Week 4 against the Lions while OT Monroe Freeling (concussion), DT Lee Hunter (foot), and DT Cam Jackson (knee) were all listed as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Panthers WR Jalen Coker (quad) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Panthers coach Dave Canales said WR Xavier Legette (knee) is week-to-week, while Coker “is more day-to-day.” Canales adds that the team “has to see Coker move around before he returns to action.” Coker remains firmly in the questionable camp at this time. He might have a chance to play in Week 4 against the Lions, but fantasy managers should make a serious backup plan.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Xavier Legette (knee) is inactive for Week 3 vs. the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Jalen Coker (ankle), meanwhile, is active. Legette made a big catch in Week 2, but he’s one of the only boats not rising with the tide of the Panthers’ ascending offense. He is off the radar in 12-team league fantasy, especially now that he’s injured.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jalen Coker (ankle) “should play” in Week 3 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Xavier Legette (knee) remains a game-time decision. Both players were officially listed as questionable on Friday. Coker has gotten off to a red-hot start this year with 16 grabs for 204 yards and a pair of scores through two weeks. Even if he’s limited by the ankle issue, the production is too good to keep on the bench. He is, at worst, a WR3 for his date with the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Xavier Legette (knee) will likely be a game-day decision for Week 3 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/xavier-legette.analysis: Legette popped up on Thursday’s injury report as a DNP and was limited on Friday. The third-year receiver underwent an MRI, but it doesn’t sound like it revealed anything too concerning given his practice status for Friday. Even if he is active, Legette isn’t on the fantasy radar this week. He’s managed just two receptions for 64 yards on four targets so far this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Panthers downgraded Jonathon Brooks (core) to out for Week 10 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Brooks will miss his seventh consecutive game as he attempts to return from a core muscle injury. He managed a week of limited sessions before initially being listed as doubtful, ultimately ruled out. Chuba Hubbard will again serve as a legitimate workhorse in a plus matchup against the Saints and can be treated as a back-end RB1 in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Jonathon Brooks (core) is doubtful for Week 10 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Brooks was previously listed as a full participant in Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices, only for head coach Dave Canales to announce on Friday that Brooks was working with the scout team, not the 53-man roster, meaning he was actually limited throughout the week. After logging three limited practices, Brooks appears unlikely to play in Week 10 given the doubtful designation. With his return window opened earlier this week, the Panthers could delay his return by two more weeks before having to either rule him out for the season or activate him from injured reserve. We will see how things go for him next week ahead of Week 11’s game against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Panthers designated Jonathon Brooks (core) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Brooks practiced in full, giving him a shot at suiting up this week. However, it won’t surprise us if they give him another week of practice before putting him back on the field because of his lengthy injury history. With Chuba Hubbard excelling in his workhorse role this year, Brooks will likely be stuck with change-of-pace duties once healthy. He is only worth stashing in deeper fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said the team is weighing whether or not to open Jonathon Brooks (core) return window this week
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Canales said the oft-injured Brooks still has “some things to clear recovery-wise” but noted that he could still have his practice window opened this week. Brooks suffered a core muscle injury in Week 2 against the Falcons and handled just 11 touches in his first two games of the year. Given his injury history, it’s hard to know how close he could truly be to dressing on game day, but even when he does return, we would still expect Chuba Hubbard to handle the majority of touches given how efficient he has been this season. In addition to Brooks, Canales said the team is also weighing when to open the return window for Xavier Legette, who has been sidelined since Week 2 with a knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jonathon Brooks is expected to have core muscle surgery and will be placed on IR.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Brooks will be sidelined for at least six weeks. It opens the door for Chuba Hubbard to dominate the Carolina backfield for the next month and a half, with AJ Dillon chipping in as a breather back. Through two game Hubbard leads the Panthers backfield with 22 rushes for 102 yards. He’s run a route on 50 percent of the team’s drop backs and have five targets. The Panthers, meanwhile, have the second highest pass rate over expected through Week 2. Hubbard will be a locked-in top-20 option going forward. Dillon can be stashed in case Hubbard gets dinged up while Brooks is recovering.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said the team is “gathering information” on Jonathon Brooks’ groin injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: He’s undergoing tests to determine the severity. That’s not normally the sort of story that ends with “and Brooks played a full allotment of snaps in Week 3,” but we’ll see. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports that Brooks is “considered week to week.” Brooks should be regarded as a drop candidate in shallow leagues on snaps and opportunities alone, but if he’s not healthy, that may expand to more leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Jonathon Brooks aggravated his groin injury in Week 2 against the Falcons and is considered “day to day.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: The good news is that this is unrelated to Brooks’ history of knee injuries and it sounds like he has a shot at suiting up for Week 3. The bad news is that Brooks originally suffered this groin injury during training camp and is still dealing with it two weeks into the season. Brooks only had five carries and one catch before exiting Week 2’s win over Atlanta. Even if he is healthy for next week’s game, Brooks is barely on the fantasy radar right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is questionable to return in Week 2 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Brooks went down on a routine tackle in the fourth quarter and was slow to get up. He eventually left for the locker room with a towel over his head. Brooks missed time late in training camp with the groin issue and it seemingly flared up against the Falcons. He had five carries for 16 yards before leaving the game. AJ Dillon will back up Chuba Hubbard if Brooks is unavailable for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Jonathon Brooks had four rushes for 14 yards in the Panthers’ Week 1 loss to the Bears, adding one catch for 48 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: In his first regular season action, Brooks played well behind lead back Chuba Hubbard, who finished the day with ten carries and three receptions. The highlight of Brooks’ day came on a sideline throw from Bryce Young that went for 48 yards. Brooks, coming off multiple major knee injuries, showed impressive burst and speed on the catch and run. That Hubbard was the team’s primary option inside the ten yard line is bad news for Brooks’ touchdown upside in the Carolina offense. For now he profiles as a bench stash in case Hubbard misses time this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Jonathon Brooks (groin) will play in Week 1 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Brooks missed time late in camp with “general soreness” that was later revealed to be a minor groin issue. He was limited in practice this week, but that seems like nothing more than maintenance for a player who has barely played football over the past two seasons. Dave Canales is understandably keeping his workload light, even in practice. Brooks is expected to split carries with Chuba Hubbard in Week 1. He will be a high-risk FLEX play before we know what his role looks like.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Cowboys placed RB Tyler Goodson (ankle/knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: It’s yet another blow to the depth of a backfield devastated by injuries this season, leaving lead back Javonte Williams again positioned well to see a workhorse role against the 49ers. The team elevated running back Israel Abanikanda in an associated move, who is likely to serve as the primary change of pace option in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Cowboys ruled out Tyler Goodson (ankle/knee) for Week 10 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: The Cowboys will be without their No. 2 running back, removing what little threat there was to Javonte Williams’ workload. Goodson should remain stashed on 12-team benches if possible, though he could miss next week as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones said RB Tyler Goodson (knee) is expected to miss some time.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Goodson has emerged as the Cowboys’ RB2 this season, and rushed 12 times for 77 yards in Week 9’s win over the Colts. He played through the knee injury he suffered in the second quarter. The fact that he played through the injury suggests this isn’t anything too serious, but it’s not uncommon to see players be sidelined in the following weeks once the adrenaline has worn off and the game is over. We’ll likely get a clearer timeline for his return in the coming days, but for now, it looks like Israel Abanikanda and/or Jashaun Corbin will be promoted from the practice squad, with Javonte Williams being the only healthy back on Dallas’ roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Tyler Goodson rushed 12 times for 77 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 9 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Goodson saw solid work early against the Colts, effectively rotating drives with starter Javonte Williams before injuring his knee in the second quarter. He was deemed questionable to return by the team after amassing 44 yards on seven carries, but returned to rotate in with Williams in the third quarter, adding an additional 33 yards after the break. Goodson could carry viable FLEX value if the Cowboys continue forward with a run-heavy approach, as they have the previous three games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Tyler Goodson rushed seven times for 14 yards in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to Arizona, adding two catches for 19 yards on his only two targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: He found 20-of-74 running back snaps against the Cardinals; not bad work but nothing that is making you consider a waiver claim either. Goodson should be held in deeper leagues as a contingency stash.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Cowboys waived RB Emari Demercado.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Tyler Goodson has had the RB2 role for the past couple of weeks and is set to continue now that Demercado was waived to make room for Tyler Smith to come off injured reserve. Demercado has now been waived twice in two months, and though he may be claimed again, he could also wind up on a practice squad next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: KPRC2’s Aaron Wilson reports the Cowboys are signing RB Tyler Goodson off the Falcons’ practice-squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Goodson will backfill the roster spot lost to placing Malik Davis on IR at the end of last week. It’s unclear whether Emari Demercado or Goodson would be the head of a committee if Javonte Williams were injured, as both of them showed up with the Cowboys after last cuts. Neither player is a must-roster as things stand.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Falcons released RB Tyler Goodson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Goodson made an impact as part of the Falcons’ running back room in the preseason but ultimately Brian Robinson Jr. will keep the backup job. Also waived/released by the Falcons were CB Darnay Holmes, DT Eric Johnson II, TE Nick Muse, OLB Azeez Ojulari, DE Cam Sample, LB Channing Tindall, DT Marlon Tuipulotu, OL Brandon Walton, DL Chris Williams, LB Josh Woods, DT Carlos Allen, WR Vinny Anthony, OL James Brockermeyer, CB Cobee Bryant, RB Nate Carter, OL Kam Dewberry, WR Dylan Drummond, RB Cash Jones, OL Riley Mahlman, WR Keelan Marion, DT Devonnsha Maxwell, OT Wanya Morris, LB Daveren Rayner, OL Jaeden Roberts, TE Joshua Simon, DB Keidron Smith, OL Andrew Stueber, LB Bralen Trice, TE Jack Velling, WR Antwane Wells Jr., and CB A.J. Woods.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Falcons signed RB Tyler Goodson, formerly of the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Goodson was slated to be a restricted free agent, but the Colts balked. He’s a decent third-down back, but behind Bijan Robinson he figures to offer little fantasy value in his age-26 season. At least his last name isn’t also “Robinson,” unlike some backups in this backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: DJ Giddens rushed eight times for 30 yards in the Colts’ Week 18 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: It was the first time Giddens saw any real work since Week 1, where he spelled Jonathan Taylor late in a blowout win over the Dolphins. With Tyler Goodson (one carry, three yards) set to become a restricted free agent in 2026, Giddens will enter the offseason No. 2 on the depth chart. He hasn’t shown much so far, but how could he? He had only 18 carries all season before this game as Taylor stayed incredibly healthy, and those 18 carries were the most among Indy’s backup runners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: Texans ruled out David Montgomery (groin) for Week 10 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Montgomery entered the weekend listed as questionable after missing the previous three games plus the team’s Week 8 bye. Fantasy managers will have to wait another week for his return, while Woody Marks retains viable FLEX status playing as the top option alongside recent signee Emari Demercado.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery (groin) is questionable for Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Montgomery got in a full practice for the first time since returning from his groin injury. It’s certainly possible he’s back, but given a likely snap count in his return, it’d be hard to trust him as more than a what-the-heck FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery (groin) returned to practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Montgomery was mostly working out with a trainer, but DeMeco Ryans said they were “pleased with the progress he was making.” It’s possible this goes down as a DNP still on the official report, but it is real progress that he’s back on the field and he now has a non-zero chance to suit up for Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: It looks like Montgomery will miss another game because of the groin issue. Woody Marks has been seeing all the work in his absence. The role has yet to produce a meaningful fantasy outing. Still, fantasy managers can’t afford to fade a player seeing the bulk of the touches in an ascending offense. Marks remains a frustrating RB2 for Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: Texans declared David Montgomery, S Reed Blankenship, TE Cade Stover, OG Febechi Nwaiwu, OT Braden Smith and OT Nate Thomas inactive for Week 9 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Montgomery will miss another week with his groin injury, allowing Woody Marks to qualify as a low-end, volume-based RB2. Montgomery did not practice at all this week. His status for the Texans’ Week 10 game against the Browns is up in the air. Fortunately for the Texans, S Jalen Pitre (shoulder) is making his return this week. Rookie TE Marlin Klein will also play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery (groin) will not play in Week 9 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Per head coach DeMeco Ryans, Montgomery remains week-to-week. He did not practice today and we assume he won’t get on the field in any capacity this week. Woody Marks will make another start. Facing a down-horrific Chargers squad, Marks should finally get going after two underwhelming starts in Montgomery’s absence. He is a locked-in RB2 for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery (groin) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Montgomery could still need more time to recover from his Week 5 groin injury. Woody Marks should be expected to start against the Chargers this weekend, at this time. Montgomery technically still has a chance to resume practicing this week, but today likely would have served as the first ramp-up session if he had a good chance of playing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans did not have an update on David Montgomery’s groin injury when speaking with the media on Monday
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Montgomery, who missed the Texans’ last two games with his injury, is coming off the team’s Week 8 bye, and there was some hope he might be able to get on the field for Week 9’s game against the Chargers. While that may still be the case, it’s possible we will need to wait until Wednesday, when the team releases its first injury report, to see how Montgomery is trending heading into the weekend. The 29-year-old running back has struggled mightily this season even when healthy, rushing for 138 yards and two touchdowns on 52 carries while averaging a dismal 2.7 YPC. Even if he is active against the Chargers, Montgomery would be hard to trust as anything more than an RB3/Flex play given his performance pre-injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports David Montgomery (groin) will not play in Week 7 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: This will be the second game in a row that Montgomery has missed due to the groin injury he suffered in Week 5. Woody Marks, who totaled 17 touches in last week’s win over the Jaguars will again lead the Texans’ backfield. He has averaged 18.0 touches per game over the last two weeks and will be a volume-based RB2 with a chance at significant upside. Safeties Jalen Pitre (AC joint) and S Reed Blankenship (concussion) will also miss this week’s game against the Giants, putting the Texans down a handful of starters with one game left before their Week 8 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports that David Montgomery (groin) is not expected to play in Week 7 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Like we said yesterday, Montgomery is still seemingly in the week-to-week camp. Woody Marks and Dare Ogunbowale will likely split backfield touches this week. The Texans used both Marks and Jawhar Jordan last week, but Jordan suffered an injured reserve-worthy injury. Marks should be in starting lineups, but he may be more of a FLEX than a reliable RB2. Ogunbowale is a low-floor PPR dart throw.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth (illness) is questionable for Week 10 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth was added to the injury report Saturday as questionable with an illness. A mid-range TE2 when healthy, Freiermuth’s potential absence likely wouldn’t change much for Darnell Washington’s fantasy outlook. Fantasy managers counting on Freiermuth will need to be proactive about alternative options as the Steelers play the Bengals on Sunday Night Football, which airs on NBC and Peacock.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freirumuth caught both of his targets for 35 yards receiving and added a rushing touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 8 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freierumuth is the Steelers’ designated tush push option, which will give him a little added fantasy value here and there. Despite the fact that Darnell Washington outproduced Freiermuth today, Freiermuth ran a route on 11 of the team’s 26 dropbacks, compared to just five for Washington. This simply wasn’t a big day for the Steelers’ passing attack, but we’d expect Freiermuth to remain a mid-range TE2 option going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 2-of-4 targets for 20 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth didn’t appear to be bothered by his calf injury, and he quadrupled the targets of Darnell Washington (4-to-1) in this game. Washington was able to convert his only target for a touchdown, however, and Freirmuth dropped what would have been a 20-yard gain in the third quarter. Freiermuth will likely get a similar amount of targets in Week 8 against the Browns, for better or worse.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 2-of-3 targets for 11 yards in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: The Muth was clearly limited by his nagging calf injury in this game. He was added to the injury report over the weekend and played through the issue despite being hit with a late questionable tag. He was spotted hobbling to the sidelines at least once during this game, though he ultimately gutted it out and played through the issue. He and Darnell Washington each played 54 of 76 offensive snaps. Better days should be ahead for Freiermuth once he’s healthy, but it will be hard to trust him as anything other than a TE2 flyer for his Week 7 game against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth (calf) is active for Week 6 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Muth was a late addition to the injury report, with the Steelers adding him on Saturday and listing him as questionable. With multiple starting receivers out this week, Muth will be asked to take on more work as a pass-catcher, moving him up the TE2 ranks. Inactive for the Steelers are WR Ben Skowronek, QB Drew Allar, QB Will Howard, CB Sean Murphy-Bunting, RB Eli Heidenreich, CB Terell Smith, and DL Kevin Jobity Jr.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Steelers are “optimistic” Pat Freiermuth (calf) will play in Week 6 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth was added to the injury report on Saturday. The team listed him as questionable for Week 6. A last-minute addition to the injury report is never a good sign, so we wouldn’t be surprised if his snaps are limited even if he is active. On the other hand, with Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman out, the Steelers may have no choice but to play a banged-up Muth more than expected. He will be a high-risk TE2 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth (calf) is questionable for Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth popped up on the injury report Saturday afternoon with a calf injury. He’s questionable for this weekend against the Buccaneers. Freiermuth would’ve been in line for a sizable workload with the Steelers down multiple wide receivers. Coming off a two touchdown performance in Week 5, fantasy managers need a backup plan in case Freiermuth is ultimately ruled out against Tampa Bay.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 5-of-7 targets for 44 yards and two touchdowns in the Steelers’ Week 5 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth ran 27 routes on 38 dropbacks, which was a distant third behind DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard; however, Aaron Rodgers is far more effective when targeting the intermediate and middle areas of the field, which makes Freiermuth a more consistent target than either of the wide receivers. With Michael Pittman (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) both hurt, Freiermuth could be a fringe TE1 next week against the Bucs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 3-of-5 targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 4 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth found the end zone late in the fourth quarter for his second touchdown of the season, tying fellow tight end Darnell Washington for fourth on the team with five targets. Washington managed to corral just two of his five targets but eclipsed the yardage total of Freiermuth with 27 yards while also adding a touchdown of his own. Both tight ends appear unlikely to contribute viable counting stats considering neither has seen more than five targets in a game during the first month of play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Steelers are going to use Jaylen Warren “a lot” while frequently utilizing two-tight end sets in Week 4 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: It sounds like Warren is belongs on the RB1/2 border with Rico Dowdle (toe) sidelined again this week. The Steelers will try to control the line of scrimmage by frequently deploying TEs Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington, both in the run game and as receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Omar Cooper (ankle) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper seemed to be trending in the right direction this week as he got in a full practice on Friday. Now he’s expected to play against the Bills, according to Zenitz. Cooper led the Jets in targets last week and will be in the WR3 mix against Buffalo this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper was limited on Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full participation on Friday. The team listed him as questionable for a reason, but he is likely on the right side of questionable at this time. With Adonai Mitchell (knee) suddenly ailing, Cooper could warrant WR3 treatment against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Omar Cooper (ankle) will be a full participant in Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Assuming all goes well, Cooper will likely be removed from the injury report before the end of the day, meaning he will be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Bills. Cooper caught eight passes for 58 yards in Week 9’s loss to the Chiefs, but that was with Garrett Wilson (concussion) sidelined. While we wouldn’t expect another 11-target outing from Cooper with Wilson expected to be active for Week 10, he could have some FLEX appeal after yet another strong showing. We will check back in with a final status update on Cooper when the team announces it later in the day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Back-to-back limited sessions have us believing Cooper has a good chance to play in Week 10 against the Bills. The role has been up-and-down as the Jets struggle to work in all their weapons. Cooper qualifies as a FLEX play against what has been a shaky Bills defense when not facing Carson Wentz this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Omar Cooper, Jr. (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper is dealing with an ankle issue he suffered in Week 9, but he should be OK for Week 10 against the Bills if he’s able to log a practice on Thursday and/or Friday. Cooper last week against Kansas City led the Jets in targets (11) with Garrett Wilson (concussion) sidelined. Wilson is expected back for Week 10. Cooper remains a viable flex play in a game that will likely see the Jets play from behind in a potentially pass-heavy game script. Buffalo’s defense has seen the tenth highest pass rate over expected in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper, Jr. caught 8-of-11 targets for 58 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper, fresh off a Week 8 zero, led the Jets in all receiving categories with Garrett Wilson (concussion) sidelined for this one. Operating primarily from the slot, Cooper got open on a few first half dump offs and gained decent yardage after the catch. Adonai Mitchell, meanwhile, was held without a catch on seven targets. As long as he’s running a decent route rate, Cooper should be flex worthy in most formats. He’ll face the pass-funnel Buffalo defense in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets placed Garrett Wilson in the NFL’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: He was officially a DNP for Wednesday’s practice. Wilson sustained a head injury in Week 8 against the Raiders and now appears to be a long shot for Week 9. Wilson this season has accounted for 27 percent of the Jets’ targets and 38 percent of the team’s air yards. His absence would make both Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper flex-viable for Week 9, along with Mason Taylor. Cooper is coming off a game in which he saw no targets while running a route on 75 percent of the Jets’ drop backs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. was not targeted in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Coming off back-to-back 100-yard efforts since rejoining the Jets’ lineup in Week 6, it was Cooper’s turn to take a zero after Adonai Mitchell had that unfortunate distinction in Week 7. Today it was Mitchell blowing up for a 100-yard day, going 7/142/1 on nine looks. This, as Garrett Wilson still commanded a team-leading 12 targets. Wilson’s unmovable presence combined with Mitchell’s target competition means Cooper is going to be a volatile WR3 going forward, but “volatile” does at least denote upside. He might not be particularly likely to tap into it for Week 9 against the Chiefs. Especially with only two teams on bye next weekend, Cooper is probably best treated as a WR4 rather than WR3.
