https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. caught 5-of-6 targets for 115 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper was an electric deep threat once again, bringing down catches for 60 and 52 yards, neither of which was his touchdown. He scored shortly after the 52-yard grab by lining up as a running back and cruising past his defender for an easy three-yard touchdown reception. Cooper Jr. is the first rookie in franchise history with back-to-back games with 100+ receiving yards and a touchdown. While we can’t say he has overtaken Garrett Wilson already, this is looking like, at worst, a co-WR1 situation. Cooper will flirt with a WR2 ranking when he takes on the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell (finger) will play in Week 7 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Mitchell has been sidelined since injuring his finger in preparation for the Jets’ Week 3 game against the Lions. It was incredibly unfortunate time for Mitchell and his fantasy managers, as his injury came just days after he went for 6-63-0 on 12 targets against the Packers. Mitchell’s return could complicate things for Omar Cooper’s fantasy managers after Cooper broke out for 6-103-1 against the Patriots last week. The Jets rank 13th in the league in plays run from 11-personnel (209) through the first six weeks of the season, which means both Mitchell and Cooper should see plenty of snaps. That said, neither player should be viewed as anything more than a WR3/FLEX play until we see how the target distribution looks with both players active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Adonai Mitchell (knee) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell remains questionable with a knee injury that put him on the injury report after getting in a full practice Friday. However concerning Mitchell’s new injury seemed, he’s expected to play, according to Zenitz. With Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) also expected to play, Mitchell is a boom-or-bust dart throw at best in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (knee) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell practiced in full today, but was added to the injury report with a new knee issue. This is a little concerning. The team could be trying to collect more info right now. We expect to hear more later today or at some point tomorrow. At this point, Mitchell must be viewed as firmly in the questionable column.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell didn’t catch any of his seven targets in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: A week after going ballistic against the Raiders, the high-variance Mitchell couldn’t come up with a grab in an embarrassing effort for a Jets offense that was without Garrett Wilson (concussion). If your fantasy league awards points for air yards, Mitchell would have been a week winner against Kansas City. Alas, he could not convert any of that opportunity into real-life production, though he came awfully close on a couple well-thrown Geno Smith downfield balls. He was second on the team in targets, trailing Omar Cooper (11). Mitchell next week against the Bills will remain a boom-bust WR3 option. Buffalo has struggled against boundary receivers all season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell caught 7-of-9 targets for 142 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Looking to bounce back from a Week 7 doughnut in his return from a marathon injury absence, Mitchell responded with by far the best game of his career. This, even as one of his two missed connections was a heinous deep drop. Geno Smith never stopped looking his way, and the quarterback was rewarded with multiple chunk gains. Smith once again failed to get fully in sync with Garrett Wilson. Smith also targeted Omar Cooper Jr. zero times. That was hard to see coming, and will be difficult to sustain going forward, keeping Mitchell as more of a boom/bust WR3/4 than weekly must start. This blow-up effort confirmed he still has life in 12-team leagues, however. That will include for Week 9 against a Chiefs defense that is admittedly much better than Vegas’ porous unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell failed to catch any of his three targets in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: To add insult to injury, Mitchell had a two-point conversion catch called back because of a penalty. Omar Cooper Jr. once again stole the show, reeling in several long catches en route to his second 100-yard game in a row. Playing in his first game in over a month, Mitchell did not appear awfully involved in the team’s game plan. The hope will be that he earns more opportunities next week, but Cooper Jr. may have already cemented himself as the team’s No. 2 receiver. Mitchell will be stuck in the WR5 ranks when he takes on the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell (finger) will play in Week 7 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell has been sidelined since injuring his finger in preparation for the Jets’ Week 3 game against the Lions. It was incredibly unfortunate time for Mitchell and his fantasy managers, as his injury came just days after he went for 6-63-0 on 12 targets against the Packers. Mitchell’s return could complicate things for Omar Cooper’s fantasy managers after Cooper broke out for 6-103-1 against the Patriots last week. The Jets rank 13th in the league in plays run from 11-personnel (209) through the first six weeks of the season, which means both Mitchell and Cooper should see plenty of snaps. That said, neither player should be viewed as anything more than a WR3/FLEX play until we see how the target distribution looks with both players active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: It is too early to say whether Mitchell and his surgically repaired finger will be ready to face the Dolphins this week. He is a worthwhile bench stash, though. Mitchell played well early in the year, pre-injury and pre-breakout from rookie Omar Cooper. It is unclear whether Mitchell will return to the No. 2 wide receiver role or if he will be asked to unseat the youngster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell has missed the past four weeks with a finger injury that required a “small procedure” to fix. Though a limited practice today doesn’t guarantee he will be back for Week 7, it’s a big step in the right direction. Mitchell had nine catches for 123 yards in his first two appearances this year. If he’s able to return this week, he would at least earn a spot on the WR3/4 border versus the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) will not play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: It was reported earlier this week that Mitchell underwent a “small procedure” on the finger he injured in practice ahead of Week 3. Given that news, it doesn’t come as much of a surprise to learn that Mitchell will miss his fourth straight game with the injury. With rookie Omar Cooper Jr. set to play in his first game since Week 1, Mitchell could face additional competition for targets when he finally returns to the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell underwent a “small procedure” on his hand.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: As expected, he did not practice today. Per Glenn, Mitchell remains week to week. This explains the lengthy absence for Mitchell, who hasn’t played since injuring his finger in practice ahead of Week 3. According to Glenn, Mitchell is moving his fingers around well, which is hopefully a sign that he will be back soon. With Omar Cooper Jr.'s practice window now open, Mitchell could return to a rather crowded receiver room once he is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker (groin) is out for Week 10’s game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Walker sat out Friday’s practice with a tight groin and was officially listed as questionable for Week 10’s game against the Falcons. Now Schultz is reporting the 26-year-old running back has been ruled out. Once that becomes official, Emmett Johnson moves into the low-end RB1 mix in a plus matchup against Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Kenneth Walker (groin) is questionable for Kansas City’s Week 10 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Not much of a surprise after he sat out Friday with what Andy Reid called a “tight groin.” This has officially waded into “we’ll see” territory over the weekend. Emmett Johnson would be a low-end RB1 with a good workload if Walker is ruled out ahead of Sunday’s games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Kenneth Walker sat out Friday’s practice with a tight groin.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Reid added “we’ll see how he feels through this afternoon, with rehab, and through tomorrow.” Not exactly a glowing endorsement for Walker playing, though we expect the injury report later today to at least read questionable. If Walker were unable to go, Emmett Johnson would probably find himself with a low-end RB1 workload against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Ken Walker had 18 rushes for 102 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets, adding four catches for 41 yards and two touchdowns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Walker sliced through a low-energy Jets defense time and again in the first half. He was more involved than usual in the pass game, taking over as KC’s primary pass catcher out of the backfield after Emmett Johnson’s big PPR performance in Week 8 against Denver. Walker would have likely had a bigger day if the Chiefs hadn’t benched their starters in the fourth quarter, up my multiple scores. This was Walker’s third multi-touchdown performance of the 2026 season, and it marks the fourth time this season he’s had at least four receptions in a game. Walker will remain a high-end fantasy play in Week 10 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Kenneth Walker rushed 21 times for 69 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos, adding four catches for 15 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Emmett Johnson stole the show today with 128 yards and a touchdown on five receptions. Johnson blew by the Broncos’ defense for a 73-yard touchdown, which alone would have been enough for a breakout performance. The good news for Walker drafters is that Johnson only carried the ball once. Walker also matched him in targets at five apiece. Walker is now coming off his two worst rushing performances of the year in tandem with the Chiefs’ first two losses. It’s safe to assume the two are related. With a down-bad Jets defense on deck, we fully expected Walker to get back on track as a top-end RB1 in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Kenneth Walker rushed 14 times for 36 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 7 loss to the Seahawks, adding 21 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Walker was held to below 4.9 yards per carry for only the second time this season while also failing to find the end zone for the second time through six games, with his longest rush going for a meager seven yards. Seattle had all the answers on the defensive side of the ball as they held the Chiefs to just 213 yards of total offense. One of fantasy’s breakout stars in the early going of the 2026 season will face another difficult matchup on the road against the Broncos in Week 8, where he remains an elite RB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Ken Walker had 19 rushes for 128 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers, adding two catches for 11 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: The Chiefs once again leaned hard on the rushing attack, running the ball 24 times while attempting 30 passes on the day. Walker breezed through a lifeless LA defense from start to finish. On many of his carries Walker was not touched until he was five or six yards beyond the line of scrimmage. Walker, who accounted for 19 of the team’s 24 rushing attempts, is perhaps the most important player in fantasy football through Week 6. He’ll be an RB1 in Week 7 against his former mates in Seattle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Kenneth Walker rushed 22 times for 177 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs’ Week 4 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Walker found the end zone twice in 19 seconds in this one. After scoring on a two-yard run in the fourth quarter, Walker then broke free for a 22-yard run on his next play after the Chiefs recovered a fumbled kickoff by the Raiders. Walker’s longest run of the game was an explosive burst down the right sideline that saw him pick up 76 yards, but he was tackled at the Raiders eight-yard line and lost out on a scoring opportunity two plays later when Tyquan Thornton came down in the end zone with an eight-yard reception. Walker has now scored multiple touchdowns in three of four games this season and has 621 yards from scrimmage and seven total touchdowns. He’s been more than fantasy managers could have hoped for through the first four weeks, but they will have to manage without him next week as the Chiefs enter their bye week. He’ll be firmly in the RB1 mix in Week 6, however, when the Chiefs play host to the winless Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Kenneth Walker rushed 18 times for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins, adding two receptions for three yards and a second score.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: The two-touchdown outing was Walker’s second in three games as a Chief after he had only one such effort for the Seahawks last season. His 20 touches were a rather remarkable total seeing as the Chiefs were limited to 49 plays with the Dolphins attempting to play keep away. He was not efficient, but Patrick Mahomes was. That’s the new reality for defenses facing the Chiefs, as this is no longer a stop Mahomes at all costs team. You now have to pick your poison, which is going to lead to many more blow-up efforts for KWIII. Perhaps that will include Week 4 in Vegas against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said RB Emmett Johnson “will continue to get more snaps.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Johnson has turned 14 touches into 103 scrimmage yards thus far. Evidently pleased with his fifth-round rookie, Reid wants to keep “allowing Emmett to grow,” in turn taking “a little bit of load off” starting RB Kenneth Walker. Reid notes that Walker wants the ball on every play and is not asking for a lighter workload, but Reid is seeking “a nice balance with those two in there,” which “keeps them even more fresh as the season goes on.” Walker, of course, remains an elite RB1. Johnson, however, should be rostered in all 12-team leagues as a high-upside bench stash that could return standalone value before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Saints plan to activate Travis Etienne (hamstring) from injured reserve ahead of Week 10’s game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne practiced in full this week and now Pelissero reports he’s in line to return against the Panthers in Week 10. The 27-year-old running back deserves FLEX consideration in a plus matchup against Carolina, though he could be on a snap count in his first game in over a month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Travis Etienne (hamstring) is questionable for New Orleans’ Week 10 game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: He did practice again today, finally hitting a full session, so he at least has cleared a full week of practices if nothing else. If Etienne does play he could be a reasonable FLEX option. There are reports that he could be on a snap count if he does play, and that mixes with the early-season usage to create a situation that isn’t necessarily guaranteed to smash. That said, the Panthers are an enticing matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Travis Etienne (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne is firmly in the questionable camp for the Saints’ Week 10 game against the Panthers. New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill believes that the Saints would keep Etienne on a snap count if he makes his return this weekend, noting “they took it easy” on Jordyn Tyson, who returned from a lengthy hamstring injury last week. If active, Etienne likely warrants low-end RB2 treatment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Travis Etienne (hamstring) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Coming off injured reserve, Etienne can practice for 21 days before the Saints must officially either activate him or shut him down. The Saints’ No. 1 running back has been sidelined since unsuccessfully trying to play through a hamstring strain in Week 3 against the Raiders. Audric Estime could warrant RB2/FLEX treatment again this week if Etienne is not ready to face the Panthers on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said the team is still deciding when it will open Travis Etienne’s (hamstring) 21-day return window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne hasn’t played since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3 against the Raiders. The 27-year-old back will need to have his 21-day return window opened before he can take the practice field, so we’ll see if Moore and the staff elect to designate him for a return ahead of Wednesday’s practice. Until that happens, Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller, and CJ Donaldson will continue to operate as the Saints’ top options, with Kamara the likely leader in what has been an underwhelming backfield this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints placed Travis Etienne on injured reserve with a hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: This is a tough break. The Saints’ high-priced free agent signee will be sidelined for at least four games. Their Week 8 bye makes him eligible to return in Week 9. Veteran RB Alvin Kamara is the next man up, followed by RB Kendre Miller. Both should be rostered in 12-team leagues. Kamara will likely get the first crack at the starting job, but he has struggled to play efficiently this season, and coach Kellen Moore gave RB CJ Donaldson the backfield’s first green zone touch last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) “will miss time” and that a timeline for his return has not yet been determined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: It’s unclear how much time Etienne will miss, but it wouldn’t be surprising if this became an injured reserve stint. Alvin Kamara could find himself in a more elevated role next week, perhaps with Kendre Miller joining him in a committee. Etienne exited Week 3’s loss to the Raiders with the injury after rushing for 57 yards on 13 carries. It had already been a tough scene for Etienne-reliant fantasy managers this year just based on how the results on the field were going; this won’t help.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints RB Travis Etienne exited Week 3 against the Raiders after suffering an apparent hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne entered the game with a hamstring injury and appears to have aggravated it on an explosive run. The Saints’ starting running back broke off a 16-yard gain in the third quarter, setting up a Saints passing touchdown on the following play. Etienne could be seen grabbing at his left hamstring at the end of the run. He had mostly been limited to modest single-digit gains before that, rushing 13 times for 57 yards and catching 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards on the day. He seems highly unlikely to return. Etienne and the other veteran running backs notably ceded the first backfield touch inside the green zone to RB CJ Donaldson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: We do not yet know today’s participation level, but Etienne logged two limited sessions to begin the week. Hopefully, we get a report pre-game revealing the injury’s severity, so we can better assess his potential usage. Given the Saints’ prior backfield workload splits and Etienne’s soft-tissue strain, he should probably be viewed as a low-end RB2/FLEX starter right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne remains limited, which keeps him in the questionable camp for the Saints’ Week 3 game against the Raiders. Saints RB3 Kendre Miller was sidelined by an illness, but those rarely impact NFL players’ availability on game day. Veteran RB Alvin Kamara should be rostered wherever he is available.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Packers RB Josh Jacobs (finger) underwent successful surgery on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Jacobs had surgery on his fractured right ring finger Friday in Los Angeles, according to Pelissero. The 28-year-old running back is expected to return in the next few weeks. In the meantime, Kaleb Johnson is the only usable Packers running back for fantasy purposes. He’s an RB3/FLEX play against the Vikings in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Josh Jacobs (finger) could miss 2-3 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: In other words, the Packers might avoid placing Jacobs on injured reserve with his surgically-repaired finger. While he’s sidelined — including in Week 10 against the Vikings — some combination of Pierre Strong, Chris Brooks, Kaleb Johnson, and MarShawn Lloyd will handle backfield duties for the pass-heavy Packers. Johnson served as the nominal lead back in Week 9 against the Patriots, while Brooks is returning from injury and should slot in as the team’s pass-catching back. Johnson can be played as a touchdown-dependent RB3 option this week against a Minnesota defense that has shown recent vulnerabilities to the run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed Josh Jacobs will undergo surgery on his fractured finger and didn’t rule out a stint on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: LaFleur confirmed previous reports that Jacobs will undergo surgery, but it sounds like he could be at risk of missing more than the three-week “maximum” that was reported. LaFleur not only said a stint on injured reserve was possible, but also noted that Jacobs playing through the injury was never an option, saying he “had no grip strength.” We don’t yet know when Jacobs will undergo his surgery, but LaFleur did confirm that it will be some time this week. With Jacobs now sidelined for the foreseeable future, Green Bay will look to MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong, and Kaleb Johnson to lead the backfield heading into Week 10 against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Josh Jacobs will undergo surgery on his fractured finger and “is expected to miss a maximum of three weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Less than 24 hours after it was reported that the team would see if Jacobs could play through his fractured finger, they have now opted for surgery. The decision to say Jacobs could be out “a maximum of three weeks” suggests he will avoid the injured reserve and that this will be more of a week-to-week thing, and that he could return before the end of the month. Jacobs has totaled 148 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns on 47 touches since returning from the Commissioner’s Exempt list. Now, the Packers will likely take a bit of a committee approach in the weeks ahead and could lean more on Kaleb Johnson, who was solid against the Patriots (14-68-1), with Jacobs and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) both sidelined. That said, all Packers running backs will be hard to trust as anything more than desperation dart throws in Week 10 when they take on a stout Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Josh Jacobs suffered a fractured finger in the Packers’ Week 9 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Jacobs exited early in the first quarter after his finger got caught in a defender’s facemask while he attempted a stiff arm. While he was never officially ruled out, Jacobs never returned to the field and was instead on the sideline in full uniform. According to Schneidman, the Packers plan to find a way for Jacobs to play through the injury, but he was unable to return in this one. Although, to be fair, he also wasn’t needed, as the Packers’ offense was in control throughout the evening. We assume Jacobs would see close to a normal workload if he is active for Week 10 against the Vikings, meaning fantasy manager can treat him as a strong RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Josh Jacobs (hand) is questionable to return in Week 9 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: This news comes from the official team account. It was hard to tell when Jacobs suffered the injury, but star running back could be seen jogging to the locker room with trainers late in the first quarter. Jacobs leaves the game with five rushing yards on four carries and will be replaced by Pierre Strong with MarShawn Lloyd (knee) being inactive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: ESPN’s Rob Demovsky reports Josh Jacobs is “operating under the assumption” he won’t miss more games despite additional allegations of abuse against him.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Jacobs is facing additional allegations of verbal and physical abuse that could jeopardize his playing status moving forward. He told Demovsky that he is “operating under the assumption that he won’t have to sit out any more games than the six he already missed while on the NFL commissioner exempt list.” Jacobs has defended himself against the allegations after his attorneys also dismissed the claims. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said earlier this week he expects Jacobs to remain on the roster as the league reviews this round of allegations. Jacobs has missed six games on the Commissioner’s Exempt List and will continue to play while the NFL looks into the new claims.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said he expects Josh Jacobs to remain on the roster while the league investigates multiple allegations of domestic violence against him.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: This doesn’t come as much of a surprise, given that NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported on Sunday that Jacobs is “going to continue to play” while the league reviews this latest round of allegations. The league is not only reviewing these latest allegations, but is also looking into whether or not Jacobs was “upfront” with them about the initial allegations that led to him being placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt list. Barring an unexpected development this week, we would expect Jacobs to be on the field against the Patriots this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Josh Jacobs is “going to continue to play, but it is possible that he gets a suspension” at the end of the league’s investigation into several claims of domestic violence against him.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: A public records request revealed three additional accusations of domestic violence against Jacobs over the weekend. That is on top of the initial incident in which Jacobs ultimately pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property. The NFL put out a statement saying they will continue to look into Jacobs’ situation. Even though Jacobs was removed from the Commissioner’s Exempt List two weeks ago, the league’s investigation was still ongoing. Rapoport notes that the league is also looking into whether Jacobs was “upfront” with them about his disturbing legal situation. Of note, Jacobs’ team pushed to have video of the most recent incident sealed from public access while the league actively sought to have it released. Rapoport makes it sound like it may take some time for a suspension to be announced, but it’s more likely than not that Jacobs is suspended because of the most recent revelations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: NBC 26 Northeast Wisconsin reports “newly released records show additional women contacted the Hobart/Lawrence (Wisconsin) Police Department to report alleged physical incidents involving Josh Jacobs.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: The Wisconsin television station received “heavily redacted” police reports on Friday evening, though they included allegations from three other women. There are multiple extremely disturbing allegations of physical violence. One alleged incident took place in January 2022. The accuser “contacted investigators in June after learning about the May investigation, telling police the allegations sounded similar to her prior experience with Jacobs.” She also said the incident had “never been reported to law enforcement, (and that she) contacted police when she believed her alleged experience with Jacobs could be relevant to the case.” The allegations highlight the folly of the NFL’s apparent wish that the situation would just go away. It has not, and now it is quite possible, if not likely, that Jacobs ends up suspended for the remainder of the 2026 season. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: New Orleans Football’s Mike Triplett reports that the Saints had Jordyn Tyson work with doctors at the University of Wisconsin to address his recurring hamstring issues.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson has dealt with recurring hamstring injuries since October 2025, and was most recently sidelined by a hamstring strain suffered on August 13th. According to Triplett, the Saints sent Tyson to be evaluated by Dr. Heiderscheit and his team, which received a $4 million research grant from the NFL in 2021 to study hamstring issues, twice during his three-month rehab program. Dr. Heiderscheit successfully treated Packers WR Christian Watson’s recurring hamstring injuries in 2024. According to Triplett, the specialists “determined that something was a little small” in Tyson’s hamstring fascia, which allowed the Saints’ training staff to update Tyson’s exercise regimen with needed alterations. Per Tyson, the changes have allowed the tissue “to fire better.” Given Dr. Heiderscheit’s track record, Tyson’s odds of remaining healthy for the rest of the season are trending upward. He warrants WR3/FLEX treatment at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Jordyn Tyson should get “a healthy dose more” snaps in Week 10 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Moore adds that the Saints will continue to increase Tyson’s usage over time, “to a point where he’s not limited.” This is great to read. Tyson isn’t even listed on the Saints’ injury report this week. He earned four targets on 16 snaps last week and should be expected to increase his workload this week, potentially to a FLEX-worthy level.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyn Tyson caught 4-of-5 targets for 30 yards in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson was activated from injured reserve over the weekend and made his NFL debut today. He got off to a nightmare start by fumbling his first career reception inside the five-yard line. The Saints didn’t go away from him after the rookie mistake and rotated him onto the field rather sporadically for the rest of the game. He was deployed as the team’s WR3, running 16 routes compared to 44 for Devaughn Vele. Those two numbers should converge in the coming weeks, but it might take some time for Tyson to overtake Vele as the team’s WR2. He will be a high-risk FLEX play for Week 10 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is active for Week 9 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson will make his NFL debut after missing the first two months of the year with a hamstring injury. We’re expecting a snap count for him this week, making him an extremely risky FLEX play. Inactive for the Saints are QB Zach Wilson, S Mike Reid, RB C.J. Donaldson, DT Christen Miller, LB Jaylan Ford, OL Mason Murphy, and DL John Ridgeway III.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports Saints WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) “should be good to go” against the Browns in Week 9.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: The oft-injured Tyson hurt his hamstring in training camp and is yet to make his NFL debut. According to Schultz, he should be good to go Sunday against the Browns. A limited participant in practice throughout the week, it’s unclear how much Tyson might play in his first game. Eventually, though, he should settle in as the Saints’ WR2 behind Chris Olave. Tyson’s return also puts a damper on the fantasy prospects of Devaughn Vele and Juwan Johnson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: We do not yet know Tyson’s participation level at Friday’s practice, but he remained limited on Wednesday and Thursday. It seems like he may need another week before he makes his NFL debut, but we don’t know for sure. If active, Tyson would be FLEX-viable. It is possible the team initially keeps him on a snap count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: The Saints’ first-round rookie is now on the wrong side of questionable. It would have been nice to see him practice in full today. That said, New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill commented positively on Tyson’s performance, saying Tyson “does not look limited.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints designated Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson aggravated his nagging hamstring late in the offseason and was placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 1. He will practice for the first time today. NewOrleans.Football’s Nick Underhill said it’s possible Tyson plays this week, though he immediately mentioned a potential snap count for the rookie. The Saints likely want to ramp Tyson up slowly to avoid another setback. He was limited in Wednesday’s session. Tyson should be stashed in every fantasy format, but managers can’t count on him as even a FLEX play for at least one more week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said the team is still deciding when it will open Jordyn Tyson’s (hamstring) 21-day return window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: When Tyson landed on injured reserve, the initial belief was that he would return sometime after the Saints’ bye week. Whether that is in Week 9 or the coming weeks is still to be determined, but we wouldn’t expect him to take the field the same week the team opens his return window. That said, opening that window for a return is the first step in getting Tyson back on the field. If he takes the field Wednesday, Tyson would then have 21 days to practice before the team would need to officially activate him from injured reserve. We could still be a few weeks away from seeing the the rookie first-rounder in action, but hopefully we get an encouraging update on his progression this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints general manager Mickey Loomis said Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) won’t practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Loomis said Tyson is “improving” in his long rehab from a major preseason hamstring injury. Tyson, who traveled with the Saints to France for their Week 7 game against the Steelers, could still be a couple weeks away as the team takes a cautious approach to his recovery. In the meantime, Bryce Lance will operate as the Saints’ No. 2 wideout behind Chris Olave. Lance over the past two weeks has a 13 percent target share and a 20 percent air yards share in the pass-first New Orleans offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.headline: Seahawks ruled out Leonard Williams (stinger) for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.analysis: The Seahawks’ defense should be fine without him against a Cardinals offense now led by rookie QB Carson Beck. The Seahawks will have LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) and OG Anthony Bradford (knee) on the field this week, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.headline: Charles Cross (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.analysis: Cross and LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) were both limited at today’s practice, giving them a chance to play on Sunday against the Cardinals. Seahawks stud DT Leonard Williams (stinger) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.headline: Leonard Williams (stinger) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.analysis: Williams missed last week due to a stinger and continues to be sidelined. He will need to practice in some fashion to have a chance at playing in Week 10 against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Quenton Nelson (knee) will have a minor procedure and is week-to-week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.analysis: Apparently, Nelson was dealing with this knee issue when Seattle acquired for him, and he recently “aggravated it to some degree.” FOX 59’s Mike Chappell notes that Nelson was never listed on the Colts’ injury report this season. This is a bummer for the Seahawks, who acquired Nelson as a win-now move. Nelson will not play in Week 9 against the Cardinals, and the Seahawks also ruled out LT Charles Cross (ankle), DT Leonard Williams (stinger) and LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.headline: Leonard Williams (stinger) did not practice in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.analysis: Williams suffered a stinger in Week 8 and was an estimated DNP for the Seahawks’ walkthrough practice on Wednesday. The veteran will need to practice in some capacity to have a chance to play in Week 9 against the Cardinals. If not, the Seahawks’ interior defensive line will be reinforced by Mike Morris, who notched his first career sack against the Bears in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.headline: Seahawks DT Leonard Williams (ankle)is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 5 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.analysis: The Seahawks will have their stud interior defender on hand against the division-rival 49ers. They will be without backup CB Julian Neal (hamstring), who suffered an injury in practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.headline: Seahawks signed Leonard Williams to a three-year, $90 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.analysis: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler was first on the news, followed by contract details from Ian Rapoport. Seattle acquired Williams from the Giants during the 2023 season. In his two full seasons as a Seahawk, Williams has totaled 18 regular season sacks plus one during the team’s postseason last year. He is now one of the five highest-paid defensive tackles on an annual basis. Williams will be under contract through the 2029 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.headline: Seahawks restructured Leonard Williams’ contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.analysis: According to Seahawks beat writer Corbin Smith, the team converted $18.745 million of Williams’ 2025 salary into a bonus while tacking on two void years to the end of his deal. The move freed up just over $14 million in cap space for the Seahawks, who will still need to make additional moves to get under the cap before the start of next season. Williams is coming off one of his best years as a pro after totaling 64 tackles, 11 sacks, and a career-high 16 TFLs in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.headline: Seahawks EDGE Leonard Williams did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.analysis: Williams popped up on the practice report with a new foot injury, listed as a non-participant for Wednesday. He has 2.5 sacks starting eight games on the Seahawks’ defensive line this season. LB Boye Mafe (knee) was limited in practice as the Seahawks get out of the bye trying to get their defense healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.headline: Seahawks LB Boye Mafe (knee) is questionable for Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.analysis: Seahawks S Julian Love (thigh) is also questionable, though multiple defenders appear ready to return. LB Jerome Baker (hamstring), LB Uchenna Nwosu (knee), EDGE Leonard Williams (ribs) and LB Derick Hall (hip) enter the game without injury designations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki sat out on Wednesday and Thursday before practicing in a limited capacity on Friday. He remains a worthwhile stash as the Lions’ No. 2 running back. His backup, Jacob Saylors (neck/hamstring), is good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki played through the injury last week, and should be expected to do so again against the Patriots this week. Fellow backup RB Jacob Saylors (neck/hamstring) is practicing in full. Vaki is the team’s top backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is active for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: No surprises here as this was reported earlier today. St. Brown remains a top-flight WR1 for his matchup with the Phins. Sione Vaki is also active and will serve as the team’s RB2. Inactive for the Lions are CB D.J. Reed, EDGE DJ Wonnum, C Cade Mays, RB Jacob Saylors, TE Jordan Meeks, DL Mekhi Wingo, and EDGE Ahmed Hassanein.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) is questionable for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki and Lions RB3 Jacob Saylors (neck) are both questionable. Vaki did not practice on Friday, having apparently suffered a new injury. Saylors was limited all week. Jahmyr Gibbs should handle his normal, sizable workload.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Sione Vaki had 11 rushes for 65 yards in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings, adding one catch for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: It was the first time this year Vaki has seen more than six carries. The Lions went ultra run-heavy in this one to combat the Vikings’ vexing blitz scheme, which led to 35 carries on the day. Vaki should be stashed in most formats in cae Jahmyr Gibbs misses any time in the coming weeks. Vaki would be a potential 20-touch weekly option in such a scenario.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: A DNP to open the week would normally be concerning, but Dan Campbell told reporters earlier today that he was going to get a lot of players “off their feet” during today’s practice. Gibbs appeared to injure his leg while awkwardly sliding to the ground on his final carry of Week 7. The fact that he isn’t listed with a leg injury on today’s report is also a good sign. Sione Vaki is the next man up if Gibbs can’t play this week, but we aren’t overly concerned quite yet. Tomorrow’s injury report will be more telling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Isiah Pacheco (back) could return in early December.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: According to Rapoport, Pacheco “had surgery to remove a body that was pressing on a nerve in his back.” The 27-year-old back is looking at a 12-week recovery, but if all goes well, he could return for the final month of the season. If the Lions don’t add anybody to their backfield in the coming days/weeks, Sione Vaki and Jacob Saylors will continue to serve as the primary backups behind Jahmyr Gibbs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Lions HC Dan Campbell said Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki could both push for RB2 touches behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: It’s hard to imagine either Vaki or Saylors having meaningful fantasy value at this point in the season, but it sounds like both will be on the field while Isiah Pacheco (back) is sidelined for at least the first four games of the season. Judging by how Campbell sounded when discussing each player, it sounded like Saylors might be closer to the official RB2, but Campbell didn’t mince words when he said, “I see Vaki getting some reps, too.” Fantasy managers interested in taking a shot on a Lions running back not named Jahmyr Gibbs can consider both Saylors and Vaki as late-round dart throws until we see how their snap shares look in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: The Athletic’s Colton Pouncy believes Sione Vaki has an opportunity to cut into Isiah Pacheco’s touches.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki was “quietly putting together an excellent training camp last year when healthy” per Pouncy and the 2024 fourth-round pick could cut into Pacheco’s touches if Pacheco continues to not look like the 2022-2023 vintage. Vaki has just seven carries in his first two seasons in the league, but has been active 27 games as a core special teams contributor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Lions declared RB Sione Vaki, LB Zach Cunningham, OL Equakun Kingsley, DL Mekhi Wingo, and DL Chris Smith inactive for Week 4 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki has missed each of the Lions’ first four games with a groin injury. He did not practice this week and does not appear to be close to returning.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown was listed as questionable in Week 9 after practicing in a limited capacity all week. He managed to suit up on game day, posting an 8/86 receiving line. He was limited in all three practices this week and once again got hit with the questionable tag. We expect him to play. He should be treated as a WR1, as usual, assuming he is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: He played through this last week, managing an 8/86 line against the Dolphins. We’d be surprised if he wasn’t removed from the injury report tomorrow after getting in two limited sessions on Wednesday and Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown played through the injury without issue last week, catching eight passes for 86 yards. The Lions’ No. 1 wide receiver should be treated as a WR1, as usual, against the Patriots in this week’s international game. St. Brown will likely upgrade to full participation on Thursday or Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 8-of-10 targets for 86 yards in the Lions’ Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown was questionable for today’s game with a rib issue. You wouldn’t know it by his usage. He ran circles around the rest of the Lions’ pass-catchers with a 38 percent target share. He led the team in yards from scrimmage and accounted for just shy of half the team’s passing production. St. Brown remains a strong WR1 option ahead of his Week 10 game against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is active for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: No surprises here as this was reported earlier today. St. Brown remains a top-flight WR1 for his matchup with the Phins. Sione Vaki is also active and will serve as the team’s RB2. Inactive for the Lions are CB D.J. Reed, EDGE DJ Wonnum, C Cade Mays, RB Jacob Saylors, TE Jordan Meeks, DL Mekhi Wingo, and EDGE Ahmed Hassanein.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is expected to play in Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown was limited in practice throughout the week. He has a knack for getting it out through injuries and will do so again today. Even at less than full strength, St. Brown shouldn’t face much resistance from Miami’s weak secondary. He remains a top-end WR1 for his Week 9 game in South Beach.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown rarely misses games due to injuries. Fantasy managers should remain optimistic about his availability. The Lions’ No. 1 wide receiver remained limited all week. Although it might hurt to take hits, we expect St. Brown to suit up this weekend. Regardless, keeping it locked to Rotoworld is a must. Updates will be provided as they roll in.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: It’d be nice to see the Sun God get in a full session, but the fact that the star wideout has been able to practice both days suggest he’ll be just fine for Week 9 against the Dolphins. He’ll be a high-end WR1 for that game and any other contest that St. Brown plays in.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown briefly left the Lions’ Week 8 win over the Vikings but managed to finish the game. A limited session today means the rib injury should be a non-issue by Sunday. The Lions should have no issues picking apart Miami’s atrocious defense this week. Per usual. St. Brown will be a high-end WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 7-of-8 targets for 46 yards in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown added ten yards on a carry, which was actually a running catch on a play in which St. Brown lined up fifteen yards behind the line of scrimmage and got a running start like you might see in the CFL. He had a touchdown catch called back in the first half and had to go to the locker room with what looked to be a knee issue. It was only the second time this season St. Brown was held to less than 60 yards. He came into Week 8 ranked fourth in expected fantasy points per game. St. Brown takes on the Dolphins in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Dont’e Thornton (back) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton’s injury woes continue. The young wide receiver spent much of the year on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. He had a back injury last week, and now another back injury threatens his availability. Thornton does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats, though he provides the team with a downfield element when active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders activated WR Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: It was his last possible day to be reinstated in his 21-day window. The fact that Klint Kubiak spent much of Thornton’s 21-day window talking about how he had to go show us something makes us think Thornton will probably just be a depth piece for the time being. The Raiders waived Jonah Laulu to make room for Thornton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) has “got to go show us something” in the final week of his 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: This is rough. Currently on injured reserve, Thornton began practicing in Week 5, activating his 21-day practice window. The young wide receiver told reporters that he was “overly confident” in his hamstring and is “ready to play.” Two weeks later, the team has not yet officially removed him from injured reserve. Per Kubiak, Thornton “had a good first week, had a good second week,” but he still has to go “out there to practice to show us that he’s ready.” He’s been practicing in full for two weeks. The fact that the wide receiver-needy Raiders have not yet activated him is not encouraging. Thornton does not need to be stashed in 12-team leagues at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Dont’e Thornton Jr. (hamstring) is getting “closer” but won’t play in Las Vegas’ Week 6 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton is in Week 2 of his 21-day window and figures to return in Week 7 or Week 8. Obviously there’s not much reason to trust him in fantasy at this time, but he may find a real role on Las Vegas’ depth chart.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders ruled out Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) for Week 5 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: The Raiders activated Thornton’s 21-day practice window this week. Despite the young wide receiver saying he feels “ready to play,” the team has determined that he needs more time. With Jalen Nailor (concussion) also ruled out, Cody White (ankle) and Malik Benson will round out three-wide receiver sets behind Tre Tucker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders WR Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) returned to practice and feels “ready to play.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton has been on injured reserve since late August, practicing in full for the first time on Wednesday. He told Raiders media that he is “overly confident” in his hamstring and is “ready to play.” With Jack Bech on injured reserve, there is room for the 23-year-old speedster to earn targets if he plays in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said it’s too early to say whether WR Dont’e Thornton Jr. (undisclosed) will resume practicing next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: The lanky speedster was placed on injured reserve late in August. He is not exceptionally talented, but he can contribute meaningfully to an NFL offense. Getting him back would help keep safeties honest. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders placed WR Dont’e Thornton Jr. on the reserved/injured list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton has been dealing with an undisclosed injury that has prevented the wideout from practicing over the last month. The 23-year-old can return in four weeks, but there’s no timeline as to when the 2025 fourth-round pick will return to the Vegas lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said Dont’e Thornton is still working his way back from an undisclosed injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: We still don’t know what Thornton is dealing with, but the second-year receiver hasn’t practiced since August 7th. Kubiak said earlier this month that he expected Thornton to return sometime during the preseason, but that didn’t come to fruition. Even if he’s able to make it back on the practice field ahead of Week 1, Thornton is unlikely to make any major contributions to the offense at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said he expects Dont’e Thornton (undisclosed) to return at some point in the preseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton has missed nearly a whole week of practice, paving the way for Jack Bech and rookie Malik Benson to see more reps. Kubiak said Thornton has “been banged up a little bit” this training camp, but did not go into further detail on his situation. Thornton caught 10 passes for 135 scoreless yards last season after generating plenty of camp hype. He is not on the fantasy radar at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane should have no issue playing against the Chargers on Monday night, nor should S Kyle Hamilton (hip), who has practiced in full in each of the last two days. Having Ioane on the field will be a big help for Jacoby Brissett in his first start for Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens’ stud rookie guard is on track to play this week, albeit with a new shoulder issue. Running backs Rasheen Ali (ankle) and Adam Randall (neck/hamstring) are practicing in full. They should play as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens did not activate Adam Randall (neck) from injured reserve for Week 9 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens’ rookie running back will have to wait to make his debut. The Ravens declared QB Kedon Slovis, WR Elijah Sarratt, OL Emery Jones Jr., DL Aeneas Peebles, CB Nate Wiggins and S Jaylinn Hawkins inactive. Hawkins is dealing with a knee injury and Wiggins, the Ravens’ No. 1 cornerback, is listed with a stinger and an illness. Slovis will serve as the emergency third quarterback. Austin Reed is the QB2. Ravens RG Vega Ioane (knee) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens declared WR Elija Sarratt FS Jaylinn Hawkins, CB Chandler Rivers, OG Emery Jones, OG Vega Ioane, DT Aeneas Peebles, and QB Joe Fagnano inactive for Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens will be without rookie guard Vega Ioane, who suffered a knee injury in last week’s loss to the Bengals. While it’s yet another blow to an already banged-up offensive line, the Ravens do have Lamar Jackson returning from his three-game absence after he suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 4. Hopefully, Jackson’s return can provide a much-needed spark to an offense that has managed just 23 points combined in its last two games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Vega Ioane (knee) won’t play in Baltimore’s Week 8 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane got in limited sessions on Thursday and Friday but was evasive when asked if he’d go at his locker yesterday. In the end, it would have been very impressive for him to play through a sprained MCL one week later. Ioane’s practice augurs well for his chances of playing in Week 10, at the very least. Week 9, on Thursday Night, might be too big of an ask.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Roquan Smith (knee) and Vega Ioane (knee) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Both players missed practice Wednesday, with their return Thursday a good step in the right direction for their availability in a marquee matchup against the Bills in Week 8. Quarterback Lamar Jackson and safety-linebacker Kyle Hamilton were also present at practice Thursday as the team inches closer to full strength.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said he is not ruling out Vega Ioane (knee) for Week 8 against the Bills yet.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens’ mauling rookie guard suffered an MCL sprain in Week 7 against the Bengals. He is likely on the wrong side of questionable for Week 8, but Minter said he has been impressed by Ioane’s resilience and thinks he could recover quickly. In the meantime, OL Emery Jones Jr. and OT Andrew Vorhees will compete for the potential starting role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Vega Ioane suffered an MCL injury and will miss time.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane went down with a knee injury on Sunday against the Bengals and did not return to the game. Though Rapoport said the injury is not considered long term, Ioane — an impressive rookie — will be sidelined for a while. Baltimore’s offensive line ranks 20th in pass block win rate and 19th in run block win rate, according to ESPN.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens OG Vega Ioane (knee) will not return in Week 7 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane exited late in the first quarter of Sunday’s game and was ruled out shortly after halftime. The rookie first-rounder appeared on 16 snaps and has started every game for the Ravens this season, splitting time between right guard and center. He was replaced by Emery Jones.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Ravens C Jovaughn Gwyn (fibula) will miss 2-3 months.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Gwyn went down with a serious leg injury in Week 3 against the Cowboys and will require surgery in the coming days, per Fowler. That will leave Lamar Jackson and the Ravens offense without their starting center for at least the next couple months. Rookie first-round pick Vega Ioane will likely start at center for the Ravens in Week 4. It’s a blow to a Baltimore offensive line that ranks 29th in ESPN’s pass blocking win rate and third in run blocking win rate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (calf) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman is firmly on track to play in the Ravens’ Monday Night Football game against the Chargers. Bateman will provide new QB Jacoby Brissett with a downfield option, but the veteran wide receiver is almost entirely reliant in ripping off one or two big plays, which has proven to be a difficult proposition for him on a weekly basis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (calf) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: The Ravens face the Chargers in Week 10’s Monday Night Football game, theoretically giving Bateman decent odds of suiting up. He does not need to be in starting lineups as a touchdown-dependent FLEX, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: He practiced in full twice on Thursday and Friday. With Ja’Kobi Lane eating into his targets and the Bengals ever-vulnerable through the air by tight ends, Bateman is probably only a deep-league play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman has been playing through this shoulder injury for a while, though he was forced to leave early last week. Bateman should now be expected to play, but he is only a boom-bust FLEX option with Ja’Kobi Lane now back in the lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman left the Ravens’ Week 6 game against the Browns and did not return, though head coach Jesse Minter told reporters on Monday that he was going to be fine. Expect the team to manage his reps in practice this week with an eye on getting him ready for Sunday. Bateman has made a handful of splash plays this year, but his production is low-volume and high-variance. He will be a low-end FLEX option for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said there’s optimism that Rashod Bateman (shoulder) will “be fine.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Sounds like another week of managed reps in practice is ahead for Bateman, but he’ll likely have a reasonable chance to suit up in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) will not return in Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: We’re not quite sure when this injury occurred, but Bateman was dealing with a shoulder injury throughout the week. He was removed from the final injury report on Friday. Bateman’s day ends without a reception on one target.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman was a surprise DNP on Thursday, but got in a full session today. He remains an uninspiring FLEX option against the Browns in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman played through the shoulder injury last week. He was limited yesterday, but coach Jesse Minter said he wasn’t worried. Downgrading to a DNP is not a good sign. Meanwhile, Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is practicing fully this week and could hop right into WR2 duties for the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: We won’t know what Bateman’s injury is until the Ravens drop their first injury report of Week 6 later today, but head coach Jesse Minter wasn’t worried. He downplayed the issue and told reporters he expects Bateman to play this week. Barring a setback, Bateman will remain a deep-cut FLEX option for Week 6 versus the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell (hip) was limited on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell is trending in the right direction for the Chargers’ Week 10 game against the Ravens. The two teams play in this week’s Monday Night Football game. Mitchell is worth stashing in 12-team leagues, but he likely lacks RB2 upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell (hip) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell should be good to go for Week 10’s Monday Night Football game against the Ravens. He and Omarion Hampton seemingly put a little distance between Kimani Vidal in the second half last week, though Mitchell only makes for a shaky bench stash.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell rushed seven times for 33 yards in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans, adding three receptions for 34 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell regularly rotated in and out as a member of the Chargers’ three-player backfield rotation, though he and Omarion Hampton remained far more involved than Kimani Vidal did in the second half. He looks spry as a rusher and receiver, ripping off double-digit gains in both facets of the game. Unfortunately, Mitchell’s biggest contribution was a fumble in enemy territory, which the Texans recovered inside the red zone. Mitchell is just a floor-based FLEX against his former Ravens team next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell had four rushes for six yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams, adding three catches for 17 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell, as usual, was third in rushing attempts, behind Omarion Hampton (9) and Kimani Vidal (8). His three targets led the backfield but didn’t amount to much. With the Bolts’ backfield being split three ways, Mitchell is going to struggle to get anything going without an explosive play or two. He should remain on most waiver wires ahead of Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell had two rushes for four yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell did not catch his only target on the day. He was third among Bolts running backs in pass routes, behind Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal. The sad state of the Chargers offense and injuries to the team’s offensive line make it nearly impossible for Mitchell to post fantasy relevant numbers for now. The Chargers are on bye in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell rushed 6 times for 11 yards in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos while adding three receptions for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: The only positive here was that Mitchell was somewhat involved in the pass game, but it was all of the check-down variety. The injuries to the Los Angeles offensive line just won’t open many holes right now, and even if Mitchell has looked more spry than Omarion Hampton, there’s more risk than reward having him in a lineup right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said he has not lost “any faith” in Omarion Hampton.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: “I don’t see any change in terms of the depth chart at all. I felt I was underutilizing a strength,” McDaniel said about the increased usage of Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal. McDaniel’s statement is good for Hampton in the sense that we know Hampton will retain a reasonable role. And it’s bad because McDaniel is all but confirming the pecking order will remain the same. Expect more low-end RB2/FLEX nonsense from Hampton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell rushed 10 times for 39 yards while catching five passes for 24 yards in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell, Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal were both equally involved in the rushing attack, and that’s not really a compliment to anyone in this group.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: He practiced all three days this week, upgrading to full on Friday, and should be a lower-end FLEX option against a tough Seahawks run defense. The good news for Mitchell is that the proof-of-concept of “the Chargers can’t run block so they should just use someone fast” worked in Week 3. He should see a reasonable amount of touches in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: The Chargers’ speedy RB2 was seen wearing a walking boot after practice on Wednesday, but that didn’t keep him from practicing today. Mitchell scored a touchdown on a red zone carry last week and could continue rotating in against the Seahawks this week. He should be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (shoulder) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris led the team in targets last week, but somehow managed just six yards on three catches. With Ladd McConkey (back) ailing, Harris could lead the team in targets again. He would only be a boom-bust FLEX in this case, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris led the team with seven targets last week, catching just three of them for six yards. Although he is not fantasy-relevant on his own, his presence theoretically helps Justin Herbert and Harris is on track to play in this week’s Monday Night Football game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris caught 3-of-7 targets for six yards in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Being this inefficient ain’t easy. Trainers examined Harris’ lower left leg after an eighth-drive incompletion in which Harris twisted as he unsuccessfully tried to high-point a pass and came down hard on his feet. Harris does not need to be in fantasy football lineups against the Ravens next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre Harris caught all three of his targets for 31 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris was the team’s WR3 behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, as usual. When McConkey is healthy, Harris operates as a part-time player without much of a fantasy floor. He should remain on waiver wires ahead of LA’s Week 9 game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will play in Week 8 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris returns to the lineup after missing Week 6, with the team’s bye week providing enough time for the veteran receiver to get back to the active game-day roster. That doesn’t mean he should be inserted into fantasy lineups after such a slow start to the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris missed Week 6 before the team’s Week 7 bye but could be held out for an additional week given the nature of his injury. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status on the team’s final injury report Friday to gauge the viability of entering him back into lineups for Week 8. Fellow wide receiver Ladd McConkey (concussion) got in his second consecutive full session and should be good to go for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris was labeled week-to-week early in Week 6 and was unable to face the Chiefs that weekend. After resting and rehabbing through the Chargers’ Week 7 bye, Harris has a chance to resume playing in Week 8. We expect to see him listed as a limited participant, but an update will be provided if he practices in full. Brenen Thompson (quad) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 6 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: He did not practice this week and Jim Harbaugh called him “week to week.” Harris stands a chance at returning after Los Angeles’ Week 7 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Tre’ Harris (hamstring) is “more of a week-to-week [thing].”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris will probably have a real chance to play in Week 8, after the Chargers’ Week 7 bye. He thudded to a 16-yard outing in his big chance last week with Quentin Johnston and Ladd McConkey out and doesn’t necessarily need to be rostered if you’re in a bye week crunch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre Harris caught 2-of-4 targets for 16 yards in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris was a complete non-factor even against the depleted Broncos’ secondary. The second-year wideout was the top target with Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston unavailable, and that extra attention didn’t help. Harris will try and bounce back in Week 6 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter got in a limited practice on Friday. He described himself as being at 70 percent health this week. The Cowboys listed DaRon Bland (ankle) and backup S Alijah Clark (illness) as questionable, and ruled out LB Donovan Ezeiruaku (ankle) and S P.J. Locke (concussion). Cowboys LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter reportedly told reporters that his “whole foot is jacked up.” That sounds bad. He was able to run today, and hadn’t in a while, but declined to say whether he will play in Week 10 against the 49ers. We suspect he will sit out this weekend’s contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter Jr. was on the practice field with his helmet on, but he ultimately watched as the rest of the defense went through the session. He was playing through the ankle issue for a while before missing Week 9 against Arizona.
