A DNP today puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 10, but things could change if he manages a limited session on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler Jr. (ankle) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: JPJ was downgraded to a limited participant in Friday before being hit with the questionable tag, causing some concern about his Week 6 availability. It looks like the light practice session may have been a precaution. The newly-minted Cowboys should be good to go versus Green Bay.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) is questionable for Dallas’ Week 6 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter downgraded from full to limited on Friday and wound up with this status despite practicing all three days this week. Peculiar. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson would be better off on Sunday if Porter wasn’t able to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Cowboys declare CB Joey Porter, LB DeMarvion Overshown, CB Cobie Durant, OLB James Houston, OG Ajani Cornelius, OT Drew Shelton and WR Camden Brown inactive for Week 5 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter’s bumpy 2026 campaign takes another surprising turn. The Cowboys’ new cornerback was set to expand his involvement this evening, but he is evidently unable to play due to an illness. Fortunately for the Cowboys, the Buccaneers’ offense is hamstrung by Baker Mayfield’s (thumb) absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter (back/conditioning/contract) is not on the injury report for Week 4 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones said on Friday, “we actually think Joey Porter will get snaps.” ESPN’s Todd Archer notes that prior to the mid-week trade, Porter was ruled out of Thursday’s game between the Steelers and Browns, saying his back was tight. He practiced the last two days “without issue.” Porter might be on a snap count this week, but it looks like he will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports there is “a chance” that Joey Porter Jr. (back/conditioning/contract) plays in Week 4 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter Jr. missed the first three games of the year with a back issue. The Steelers also listed conditioning under his name on the injury report and even took the back injury off entirely at one point. All of that is to say that his absences were ultimately contract-related, which everyone knew in the first place. He was ruled out for Thursday’s game by Pittsburgh, but is eligible to play for the Cowboys this week if they can get him up to speed on the playbook ahead of Sunday’s game. He will likely play on specific packages if he does suit up, but that would still be an upgrade for a banged-up Dallas secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Cowboys “will not be immediately extending Joey Porter Jr.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Schultz added that the plan is to have him play first and “the contract will take care of itself from there.” That’s not exactly what Porter Jr. was looking to get out of this move, but it also points to the fact that his relationship with the Steelers was simply fractured beyond repair. Pittsburgh’s somewhat archaic rules around contract negotiations drove a wedge between them and their star corner. They don’t extend players during the season and, with rare exceptions, they do not guarantee money beyond the first year of a new deal. If Porter Jr. suits up next week and puts a few good games on tape, we suspect the Cowboys will feel comfortable giving him the contract he wanted from the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reports that the Cowboys have acquired Joey Porter Jr. in a trade with the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: In exchange for Porter, the Cowboys will send the Steelers a second-round selection in 2028 as well as a conditional sixth-round pick. Pelissero noted in his blog that trade talks between Dallas and Pittsburgh had picked up over the past few weeks, and the deal will soon become official. Porter has yet to play a snap in 2026 as he has dealt with a back injury, and also a contract dispute. The 26-year-old is one of the more talented corners in football, and Dallas has struggled considerably to stop the pass over the first three weeks. Assuming good health, Porter should be a vast improvement over what the Cowboys have gotten out of their corners to begin 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Cowboys ruled out Jake Ferguson (knee/ankle) for Week 10 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: This was the expected outcome. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters on Monday that Ferguson will likely be out for “multiple weeks” after suffering a knee injury. He was already dealing with an ankle injury when it happened. Ferguson does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: No surprises here as Ferguson is expected to miss multiple weeks, according to Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer. Ferguson was barely putting up TE2 numbers when healthy, so we’re not expecting much from Brevyn Spann-Ford as the next man up. Fantasy managers should aim higher on the waiver wire this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Jake Ferguson (knee) will likely be out “multiple weeks” after going down in Week 9 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: Ferguson exited Sunday’s game against the Colts after taking a nasty hit to his knee. While he was able to walk off under his own power and was later ruled “questionable” to return, the 27-year-old vet never got back into the game. Ferguson has caught just 19 passes for 136 yards and four touchdowns this season, with his best game coming in Week 2 (4-43-2) against the Commanders. Brevyn Spann-Ford, a 2024 UDFA, will likely take over in Ferguson’s absence but shouldn’t be trusted as anything more than a boom-or-bust TE2 at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson (knee) is questionable to return to Week 9 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: The term “questionable” is a vast understatement based on the replay, although the veteran tight end did walk off the field under his own power. The replay and initial reaction from Ferguson did not look good. Expect an update from the team following the game. Ferguson caught both targets for 21 yards and a touchdown prior to departing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle) is ankle for Week 9 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: Ferguson entered the weekend listed as questionable after being unable to practice until Friday, where he logged a limited appearance. That was apparently enough for the veteran tight end to play through the ailment, although Brevyn Spann-Ford could be more involved than normal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle) is listed as questionable for Week 9 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: Ferguson wasn’t able to practice Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to get in a limited session Friday to give him at least a chance to play Friday. Luke Schoonmaker (groin) was also listed as questionable with limited practices all week. If Ferguson is able to play, he’s in the TE2 vicinity against Indianapolis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle) did not participate in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: This makes two straight missed practices for Ferguson because of his ankle injury suffered in Week 8 versus the Cardinals. At this point, it seems unlikely that he’ll be able to play in Week 9 against the Colts, and there are better fantasy options even if he were to be able to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: The Cowboys’ No. 1 tight end suffered an ankle injury in Week 8 against the Cardinals. Ferguson is not in the TE1 ranks even when he is healthy, but his absence could help others earn a couple of extra targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle) left Dallas’ Week 8 game against the Cardinals and is questionable to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: He left in the first quarter. Hopefully his trendlines discouraged you from starting him, if not, we’re afraid it might be a zero for you. He was spotted on the sideline walking off.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson failed to catch his lone target in the Cowboys’ Week 7 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: Ferguson has almost entirely fallen out of favor in the Dallas offense, his snap count over the past two weeks has fallen to just 54.8 percent. He has yet to catch more than four balls, clear 43 yards, or see more than six targets in a game this season, leaving his fantasy value in the dumps when he’s held out of the end zone. Ferguson will be a difficult start despite a glowing matchup against the Cardinals in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) is not on the Cowboys’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens makes his return after sitting out in Week 9. He played through the injury in Week 8, which may have been the wrong decision. The Cowboys’ No. 2 wide receiver encouragingly upgraded from limited to full participation today and can be treated as a WR2 in what should be a high-scoring game against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens is still stuck in the questionable column, though his continued participation is a good sign. The team allowed him to play through the injury in Week 8 against the Cardinals, which was probably the wrong call. He sat out last week despite practicing in a limited capacity. Hopefully, he upgrades to full participation tomorrow. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said George Pickens (hamstring) is expected to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens missed Week 9 with the hamstring issue. He was limited in practice throughout the week, but the team ultimately chose to hold him out for Sunday’s game. We expect one week off to be enough for the veteran wideout. Assuming things go well in practice, Pickens will be back in the WR2 ranks when the Cowboys take on the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) is inactive for Week 9 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens played through the issue last week but will ultimately be held out in Week 9. Tight end Jake Ferguson is active after failing to practice until a limited showing Friday. Ryan Flournoy steps into a featured role for the Cowboys against the inside-funnel Colts defense. Fantasy managers can insert Flournoy into rosters as a viable FLEX considering he leads the team in slot rate through the first half of the season. Also inactive for the Cowboys are LB DeMarvion Overshown, WR KaVontae Turpin, CB Joey Porter Jr., LB Tyrus Wheat, OL Ajani Cornelius, and TE Luke Schoonmaker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Earlier today, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he is “hopeful” that Pickens will be available for this weekend’s game against the Colts. Pickens ended up being limited in practice all week and appears to be truly questionable to play. If active, he is a WR2 against a beatable Colts defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: Speaking on 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said he is “hopeful” George Pickens (hamstring) will play in Week 9 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens has been limited in each of the Cowboys’ first two practices to start the week, which would seem to be a good sign for his Week 9 availability. We’ll get a better sense of where things stand when the Cowboys release their final injury report on Friday and give Pickens a designation heading into the weekend, but Schottenheimer’s optimism is a good sign. Owner Jerry Jones advocated for Pickens getting the ball more this week after Week 8’s loss to the Cardinals, so if he is active, the star receiver could be primed for a bit of a squeaky wheel game in a plus matchup against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) was limited during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens was also limited during Wednesday’s session. The 25-year-old still seems to be on target to play in Week 9 against the Colts, but fantasy managers would obviously like to see Pickens get in a full session before that contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: On the plus side, Pickens is no longer listed with a shoulder injury. Hopefully, Pickens upgrades to full participation tomorrow, and puts this hamstring strain behind him. Team owner Jerry Jones told reporters earlier this week that Pickens needs to get the ball more. The squeaky wheel often gets greased. The Cowboys’ Week 9 game against the Colts looks like a solid bounce-back spot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: Speaking on the Pat McAfee Show, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said “I was told the Dallas Cowboys aren’t trading George Pickens.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Rapoport added that “as of right now, there’s nothing there,” as far as a potential trade is concerned. Pickens, who is playing out the season on the franchise tag, hasn’t produced at the level he did in 2025 when he broke out for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns, but he remains a focal point in the offense despite his underwhelming production. Pickens still ranks 14th in the league among all receivers in targets and is 12th in total air yards. Despite the Cowboys’ disappointing 3-5 record, they remain in the race to win what has been an underwhelming NFC East. With team owner Jerry Jones saying earlier that Pickens needs to be targeted more, it’s safe to assume he will remain with the Cowboys for the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said George Pickens “needs the ball coming in his direction more.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Jones apparently isn’t happy with Pickens’ usage through Week 8. Pickens has been targeted on 22 percent of his pass routes on the season, well below CeeDee Lamb’s 34 percent rate. He’s accounted for 31 percent of the team’s air yards, nearly the same rate he saw in 2025. In the Cowboys’ humiliating Week 8 loss to the Cardinals, Pickens had nine targets, one short of Lamb’s ten. Perhaps Jerry has not adequately studied the spreadsheets. Either way, Pickens remains an upside WR2 headed into Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: Trent Williams (shoulder) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: Williams evidently injured his shoulder during the 49ers’ practice on Thursday, as did LB Dre Greenlaw (knee). 49ers OT Vederian Lowe would be Williams’ replacement if he cannot play. 49ers starting perimeter CBs Renardo Green (back) and Deommodore Lenoir (foot), and slot DB Upton Stout (shoulder) are also questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: 49ers LT Trent Williams (stinger) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: The 49ers will have their stud left tackle active on Sunday. 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw (quad bruise) is questionable to play. 49ers EDGE Nick Bosa (calf) and DL Mykel Williams (knee) have both been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: 49ers LT Trent Williams (stinger) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said earlier this week that Williams was expected to resume practicing today. The fact that he is on track is a good sign for his Week 4 availability. 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw (bruised quad) is still sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: 49ers LT Trent Williams (neck) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: Williams still has a chance to play in Week 4 against the Broncos, and he does not necessarily need to practice. The 49ers could choose to play it conservatively by sitting him until he is fully ready to go, though. We will see how the week unfolds.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said Trent Williams (stinger) “should be good to go by Thursday.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: The 49ers don’t play until Sunday, so we’re assuming Shanahan is referencing when we should first expect Williams to take the practice field this week. Williams suffered what was classified as a stinger in Week 3’s win over the Cardinals, but appears to have avoided any serious injury. Shanahan said the team plans to manage he and LB Dre Greenlaw (quad) throughout the week, and didn’t rule out either player playing in Week 4 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said the team is still gathering information on WR Mike Evans’ (ribs/oblique) injuries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: According to ESPN’s Nick Wagoner, “it was unclear exactly what happened to Evans.” He got hit hard in the sternum on a catch over the middle, but remained in the game for a few plays before needing help from the training staff to get off the field. Shanahan said the team couldn’t tell if Evans broke a rib or injured his oblique, but he believes those questions will be answered tomorrow, indicating Evans will likely undergo imaging. He entered the game with a hip injury. Wagoner adds that LT Trent Williams (stinger) and LB Dre Greenlaw’s (quad) injuries “seemed less severe” than Evans’ injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: Trent Williams (stinger) is questionable to return Week 3 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: Williams left in the third quarter, taking the cart to the 49ers locker room. The veteran left tackle was officially diagnosed with a stinger and is questionable to return. Vederian Lowe is in at left tackle with Williams out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: 49ers listed RB Christian McCaffrey, OT Trent Williams, LB Dre Greenlaw, and EDGE Nick Bosa as resting non-participants for Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: McCaffrey and Williams were listed as DNP simply for rest, while Bosa had a rest/knee designation and Greenlaw had a rest/Achilles designation. This is notable as the 49ers have several key veterans who have dealt with injuries throughout their career and practice reps will be managed for these players, especially coming off a Week 1 in Australia. McCaffrey reportedly dealt with cramps in the 49ers’ Week 1 win over the Rams; though he is not injured, his experiences with Achilles tendinitis will certainly lend to rest days throughout the season. We expect the 49ers to continue to rest veterans in practice throughout the season in an effort to remain healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: 49ers’ OT Trent Williams said Wednesday that he is unsure if he will play beyond 2027.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: Fresh off a two-year contract extension signed in April, Williams enters his 17th season in the league and said 2027 will “probably be his last.” The 12-time Pro Bowl tackle has been a mainstay for the 49ers up front since being acquired prior to the 2020 season, receiving All pro honors in 2021, 2022, and 2023. “I’m toying between the idea of going until I can’t no more and just leaving while I still got some good product left and I get ran out of the league, " Williams said Wednesday. “It’s hard not to compete when you can, so we’ll see.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.headline: 49ers signed Trent Williams to a two-year, $50 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-will.analysis: Williams and the Niners appeared to be at an impasse earlier this offseason after the team opted not to pick up his $10 million option bonus and reporters noted that the 38-year-old was said to be available in trade. Williams had one year left on his old deal, but with his new contract extension, he will be under contract through 2027. Of the $50 million Williams is set to receive, $34 million will be guaranteed. He allowed just four sacks on 32 pressures last season, per PFF, earning a 79.9 PFF pass-blocking grade.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) is not on the 49ers’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: The 49ers could end up limiting Samuel’s snaps in his first game back, but when he is on the field, he will likely be treated as the team’s No. 1 wide receiver. Samuel should be in fantasy football lineups as a WR3 with decent upside in what is expected to be a high-scoring game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel is still stuck in the questionable column, but his continued participation tentatively puts him on track to play in a fantasy-friendly matchup against the Cowboys in Week 10. If active, Samuel could end up serving as the 49ers’ No. 1 wide receiver. He would warrant WR3 treatment in this scenario.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will resume practicing in a limited capacity on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel now has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys’ fantasy-friendly defense. The 49ers could play things cautiously and give him more time off, but an early-week return is usually a good sign. With much of the 49ers’ pass-catching corps still banged up, Samuel could return to a WR3/flex-worthy workload right away. He should be added wherever he is available. Samuel later told reporters that he feels “ready” to play on game day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: 49ers ruled out Deebo Samuel (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel, Mike Evans (Achilles) and Christian Kirk (knee) are all sidelined, potentially leaving Demarcus Robinson (ankle) as a featured receiver if he can play. Samuel can continue to be stashed on benches in 12-team leagues, though his return timeline remains somewhat opaque.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) was not seen at Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Neither Samuel nor Mike Evans (Achilles) was seen at the practice, and the same goes for Christian Kirk (knee). Kirk still has a chance to play, but it seems very unlikely that Brock Purdy will have Samuel lined out wide for Week 9 against the Raiders. His next chance to play will be Week 10 against the Cowboys, barring something unforeseeable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: 49ers GM John Lynch said it’s likely that Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will not play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Lynch said the same about Mike Evans. Samuel hasn’t played or practiced since going down with a hamstring injury in Week 5. It’s unclear when he will return to the field. The fact that the 49ers didn’t place him on injured reserve when he suffered the injury suggests they expected him to miss fewer than four games. Week 9 will be his third absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel remains sidelined by his Week 5 hamstring strain. He still has a chance to resume practicing in time to face the Raiders this weekend, but it would have been nice to see him take the field today. The 49ers were on bye in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: 49ers declared DE Nick Bosa, WR Mike Evans, WR Deebo Samuel, LB Luke Gifford, LB Garret Wallow, S Marques Sigle, and QB Kurtis Rourke inactive for Week 7 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: None of these comes as a surprise. All of Bosa, Evans, and Samuel were already ruled out earlier in the week, and Sigle has missed multiple weeks with an ankle injury. Brandin Cooks and Christian Kirk are likely to lead the 49ers’ pass catchers against the Falcons this week, and both are worth adding in deeper formats in case either emerges as a legit weapon while Evans (Achilles) and Samuel (hamstring) are sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) won’t play in San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel hasn’t practiced since injuring his hamstring in the latter stages of Week 5’s win over the Seahawks. He’ll get the Week 8 bye to heal up. It does seem like there’s at least some chance he could get active for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Neither did Mike Evans, who is dealing with Achilles tendinitis. These absences shouldn’t come as much of a surprise. Evans is expected to miss Week 7 after aggravating his Achilles issue on Monday. Samuel is expected to miss “at least a couple of weeks” and has been sidelined for just one game so far. Jordan Watkins and Brandin Cooks are in line to start for the 49ers this week. What a time to be alive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: 49ers ruled out Mike Evans (Achilles) for Week 10 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Losing Evans for this one is a bummer. The 49ers’ and Cowboys’ offenses should facilitate a high-scoring game environment. Regardless, the 49ers are smartly prioritizing Evans’ long-term health. Whenever he returns, he is likely to be full-go. Keep him stashed on fantasy football benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) will not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: At this point, Evans seems like a long shot to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys. The 49ers allowed Christian McCaffrey to try to play through his Achilles tendinitis and it did not go well. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan indicated they learned from the experience and will let Evans get fully healthy before allowing him to retake the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: The 49ers are smartly allowing Evans to fully recover from his Achilles tendinitis rather than allowing him to try to play through it. On Sunday, NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported that Evans was “questionable at best” for Week 10 against the Cowboys. He should probably be considered doubtful to play at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: 49ers declared WR Mike Evans, WR Deebo Samuel, QB Kurtis Rourke, OT Enrique Cruz, LB Tatum, Bethune, and DL Khalid Kareem inactive for Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans will miss at least one game with his lingering Achilles injury. Look for the Niners to be careful with their WR1 in the coming weeks. Demarcus Robinson, coming off an injury, will return to the lineup against Vegas and likely operate as the Niners’ top wideout. Robinson will be flex-viable against a porous Vegas secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Mike Evans (Achilles) is “questionable at best” for Week 10 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: The 49ers bungled Christian McCaffrey’s Achilles tendinitis in 2024 and are determined to get it right this time around with Evans. That means taking an extra cautious approach with his return to the field. He’s already been ruled out for Week 9 and now Week 10 sounds like a long-shot. Demarcus Robinson, who returned from injured reserve earlier this week, is somehow the team’s WR1 for today’s game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: 49ers ruled out Mike Evans (Achilles) for Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans is dealing with tendinitis in his Achilles tendon that initially cropped up in Week 6. When speaking with the media earlier this week, general manager John Lynch said the team hopes to get Evans back in the “coming weeks,” which means he should tentatively be considered questionable to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) was not present at Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans wasn’t spotted at practice, nor was Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Neither player is expected to play against the Raiders on Thursday, and Thursday’s missed practice seems to clinch that. The 49ers’ receiving crops are in dire straits, with Christian Kirk also not practicing with his knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: 49ers GM John Lynch said it’s likely that Mike Evans (Achilles) will not play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: The same is true of Deebo Samuel, who has a calf injury. Evans has been dealing with the Achilles issue for a few weeks. The fact that a Week 8 bye wasn’t enough to get him back on the field suggests this will be something he deals with for potentially the rest of the year. Demarcus Robinson is expected to return from IR this week. Robinson, Christian Kirk, Jordan Watkins, and Brandin Cooks will all be in the mix for starting roles this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: We had hoped to see Evans practice today, following the 49ers’ Week 8 bye, but evidently, he needs more time to rest and recover. The 49ers’ No. 1 wide receiver should currently be viewed as questionable to play in Week 9 against the Raiders. The 49ers have playoff aspirations, so the team could choose to hold him out this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: 49ers declared DE Nick Bosa, WR Mike Evans, WR Deebo Samuel, LB Luke Gifford, LB Garret Wallow, S Marques Sigle, and QB Kurtis Rourke inactive for Week 7 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: None of these comes as a surprise. All of Bosa, Evans, and Samuel were already ruled out earlier in the week, and Sigle has missed multiple weeks with an ankle injury. Brandin Cooks and Christian Kirk are likely to lead the 49ers’ pass catchers against the Falcons this week, and both are worth adding in deeper formats in case either emerges as a legit weapon while Evans (Achilles) and Samuel (hamstring) are sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez had three limited sessions ahead of this week and, should the Jaguars bludgeon the Titans, would profile to get some between-the-tackles work with Bhayshul Tuten dealing with ankle and foot injuries and not getting in much practice time. He’ll be a reasonable FLEX play against Tennessee.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez played through the hand injury without issue last week, totaling 10 carries and two receptions on Thursday night. He should again handle a FLEX-worthy workload against the Titans in Week 10, with Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) managing something.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez was limited last week and played through the hand injury in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens. He was limited again to open Week 10 but is still trending to play against the Titans. With Bhayshul Tuten still dealing with ankle and foot injuries, Rodriguez is a good bet to split touches this week and achieve FLEX value against a weak Titans defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed 10 times for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens, adding 13 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez split time with lead back Bhayshul Tuten in the first half before soaking up most of the backfield work in the third quarter. Both backs would then cede primary duties to special team ace Ameer Abdullah in the fourth quarter when the game was well in hand. Rodriguez has seen his fantasy value plummet of late with the emergence of Tuten as a borderline workhorse, a situation that was heavily influenced by Tuten’s lack of practice ahead of Thursday Night Football. The long week appears likely to provide the time needed for Tuten to return to full strength, leaving Rodriguez as a touchdown-dependent FLEX when the Jaguars face the Titans in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez remained limited all week, as did many Jaguars on the Week 9 injury report. It seems likely that the team simply took a conservative approach to their Thursday Night Football preparation. Rodriguez could end up being the Jaguars’ starter this week, with Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) labeled a game-time decision after failing to practice all week. Rodriguez warrants RB2 treatment if this is the case. Add him everywhere.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Liam Coen said Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) will be a game-time decision for Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Tuten did not practice on Tuesday. Coen told reporters he would get in a limited session today. Tuten himself told Coen he feels better today and he toughed it out through the injury on Sunday. He appears to be on the right side of questionable for Thursday’s contest, but fantasy managers will want to check inactives before kickoff to be sure. If he can’t go, Chris Rodriguez will get the bulk of the carries for the Jags.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) was limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: This appears to be a non-issue as the veteran change of pace back should be fine for Thursday Night Football against the Ravens. Of greater concern was the absence of lead back Bayshul Tuten, something fantasy managers of both players will want to monitor as Thursday draw nearer. Rodriguez would seemingly be in line for a featured role if Tuten is unable to play on a short week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed six times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts, adding a 17-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez was still getting out-snapped and out-produced by a percolating Bhayshul Tuten, but he managed to contribute a 28-yard score in a blowout victory. Rodriguez hit the hole then emerged to an abandoned mall of a Colts defense. With the Jaguars heading on the road for a short-week Thursday night date with a Ravens team operating without Lamar Jackson, expect lots of “get me out of here” Jags rushes in Baltimore, locking Rodriguez in as a Week 9 FLEX play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed 11 times for 55 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: He failed to catch his only target. Rodriguez was churning out success rate on the regular in the first half. The Jaguars curiously went away from him in the second half, as he played just 21-of-70 snaps and had only one carry after halftime. He’s not a must-hold through the bye week, but this game is the proof-of-concept that he can be an effective weapon for the Jaguars if they want to use him as a between-the-tackles pounder.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed two times for five yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez was all but phased out of the rotation in this game. His most notable touch was a goal line carry which he was stuffed on and then fumbled the ball away. He was called down on the field. Even though replay clearly showed him losing the ball, there was no clear recovery and the refs didn’t bother overturning the non-fumble. Rodriguez may still be the occasional touchdown vulture, but his role has been reduced to the point where fantasy managers can safely cut ties with him on the next run of waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.headline: Cardinals ruled out Hjalte Froholdt (concussion) for Week 10 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.analysis: The Cardinals will be without Froholdt, their starting center, against a Rams team that is likely to rely on its ground game and ascending defense while navigating pass-catcher injuries. This makes life a little harder for rookie QB Carson Beck, who will make his first NFL start this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.headline: Hjalte Froholdt (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.analysis: Froholdt is the Cardinals’ starting center and is trending to miss Week 10 against the Rams as he deals with a concussion. Backup interior offensive lineman Jon Gaines (ankle) also missed practice, leaving the Cardinals’ offensive line depleted with a matchup against Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald coming up this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.headline: Cardinals signed C Hjalte Froholdt to a two-year, $20 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.analysis: A nice scrapheap find by the Cardinals, Froholdt bounced around the NFL playing 14 games for the Patriots and Browns in 2020 and 2021 before becoming a full-time starter in Arizona in 2023. He’s started every game since. This isn’t exactly a contract extension that sets a market — no agent bragging is coming here — but it’s a reasonable decision for a player who has bounced around the league and hasn’t had a major contract yet entering his age-30 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.headline: Cardinals C Hjalte Froholdt (elbow) returned to Week 16 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.analysis: Froholdt injured his left elbow in the first half and was taken to the locker room for examination. He required a moment to collect himself after the play, seemingly in a lot of pain. The team concerningly labeled him as questionable to return. The last healthy starter from Arizona’s preseason offensive line starters, Froholdt successfully returned partway through the second half.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.headline: Cardinals C Hjalte Froholdt (illness) was added to the injury report and is questionable for Week 16 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.analysis: Players typically played through illness-related questionable tags, but Froholdt was obviously added to the injury report very late. The Cardinals are already without left tackle Paris Johnson while left guard Evan Brown is listed as questionable with a neck injury. Arizona could be down three starting linemen for their matchup with Carolina if Brown and Froholdt both sit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.headline: Cardinals signed C Hjalte Froholdt to a two-year contract extension worth $8 million.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.analysis: Froholdt entered the 2023 season with little experience at center but quickly established himself as the anchor of Arizona’s offensive line, which performed admirably down the stretch of the season. Froholdt played all 17 games last season, and 1,123 offensive snaps. A former Patriots draft pick who spent time with the Browns, Froholdt seems to have found a place in Arizona.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.headline: Cardinals signed OL Hjalte Froholdt, formerly of the Browns, to a two-year, $4.6 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.analysis: Froholdt is being signed for his versatility. He started games at right guard and center last season while manning left tackle for a few snaps. The 26-year-old will probably end up seeing plenty of playing time for the rebuilding Cardinals and their shaky offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.headline: Patriots placed G Hjalte Froholdt (shoulder) on injured reserve, ending his season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.analysis: The Patriots selected Froholdt with the No. 118 overall pick in the 2019 NFL draft. His absence isn’t ideal for the Patriots’ depth on the offensive line, but he wasn’t expected to be more than a backup option if healthy in 2019.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.headline: Patriots selected Arkansas G Hjalte Froholdt with the No. 118 overall pick in the 2019 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.analysis: Froholdt (6’5/306) made 37 starts on the Razorbacks’ offensive line after converting from defensive tackle, dabbling at center but mainly manning right guard and earning second-team All-SEC in 2018. PFF College credited Froholdt with the SEC’s top pass-blocking efficiency rating last season, allowing just five QB pressures and zero sacks. A Denmark native, Froholdt’s short arms (31 ¼") and moderate athleticism limit his ceiling, but his interior flexibility raises Froholdt’s floor, and he offers starter potential at center or guard. The Patriots have done a great job at developing offensive linemen in the past, maybe Froholdt can be the next feather in their cap.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.headline: Patriots selected Arkansas G Hjalte Froholdt with the No. 118 overall pick in the 2019 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hjalte-fro.analysis: Froholdt (6’5/306) made 37 starts on the Razorbacks’ offensive line after converting from defensive tackle, dabbling at center but mainly manning right guard and earning second-team All-SEC in 2018. PFF College credited Froholdt with the SEC’s top pass-blocking efficiency rating last season, allowing just five QB pressures and zero sacks. A Denmark native, Froholdt’s short arms (31 ¼") and moderate athleticism limit his ceiling, but his interior flexibility raises Froholdt’s floor, and he offers starter potential at center or guard. The Patriots have done a great job at developing offensive linemen in the past, maybe Froholdt can be the next feather in their cap.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Micah Parsons (knee/illness) will not play in Green Bay’s Week 10 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons got in limited sessions all week and seems to be in line to play in Week 11 assuming he can upgrade to full work. The Packers have slowplayed his return and have been rewarded as their defense has been able to play quite well without him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Micah Parsons (knee/illness) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons seemingly has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Vikings, but he remains in the questionable column at this time. Packers DC Jonathan Gannon has done well with Parsons sidelined. Getting him back will only improve the unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Micah Parsons (knee) was ruled out for Week 9 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons was cleared to resume individual activities but was never likely to play against the Pats this week. The next chance for Parsons to play will be Week 10 against the Vikings, and there’s at least a smidgen of optimism he could be back for that contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Micah Parsons (knee) is a “full go” to do individual work at practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: That doesn’t mean Parsons is a “full go” for Week 9 against the Patriots, however, as the pass rusher comes back from a season-ending knee injury in 2025. Parsons could return soon for a Green Bay defense that ranks 12th in pressure rate and 16th in quick pressure rate on the season. Look for the team to ease Parsons into action to make sure he’s OK for the final stretch of the regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said he expects Micah Parsons (knee) to practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons is not expected to suit up in Week 9 against the Patriots, but this is the next step in his recovery as he looks to return to the field. On Sunday, it was reported that the Packers were targeting a Week 12 return for Parsons, which would mean he plays on Thanksgiving Eve against the Rams if all goes according to plan.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Micah Parsons (knee) is targeting a Week 12 return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons is still working his way back from the torn ACL he suffered late in the 2025 season. Per Rapoport, Parsons is expected to return to practice this week, meaning he will be designated to return from injured reserve in the coming days. He will then ramp up for a few weeks before hopefully returning in Week 12 against the Rams. Green Bay’s Week 11 bye will give him some extra time to get fully up to speed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Micah Parsons (knee) is expected to practice next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: If Parsons returns to practice next week, the Packers will have a 21-day window where he can practice before activating him to the 53-man roster. Pelissero also reported that Parsons’ most likely return date is in Week 11 against the Rams. Including the playoffs, Green Bay is 5-8 since Parsons tore his ACL last December.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said “there’s a chance” Micah Parsons (knee) practices next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: When asked about Parsons’ chances of practicing next week, LaFleur said, “I sure hope so.” He followed that up with, “I’m saying there’s a chance.” Parsons opened the season on the PUP list after an ACL tear late last season. The Packers have a Thursday game for Week 8, leading to a mini-bye where Parsons’ door to practice is at least cracked open.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Packers EDGE Micah Parsons (knee) still isn’t practicing.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: The Packers play the Cowboys on Sunday Night Football on NBC and Peacock in Week 6, but Parsons still isn’t practicing. According to Pelissero, it’s unlikely the 27-year-old defensive end plays before Green Bay’s matchup with the Patriots in Week 9 at the earliest. The Packers’ defense has certainly struggled without Parsons, but they have enough offensive firepower to win shootouts, which only adds to the fantasy floor for Jordan Love and Green Bay’s skill players.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers EDGE Micah Parsons (knee) isn’t expected to practice next week and could return in November, reports the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons is coming back from tearing his ACL late last season. The 27-year-old defensive end didn’t practice this week and isn’t expected to practice next week, according to Pelissero. Parsons hasn’t had any setbacks in his rehab, but still isn’t ready for the Packers to open the 21-day window for him to practice before he’s activated. Pelissero points out that it could be November before Parsons is ready for game action. Green Bay is 1-2 this year and 1-8 without Parsons in the lineup over the last two years (including playoffs).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is not on the Rams’ final injury report for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson upgraded to full participation today. Tyler Higbee (illness) was limited. Both players were cleared to play. Davis Allen (oblique) is questionable, sandwiching a Thursday absence between two limited sessions. The Rams must be smart with their skill position players’ health, while asking as much as they can from their available players.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson should play through his injury again this week. Unfortunately, Tyler Higbee (illness) did not practice, as a new addition to the injury report, and Davis Allen (oblique) was downgraded to being a non-participant. The running backs are going to get all the work they can handle this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) did not practice in Wednesday’s walk-through.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Ferguson was listed as a DNP for the Rams’ Wednesday walk-through. Rams head coach Sean McVay said earlier this week that Ferguson is likely out a couple week, so this comes as no surprise. Meanwhile, fellow tight ends Davis Allen (oblique) and Colby Parkinson (ribs) were both listed as limited participants. Allen and Parkinson are trending towards playing in Week 10 against the Cardinals, with Parkinson operating more as a pass-catcher and Allen as a blocker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports Puka Nacua (knee, toe) will not miss the rest of the regular season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Graziano said there’s an outside chance the Rams won’t put Nacua on injured reserve ahead of Week 10. Rams sources “were very adamant that Nacua’s injury isn’t season-ending and that they hope to get him back around that Week 14, Week 15 time.” With Davante Adams (hamstring) also sidelined, look for the Rams offense to be unusually run heavy in the coming weeks. That should mean more work for Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson could see an uptick in targets too. If Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) is ever able to return to game action, he could profile as the team’s top target. Nacua had seen 44 percent of the Rams’ first-read targets this season, the highest rate in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is active for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson managed to draw a questionable tag entering the weekend after logging a limited practice on Friday. Despite being a DNP for two of the Rams’ three practices this week, he should be available to play his normal role in the Rams’ TE-heavy scheme. Parkinson has caught 14 passes for 103 yards and one touchdown this season and will not be on the fantasy radar this week. The Rams declared QB Ty Simpson, LS Joe Cardona, LB Darryl Peterson III, OL Bill Murray, OL Keagan Trost, and LB Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson sat out on Wednesday and Thursday. His Friday participation level has not yet been released, but he is probably on the wrong side of questionable at this time. Parkinson does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues, especially with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) expected to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Rams head coach Sean McVay announced Parkinson would be a DNP on Wednesday. The 27-year-old has been dealing with a rib injury since Week 7, missing the Rams’ Week 8 game against the Chargers. Starting out DNP puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Rams declared TE Colby Parkinson, QB Ty Simpson, LS Joe Cardona, OT Keagan Trost, and DE Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 8 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson will miss at least one game with a rib injury he sustained last week against the Raiders. His absence could have a big impact on playing time for both Davis Allen — who had two touchdown grabs last week — and Tyler Higbee, the de facto TE1 in the LA offense. Both tight ends are better options against the Chargers with Parkinson sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is questionable for Week 8 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson gutted out an injury to his midsection against the Raiders a week ago when he was in and out of the lineup while clearly dealing with significant discomfort. He was unable to practice through Thursday this week, prompting the questionable designation ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Chargers. Already down multiple primary pass catchers, the Rams could see further concentration of volume should Parkinson miss, a situation that could also pave the way for Davis Allen to see an uptick in opportunities in the 12- and 13-personnel-heavy Rams offense. Fantasy managers likely won’t get further updates on Parkinson’s status before the team releases inactives 90-minutes prior to first kick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson will have one more chance to get back no the practice field Friday to avoid an injury designation entering the weekend. The veteran tight end was in and out of the team’s Week 7 game with the injury but managed to finish it, apparently feeling much worse after the adrenaline wore off. Fantasy managers of Parkinson and Tyler Higbee will want to track Parkinson’s status closely to end the week. An absence from Parkinson could also bring Davis Allen into the fantasy spotlight after the young tight end scored twice against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.headline: Charles Cross (ankle) won’t play in Seattle’s Week 10 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.analysis: He did resume practicing on Thursday, but it was a quick hook and a Friday DNP. Still, it’s an encouraging sign for his status for Week 12 — after the Week 11 bye — that he was able to get on the practice field at all.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.headline: Charles Cross (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.analysis: Cross and LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) were both limited at today’s practice, giving them a chance to play on Sunday against the Cardinals. Seahawks stud DT Leonard Williams (stinger) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.headline: Charles Cross (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.analysis: Cross remains sidelined with a high ankle sprain he suffered in Week 7. He is yet to return to practice and therefore is trending towards missing Week 10 against the Raiders; a full practice participation would be needed to feel confident about his chances of playing this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Quenton Nelson (knee) will have a minor procedure and is week-to-week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.analysis: Apparently, Nelson was dealing with this knee issue when Seattle acquired for him, and he recently “aggravated it to some degree.” FOX 59’s Mike Chappell notes that Nelson was never listed on the Colts’ injury report this season. This is a bummer for the Seahawks, who acquired Nelson as a win-now move. Nelson will not play in Week 9 against the Cardinals, and the Seahawks also ruled out LT Charles Cross (ankle), DT Leonard Williams (stinger) and LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.analysis: Shaheed seems likely to miss another week, though he could technically still turn things around tomorrow. Seahawks LT Charles Cross (ankle) also remains sidelined on Thursday, and LG Quenton Nelson (knee) was downgraded to a non-participant. Hopefully, Nelson’s absence is precautionary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.headline: Jordan Schultz reports Charles Cross (ankle) suffered a high-ankle sprain in Sunday night’s win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.analysis: He’ll be week-to-week. An ankle sprain isn’t quite as devastating for offensive linemen since they don’t have to move quite as much as other positions, but it wouldn’t be surprising if Cross missed multiple weeks. He also could be a candidate for a quick IR stint. Josh Jones filled in at left tackle for Cross and would seem to be the short-term replacement.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.headline: Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (ankle) is not on the injury report for Super Bowl LX against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.analysis: The Seahawks had Emmanwori take the day off to receive treatment on Thursday, after spraining his ankle on Wednesday. Emmanwori suffered a high-ankle sprain in September and sprained the same ankle this week, but imaging indicated he avoided a high-ankle sprain this time. He practiced fully today, which is a great sign for his readiness to play a normal allotment of snaps on Sunday. Seahawks LT Charles Cross (foot) was also cleared to play after practicing fully today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.headline: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (oblique) practiced fully on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.analysis: This is great news. A report from this afternoon indicated that Darnold would again participate in a limited capacity, as he has done since injuring his oblique during the Seahawks’ final Divisional Round practice. Darnold is ready to go for Super Bowl LX against the Patriots. Seahawks LT Charles Cross (foot) remains limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.headline: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (oblique) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.analysis: Also limited was LT Charles Cross (foot). Darnold and Cross have been limited in practice for the playoffs, but have played through their respective injuries. The Seahawks’ passing game has operated well in their two playoff games and neither player will be at risk of being limited for the Super Bowl, barring setbacks in practice. Expect both to fire it up in a battle for the Lombardi Trophy against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.headline: Charles Cross (foot) is not on Seattle’s final injury report for the NFC Championship game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charles-cr.analysis: Despite not practicing either of the first two sessions of the week, Cross will start against the Rams. Backup T Josh Jones (knee/ankle) is questionable, and third-string left tackle Amari Kight (knee) is doubtful. Cross would appear to be on the spot to play through the pain if neither of his backups were cleared.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) is not on Seattle’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: He’ll return to his boom/bust fantasy role as Seattle’s field-stretcher and punt returner after missing a few weeks due to this knee injury. Shaheed practiced in full all week and should not have any real limitations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed has missed the last two weeks with a knee injury, but he was able to practice in full to open Week 10. A full practice participation is a good sign we’ll see Shaheed on the field for Week 10 against the Raiders. He has been splitting WR2 opportunities with Cooper Kupp this year and belongs on fantasy benches until further notice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Seahawks ruled out Rashid Shaheed (knee) for Week 9 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: The Seahawks will again be without their speedy, underused wide receiver. Fortunately, Tory Horton (hand) was removed from the injury report and will play this week. He will catch passes thrown by Drew Lock (elbow).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed seems likely to miss another week, though he could technically still turn things around tomorrow. Seahawks LT Charles Cross (ankle) also remains sidelined on Thursday, and LG Quenton Nelson (knee) was downgraded to a non-participant. Hopefully, Nelson’s absence is precautionary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) did not practice in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Also not practicing is OT Charles Cross (ankle). Both missed Week 8 against the Bears and are still out with their respective injuries to open the week. They will need to practice in some fashion to have a chance at returning for the Seahawks offense in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Seahawks ruled out Rashid Shaheed (knee) for Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed reportedly avoided a major injury in the collision with teammate Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the end zone in Week 7, an injury that will claim at least one game from the veteran speedster. There’s not really a ton of fantasy value behind Smith-Njigba in Seattle, although veteran Cooper Kupp could see a target or two trickle his way in Shaheed’s absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) remained sidelined for Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed is now firmly on the wrong side of questionable heading into Monday evening’s game against the Bears. If he was in your third receiver or second FLEX spot in a 14-team league, it is time to start making other plans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed received positive news on his knee injury that caused him to leave Sunday’s blowout win over the Chiefs, but there’s a pretty good chance that he’s going to miss at least Week 8’s game against Chicago on Monday. Assuming that’s the case, it will lead to more snaps for Tory Horton both as a receiver and as the primary returner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said the “early returns are positive” on Rashid Shaheed’s knee injury he suffered in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Macdonald didn’t elaborate on how much time Shaheed could miss, if any, but it doesn’t sound like this is expected to be a long-term injury based on what he had to say on Monday. Shaheed’s impact is largely felt in the punt and kick return game, as he has just 16 receptions for 163 scoreless yards on the season for Seattle. We will update his practice status throughout the week, but Shaheed won’t have any fantasy relevance even if he does suit up next week against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) is questionable to return in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed was involved in a collision with teammate Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the end zone on an interception in the waning moments of the first half and did not retake the field out of the break. Tory Horton received the kickoff to begin the second half, after which Shaheed was deemed questionable to return with a knee injury. Expect Cooper Kupp and Horton to see a small bump in opportunity behind Smith-Njigba for the remainder of the game. Shaheed caught 2-of-3 targets for one yard prior to departing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) is not on Seattle’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock will step in as the starter again as Seattle takes on the Raiders, and he should profile as a reasonable superflex QB2. He was limited in all three practices this week, ceding some practice snaps to let Jalen Milroe run the show. The re-injury risk here does not quite appear to be zero.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock reportedly resumed throwing today, which is good to hear. He told reporters that the oblique injury is on the right side of his body, on the back of the muscle, which he thinks makes it easier to throw the football than when he had an oblique injury on the left side of his body two years ago. Lock is a QB2 this week against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) will not “take every rep and throw” during Week 10 practices.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock was a limited practice participant through Week 9 practices before starting on game day. We expect that to be the case again this week. Fellow backup QB Jalen Milroe will take some first-team reps to help preserve Lock for the Seahawks’ Week 10 game against the Raiders. Given the injuries, Lock is likely just a mid-to-low QB2 despite the soft matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said the team expects Drew Lock (oblique) to start in Week 10 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Speaking on Monday, Macdonald said that tests on Lock’s oblique injury were “good” and that they believe his injury is something the team can manage. Lock has been solid in three games for the Seahawks this season, throwing for 597-5-0 while completing 71.1 percent of his passes. He draws a favorable Week 10 matchup against the Raiders and could be on the radar as a mid to low-end QB2 that may have some stream appeal in 2QB/Superflex leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock suffered an oblique injury today, and his status for Week 10 against the Raiders is “up in the air.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Macdonald also said that he does not know whether Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) will be healthy enough to play. Lock has also been dealing with tendinitis in his throwing-arm elbow. If both Lock and Darnold are ruled out, it will be Jalen Milroe who leads the Seahawks’ offense against the Raiders next week. Milroe would warrant starting consideration in two-quarterback leagues thanks to his rushing abilities.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock completed 19-of-28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ 17-3, Week 9 win over the Cardinals, adding 16 yards on five carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock appeared to suffer discomfort in the third quarter following an incomplete pass attempt, holding his side or oblique and grimacing in pain as he made his way to sideline. He would get checked in the medical tent but returned without missing a down. Lock looked poised in the pocket and in control of the offense throughout, leaning on his alpha wide receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba early before the team went into preservation mode with a sizable lead in the second half. Lock could be looking at another start or two, pending the length of recovery from a cracked rib for Sam Darnold. The team passed an update on Lock’s oblique injury following the game, indicating that the veteran journeyman would undergo follow-on testing but that his status for Week 10 could be in doubt. He’ll be nothing more than a deep-league potential streamer against the Raiders, if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Sam Darnold (quad) could “potentially” miss Week 10 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Garafolo added that Darnold is dealing with a cracked rib, though it sounds like the quad issue is what’s preventing him from playing. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald called Darnold “week to week” on Wednesday. They get their bye in Week 11, so holding him out for one more game to get an extended break makes the most sense. Fantasy managers should plan on Darnold missing Week 10 in addition to today’s game against Arizona. Drew Lock will start today. As long as his elbow issue doesn’t flare up, he will be in line to start next week as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Seahawks QB Drew Lock (elbow) has severe tendonitis in his elbow.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Pelissero reiterated that Lock looked good in practice and will start against the Cardinals in Week 9. Still, Lock has been dealing with this since earlier this season and at one point wasn’t able to throw because of it. Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald said earlier this week he didn’t know how much Lock will be able to throw. Despite his play in relief of Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) earlier this year, Lock isn’t a priority in 1QB leagues. Jalen Milroe could even be worth stashing in deeper formats given that Lock’s tendonitis could flare up at anytime.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock (elbow) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock has dealt with an injury in his throwing-arm elbow for multiple weeks. He was limited at each Week 9 practice, but told reporters that he was feeling good late on Wednesday. It is tough to say whether this will impact him on game day, but he warrants QB2 treatment against the Cardinals’ soft defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock (elbow) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock has been dealing with an injury in his throwing arm since Week 7, but he told reporters that he is feeling good now. Lock played very well as Sam Darnold’s replacement earlier this year. As long as the elbow holds up, Lock should be expected to do so again. He is a viable QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell (knee) is doubtful for Miami’s Week 10 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: He did not practice Thursday or Friday after aggravating his surgically repaired knee in practice on Wednesday. The Dolphins have no reason to push Bell, so we’d be stunned if he played. Not that you were looking for reasons to lean into a Kyle McCord start, but Bell’s injury should free up targets for Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas on the FLEX line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: The Dolphins were regularly limiting Bell’s practice reps earlier this season, so this may just be routine maintenance. The rookie wide receiver was limited yesterday. Bell has not yet established himself as a fantasy-relevant player, and he is unlikely to do so in Kyle McCord’s first start, especially if his surgically repaired knee is bothering him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell failed to catch his only target in the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: With nine targets over his previous two games, Bell looked to be building some momentum headed into Week 9. Instead, he posted the dreaded goose egg. The good news is that Bell ran a route on 77 percent of Malik Willis’s dropbacks. He’s running as the team’s WR3, but there’s barely enough passing volume to keep the WR1 in the FLEX mix. Bell remains an interesting dynasty stash, but he is not on the redraft radar headed into Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell caught 4-of-5 targets for 31 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: The third-round rookie was limited to short-area work in today’s loss to the Patriots, but his five targets and four receptions both tie for career highs. He also lost two yards on a run play. Bell has had a few gaffes this year, but he is seemingly recovering well from last year’s ACL surgery. He is a player worth stashing on benches in many 12-team leagues, and could warrant WR5 treatment against the Lions next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell caught 3-of-4 targets for 25 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: Bell finished second on the team in targets but fourth in receiving yards. Caleb Douglas was finally healthy this week and stole the spotlight with 70 yards and two touchdowns despite seeing just three targets. After being held without a catch in back-to-back games, Bell’s modest Week 7 showing is still a step in the right direction. On the other hand, he simply isn’t seeing enough targets to be a weekly fantasy consideration right now. He should remain on the waiver wire in most fantasy leagues this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell caught neither of his two targets in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals, adding one carry for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: Bell was targeted just twice on the day, catching neither target. He did see a carry on an end-around play, rushing for 26 yards on his sole touch of the game. He has ramped up to a starting receiver’s workload of snaps, ranking second among Dolphins receivers with 41 snaps. Though Bell is the field more, he has yet to be a key part of the Dolphins offense and will see less opportunities once Caleb Douglas (ankle) returns. Bell is best left on fantasy benches when the Dolphins come out of their Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell (knee) is not on Miami’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: He’ll be a FLEX dart throw against the Bengals. Bell continues to get listed with his knee injury as the Dolphins bring him along slowly, but he seems wheels up for Sundays as things currently stand.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: The Dolphins have been managing Bell’s practice reps for a few weeks, but it hasn’t been an issue on Sundays. He ran 85 percent of the routes in Week 4 and his route share has gone up in every game. He is in the WR5 range headed into Week 5 versus the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell caught 0-of-3 targets in the Dolphins’ Week 4 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: Bell’s Week 4 outing was heartbreaking. His near-68-yard touchdown on the Dolphins’ third drive will live with him, and fantasy managers alike, for a while. Malik Willis rolled right out of the pocket, facing pressure and lobbed a wobbly pass to Bell downfield. The rookie wide receiver caught it, took off downfield, stumbled through a leg grab and ran into the end zone. Unfortunately, the officials determined Bell had stepped out of bounds, along the right sideline, during the scramble drill. Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley did not challenge it. Upon replay, one can make the case that his pinky toe’s shadow grazed the white line, but it was an awfully close call. Aside from that, Willis sent him a wobbly, incomplete overthrow beyond the sticks on the Dolphins’ first drive and later tried to force a fadeaway jumper to him 25 yards downfield. The pass was contested and fell incomplete. The talent is there. Despite the rough outing, Bell warrants FLEX consideration against the Saints in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: Bell posted a 4/67 receiving line last week, though the Dolphins are still managing his reps. The Vikings’ blitz-based defense poses problems for Miami, limiting Bell to WR4 status this week. The rookie wide receiver should be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson (concussion) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: All three of the Jets’ starting wide receivers are questionable to play, though Wilson practiced in full practice and is expected to play.
