Wilson could handle a hefty workload if he is indeed cleared to play, as expected, and one or two of the others are limited or ruled out. Wilson is a WR2 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said he is “confident” that Garrett Wilson (concussion) will play in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Glenn said Wilson has one more step to clear before he is out of the league’s concussion protocol. Wilson missed last week’s game against the Chiefs due to his brain injury, but has practiced in a limited capacity twice this week and is trending toward a return. We will get a final update on Wilson once he has officially cleared the protocol, but fantasy managers can start him as a mid-to-high-end WR2 in a game that could feature plenty of points against a high-powered Bills offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson still needs to be officially cleared from concussion protocol to play, but two limited sessions have him with a real chance to be active in Week 10 after missing Week 9. If he can play, Wilson will likely be an upside fantasy WR2 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: ESPN’s Rich Cimini reports the 49ers and Chiefs “were interested” in Garrett Wilson ahead of the trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: The Jets made it clear they were not moving Wilson early in the process, so we can’t imagine trade talks between them and either team made it very far. Cimini notes that the Jets could revisit a Wilson trade in the offseason. Wilson told reporters earlier this year that he loves it in New York, but he loves winning more. The Jets haven’t done much of that since Wilson was drafted. This will be a storyline to watch in the offseason, though we suspect he’ll remain in New York for the foreseeable future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said he’s “very hopeful” Garrett Wilson (concussion) will play in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson was sidelined in last week’s loss to Kansas City with the head injury he sustained in Week 8. Omar Cooper, Jr. functioned as the team’s top receiver with Wilson sidelined while Adonai Mitchell couldn’t reel in any of his seven targets from Geno Smith. Wilson would be a top-24 option in Week 10 against Buffalo if he can return to action. The Bills secondary allows the 13th highest fantasy points per target to boundary wideouts this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets declared Garrett Wilson, Tim Patrick, Nahshon Wright, Joseph Ossai, Trevin Wallace, Kohl Levao, and Blake Freeland inactive for Week 9 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson suffered a head injury last week and did not practice this week as he remained in the NFL’s concussion protocol. Look for Omar Cooper, Jr. and Adonai Mitchell to see more routes and targets against a tough KC secondary. Mitchell is likely to function as the team’s top wideout with Wilson sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Garrett Wilson (concussion) will not play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson has not practiced this week and has now been ruled out for Sunday’s game against the Chiefs. Wilson has caught 43 passes for 527 yards and three touchdowns this season and saw 12 targets in last week’s loss to the Raiders. His absence means both Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper should see expanded roles, but both players will be hard to trust as anything more than WR3s against a stout Chiefs defense. In addition to Wilson, the Jets also ruled out LB Trevin Wallace (groin) for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson (concussion) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson did not practice on Wednesday and will go down as a DNP today as well. He is a long-shot to suit up for the Jets’ Week 9 game against the Chiefs. His absence will free up targets for Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. The two have alternated spike weeks and zeroes over their past two games. Now both should have stable fantasy floors for at least one game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets placed Garrett Wilson in the NFL’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: He was officially a DNP for Wednesday’s practice. Wilson sustained a head injury in Week 8 against the Raiders and now appears to be a long shot for Week 9. That includes giving him a one-year, $20 million contract that features a no-tag clause this offseason. Hunter leads the NFL with eight sacks but his team sits at 2-4. With Minnesota’s season circling the drain, it would be smart for them to get something for Hunter instead of holding onto him for a lost season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: Vikings signed DE Danielle Hunter to a one-year $20 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: Hunter’s contract includes $17 million in guaranteed money, a no-tag clause, and ultimately ends his brief hold-in with the team. Dating back to 2022, Hunter and the Vikings have gone back and forth in contract negotiations, which led to Hunter being the subject of trade rumors earlier this offseason. Since entering the league in 2015, Hunter has totaled 71 sacks, 85 TFLs, and three Pro Bowls. The no-tag clause gives the veteran pass rusher a chance to earn a significant payday in 2024 — either from the Vikings or via free agency.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Danielle Hunter has reported to Vikings training camp but that he isn’t expected to practice until “his situation gets resolved.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: Hunter skipped the Vikings’ mandatory minicamp earlier this offseason after being the subject of trade rumors earlier. The veteran pass rusher is also in search of a new extension, which he’s been hoping to secure dating back to last year. Hunter totaled 10.5 sacks and 12 TFLs for the Vikings in 2022 and was named to his third Pro Bowl. Because he reported to training camp, Hunter can’t be fined, but there are multiple ways he can stay off the field while he and the team figure out what to do next.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports Vikings EDGE Danielle Hunter is planning to skip the team’s mandatory minicamp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: Hunter has been the subject of trade rumors for the last two offseasons. The veteran pass rusher was in search of a contract extension last offseason but ultimately played on his deal. Now in the final year of his contract, Hunter, who totaled 10.5 sacks and 12 TFLS last season, is still in search of a new deal. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported last week that teams have already begun contacting the Vikings about a potential trade for Hunter, but little has materialized since then. Set to earn just $5.5 million this season, Hunter is more than deserving of a new deal, whether it’s from the Vikings or another team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports “teams have been calling” the Vikings about trading for EDGE Danielle Hunter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: The trade rumors started last offseason when the Vikings were looking for cap space and Hunter was seeking a contract extension. He ultimately stayed in Minnesota, but that didn’t stop the rumor mill from firing up again this offseason. Per Rapoport, Hunter is only set to make $5.5 million this year, making a trade for him feasible even for teams tight on cap space. Hunter appeared in all 17 games last year and totaled 10.5 sacks plus 12 TFLs. He missed the majority of the 2021 season but tallied 14.5 sacks in each of the previous two years.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: Will Anderson (ankle) is questionable for Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: Anderson was added to the report as limited on Thursday and did not practice on Friday, throwing his status into major doubt ahead of Houston’s game in Cleveland. He has been listed with an ankle before this year, and with Danielle Hunter suddenly out, Cleveland’s pass offense could see some efficiency boosts against the Texans without their star rushers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: Texans EDGE Will Anderson (ankle) is not on Houston’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: It wound up being a DNP-Limited-Full workload progression for Anderson, who should remain a terror against the Titans in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: Texans EDGE Will Anderson (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: Anderson popped up on the injury report with an ankle issue to open the week. As one of the league’s elite pass-rushers, the 25-year-old is a key cog to the Texans defense. He did not practice Wednesday, putting his Week 5 status in jeopardy. Anderson still has chances to practice later this week and play against the Titans, but any time missed puts the 0-4 Texans in an even deeper hole.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: Texans signed DE Will Anderson to a three-year, $150 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: Anderson’s deal will make him the highest-paid non-QB in NFL history. The star pass rusher will receiver $134 million in guaranteed money on his new deal and is now under contract with the Texans through the 2023 season. Anderson entered the league in 2023 after molding himself into the nation’s top pass rusher at Alabama. He has shown steady growth during each of his three seasons and has posted double-digit sack totals in each of his last two seasons, earning First-team All-Pro honors in 2025 while finishing second in Defensive Player of the Year voting. With Anderson now extended, the Texans can now shift their focus to C.J. Stroud, whose fifth-year option they recently picked up to keep him under contract through 2027. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter , Anderson’s deal will also include a no-trade clause.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer believes “it would be a stunner” if Texans EDGE Will Anderson signed for less than $50 million per season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: The Texans and Anderson have been mutually interested in an extension for most of the offseason, though it hasn’t happened yet. The sticker shock is surely there reading "$50 million a year,” but it’s essentially no different than the $46 million that Micah Parsons got per season as part of his trade to the Packers given inflation. It shouldn’t surprise anyone when the deal comes in this high, but the rest of Houston’s offseason maneuverings (how much cap space do they still need available for 2026, etc) could be holding the extension up given just how large the contract will be.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: Texans exercised the fifth-year option for EDGE Will Anderson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: Anderson has been a star pass rusher since being drafted No. 3 overall in the 2023 NFL Draft. He totaled 23 sacks over the past two seasons and was a First-Team All-Pro in 2025. With the fifth-year option, Anderson is now set to make $21.512 million in 2027. The Texans will certainly want to extend the 24-year-old as a cornerstone of the defense, but they get him under contract for an additional year for now. Anderson will be headed to reset the pass-rushing market with a prospective extension.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports extending Will Anderson “is a priority” for the Texans this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: Anderson has totaled 23 sacks over the last two seasons and has wasted little time establishing himself as a premier pass-rusher in the league. The former No. 3 overall pick is entering the fourth-year of his contract and will have his fifth-year option picked at some point in the coming weeks. When he signs his deal, Anderson, 24, could reset the market for pass rushers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: Will Anderson (chest/shoulder) is not on Houston’s final Week 14 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: He practiced in full on Friday and should be fine. In IDP leagues, it would be a disappointment if Anderson did not provide at least a half-sack or so against a Chiefs offensive line that looks likely to be down several starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: Texans EDGE Will Anderson (chest) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: DeMeco Ryans said yesterday that Anderson would be fine. He’s been receiving some sporadic rest under the chest tag over the past couple of weeks. He’ll likely be cleared off the injury report on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.headline: Will Anderson (shoulder/chest) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-ander.analysis: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters earlier today that Anderson will be fine. The DNP is likely just a rest day for the cornerstone of the Texans’ defense. Anderson has 10.5 sacks and three forced fumbles this year. He should return to practice later this week. We fully expect to see him on the field, giving Patrick Mahomes trouble on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) won’t play in Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison did not practice on Thursday or Friday and it’s possible this develops into a longer-term injury. Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson will step in as reasonable FLEX plays with Harrison’s snaps off the table. The Texans probably won’t score 40 points again, but they have struggled to move the ball on the ground and should throw plenty against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison was limited yesterday and sat out today. That series of events typically suggests that the player was injured in practice. Harrison is firmly on the wrong side of questionable at this time. He can be stashed in 12-team leagues, but it may take him a while to get back into form.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison is tentatively on track to play in Week 10 against the Browns, but hamstring strains can be tough for wide receivers to immediately bounce back from, and we do not know whether the injury occurred today or last Sunday. Harrison’s practice participation tomorrow will tell us more. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison caught 2-of-3 targets for 20 yards in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison was fairly quiet today, though CJ Stroud picked on Chargers CB Duke Shelley on the Texans’ seventh drive, and Harrison did manage to get in on the fun, beating Shelley for a 15-yard, tip-toe catch along the right sideline. Harrison remains a boom-bust FLEX against the Browns next week, as he continues adjusting to the Texans’ offensive scheme.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan M Alexander reports Jaylin Noel (toe) is expected to miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: It’s a rough blow for Noel, who had been extremely efficient on his targets. It does clear up space for some of Houston’s other receivers. The recently-activated Tank Dell and recently-acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. will benefit a bit from one fewer mouth to feed after the Texans come off bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison caught 1-of-4 targets for six yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison had to come back to the ball in the end zone, one that was placed to his back shoulder by C.J. Stroud to fit it around a zone defender. That was the good. Harrison also added an egregious drop while playing just 13 snaps. Your guess is as good as ours about fantasy value here as we sort through the names. Harrison doesn’t necessarily need to be rostered through his Week 8 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught 3-of-4 targets for 34 yards in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: It tied his season-high for receptions in four games with Arizona. Harrison played just 12 snaps. The Texans do seem dedicated to giving him the ball — as you’d hope after he was acquired for a second-round pick — and we imagine he’ll be in the FLEX conversation next week against the Giants after a full week to hone trust with the coaching staff. His first two catches were on in-breaking routes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said Marvin Harrison Jr. will play in Week 6 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: It’s a slightly short turnaround for MHJ, who was traded to the Texans on Sunday, and a weird travel schedule with Houston flying to London to take on the Jags. On the other hand, a week is still more than enough time to get Harrison Jr. installed at least as a part-time player. He isn’t much of a fantasy option this week, but a week or two of practice reps could get him in the FLEX mix if Houston proves to be a better fit for the former No. 4 overall pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Texans acquired WR Marvin Harrison Jr. from the Cardinals in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison, 24, gets a fresh start partway through his third NFL season. The former first-round pick has averaged just 47.8 receiving yards per game in 33 career games. Adjusting to a new scheme on the fly could be challenging, and Harrison has not proven himself to be a reliable fantasy contributor. It could be tough sledding for fantasy managers, but if Harrison quickly adjusts to his new team, he has a clear runway to No. 2 wide receiver duties next to Nico Collins. He should be rostered in 12-team leagues. The Cardinals are also sending a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Texans in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Cardinals declared Marvin Harrison Jr., QB Carson Beck, CB Starling Thomas, Andrew Wingard and DL Andrew Billings inactive for Week 5 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Life continues to be rough for fantasy managers rostering Harrison. The soon-to-be ex-Cardinal will not participate in what should be a fantasy-friendly game against the porous Lions defense. Bummer. Still no definitive word on where he will end up next week. Trey McBride, Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne benefit from his absence. The Cardinals will be without Wingard, one of two starting safeties, but will have DT Walter Nolen (calf) available to them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell (hand/shoulder) is not on Houston’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The diminutive speedster got in back-to-back full practices and should see a reasonable workload against the Browns. He’s a low-end WR3 or high-end FLEX play at this point, with more upside possible if he’s able to repeat last week’s target share.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell (hand/shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: Dell is firmly on track to play in Week 10 against the Browns. He led the team with nine targets last week, catching four passes for 105 yards and one touchdown. The coaching staff reportedly drew up a play just to get him over the century mark. He is a FLEX starter this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell (hand/shoulder) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The Texans’ diminutive wide receiver led the team with nine targets last week, and evidently got a little banged up in the process. Dell’s early-week participation puts him on track to face the Browns this weekend though. He is a FLEX starter, assuming he is good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell caught 4-of-9 targets for 105 yards and one touchdown in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The Texans seemed fairly comfortable using Dell in this one, getting him going with a screen pass on the opening drive. His biggest play of the day was a 63-yard touchdown via a go route, in which he simply ran past his coverage defender down the right sideline. CJ Stroud hit Dell in stride and he continued on down the field and into the end zone. Dell managed to earn an end zone target on the Texans’ 11th drive, but was unable to secure it. Dell is officially on the WR3/FLEX radar for Week 10 against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan M Alexander reports Jaylin Noel (toe) is expected to miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: It’s a rough blow for Noel, who had been extremely efficient on his targets. It does clear up space for some of Houston’s other receivers. The recently-activated Tank Dell and recently-acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. will benefit a bit from one fewer mouth to feed after the Texans come off bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell caught his only target for 43 yards in Houston’s Week 7 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: He added a two-yard rush on an end around. While it was good to see him back on the field, it should be noted that it looked like his 43-yard catch glanced off Jaylin Noel’s hands and seemed to immaculately find it’s way into Dell’s as he scampered off for some yards after the catch. Dell further confounded the Houston Wideout Situation, playing just 14 snaps. We have no idea what to trust here beyond Nico Collins. Dell seemed to be running just fine, though it sounded like at times his delay in getting up to speed was about recovery. We’ll all get the Week 8 bye to sort this one out. Dell isn’t a must-roster through it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Tank Dell (knee) will play in Week 7 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: Dell will make his long-awaited return next week against the Giants. By the time he takes the field in Week 7, Dell will have been more than 22 months removed from his last regular-season game, which came in Week 16 of the 2024 season. Dell suffered a torn ACL, LCL, and MCL, along with a dislocated knee, in that game against the Chiefs and has been on a long road to recovery. He’ll join a crowded receiver room that recently acquired Marvin Harrison Jr., and Jaylin Noel has posted a solid 17-334-2 line through the first six weeks of the season and topped 100 yards in Sunday’s win over the Jaguars. Targets could be hard to come by for Dell, but his return next week is an impressive feat on its own given the injury he had to work through.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Texans ruled out Tank Dell (knee) for Week 6 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The Texans depart for London tonight to face the Jaguars on Sunday, and Dell will remain in Texas. He is currently practicing in full, but the team has not yet cleared him for game-day activities. Dell does not need to be stashed in 12-team leagues at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell (knee) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The Texans are facing the Jaguars in London this week. If Dell travels, that would indicate that Dell has a chance to play for the first time since suffering a multi-ligament tear in 2024. He would be a low-floor FLEX if he is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell (knee) won’t play in Houston’s Week 5 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: He did not practice on Friday and was ruled out. The Texans reportedly pushed hard on Dell in full pads on Thursday’s practice despite the questionable listing, it seems his body did not react as they’d hoped. This leaves Jaylin Noel in a potential FLEX-useful spot against a rough Titans secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks (knee) is not on Houston’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Marks was cleared after a full practice on Friday. Unfortunately, David Montgomery also got in a full practice and is questionable. Marks will retain RB2 status if Montgomery sits, but would probably go back in the FLEX bin if both are active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Per Aaron Wilson, he injured the knee in Wednesday’s practice and was experiencing discomfort. We don’t necessarily think Marks is in major trouble yet considering “discomfort” isn’t exactly a major injury, and he has been remarkably durable in game. But there is certainly a chance he’ll miss Week 10’s game against the Browns and fantasy managers should be prepared to pivot on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Marks should be good to go for the Texans’ Week 10 game against the Browns, though this backfield is awfully banged up. Marks totaled 18 carries and four targets last week, and should again handle a sizable workload this week. Unfortunately, he has not proven to be an efficient player and may need to score a touchdown to return RB2 value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: David Montgomery (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: It looks like Montgomery will miss another game because of the groin issue. Woody Marks has been seeing all the work in his absence. The role has yet to produce a meaningful fantasy outing. Still, fantasy managers can’t afford to fade a player seeing the bulk of the touches in an ascending offense. Marks remains a frustrating RB2 for Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks rushed 18 times for 70 yards in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers, adding one reception for four yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Marks was able to earn four targets in this one, but he caught only one of them. He was heavily involved as a rusher, regularly churning out short-to-intermediate ground gains, but without steady receiving production, he is stuck in the low-end RB2 tier with touchdown-dependent upside. He will qualify as such next week against the Browns if David Montgomery (groin) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: David Montgomery (groin) will not play in Week 9 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Per head coach DeMeco Ryans, Montgomery remains week-to-week. He did not practice today and we assume he won’t get on the field in any capacity this week. Woody Marks will make another start. Facing a down-horrific Chargers squad, Marks should finally get going after two underwhelming starts in Montgomery’s absence. He is a locked-in RB2 for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks rushed 19 times for 66 yards in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants, adding one catch for 15 yards on his only target.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Marks was the only game in town for the Texans, playing 54-of-61 snaps, but couldn’t convert the empty-box looks he was getting into real fantasy value. It was actually a reasonable game compared to most Texans box scores this year. Marks looked to have been hurt at one point in the third quarter but was able to escape the tent and go right back to work. Assuming David Montgomery (groin) is back after the bye week, Marks will head back to FLEX work on most fantasy rosters.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports David Montgomery (groin) will not play in Week 7 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: This will be the second game in a row that Montgomery has missed due to the groin injury he suffered in Week 5. Woody Marks, who totaled 17 touches in last week’s win over the Jaguars will again lead the Texans’ backfield. He has averaged 18.0 touches per game over the last two weeks and will be a volume-based RB2 with a chance at significant upside. Safeties Jalen Pitre (AC joint) and S Reed Blankenship (concussion) will also miss this week’s game against the Giants, putting the Texans down a handful of starters with one game left before their Week 8 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports that David Montgomery (groin) is not expected to play in Week 7 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Like we said yesterday, Montgomery is still seemingly in the week-to-week camp. Woody Marks and Dare Ogunbowale will likely split backfield touches this week. The Texans used both Marks and Jawhar Jordan last week, but Jordan suffered an injured reserve-worthy injury. Marks should be in starting lineups, but he may be more of a FLEX than a reliable RB2. Ogunbowale is a low-floor PPR dart throw.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: David Montgomery (groin) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: We were told early last week that Montgomery is week-to-week. Today’s absence suggests he is still week-to-week and will likely be ruled out again on Friday, though we do not know that for sure. We will provide an update before then if his status changes. In the meantime, Woody Marks will get the start again this week, potentially with less touch competition. Jawhar Jordan totaled 50 yards and a touchdown on seven total touches last week, but was surprisingly placed on injured reserve today. Dare Ogunbowale remains a receiving factor, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.headline: Peter Skoronski (hamstring) won’t play in Tennessee’s Week 10 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.analysis: Not exactly what the Titans needed, losing their best offensive lineman ahead of hosting the division leaders, but it’s what they’ll get. Skoronski should be considered questionable for Week 11 as well after not practicing at any point this week following Tennessee’s Week 9 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.headline: Peter Skoronski (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.analysis: The Titans’ starting left guard is very unlikely to play in Week 10 against the Jaguars, who field a top-tier defense. Skoronski has been sidelined since injuring his hamstring in Week 8 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.headline: Peter Skoronski (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.analysis: A DNP after the bye puts Skoronski on the wrong side of questionable to start the week. Skoronski went down with the hamstring issue during the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals. Garrett Dellinger took his spot in the lineup then and could be in line for his first career start this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.headline: Titans signed OG Peter Skoronski to a four-year, $100 million extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.analysis: Through three NFL seasons, Skoronski has established himself as a top-tier pass protector and run blocker in the Titans’ left guard spot. His 84.5 PFF pass-blocking grade and 73.2 PFF run-blocking grade from last season are both career highs and compare favorably to his counterparts across the league. His new deal includes $88 million guaranteed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Titans plan to exercise their fifth-year option on OL Peter Skoronski.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.analysis: There had been talks earlier in the offseason of the team working to extend their veteran offensive lineman but it appears as if the two sides fell short in a resolution, ultimately leading to the team exercising their fifth-year option. Skoronski took a massive step forward in his third professional season, ending 2025 with the sixth highest composite grades amongst guards. Expect the two sides to continue contract discussions into the new year as the Titans continue their rebuild with eyes on the future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.headline: Titans GM Mike Borgonzi said the team’s goal is to “get something done” with OL Peter Skoronski.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.analysis: Skoronski is entering his fifth-year option offseason off the best year of his career. The 24-year-old put up a 79.0 PFF grade — compared to 60.4 and 61.6 in his first two seasons — and turned into one of the main linchpins of the line. Given how much cap space they have and how few truly great players are in this free agent class, it wouldn’t be surprising to see the Titans try to get out in front of keeping Skoronski.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.headline: Titans LG Peter Skoronski (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.analysis: Skoronski never left Sunday’s game with the foot issue, giving Titans some home that he’s being held out of Wednesday’s practice as a precaution. Logan Bruss will likely take his spot in the lineup if Skoronski can’t suit up this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.headline: Titans OG Peter Skoronski returned to practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.analysis: Skoronski has missed the last three games after an emergency appendectomy, so it’s good to see him back out on the field. Since he was also listed as a full participant, it seems likely that the first round pick will return to the field on Sunday, which is good news for both Ryan Tannehill and Derrick Henry ahead of a game against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.headline: Titans LG Peter Skoronski (appendectomy) is expected to return to practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.analysis: Skoronski underwent an emergency appendectomy earlier this season and has missed the last three games as a result. Now, head coach Mike Vrabel said he expects Skoronski to return to practice this week, leaving the door open for a possible return in Week 5 against the Colts. We’ll know more about Skoronski’s status as practice begins on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.headline: Titans LG Pete Skoronski (appendectomy) will not play in Week 4 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/peter-skor.analysis: Skoronski has been out for two weeks because of the appendectomy and will miss at least one more game because of the issue. With Ryan Tannehill’s mobility declining in his age-35 season, the loss of a starting lineman is a notable issue for the Titans. Expect the Bengals to get to him multiple times in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is doubtful to play in Week 10 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Iosivas is still technically on injured reserve, although the team designated him to return this week. Fellow injured reserve players, CB Jalen Davis (hamstring) and OG Brian Parker (knee), are also listed as doubtful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Bengals designated Andrei Iosivas (thumb) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Iosivas will practice today for the first time since injuring his thumb in Week 2. The Bengals have 21 days to officially activate him from injured reserve, though he practiced in full today. He will likely reclaim his No. 3 role once healthy, though we don’t expect much fantasy value to come of it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Bengals placed Andrei Iosivas (thumb) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Head coach Zac Taylor said Iosivas is expected to return at some point this year. Colbie Young and Dohnte Meyers will both be in the running for the WR3 role, though it’s not a role that produces fantasy points unless one of Tee Higgins or Ja’Marr Chase goes down.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Andrei Iosivas caught his only target for seven yards in Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: He played 32-of-60 snaps as the Bengals have spread the ball around, letting Colvie Young (1/7 on one target) and Dohnte Meyers (0/0 on one target) also get involved against the Texans. Iosivas looks like a poor FLEX risk in Week 3 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Bengals WR Andrei Iosivas caught 2-of-2 targets for 20 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Iosivas was on the field for two drives, taking 10 of the first 13 snaps and playing alongside QB Joe Burrow. Fourth-round rookie WR Colbie Young subbed in, taking one snap on the second drive and remained on the field after the starters left. He looked good hauling in a 20-yard gain on 3rd-and-16 from QB Joe Flacco. The battle for the Bengals’ WR3 role continues with Iosivas seemingly ahead of the rookie.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. reports that WR Colbie Young and WR Andrei Iosivas are still competing for the Bengals’ WR3 role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Young, the rookie, “has seemingly stacked at least one impressive catch per day.” Iosivas has had “a few notable drops,” but he reportedly “appears as polished and athletic as ever at getting open.” Both players could be worth late-round picks in best ball formats, but neither one is likely to return FLEX value in re-draft without WR1 Ja’Marr Chase or WR2 Tee Higgins missing time. Iosivas is entering a contract year, and the team just spent a fourth-round pick on Young. An in-season breakout from the rookie would make things easier from a salary cap perspective. Dehner also notes that former CFL WR Dohnte Meyers “has been a talk of camp” thus far.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: ESPN’s Ben Baby reports that Bengals rookie WR Colbie Young is competing for OC Dan Pitcher’s “passing target No. 3" role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Baby’s practice notes indicate that incumbent No. 3 WR Andrei Iosivas and No. 1 TE Mike Gesicki are the other two competitors for the role, and both players “had productive springs.” Pitcher also said RB Chase Brown “can sometimes be viewed as a slot receiver,” but those types of comments are common in the summer and rarely pan out in the fall. Iosivas and Gesicki have been helpful contributors, but the fact that the team is searching for an answer at the No. 3 receiving role is indicative of their ceilings. Pitcher believes Young is “going to fight and battle” this summer, and thinks there are things Young “can do quickly and help us.” If he can actually become the team’s third-most voluminous target earner, he could pay off as a late-round best ball pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. believes the Bengals will add competition for Andrei Iosivas’ No. 3 receiver role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: This isn’t a front-page headline or anything, but OC Dan Pitcher did say that Iosivas “would probably tell you that there were points last year that he was happy with his play and points where he felt he needed to be better.” Entering the final year of his rookie contract, Iosivas could be pushed by Mitchell Tinsley or a draft pick for playing time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Andrei Iosivas caught 2-of-3 targets for 10 yards in the Bengals’ Week 18 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Iosivas proved to be a capable depth option in 2024, but there wasn’t much room for his role to grow this year. He appeared in all 17 games and totaled 34 grabs for 435 yards. His 2025 stat line was nearly identical to 2024’s, except for a notable drop in touchdowns. He scored six times last year compared to two touchdowns this time around. For fantasy purposes, Iosivas only cracks the weekly FLEX ranks when one of Ja’Marr Chase or Tee Higgins is sidelined. He won’t be on the redraft radar for his fourth NFL season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Bengals WR Tee Higgins (concussion) was not spotted at practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Oh, dear. This is unfortunate. Higgins practiced in a limited capacity on Wednesday. If he is unable to participate today, it likely means that he suffered a setback. The Bengals face the Dolphins this week. Both teams have been eliminated from playoff contention. With Higgins sidelined, the Bengals had WR Andrei Iosivas operate as the No. 2, while Mitchell Tinsley handled No. 3 duties.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (finger/rest) is not on Tennessee’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: A Friday tradition unlike any other. Pollard, somehow still a Titan, will suit up as an fringe RB2 against the Jaguars on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (finger/rest) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard practiced in full yesterday, despite the finger injury. The Titans added the rest label to his listing today, indicating his absence is simply load management. We do not expect his snaps to be impacted by the finger injury this weekend. Tyjae Spears (knee) resumed practicing, though, which could hurt Pollard’s snap share. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Titans are holding on to Tony Pollard at the trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Keeping a 29-year-old running back on the final year of his contract on your 1-7 cellar franchise is certainly a choice a team is allowed to make. We don’t know if it’s the one we’d make, but Pollard will be here to hover around RB2 value in games the Titans are pesky and RB3 value in games where the Titans offense plays as we’ve come to expect.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Titans aren’t interested in trading RB Tony Pollard.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: A previous report from Albert Breer suggested the team might be willing to trade Pollard, who is in the last year of his contract, for a fourth-round pick. Schefter threw cold water on that theory, reporting Tennessee isn’t interested in trading the 29-year-old running back. Showing fresh legs in recent weeks, Pollard is a solid RB2 the rest of the way even on a struggling Titans offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer thinks the Titans might be willing to trade away Tony Pollard in exchange for a fourth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Breer believes a fourth-round pick “seems like a lot” to give up for an aging running back who is set to enter free agency at the end of the year. So, Pollard might end up staying in Tennessee. Breer adds that the Titans could also consider trading away Calvin Ridley for a worse Day 3 pick, but he isn’t sure if the team is eager to get rid of pass catchers while they are attempting to develop their young quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 21 times for 117 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals, adding three receptions for 20 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard had his second-straight multi-touchdown game, scoring the first touchdown of the game on a 40-yard scamper with multiple missed tackles and a stiff-arm in the first quarter. With Tyjae Spears out, Pollard was the only Titans running back that got touches. He recovered his own fumble in the second half and added a one-yard score in the third quarter. He was also dropped for a safety in the third quarter on a head-scratching delayed hand-off to give the Bengals two points. Pollard enters the Titans’ Week 9 bye with several trade rumors swirling; if he is still in Tennessee, Pollard is a fantasy RB2 for Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: With two DNPs to start the week, Spears looks unlikely to play on Sunday. He also missed Week 7 with the knee issue. Tony Pollard racked up 28 touches and scored three rushing touchdowns. While we’re not banking on another multi-score outing anytime soon, his role alone is worth an RB2 ranking if Spears remains out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard had 25 rushes for 129 yards and three touchdowns in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns, adding three catches for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard, whose last big game before Sunday was against these same Browns in 2025, scored two first quarter touchdowns against a Cleveland rush defense that seemed uninterested in tackling Pollard. He scored a third rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter, and could have had a fourth score if not for a Browns goal line stand. Pollard has seen big workloads with Tyjae Spears (knee) sidelined but hadn’t done much with the opportunity before Sunday. The Titans offense operated quickly, using no-huddle through much of the game. That created more play volume that benefited Pollard and the rest of the Titans offense. As long as Spears remains sidelined, Pollard should remain in 12-team lineups next week against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Titans declared RB Tyjae Spears, WR Calvin Ridley, RB Nick Singleton, TE Kylen Granson, T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, DT Jackie Marshall, and CB Jaylon Jones inactive for Week 7 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: As Spears’ knee injury lingers, Tony Pollard continues to see a nice but ultimately meaningless workload in the Tennessee backfield. Pollard has seen at least 14 carries in every game since Week 2, though he only has eight receptions on the season. His lack of involvement in the pass game means Pollard will be a touchdown-dependent flex play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 19 times for 76 yards in the Titans’ Week 6 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard was targeted only once, finishing without a reception. Pollard has somewhat surprisingly banished No. 2 Tyjae Spears to pure breather back status, but the Titans’ overall play volume and touchdown opportunities are so limited that he is still struggling to achieve weekly RB2 status. He has nevertheless shored up his RB3/FLEX floor. That is where you will find him in the Week 7 ranks against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 10 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: If Spears can play, this is theoretically the kind of blowout game script that sets him up for FLEX value via PPR scam. We wouldn’t advise chasing it, but we wouldn’t be surprised if it happened. Spears got in a full practice today, which would seem to leave him on the optimistic side of questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears was listed as a limited participant on today’s injury report, theoretically giving him a chance to play in Week 10 against the Jaguars’ elite run defense. Spears’ potential return could lower Tony Pollard’s snap share a tad, though Spears does not need to be rostered in 10-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears’ lingering knee issue appeared to get worse a few weeks ago when the team scratched him for Week 7. He was held out the following week and even their recent bye doesn’t seem to have done the trick. Tony Pollard will continue to see a glut of touches until Spears gets healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) won’t play in Tennessee’s Week 8 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears had three DNPs and has not practiced since last Thursday. Michael Carter filled down as the third-down back last week, though all that actually meant is that Tony Pollard got full-time workload. We expect that to continue in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: With two DNPs to start the week, Spears looks unlikely to play on Sunday. He also missed Week 7 with the knee issue. Tony Pollard racked up 28 touches and scored three rushing touchdowns. While we’re not banking on another multi-score outing anytime soon, his role alone is worth an RB2 ranking if Spears remains out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears had been playing through the knee issue for a few weeks before being sidelined because of it in Week 7. A DNP today suggests he will miss at least one more game. Tony Pollard will handle the bulk of the backfield touches again this week. He remains a volume-based RB2 versus the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Titans declared RB Tyjae Spears, WR Calvin Ridley, RB Nick Singleton, TE Kylen Granson, T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, DT Jackie Marshall, and CB Jaylon Jones inactive for Week 7 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: As Spears’ knee injury lingers, Tony Pollard continues to see a nice but ultimately meaningless workload in the Tennessee backfield. Pollard has seen at least 14 carries in every game since Week 2, though he only has eight receptions on the season. His lack of involvement in the pass game means Pollard will be a touchdown-dependent flex play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 7 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears has been active off a questionable line twice since Week 4. We’d imagine he’d get there again after a limited Friday session. The touch upside just isn’t there for him to be more than a deep-league FLEX play at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears notched a one-yard carry and seven-yard reception in the Titans’ Week 6 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears’ two touches were a new season low, though he’s now been held to three or fewer in three of the past four weeks. The Titans have decided Tony Pollard is more of an every-down back than committee member, erasing what had been low-end FLEX status for his “1B” backfield partner. Despite his supposed contingency value, Spears is droppable if you find yourself in a roster crunch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears is active for Tennessee’s Week 6 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: He was questionable after a full practice, but will play against the Colts as a reasonable-if-unexciting FLEX option. Inactive for the Titans are S Kevin Winston Jr., CB Alontae Taylor (coach’s decision), RB Nick Singleton, T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, TE Kylen Granson, DL Jordan Elliott and DT Jackie Marshall.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylon-moo.headline: Chiefs ruled out RT Jaylon Moore (concussion) for Week 10 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylon-moo.analysis: Moore will unfortunately miss this weekend’s game against the Falcons, who field a capable defensive tackle unit. Atlanta has not defended the run well, though, so the Chiefs should be able to get by without him. Chiefs CB Mansoor Delane (shoulder) is questionable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylon-moo.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylon-moo.analysis: Right tackle Jaylon Moore was also held out of practice with a concussion. Rice went down with the hamstring issue in Week 4. Even with a bye week to heal before Week 6, he wasn’t ready to return. A DNP today suggests he will miss at least one more game. Xavier Worthy led the Chiefs with seven catches for 73 yards in his absence last week. He would be in line for another high-usage game if Rice remains out for Week 7’s game against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylon-moo.headline: Chiefs OT Jaylon Moore (illness) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylon-moo.analysis: Chiefs RG Trey Smith (back) joins Moore in the questionable column, while LT Josh Simmons (personal) has once again been ruled out. On the plus side, both Moore and Smith are expected to play, “barring setbacks.” This is a consequential game for the Chiefs (5-3) and the Bills (5-2) that could shift playoff seeding down the road. The Bills notably lost star DT Ed Oliver (biceps) for the season last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylon-moo.headline: ESPN’s Nate Taylor reports that Chiefs LT Josh Simmons “is expected to rejoin the team in a few weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylon-moo.analysis: Yesterday, The Athletic’s Jesse Newell identified Week 11 as a “natural target date” for Simmons to resume playing. Taylor agrees, writing, “a logical time for Simmons to return to the Chiefs could be in early November, during the team’s bye” in Week 10. Until Simmons returns, veteran OT Jaylon Moore will continue manning the left tackle spot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylon-moo.headline: Chiefs agreed to terms with OT Jaylon Moore, formerly of the 49ers, on a two-year, $30 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylon-moo.analysis: $21.24 million is fully guaranteed at signing per ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Moore has been Trent Williams’ understudy with the 49ers for the last four years after they selected him in the fifth round of the 2021 NFL Draft. He has just 831 snaps in four years with the 49ers, but finished 2024 with a 73.1 PFF pass block rating and started five games down the stretch. This is a projection contract for Moore, but the Chiefs clearly believe there’s something here. Moore will now be penciled in as Kansas City’s left tackle, protecting Patrick Mahomes’ blindside after a tough year for the trio of D.J. Humphries, Wanya Morris, and Kingsley Suamataia. Suamataia reportedly is moving to left guard this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylon-moo.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said G Aaron Banks (knee) and T Jaylon Moore (quad) will miss the final two games of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylon-moo.analysis: Banks has an MCL sprain and Moore had a quadriceps strain. Aaron Banks wraps up the third of four years on his rookie deal with a career-best 65.4 PFF blocking grade and will likely profile as a starting guard in the final year of his contract next season. Moore will be a free agent this offseason and has played well in limited time in each of the last two years, he could be an intriguing low-cost addition for a team looking for a swing tackle, or perhaps a team looking to give him a chance to start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylon-moo.headline: 49ers LT Jaylon Moore (quad) is questionable to return in Week 16 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylon-moo.analysis: Moore got the start at left tackle with Trent Williams sidelined. He went down in the third quarter, limped off the field, and headed straight for the blue tent. Spencer Buford has taken his spot in the lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylon-moo.headline: 49ers selected Western Michigan OG Jaylon Moore with the No. 155 overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylon-moo.analysis: Moore (6'4/311) ultimately became a three-year starter at left tackle for Western Michigan after signing as a tight end and transitioning to defensive end his redshirt year. Moore, who earned second-team All-MAC honors in both 2019 and 2020, tested as an 8.76 RAS athlete as a guard at his pro day, showing out better than the size-adjusted 80th percentile in the bench (27), vertical (30.5 inches) and broad (8 feet, 10 inches). Moore’s athleticism is apparent on film, a smooth, rhythmic mover that explodes out of his stance and picks off targets in the second level and as a lead-blocker on screens. He comes with a ropey 82-inch wingspan and massive 11-inch hands. But Moore’s lack of anchor and propensity to mirror too high and narrow led to issues against both speed and power. He gave up seven sacks and 28 pressures over 1,129 pass-pro reps to a low-level of competition. We think his best fit in the NFL is kicking inside to guard for a zone-running team, where Moore’s mobility will be accentuated and his lack of play strength will be mitigated.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy (hamstring) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Patrick Mahomes will have his speedy wide receiver on the field this weekend. Unfortunately for Worthy, he may be operating in a reduced role with Josh Downs now in Kansas City. Worthy can still be rostered in 12-team formats, but his play could be even more volatile.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: We got word early on Wednesday that Worthy would suit up for practice. He ended up being a full participant and remained full today, putting him firmly on track to play in Week 10 against the Falcons. Worthy is down to being a touchdown-dependent FLEX with Josh Downs now on the roster, but his presence helps out Patrick Mahomes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy (hamstring) practiced on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Head coach Andy Reid told reporters Worthy is “actually feeling pretty good.” Worthy went down with a hamstring injury late in the Chiefs’ win over the Jets on Sunday. The fact that he’s able to practice in any capacity today suggests he will be good to go for Week 10 against the Falcons. With Josh Downs now in the mix for targets, Worthy’s days as a relevant fantasy option appear to be over.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy sustained a hamstring injury in Week 9 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy hobbled off the field after a fourth quarter reception in the KC victory. It appeared to be the serious kind of hamstring injury but we won’t know the extent of it until the team tests the speedy receiver. Worthy had caught all six of his targets for 48 yards before exiting the game. An absence of Worthy would likely free up more targets for Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice. The team’s running backs could also see an uptick in targets if Worthy misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 3-of-6 targets for 13 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: With Rashee Rice back after missing two games because of a hamstring issue, Worthy was relegated to WR2 duties once again. Per usual, he didn’t do much while Rice racked up PPR-friendly receptions. Worthy was, however, the intended target on a pair of red zone attempts in the third quarter. Pat Surtain easily broke up one pass that was left a bit short and Worthy actually fought to knock another one down that should have been intercepted by Riley Moss. Worthy has topped 25 yards in one game with Rice again. He’s simply not a part of the Chiefs’ plans on offense when they’re at full strength. Fantasy managers can feel free to cut him loose on this week’s run of waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 3-of-6 targets for 11 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 7 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy struggled to separate from primary coverage of the Seahawks throughout, also committing a drop in a crucial situation in the second half. The Chiefs continue to show hesitancy in utilizing Worthy in a downfield role, which is of particular concern for his fantasy managers considering the absence of Tyquan Thornton. Worthy is better left on fantasy benches ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the stingy Broncos, particularly if Rashee Rice returns from injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught all seven of his targets for 73 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: The Chiefs, with Rashee Rice (hamstring) sidelined, made every effort to force feed Worthy near the line of scrimmage in this one. That resulted in Worthy leading the KC offense in both targets and receiving yards, with a long reception of 19 yards. Most of his Week 6 touches were of the gadget variety. Increased usage should give Worthy a sturdy PPR floor for now. He should be considered a flex play next week against the tough Seattle secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Rice appeared to have a good chance at suiting up for Week 6 when Andy Reid spoke about it after Week 4’s win over the Raiders. Reid only said he “tweaked” his hammy. Even with a bye week to rest, it looks like Rice is now on the wrong side of questionable for Week 6. With Tyquan Thornton on IR, Xavier Worthy may be tasked with WR1 duties this week. He totaled four catches for 70 yards in his last outing and would be a solid FLEX play versus the Chargers if Rice can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 4-of-7 targets for 70 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 4 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy saw a season-high seven targets in this one after Rashee Rice (hamstring) exited just a few plays into the game. Worthy came up with a handful of key plays for the Chiefs, with his biggest coming on a 41-yard reception that put the Chiefs in position for a short touchdown pass to Tyquan Thornton a few plays later. The Chiefs now head into their Week 5 bye, but they could be down multiple receivers, with Rice and Thornton (ankle) both suffering injuries in this one. While we don’t yet know the extent of Rice’s injury, Thornton’s ankle injury looked like a potential season-ender. Worthy could well be worth a stash in leagues where he is still available, as he could soon be the top receiver for the Chiefs when they return in Week 6 to face the Chargers. Second-year receiver Jalen Royals, who ran 21 routes in this game, could also see an expanded role in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 2-of-2 targets for 20 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy was also shaken up by a big hit but was never announced with an injury. Patrick Mahomes attempted only 24 passes this afternoon, but that’s still a disappointing target total for the third-year pro. 23-year-old Worthy is now sitting on just 10 catches for 63 yards through the Chiefs’ first three games. Even with this offense showing major year-over-year improvement, it’s getting harder to keep the WR4 faith with Worthy. The Raiders are a plus Week 4 matchup in Vegas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes Blake Corum’s development as a pass catcher has helped the Rams deal with increasing blitz rates.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Leaning on Corum and No. 1 RB Kyren Williams has helped the Rams achieve a three-game winning streak, and Atkins notes that the Rams are 4-0 this season when Corum plays at least 30 percent of the offensive snaps. His development as a receiver and pass protector has erased run-pass tells pre-snap. Corum’s development as a weapon in the screen game, specifically, has allowed the Rams to beat the increasing blitz rates they have faced since Davante Adams (hamstring) was lost as a downfield receiving weapon. Corum belongs in starting lineups on a weekly basis at this point, as he establishes himself as a reliable RB2 in both real life and fantasy football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed 11 times for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 9 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum continued to split drives with Kyren Williams, but he was easily the better back in Sunday’s win over the Commanders. Corum ripped off several strong runs on the opening drive of the third quarter and capped a 69-yard offensive drive with a two-yard score to put the Rams up 13-10. He failed to haul in either of the two targets that came his way, but this was the kind of fantasy week we have come to expect from Corum, who has now had double-digit carries in three straight games. He has also found the end zone in each of those games and will be a boom-or-bust RB2 in Week 10 against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Kyren Williams had 16 rushes for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers, adding one catch for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: The more efficient Blake Corum had 11 rushes for 73 yards and did not see a target in a run-heavy Rams offense. Williams led the LA backfield in routes but only had one look from Matthew Stafford. He was stuffed at the line of scrimmage a handful of times in the first half. The rushing volume in the Rams offense of late should make both Williams and Corum fantasy relevant every week, including next week against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum had 11 rushes for 73 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Kyren Williams led the LA backfield with 16 carries for 56 yards. Corum was much more efficient as a rusher against the Chargers, regularly bursting through the line of scrimmage and shedding tacklers on a couple second half runs. The Rams have been run heavy since Davante Adams went down with a serious hamstring injury a few weeks ago. That’s generated more opportunity for Corum, who last week had 17 rushes. He ranks 44th among running backs in expected fantasy points per game in 2026. That kind of usage should make Corum flex-viable for now. He gets the Commanders in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum had 17 rushes for 93 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders, adding one catch for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum had the lead in carries until the final drive of the game, when the Rams turned to Kyren Williams to seal the victory following a short-lived Raiders comeback. Corum’s fantasy day could have been much bigger if he hadn’t had two touchdowns called back on penalties along with another chunk gain. Despite running cold on luck, Corum’s role continued to grow even after Williams complained publicly about the backfield workload split last week. Williams logged 18 routes against the Raiders while Corum ran just nine. Look for the Rams to be more run heavy in the coming weeks with Davante Adams out indefinitely with a hamstring injury, putting Corum in play as a weekly flex. He gets the Chargers in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed nine times for 42 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, adding two receptions, 18 yards and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum got the Rams’ second drive all to himself before re-entering the game on the fourth drive and splitting reps with Kyren Williams thereafter. Rams coach Sean McVay seemingly rewarded Corum for powering through contact on a third-down conversion from the Cardinals’ 19-yard line by allowing him to remain on the field for the scoring-position sequence. Two plays later, Corum was scampering upfield for a 15-yard receiving score after hauling in a pass in the flats. He ran hard the rest of the way, but the Rams got off just 20 rushing attempts today, surprisingly playing in a trailing game script for the entire second half, as the Cardinals achieved victory via voluminous field goals. Corum is an RB3/FLEX against the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed five times for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills, adding 53 yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum provided a much needed spark in relief of lead back Kyren Williams, contributing three clutch receptions that kept drives alive in addition to a third quarter touchdown. That said, his modest volume continued while Williams turned in a third straight game with 20 or more opportunities, including 28 total targets in that stretch. Corum remains a top fantasy handcuff but is unlikely to return useful fantasy weeks for as long as Williams is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed five times for 14 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles, adding a seven-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum was employed as a pure breather back this afternoon, as he got out-touched 26-6 by Kyren Williams. Four of Corum’s handles came on one first quarter series. With the 1-2 Rams staring down the barrel of 1-3 as they trailed by two scores for several quarters, they circled the wagons around their most established players, and that does not yet include Corum. The third-year pro will undoubtedly pop up for more 10-12 carry afternoons, but he’s fading from FLEX relevance as Williams gets re-established in the low-end RB1 mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams need more from Blake Corum in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Atkins believes Puka Nacua’s (groin) impending return will lighten the box, in turn making life easier on the run game and preventing the opposition from blitzing as frequently as the Broncos did last week. Corum has not established himself as a reliable weekly contributor in fantasy. Perhaps positive impacts from Nacua’s return trickle down to the Rams’ No. 2 running back. Kyren Williams remains a locked-in starter. Keep Corum stashed for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 15 times for 88 yards in the Rams’ Week 3 loss to the Broncos, adding 70 yards on six receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Williams’ 70 yards through the air were a career-high mark in receiving for a single game, returning yet another RB1 fantasy performance despite sharing backfield work with Blake Corum. Corum managed only 15 yards on six carries and caught two passes for zero additional yards. Furthermore, Corum has still not seen a carry inside the red zone through three games of the 2026 season. Williams remains a surefire RB1 ahead of a difficult matchup against the Eagles in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: As usual, Kamara’s back listing has not prevented him in any real way from playing. A potential Travis Etienne activation off injured reserve could cut into his FLEX value in Week 10, but if Etienne stays on IR, Kamara will be a reasonable play against a rough Panthers run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: The Saints’ veteran running back is just having his reps managed. With Audric Estime playing well and Travis Etienne (hamstring) potentially returning, Kamara does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats at this time. Kamara will continue to chip in on passing downs, though. Backup RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: We expect to see Kamara listed with his typical NIR-rest/back designation when the team’s official injury report is released later today. An update will be provided if this is not the case. With Travis Etienne (hamstring) now practicing and Audric Estime playing well, Kamara is barely fantasy-relevant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara rushed six times for 32 yards in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns, adding three catches for 17 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: The Saints added Audric Estime via waivers on Monday and he went on to lead the team in carries today. He saw 15 rushes plus one target. Estime also found the end zone after Kamara was tackled at the two-yard line. Kamara was the team’s primary back on passing downs, but his role between the tackles remained incredibly limited. With Travis Etienne potentially returning next week, his role could take another hit in Week 10. He remains a low-upside RB4 for his upcoming matchup with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara has no injury designation for Week 9 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara was limited due to rest and a back injury, but unsurprisingly, he’ll be good to go for Sunday’s contest against the Browns. The Saints’ run game is a disaster, but Kamara should be involved enough in the pass game to make him a decent FLEX play for that contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: The way the team listed Kamara indicates that the back injury will not keep him from playing, but he is clearly still hurt. Kamara has been entirely ineffective this season and can only be viewed as a touchdown-dependent FLEX. CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was unable to practice today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Donaldson aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 7 against the Steelers and did not return. He also entered the league’s concussion protocol after the game. A limited session today means he’s making progress on both fronts. He should be good to go for Week 9. The same is true of Alvin Kamara, who got a rest day today, despite his back injury also being noted on the report. Both backs will mix in behind Kendre Miller on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara rushed six times for five yards in the Saints’ Week 8 loss to the Steelers, adding seven receptions for 57 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Tyler Shough ended up leading the Saints with seven rushing yards. Yikes. Kamara was effective as a receiver out of the backfield, but to say that New Orleans struggled to run the ball is quite the understatement as they finished with 18 yards on 17 attempts. The good news for fantasy managers that used Kamara is that he was effective out of the backfield as a receiver, but it’s a modest day for the 31-year-old. Kamara and the Saints will try and get something going after a bye against the Browns in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was removed from the injury report for Week 7’s game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara was still listed as limited in Friday’s practice, but the Saints feel confident enough in his health to clear him for Week 7. Kamara found the end zone last week on a 31-yard reception, but has largely been inefficient with his touches this season. He seen 14 opportunities to Kendre Miller’s 30 over the last two weeks and will be hard to trust as anything more than a touchdown-dependent RB3 against the Steelers. The only players on the Saints carrying injury designations into the weekend are guard Cesar Ruiz (knee) and DL Nathan Sheperd (illness). Both are listed as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: He’s played through this listing for a few weeks now, and though he’ll sometimes get dinged up in game, appears no worse for the wear. Kendre Miller feels like the more viable back in a normal game script right now, with Kamara playing more on passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.headline: Derrick Harmon (foot) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 10 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.analysis: He got in a full practice on Friday and spoke with reporters as well. Based on that, we’d guess he’s got a good chance to be activated off injured reserve and play against the Bengals in the first week of his 21-day window.
