https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.headline: Steelers opened Derrick Harmon’s (foot) 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.analysis: The Steelers’ talented interior defender reportedly has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Bengals. Harmon suffered his foot injury early in Week 4 against the Browns. This season he has totaled 12 tackles, one TFL, 1.5 NFL sacks and a forced fumble. Getting him back will be a plus for the Steelers’ defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Derrick Harmon (foot) will be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.analysis: He’ll be eligible to return in Week 9. Harmon had shown some increased pass rush ability in his four games so far this season and this is a tough loss for the Steelers defense in the short-term.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Derrick Harmon (foot) “is expected to miss a few weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.analysis: Rapoport noted that IR is an option, but the injury is not considered long-term. Harmon suffered the foot injury on Thursday against the Browns. He was carted to the locker room and was later spotted wearing a boot on the sidelines. The second-year tackle had 1.5 sacks in three games before leaving Week 4 early. His potential breakout campaign will now be put on hold for upwards of a month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.headline: Steelers coach Mike Tomlin said DT Derrick Harmon (knee) won’t play in Pittsburgh’s Week 14 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.analysis: That’s two weeks in a row on the sideline for Harmon, who the Steelers badly missed on Sunday as the Bills ran all over them. Derrick Henry deserves a small rankings bump based on this news.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.headline: Steelers coach Mike Tomlin said LT Broderick Jones (neck) won’t play in Pittsburgh’s Week 13 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.analysis: Jones played 49 snaps in Week 12 before giving way to Calvin Anderson at left tackle. Anderson is the likely replacement in Week 13. Tomlin also said that rookie DT Derrick Harmon (knee) will miss this game as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.headline: Steelers DT Derrick Harmon (knee) is active for Week 3 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.analysis: The No. 21 overall pick will make his NFL debut today after missing the first two weeks of the season with a knee issue. Running back Kaleb Johnson is active despite making a catastrophic blunder on a kickoff last week that resulted in a Seahawks touchdown. He won’t return kicks but could still be in the backfield mix for a few snaps. Inactive for the Steelers are CB Joey Porter Jr., S DeShon Elliott, OLB Alex Highsmith, G Andrus Peat, and DT Esezi Otomewo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.headline: Steelers DT Derrick Harmon (knee) is questionable for Week 3’s game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.analysis: He got in a full session on Friday after two limited sessions on Wednesday and Thursday and looks to be on the optimistic side of questionable to make his NFL debut in Week 3. Harmon suffered an MCL sprain in Pittsburgh’s preseason finale and, should he be active on Sunday, will wind up missing about a month as forecasted at the time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.headline: Steelers DT Derrick Harmon (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.analysis: Harmon could still suit up on Sunday, even if he remains limited tomorrow, but we would expect him to be on a snap count if that is the case. The Steelers need their rookie defensive tackle back badly. Porter remains sidelined by his hamstring injury and does not appear to be close to returning.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.headline: Steelers DT Derrick Harmon (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-ha.analysis: Harmon’s return to practice could not have come at a better time. Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin already said CB Joey Porter Jr. (hamstring) is “questionable at best” to play in Week 3 against the Patriots. He was unable to practice, as was S DeShon Elliott (knee). Steelers LB Alex Highsmith (ankle) is likely due for an extended absence, though he was able to avoid being placed on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) is not on Pittsburgh’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: We’ll see if he goes back to being a thorn in the ceiling cases for the remainder of the Steelers’ offensive players against the Bengals. Skowronek has no standalone value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) is inactive for Week 8 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Steelers declared WR Ben Skowronek, QB Drew Allar, QB Will Howard, CB Brandin Echols, RB Eli Heidenreich, and CB Doneiko Slaughter inactive for Week 8 against the Browns. Skowronek will miss this game with a calf injury while Echols and Slaughter deal with hamstring injuries. Howard will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 8 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: He was limited all three days. Skowronek carries no standalone value but could eat into snaps for the other Steelers receivers if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek is not fantasy-relevant and should not be picked up in 12-team formats. His potential return provides Aaron Rodgers with a trusted target. Skowronek also serves as a reliable run blocker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) will not play in Pittsburgh’s Week 7 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Ruled out on Thursday before traveling, Skowronek probably has a real chance to get back in Week 8. With Marquez Valdes-Scantling now on the roster, Skowronek has likely lost whatever desperation fantasy value he might have had either way.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Ben Skowronek (leg) has been ruled out for Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: We weren’t exactly worried about Skowronek siphoning many targets away, but with him out of the pecking order entirely Germie Bernard should be a wheels-up WR3 for Week 6 now that both Skowronek and Roman Wilson have been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek has been ruled out for Week 5 against the Colts with a calf injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: There hasn’t been a lot of word on what happened to Skowronek. He went into the blue medical tent in the second quarter to have his leg looked at and then headed into the locker room. When the Steelers returned the kickoff to start the second half, Skowronek, who is a key special teamer, was not on the field. He was ruled out shortly after. With Michael Pittman Jr. already out, the Steelers are getting a little thin with their wide receiver depth.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek caught his only target for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 1 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: It was a play-action pass where Skowronek went against the flow of the defense and it almost operated like a screen, with Steelers receivers blocking downfield to create an easy crease for the 28-year-old receiver. Skowronek doesn’t need to be chased in fantasy leagues after only playing 10 of 53 snaps for the Steelers in this one. He’s operating more-or-less in a timeshare for Pittsburgh’s third receiver role with Roman Wilson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers re-signed WR Ben Skowronek to a two-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek caught five passes for 69 yards with the Steelers last season while playing in a very limited role. Skowronek’s 46 routes run and five targets marked the second fewest amongst any receiver on the team in 2024. A good blocker and willing special teamer, Skowronek probably has an inside track to a roster spot even if what he does isn’t worthy of fantasy interest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers WR Ben Skowronek (hip) is questionable to return to Week 16 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek was involved early, catching both targets for 25 yards, but departed early in the second quarter with a hip injury and was deemed questionable to return by the team. Already shorthanded at wide receiver due to the continued absence of George Pickens, it will be up to Calvin Austin, Van Jefferson, and Mike Williams to step up for a team fighting to clinch the AFC North against their great division rivals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers will be in line for a FLEX-worthy workload against the Titans. The good news is that the over/under has climbed to 46.5 after last week’s date with Joey Fagnano, leaving Meyers as a more viable touchdown threat in Week 10 than he was in a limited passing workload against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers was limited at today’s practice. He is on track to play through the injury this week after doing so successfully last week, along with a hamstring injury. The Jaguars’ dominance has rendered Meyers somewhat of a touchdown-reliant FLEX starter, though this is a soft matchup against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers was listed with hamstring and ankle injuries last week, but played through them in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens. It is discouraging that he did not practice after a mini-bye, but the good news is that he only has the ankle designation now, no hamstring. Meyers is not yet in jeopardy of missing Week 10, but will need to practice in some fashion for fantasy managers to feel confident about his chances of playing against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 4-of-6 targets for 65 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: All four of Meyers’ receptions came before the half in what remained a tighter game until just before the half, when alpha wide receiver Parker Washington took a simple slant for a 50-yard touchdown with under a minute remaining before the break. As has been the case on numerous occasions this season, Jacksonville coasted in the second half, limiting overall pass volume after the break. Meyers narrowly missed his first touchdown since Week 3 as he was tackled at the one on the team’s first possession. He remains a viable FLEX option ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: The Jaguars keep many of their injured players limited all week, Meyers included. The move was likely just a conservative measure, given the short practice week. The Jaguars will likely take a run-heavy approach against a Ravens team playing with their QB3. Meyers is just a FLEX, given the expected game script.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: The veteran receiver played through both ailments in Week 8 but was limited to only 54 percent of the team’s offensive snaps in a blowout win. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his status in the coming days, with the expectation that he continues to play through the injuries against the Ravens on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 2-of-3 targets for 24 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers wasn’t the only Jags pass catcher to post an empty box score in a 42-7 obliteration where Trevor Lawrence attempted only 14 passes, though he’s now been held to two or fewer receptions in 4-of-7 games. For a supposed “floor” player, that is not going to cut it, especially since Meyers is not the ceiling threat in this offense. With volume likely to remain in short supply for Thursday’s short-week tilt with the Lamar Jackson-less Ravens, Meyers is not a compelling WR3 for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle/hamstring) is active for Jacksonville’s Week 8 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: As expected based on the morning reporting. Meyers can be trusted as a WR4/FLEX mix against the Colts. Inactive for the Jaguars are S Antonio Johnson (knee), WR CJ Williams, CB Alijah Huzzie, LB Jamal Hill, DE Wesley Williams and DT Albert Regis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jakobi Meyers (ankle/hamstring) is “good to go” for Week 8 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers was limited in the Jags’ first two practices of the week before being downgraded to a DNP on Friday. The team listed him as questionable, though the DNP was likely maintenance in hindsight. Meyers has topped three catches or 50 yards in just two games this year. He did, however, see 10 targets in the Jags’ Week 6 loss to the Texans before their bye. Meyers is in the WR4 mix for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring, ankle) did not practice Friday and is questionable to play in Week 8 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers managed back-to-back limited sessions to begin the week of preparation but was downgraded to a “DNP” Friday, ultimately drawing the questionable tag for Week 8 against the Colts. An absence could require additional offensive snaps for two-way player Travis Hunter and a slight uptick in route rate for Brian Thomas Jr and Josh Cameron. This is one to monitor for fantasy managers of all Jacksonville pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: He practiced on Friday and, as it was last week, the Jaguars cleared him with just one practice. He’ll be an upside RB2 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten sat out all three practices before playing in last week’s Thursday Night Football game, totaling 12 carries in the process. We tentatively expect him to play in Week 10 against the Titans, and he should be in fantasy football lineups even if he sits out or is limited on Friday. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten was listed as DNP with the same ankle/foot injuries he played through last Thursday. He was clearly limited in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens and it is a bit discouraging that he starts out Week 10 not practicing after a mini-bye. It’s still early in the week, so this may just be injury maintenance for the 23-year-old. A practice later in the week will ease fantasy managers’ concerns, but a split in touches with Chris Rodriguez is certainly on the table again for Week 10 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 12 times for 29 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten started after failing to practice in any capacity this week, capping off the opening drive with a score from one yard out. He would split time with Chris Rodriguez for the rest of the first half before giving way to the combination of Rodriguez and special teams ace Ameer Abdullah for the bulk of the second half with the game in hand. Tuten should see his volume tick back up toward lead back territory when the Jaguars face off against the Titans in Week 10, where he will return to RB2 status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) is “good to go” after completing his pre-game workout for Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: The Jaguars have routinely killed the clock with their efficient ground game this season, oftentimes pulling Trevor Lawrence early. With the Ravens starting QB Joe Fagnano (ankle) tonight, the Jaguars should again enjoy a run-heavy game script, expectedly playing with a lead. Tuten is an RB1, having avoided suffering a setback this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) “should be” good for Week 9 against the Ravens, barring any pre-game setbacks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten did not practice at all this week, though the Jaguars notably kept many injured players limited, so it is possible that his absences were mostly precautionary. Tuten injured his ankle and foot in Week 8 against the Colts, but still managed to total 159 scrimmage yards, two catches and two touchdowns. He is an RB1 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Jaguars coach Liam Coen told reporters earlier today that Tuten will be a game-time decision for this week’s Thursday Night Football game. He also told reporters that Tuten would get in a limited session today. Unfortunately, that did not happen. Tuten logged his third DNP of the week instead. Conversely, Chris Rodriguez (hand) logged three limited sessions and was removed from the injury report. As things currently stand, Tuten is on the wrong side of questionable, while Rodriguez appears to be the likely starter. Rodriguez should be added in all 10- and 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Liam Coen said Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) will be a game-time decision for Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten did not practice on Tuesday. Coen told reporters he would get in a limited session today. Tuten himself told Coen he feels better today and he toughed it out through the injury on Sunday. He appears to be on the right side of questionable for Thursday’s contest, but fantasy managers will want to check inactives before kickoff to be sure. If he can’t go, Chris Rodriguez will get the bulk of the carries for the Jags.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) was not spotted at Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: After being an estimated DNP on Monday, Tuten was not spotted at Tuesday’s practice. With the Jaguars playing Thursday, this is a bit concerning for his Week 9 availability, as he will likely need to get in a limited practice on Wednesday if he hopes to suit up. In the event he can’t go, Chris Rodriguez, who ran for 41 yards and a touchdown on six carries last week, would be in line to handle a significant workload against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten briefly left the team’s Week 8 win in the first quarter but returned to amass 159 total yards and two touchdowns against the overmatched Colts. Fantasy managers will want to track his status closely as the team makes a quick turn to face the Ravens on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.headline: Eagles released OT Fred Johnson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.analysis: Johnson is a decent bet to receive interest via the waiver wire. He has played for the Eagles since 2023, logging 1,589 offensive and special teams snaps combined. While he primarily contributed as a traditional tackle, the Eagles would at times line him up as an extra blocker at tight end. He is not a reliable starter, but can still contribute in the right situation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.headline: Eagles C Drew Kendall (knee) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.analysis: With C Cam Jurgens now a Raven, Kendall is the Eagles’ starting center. Unfortunately, he is not practicing this week, leaving practice squad C/OG Jake Majors as his potential Week 5 fill-in. Potential starting OT Fred Johnson (knee) is practicing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.headline: Eagles re-signed OL Fred Johnson to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.analysis: Johnson returns to the Eagles after starting eight games for them in 2025. The 28-year-old swing tackle has spent each of the last three seasons in Philly, developing as a valuable piece on the offensive line. Though he did not find a starting job elsewhere, Johnson has the opportunity to contribute to the Eagles’ blocking under a new offensive line coach in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.headline: Jaguars traded T Fred Johnson to the Eagles in exchange for for a 2026 seventh-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.analysis: Johnson returns to the Eagles after signing with the Jaguars in March. The 28-year-old will likely be a backup bookend for Philadelphia; a role that he served for the majority of the 2024 season with the club.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.headline: Jaguars signed T Fred Johnson, formerly of the Eagles, to a one-year contract
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.analysis: The six-year veteran played the last two seasons with the Eagles. He started six of 17 games during the 2024 regular season and appeared in all four games during the playoffs, including Super Bowl LIX. The Jaguars have already signed free agents Patrick Mekari and Robert Hainsey this offseason in hopes of bolstering their offensive line. Pro Football Focus graded the Jacksonville offensive line as the league’s 12th-worst pass blocking unit in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.headline: Eagles DT Milton Williams (foot) was limited in Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.analysis: The quietly productive defensive tackle was added to the injury report this week after practicing with a clean bill of health in Week 1. His consecutive limited participant designations are a positive sign for his Monday night availability. CB Isaiah Rodgers (hand) and LB Devin White (ankle) continued practicing in full. Backup LT Fred Johnson (thumb)

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.headline: Bucs signed G Fred Johnson, formerly of the Bengals, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.analysis: The Bengals released Johnson this week after adding La’el Collins to their offensive line. He’ll join a Bucs offensive line graded by Pro Football Focus as the NFL’s fifth-best pass-blocking unit in 2021.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.headline: Bengals waived OG Fred Johnson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.analysis: Johnson was originally extended a tender offer as a restricted free agent, an offer the team announced he signed on Tuesday morning. The Bengals were no longer interested in bringing back Johnson after adding La’el Collins, however, so they are sending him to waivers. Any team that claims him off waivers will owe the roughly $2.4 million value of the restricted free agent tender Johnson signed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.headline: Bengals re-signed OL Fred Johnson to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.analysis: The Bengals last week extended a right or first refusal to Johnson, a restricted free agent. Johnson in 2021 was the team’s top-graded run blocker, per Pro Football Focus. He’ll likely be a rotational guard in 2022 for what will be an improved Cincinnati offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.headline: Bengals extended a right of first refusal tender to restricted free agent OL Fred Johnson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/fred-johns.analysis: He would make $2.433 million on the tender in 2022. He’s undrafted, so there would be no compensation if another team made an offer for Johnson. A depth piece for the Bengals, Johnson was the team’s top-graded run blocking tackle in 2021, per Pro Football Focus. He should have a rotational role in 2022 with the Bengals determined to bolster their offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams ruled out Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson is expected to be out for a couple of weeks, though the Rams are fortuitously on bye in Week 11. The rest of the Rams’ tight ends are in varying states of health. Colby Parkinson (ribs) will likely play through his injury again. Tyler Higbee (illness) and Davis Allen (oblique) did not practice on Thursday. Their game status has not been revealed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) did not practice in Wednesday’s walk-through.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson was listed as a DNP for the Rams’ Wednesday walk-through. Rams head coach Sean McVay said earlier this week that Ferguson is likely out a couple week, so this comes as no surprise. Meanwhile, fellow tight ends Davis Allen (oblique) and Colby Parkinson (ribs) were both listed as limited participants. Allen and Parkinson are trending towards playing in Week 10 against the Cardinals, with Parkinson operating more as a pass-catcher and Allen as a blocker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Speaking after Week 9’s win over the Commanders, Rams head coach Sean McVay said Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) will likely be out a “couple [of] weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson was set to return in Week 9 against the Commanders prior to suffering a pulled hamstring. According to McVay, the second-year tight end was going to be a “big part” of the Rams’ offensive game plan against the Commanders, which should be good news to fantasy managers still holding out hope for a return. Based on McVay’s comments, we can safely assume Ferguson won’t be playing in Week 10 against the Cardinals, and then the Rams head into their bye. If all goes well in his recovery, it’s possible he could return on a short week in Week 12 to play against the Packers, but we likely won’t have more clarity on that until after their bye. For now, Ferguson remains a worthwhile stash in leagues where you can afford to do so, but it’s hard to say with any confidence when we should expect him to be back on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams ruled out Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) for Week 9 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson was set to make his return from injured reserve, having rehabilitated his early-season ankle injury. Unfortunately, he strained his hamstring in practice today and has now been ruled out. With Colby Parkinson (ribs) questionable, Tyler Higbee sneaks back into the TE1 conversation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters that Terrance Ferguson (ankle) is expected to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson will be able to play for the first time since he suffered his medial ankle sprain in Week 3. The second-year tight end offers some volatility, but there’s no denying that there’s upside in his profile. Just don’t be shocked if it isn’t on full display just yet in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was spotted at practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson had his 21-day practice window open up, and it’s a positive sign that he’s been able to practice on back-to-back days. There’s no guarantee he’ll play in Week 9 against the Commanders, but even if he misses that contest, it seems likely the second-year tight end will be back for the second half of the campaign.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams opened Terrance Ferguson’s (ankle) 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters that Ferguson will be limited today. The Rams could get their top receiving tight end back on the field this week, but they have slow-played his rehab thus far. It would be unsurprising to see him sit out this weekend. He should be added where available, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Terrance Ferguson (ankle) will not be designated to return from injured reserve this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported last week that Ferguson’s return was still going to take “some time.” That doesn’t make it sound like he’s awfully close to getting back on the field. Tyler Higbee leads the Rams’ tight end room in routes since Ferguson went down, but his production has vanished over the past two weeks. Colby Parkinson scored in Week 6 and Davis Allen found the end zone twice last week. Higbee remains the best fantasy option of the bunch, but he’s nothing more than a low-end TE2 for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Terrance Ferguson (ankle) “will take some time” to come off injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson is eligible to come off injured reserve next week, but Schefter reports that a source told him Ferguson’s recovery “will take some time.” The Rams placed Davante Adams on injured reserve this week and are in desperate need of pass-catching help behind Puka Nacua. Ferguson is a rising receiving tight end for the Rams, but has been on injured reserve since suffering an ankle injury in Week 3. Though he is a good IR stash for fantasy purposes, Ferguson is going to take longer than the minimum four weeks to return. Without a good timeline for return, he can be released from fantasy rosters in dire need of more immediate help during bye weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams placed Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This escalated quickly. Ferguson briefly returned in Week 3 after getting X-rays on his injured ankle, but he was ultimately unable to continue. Ferguson can be kept on squads possessing an injured reserve spot, but dropping him for a needed starter makes sense. He will be eligible to return in Week 8 against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) is questionable for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: The Rams were optimistic about McDuffie practicing on Thursday and playing on Sunday. The former did not happen. It sounds like he has a chance to play this weekend, but his recovery appears to be going slightly slower than expected. Rams S Kam Curl (toe) is also questionable to play, though LG Steve Avila (hamstring) has been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: Earlier today, we were told that McDuffie would resume practicing today. It turns out that report was wrong. McDuffie is on the wrong side of questionable. Myles Garrett (knee) was limited. Steve Avila (hamstring) and Kam Curl (toe) did not practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: Yesterday, The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reported that the Rams were hopeful that McDuffie would play in Week 10 against the Cardinals. He is tentatively on track to do so with today’s return to practice. The Rams will potentially morph into a run-heavy team that relies on the defense to generate turnovers with their top-two wide receivers and top tight end sidelined. McDuffie can help them accomplish that.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports that Trent McDuffie (back) will not practice on Wednesday, but the Rams are hopeful he will play in Week 10 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: Groin and back injuries have plagued McDuffie for some time, but it sounds like he has a chance to face the division-rival Cardinals in Week 10. With the Rams’ receiving corps ailing, Los Angeles could turn into an old-school team, featuring a high-volume run game and a lockdown defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) is inactive for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie was a DNP in practice all week but still managed to get a questionable designation entering the weekend. That said, the team’s decision doesn’t come as much of a surprise given the fact that he was unable to get on the field last week. Fortunately for the Rams, they faced a depleted Commanders receiving corps, and they will have both Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald on the field for the first time together.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Jordan Whittington (back) is questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: Whittington has just two catches on the season, and with head coach Sean McVay suggesting he wants to get Tutu Atwell more involved, it seems unlikely Whittington will have a role as more than a returner even if he can play against Washington come Sunday. Trent McDuffie (back) is also questionable for that contest, and won’t practice Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) limited again on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: Garrett has a chance to face the Commanders this week, but he still belongs in the questionable column at this time. Rams CB1 Trent McDuffie (back) and S Kam Curl (foot) both missed practice for the second time this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie played through a groin injury in Week 8 and seemingly picked up a new back injury during the game. Rams head coach Sean McVay said McDuffie will be a DNP Wednesday, indicating the 26-year-old’s back issue is more than a minor flare-up. It’s possible he is getting the day off to rest the groin and back injuries, but Rams fans should keep an eye on his practice status the rest of the week. It’s safe to say McDuffie is truly questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said he did not have an official update on Trent McDuffie (back), adding, “he looks like he’s feeling OK.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie missed Weeks 6-7 with a groin injury that he suffered in practice. He played through a questionable tag this week after three straight limited practices. Until we get an official update, McDuffie should probably be considered questionable to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) is questionable for Week 8 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie has missed the previous two games as he tends to a groin injury suffered ahead of Week 6. He made it back to the practice field this week but was unable to prove healthy enough to avoid the questionable designation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) is questionable for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters that he expects Garrett to play. This is unfortunate news for the Cardinals, who will be led by rookie Carson Beck in his first NFL start. Garrett played very well last week against the Commanders, but his preseason knee issue is apparently still bothering him. Hopefully, he can get healthy before the season’s end.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Earlier today, we were told that McDuffie would resume practicing today. It turns out that report was wrong. McDuffie is on the wrong side of questionable. Myles Garrett (knee) was limited. Steve Avila (hamstring) and Kam Curl (toe) did not practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s walk-through.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett returned from injured reserve and played in Week 9 against the Commanders. A limited listing indicates the 30-year-old will be managing his practice reps as he ramps back up from the knee injury. Expect Garrett to play in Week 10 against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams activated EDGE Myles Garrett (knee) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: No surprise here as Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters Friday that Garrett is expected to play in Week 9 against the Commanders. The Rams are 4-4, but will finally have Garrett and Aaron Donald on the same defensive line. That could cause problems for opposing offensive lines, starting with Washington’s on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters Friday that Myles Garrett (knee) is expected to play against the Commanders in Week 9.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett will need to come off injured reserve, with the Rams likely making that transaction closer to gametime. The 30-year-old has been as good as any defensive player in football, and for the first time he’ll get to be on the same field as Aaron Donald as teammates. Best of luck, Commanders’ offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Myles Garrett (knee) “is on track to be activated ahead of Sunday vs. the Commanders.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett has practiced all week and will likely be activated in the next 24 to 48 hours. The star pass-rusher who was acquired by the Rams in a blockbuster trade this offseason played in just one game for the Rams this season and did not record a tackle. Now, after undergoing knee surgery to correct a nagging injury, Garrett is all but set to return against the Commanders after missing seven straight games. His return will provide a much-needed boost to a Rams defense that ranks near the bottom of the league in sacks (12) through the first half of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) limited again on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett has a chance to face the Commanders this week, but he still belongs in the questionable column at this time. Rams CB1 Trent McDuffie (back) and S Kam Curl (foot) both missed practice for the second time this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) was able to practice again Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett has now been able to participate in back-to-back practices. The 30-year-old star defender appears to be ready to roll for Week 9 against the Commanders, but a decision on Garrett’s availability likely won’t be made until Friday at the earliest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) will practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters that Garrett will be limited today. The team could still give him another couple of weeks to ramp up, but he at least has a chance to play in Week 9 against the Commanders. Garrett underwent surgery on his injured knee back in September.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Sean McVay said Rams will open the 21-day practice window for Myles Garrett.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett will reportedly retake the practice field this week as he looks to make his return from injured reserve, a welcome sight for fans and the team, alike. Garrett played only 40 defensive snaps in Week 1 before suffering the injury that would cost him the following seven games. His eventual return will bolster a defense that has been underperforming preseason expectations, bringing a jolt to a team currently stuck at .500 with a 4-4 record. We’ll know more of the timing of his activation throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua’s (knee/toe) return timeline has not changed.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: A few days ago, McVay told reporters that Nacua would not be placed on injured reserve due to transaction limitations, so it was a bit surprising to see him land there yesterday. The move prompted some concern. He was initially expected to return in Week 14 or 15, and he will officially be eligible to return on the latter date against the Cowboys. As of today, he is on track to do so, just in time for the fantasy football playoffs. Nacua should not be dropped in any format. He will be a WR1 upon returning.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams placed Puka Nacua on injured reserve with knee and toe injuries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua will be eligible to return for the Rams’ Week 15 game against the Cowboys. The Rams are on bye in Week 11, and he is required to miss at least four games. It was previously reported that Nacua was expected to return in Week 14 or 15. Shortly before the team made this announcement, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said that the team was “confident” Nacua would return in that timeframe. Rams coach Sean McVay previously said that the Rams would not place him on injured reserve due to transaction limitations. It is unclear whether anything has changed. Nacua suffered PCL and MCL sprains, along with a turf toe injury in Week 10 against the Commanders. ESPN’s Adam Schefter specifically cited Nacua’s MCL sprain after the move was made, adding that McVay said Nacua will miss “extended time.” Nacua should be stashed on fantasy football benches at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (knee, toe) will not be placed on injured reserve for roster mechanics reasons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: The Rams are running out of return from IR designations. Putting Nacua on injured reserve would prevent another player from coming back later in the season, so he will simply take up a 53-man roster spot while he recovers. McVay made it clear that Nacua will still be out for a while. Nacua is expected to return at some point this year, though whether or not the Rams are still in the playoff hunt once he’s healthy could factor into the timeline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports Puka Nacua (knee, toe) will not miss the rest of the regular season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Graziano said there’s an outside chance the Rams won’t put Nacua on injured reserve ahead of Week 10. Rams sources “were very adamant that Nacua’s injury isn’t season-ending and that they hope to get him back around that Week 14, Week 15 time.” With Davante Adams (hamstring) also sidelined, look for the Rams offense to be unusually run heavy in the coming weeks. That should mean more work for Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson could see an uptick in targets too. If Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) is ever able to return to game action, he could profile as the team’s top target. Nacua had seen 44 percent of the Rams’ first-read targets this season, the highest rate in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (knee/turf toe) is likely headed to injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: An MRI on Monday revealed a sprained MCL and PCL for Nacua, who also suffered a turf toe injury on the Rams’ final offensive play in Sunday’s win over the Commanders. Nacua caught 14 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown in the win, drawing a target on 44.2 percent of Stafford’s pass attempts. It goes without saying that this creates a massive problem for a Rams passing game that has failed to find a serviceable WR2 sans Davante Adams (hamstring). Now, McVay and company will be faced with a new challenge as they try to replace Nacua with the likes of Tutu Atwell, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield, or a player not yet on the roster. Long believed to be buyers ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, it seems like a foregone conclusion that GM Les Snead will do what he can to acquire a playmaker for Matthew Stafford with whatever draft picks he still has at his disposal. The Rams currently only hold one pick in the first three rounds of the 2027 NFL Draft but still hold their first-round picks in 2028 and 2029, per Spotrac.com.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Puka Nacua (knee) will undergo an MRI on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Rams fans and fantasy managers will be holding their collective breath as they await the results of tomorrow’s MRI. According to Garafolo, Nacua suffered a knee injury on the Rams’ final offensive snap of the game when he took a rush attempt for five yards before the Rams punted the ball away. Nacua took a low hit from Commanders safety Jeremy Reaves, but didn’t appear to suffer a serious injury in real time. Garafolo reports, “the team does not believe [Nacua] suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging Monday will tell more.” It goes without saying that the Rams can ill-afford to lose another receiver, especially one of Nacua’s caliber. We will be sure to check back in with any updates on his injury as they come.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua caught 14-of-19 targets for 150 yards and one touchdown in the Rams’ Week 9 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua was targeted early and often by Matthew Stafford in this one. He caught three-of-four targets for 29 yards on the Rams’ first offensive drive and entered halftime with a 9-86-0 line on 11 targets. Coming out of the half, Nacua immediately caught back-to-back passes of 12 and 15 yards on a drive that ended with a Blake Corum touchdown run, and in the fourth quarter he made an impressive leaping grab for a seven-yard score to put the Rams up 20-13. Nacua has now scored in each of his last three games and has topped 100 yards three times this season. He’s the only reliable target in the Rams’ passing game and will, as usual, profile as a high-end WR1 next week against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua caught 11-of-12 targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua, with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined, again dominated targets in the newly run-heavy LA offense. No other Rams pass catcher saw more than four targets on the day. Nacua’s touchdown came on a well-designed screen in the second half at the end of a long drive for the run-first Rams offense. Nacua, who had 41 targets over his prior four games, is among the safest players in fantasy football. He matches up against the Commanders in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua caught 8-of-10 targets for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders, adding two rushes for ten yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua, dealing with a calf injury, didn’t appear to be 100 percent but still got by just fine against a beatable Vegas secondary. He caught one of Matthew Stafford’s three touchdowns and led the Rams offense with ten targets. Nacua has a good chance of leading the NFL in targets for the remainder of the season with Davante Adams (hamstring) out indefinitely. His role in the LA offense makes Nacua one of the most dangerous fantasy options in the game. He gets the Chargers secondary in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua (calf) is active for Week 7 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Start him. The Rams clearly feel comfortable with their superstar playing today, and we should too. Nacua’s upside is too high for him to remain on fantasy football benches. Reporting on Nacua’s ailment suggests he is not necessarily dealing with a strain. It can perhaps be best described as muscle fatigue, though we are doctors here at Rotoworld. Re-injury is possible, but we can safely expect him to handle a large workload whenever he is on the field. Nacua is a high-end WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Tailese Fuaga (knee) won’t play in New Orleans’ Week 10 game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Fuaga has a knee sprain, per Kellen Moore. It sounds like a short-term thing and Moore has said he won’t need to go on injured reserve. Asim Richards and Mason Murphy are the backup tackles and Richards played left tackle while Kelvin Banks was sidelined earlier this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Taliese Fuaga (knee) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: The Saints’ right tackle was added to the injury report today, which is extremely unfortunate. The team is already without center Erik McCoy (biceps). Hopefully, this is only a minor issue for Fuaga.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints RT Taliese Fuaga (ankle) will not play in New Orleans’ Week 14 game against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Fuaga played in Week 13, but appears to have injured his other ankle — this is not the same ankle he was on the report for earlier in the year — somewhere along the way despite playing 100 percent of the snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints declared S Ugo Amadi, CB Rejzon Wright, RB Audric Estime, OT Taliese Fuaga, DT John Ridgeway III, and DT Khristian Boyd inactive for Week 12 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Fuaga has been sidelined with an ankle injury for the last few weeks. He was a limited practice participant on Friday, but is still not yet ready to go. Estime is also inactive in the backfield with Alvin Kamara (ankle) good to go for Week 12 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints ruled out OT Taliese Fuaga (ankle) against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: The Saints’ depleted offensive line is in rough shape. Fuaga has a long way to go in his development, having allowed 22 quarterback pressures and three sacks this season, but downgrading to his backup, OT Asim Richards, won’t be any better. They face the Panthers this weekend, who field a solid defensive tackle unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said RT Taliese Fuaga (ankle) has a high-ankle sprain and is unlikely to play this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Ditto Jack Stoll. Fuaga has played through multiple injuries this year, with a knee and back listing. The second-year tackle has played up to his form last year, with a 65.0 PFF rating in 473 dropbacks. Asim Richards replaced him for the final two snaps of Week 9’s loss to the Rams and would be next man up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints RT Taliese Fuaga (knee/back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: The Saints’ right tackle is now firmly on track to suit up in Week 4 against the Bills. Fuaga entered Week 2 with a knee injury and exited Week 2 with a back injury as well. The 23-year-old was unable to play in Week 3 against the Seahawks. Saints EDGE Chase Young (calf) and OG Dillon Radunz (toe) remain sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints RT Taliese Fuaga (knee/back) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Fuaga missed Week 3 with the pair of injuries. Trevor Penning was active but did not play. Penning was upgraded to a full participant in Wednesday’s practice and could be ready to make his first start by Sunday. Getting both linemen back in the trenches would be a notable boost for Spencer Rattler as he searches for his first NFL win.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints declared RT Taliese Fuaga, EDGE Chase Young, OG Dillon Radunz, WR Devaughn Vele, WR Trey Palmer, RB Devin Neal and DT Khristian Boyd inactive for Week 3 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Fuaga played through his knee injury last week but he picked up a back injury in-game and was unable to practice at all this week. Young (calf) has yet to suit up in 2025. Saints LG Trevor Penning (toe) was limited all week, but New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill and Mike Triplett both expressed skepticism as to whether he was healthy enough to start against the Seahawks today. The offensive line will remain worryingly short-staffed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints ruled out EDGE Chase Young (calf) for Week 3 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Friday’s injury report has not yet been released but as of Thursday, Young remains a non-participant. The Saints will also be without OG Dillon Radunz (toe), who started in Week 2 against the 49ers. Saints LG Trevor Penning (toe) and RT Taliese Fuaga (knee/back) are both questionable for Week 3 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) won’t play in New Orleans’ Week 10 game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: The passing-down blocking back’s absence should create more opportunities for Alvin Kamara and, possibly, Travis Etienne in the passing game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: The Saints’ veteran running back is just having his reps managed. With Audric Estime playing well and Travis Etienne (hamstring) potentially returning, Kamara does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats at this time. Kamara will continue to chip in on passing downs, though. Backup RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: On the plus side, Donaldson is no longer listed with a concussion. Audric Estime played well last week and Travis Etienne (hamstring) is practicing now, though. Donaldson could be phased out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Donaldson wasn’t able to practice again Friday, and the 22-year-old tailback won’t be available for the Week 9 skirmish against Cleveland. Alvin Kamara will likely be the top option — and would have been even if Donaldson could play — in that contest, assuming his back injury allows him to play, of course. This is not a great situation, folks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: The way the team listed Kamara indicates that the back injury will not keep him from playing, but he is clearly still hurt. Kamara has been entirely ineffective this season and can only be viewed as a touchdown-dependent FLEX. CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was unable to practice today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Donaldson aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 7 against the Steelers and did not return. He also entered the league’s concussion protocol after the game. A limited session today means he’s making progress on both fronts. He should be good to go for Week 9. The same is true of Alvin Kamara, who got a rest day today, despite his back injury also being noted on the report. Both backs will mix in behind Kendre Miller on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Donaldson is the third member of the Saints’ backfield committee. While he will get a few touches this week, he is not getting enough work for fantasy relevance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: The pass-protecting back looks likely to continue to mix in and limit snaps for the fantasy-valuable members of the backfield in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: A limited practice to start the week is usually maintenance. Donaldson looked good last week, running for 39 yards on six attempts, though he did commit one fumble. Donaldson is one of three backs seeing work for the Saints, and none of them have made a strong case to get more touches. Donaldson is a weak FLEX option for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson rushed six times for 39 yards and a fumble in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: A messy Saints committee backfield had Donaldson get the second-most snaps among New Orleans running backs against the Giants. He and Alvin Kamara were the passing-down backs while Donaldson also had a 17-yard run, the longest run by a Saints running back on the day. His first-career touchdown was called back in the third quarter after he was ruled down just shy of the goal line. The 22-year-old rookie has had a surprisingly high utilization early in the season and will continue to be involved while Travis Etienne is out. Despite this, his fantasy impact will mainly be to dilute Kamara and Kendre Miller’s fantasy values. Donaldson should only be rostered in the deepest of leagues heading into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (toe) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 10 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: He made it back on to the practice field on Friday, so he’s probably on the optimistic side of questionable at this point. Todd Monken did say at his Friday presser that Boston is “trending in the right direction.” Boston did miss the first two sessions of the week but has been no stranger to the injury report this year and has tended to gut it out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (toe) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: This morning, Boston told reporters that he was hoping to resume practicing today. Unfortunately, he was unable to do so. That said, Boston’s toe injury is feeling better and things are “trending up” at the moment. It sounds like the rookie wide receiver has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Texans and would be a WR3/FLEX if so.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (toe) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston continues to pick up lower-leg injuries, but last week’s calf issue did not slow him down. The Browns have begun varying Boston’s usage, no longer limiting him to high-variance downfield work. Adding short-to-intermediate opportunities only enhances his outlook. If he can play this weekend, he will be a WR3/FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 6-of-7 targets for 98 yards in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Like clockwork, Boston beat his man for a massive play again this week. Boston plucked a deep ball right off Kool-Aid McKinstry’s helmet and ran inside the five-yard line for a 60-yard gain early in the third quarter. It was his league-leading fourth catch of 40+ yards this year. Despite operating as a deep threat, Boston went on to lead the Browns in all receiving categories except touchdowns. Boston continues to look like a high-end boundary receiver in the mold of Tee Higgins or Mike Evans. While he’s got a long way to go to match those players, the early returns have been promising. Boston will remain a high-ceiling WR3 when he takes on the Texans next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (calf) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston will once again play through a lower-body injury. The rookie downfield wide receiver has played unproductively as of late, but he remains a threat to rip off a long gain. He will be catching passes from Shedeur Sanders this weekend. Hopefully, the two form a strong connection quickly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (calf) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston is on track to face the Saints this week, but lower-body injuries have limited his production since Week 4. The Browns are also likely to have Shedeur Sanders under center, adding an unknown variable to the mix as the two players hone their chemistry. Boston is likely just a boom-bust FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (calf) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: A limited designation for the first practice of the week is usually nothing to worry about. We’ll assume as much for now. Boston has been racking up targets and air yards without much to show for it in his box scores over the past month. He hasn’t eclipsed 50 yards in a game since Week 4. A date with New Orleans’ struggling defense should help him get back on track as a WR3 for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 6-of-11 targets for 37 yards in the Browns’ Week 8 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: The good news is that Boston’s route tree wasn’t limited to deep shots, but the bad news is that the production did not follow. The rookie was second on the team in targets, played the most snaps, and ran the second-most routes of any receiver, but the Browns’ passing attack could never get going. Boston was close to a bigger day after he made a great one-handed catch in the end zone, but he could only get one foot in bounds. He’ll continue to be a boom-or-bust option but has a chance to boom against the Saints next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 3-of-8 targets for 25 yards in the Browns’ Week 7 win against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston was third in targets among Browns pass catchers and saw lots and lots of air yards from Deshaun Watson, who nearly connected with Boston for two long touchdowns on the day. So it goes with a high-variance downfield option like Boston, who now has three straight quiet outings. With a 45 percent air yards share headed into Week 7, Boston will certainly have his big box scores in the coming weeks. Predicting when that might happen will be tough for fantasy managers. He should be a flex play in Week 8 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: He’ll be on the WR3 line in a good matchup against the Titans. Boston finally had a clunker last week against Baltimore, but he’s been remarkably consistent otherwise and should find easier footing against Tennessee’s rough back seven.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will not play in Atlanta’s Week 10 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: He didn’t practice all week and enters Atlanta’s Week 11 bye off two completely lost weeks. The rookie hasn’t made much of an impact so far and doesn’t necessarily need to be kept on rosters in non-dynasty leagues at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: He was instantly ruled out ahead of Atlanta’s date in Madrid last Monday and has not practiced since. With the bye on tap in Week 11, we’d expect Branch to sit against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch suffered the hamstring injury in Week 8 and missed last week’s game because of it. He appears to be on pace to miss another game. With just 10 catches to his name after nearly as many weeks, 2026 is shaping up to be an underwhelming start to Branch’s career.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Brian Robinson (hamstring) is questionable for the Falcons’ Week 9 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Robinson was briefly listed as questionable only for head coach Kevin Stefanski to rule him out shortly after the initial report. Robinson was limited in practice throughout the week, but the Falcons are opting to play it safe, likely hoping another week on the sidelines will lower the chances of re-injury. Rookie WR Zachariah Branch (hamstring) has also been ruled out for the game after picking up an injury in last week’s loss to the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will not play in Week 9 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch suffered a hamstring injury in Week 8’s shutout loss to the Buccaneers and will miss next week’s game against the Bengals in Madrid. The rookie third-rounder has caught just 10 passes for 64 scoreless yards this season and has also served as the Falcons’ primary kick and punt returner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: It seemed like Branch would be in for a bigger role in Week 7 with Olamide Zaccheaus out with a shoulder injury. However, Branch ran a route on just 18 of 37 dropbacks and was only targeted twice. It doesn’t seem like he’s anywhere close to playing a large enough role for fantasy value and doesn’t need to be held through the bye weeks in redraft leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Falcons declared WR Olamide Zaccheaus, QB Jack Strand, QB Andy Dalton, RB Brian Robinson Jr., LB Divine Deablo, CB Avieon Terrell, and DB Billy Bowman Jr. inactive for Week 7 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) was ruled out earlier in the week, and Zaccheaus is dealing with a shoulder injury and will not be able to suit up for this one. That could mean more work in the receiving game for rookie Zachariah Branch, who might be worth a stash in deeper formats in case a solid game today earns him a bigger role moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch caught both of his targets for 14 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch’s primary duties still come on kick and punt returns, but Kevin Stefanski made it a point to get him more involved this week. He was held without a catch or even a target in Week 1. Branch isn’t on the fantasy radar yet, but dynasty managers can be pleased with his role taking a step in the right direction.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch had no targets in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: On one hand, no targets is bad. On the other hand, Branch played one more snap than Olamide Zaccheaus and ran only three fewer routes. This is not a passing attack that you want pieces of right now, but there is a chance that Branch could take the WR3 role by the middle of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will play in Week 1 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch was limited by the hamstring issue for the first two practices of the week. He got up to a full practice on Friday and was cleared for Week 1. Branch will likely see a few designed touches in his NFL debut, but fantasy managers will want to wait until he overtakes Olamide Zaccheaus on the depth chart before getting him into their lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: James Pearce Jr. (back) is questionable for Atlanta’s Week 10 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Pearce got in two limited sessions on Thursday and Friday after missing Wednesday’s practice. He would appear to be on the optimistic side of questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: James Pearce Jr. (back) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday DNP for the 23-year-old. Pearce Jr. will probably at least hit the questionable line on Friday and has a chance to be cleared off altogether if things trend in the right direction. Kevin Stefanski did not seem overly concerned about his status when asked about it, saying the Falcons “also want him to get healthy and feel good.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: James Pearce Jr. (back) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: The former No. 26 overall pick made his season debut last week. A back injury flared up on him headed into the week, but he ultimately pushed through it on Sunday. It’s unclear if the team is just managing his reps with the DNP today or if the issue got worse. Tomorrow’s injury report will be more revealing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: Falcons EDGE James Pearce Jr. (back) is active for Week 9 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Pearce Jr. just finished serving his eight-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy. A back issue then flared up in practice, but he’s good to go for his 2026 debut. Inactive for the Falcons are QB Andy Dalton, QB Jack Strand, WR Zachariach Branch, DB Billy Bowman, DB Robert Longerbeam, and DE Drake Jackson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: James Pearce is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Pearce’s status is related to a back injury that apparently flared up in Friday’s practice, per head coach Kevin Stefanski. Pearce was a full participant in practice, and teams said he will operate on a pitch count, so it seems highly unlikely he will be scratched on game day. In addition to Pearce, the Falcons also listed LB Yasir Abdullah (hamstring), WR Beaux Collins (hip), LB Divine Deablo (forearm), and OT Cameron Williams (ankle) as questionable for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: Falcons DE James Pearce returned from his eight-game suspension and is eligible to play in Week 9 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Pearce is eligible to play in Week 9 against the Bengals and will likely join the team when it flies to Madrid for the international matchup. Pearce’s return should provide a nice spark to the 17th-ranked Falcons’ defense after the 2025 first-rounder racked up 10.5 sacks and 10 TFLs as a rookie while totaling 26 tackles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said James Pearce Jr. (suspension) will be added back to the Falcons 53-man roster next week when eligible.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: “He’s done everything that we have asked, everything that he has been allowed to do, he’s done a great job,” Stefanski said while saying that Pearce would play in Madrid against the Bengals. Pearce was suspended after violating the league’s personal conduct policy for three felonies and one misdemeanor for his role in a car chase with ex-girlfriend, WNBA player Rickea Jackson. Pearce’s felony charges were aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi reports that the NFL suspended Falcons EDGE James Pearce for the first eight regular season games.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: The NFL determined that Pearce violated the league’s Personal Conduct Policy. He will be suspended without pay, but is allowed to participate in all preseason activities, including games. The suspension begins on August 30th, and he will be eligible for reinstatement on November 2nd. The Falcons go on bye in Week 11, so Week 9 marks his earliest possible return to the field. Pearce was arrested in February and initially charged with three felonies and one misdemeanor, including aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police, and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall believes the NFL is “likely” to suspend Falcons EDGE James Pearce Jr.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Atlanta “appears to be waiting” on the league to decide how they want to punish Pearce. Cameron Sutton was suspended eight games in 2024 for a similar incident, which Kendall mentions and certainly could serve as a blueprint for how this plays out. Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said they have not received any communication from the league on this subject. It certainly would be surprising if Pearce weren’t eventually suspended to some extent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: Fox5 Atlanta’s Justin Felder reports James Pearce will be in attendance for Falcons minicamp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Pearce is in the middle of an ongoing legal situation stemming from a February arrest that resulted in him being charged with three felonies and one misdemeanor. The 22-year-old pass-rusher recently entered a pre-trial intervention program that can result in all charges being dismissed if he meets the conditions of the program, and the league is reportedly “closely monitoring all developments” with Pearce. We don’t yet know if the league plans to hand down a suspension to Pearce, but it wouldn’t be surprising if some disciplinary action was taken after everything is resolved in his case.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.headline: Jordan Schultz reports the Eagles are waiving WR Hollywood Brown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.analysis: The trade market did not materialize for Mr. Brown, who has eight targets in four active games with the Eagles this year. He’ll look to catch on elsewhere down the stretch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.headline: Jordan Schultz reports teams seeking wideout help believe Hollywood Brown could be traded in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.analysis: Brown had two rushes for 12 yards against the Titans in Week 2 (not receptions) and has been inactive in every other week of the season. So, yeah, we guess he could be had. As could any of the several veteran receivers on losing teams who actually have caught a pass this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.headline: Eagles declared WR Hollywood Brown, RB Saquon Barkley, S Michael Carter II, EDGE A.J. Epenesa, EDGE Jalyx Hunt, and QB Joe Milton inactive for Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.analysis: Despite the Eagles’ absurdly lengthy injury report, they only had one player listed as questionable for Week 6. That was center Drew Kendall, who is active. Brown was dealing with an ankle issue earlier this week but was cleared from the injury report on Friday, making him a healthy scratch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.analysis: Wicks suffered the hamstring injury in practice last week but played through the injury in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars. Also limited was Hollywood Brown (ankle). Brown has not played since suffering an ankle injury in Week 2 but has a chance to return this week. Expect Wicks to play in Week 6 while Brown is truly questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.analysis: Wicks was listed as a limited participant today, indicating that he strained his hamstring during Thursday’s practice. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) still sidelined, rookie WR Makai Lemon could be the de facto top receiver, though the team has struggled to use him effectively thus far. Hollywood Brown (ankle) also remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.headline: Eagles WR Devonta Smith (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
