https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.analysis: Smith still has not returned to practice since last week, continuing to deal with a hamstring injury. Given his lack of practice reps ahead of travelling to London for Week 5, Smith is on the wrong side of questionable for this week’s matchup against the Jaguars. Also not practicing was WR Hollywood Brown (ankle). The Eagles will play Week 5 with a severely banged-up skill position group.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.headline: The Philly Voice’s Jimmy Kempski believes Eagles WR Dontayvian Wicks will “probably” be the team’s No. 2 wideout if A.J. Brown is traded this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.analysis: Wicks should slot in as the Eagles WR behind DeVonta Smith, Kempski said, because the former Packer is “younger, the Eagles invested more in him than they did in [Marquise] Brown, he is under contract for two years vs. one for Brown, and he seemingly already has the trust of offensive coordinator Sean Mannion.” The Eagles acquired Wicks from Green Bay this month in exchange for a 2026 fifth round draft pick and a 2027 sixth rounder. He had 108 receptions, 1,328 yards, and 11 touchdowns over three seasons with the Packers, operating mostly as a high-variance downfield threat. Kempski described Wicks as “a hard-nosed, rugged player who offers far more as a blocker in the run game than [A.J.] Brown does. How much that actually should matter is debatable, but my sense is that it will matter a lot in this new scheme.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.headline: Eagles acquired WR Dontayvion Wicks from the Packers in exchange for a 2026 fifth-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter breaks the news, adding that Wicks will now sign a one-year, $12.5 million extension with the Eagles. Over the last four weeks, they also signed WR Hollywood Brown and WR Elijah Moore as well. Schefter reminds us that if the Eagles were to trade away WR A.J. Brown, that would probably happen after June 1st, “when the cap burden would be more manageable for the Eagles.” As things currently stand, Wicks will likely compete for WR3 duties. The trade also leaves Packers WR Christian Watson, WR Jayden Reed and WR Matthew Golden as the team’s top-three options after allowing WR Romeo Doubs to sign with the Patriots last month. The Eagles tacked on an additional year to Wicks’ contract after the deal, tying him to the franchise through the 2027 season. The extension includes $12.5 million in maximum money with $9 million guaranteed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.headline: Eagles signed WR Hollywood Brown, formerly of the Chiefs, to a one-year contract worth up to $6.5 million.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.analysis: This move could be interpreted one of two ways. Brown could be slotted into the distant WR3 role behind A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith, or he could be a No. 2 option behind Smith if the Eagles eventually part ways this offseason with the mercurial Brown. Brown in 2025 was an afterthought in the Kansas City, totaling 587 yards and five touchdowns over 16 games. He was targeted on a ho-hum 20 percent of his pass routes last year as a part-time player in a dysfunctional Chiefs offense. Brown, entering his age-29 season, could have some WR3/4 value in deeper fantasy formats if the Eagles trade away Brown in the coming weeks or months.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.headline: Hollywood Brown caught 2-of-4 targets for 13 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 18 loss against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquise-b.analysis: Following a 10-catch, 99-yard performance in Week 1 against the Chargers, Brown was a non-factor in the pass-heavy Kansas City offense this season, totaling 536 yards and four touchdowns over 16 games. As the third or fourth option in the passing offense, Brown was treated as a rotational player even when the Chiefs struggled with wideout absences. After a highly disappointing two-year run with KC, Brown will likely play elsewhere in 2026. He’ll be a free agent this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.headline: Cardinals signed TE Elijah Higgins to a three-year, extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.analysis: Just weeks after earning a rare blurb from us here at Rotoworld, Higgins followed up his blurb-worthy performance with a three-year extension. The 26-year-old tight end has caught 18 passes for 162 yards and one touchdown this season, and is a year removed from the 30-301-0 line he posted last year. With the Cardinals hurting at receiver, it’s possible Higgins could see an expanded role going forward, especially after signing this deal, which can net him up to $26.8 million.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.headline: Elijah Higgins caught 2-of-4 targets for 10 yards in Arizona’s Week 8 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.analysis: It’s as close as Arizona had to a third real receiver, as Higgins out-targeted Simi Fehoko and Reggie Virgil (as well as Devin Duvernay) after Kendrick Bourne left with a high-ankle sprain. Virgil could find himself in the TE2 ranks if Arizona runs out Fehoko next week as their other outside receiver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.headline: Elijah Higgins caught 7-of-8 targets for 91 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 16 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.analysis: Higgins’ seven receptions and 91 yards both led the team. His eight targets tied for the team high. The former dynasty darling looked great as a post-catch producer, fighting his way through contact for chunk gains. He does not need to be rostered in re-draft leagues as this felt more like a specific matchup bit against the Falcons today, but it’s good to see that he has this kind of game in him when needed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.headline: Elijah Higgins caught 1-of-2 targets for three yards in Arizona’s Week 15 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.analysis: Higgins played 42-of-62 snaps for the Cardinals on offense and watched Trey McBride catch a lot of targets. We salute his selflessness.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.headline: Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon said Trey McBride (concussion) is trending toward playing in Week 5.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.analysis: McBride was able to practice on Wednesday. Gannon said McBride’s prospects look “good” for this Sunday’s game against the 49ers after he missed Week 4 against Washington. McBride’s late week practice participation will be key if he’s going to suit up against the Niners. Elijah Higgins would once again work as the team’s TE1 if McBride can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.headline: Elijah Higgins caught 2-of-3 targets for 12 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 4 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.analysis: Filling in for Trey McBride (concussion), some fantasy managers hoped Higgins, a former receiver, could turn into a quality one-week fantasy option. That didn’t quite come to fruition, as Higgins managed just two receptions on three targets for a forgettable Week 4. McBride is expected to return in Week 5 against the 49ers if he clears concussion protocol.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.headline: Trey McBride caught 6-of-6 targets for 67 yards and recovered a fumble for a touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 2 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.analysis: McBride saw heavy usage along with Marvin Harrison Jr. in the Cardinals’ win. He is definitively Kyler Murray’s No. 2 target and will continue to be a top-two option in the offense. Elijah Higgins was the only other tight end to catch a pass, on an 18-yard touchdown score. Though he did not catch a pass for a score, McBride scored by recovering a James Conner fumble in the endzone in the fourth quarter. Fantasy managers will take that score, along with the schemed usage that McBride was seeing over the secondary pass-catchers. McBride is a TE1 heading into Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.headline: Elijah Higgins caught 4-of-4 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 15 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.analysis: Higgins was second on the team in receiving yards today with Marquise Brown leaving early and Michael Wilson being ineffective (no catches). He caught a late garbage touchdown on the the Cardinals’ final possession, as the 49ers had already put up 45 points.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.headline: Cardinals declared LB Joshua Woods, CB Starling Thomas, OL Carter O’Donnell, OL Ilm Manning, and TE Elijah Higgins inactive for Week 3 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.analysis: The Cardinals are at near full-strength heading into Week 3. We’ll see how that fares against the league’s No. 1 defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.headline: Dolphins released CB Justin Bethel.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-hig.analysis: Bethel is a special teams expert who is set to enter his 11th NFL season. If he’s on a roster in 2023, it most likely won’t be the Dolphins, after the team made him a part of their cuts to trim the roster down to 53 players. In addition to Bethel, the Dolphins also released/waived WR Robbie Chosen, RB Myles Gaskin, DT Da’Shawn Hand, TE Tyler Kroft, CB Parry Nickerson, OT Cedric Ogbuehi, DB Jamal Perry, LB Malik Reed, CB Ethan Bonner, TE Tanner Conner, LB Cameron Goode, OT Ryan Hayes, TE Elijah Higgins, WR Braylon Sanders, CB Bryce Thompson, OL Alama Uluave, CB Trill Williams, and WR Daewood Davis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Bam Knight will play in Week 10 against the Rams after clearing concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: After being upgraded to a full participant on Thursday, Knight is officially off of the injury report and good to go for Sunday’s game against the Rams. Both Knight and Tyler Allgeier are expected to factor heavily into the Cardinals’ running game this weekend, especially with Carson Beck making his first career start with a depleted receiving corps. Both Knight and Allgeier will be fringe RB3/Flex plays in a game that could prove tough for the Cardinals’ banged-up offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Bam Knight (concussion) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Knight is on track to resume his lead rushing role this week. Unfortunately, the Cardinals face the Seahawks, potentially rendering Knight a touchdown-dependent FLEX starter against their elite defense. Hopefully, Knight remains setback-free for the rest of the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Bam Knight (concussion) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Knight sat out in Week 9 against the Seahawks, but he is on track to resume his lead rushing role against the Rams this week. He was seen wearing a yellow non-contact jersey today, and will likely be listed as limited. The Rams’ defense is enjoying improved health and playing well. Knight will likely handle a FLEX-worthy role, but producing a ceiling game against this defense may be unlikely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Cardinals declared RB Bam Knight, CB Starling Thomas V, LB Eku Leota, OL Jayden Williams, OL Jon Gaines III, and OL Albert Reese IV inactive for Week 9 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Knight’s absence due to a concussion leaves Tyler Allgeier alone atop the running back depth chart with rookie Jeremiyah Love on injured reserve. The matchup is far from ideal against the Seahawks on the road, but Allgeier appears to be in line for a legitimate workhorse role and can be started as a viable RB2. The Cardinals press forward with veteran journeyman Gardner Minshew under center following the trade of Jacoby Brissett this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Bam Knight (concussion) will not play in Week 9 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: LaFleur also ruled out OL Jon Gaines II (ankle) and OT Jayden Williams (knee). Knight has been a DNP all week after suffering a concussion in Week 8’s win over the Cowboys and will officially be sidelined for Week 9. His absence, along with Jeremiyah Love’s (ankle) could create a bell cow role for Tyler Allgeier, who totaled 191 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns in last week’s win, while fourth-year vet Evan Hull could also work into the mix. Allgeier’s volume alone will put him in the RB2 conversation this week despite the tough matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Bam Knight (concussion) was not spotted at Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: It appears it’ll be another DNP for Knight as he entered the concussion protocol following Sunday’s win over the Cowboys in Week 8. The 25-year-old tailback seems unlikely to be able to go in Week 9 against the Seahawks, but there should be further updates on Knight’s status soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Bam Knight (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Knight entered concussion protocol after a hit to the head in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Starting out as a DNP this week means he still has a few steps to go to clear protocol by Sunday. Unless he can progress through protocol quickly, Knight is on the wrong side of questionable for Week 9 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Bam Knight is in the league’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Knight will need to clear protocol if he hopes to suit up in time to play in Week 9 against the Seahawks. The former UDFA has turned in a solid season thus far for the Cardinals, rushing for 28-168-0 while adding another six receptions for 43 additional yards. With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) likely to miss time, Knight could again find himself in a split with Tyler Allgeier when he returns. The Cardinals will likely need to address their running back room at some point in the week with Allgeier currently being the only healthy back on the roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: FOX’s Pam Oliver reports Zonovan Knight (head) left Arizona’s Week 8 game against the Cowboys and won’t return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: She got word from Mike LaFleur that Knight would be out. Knight wasn’t officially given an injury declaration as of yet, but it was a fairly textbook shoulder-to-the-head that caused a fumble towards the waning moments of the second half. Knight had 18 total yards on three carries and one catch before leaving. We would be surprised, given how brutal the hit he took looked, if he were available for Week 9. This leaves Tyler Allgeier as the lone healthy back for the second half of this game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Tyler Allgeier (toe) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Allgeier popped up on the injury report with a toe issue as rookie Jeremiyah Love (ankle) returned to practice in a limited fashion. Though we don’t know the severity of Allgeier’s injury, it may be worth keeping Bam Knight rostered despite Love’s return. If Allgeier cannot play in Week 8 against the Cowboys, Knight will get another week of fantasy viability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) is questionable for Week 10 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Despite the questionable designation, it’s safe to say Phillips is trending in the right direction after being upgraded to a full participant for Friday’s practice. Barring any unexpected setbacks, we would assume Phillips will be good to go against the Saints. The Saints also listed CB Will Lee (hamstring) and OL Brady Christensen (hamstring) as questionable, and CB Mike Jackson (groin) as doubtful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips practiced in full yesterday. Today, he was only limited. Hm. Today’s lightened workload could be a planned load management decision, but tomorrow’s practice participation will be worth watching for the Panthers’ top pass rusher. The Panthers’ stud LG Damien Lewis (knee) was also downgraded today, while starting perimeter CB Mike Jackson (groin) remained a full participant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Panthers declared LB Jaelan Phillips, QB Haynes King, CB Will Lee III, RB AJ Dillon, LB Bobby Okereke, OG Damien Lewis, and DT TeRah Edwards inactive for Week 9 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips and Lewis were both ruled out before the weekend, so there’s nothing too surprising to see here. The Panthers hope to end a two-game losing streak this week at home against a stout Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Panthers ruled out Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips did not practice at all this week, after sitting out the Panthers’ last two games. Losing a key edge rusher will make things harder for the Panthers’ defense. Bo Nix should have decently comfortable pockets, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) will not play in Week 8 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Carolina also ruled out left guard Damien Lewis, who is dealing with a knee issue. Phillips also missed last week’s game because of a hamstring injury. The hope is that the mini-bye after Thursday Night Football is enough to get him back for Week 9. Phillips has 2.5 sacks this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Panthers declared EDGE Jaelan Phillips, TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, QB Haynes King, RB AJ Dillon, C Sam Hecht, OT Stone Forsythe, and EDGE TeRah Edwards inactive for Week 7 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips is a big loss, but it’s an otherwise quiet list for the Panthers vs. a more-injured and undermanned Bucs squad. Phillips is week to week after pulling his hammy in Week 6 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) is questionable to return to Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips came into this game questionable with a hamstring injury but was able to suit up. Unfortunately, he got hurt early in the first quarter and is unlikely to return. Considering he had the bye week to heal and is not 100 percent, it seems likely that the EDGE rusher will miss some time with the injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Taylor Moton (blood clots) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Moton is tentatively on track to make his return from injured reserve this week. Meanwhile, RT Monroe Freeling (knee) sat out on Wednesday. Panthers DT Tershawn Wharton (neck) is practicing in full, while EDGE Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) was limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said he is “hopeful” Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) will be able to play in Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips went down with a hamstring injury late in Sunday’s game against the Lions and didn’t return to the field. For a player with Phillips’ injury history, there were immediate concerns regarding the severity of the injury, but with a Week 5 bye on tap, the hope is Phillips won’t miss much time, if any. Phillips has totaled two sacks in his first four games of the season. In addition to Phillips, the team is also hopeful that OT Monroe Freeling (knee) will be able to return in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Devin Lloyd (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Lloyd was one of the Panthers’ premier free agent additions this offseason, and he’s already proven to be worth the investment. Lloyd terrorized the Falcons in Week 2 with a sack and two interceptions, one of which was a pick-six. Fellow free agent acquisition Jaelan Phillips was also absent from practice today. He is dealing with a back injury. Though the Browns aren’t a particularly good offense right now, it would still be a massive boon for them if Lloyd and Phillips are out for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) will play in Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Despite his listing with a limited practice on all three days this week, Henry was cleared from the injury report and is set for a normal role versus Detroit in Munich, Germany. Though he typically jostles each week for snaps and target share with promising rookie Eli Raridon, Henry remains one of New England’s most logical aerial threats in the red zone. Fantasy managers desperate for tight end help could do worse than throwing a dart with Henry.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) is listed as questionable for Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Despite his uncertain status, Brown, who was limited in all three practices during the week, will make the trip across the Atlantic Ocean with the Pats before their game in Munich, Germany. The veteran has missed two straight contests, and New England may decide to rest him once again before the team’s Week 11 bye. Should Brown suit up, he would sit in the WR2/WR3 tiers against a Detroit secondary that’s improved lately but has been generally friendly to receivers most of the season. If Brown can’t go, DeMario Douglas would take that baton as the top target; Mack Hollins, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams would see a boost into stronger Flex territory, and tight end Hunter Henry would slot into a more stream-worthy status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: He played off a questionable tag last week with a more checked practice report, so we’d be surprised if Henry didn’t go on Sunday. He has a real chance of being cleared off the injury report altogether on Friday after a pair of limited sessions to open the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry played through the foot issue last week despite a severely limited practice regimen throughout the week. He only caught three passes for 35 yards, though the Pats failed to get much going on offense while the game was competitive. He should rebound as a high-end TE2 for his Week 10 date with the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry caught 3-of-3 targets for 35 yards in the Patriots’ Week 9 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry was playing through a foot injury in this one, but still ended up leading all Patriots tight ends in routes run (22). Prior to his injury-shortened outing in Week 8, Henry was riding a four-game streak of double-digit PPR performances, but he wasn’t able to get there this week. Hopefully, he didn’t suffer any setbacks this week and will be a viable streaming option in what could be a plus matchup next week against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) is active for Week 9 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: It was reported earlier in the day that Henry had a “realistic” shot at suiting up this week after he managed to log a limited practice on Friday. Henry will profile as a high-end TE2 with A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) out this week. In addition to Brown being out, the Patriots also declared RB TreVeyon Henderson, CB Charles Woods, OT Dametrious Crownover, and QB Behren Morton inactive for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Hunter Henry (foot) has a “realistic chance to play” in Week 9 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry only practiced once this week but still received a questionable designation on Friday. Eli Raridon would have taken his spot in the lineup, but it sounds like Henry will give it a go. He will be a high-end TE2 for his matchup with the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) has been ruled questionable for Week 9 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: The Patriots are down A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) on top of their other skill-position issues, so if Henry can go, he could see a considerable amount of targets against the Packers. He didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday, however, so it seems unlikely. Eli Raridon is inline to be the top tight end option if Henry can’t play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: It’s looking like rookie Eli Raridon will operate as the Patriots’ No. 1 tight end in Week 9 against the Packers. Henry has not participated in football activities since injuring his foot early in Week 8 against the Dolphins. Raridon would warrant streaming TE1 consideration if he gets the start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) was not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry could ultimately get in a limited session later in the day, but this certainly looks like a DNP. The veteran tight end injured his foot early in the Pats’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins and did not return. Rookie Eli Raridon will take his spot in the lineup if Henry is unable to play this week. Raridon is averaging an impressive 13.3 yards per catch while mixing in behind Henry this year. He would immediately be in the TE2 mix if Henry is ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.headline: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Israel Abanikanda will serve as the team’s RB2 in Week 10 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.analysis: Abanikanda will get the practice squad elevation over Kendre Miller, who recently signed with the team after being released by the Saints. Abanikanda has spent part of the last two seasons with the Cowboys and had a solid preseason, rushing for 91 scoreless yards on 22 carries while adding three receptions for 16 yards. We wouldn’t expect Abanikanda to see enough meaningful work to be fantasy relevant this week but he could be worth a stash in deeper leagues as insurance for Javonte Williams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.headline: Cowboys declared WR Camden Brown, RB Israel Abanikanda, OLB Tyrus Wheat, CB Caelen Carson, and OT Ajani Cornelius inactive for Week 1 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.analysis: Javonte Williams should see all the volume he can handle with the Cowboys entering Week 1 with a recent signee and a practice squad elevation as depth behind their lead back. There weren’t any other surprises outside of the lack of backfield depth.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.headline: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports that Cowboys Malik Davis (hip) will have surgery and be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.analysis: It is unclear whether this is a season-ending injury or if Davis has a chance to return later in the year. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported earlier that the Cowboys were “bracing for an extended absence” and that a source told him, “it’s bad.” It sounds like Davis’ 2026 season may be over. Cowboys RB Emari Demercado now sits behind starting RB Javonte Williams, and RB Israel Abanikanda is on the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Cowboys “are bracing for an extended absence” after RB Malik Davis suffered a hip injury on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.analysis: Regarding Davis’ injury, Fowler’s source said simply, “it’s bad.” The Cowboys’ No. 2 running back is undergoing further testing, but we expect them to place him on injured reserve before long. The Cowboys waived RB Jaydon Blue and RB Phil Mafah last month. Blue has since signed with the Eagles’ practice squad. The Cowboys have RB Emari Demercado on the active roster behind RB Javonte Williams. Currently, only RB Israel Abanikanda is on the practice squad in Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.headline: Cowboys released RB Israel Abanikanda.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.analysis: The Cowboys also released/waived LB Justin Barron, RB Jaydon Blue, CB Trikweze Bridges, CB Josh Butler, S Zion Childress, RB Jashaun Corbin, DT Tommy Dunn, G Chris Glaser, T Sebastian Gutierrez, WR Jordan Hudson, T Marcellus Johnson, G Trevor Keegan, TE Zack Kuntz, LB Isaiah Land, RB Phil Mafah, DT Dayo Odeleye, LB Langston Patterson, T Shiyazh Pete, WR Anthony Smith, WR Jaden Smith, CB Reddy Steward, DT Jay Toia, TE Michael Trigg, TE Mitch Van Vooren, G DJ Wingfield, DT DJ Withers, S Julius Wood, WR Tyler Johnson, CB Derioin Kendrick, WR Denzel Mims, LB Curtis Robinson, WR Marquez Valeds-Scantling, LB Sam Williams, TE DJ Rogers and placed LB Marist Liufau and CB Devin Moore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.headline: Cowboys RB Malik Davis was held out with the starters in Friday’s preseason game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.analysis: Davis appears to have secured a roster spot, but we won’t know for sure until Sunday. The broadcast initially referred to him as the starter, but it was instead RB Phil Mafah who took the field. Mafah dominated backfield touches throughout the first half, repeatedly running into Saints defenders on runs up the middle. He was spelled by RB Israel Abanikanda. Cowboys RB Jaydon Blue does not seem to be playing this evening. Last Sunday, The Athletic’s Jon Machota predicted Blue would seize the No. 2 running back job from Davis in-season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.headline: Cowboys RB Jaydon Blue (shoulder) resumed participating in team drills on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.analysis: The good news is that Blue took “some” snaps in team drills for the first time this week, according to ESPN’s Todd Archer. The bad news is that Blue was the fourth player up behind starting RB Javonte Williams and fellow backups RB Malik Davis and RB Israel Abanikanda. Earlier today, COO and co-owner Stephen Jones said Blue and RB Phil Mafah were being “pushed” by Davis. While it’s possible the team is just easing Blue back into action, his spot in the rotation, coupled with Jones’ comments, is concerning. He had received positive reviews to this point, but a fantasy-related reassessment may be in order. The backfield rotation in Saturday’s preseason game against the Cardinals is worth tracking.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.headline: Packers signed WR Mecole Hardman to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.analysis: Hardman was waived at last cuts but decided that staying with the Packers made sense. The 27-year-old will likely be elevated in Week 1 if Jayden Reed’s injury is as serious as it seems. Also joining the Packers practice squad are: QB Clayton Tune, RB Israel Abanikanda, DL Deslin Alexandre, DB Johnathan Baldwin, T Brant Banks, DL James Ester, LB Jamon Johnson, K Mark McNamee, DL Arron Mosby, WR Isaiah Neyor, WR Will Sheppard, DB Jaylin Simpson, and LB Kristian Welch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.headline: Packers waived RB Israel Abanikanda.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.analysis: In three preseason games, Abanikanda rushed 24 times for 71 yards, one touchdown and one fumble and caught 2-of-4 targets for 14 yards. He could return to the Packers via the practice squad. The Packers released DL Deslin Alexandre, DB Johnathan Baldwin, T Brant Banks, LB Jared Bartlett, G Tyler Cooper, RB Tyrion Davis-Price, DL James Ester, CB Tyron Herring, WR Julian Hicks, C Trey Hill, RB Amar Johnson, WR Cornelius Johnson, LB Jamon Johnson, CB Kalen King, G JJ Lippe, TE Johnny Lumpkin, K Mark McNamee, DL Arron Mosby, WR Isaiah Neyor, DL Devonte O’Malley, WR Will Sheppard, DB Jaylin Simpson, G/C Lecitus Smith, TE Messiah Swinson, T Kadeem Telfort and LB Kristian Welch. The Packers placed C/G Jacob Monk placed on injured reserve with a designation to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.headline: Packers signed RB Israel Abanikanda, formerly of the 49ers, to a contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/israel-aba.analysis: Abanikanda moves from one Shanahan system to another. Unfortunately, for the one-cut-and-go runner, the Packers’ running back unit is even deeper than the 49ers’. He is unlikely to find a fantasy-relevant role in Green Bay.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) is listed as questionable for Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Despite his uncertain status, Brown, who was limited in all three practices during the week, will make the trip across the Atlantic Ocean with the Pats before their game in Munich, Germany. The veteran has missed two straight contests, and New England may decide to rest him once again before the team’s Week 11 bye. Should Brown suit up, he would sit in the WR2/WR3 tiers against a Detroit secondary that’s improved lately but has been generally friendly to receivers most of the season. If Brown can’t go, DeMario Douglas would take that baton as the top target; Mack Hollins, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams would see a boost into stronger Flex territory, and tight end Hunter Henry would slot into a more stream-worthy status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Two limited practices would seem to have him with a real chance to play in Munich, and the fact that he made the trip at all makes it seem likely he’ll have a real chance to go. We’d consider him on the optimistic side of questionable heading into Friday’s practice report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown traveled to Germany with the team and is already practicing to start the week, giving him a shot at suiting up on Sunday morning. Given his lengthy history of knee issues, it still wouldn’t surprise us if he gets another week off. Brown would be in line for a strong workload and WR2 fantasy numbers if active. Fantasy managers will want to monitor this situation throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said the team plans to bring A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) to Germany ahead of Week 10’s game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: This doesn’t mean Brown will suit up against the Lions, but it is an indicator that the team thinks he has a chance to play if he can have a good week of practice. Brown has missed the Patriots’ last two games after a knee injury flared up following Week 7’s game against the Bears. He did not get on the practice field at all last week, so even a few limited sessions would be an improvement for the 29-year-old receiver. In three games this season, Brown has caught just 9-of-20 targets for 101 scoreless yards. That said, if he’s healthy enough to play in Week 10, he could be primed for a breakout against a lowly Lions secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown was unable to practice again Friday, and the 29-year-old will not be able to roll against the Green Bay secondary. It’s a second-consecutive missed game for Brown, who has played in just three games since his blockbuster deal to the Patriots prior to the season. DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will be Drake Maye’s top wideout targets for the game against Green Bay. Not ideal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown seems highly unlikely to play in Week 9 against the Packers. The Patriots could shut him down for a little while, with the goal of getting his degenerative knee and early-season high-ankle sprain healed. For now, fantasy managers should make backup plans in the short term.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown’s recurring knee issue flared up during practice last week. He was downgraded to a DNP on Thursday and Friday. The Pats then ruled him out over the weekend. Brown has been dealing with this injury for years, and it was something the Pats acknowledged when they traded for him in the offseason. It wouldn’t be surprising for the team to give him multiple weeks off in preparation for a playoff run. Head coach Mike Vrabel sidestepped a question about putting Brown back on injured reserve. At a minimum, we’re not expecting Brown to suit up this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said “we’ll see” when asked if A.J. Brown (knee) could practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: This is basically a non-answer from Vrabel, who said the team will see how Brown progresses through the week and how he responds to treatment. Brown missed Week 8’s game against the Dolphins after he suffered what was described as a flare up” of a knee issue that has plagued him for some time. It’s far too early to assume Brown will be able to go in Week 9 against the Packers given the timing of his injury last week, so his status will be one to keep an eye on throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (knee) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: This was always thought to be the case after Brown missed Thursday and Friday with a “flare up” of an existing knee injury, the same issue that ultimately saw the Rams back out of trade negotiations this offseason. Brown’s absence comes at a horrible time for a team already without Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs, leaving only DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism as healthy wide receivers on the active roster. Fantasy managers in a bind could consider taking a shot on upside through Williams’ downfield role against a Dolphins team bleeding explosive passing through the first seven weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said A.J. Brown (knee) is questionable for New England’s Week 8 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: This feels like a very optimistic questionable after Brown missed the last two practices of the week with a new knee tweak. Brown-reliant managers should be making contingency plans ready for Sunday. “We’ll see when he comes in tomorrow, and we’ll make a decision,” Vrabel said.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is questionable for Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Despite some belief that Stevenson could miss a short period of time due to a knee injury he suffered late in Week 9’s loss to the Packers, the 28-year-old back will have an outside chance at suiting up against the Lions after logging back-to-back limited practices to close out the week. Backup Corey Kiner is expected to step into an expanded role if Stevenson is unable to go, but will be hard to trust as anything more than an RB3/FLEX play if Stevenson does suit up. With the Pats and Lions set to face off at 9:30 AM EST in Germany, fantasy managers will want to check early inactives before setting their lineups if they either player on their roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday DNP. Post-Week 9 reports had Stevenson with a chance to miss a short period of time, but a limited session at least points to the idea that he could play in Munich on Sunday morning. Fantasy managers reliant on Stevenson or dabbling with Corey Kiner will want to keep an eye on Friday’s injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson is expected to miss some time because of the knee issue. With their bye next week, it makes sense for the Pats to hold him out on Sunday and give him an extra week of rest. With TreVeyon Henderson already ruled out, Corey Kiner is the next man up in this backfield. As the only game in town for touches, he will push for an RB2 ranking this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) could miss a “short period of time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Reporting Monday, Schefter relayed that Stevenson is dealing with a knee tendon issue that could “sideline him for a short period of time.” While the report is about as vague as possible, fantasy managers will want to begin exploring alternatives for a running back that has outperformed his preseason draft capital through the first half of the season. TreVeyon Henderson remains sidelined indefinitely with what is being called an illness, which could leave Corey Kiner atop the depth chart in the backfield in the immediate future. The Patriots next play the Lions in Week 10, where Kiner would be a viable FLEX play, should Stevenson and Henderson miss. Schefter adds that the tendon issue is not expected to require surgery.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) will not return in the Patriots’ Week 9 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson suffered his knee injury late in the third quarter, but was eventually able to make it to the field under his own power. After spending a few moments in the blue medical tent, Stevenson went to the locker room and was ruled out soon after by the team. The 28-year-old back managed just 32 scoreless yards on six carries, but hauled in a 30-yard reception from Drake Maye in the second quarter, finishing the day with a 3-46-1 line on four targets. With TreVeyon Henderson (illness) sidelined with neurological concerns, the Patriots could be looking at using Corey Kiner as their top back entering Week 10 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (undisclosed) exited in the third quarter of Week 9’s game against the Patriots and went to the locker room.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson was slow to get up after a play late in the third quarter and was seen going to the locker room shortly after leaving the field. He spent some time in the blue medical tent, but the team has not disclosed what he is dealing with. Stevenson has rushed six times for 32 yards so far and has caught another three passes for 46 yards and a touchdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed 19 times for 82 yards in the Patriots’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins, adding three receptions for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson was held out of the end zone against the Dolphins, but comfortably paced his team with 22 touches and was handed the ball on each of the Patriots’ first three plays. Stevenson ran hard on inside runs and played well as a receiver, as usual. A fake pitch from inside the Dolphins’ five-yard line had at least one Dolphins defender convinced that Stevenson was headed for the end zone, but Drake Maye kept the ball and ran it into the end zone himself. Stevenson remains firmly in play as an RB2 next week against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed six times for 22 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 93 yards and a touchdown on five receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson scored one of the more improbable touchdowns you will see late in the second quarter. After taking possession with just 14 seconds remaining on the clock, Drake Maye completed an 18-yard pass to A.J. Brown to place the ball near midfield with three seconds remaining before the half. Instead of heaving the ball deep on a Hail Mary, Maye dumped the ball off to Stevenson in the flat with blockers out front. Stevenson would do the rest on his way to a 48-yard score as time expired in the second frame on a score that never really should have happened. The six carries go down as a season-low for the veteran back, although 11 opportunities handily led the team. Stevenson has not seen more than 14 carries since Week 1 and is not finding paint frequently enough to remain a consistent RB2, making him a shaky weekly start moving forward. That holds true ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed 14 times for 36 yards in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson was not targeted in the passing game. He didn’t make any big mistakes — that would be TreVeyon Henderson with his third quarter fumble — but like Hendo, Stevenson found himself mostly on the bench late as the Pats surprisingly rode No. 3 back Corey Kiner in closeout mode. Kiner received 11 carries in the game’s final 16:30. Speaking afterward, coach Mike Vrabel literally called it a hot-hand situation. The “hot hand” is something Stevenson rarely develops, so he can ill afford this backfield becoming a three-man committee. For now, Stevenson is still the Pats’ No. 1 running back. but things just got a little dicier heading into Thursday’s short-week matchup with the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson had 13 rushes for 64 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders, adding three catches for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson was splitting the backfield workload with TreVeyon Henderson before Henderson sustained a potentially serious ankle injury in the second quarter and did not return. Stevenson was somewhat efficient with his opportunities, breaking a few tackles against a low-energy, low-effort Raiders defense. His touchdown came on a goal line carry in the first half. It was his second score of the year. Stevenson will be a top-12 fantasy option next week against the Jets if Henderson is sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) will not play in Week 10 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Head coach Robert Saleh said he is hopeful Tate will be able to return in Week 11 when the Titans visit the Cowboys, but his availability for that game will be determined once the Titans begin prepping for Dallas. In the meantime, the Titans will likely go with Wan’Dale Robinson and Chimere Dike as their top two wideouts after the pair led the team in routes run in Week 8 against the Bengals, with Elic Ayomanor also seeing some work (30 routes). Playing against a stout Jaguars defense will make all of the Titans’ receivers hard to trust as anything more than WR3/WR4 plays, while TE Gunnar Helm could also see more work after earning a season-high eight targets vs. the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) worked out with trainers on the side during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: He did not elevate beyond an official DNP today, but this is an actual step after Tate missed four consecutive practices and Week 8 sandwiched around their Week 9 bye. He’ll have a non-zero chance to play this week heading into Friday, but you have to imagine the best we’ll see on Friday is a questionable tag.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: It’s a little concerning considering the Titans are coming off their bye week. Tate suffered the shoulder injury three weeks ago, and unless he can log a practice tomorrow or Friday, he’s likely to miss this week’s game against the Jaguars. His absence would make Wan’Dale Robinson viable in PPR formats, along with Chimere Dike, who led the Titans in receiving against the Bengals in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) is out for Week 8 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate’s game-day designation comes on the heels of three missed practices this week. His absence leaves behind an alpha’s target share to go claimed by the remaining pass catchers, most notable of whom is slot man Wan’Dale Robinson. Robinson also draws the top matchup on paper against he inside-funnel nature of the Cincinnati defense, appearing to have a clear path to leading the team in targets and receiving. Fantasy managers can start Robinson as a viable WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate was a DNP all week and is at risk of missing Week 8’s game against the Bengals. The team will announce his official status shortly, but if he is unable to go, Wan’Dale Robinson and Elic Ayomanor would be the early favorites to see an uptick in targets against a Bengals secondary that ranks 18th in points allowed to opposing receivers this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate has now missed two practices with the shoulder issue, making him truly questionable for Sunday’s game versus the Bengals. Tate has been operating as the Titans’ clear WR1, meaning there would be plenty of opportunities up for grabs if he can’t go. Wan’Dale Robinson could be in line for more targets, but his slot-only role doesn’t have much overlap with Tate’s job. Second-year wideout Elic Ayomanor might be the best bet to see more work if Tate is out this week, though that would only move him into the WR4 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Apparently Tate picked up the shoulder injury in Week 7’s loss to the Browns, when he caught five passes for 69 scoreless yards. If Tate is unable to practice headed into the weekend, Elic Ayomanor, who last week ran a route on 79 percent of the team’s drop backs and had 44 yards on three catches, would likely be the de factor WR1 for Tennessee. Tate has dominated air yards and targets this season and profiles as a positive regression candidate in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate caught 5-of-7 targets for 69 yards in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: It was another solid if unspectacular outing for the rookie. The Titans operated a fast-pace offense through much of the game against Cleveland, using no-huddle for long stretches of the ballgame. That seemed to put Cam Ward in some sort of rhythm — to the benefit of a few Titans skill position players. Tate now has at least six receptions in three of his past four outings. Tate, who entered the week with a 46 percent air yards share and a 25 percent target share, is an every-week starter who could be a WR3 option next week against a pass-funnel Bengals defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate caught 6-of-7 targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 6 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate’s eight-yard fourth quarter score was the first of his career. He simply beat the defense to the spot in the end zone. Although the touchdown was great, it was Tate’s 19-yard grab early in the third frame that was the highlight of the day. He skied over CB Justin Walley. Playing much better football of late even as second-year QB Cam Ward struggles to return the favor, Tate has stabilized his WR3 value and will be pushing for WR2 status with injuries mounting and bye weeks in full swing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate caught 1-of-5 targets for six yards in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Well, at least last week was good. He did have a 40-plus yarder pulled off the board because of a holding penalty. Next week offers a more welcoming Colts defense and Tate should have a path to low-end WR3 numbers there.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Jordan Davis will not play in Week 10 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: Neither Davis nor recently acquired safety Jessie Bates had bye weeks with their previous teams, which Coen noted when announcing that the two players would be sidelined for Week 10. The decision to sit both players will essentially give them a “bye week,” and it conveniently comes in a week when the Jaguars face an inferior opponent in Tennessee. Both players should be good to go in Week 11 when the Jaguars visit the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Eagles traded DT Jordan Davis to the Jaguars in exchange for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: While the rest of the league waits to make moves ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, the Jaguars have spent Monday wheeling and dealing to improve the defensive side of the ball. Davis is the latest to join the Jaguars, who also acquired S Jessie Bates and DT Davon Godchaux in hopes of shoring up their top-10 defense. Davis signed a three-year, $78 million contract extension with the Eagles earlier this offseason and has been a staple along their defensive line since being drafted 13th overall by them in 2022. Davis has totaled 31 tackles, 1.5 sacks, and two TFLs this season and posted a career-high 4.5 sacks in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Jordan Davis (ankle) told reporters x-rays were negative on his ankle and he feels “OK” at this point.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: Davis is still a candidate to be limited in practice this week, but it doesn’t look like this injury is a major threat to send him to injured reserve or anything like that. Talking with the media after the game is a good sign for his future ability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Jordan Davis went to the locker room in the middle of Week 6 against the Panthers with a leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: Jordan Davis was at the bottom of a pile on a 3rd-down run in the fourth quarter and remained down on the field. He was slow to get up and did leave the field under his own power, but he was moving very gingerly as he walked into the locker room. It’s unclear right now if the injury is to his ankle or his knee, but we should get an update after the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Eagles signed DT Jordan Davis to a three-year, $78 million extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: The deal includes a whopping $65 million in guaranteed money. Davis is now tied to the Eagles through the 2029 season after becoming the highest-paid nose tackle in NFL history with the extension. The former No. 13 overall pick in 2022 notched the second most solo tackles in 2025 amongst defensive linemen and also contributed five sacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Eagles DT Jalen Carter (heel) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: On the plus side, fellow DT Jordan Davis (shoulder) continues to practice in full and LG Landon Dickerson (ankle) at least remained limited rather than experiencing a downgrade. Hopefully, this is just a pre-planned rest day for Carter, who sat out in the Eagles’ Week 6 upset loss to the Giants. The G-Men ran the ball aggressively, totaling 172 yards and four touchdowns on 48 carries. The Vikings could employ a similar game plan with RB Jordan Mason if Carter is again out this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Eagles DT Jordan Davis lost 26 pounds this offseason and is expecting to play more snaps.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: Davis now tips the scales at 330 pounds. This is the lightest he’s been since his sophomore year at Georgia, per PHLY Eagles’ Zach Berman. Davis has functioned as a rotational player since the Eagles drafted him in the 2022 NFL Draft’s first round. A well-conditioned Davis on the field for all three downs could take a step forward in his fourth season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Eagles exercised the fifth-year option for DT Jordan Davis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: After Eagles general manager Howie Roseman declined to say whether the team would pick up Davis’ option just two weeks prior, the team made the call after Davis played his second straight 17-game season for the dominant Philly front seven. Davis, who has 3.5 sacks and five tackles for loss over his past two seasons, was graded by Pro Football Focus as 2024’s 40th-best defensive tackle. He will make $12.9 million in the 2026 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Eagles GM Howie Roseman declined to disclose if the team would pick up Jordan Davis’ fifth-year option.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: “The absence of a decision on Davis logically suggests the Eagles are still weighing their options ahead of the May 1 deadline,” writes The Athletic’s Brooks Kubena. Perhaps the Eagles are leaving their options open because of certain draft scenarios, but Davis has been a fine rotational player for the Eagles in his first three seasons. Davis has generated a 70.9 or better PFF grade in all three of his seasons to date, but has yet to play more than 561 snaps for the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Jordan Davis (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: Davis being added to the injury report on Thursday is a bit concerning, but the fact he was able to log a limited session is still encouraging. We’ll see how he fares in Friday’s practice, but for now, we’d expect him to suit up for Week 8 against the Commanders. In addition to Davis, the Eagles also added CB James Bradberry (ankle) and LB Zach Cunningham (ankle) to the practice report. Both were listed as limited participants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter released a statement saying Lamar Jackson (thumb) will be out for the next 6-10 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: On the short end of this timeline, Jackson could return in Week 16 against the Browns. On the long end, Jackson would be looking at returning around the Wild Card or Divisional Round of the playoffs if the Ravens make the postseason. This timeline closely aligns with the 6-9 week absence NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported earlier in the week. If this isn’t a season-ender for Lamar, it will be close, and how the Ravens perform over the next several weeks with Jacoby Brissett under center will likely determine whether the Ravens dress him for the final few weeks of the season, even if he is ready to go. Minter said that Jackson is “doing well” after suffering his injury in Week 8 against the Bills, which is encouraging, but we’re a long way from knowing if a return for Jackson is truly in the cards. The 4-5 Ravens have lost their last four games but hope to turn things around on Monday night when they play host to the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Lamar Jackson is out for 6-9 weeks with a fractured and dislocated thumb.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Per Rapoport, Jackson has already told his teammates he plans to return this season. While even the short end of that timeline would only have Jackson back in Week 15, it’s an optimistic turn of events for a quarterback who was previously expected to miss the rest of the season. At a nine-week return, Jackson would need Baltimore to make the playoffs to have a shot at returning this year. Jacoby Brissett will likely close out the fantasy season as Baltimore’s starting quarterback, but there’s a chance we get Jackson back for a final game or two in the regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports that the Ravens are willing to make Lamar Jackson the highest-paid player in NFL history.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Well, that’s good, because it will assuredly take a record-setting deal to keep him in a Ravens uniform. Jackson has an $84.34 million salary cap hit next season, so the team has to do something with his contract. Jackson has a no-trade clause and a no-franchise tag clause — he possesses a ton of leverage. Per Palmer, the two sides will not negotiate a new deal in-season, so they will try to get something done between the end of the season and the beginning of free agency, which starts in March 2027.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Lamar Jackson is “likely out for the season” after suffering a thumb injury in Week 8’s loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Head coach Jesse Minter didn’t dismiss the possibility of this being a season-ending injury for Jackson when asked about it after the game, but the optics on the field weren’t good, and the team wasted little time announcing he would undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve. It wouldn’t be at all surprising to learn in the days ahead that Jackson’s season is over, but the team will likely wait until after he has his surgery to make any formal announcement. With Jackson and Tyler Huntley (toe) both being sidelined, rookie UDFA Joe Fagnano is slated to start on the short week on Thursday against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (thumb) will undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: When asked if this is a potentially season-ending injury for Jackson, Minter’s response was, “We’ll see.” After seeing Jackson’s injury on replay, it was easy to assume the Ravens’ QB1 would be looking at another multi-week absence, but this sounds like the worst-case scenario. If Jackson doesn’t land on season-ending IR, he would be required to miss at least four games before he could even consider a return. Adding insult to injury, the Ravens also lost backup Tyler Huntley in this game to a toe injury, meaning rookie UDFA Joe Fagnano could be in line to start on Thursday night against the Jaguars in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (thumb) will not return in Week 8’s game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Jackson’s day officially ends after one play. The two-time MVP injured the thumb on his throwing hand on his first and only dropback of the day and immediately went to the locker room. The urgency with which Jackson was ushered from the field, coupled with how quickly he was ruled out, suggests this could be a serious enough injury that will result in another multi-game absence for Jackson. Tyler Huntley will be under center for the remainder of Week 8’s game against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (thumb) is questionable to return in Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Shortly after he exited the field the team announced that Jackson was questionable to return after suffering a thumb injury on his throwing hand. Tyler Huntley immediately took over for Jackson, as the Ravens’ offense went three-and-out on their first drive of the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (hand) exited in the first quarter of Week 8’s game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Jackson dropped back to pass on the Ravens’ first offensive play of the game and immediately headed for the sideline after hitting his hand on Bills LB Greg Rousseau. The injury was to Jackson’s throwing hand and appeared to be to his thumb, judging by what we could see on slow-motion replay. Trainers covered Jackson’s hand with a towel and immediately ushered him to the locker room. We will check back in when we receive more information on his status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe said Lamar Jackson (ankle) “won’t be 100 percent” in Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: The good news, per Wolfe, is that Jackson will still be able to move despite playing on a bum ankle. Jackson told reporters the pain is “bearable” earlier in the week, which didn’t exactly inspire confidence from Ravens fans and fantasy managers. On the other hand, if Jackson is out there, we expect him to be mobile enough to lead a top-flight offense. A date with the Bills, which features the highest game total of the week, should also create an incredible environment for fantasy production. He is back at the top of the QB1 mix for a likely shootout with the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) will play in Baltimore’s Week 8 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: “We do think we will have Lamar this game,” Minter said. Jackson practiced in full on Friday and has missed the last three weeks with his high-ankle sprain. He was officially cleared off the injury report. Jackson told reporters that he feels like “I’m no longer a statue.” Jackson will be “safe” to use as a QB1 against the Bills in what profiles as a fantasy points bonanza.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.headline: Falcons signed CB C.J. Henderson to a two-year extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.analysis: The former 2020 first-rounder can earn up to $20 million on his new deal, per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, with $11 million being guaranteed. Henderson was drafted No. 9 overall by the Jaguars in 2020, but has since bounced around to the Panthers, Texans, and Steelers, and was actually cut by the Falcons in August 2025 during final roster cutdowns after camp. Since then, Henderson has played his way not only onto the 53-man roster, but into a starting role. He has started six of the eight games he has appeared in for Atlanta this season, totaling 41 tackles, nine pass breakups, and one fumble recovery while earning a PFF coverage grade of 65.3. Playing almost exclusively on the outside, he has allowed opposing receivers to go for 252 yards and three touchdowns on 44 targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.headline: Falcons released CB C.J. Henderson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.analysis: The 2020 first-rounder only played in Week 3 of the preseason, notching a 71.7 PFF coverage grade in 14 coverage snaps. Henderson, 27 in September, will look to catch on elsewhere as the season starts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.headline: Falcons agreed to terms with CB C.J. Henderson, formerly of the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.analysis: Per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Henderson still has to pass his physical. The deal will be official once that happens. Henderson spent a month on the Steelers’ practice squad last year before being called up to the active roster. He did not, however, appear in a single game as a Steeler. His last live reps came with the Panthers in 2023. He made 10 starts, appeared in all 17 games, and broke up six passes with two interceptions. The team correspondingly released OT Tyrone Wheatley Jr. with an injury designation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.headline: Falcons worked out CB C.J. Henderson, formerly of the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.analysis: Henderson logged zero defensive snaps with the Steelers last season. He would likely compete for a backup role, should the Falcons bring him aboard.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.headline: Panthers agreed to terms with CB C.J. Henderson, formerly of the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.analysis: The ex-Jaguars draft bust started 17 games in Carolina over the past two seasons. He was a versatile but ineffective presence for last year’s league-worst team. Still somehow only 25, he will look to provide depth and take a step forward under defensive-minded head coach DeMeco Ryans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.headline: Panthers CB C.J. Henderson (concussion) ruled out for Thursday night against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.analysis: Henderson suffered a concussion in the second quarter against the Colts and wasn’t able to recover in time for Thursday night’s game. With EDGE Brian Burns (concussion) also ruled out, this Panthers defense is not in a great spot, even against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.headline: Panthers CB C.J. Henderson (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 9 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.analysis: Henderson was injured while making a tackle on Jonathan Taylor in the second quarter. He’s Carolina’s top cornerback, so it would be a big loss regardless, but the Panthers are also without top safety Vonn Bell. That could create some issues in the second half against Gardner Minshew, Michael Pittman Jr., and the Colts offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.headline: Panthers DB C.J. Henderson is questionable to return to Week 3 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.analysis: Henderson left the contest late in the first quarter and was seen on the sideline with ice on his ankle. He was declared questionable to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.headline: Panthers did not exercise the fifth-year option on DB C.J. Henderson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.analysis: This isn’t all that surprising given how Henderson’s career has unfolded. Since being selected by the Jaguars with the No. 9 overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft, Henderson was traded to the Panthers for a third-round pick and tight end Dan Arnold last September, and has struggled to hang with NFL receivers since entering the league. He started 10 games last season for the Panthers and allowed a career-high 642 yards and five touchdowns while earning a PFF coverage grade of 48.9. He’ll enter 2023 on a prove-it year with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Panthers are trading Dan Arnold and a third-round draft pick to the Jaguars in exchange for CB C.J. Henderson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-henders.analysis: Henderson has reportedly been on the trading block since August. With Carolina needing secondary help after losing Jaycee Horn indefinitely to a foot injury, the Panthers made the move, dealing Arnold to Jacksonville. The Jags lost James O’Shaughnessy (ankle) for at least a few weeks and started journeyman TE Jacob Hollister Sunday against Arizona. Arnold should immediately step in as the team’s top pass-catching tight end in an offense that made O’Shaughnessy fantasy viable for the season’s first couple weeks. Arnold has flashed when given the chance. He had seven catches for 84 yards in three games with the Panthers. Rookie Tommy Tremble -- who caught a 30-yard pass and scored on a short rushing attempt in Week 3 -- profiles as Carolina’s pass-catching tight end after Arnold’s departure. The Darnold-to-Arnold era was short lived.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cameron-th.headline: Falcons signed DE Cameron Thomas to a three-year contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cameron-th.analysis: Thomas has started all nine games he has appeared in for the Falcons this season. The 26-year-old lineman spent the previous two seasons in Cleveland with head coach Kevin Stefanski, and then joined Stefanski in Atlanta on a one-year deal this offseason. Thomas has totaled 25 tackles, two sacks, and one TFL this season for the Falcons, earning a PFF grade of 77.2. His deal is worth up to $33 million and he will now be under contract through the 2029 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cameron-th.headline: Falcons agreed to terms with EDGE Cameron Thomas, formerly of the Browns, one a one-year, $3.1 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cameron-th.analysis: A 2022 third-round pick of the Cardinals, Thomas ended up in Cleveland following a brief sojourn with the Chiefs. He notched 2.5 sacks in Cleveland last season. Seemingly maxed out as a 300-snap pass-rushing specialist, Thomas is headed into his age-26 campaign.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cameron-th.headline: Browns claimed EDGE Cameron Thomas off waivers from the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cameron-th.analysis: Thomas played just six snaps with the Chiefs in 2024, but was a solid rotational edge for the Cardinals in 2022 and 2023. The Browns will get a look at him over their last six games of the season. Kansas City acquired him at final cuts, and Thomas will be on year four of his rookie deal for the Browns in 2025 if they want him back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cameron-th.headline: Chiefs declared DE Cameron Thomas, OL C.J. Hanson, OT Ethan Driskell, and DT Marlon Tuipulotu inactive for Week 3 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cameron-th.analysis: The biggest news out of Kansas City heading into Week 3 is the absence of running back Isiah Pacheco. Also, running back Kareem Hunt was signed to the practice squad and not elevated prior to the team’s Sunday Night Football game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cameron-th.headline: Chiefs declared DE Cameron Thomas, DT Marlon Tuipulotu, OT Ethan Driskell and OL C.J. Hanson inactive for Week 2 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cameron-th.analysis: Not exactly the most exciting list of inactives. Hollywood Brown (shoulder) was placed on injured reserve earlier in the week, for those that missed that news.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cameron-th.headline: Chiefs acquired LB Cameron Thomas from the Cardinals for a future seventh-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cameron-th.analysis: Thomas was a third-round pick in the 2022 NFL draft and a second-team All-American in his last year at San Diego State. Thomas gives the Chiefs more edge depth as they wait for the return of injured pass rusher Charles Omenihu.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cameron-th.headline: San Diego State DL Cameron Thomas (undisclosed) left Tuesday’s Senior Bowl practice and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cameron-th.analysis: It was a curious situation for Thomas (6'5/265), as the American Team had yet to put their helmets on for drills when Thomas walked off the field under the supervision of Lions trainers. He later returned to the sideline in street clothes with his status very much in doubt for the rest of the week. A standout performer for the past three seasons, Thomas took his game to another level in 2021, recording an impressive 77 pressures and 44 hurries while earning a superb 89.4 defensive grade from Pro Football Focus. It’s an unfortunate break for the promising edge rusher, hopefully he will still be able to suit up by this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cameron-th.headline: Pro Football Focus’ Anthony Teash passes along that San Diego State redshirt sophomore DT Cameron Thomas logged three or more quarterback pressures in eight games last season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cameron-th.analysis: You want to see Thomas at his most disruptive, check out his performance against New Mexico State from last fall. Treash relays that in that contest, the 6-foot-5, 260-pounder recorded a whopping eight pressures. He posted PFF grades over 80 as both a run-defender and pass-rusher in 2019. Teash slots in Thomas as the No. 4 returning interior defensive lineman for the 2020 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 5-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers was clearly not a point of emphasis in a game expected to carry significant weather impacts. Despite the weather subsiding in the second half, McCarthy remained fixed on Isaiah Likely, feeding the veteran tight end 11 targets. The matchup also played a role in the game plan, with the Commanders missing numerous key linebackers while blitzing at an above average rate. Nabers is in a good spot to bounce back against the Jaguars in Week 11, where he’ll return to WR1 status in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 5-of-8 targets for 43 yards in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Entering the game with four straight 100-yard performances, Nabers had a day of what ifs. Banged up early but no worse for the wear, Nabers played snaps with two different QBs as J.J. McCarthy missed part of the third quarter with a hip issue. McCarthy returned only for Nabers to drop a should-have-been 20-yard touchdown in the end zone. Frustrating, but 9.43 PPR points on a “down” day is not the worst outcome. Nabers and McCarthy have only four days to heal up for Thursday’s short-week date with the Commanders, but Nabers’ status is not in doubt, while he will remain a high-end WR1 even if Jameis Winston returns under center for the G-Men.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: The Giants have smartly limited Nabers’ practice participation levels at times this season, allowing him to play very well while returning from last year’s season-ending knee injury.
