Nabers belongs in fantasy football lineups in this divisional showdown, as usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) returned to practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers was a surprise DNP with a knee injury on Thursday, but said after practice that he expected to play. His return to the field on Friday suggests he will be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Eagles, but we will still check in with a final status when the Giants announce player designations for the weekend. Assuming he is good to go, Nabers should be treated as a normal must-start receiver against a down-bad Eagles team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers worked with trainers today instead of practicing with his teammates. He told reporters after practicing that he is “good” to go for Week 9 against the Eagles. We believe him. The Giants have managed his reps at times during the practice week this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (undisclosed) was seen working off to the side with trainers on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: The Giants have limited Nabers’ practice reps from time to time this season. Although he may end up being listed as a non-participant, we are not currently concerned about his Week 9 availability. The Giants’ No. 1 wide receiver is fully dressed in his typical practice attire. An update will be provided when more info is released.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 7-of-11 targets for 111 yards in New York’s Week 7 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: He toasted Derek Stingley Jr. a few times and found a 42-yarder early on in the proceedings. Nabers didn’t come close to scoring, but that was mostly a result of Houston’s bad run defense being an easy mark. He’ll retain WR1 status once he’s back from New York’s Week 8 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: SNY TV’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants will stick with J.J. McCarthy as the starter “for the foreseeable future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: According to Hughes, “this is the player they targeted and wanted” as their quarterback the minute Jaxson Dart (knee) got hurt. Hughes acknowledges that coach John Harbaugh could eventually bench McCarthy later in the year, but it will take more than a bad “game or two” for that to happen. In the meantime, the weekly fantasy football outlooks for Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are more volatile than they were with Jameis Winston at the helm. Selling high could make sense. Hughes adds that McCarthy would have to play like a top-10 quarterback to make the coaching staff consider him for the starting role next season. That outcome seems highly unlikely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 12-of-15 targets for 165 yards in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers was once again heavily involved in the Giants’ passing game, getting the first offensive touch for New York. He saw 15 targets and tallied 165 scoreless yards on the day, with over half of this yardage coming with J.J. McCarthy in the fourth quarter. It’s the third straight 100-yard game for Nabers, who is now fully ramped up from his torn ACL last year. The Giants may be debating between Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy as the starting quarterback for next week. Regardless of the starter, Nabers sees enough volume to be a borderline WR1 for Week 7 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 11-of-20 targets for 121 yards and one touchdown in the Giants’ Week 5 tie with the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers saw 15 of his targets come in the second half after the Giants opted to abandon a mostly useless ground game in a game they trailed for most of the afternoon. Nabers came up with multiple big plays as the Giants mounted their comeback attempt, with his biggest coming on a leaping 17-yard touchdown in the end zone to tie the game at 27-27 with under two minutes to go in the game. Nabers had a key drop on a screen pass in overtime that had a chance to set up a big gain, but he made up for it later in the game with a 28-yard gain as the Giants were trying to position themselves for a potential game-winning field goal attempt. Nabers has now gone for 100-plus yards in back-to-back weeks and has found the end zone in both of those games. He seems to finally be hitting his stride after a slow start to the season, and will profile as a high-end WR2 in next week’s game against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 3-of-4 targets for 62 yards in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: The New York wide receivers were clearly limited by a game plan to feature tight end Isaiah Likely, with the starting trio of Malik Nabers, Fields, and Darnell Mooney combining for just 10 receptions, one more than the nine of Likely. Even so, Fields continued to demonstrate a strong connection with quarterback J.J. McCarthy as the rookie finished second on the team in receiving despite seeing only four targets. The highlight of the game came in the second half when McCarthy threaded a ball over one defender and underneath two more down the left sideline for a 25-yard gain to Fields. Although his weekly volume likely won’t be vast enough to return consistent fantasy production without an injury to Nabers or Likely, Fields continues to show the growth dynasty managers were hoping for.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: Although this was a step back on Fields’ pre-bye performance of 4/83, it was actually only the second time all season he caught more than two passes. He continues to head in the right direction as J.J. McCarthy provides some upside hope for this offense. That being said, McCarthy’s (hip) status is questionable for Thursday against the Commanders, while Fields has still not proven his WR4 bonafides. He mostly remains an end-of-bench stash in conventional 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 4-of-5 targets for 83 yards in New York’s Week 7 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: It should be noted that the Texans defense is giving up points to wideouts by the bushel this year, but in J.J. McCarthy’s first start, Fields was heavily involved. This bested his career-best yardage total by 31 yards and he added a career-high 47-yard catch-and-run. Fields doesn’t necessarily need to be added in most fantasy leagues at this point but he’s definitely making inroads towards WR4 status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-8 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: Fields saw a season-high eight targets, but caught just two of those passes for 19 yards. The Giants passing game behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely isn’t productive for fantasy purposes. Darnell Mooney had a carry for 20 yards while Charlie Jones caught 2-of-3 passes for 66 yards. Fields is the best option past Nabers and Likely, but he can be left on fantasy benches for Week 7 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-3 targets for 52 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 4 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: Fields has now caught exactly two passes in each of his first four NFL appearances. His 12-yard touchdown was the first of his career. Jameis Winston was flushed from the pocket and found Fields on the run. The duo later connected on a similar play for a non-scoring 40-yard grab. Today was the first time Winston showed any signs of life in place of Jaxson Dart, though Fields is still going to be a tough sell WR4 in this depressed offensive environment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught both of his targets for 19 yards in the Giants’ Week 3 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: Fields hasn’t caught more than two passes in a game this year. He finished third on the team in targets in Week 3. Fields is on the field plenty, he just isn’t earning that many opportunities. He is not a viable fantasy option for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-6 targets for 30 yards in the Giants’ Week 2 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: Fields struggled alongside the rest of the Giants in a game played mostly with backup quarterback Jameis Winston under center. Jaxson Dart departed after the team’s first possession with what looked like an MCL sprain based on the mechanism of the injury, something that could force missed contests from the normal starter. That would position Fields in a difficult spot to return usable counting stats in the short term. He gets the struggling Titans in Week 3, where he’ll be best left on fantasy benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-4 targets for 25 yards in the Giants’ Week 1 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: The rookie wide receiver showcased a polished all-around skillset, reinforcing offseason reports that he had locked down the WR2 role opposite Malik Nabers. His 6'4, 220-pound frame was on full display as he was continually utilized as both a down-blocker and blocker in the second level on runs, something that should allow him to continue to operate as the clear-cut WR2 for the Giants throughout his rookie campaign. That said, the box scores highlights the obvious distinction that his snap rate — he led all Giants wideouts with 50 — won’t always translate to fantasy production while playing alongside Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely, the latter two of whom commanded 17 targets on 29 Jaxson Dart pass attempts. The good news is that he played well ahead of veterans Darnell Mooney and Odell Beckham Jr., with Mooney having 39 snaps and Beckham just 11. Fantasy managers are best off viewing Fields as a high-end stash at the end of benches for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan believes WR Malachi Fields “will likely start as the Giants’ No. 2 receiver opposite Malik Nabers.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: This isn’t the first time Raanan has suggested Fields could have the inside edge as the Giants’ WR2. Earlier this month, he said the rookie third-rounder was making an “early claim” for the role, which doesn’t come as much of a surprise given the thin receiving corps the Giants are currently working with. The 6-foot-4, 220-plus-pound receiver has an excellent catch radius and made a name for himself with his ability to haul in contested targets during his days at Virginia and Notre Dame. It seems highly unlikely that Fields would make enough of an impact to be considered a reliable fantasy contributor, but he could be worth a late-round/stash in drafts to see how things unfold for him in the weeks to come.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 3-of-3 targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in the first week of the preseason against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: It’s a game that The Athletic’s Dan Duggan says “strengthened his push for the No. 2 receiver job.” His touchdown pass was from Jaxson Dart, but he was one of several receivers getting first-team snaps. It’s hard to believe Fields will be relevant early in 12-team redraft leagues unless Malik Nabers suffers a setback, but he’s squarely on the fantasy radar after a big camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 9-of-11 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely as clearly the going-in game plan in a game expected to be heavily influenced by weather. The rain cleared in the first half but Likely remained the featured option through the air, likely influenced by heavy blitz rates and unrelenting pressure from the Washington defense. The 11-target game was the fifth time this season that the veteran tight end hit double-digit targets but the first time doing so with J.J. McCarthy under center. Likely remains a surefire TE1 ahead of a difficult matchup against the Jaguars in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 5-of-6 targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Although it was another down day in the yardage department by his recent standards, Likely got the fantasy job done with his score and five receptions. It also wasn’t a bad outcome in a contest where J.J. McCarthy missed time with a hip injury and the Giants attempted only 27 throws vs. a reeling Eagles team. Likely’s touchdown was a five-yarder where he took advantage of mass defensive confusion at the goal line. It is unclear if McCarthy will be ready for Thursday’s short-week date with the Commanders, but Likely will remain a high-end QB1 even if Jameis Winston returns under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan reports Isaiah Likely (undisclosed) expressed confidence that he’ll be fine after the bye week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely was spotted limping at times during Week 7’s win over the Texans, which helps explain his subpar production. We’ll keep an eye on this one coming out of the bye, but we’re certainly not expecting anything serious here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 2-of-4 targets for 12 yards in New York’s Week 7 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: It was his first game with fewer than five targets all season. New York’s passing game simply targeted Houston outside the numbers and they ran the ball effectively enough that they didn’t need to feed Likely. He’ll be on the TE1 line in Week 9 against the Eagles once the Giants return from their bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: SNY TV’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants will stick with J.J. McCarthy as the starter “for the foreseeable future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: According to Hughes, “this is the player they targeted and wanted” as their quarterback the minute Jaxson Dart (knee) got hurt. Hughes acknowledges that coach John Harbaugh could eventually bench McCarthy later in the year, but it will take more than a bad “game or two” for that to happen. In the meantime, the weekly fantasy football outlooks for Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are more volatile than they were with Jameis Winston at the helm. Selling high could make sense. Hughes adds that McCarthy would have to play like a top-10 quarterback to make the coaching staff consider him for the starting role next season. That outcome seems highly unlikely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 6-of-11 targets for 99 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely scored his fifth touchdown of the season and third over the last two games. He also caught a two point conversion, with all his scoring coming in the fourth quarter from J.J. McCarthy. The pass-heavy game script helped Likely salvage his fantasy day late in the game as he saw double-digit targets for the third straight game and fourth time this season. Now averaging 9.8 targets per game, Likely is squarely in the fantasy TE1 ranks heading into a tough Week 7 matchup against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (foot) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Theo Johnson has a neck injury and was limited in practice. Both tight ends should be able to suit up on Sunday. Coming off a career-high in targets (13), Likely is looking more like a top-five fantasy tight end every week. He should be in every fantasy lineup for his Week 6 date with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 11-of-13 targets for 94 yards and two touchdown in the Giants’ Week 5 tie with the Commanders
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely set a new career-high with 11 receptions in this one, and came up with two clutch touchdowns in the process. His first score came on a three-yard strike from Jameis Winston on a third-and-goal play that the Giants needed to stay in the game, cutting the Commanders’ lead to 19-13. Then, in the fourth quarter and with the Giants facing a fourth-and-eight, Likely turned an eight-yard reception upfield for a 17-yard touchdown that nearly looked like a fumble and turnover at the goal-line. Likely has been targeted 25 times in his last two games and has now gone for 66 or more yards in three of five games to start the season. He’s starting to show good chemistry with Jameis Winston and will be on the TE1 radar in next week’s game against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (knee/groin) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 5 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: The Giants’ passing offense is tethered to Jameis Winston’s scattershot arm, but Likely has a favorable matchup against the Commanders’ defense this week. He can be started as a low-end TE1 in this divisional showdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (knee/groin) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely is on track to face the Commanders’ fantasy-friendly defense in Week 5. Ideally, we will see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow. The Giants’ starting tight end warrants TE1 treatment thanks to his workload and plus matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo rushed 18 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders, adding 44 yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo immediately returned to a workhorse role following the shortcomings of Devin Singletary in Week 10, the latter of whom saw but one opportunity to the 22 of Skattebo. The Skatt-man bookended halftime with a score from one yard out on the team’s final possession of the first half and a score from 13 yards out on the team’s first possession of the second half, earning two backflips in the process. The second-year back also escaped down the sideline for a 34-yard reception in the first quarter to pad his counting stats. Despite the resurgence in workload, Skattebo will be a borderline FLEX option in a difficult matchup against the pass-funnel Jaguars in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler said to “expect a lot of Cam Skattebo” in Week 10 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: The Giants host the Commanders for this week’s Thursday Night Football game. The open-air stadium is currently experiencing heavy rain, and Fowler indicates the rainfall will continue this evening. Devin Singletary will back up Skattebo, but the touch distribution will heavily “slant” toward Skattebo, solidifying his status as an RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo was listed as doubtful for Week 9. He reportedly pushed to play, but the team smartly chose to hold him out. He logged two full practices this week and is good to go for Thursday’s game. Without much competition for touches, Skattebo is back in the RB2 mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports the Giants inquired about Bijan Robinson’s availability before the NFL’s trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: “They were certainly big game hunting,” Raanan said. Though the thought of the Falcons parting ways with the centerpiece of their offense sounds ridiculous, it’s clear John Harbaugh and the Giants see themselves as a postseason team that won’t be content with a playoff berth. The inquiry on Bijan speaks to the Giants’ ongoing skepticism of Cam Skattebo as a true lead back. The team has done everything they can to prevent Skattebo from taking on a big backfield workload. In Week 10 against the Commanders, with a flurry of backfield injuries and Devin Singletary coming off one of the worst running back performances in NFL history, the Giants might have no choice but to feed Skattebo, who should be started in all 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: He should be good to go and handle low-end RB2 duties against the Commanders. Seemingly always at his best after a week off — which makes sense due to how physical he plays — don’t be surprised if Skattebo puts up some major fantasy points on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Head coach John Harbaugh said earlier Monday that Skattebo would be “full go” for Thursday night’s game against the Commanders. It’s good news for a New York football team that struggled mightily to run the football consistently with veteran journeyman Devin Singletary spearheading the backfield against the Eagles in Week 9. Skattebo appears likely to reclaim lead back duties moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Cam Skattebo (hamstring) will be “full go” in Week 10 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Harbaugh said Skattebo was “very close” to playing in Week 9 against the Eagles, but they opted to sideline him, focusing on the second game they would play four days later. With the Giants set to face the Commanders on Thursday, Skattebo should be well rested and ready to play in his first game since Week 7, when he first suffered his injury. Skattebo totaled 71 scoreless yards on 15 touches in Week 5 against the Commanders and will be in the RB2 mix upon returning this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is inactive for Week 9 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: With Skattebo down, the G-Men have been forced into a Devin Singletary start. Someone named “Gregory Desrosiers” appears to be the RB2. Expect a pass-focused game plan vs. Philly’s crumbling defense. Also inactive for the Giants are CB Colton Hood, CB Nikko Reed, OL Josh Sills, OL Marcus Mbow, TE Thomas Fidone II and DL C.J. Okoye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is “pushing to play” in Week 9 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo was listed as doubtful for Week 9 after getting in a single limited practice this week. Players rarely suit up after getting the doubtful tag, but it’s not out of the question. Even if he is ruled out with inactives, the fact that Skattebo is pushing to play means he should be good to go for Week 10. Devin Singletary will handle the bulk of the backfield touches if he can’t go this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: NFL insider Josina Anderson reports the Giants “cooled on acquiring Colts RB Jonathan Taylor because of price.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: She added that the Giants have resolved to move on from the trade talks ahead of their Week 9 date with the Eagles. Things change quickly in the NFL and this report doesn’t guarantee that Taylor won’t be a Giant. On the other hand, Anderson’s reporting doesn’t leave much room error. With the Colts’ asking price reportedly being through the roof, the Giants are content with Cam Skattebo as their top back. Devin Singletary is expected to start this week with Skattebo banged up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: J.J. McCarthy completed 23-of-36 passes for 293 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Giants’ 24-21, Week 10 loss to the Commanders, adding 34 yards on six carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: McCarthy appeared to be in complete control throughout before a game-sealing interception with under a minute to play in a three-point game. He demonstrated plus pocket presence and made numerous dime-worthy throws, the most impressive of which was a 25-yard dart to rookie Malachi Fields that was put in the only place where Fields could come down with the ball, over one defender and underneath two more down the left sideline. McCarthy leaned heavily on Isaiah Likely, feeding the veteran tight end 11 targets in what appeared to be a matchup-based game plan in the face of an aggressive pass rush. The Giants fall to 5-3-1 with the loss and pass the first tie-breaker to the Commanders after the two teams’ tie earlier this season. The Giants get a difficult matchup against arguably the most well-rounded roster in the AFC when they host the Jaguars in Week 11, where McCarthy falls to a mid-range QB2 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: J.J. McCarthy (hip) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: McCarthy was upgraded to a full practice yesterday and remained full today. He’s good to go after getting banged up in the team’s Week 9 win over the Eagles. McCarthy made a few big plays against Philly, but his accuracy issues were compounded by five sacks. His shine as a high-end QB2 has all but evaporated.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: J.J. McCarthy (hip) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: He’ll be ready to take on the Commanders on Thursday night barring a major setback. McCarthy can be penciled in as a mid-range QB2 for the game given the Commanders’ pass-funnel nature.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: J.J. McCarthy (hip) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: The official designation seems to track with the prevailing sentiment from the team, with the expectation that he’ll be able to play through the hip discomfort sustained in Week 9. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his level of participation during the remainder of the week, but it appears as if McCarthy will be out there on Thursday Night Football against the Commanders. The pass-funnel nature of the matchup and expected presence of McCarthy is a boost to the fantasy upside of Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said J.J. McCarthy (hip) looks “like he’s going to play” in Week 10 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: Harbaugh said McCarthy is “doing well” after briefly being knocked out of Sunday’s game against the Eagles with a hip injury. McCarthy was in visible pain on the sideline at times, but was able to finish the game. We’ll see how things shape up over the week as the Giants prepare for a short turnaround ahead of Thursday night’s game against the Commanders. If he’s healthy enough, McCarthy will get the start against a Commanders defense that has struggled mightily at times against the pass this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: J.J. McCarthy completed 12-of-19 passes for 127 yards in the Giants’ 19-11, Week 9 win over the Eagles, adding four carries for 22 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: Taking a beating before his third quarter hip injury, McCarthy had a much more “Minnesota day” against the Eagles, with the huge exception he again avoided turnovers. Although McCarthy’s third down decision-making was leaving a little something to be desired, his ability to avoid the big mistake was paramount in a contest where the G-Men simply had to outlast a team starting its No. 3 quarterback. He did that, finding Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely for a handful of down-field completions along the way. That does not included a dropped 20-yard touchdown from Nabers. This was McCarthy’s “worst” showing in three appearances as a Giant, but it was still promising on the whole. Now McCarthy needs to find out how sore he is going to be on Monday after really taking a walloping. He could end up highly questionable for Thursday’s short-week date with the Commanders. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: J.J. McCarthy (hip, questionable) returned before the end of the third quarter in the Giants’ Week 9 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: McCarthy, who presumably received some sort of pain-killing injection after twice collapsing in the third quarter, returned for the final play of the frame. He screamed at his offensive linemen to pump them up before doing so. Never a dull moment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: J.J. McCarthy suffered a hip injury in the Giants’ Week 9 game against the Eagles and is questionable to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: Jameis Winston, of course, is now in the game. McCarthy took a thunderclap third quarter hit from Eagles LB Zack Baun and struggled to his feet. He attempted to warm back up on the sideline before literally collapsing while trying to throw. He then headed to the blue tent before making his way to the locker room. We suppose he is genuinely questionable, but on the wrong side of the tag. McCarthy had been taking an absolute beating before going down, absorbing five sacks, many of which were of the spine-rattling variety.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: Giants GM Joe Schoen, asked about the future of the team’s quarterback position said: “To have two young guys with Jaxson and J.J., both talented players, it’s a good position to be in.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: In other words, it wasn’t exactly an endorsement that Jaxson Dart is the franchise quarterback. Dart, out for the year with a meniscus repair, will enter the third year of his rookie contract as the likely favorite to start assuming Nine hasn’t just blossomed into a great quarterback overnight. But it sounds like the Giants are at least open to the idea that McCarthy could alter the calculus here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: J.J. McCarthy completed 20-of-28 passes for 252 yards in New York’s 27-21, Week 7 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: Nine threatened a really good box score, crossing 200 yards by the third quarter, but both the Texans (playing more aggressive coverage) and the Giants (using Jameis Winston in short-yardage situations) conspired to keep McCarthy scoreless. Still, it was a nice debut start. McCarthy took three sacks but had zero turnovers while managing a handful of nice throws. The Giants head on bye in Week 8, but McCarthy has played like he could be a reasonable superflex QB2 against the Eagles in a few weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks caught 2-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks fought through clear discomfort after coming into the game listed questionable following a Wednesday downgrade on the practice report, catching two early passes for 27 yards before succumbing to the inside-funnel nature of the New York defense. Quarterback Jayden Daniels directed 22 of his 33 pass attempts to the trio of Stefon Diggs, Chig Okonkwo, and Ben Sinnott over the middle of the field. Burks’ situation is unlikely to improve in Week 11 with lockdown perimeter corner DJ Turner on deck.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks got in a limited session on Tuesday, but was held out of practice on Monday and Wednesday. It is entirely possible that the Commanders are just exercising caution and Burks will play his normal allotment of snaps, but this sure seems like a scenario where he could end up being a decoy. Burks should be viewed as a boom-bust FLEX with a very low floor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said he expected Treylon Burks (foot) to be active for Week 10 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks, according to Quinn, did not practice Wednesday in preparation for Thursday night’s game against the Giants. He missed Week 9 against the Rams with a foot injury. The Commanders’ best downfield threat with Terry McLaurin sidelined, Burks profiles as a high-variance WR4 option this week. The Giants have faced deep passes at the league’s 16th highest rate this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: It’s an upgrade from an estimated DNP on Monday. Dan Quinn has previously said that he’s optimistic Burks will play, but it’s likely that he’ll hit the questionable line tomorrow barring a full practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Commanders listed Treylon Burks (foot) as DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Hours after head coach Dan Quinn said he was “optimistic” that Burks would play in Week 10 against the Giants, the Commanders listed him as an estimated DNP for Monday. While they didn’t formally practice, the fact that the team is saying he wouldn’t have gotten on the field today isn’t an encouraging sign for a player who missed all of last week’s practices as well. The good news is there are still more practices to go, meaning Burks could still be upgraded before Thursday night’s game. We’ll see if his status changes on Tuesday when the Commanders take the practice field for the first time on the short week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said he is “optimistic” that Treylon Burks (foot) will play in Week 10 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks sat out in Sunday’s loss to the Rams due to a foot injury that kept him off the practice field all week. Quinn’s optimism suggests he will at least be listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report and will get on the field in some capacity on Tuesday and Wednesday. Burks has been a solid downfield threat for the Commanders this year, catching 12 passes for 233 yards and two touchdowns. Even if he is active, fantasy managers can avoid him outside of deeper leagues, where he could be a viable desperation play as a WR4. In addition to Burks, Quinn also said he was hopeful CB Amik Robertson (ankle) would be ready to play on Thursday against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Commanders declared WR Treylon Burks, QB Athan Kaliakmanis, CB Fabian Moreau, CB Isaac Yiadom, and OG Tanoa Togiai inactive for Week 9 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: The Commanders find themselves incredibly thin at receiver with Burks (foot), Terry McLaurin (knee), and Dyami Brown (calf) all sidelined for this one. Stefon Diggs, along with rookie Antonio Williams could both be in line for busy days against a Rams secondary that will be without CB Trent McDuffie.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Commanders ruled out Treylon Burks (foot) for Week 9 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: The Commanders’ wide receiver corps continues to lose players. Burks and Dyami Brown (calf) will both be sidelined this weekend, leaving Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams and Chig Okonkwo to operate as the top pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: The Commanders’ thin wide receiver corps could get thinner. Burks, the team’s top downfield receiver, is on the wrong side of questionable for this week’s game against the Rams. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks was limited-DNP-limited due to the foot injury last week, but played through it for five targets in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles. He starts out this week as a DNP as the Commanders manage his injury. Given he already played a game with the injury, Burks is still likely to play in Week 9, though he will need to get a practice in later this week to feel better about his chances of playing against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.headline: Ben Sinnott caught all four targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.analysis: Sinnott entered the game with just one reception this season while playing as the primary blocking tight end alongside Chig Okonkwo. Okonkwo departed in the second quarter with a back injury and returned to start the second half, with the time off the field paving the way for Sinnott to triple his year-to-date reception total and score his first touchdown of the season. He would add one reception in the second half to push his total to four. The touchdown reception also came with a bit of intrigue as the pass appeared to be targeting Stefon Diggs in the end zone. Sinnott was on a crossing route at the goal line and happened to cross paths at the perfect time. He will not be fantasy viable for as long as Okonkwo remains healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.headline: Commanders TE Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.analysis: Okonkwo is on the wrong side of questionable at this point. He sat out in Week 2 and has not yet resumed practicing. Backup TE Ben Sinnott earned just one target last week. He does not need to be rostered.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.headline: Chig Okonwko (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.analysis: Okonkwo left Week 1 in the third quarter with the hamstring issue and did not return. A DNP today puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 2. John Bates and Ben Sinnott each ran 10 routes on Sunday. They would likely split Okonkwo’s role if he can’t suit up, meaning their isn’t much fantasy value to be had here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.headline: Commanders HC Dan Quinn did not have an update on Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.analysis: Okonkwo’s name will be one to look for on Wednesday when the Commanders release their first injury report. The 27-year-old tight end exited in the third quarter of Sunday’s game against the Eagles and did not return to the field. If he’s unable to play in Week 2 against the Cowboys, the Commanders would be looking at using John Bates and unproven third-year tight end Ben Sinnott as their top two options. Neither should be trusted for fantasy purposes if Okonkwo is out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.headline: ESPN’s John Keim reports “the belief in Washington is that the tight ends fit better in David Blough’s offense than they did under Kliff Kingsbury.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.analysis: Keim went as far as to say that a league source was confused when the Commanders drafted Sinnott at No. 53 overall a year ago because he didn’t think the tight end was a fit for Kingsbury’s system. That source was spot on. Sinnott managed just 16 catches for 142 yards and two touchdowns through two seasons. Kingbury has since been fired and replaced by Blough, who previously held the title of assistant quarterbacks coach. Keim called out a deep shot and an intermediate throw over the middle to Sinnott as plays that are indicative of how Blough will use his tight ends in the regular season. Though free agent addition Chig Okonkwo is penciled in as the starter, Sinnott should get more run in his third season. Dynasty managers can leave the light on for him, even if he isn’t a consideration in redraft leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.headline: The Athletic’s Nicki Jhabvala reports Chig Okonkwo has impressed coaches in offseason practices with his speed and versatility.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.analysis: Okonkwo, who in March signed a three-year deal worth up to $30 million, has been an offensive highlight for Washington under first-year OC David Blough. “He has rare speed and versatility, and his knack for collecting yards after the catch only adds to his appeal,” Jhabvala said, adding that the Commanders could “use a heavy dose of multiple tight end sets” under Blough this season. While last year in Tennessee was a down season for Okonkwo — he ranked 30th among tight ends in yards per route run — he has proven to be efficient in the past. Over four seasons with the Titans he was targeted on 19 percent of his pass routes. Okonkwo could be a 12-team fantasy option in 2026 if Jayden Daniels stays healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.headline: Ben Sinnott caught both of his targets for three yards in the Commanders’ Week 18 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.analysis: Sinnott spent his second year seldom-used, sitting behind veteran Zach Ertz for much of the season. He started seeing double-digit passing-down snaps from Week 15 onwards, after Ertz tore his ACL. Sinnott only caught 11 total passes for 114 yards and a touchdown. The 23-year-old will enter his third season in 2026 and may finally be in line for the starting tight end role with Ertz unlikely to return. Sinnott is a former second-round pick who deserves TE2 consideration in Dynasty leagues due to his high draft capital if the Commanders decide to not touch the tight end room this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.headline: Commanders placed TE Zach Ertz on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.analysis: Ertz’s 2025 season is over after a Week 14 cheap shot resulted in a torn ACL for the 35-year-old veteran. He ends the season with 50 receptions for 504 yards and four touchdowns. Ertz was tenth among tight ends in catches and 12th in yardage before the injury. John Bates will likely operate as Washington’s TE1 for now, though Ben Sinnott could mix in as the Commanders play out the rest of their lost season. Neither Bates nor Sinnott should be played in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.headline: Commanders declared TE Ben Sinnott, WR Treylon Burks, QB Jayden Daniels, OT George Fant, LB Ale Kaho, WR Terry McLaurin, and OT Trent Scott inactive for Week 11 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.analysis: The Commanders ruled out the biggest names on this list early in the week, so there aren’t many surprises here. Sinnott, the 2024 second-round pick, has just three catches for 33 yards and one touchdown this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said TE Ben Sinnott has been among the young players who had stood out in offseason practices.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-sinnot.analysis: Sinnott heads into his sophomore season after a rookie campaign that saw him play well behind veteran Zach Ertz, who re-signed with Washington in March. Sinnott, a second round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, caught all five of his targets for 28 yards and a touchdown in 2024; his touchdown came on a fake punt. It would appear Sinnott’s only viable path to real playing time in the Commanders offense would be Ertz missing time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught both targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Williams cashed in on his first target of the game for a 31-yard score in the third quarter, adding one additional grab for 11 yards in the final frame. The electric rookie continues to play starters snaps and challenge for the team lead in route rate but had yet to get completely on the same page with quarterback Jayden Daniels, the latter of whom leaned heavily on Stefon Diggs and tight end Chig Okonkwo in this one. The talent is undeniable for Williams, but fantasy managers would love to see a bump in targets before feeling comfortable entering him into starting lineups. Williams’ next chance to return a usable fantasy outing comes in Week 11 against the inside-funnel Bengals, where he should avoid the primary coverage of lockdown corner DJ Turner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught 3-of-6 targets for 25 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Fantasy managers hoping for a breakout performance from Williams, with Terry McLaurin (knee), Treylon Burks (foot), and Dyami Brown (calf) all sidelined, will be left wanting more. Instead, veteran journeyman Van Jefferson stepped up, catching five passes for 58 yards and a touchdown on a team-high seven targets, while Williams was largely an afterthought. Of the six targets Williams saw on Sunday, three came in the fourth quarter with the Commanders trailing 20-13. The rookie has caught 8-of-13 targets for 79 scoreless yards over the last two weeks and will be hard to trust as anything more than a WR3/WR4 in Week 10 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught 5-of-7 targets for 54 yards in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Williams mostly operated in a short area role but added a 30-yard grab up the seam in the fourth quarter to pad his counting stats for fantasy managers hoping on a second-half rookie breakout. While the fantasy returns have yet to pop, managers can continue to hold the electric rookie in the hopes his role grows in the coming weeks. That said, he is likely best left on fantasy benches until his route structure improves.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Burks downgraded from a limited showing Wednesday to a “DNP” Thursday, indicating he might be headed toward an absence when the Commanders take on the Eagles on Sunday Night Football. Considering the team is already without Terry McLaurin, who was lost for the season in Week 6, this would appear to be setting up for the best chance for rookie Antonio Williams to finally break out in Washington. Fantasy managers will want to confirm the status of Burks on the team’s final injury report Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said he doesn’t anticipate Stefon Diggs taking on a larger role with Terry McLaurin lost for the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Quinn did mention usage from “elsewhere” and the name “Antonio Williams” came up. Williams won’t be a buzzy waiver wire claim this week but could find himself in a reasonable WR3/WR4 sort of situation as the year unfolds.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Terry McLaurin (knee) tore his patellar tendon and will miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: It’s another rough blow for Washington’s No. 1 wideout, who will now have missed most of the last two seasons with injuries with the book closed on a 15-catch, 230-yard 2026 season in just five games. Entering his age-32 season in 2027, McLaurin will be a release or restructure candidate with a $34 million cap hit. The Commanders could save $16 million by releasing him without getting into post-June 1 antics. In the short term fantasy calculus, Stefon Diggs will slide in as Washington’s No. 1 receiver and Chig Okonkwo will also get a boost. Antonio Williams figures to see more snaps going forward as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught 3-of-4 targets for 50 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: While the yardage total looks solid on paper, the fact that Williams had only four targets in a game in which veteran wide receiver Terry McLaurin departed in the first quarter and quarterback Jayden Daniels attempted 40 passes is concerning. Williams continues to flash big play upside through a multitude of injuries to teammates but has yet to fully take advantage of the increase in opportunity, something fantasy managers will hope corrects when the Commanders come out of their bye to face the Eagles in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Terry McLaurin (hamstring) will “most likely” be a game-time decision for Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Keep it locked to Rotoworld, folks. Hopefully, we get word on McLaurin’s status on Saturday, but it appears as though we may have to wait until Sunday morning. Fowler adds that rookie WR Antonio Williams “could be a factor in the passing game regardless of whether McLaurin plays.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) will not play in Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Diggs did not practice this week and was ruled out by the team shortly after Friday’s practice concluded. His absence will give rookie Antonio Williams, who ran 30 routes last week, a chance to take on a bigger role. Williams tied for the team lead with eight targets in Week 4’s game against the Colts and could be treated as a desperation WR4/FLEX play. Fantasy managers considering Williams for their lineups may want to check the weather, as rain and wind are currently forecasted for the area, which could create a suboptimal environment for Washington’s passing game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Diggs didn’t appear to get hurt during the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts, but it looks like he felt something after the game. With Terry McLaurin also sidelined for today’s practice, Antonio Williams could be the Commanders’ No. 1 receiver in Week 5. He saw eight targets on Sunday, only one fewer than Diggs. The Commanders’ absurdly long injury report will be one to monitor as the week progresses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 6-of-10 targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs and the Washington pass offense went as Jayden Daniels went, with the dual threat quarterback mixing perfectly thrown passes with completely errant ones, two of which were directed toward Diggs. A third incompletion bounced off Diggs’ helmet as the veteran receiver should have drawn a defensive pass interference penalty, with the ball eventually ruled an incompletion upon further review after Treylon Burks appeared to come down with what would have been one of the wilder receptions of the season. Daniels’ best pass of the game came on the game-winning touchdown to Diggs in the flat on a crosser, threaded between two defenders. Diggs made a third miss as he took it into the end zone from 32 yards out to send the team to a 3-5-1 record, now two games behind the Giants with the first tie-breaker in hand. He will remain a volatile WR3 on capped routes against the Bengals in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 3-of-5 targets for 51 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: With the Commanders down three receivers, Diggs appeared prime for a decent day against a Rams secondary that was down two corners. Instead, the 32-year-old receiver was outshone by journeyman Van Jefferson for most of the day until the final drive of the game. With the Commanders looking to mount a game-tying drive, Diggs broke free into the secondary to make a 42-yard reception, which accounted for nearly all of his receiving production. In two games without Terry McLaurin, Diggs has averaged just 5.5 targets per game and totaled 89 yards and a touchdown. He’s far from the target hog he was in his prime, and shouldn’t be treated as anything more than a WR3/WR4 on Thursday night against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 3-of-6 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Offensive coordinator David Blough has made good on his promise not to increase the route participation or snap rate of the veteran receiver in the absence of Terry McLaurin, effectively keeping Diggs relegated to a situational role primarily from the slot. That has left Treylon Burks and rookie Antonio Williams to lead the team in routes the previous two weeks while limiting the true ceiling of Diggs in the process. Consider Diggs a touchdown-dependent FLEX option in a difficult matchup against the Rams in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring) is not on Washington’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: He should be a mid-range WR3 with Terry McLaurin out of the picture in Washington. Diggs practiced in full each of the last two sessions of the week after a Wednesday DNP.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring) practiced in full Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs shook of the absence Wednesday with a full showing Thursday, indicating he is tracking well to suit up when the Commanders face off against the Eagles on Sunday Night Football. The tam previously indicated that Diggs’ modest role would not grow in the absence of Terry McLaurin, potentially paving the way for rookie Antonio Williams to see an increase in role and opportunity in the second half of the season. Fantasy managers will want to confirm Diggs’ status on the final injury report Friday, but it appears as if he will be available in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring/rest) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn already said Diggs won’t practice Wednesday, so this is not a surprise. Quinn also confirmed the veteran will return to practice Thursday and the additional rest designation should stave off concerns of Diggs dealing with a long-term injury. He should be in the WR3/FLEX mix for Week 8 against the Eagles. Also not practicing for the Commanders was TE John Bates (shoulder).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Stefon Diggs will practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs won’t practice Wednesday with an undisclosed injury. He should be fine for Washington’s Week 8 matchup against the Eagles, however. Diggs could see a slightly bigger role in the Commanders offense with Terry McLaurin (knee) done for the year. Diggs drafters should keep an eye on the veteran’s practice status in the coming days. Diggs has been targeted on a team-high 28 percent of his pass routes in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said he doesn’t anticipate Stefon Diggs taking on a larger role with Terry McLaurin lost for the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Quinn did mention usage from “elsewhere” and the name “Antonio Williams” came up. Williams won’t be a buzzy waiver wire claim this week but could find himself in a reasonable WR3/WR4 sort of situation as the year unfolds.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Terry McLaurin (knee) tore his patellar tendon and will miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: It’s another rough blow for Washington’s No. 1 wideout, who will now have missed most of the last two seasons with injuries with the book closed on a 15-catch, 230-yard 2026 season in just five games. Entering his age-32 season in 2027, McLaurin will be a release or restructure candidate with a $34 million cap hit. The Commanders could save $16 million by releasing him without getting into post-June 1 antics. In the short term fantasy calculus, Stefon Diggs will slide in as Washington’s No. 1 receiver and Chig Okonkwo will also get a boost. Antonio Williams figures to see more snaps going forward as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 6-of-7 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: While the end line looks good in the box score, the fact that Diggs continued to operate in a situational role following the departure of Terry McLaurin in the first quarter was somewhat concerning for the veteran receiver’s upside potential in McLaurin’s absence, although the fact that he came into the game listed as questionable with a hamstring injury could have influenced his snap rate. Either way, Diggs continues to produce when on the field, returning significant value for fantasy managers that invested a middle-round pick for his services this summer. Diggs will be an upside WR3 when the Commanders take on the division rival Eagles in Week 8 following their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Austin Ekeler rushed nine times for 26 yards in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants, adding 26 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: The veteran in-season addition’s 13 opportunities matched that of starter Rachaad White, the latter of whom played the team’s first two drives before splitting the workload the rest of the way. Ekeler also split red zone work, although it was White that nearly missed a touchdown on a seven-yard run that was tackled at the one in the second quarter. Either way, the near-even split between the two caps the fantasy upside of both backs in the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt, with neither on the fantasy radar ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Commanders ruled out RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) for Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: No surprise here. Croskey-Merritt has been dealing with a groin injury since the start of the season. This week he couldn’t practice and has since been officially ruled out for the Commanders’ Monday Night Football matchup against the 49ers. Croskey-Merritt will get a two-week break with Washington on bye in Week 7. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler figure to handle the majority of the backfield touches in his absence with White being the preferred fantasy option between the two.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: Ekeler continues to practice in a limited capacity while wearing a red non-contact jersey. He has a chance to play on Monday night, but he is clearly hurting. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) remains sidelined and Rachaad White (shoulder) has been downgraded to limited. It’s an ailing backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: Ekeler and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) are both ailing, though the latter player sat out entirely. Rachaad White (shoulder) and Jeremy McNichols (quad) are both practicing in full. Croskey-Merritt is the only fantasy-relevant Commanders running back at this time, assuming he is good to go on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Austin Ekeler rushed four times for 29 yards in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts, adding one catch for 11 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: Ekeler made his 2026 debut in London and immediately operated as the Commanders’ backup with Rachaad White out. The team did, however, give four running backs multiple touches in this game. Ekeler’s role could grow as he gets more reps under his belt this year, but he could just as easily be made inactive once White is healthy. He’s only worth stashing in the deepest of leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) will not play in Washington’s Week 4 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: He didn’t practice at any point this week after suffering a shoulder injury in Week 3. He has to be considered questionable for Week 5 at this point. ‘Bill’ Croskey-Merritt figures to shoulder the majority of the workload for the Commanders this week and is a reasonable FLEX play against the Colts. Freshly-signed Austin Ekeler figures to handle third-down work.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: With two DNPs to start the week, White looks unlikely to suit up for Week 4 against the Colts. Austin Ekeler traveled with the team after signing with the team earlier this week, so he could ultimately take on White’s role. Backup running back Kayton Allen could also see more work, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt remains the clear lead back in Washington for now. He is on the RB2/3 border for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Rachaad White is receiving treatment for his shoulder injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: It sounds like White will be a question mark headed into Washington’s Week 4 game against the Colts in London. Quinn added that it’s too early to tell whether Austin Ekeler, who signed with the Commanders this week, will be active for Week 4. Jacory Croskey-Merritt could see a significant bump in carries and pass routes — and maybe targets — if White is sidelined this week. JCM, who has 58 percent of the team’s carries through three games, would be a nice flex option in that case.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Commanders re-signed RB Austin Ekeler.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: Ekeler is fully recovered from a torn Achilles that ended his 2025 season after just two games. The 31-year-old running back returns to a familiar place in Washington and will sign to the 53-man roster, making him immediately eligible to play in Week 4. We expect him to have a bit of a ramp-up period before being active on game days, but Ekeler could end up having a meaningful role in a backfield that has struggled to get going through the first three weeks. Ekeler may be worth a stash in deeper leagues, but we’ll have to see what kind of role he has before we can consider putting him in lineups. Ekeler met last week with the Panthers about possibly joining their practice squad but a deal was never reached.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: ESPN’s Mike Kaye reports Austin Ekeler is not expected to sign with the Panthers today.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: Ekeler worked out for the Panthers today. Kaye noted that the workout went well, so it’s possible Ekeler lands with the team in the future. With Jonathon Brooks (groin) on injured reserve, the Panthers need to make an addition or two at running back, even just for some extra depth. Regardless of who they sign, Chuba Hubbard is set for a workhorse role for the foreseeable future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed 11 times for 47 yards in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants, adding five yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White started in name only, playing the first two drives before splitting backfield duties with fellow veteran Austin Ekeler for the remainder of the game. The two backs ended with the same number of opportunities while also splitting red zone work, with White narrowly missing a touchdown in the second quarter on his second longest run of the evening, a seven-yard scamper up the gut that was stopped at the one. His lone explosive run went for 18 yards, with those two carries accounting for more than 50 percent of his yardage total on the ground. White has fallen into a strict timeshare in the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt and brings little fantasy upside ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 28 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams, adding two receptions for 41 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White’s 28 rushing yards led all Commanders running backs, but his biggest play of the game came through the air. In the second quarter, White turned a short screen pass upfield for a 45-yard gain, positioning the Commanders for a touchdown, which came on the following play when Van Jefferson found the end zone for a seven-yard score. White’s only other catch went for a four-yard loss, but the 41 receiving yards still set a new season-high for him. The 27-year-old free agent signee has three touchdowns this season and hasn’t totaled more than 80 yards from scrimmage in any game this season. He will be a fringe RB2/RB3 against the Giants, with Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) still sidelined for a few more weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed 11 times for 55 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles, adding five yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White averaged just over two yards per carry on his first eight attempts before breaking loose for a 33-yard gain entering the final two minutes of the fourth quarter. He would find the end zone two plays later to salvage an otherwise underwhelming fantasy outing while operating in a three-way timeshare with Austin Ekeler and Jeremy McNichols. Although White’s fantasy value is clearly higher in the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt, his performance in Week 8 goes down as his first fantasy-viable start through the first eight weeks of the 2026 season. Fantasy managers are likely better off exploring alternatives ahead of a poor matchup against the Rams in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 27 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers, adding 30 yards and a touchdown on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: The Commanders immediately found themselves in a negative game environment, managing just 17 offensive plays and 90 yards of total offense in the first half. While White found the end zone from nine yards out in the fourth quarter on an in-breaking route, the backfield split amongst White, Jeremy McNichols, and Austin Ekeler was troubling for fantasy managers looking to the former as a potential option with lead back Jacory Croskey-Merritt on injured reserve. White and the Commanders head to their bye week at a 1-4-1 record and some serious questions to answer, the least of which is the current state of their backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Commanders ruled out RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) for Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: No surprise here. Croskey-Merritt has been dealing with a groin injury since the start of the season. This week he couldn’t practice and has since been officially ruled out for the Commanders’ Monday Night Football matchup against the 49ers. Croskey-Merritt will get a two-week break with Washington on bye in Week 7. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler figure to handle the majority of the backfield touches in his absence with White being the preferred fantasy option between the two.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: Croskey-Merritt has played through multiple injuries this year. We still think he has a chance to face the 49ers in Week 6’s Monday Night Football game. Rachaad White (shoulder) sported a red non-contact jersey for the first time this week, and was downgraded to limited today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: Ekeler and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) are both ailing, though the latter player sat out entirely. Rachaad White (shoulder) and Jeremy McNichols (quad) are both practicing in full. Croskey-Merritt is the only fantasy-relevant Commanders running back at this time, assuming he is good to go on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 18 yards in the Commanders’ Week 5 tie against the Giants, adding one reception for two additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White continued to serve as the RB2 behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt and led the backfield with 11 snaps on third down. While his role remained largely the same, even with Austin Ekeler active, White offered nothing of fantasy value in this one. He saw only one target on the afternoon, and could continue to have his fantasy upside limited as long as Jayden Daniels is scrambling away from pressure rather than dumping it off to his checkdown options. Fantasy managers should avoid White in Week 6 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) will play in Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: In addition to White, the Commanders will also get RG Sam Cosmi back after missing the last two games with a concussion. White will likely return to his role as the team’s third-down/pass-catching back, but could be at risk of having Austin Ekeler eat into some of his workload. Fantasy managers hoping for White to return to the 10.3 touches/gm he was averaging before his injury may want to temper expectations and leave him on the bench while we wait to see how Ekeler is factored into the game plan.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: He looks to be on track to return to the backfield in Week 5. What percentage of carries that leaves him in a post-Ekeler world appears to be open to interpretation. We would not recommend starting him in any reasonably-sized league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 23-of-33 passes for 249 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Commanders’ 24-21, Week 10 win over the Giants, adding 28 yards on 10 carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: A late second quarter touchdown drive that was sparked by a long reception by veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs was capped off by tight end Ben Sinnott’s first touchdown of the season to send the Commanders into the half with a three-point lead. The two sides would trade touchdowns in the third quarter before the wheels appeared to fall off for Washington, with their first three possessions of the final frame going turnover on downs, interception, and interception, allowing the Giants to nurse a four-point lead inside the two-minute warning. Daniels drove the field in 49 seconds on just three plays, connecting with Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown with under a minute remaining. The Commanders would escape on the backs of a Rasul Douglas interception to send the team to a 3-5-1 record, now two games back of the Giants and with the first tie-breaker in hand following the previous tie. Daniels will look to keep the momentum going in a Week 11 meeting with the surging Bengals, where he will be an upside QB1 in another must-win game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 24-of-35 passes for 273 yards and one touchdown in the Commanders’ 20-13, Week 9 loss to the Rams, adding four runs for 16 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels played mostly mistake-free football in this one, but a lost fumble on a strip-sack by Myles Garrett near the end of the first half proved costly as the Commanders had a chance to add to their 10-3 lead before halftime. His lone touchdown pass of the day came on a seven-yard pass to Van Jefferson, who surprisingly ended up leading the Commanders with 58 receiving yards on the day, but Daniels and the offense struggled to generate much offense in the second half against a defensive front that featured both Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett together for the first time. Daniels saw 115 of his passing yards come on his final two drives of the game as he attempted to mount a comeback, but some off-target throws and two sacks on the game’s final drive all but buried any hopes of a comeback. Daniels’ disappointing showing on the ground marks the third straight week in which he has rushed for 23 or fewer yards, and he has managed only 10 rush attempts over that stretch. Now sitting at 2-5-1 on the season, Daniels and the Commanders will look to turn things around on a short week as they prepare to face the Giants on Thursday Night Football. He profiles more as a low-end QB1 until he begins to add more value in the rushing game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 16-of-29 passes for 217 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ 27-10, Week 8 win over the Eagles, adding 23 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels started the game going 4-of-10 passing in the first quarter, which included an interception that was called back due to penalty, two false start penalties in the red zone, and a missed field goal, causing the Commanders to quickly fall into a 10-point deficit. They would clean things up from there as they rattled off 27 unanswered points to improve to 2-4-1 as they chase the division-leading Giants. A 53-yard completion to Treylon Burks and 30-yard completions to Antonio Williams and Stefon Diggs gave the offense explosive plays in key situations during the final three frames to boost Daniels’ counting stats despite poor efficiency. The win was the first victory in a Daniels start since 5 October of the 2025 season as the Commanders saved their season, at least for the moment. They get a difficult matchup against the Rams in Week 9, where Daniels will remain a middling QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes it could make long-term sense for the Commanders to acquire Brian Thomas, Jr.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Shipley mentions the Commanders and Rams as wideout-desperate teams who might be interested in trading for Thomas before the NFL’s trade deadline. The Jaguars have apparently soured on the one-time burgeoning star in recent weeks; against the Texans in Week 6, Thomas ran a pass route on just 28 percent of the Jags’ drop backs and saw two targets. The Commanders, meanwhile, lost Terry McLaurin to a potentially long-term knee injury on Monday night. Thomas, per Shipley, “is not a trade that would make a ton of sense for a Commanders team that might be losing a ton of games and needs their picks to rebuild ... but it would make sense for a general manager who needs to keep his job to give his quarterback a familiar and talented target. Daniels was Thomas’ quarterback during their final seasons at LSU, and the connection between the two could go a long-way toward solving some of Washington’s long-term issues at the wide receiver position.” BTJ’s fantasy prospects would get a big boost if he were to land in Washington in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 29-of-40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns in the Commanders’ 23-17, Week 6 loss to the 49ers, adding 10 yards on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: The Commanders gained just 90 yards of total offense and ran just 17 offensive plays in the first half, taking a 20-3 deficit into the break. Two quick touchdown drives to end the third quarter and begin the fourth quarter had the team in position to pull off an improbable comeback but two critical errors from Daniels sank that effort. The first error occurred on fourth down in the red zone with just over two minutes to play, when the team was late to break the huddle and ended up taking their first timeout down by six. They would fail to convert but would get the ball back with no timeouts and 52 seconds left. Daniels then committed an intentional grounding penalty from the San Francisco 28 with 16 seconds left, which incurred a loss of down and a 10-second runoff on the clock. The game would end on the following play. That now makes consecutive contests with late-game clock mismanagement that cost the Commanders potential wins. Rumors continue to swirl about a potential coaching change as the Commanders limp into their bye at a 1-4-1 record.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 17-of-25 passes for 199 yards in the Commanders’ 27-27, Week 5 tie with the Giants, adding nine carries for 103 additional yards and two touchdowns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels turned in one of the best games of his career on the ground on Sunday against the Giants. Daniels broke off an uncontested 38-yard touchdown run in the third quarter to put the Commanders up 19-6, and later broke free for a 26-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter to again extend the Commanders’ lead. Both runs came on scrambles where the Giants seemingly forgot Daniels was a threat to run at any moment, and Daniels made the most of his opportunities.
