With the Commanders in range for a game-winning field goal late in overtime, Daniels inexplicably took a sack with no timeouts left on what appeared to be an attempt to center the ball in time for the game-winning try. We’ll likely get an explanation from both Daniels and head coach Dan Quinn on that final play, but Washington snatched defeat from the jaws of victory to move to 1-3-1 on the season. Despite the late-game gaffe, Daniels looked on-point for most of the afternoon, but struggled at times against the blitz, as the Giants brought pressure in several key spots to force Daniels to get the ball out quick or throw it away. Daniels looked like the elite dual threat fantasy managers want to see, and will be firmly in the QB1 ranks in next week’s game against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports “there are doctors around the NFL who believe it’s a matter of when, not if, Jayden Daniels hurts his left elbow again.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Schefter immediately added the caveat that the “overwhelming opinion” among doctors was that playing with a brace was a viable option. Daniels reportedly contemplated surgery after dislocating his elbow for the second time in less than a year. He opted against it and missed two games. Daniels is now set to return for Week 5 against the Giants. The Commanders could scale back his rushing for the time being, but OC David Blough already dismissed the idea that the playbook would be limited because of Daniels’ elbow injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Jayden Daniels (elbow) is “not 100 percent” healthy yet.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Rapoport, typically cheery on the injury front, said that there are still “a lot of questions, going forward, for Jayden Daniels.” The bottom line is that Daniels is still rehabbing the elbow in his non-throwing arm. He should be able to throw and run effectively, putting him squarely in the QB1 tier, but re-injury risk remains a factor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Jayden Daniels (elbow) will start in Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels appeared to be close to playing in Week 4 against the Colts before ultimately being ruled out. His being upgraded to a full participant in Thursday’s practice suggested he was a virtual lock to start in Week 5, barring any unexpected setbacks. Daniels will wear a brace on his left arm for the rest of the season in hopes of avoiding a three-peat of his dislocated elbow. Daniels will be without Stefon Diggs (hamstring) for Sunday’s game, and rainy/windy conditions are currently in the forecast. We’ll conservatively project him as a mid-to-low-end QB1 in what could be less-than-ideal conditions on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough said Jayden Daniels is a “full go” when asked if his elbow injury would create any limitations in the game plan.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels is practicing in full and is expected to return to the lineup this week. He has suffered the same elbow dislocation twice in the past year, but his game-changing running ability is a big part of what makes Daniels a potential superstar quarterback. Blough might be more tactile with how he calls quarterback runs, but they will still be in the playbook this week. Daniels will be a low-end QB1 once he is officially cleared to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (back) is questionable to return to Week 10 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo was accompanied by trainers to the locker room after failing to play on a three-and-out possession in the second quarter against the Giants. The team deemed him questionable to return before the subsequent possession. Okonkwo caught both targets for 17 yards prior to departing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (hip) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo is one of many fringe TE1/2 candidates on any given week. He does not need to be in fantasy football lineups, but he can act as a serviceable fill-in, though his upside is most touchdown-dependent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (hip) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: That ought to put him firmly in the mix to play on Thursday against the Giants. Okonkwo is coming off a 6/57 game on seven targets against the Rams and figures to again be a reasonable low-end TE1 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (hip) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: This is a new injury for Okonkwo, who caught a 16-yard pass on the final play of Sunday’s loss to the Rams as the Commanders were looking to tie the game. Okonkwo has gone for 57 or more yards in three of his last four games and would be on the streaming radar as a boom-or-bust TE2 on Thursday against the Giants if he can play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught 6-of-7 targets for 57 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo’s seven targets tied Van Jefferson for the team high in this one. Okonkwo hauled in a 15-yard reception on the Commanders’ opening drive, and on the final play of the game, he caught a 16-yard pass and then tossed it to Rachaad White in hopes of keeping the play alive after time had already expired. Okonkwo has gone for 50-plus yards in three of his last four games and is seeing enough work in the passing game to be on the streaming radar for Week 10’s game against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught 2-of-4 targets for 32 yards in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo flashed his athletic ability with a full-stretch reception in the second half but it was not enough to overshadow a first quarter fumble. The spry veteran has now been held to four receptions or fewer in four of five appearances in the low volume Washington pass offense, unable to return consistent fantasy value through the absence of Terry McLaurin. He is best left on fantasy benches in a Week 9 matchup against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Terry McLaurin (knee) tore his patellar tendon and will miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: It’s another rough blow for Washington’s No. 1 wideout, who will now have missed most of the last two seasons with injuries with the book closed on a 15-catch, 230-yard 2026 season in just five games. Entering his age-32 season in 2027, McLaurin will be a release or restructure candidate with a $34 million cap hit. The Commanders could save $16 million by releasing him without getting into post-June 1 antics. In the short term fantasy calculus, Stefon Diggs will slide in as Washington’s No. 1 receiver and Chig Okonkwo will also get a boost. Antonio Williams figures to see more snaps going forward as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: ESPN’s John Keim reports Terry McLaurin’s knee injury is considered “significant.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Washington head coach Dan Quinn said after the team’s Monday night loss to the 49ers that there was “fear” McLaurin could be lost for the long-term after going down with a non-contact injury and was carted to the locker room. McLaurin has functioned as the team’s lone downfield threat for much of the season, and could be replaced with Treylon Burks, who on Monday night caught four balls for 66 yards before sustaining a late-game injury. Antonio Williams and Dyami Brown could also see an increase in routes and targets if McLaurin is sidelined for a while. Look for Chig Okonkwo to see an uptick in targets too. Okonkwo had seven grabs for 69 yards against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught all seven targets for 69 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo was thrust into an increased role with the departure of lead wide receiver Terry McLaurin in the first quarter, operating as the primary option through the air for much of the game. Veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs continued to operate in a situational role, making Okonkwo a priority start when the Commanders come out of their Week 7 bye to face the Eagles in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said he is hopeful Diggs will get some practice reps in later this week. Diggs missed Week 5 with the hamstring issue, and a DNP today puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 6, even if Quinn remains optimistic. Terry McLaurin and Chig Okonkwo led the team in receiving last week. McLaurin should pull away from Okonkwo as he puts more time between himself and the hamstring injury that previously knocked him out for a week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.headline: Giants declared CB Paulson Adebo, OT J.C. Davis, OL Josh Sills, CB Nikko Reed, DT C.J. Okoye, TE Thomas Fidone and OLB Malik Harrison inactive for Week 10 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.analysis: The Giants are seemingly demoting Adebo, who entered the season and one of the team’s top-three cornerbacks. Colton Hood will take his place. Aside from that, Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and J.J. McCarthy (hip) are good to go tonight, in what is expected to be a rainy Thursday Night Football game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.headline: Giants EDGE Kayvon Thibodeaux (shoulder) won’t play in New York’s Week 12 game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.analysis: He did not practice all week and is in some danger of an IR placement on Saturday. New York also ruled out veteran CB Paulson Adebo (knee), which should help open up room in the secondary for Detroit’s receivers in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.headline: Giants CB Paulson Adebo (knee) is active for New York’s Week 11 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.analysis: Adebo has not played since Week 7, so the Giants will have their big offseason CB addition back in the fold to try to contain Jordan Love on the rare occasions when Matt LaFleur actually unleashes him. Bobby Okereke (shoulder) is also playing off a questionable tag. Inactive for the Giants are: OLB Kayvon Thibodeaux (shoulder), QB Jaxson Dart (concussion), WR Darius Slayton (hamstring), S Tyler Nubin (neck), DL Chauncey Golston (neck), DL Rakeem Nuñez-Roches (toe) and lone healthy scratch OT James Hudson III.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.headline: Giants ruled out OLB Kayvon Thibodeaux (shoulder) for Week 11 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.analysis: Thibodeaux was visibly in pain last weekend, so his absence is unsurprising. The Giants also ruled out his backup, OLB Chauncey Golston (neck), and listed starting DT Rakeem Nunez-Roches (toe) as doubtful. Two more starters, LB Bobby Okereke (shoulder) and CB Paulson Adebo (knee) are listed as questionable. Good news for the Packers’ offense, which has been heavily scrutinized in recent weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.headline: Giants CB Paulson Adebo (knee) won’t play in New York’s Week 9 game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.analysis: Neither will Cor’Dale Flott (concussion) — this is good news for Jauan Jennings, who figures to be the only 49ers wideout playable in most fantasy leagues while other targets flow to Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle. Disappointment Deonte Banks played all 59 snaps last week and the Giants also heavily employed Korie Black and Andru Phillips.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.headline: Giants EDGE Brian Burns (hip) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.analysis: Defensive backs Paulson Adebo and Jevon Holland were also held out of practice. The good news is that Burns, who has nine sacks this season, told reporters he fully expects to play on Sunday. Barring a surprise, the NFL’s sack-leader will be ready to face the Eagles by kickoff.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.headline: Giants restructured Paulson Adebo’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.analysis: The team also reworked Jevon Holland’s contract, creating over $4.8 million in cap space, according to ESPN’s Field Yates. Simple restructures are common practice in the NFL and teams typically have the option to do so whenever they want to. The moves could be intended to clear up space for a trade, but NFL trades are rarer than fans want to admit. It’s more likely that they were done to create some freedom for minor free agent moves as the season progresses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.headline: Giants agreed to terms with CB Paulson Adebo, formerly of the Saints, on a three-year, $54 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.analysis: The former Saints corner heads to New York to be their lead defensive back. Adebo is currently recovering from a broken femur, but the Giants seemingly did their due diligence on the injury and are confident in a full recovery. Adebo totaled 10 pass breakups and three interceptions despite playing in just seven games last year. He will be a key addition for a Giants defense that ranked 21st in points allowed last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.headline: Saints CB Paulson Adebo (leg) is making progress in his recovery after suffering a broken femur.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.analysis: The soon-to-be free agent cornerback posted a video selfie that showed the 25-year-old dunking a basketball on Sunday, The Saints’ cornerback corps was in dire straits at the end of last season, with Adebo sidelined and former No. 1 cornerback Marshon Lattimore having been traded to the Commanders. Adebo’s recovery may force him to take a “prove it” deal this offseason, but there’s enough talent for him to earn a long-term deal if he can stay healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.headline: Saints CB Paulson Adebo has been diagnosed with a broken right leg.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/paulson-ad.analysis: What was originally deemed a knee injury was actually a broken femur. It should be a season-ender for the 25-year-old, who is undergoing surgery Thursday evening. It’s a brutal blow for a 2021 third-rounder in the final year of his rookie deal. It leaves the Saints short-handed at corner, and clouds Adebo’s looming free agency. Perhaps he could end up back in New Orleans on something of a “prove it” deal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Commanders declared QB Athan Kaliakmanis, CB Isaac Yiadom, DT Ricky Barber, G Tanoa Togiai, C Lucas Patrick and TE Colson Yankoff inactive for Week 10 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: Among the Commanders’ players who are currently healthy enough to practice, most of them will play. Treylon Burks (foot) could end up being a decoy, but Chig Okonkwo (hip) should be good to go. Only Yiadom and a few others are unable to go on Thursday night, though tonight’s kickoff could be delayed by weather.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Commanders waived DT Ricky Barber.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: The second-year player is headed to waivers. The Commanders correspondingly promoted CB Isaac Yiadom to the active roster. Barber could be re-signed to the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Saints CB Isaac Yiadom (hamstring) is active for Week 8 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: Yiadom has been sidelined since straining his hamstring in Week 4. Although the Buccaneers are without WRs Mike Evans (collarbone/concussion) and Chris Godwin (fibula), their deep receiving corps, led by rookies WR Emeka Egbuka and WR Tez Johnson, still poses problems for defenses. Yiadom’s return is helpful. The Saints declared OG Xavier Truss, TE Zaire Mitchell-Paden, DB Ugo Amadi, CB Rejzohn Wright, DL Jonah Williams and DT Khristian Boyd inactive for Week 8 against the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Saints signed CB Isaac Yiadom, formerly of the 49ers, to a three-year, $9 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: Yiadom returns to the Saints, who he played for in 2022 and 2023. The 29-year-old corner joined the 49ers on a one-year deal last offseason and appeared in all 17 games while making five starts. In those games, Yiadom totaled 46 tackles and one interception while also breaking up six passes and earning a PFF coverage grade of 55.3. One of Yiadom’s best seasons as a pro came in 2023 while with the Saints, where he broke up a career-high 13 passes. His signing doesn’t fully address the secondary problems the Saints had last season, but he’s a good depth signing who should be able to provide them plenty of snaps at a good value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: 49ers agreed to terms with CB Isaac Yiadom, formerly of the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: The 49ers will become Yiadom’s fifth team over the last five years, as the former third round pick has also spent time with the Texans, Packers, and Giants. Yiadom played on 517 defensive snaps last season, earning a PFF coverage grade of 80.4 while allowing 22 catches for 289 yards and three touchdowns on 44 targets. The veteran corner has started in 28 of the 87 games he’s appeared in for his career, and is likely more of a depth signing at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Texans declared TE Pharaoh Brown (shoulder) inactive for Week 4 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: Houston will only have O.J. Howard and Jordan Akins (an elevation) active at tight end with TE Brevin Jordan (ankle) also ruled out on Friday. WR Tyler Johnson is active for the first time this season. Also inactive for the Texans are OL Austin Deculus (ankle), CB Isaac Yiadom (thigh), LB Jake Hansen, DL Michael Dwumfour, and DL Demone Harris.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Texans TE Pharaoh Brown (shoulder) is active for Week 3 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: Brown going may cut into the viability of OJ Howard as a barebones TE streamer this week -- Brown bounced back from a Thursday DNP with a full practice on Friday. Both will have some freed up targets by the absence of Brevin Jordan (ankle), who was ruled out on Friday. Also inactive for the Texans are DL Kurt Hinish (foot), OL Austin Deculus (ankle), DB Isaac Yiadom (thigh), LB Jake Hansen, and WR Tyler Johnson. No practice squad elevation for Jeff Driskel means the Texans will actually use backup QB Kyle Allen for the first time all season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Texans signed CB Isaac Yiadom to an undisclosed contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: Yiadom spent last year as a Packers depth cornerback and didn’t impress. He’s yet to post a PFF Grade over 57 in any of his four seasons and allowed six touchdowns in 42 targets in 2020 per Sports Info Solutions charting. Nobody should ever be confident of where things stand with the Texans, but Yiadom is likely just fighting for a roster spot as a special teamer/depth player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Pro Football Network’s Aaron Wilson reports that the Texans are working out free agent CB Isaac Yiadom.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: It appears to be cornerback workout day for the Texans with Malcolm Butler also in town. Yiadom played fewer than 100 defensive snaps last year for the Packers. He’s got outside cornerback traits, but has not been able to convert them into good results to this point. He’s still only 26 years old.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Packers acquired CB Isaac Yiadom from the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: It is the second time in as many summers Yiadom has been traded, as he was acquired by the Giants from the Broncos on the eve of last season. He ended up making 10 starts for the G-Men, but was not effective. Last year’s trade price was a seventh-rounder, and this will certainly be something similar. If he makes the 53-man roster, Yiadom will ideally slot in as a special teamer with the experience on defense to step in during a pinch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff (chest) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: That should alleviate any concern that he’d miss Sunday morning’s Munich kickoff against the Patriots. Goff will be a low-end QB1 for that one assuming no major negative news hits on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff (chest) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: Goff had his worst game of the year in the Lions’ Week 9 win over the Dolphins. Perhaps this injury was bothering him. On the plus side, Goff is already practicing in a limited capacity, so we do not expect it to impact his availability for Week 10 against the Patriots. It is worth monitoring his practice participation level this week, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 17-of-25 passes for 170 yards and an interception in the Lions’ 19-9, Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: The Lions undoubtedly played down to their opponents in this game, putting up six points in the first half before finding slightly more success after the break. Things got off to a rocky start with an easy interception for Dolphins defensive back Chris Johnson. Goff was hit as he threw the ball and it wobbled right into Johnson’s arms. The Lions had one drive go for more than 50 yards. Jahmyr Gibbs punched in the score at the end of the drive, taking home the only Lions touchdown of the day. Goff should have no issues turning things around against the Patriots next week. He will remain near the top of the QB1 ranks for Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 18-of-25 attempts for 176 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: Goff, like all quarterbacks against the Vikings, seemed lost from start to finish, unable to decipher to intricate Vikings blitz scheme. He was sacked four times and saw pressure on seemingly every drop back before the Lions abandoned the pass game for the run game in the second half. Sunday marked only the second game this season in which Goff did not have multiple touchdown throws, and the first time he has not eclipsed 200 passing yards. Goff should be able to get back on track next week against a bad Dolphins defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 22-of-32 passes for 303 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ 20-17, Week 7 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: In a game that felt like it should have featured far more points, Goff and the Lions narrowly walked away with the win. He led an explosive opening drive that included a 28-yard pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown and a 24-yard pass to Jameson Williams, and ended with a 16-yard touchdown pass to Williams to put the Lions up 7-0 early. Goff would again connect with Williams for a 10-yard touchdown pass in the third quarter, and narrowly missed linking up with him for a third touchdown when Williams was forced out of the end zone on a catch on fourth-and-five from the Packers’ six-yard line. Goff did lose a fumble in this one on a botched snap exchange with his center, but it was an overall strong outing for the Lions’ signal-caller. Goff has yet to throw an interception this season and has now thrown for over 300 yards in three of his six games this season. He’ll be a fringe QB1/QB2 next week at home against the 6-0 Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 19-of-30 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in the Lions’ 45-21, Week 5 win over the Cardinals, adding one rush for a one-yard touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: Sacks and a few errant throws under pressure derailed the Lions’ first three drives. Goff got things back on track after that, guiding the offense to seven straight scoring drives, including six touchdowns. He even punched in a one-yard rushing touchdown via a quarterback sneak, marking his first rushing score since 2023. Goff could have boosted his passing yards total with a likely explosive gain by targeting an open Jameson Williams on the first drive after halftime, but he instead checked down to Sam LaPorta in the flats for an eight-yard pickup. The Lions are on bye in Week 6, but Goff will be a locked-in QB1 against the Packers in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 32-of-52 passes for 412 yards and one touchdown in the Lions’ 32-26, Week 4 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: Goff has now thrown a touchdown pass in 27 straight contests, a streak that started in the team’s Thanksgiving day contest against the Bears in 2024. He could move into sixth on the all-time list for consecutive games with a touchdown pass should he throw for at least one touchdown in each game this season. He came within four minutes of breaking that streak against the Panthers, needing a late touchdown to tight end Sam LaPorta to keep it alive in a game the Panthers dictated with their defense throughout. Goff also maintained his clean sheet of no interceptions thrown to start the season but it wasn’t enough to overcome a defense that ceded 445 yards of total offense to a Panthers team without two of their top three wide receivers in Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette. The Lions fall to 2-2, now two games behind the division-leading Vikings through the first month of play. Goff remains a surefire QB1 ahead of a potential shootout against the Cardinals in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 25-of-32 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ 31-24, Week 3 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: Goff and the Lions got off to a slow start with just three points over their first three drives. Things started to click before halftime and Goff rode that momentum to 21 points after the break. Excluding a few kneel-downs to end the game, Detroit scored on five of their final six drives. The Lions have scored exactly 31 points in all three of their games this year. That may be a bit higher than their projection for Week 4 against the Panthers, but not by all that much. Goff will remain in the QB1 mix versus Carolina next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 26-of-38 passes for 327 yards and four touchdowns in the Lions’ 41-31, Week 2 loss to the Bills, adding seven yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: The Lions staked the Bills to a 21-point lead early in the second quarter, eventually taking a 27-10 deficit into the break. The closest they would get the rest of the game was a 10-point deficit, but the offense finally came alive in the final two frames. Goff tossed a pair of touchdowns to alpha wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and one each to Sam LaPorta and Jahmyr Gibbs, salvaging the poor team performance with an elite fantasy score for managers brave enough to start him on the road in the elements. The Lions fall to 1-1 ahead of a much more forgiving home matchup against the Jets in Week 3, where Goff will look to return another QB1 performance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 26-of-39 passes for 206 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ 31-30, Week 1 overtime win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: Goff struggled to get much going early on this game, putting up seven points in the first half. The Lions quickly dropped 14 in the third quarter but took their foot off the gas with the Saints struggling to do much of anything. That nearly came back to bite them as Tyler Shough led a frantic comeback while the Lions amassed three points in the final frame. An overtime touchdown to Amon-Ra St. Brown proved to be just enough to come home with the win, though it required a failed two-point conversion from the Saints. Despite the slow start, Goff should return to the QB1 ranks when he squares off with the Ravens next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Cade Mays (ankle) will not play in Detroit’s Week 10 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: He did not travel to Munich with the team and has not practiced since injuring his ankle in Week 8. Juice Scruggs will continue to fill in at center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Cade Mays (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: The Lions are at their best when the offensive line is in good health. Mays missed multiple games early in the year with a wrist injury. He is now sidelined by an ankle injury. Hopefully, he can resume practicing before long. Lions S Kerby Joseph (knee) and S Brian Branch (hip) were both limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions ruled out Cade Mays (ankle) for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Brutal. Mays returned from injured reserve in Week 7 due to a preseason wrist injury. He injured his ankle in Week 8. The Lions ruled out S Kerby Joseph (knee) and CB D.J. Reed (hip), yet S Brian Branch (concussion) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Cade Mays (ankle) is questionable to return in Week 8 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Mays went down with the injury in the second quarter. His absence will make it even tougher for the Detroit offense to navigate the Vikings’ complex blitzing schemes. Mays has dealt with injuries for much of the past month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Cade Mays (wrist) is active for Week 7 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Detroit will get back it’s highly-paid free agent acquisition from this past offseason after a preseason wrist injury. The Lions declared TE Jackson Meeks, S Bishop Fitzgerald, C Seth McLaughlin, DL Mekhi Wingo, and DE Ahmed Hassanein inactive against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions activated Brian Branch from the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: The team also activated center Cade Mays from the reserve/injured list. Week 7 will be the first game of the year for both players. Branch tore his Achilles in Week 14 last year and has been out ever since. Currently in last place in the NFC North, the Lions desperately needed this infusion of talent to get their season back on track.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Cade Mays (wrist) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 7 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Questionable but fully expected to play after three full practices, Mays should add some more teeth to the Lions’ run game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions C Cade Mays (wrist) is practicing in full ahead of Week 7’s game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Mays seems likely to be activated off injured reserve ahead of the game given Dan Campbell’s public statements on the matter, him giving a presser today, and the trend to full sessions following the team’s Week 6 bye. It should be an upgrade for Detroit’s offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions ruled out C Cade Mays (wrist) for Week 5 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Mays and S Brian Branch (Achilles) are not yet ready to return from their injuries. Starting CB Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring) has been ruled out as well, and DL Tyleik Williams (foot) is questionable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions activated C Cade Mays’ (wrist) 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: This is a big deal for fantasy purposes. The Lions signed Mays to a three-year, $25 million contract this offseason, shoring up their center position with a reliable prime-age starter. Mays injured his wrist early in August, so he has not yet taken the field on game day with his new team. The Lions’ permissive defense continues to put the offense into pass-heavy game scripts. Getting Mays back on the field will fortify Jared Goff’s protection. He was limited on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: D.J. Reed (hip) won’t play in Detroit’s Week 10 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Reed has not practiced since injuring his hip in Week 8. The Lions’ secondary remains a patchwork effort against Drake Maye and the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions ruled out Cade Mays (ankle) for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Brutal. Mays returned from injured reserve in Week 7 due to a preseason wrist injury. He injured his ankle in Week 8. The Lions ruled out S Kerby Joseph (knee) and CB D.J. Reed (hip), yet S Brian Branch (concussion) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions declared RT Blake Miller, LG Christian Mahogany, CB Keith Abney, EDGE Ahmed Hassanein, CB Ennis Rakestraw, LB Jimmy Rolder and DL Mekhi Wingo inactive for Week 2 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Losing Miller and Mahogany for this one is unfortunate, especially with C Cade Mays (wrist) on injured reserve. The Bills, however, lost DT Ed Oliver to a pre-game hip injury. This should be a high-scoring, fantasy-friendly game environment tonight. Lions CB D.J. Reed (foot) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: D.J. Reed (foot) is questionable for Week 2 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Reed was a mid-week addition to the injury report because of his foot issue. He was limited for the final two practices of the week. Reed is likely on the optimistic side of questionable, but we won’t know for sure until the Lions release their inactives 90 minutes before kickoff.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions CB D.J. Reed (foot) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: He was a surprise addition to the report on Tuesday. The Lions secondary, already starting a wave of low-level veteran free agents like Rock Ya-Sin, Avonte Maddox, and Chuck Clark, can ill-afford to lose Reed before taking on the Bills on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions CB D.J. Reed (hamstring) is active for Week 12 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Reed, a critical part of the Detroit secondary, will suit up for the first time since sustaining a serious hamstring injury in early October and landing on injured reserve. It’s not the best development for Jameis Winston and the Giants pass catchers. The Giants were massively run heavy in Week 11 against the Packers. Lions declared CB Terrion Arnold, RB Craig Reynolds, CB Nick Whiteside, DL Quinton Jefferson, and DL Mekhi Wingo inactive against New York.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (elbow) is not on Detroit’s final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Good thing, too, because the entire rest of the Lions defense found their way on to this report. Terrion Arnold (concussion), Kerby Joseph (knee) and Josh Paschal (back) were all ruled out. D.J. Reed (hamstring) and Amik Robertson (hamstring) are questionable. Both A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith should see slight matchup uggrades given the CB injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions S Brian Branch (foot) is scheduled to undergo an MRI after he was limited in practice for the second straight day on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: The Detroit Free Press’ Dave Birkett reports that Branch “worked out on the side during individual drills at practice Wednesday and had a noticeable limp as he left the locker room Thursday.” The Lions’ secondary could be extremely short-staffed against the Chiefs on Sunday night. Birkett notes that starting CBs, D.J. Reed and Terrion Arnold, are out indefinitely with hamstring and shoulder injuries. The Lions placed backup CB Khalil Dorsey on injured reserve this week and No. 3 safety Avonte Maddox “showed up on the injury report Thursday with a hamstring injury.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions HC Dan Campbell said CB D.J. Reed will be “out indefinitely” with a hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Fellow cornerback Terrion Arnold is also expected to miss significant time with a shoulder injury, leaving the team extremely shorthanded on the back end ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Chiefs. Safety Kerby Joseph has been tending to a knee injury as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions S Kerby Joseph (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: As expected, cornerback D.J. Reed was also listed as a DNP. He is a candidate for injured reserve after suffering a hamstring injury in Week 4. With multiple starters in their secondary injured, the Lions look like a relatively easy defensive matchup for Week 5. Unfortunately for the Bengals, their offense doesn’t look remotely capable of taking advantage of such a situation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Kerby Joseph (knee) won’t play in Detroit’s Week 10 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Joseph got in a full practice session with the Lions on Thursday, but will not travel to Munich with the club. It sounds like he’ll have a real chance to play in Week 11 when the Lions head back to the states.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Cade Mays (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: The Lions are at their best when the offensive line is in good health. Mays missed multiple games early in the year with a wrist injury. He is now sidelined by an ankle injury. Hopefully, he can resume practicing before long. Lions S Kerby Joseph (knee) and S Brian Branch (hip) were both limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions ruled out Cade Mays (ankle) for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Brutal. Mays returned from injured reserve in Week 7 due to a preseason wrist injury. He injured his ankle in Week 8. The Lions ruled out S Kerby Joseph (knee) and CB D.J. Reed (hip), yet S Brian Branch (concussion) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Kerby Joseph (knee) will not play in Detroit’s Week 8 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Dan Campbell said Joseph has been used only in individual and group practices so far and that he’s handled that well. Next week he’ll get in on real practice. Joseph probably stands a decent chance of being active for Week 9 assuming he acclimates well to that.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Kerby Joseph (knee) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Joseph dealt with a cartilage issue in his knee last year and has spent the entirety of 2026 working his way back from it. As of a month ago, Dan Campbell didn’t sound optimistic that Joseph would be able to play at any point this year. Joseph is currently on the PUP list. His return to practice means the team has opened his 21-day practice window. We expect them to use most of the window to ramp Joseph up to full speed, but it’s still a great sign for the playmaking safety.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions S Kerby Joseph (knee) is hopeful he’ll be available later this season, reports NFL Insider Tom Pelissero.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Lions HC Dan Campbell didn’t sound optimistic about the prospects of Joseph, who is dealing with a potentially career-threatening knee cartilage issue, helping the Lions this year. In two separate media appearances in the last week, Campbell said that there wasn’t anything he could say about Joseph that would make anyone “feel good.” Pelissero reported Saturday morning that Joseph, who missed all of training camp and hasn’t played since last year’s Week 6 loss to the Chiefs, is hopeful he’ll be available to help the Lions down the stretch. While that may be the case, whether Joseph is able to return to play this year remains an open question. Without Joseph and S Brian Branch (Achilles), the Lions are severely shorthanded in the backend heading into Week 3’s home matchup against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell said S Brian Branch (Achilles) “has a chance” to resume practicing sooner than S Kerby Joseph (knee), “but it won’t be this week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Campbell spoke in a dejected tone when asked about the Lions’ safety duo returning to practice, particularly when discussing Joseph’s outlook. Campbell said Joseph did not suffer a setback, but stopped short of fully explaining the situation. It sounds like Joseph’s recovery stalled. The training staff was focused on strengthening Joseph’s knee, “but there was a little time there where we weren’t able to do everything we needed to do.” The Lions will not ask Joseph to play until he gets his knee as strong as it can possibly be, “and he feels comfortable.” Branch could return to practice in the coming weeks, but at this point, Joseph’s career status seems like it might be up in the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions S Kerby Joseph will begin the season on the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Joseph is still nursing a knee injury that hampered him last season. He will remain on the PUP list to open the season, meaning he will miss a minimum of four games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions placed S Kerby Joseph on the active/PUP list with a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Just yesterday, Joseph implied via social media that he would avoid the physically unable to perform list. So much for that. Joseph dealt with a recurring knee issue for the entire 2025 season, which was first reported on at the end of July 2025, roughly three months after the Lions made him the NFL’s highest-paid safety. Given Joseph’s post, one imagines he has a chance to resume practicing relatively soon, but only time will tell. Branch suffered an Achilles tendon rupture in Week 14 last year. As of June 13th, Lions coach Dan Campbell said there was no timetable for his return. The Lions also placed TE Tyler Conklin on the physically unable to perform list.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.headline: Lions S Kerby Joseph (knee) implied that he’ll avoid the PUP list ahead of training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kerby-jose.analysis: Lions veterans won’t report to training camp until Monday, but Joseph implied in a tweet on Saturday morning that he’ll avoid the PUP list. In response to a question about going on the PUP list, the 25-year-old safety wrote, “How much y’all wanna bet I’m not on there.” It’s not much, but it’s the first positive signal for Joseph’s health in quite some time. After missing the last 11 games of the 2025 season with a knee injury, Joseph was held out of minicamp. In early June, Dan Campbell told reporters he didn’t know what to expect from Joseph this season. Joseph started all 17 games in 2024, when he had a league-leading nine interceptions and was named a first-team All-Pro. The former third-round pick in the 2022 NFL Draft signed a massive four-year, $86 million extension prior to last season. Joseph’s 20 interceptions are the second-most all-time for a safety in his first four seasons (Ed Reed, 22). A healthy Joseph would be a game-changer for the Lions defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.headline: Packers coach Matt LaFleur indicated that Luke Musgrave (neck) “probably” will not play in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.analysis: Earlier this season, the Packers thought that Musgrave had a chance to return. Unfortunately, it appears as though that is no longer the case. The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman believes Musgrave’s “tenure with the Packers is all but over.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.headline: Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst said he expected TE Luke Musgrave (neck) to play at some point in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.analysis: Musgrave is coming back from a neck injury with no clear timeline for a return to action. The Packers last week signed Jonnu Smith, who will play behind Tucker Kraft to start the regular season. Smith could be an interesting waiver add if Kraft — returning from a major knee injury — misses any time in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.headline: Packers signed Jonnu Smith, formerly of the Steelers, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.analysis: Smith reunited with Arthur Smith in Pittsburgh last year and posted 38 catches for 222 yards and two touchdowns. Even with NFL players actively returning to college football, Jonnu was unable to find a way to follow his favorite offensive coordinator to Ohio State. All signs point to Tucker Kraft being fully recovered from his torn ACL by Week 1, but backup tight end Luke Musgrave remains sidelined with an injury of his own. Smith won’t be on the fantasy radar as long as Kraft is healthy, but he should be a solid depth option for the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.headline: Luke Musgrave caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Packers’ Wild Card Round loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.analysis: Musgrave wasn’t involved despite the Packers throwing 46 times in the loss, and the 2023 second-round pick finishes a disappointing campaign with another ineffective fantasy outing. He ended the year with just 24 catches for 252 yards, and even after Tucker Kraft went down with his ACL injury in Week 9, he didn’t he didn’t make an impact with zero touchdowns and just one game with over four catches. The 25-year-old is under contract for one more year, and there’s no reason to think he should be on radars when draft season begins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.headline: Luke Musgrave caught 3-of-3 targets for 38 yards in the Packers’ Week 16 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.analysis: Musgrave’s 38 receiving yards mark his second-highest total of the season and come on the heals of the 4/52/0 receiving line he had last week. Musgrave has yet to find the end zone this season and is averaging just 2.0 targets per game. He won’t be on the fantasy radar for Week 16 against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.headline: Luke Musgrave caught 4-of-6 targets for 52 yards in the Packers’ Week 15 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.analysis: The six targets Musgrave saw on Sunday set a new season high, as did his 52 receiving yards. Musgrave’s production saw a nice boost, thanks in part to a 26-yard reception on the Packers’ second drive of the game. Sunday’s game against the Broncos marked the first time this season that Musgrave has surpassed 34 receiving yards. He can be left on waivers for Week 16’s game against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.headline: Luke Musgrave caught 2-of-4 targets for 22 yards in the Packers’ Week 14 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.analysis: The good news is that Musgrave, along with Christian Watson and Jayden Reed, led the Packers in targets. The bad news is that Matt LaFleur deployed a three-headed committee at tight end. Musgrave, Josh Whyle, and Josh Fitzpatrick all run between 30 and 40 percent of the routes. Until Musgrave separates from the pack, he will be on the outside of the TE2 ranks looking in.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.headline: Luke Musgrave caught 1-of-1 targets for 23 yards in the Packers’ Week 13 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.analysis: Musgrave was barely involved as the Packers’ wide receivers stole the show against the Lions. Packers QB Jordan Love did give him one opportunity, flinging a play-action pass his way on the fourth drive. Musgrave dove and successfully secured the pass, bringing the ball down to the Lions’ 11-yard line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.headline: Luke Musgrave caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards in Green Bay’s Week 12 win over the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.analysis: Since taking over for Tucker Kraft in Week 10 as the full-time starter at Packers tight end, Musgrave has 29 yards on seven targets. You can do better.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.headline: Luke Musgrave caught 1-of-2 targets for -1 yards in the Packers’ Week 11 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-musgr.analysis: Musgrave’s “missed connection” frankly probably should have been a lost fumble, but the review command center predictably decided he didn’t “complete the process.” Stuck on four catches for 22 yards over the past two weeks, Musgrave so far isn’t stepping up during Tucker Kraft’s absence. With tight end deep if not necessarily productive this year, Musgrave isn’t really forcing his way into the top 24. That includes for Week 12 against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman believes the Packers should not sign MarShawn Lloyd to an extension after next season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Schneidman believes it is “not possible” to sign Lloyd to an extension after the 2027 season because of the young running back’s poor play. Lloyd is still trying to beat defenders around the edge with speed, rather than running north-south when he needs to. Although the injuries are mostly behind him, he has failed to live up to preseason expectations. Lloyd does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: Marshawn Lloyd (knee) was not listed on the Packers’ Wednesday injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Lloyd was presumably a full go in practice on Wednesday as he did not appear on the Packers’ injury report at all to open Week 10. This indicates he will be ready to play this week against the Vikings, despite missing Week 9 due to a knee injury. With Josh Jacobs out, Lloyd will see backfield opportunities once again. Kaleb Johnson projects to get a shot at the lead back role initially, but Lloyd has a passing-down role in the backfield. In the midst of an inefficient season and facing a daunting Vikings defense, Lloyd is a shaky FLEX at best for fantasy teams in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman believes Kaleb Johnson could have a chance to be the Packers’ lead rusher in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: With Josh Jacobs out with a broken finger, Johnson led the Packers with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown in the team’s Week 9 drubbing of the Patriots. Forty-four of those yards came on explosive rushes. Pierre Strong, meanwhile had eight carries on the day. MarShawn Lloyd was sidelined with a knee issue but could be back in the Green Bay lineup soon. Lloyd’s shocking lack of production this season could, according to Schneidman, give Johnson a real chance to seize lead back duties. Head coach Matt LaFleur after the team’s Week 9 win seemed to imply there are some pass protection concerns for Johnson. That would probably mean Chris Brooks, who’s expected to return from an ankle injury in Week 10, gets the third-down role while Jacobs is sidelined. The Packers this week take on an elite Minnesota offense that teams have run on in recent weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Josh Jacobs will undergo surgery on his fractured finger and “is expected to miss a maximum of three weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Less than 24 hours after it was reported that the team would see if Jacobs could play through his fractured finger, they have now opted for surgery. The decision to say Jacobs could be out “a maximum of three weeks” suggests he will avoid the injured reserve and that this will be more of a week-to-week thing, and that he could return before the end of the month. Jacobs has totaled 148 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns on 47 touches since returning from the Commissioner’s Exempt list. Now, the Packers will likely take a bit of a committee approach in the weeks ahead and could lean more on Kaleb Johnson, who was solid against the Patriots (14-68-1), with Jacobs and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) both sidelined. That said, all Packers running backs will be hard to trust as anything more than desperation dart throws in Week 10 when they take on a stout Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: Packers declared RB MarShawn Lloyd (knee), LB Zaire Franklin, OL Donovan Jennings, OL Sean Rhyan, OL Travis Glover, and TE Josh Whyle inactive for Week 9 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Pierre Strong and Kaleb Johnson will serve as the backups to Josh Jacobs with Lloyd sidelined. DB Keisean Nixon, who was listed as questionable entering the weekend, is active after being slowed by a groin injury earlier in the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: MarShawn Lloyd (knee) is questionable for Week 9 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Lloyd popped up on Thursday’s injury report with the knee issue, and now appears to be a game-time decision. Chris Brooks (ankle) is also questionable for the Week 9 tilt, so there could be depth issues for the Pack behind Josh Jacobs, who has struggled in his return to action as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: MarShawn Lloyd was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday’s practice due to a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Lloyd was good to go for Wednesday’s session, so this appears to be a new issue. Chris Brooks was also limited by his ankle injury for a second-straight practice. Lloyd and Brooks — if healthy — will be the backups to Josh Jacobs for Week 9, and don’t offer much fantasy upside, if any.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: Josh Jacobs rushed 21 times for 39 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers, adding six catches for 13 yards and another score.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Jacobs’ fantasy game was salvaged with two scores, but the tailback didn’t look particularly spry in the process. He had a long gain of just six, and there was almost no burst even against the porous Panthers’ run defense. He was involved in the passing game, but again, outside of his four-yard receiving score, there really wasn’t much there. It’s clear this is Jacobs’ backfield despite the scuffles, as MarShawn Lloyd had just three touches in the contest for seven yards. He’s a volatile low-end RB1 candidate for Week 9 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: Pierre Strong rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys, adding 39 yards on five receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Strong’s 17 opportunities handily led the backfield on a night MarShawn Lloyd was in and out of the game due to an early injury scare. Even so, he managed only 2.8 yards per carry. With Josh Jacobs expected to be activated off the commissioner’s exempt list on Monday, Strong, Lloyd, and Kaleb Johnson can safely be returned to the waiver wire from whence they came.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: MarShawn Lloyd rushed 10 times for 31 yards and a two touchdowns in the Packers’ Week 5 win over the Bears, adding a six-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Although he notched a receiving score in Week 2, these were the first two rushing touchdowns of Lloyd’s career. Awesome stuff, though a player who was averaging 2.7 yards per carry coming into this afternoon saw that number sit at just 3.1 against the Bears. The Pack also got journeyman Pierre Strong involved in their increasingly frustrating backfield committee. Strong was mostly just absorbing Chris Brooks’ (ankle, injured reserve) lost work, but that of course means Lloyd wasn’t seeing a bigger workload. Although the scores are nice, Lloyd is still lacking an RB2 profile heading into Week 6. He will be a low-upside FLEX vs. the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.headline: Former Bucs head coach Bruce Arians says he has “the itch” to coach football again.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.analysis: Arians detailed a myriad of health issues that he dealt with in his final season as the Bucs’ head coach. He tore his Achilles and eventually injured his back. Arians was also monitoring an aneurysm in his heart at the time. He stepped away from coaching after the 2021 season but remained with the Bucs in an advisory role for some time. Arians won 13 games in his final season as a head coach and took home the Lombardi Trophy in his penultimate season. Now 74 years old, Arians wouldn’t be the long-term answer for a team, but he could be an option for a team in a win-now window.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.headline: Buccaneers head coach Bruce Arians is retiring and will join Tampa Bay’s front office.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.analysis: Per NBC’s Peter King, 69-year-old Arians is taking a “senior consultant” role in the Bucs’ front office, and DC Todd Bowles has been promoted to head coach. There were whispers of a potential Arians retirement after last season, but he seemed all in at another run in 2022. Especially with Tom Brady coming back, the timing of this is odd, but Arians wants to go out on top rather than in a rebuild. There have also been rumors that Arians and Brady’s relationship is strained, but that isn’t believed to be true. Arians handpicked Bowles as his successor. “With the organization in probably the best shape it’s been in its history, with Brady coming back, I’d rather see Todd in position to be successful and not have to take some [crappy] job,” Arians said. “I’m probably retiring next year anyway, in February. So, I control the narrative right now. I don’t control it next February because [if] Brady gets hurt, we go 10-7, and it’s an open interview for the job. I got 31 [coaches and their] families that depend on me. My wife is big on not letting all those families down.” Respect to Arians, that’s a classy move, especially if he wasn’t all the way in on coaching this year. Arians retires with a career 89-51-1 coaching record, one Super Bowl title, and two Coach of the Year awards. Arians has a shot at the Hall of Fame.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.headline: Bucs coach Bruce Arians said a trade for a veteran quarterback seems “out of the question.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.analysis: Arians noted that the team has about eight quarterbacks on their board but teams have been unwilling to part with their proven veterans. The Bucs may also be making inadequate offers but Arians has a point. GMs and owners are hesitant to move on from an established option at quarterback, evidenced by the lack of trades involving passers in recent years. With Tom Brady riding off into the sunset, Kyle Trask is the only quarterback on Tampa Bay’s roster. The Bucs are barely above the cap and will be losing numerous high-end players to free agency. This may ultimately force them to look to a cheap free agent or the draft for their next quarterback

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.headline: Sports Business Journal’s Ben Fischer reports that the Buccaneers will be the home team in the NFL’s first regular season game in Germany in 2022.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.analysis: It’s been widely rumored that the Chiefs will be the away opponent, but that likely won’t be confirmed for a bit. The NFL is surely hoping that German fans will be treated to better than Blaine Gabbert. The game will be in Munich.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.headline: Pro Football Network sources report that there is a “major exodus expected” from Tampa Bay following Tom Brady’s retirement.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.analysis: Looking slightly beyond the surface, this shouldn’t be too surprising. It seems probable that Rob Gronkowski follows Brady into retirement. Gronkowski, WR Chris Godwin, C Ryan Jensen, and CB Carlton Davis are all unrestricted free agents. Head coach Bruce Arians has reportedly told his staff that they are free to look for other jobs around the league regardless of whether it’s a promotion or not. The Bucs got a Super Bowl ring, but the future looks incredibly grim without Brady. This team could look completely different next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.headline: Speaking Monday, Bucs HC Bruce Arians said that he would call plays for the Tampa offense in 2022 if Byron Leftwich took a head coaching job elsewhere.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.analysis: This seems like newly-relevant news with Leftwich apparently the top target of the Jacksonville Jaguars head-coaching search. Arians has been successful as a play caller so this probably won’t diminish the Bucs offense in any way as long as Tom Brady is back in the saddle for 2022.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Bucs coach Bruce Arians is expected to return next season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.analysis: This wasn’t a given with Arians the second-oldest coach in the league. Arians also has a history of health concerns and spent time on the COVID list this year. The Bucs are expected to pick up their team-option this offseason on Arians, who’s signed through 2022.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.headline: Bucs coach Bruce Arians (COVID-19) will coach in Week 17 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.analysis: Arians was forced to isolate away from the team after testing positive for COVID earlier this week. Wide receivers coach Kevin Garver is also returning from isolation ahead of Week 17. The Bucs are 13-point favorites versus the Jets this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.headline: Buccaneers coach Bruce Arians tested positive for COVID-19.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.analysis: Longtime assistant Harold Goodwin will take over Arians’ head-coaching duties in his absence. The latter will isolate from home in the interim, potentially returning in time to coach in Week 17 if the new five-day quarantine protocols are immediately put into action.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.headline: Buccaneers revised coach Bruce Arians’ contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bruce-aria.analysis: He’ll remain under contract through the 2022 season but receive a pay raise upon signing the new deal. It’s a generous reward from the Glazer family after the 68-year-old coach helped in obtaining the team’s second Super Bowl win in franchise history. General Manager Jason Licht also agreed to a new deal that tacked on multiple years to his current one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Ravens signed K Harrison Mevis to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: The team added Riley Patterson to their active roster yesterday, but both kickers will likely have a chance to earn the job in practice this week. We aren’t expecting great fantasy numbers from either kicker with Lamar Jackson no longer fueling the offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Ravens worked out K Harrison Mevis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: Riley Patterson also worked out for Baltimore. Tyler Loop is on injured reserve and Jake Moody got nabbed off their practice squad, leaving Baltimore without a kicker. One of Mevis or Patterson should get signed in the next few days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports that Blake Grupe suffered a knee injury in their Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: Bringing back Harrison Mevis, whom the Rams waived five days ago, is one option, but it is unclear whether either side wants a reunion. The Rams might want to bring a few special teams contributors aboard while they’re at it. Grupe was injured during a tackle attempt because yet another return had scooted right past the Rams’ special teams coverage unit. The Rams rank outside the top 25 in average kick return yards allowed and average punt return yards allowed. Minimizing kicker tackling attempts in the future is probably a good call.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Rams waived K Harrison Mevis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: Mevis, I told you six times before, you don’t work here no more. The Thiccer Kicker hit 12-of-13 for the Rams after coming in late last season and 39-of-39 extra points. He doesn’t quite have the distance of some of the league’s best kickers, but we expect him to continue to get chances at 24.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Rams signed K Blake Grupe off the Jets practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: Going 5-for-9 on the season will get you replaced in the modern NFL, as Thiccer Kicker Harrison Mevis is learning. It’s not totally fair, one of those was blocked, but clearly the Rams were not happy with how things were trending. Grupe is a worthwhile pickup in leagues that still use kickers. He went 11-for-11 for the Colts last year after being released by the Saints at midseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Rams tendered OL Justin Dedich, K Harrison Mevis, WR Xavier Smith.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: The team will maintain control of three players that surprised in 2025, including “thiccer kicker” Harrison Mevis. The tendering of exclusive rights free agents ties the three to the franchise through the 2026 season considering they are unable to negotiate with other teams. At least for now, it appears as if the Rams will continue forward with Mevis as their place kicker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Harrison Mevis made his only field-goal attempt in Los Angeles’ NFC Championship loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: Mevis finishes the year 12-of-13 on field goals — missing one against the Seahawks in Week 16 — and hit all 39 of his regular season extra point attempts. He was perfect in the playoffs on five field goals and nine extra-point attempts. The 23-year-old was a find for the Rams and should enter the starting kicker conversation in most fantasy leagues that use kickers in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Harrison Mevis made 2-of-2 field goals in the Rams’ Week 15 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: He hasn’t missed yet, going 5-for-5 on field-goal attempts and 27-of-27 on extra points. The Rams talked a big game about Joshua Karty eventually getting the job back when they waived him, but Mevis is not giving the former incumbent an inch of space to get active. The Thiccer Kicker will remain a low-end K1 against the Seahawks in Week 16.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Harrison Mevis converted his lone field goal attempt and all six of his extra point attempts in the Rams’ Week 14 win against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: Mevis has proven a fine weekly fantasy play thanks to the high-powered Rams offense and the positive game script it creates. He’s made all three of his field goals this season and has yet to miss an extra point. He should be in fantasy lineups next week against the Lions in what should be a high-scoring affair. The Lions have allowed 1.7 field goal tries per game this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Harrison Mevis will again be the team’s kicker in Week 11 against Seattle.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: Mevis, the “Thiccer Kicker,” did not attempt a field goal against the 49ers, settling for six made extra points. Seattle will probably force some more attempts this week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Broncos have revoked their trade for Chargers LB Daiyan Henley because of a failed physical.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: The move, or lack thereof, was announced by Denver around midnight, and Rapoport later gave the reasoning. Henley has been playing through a knee issue for multiple weeks, though he has also dealt with other injuries that could have caused the Broncos to back out. Denver originally agreed to give fourth- and fifth-round picks to acquire Henley. He will now return to the Chargers. As Rapoport points out, the 0-8 Chargers now officially made zero trades ahead of the deadline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Broncos acquired LB Daiyan Henley from the Chargers for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: The Chargers finally make a move, dealing a player who was considered a burgeoning star a few years ago away for a light deadline return. Henley had a career-worst 38.3 PFF coverage grade this year but is still a good tackler and should give the Broncos some oomph on run defense down the stretch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers LB Daiyan Henley (illness) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 3 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: It’s kind of surprising that the illness has lasted this long — Henley drew another DNP in practice on Friday after also missing Wednesday — and even despite him playing through it on Monday Night it’s certainly possible he sits this game out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers LB Daiyan Henley (illness) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: Henley was added to the Chargers’ injury report prior to their Monday night game with an illness. He played in the team’s win over the Raiders, so a missed practice two days later is a surprise, but not concerning yet. Henley is still on track to play in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers LB Daiyan Henley (illness) is questionable for Week 2’s game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: The Chargers announced on Monday that Henley will be added to the injury report due to an illness. The third-year linebacker totaled eight tackles and a sack in the team’s Week 1 win over the Chiefs, and would join fellow linebacker Denzel Perryman on the sideline if he is unable to play. It’s not often we see players miss games due to illnesses, so we would still expect to see Henley suit up despite this late development.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers LB Daiyan Henley said he has fully recovered from offseason shoulder surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: Henley played through a torn labrum for four months while breaking out in his second NFL season last year. The 25-year-old totaled 92 tackles, 13 quarterback pressures, six pass breakups and one interception. He now has ample time to ramp up ahead of the 2025 NFL season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers LB Daiyan Henley (shoulder) expects to be ready for training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: Henley had surgery to repair a torn labrum that he played through for the final four months of the season. Henley told ESPN’s Kris Rhim that he expects to be “100 percent” before training camp. If for whatever reason Henley is slow coming back, it could be an opening for 2024 third-rounder Junior Colson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers LB Daiyan Henley expects to undergo surgery on his injured shoulder this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: Henley told The Athletic’s Daniel Popper that he suffered a torn labrum in his shoulder during the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Chiefs. Henley nonetheless finished with 49 tackles in run defense and 50 in coverage this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers selected Washington State LB Daiyan Henley with the No. 85 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: Henley (6’1/225) worked his way up the college ranks, spending 2017-2021 at Nevada where he was named Second Team All-Mountain West Conference before transferring as a graduate to Washington State. He made a seamless transition to the Power Five level, earning First Team All-Pac-12 recognition while becoming the first Butkus Award finalist in Wazzu history. A textbook finisher thanks to his 33” arms, Henley led the P5 with a 90.3 PFF tackling grade thanks to his relentless motor and pristine 5.2% missed tackle rate last year. He ran a 95th percentile 4.54s 40-yard dash and has had demonstrable success in coverage, holding opponents to a 39.0 NFL Passer Rating when targeted and picking off four passes in 2021. He can sometimes make bad reads and needs to keep his pad level low when engaging blockers. However Henley has shown the ability to be a complete linebacker, be it bringing pressure off the edge with ferocity, crashing down on run plays or, dropping into coverage. A physical middle linebacker whose play strength far outweighs his size, Henley has legitimate NFL starter potential.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Former Washington senior LB Daiyan Henley transferred to Washington State as a graduate
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: Henley (6'1"/220) is a big pickup for the Cougars. He was a second team All-Mountain West linebacker, racking up 94 tackles (two for loss), four interceptions, three fumble recoveries and he scored two defensive touchdowns. USC was also in for his services, but he chose WSU.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.headline: Deommodore Lenoir (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.analysis: Lenoir and Renardo Green (back) were among the two 49ers cornerbacks not practicing on Wednesday. Fellow cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder/neck) was a limited participant. With the slew of secondary injuries, the Cowboys wideouts will have an easier chance at chunk gains against San Francisco for week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Gracen Halton suffered a season-ending ankle fracture.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.analysis: The fourth-round rookie finishes the year with 10 tackles, eight quarterback pressures and two sacks. Shanahan also told reporters that starting cornerbacks Renardo Green (back) and Deommodore Lenoir (foot) picked up injuries in today’s game against the Raiders. The defense has been hit hard by injuries this season. Hopefully, the cornerbacks are back before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.headline: 49ers declared CB Deommodore Lenoir (calf) active for Week 11 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.analysis: Lenoir entered the weekend with a questionable tag due to a calf injury. He suffered the injury in Thursday’s practice but is active after experiencing some tightness. The 49ers declared RB Jordan James, WR Jordan Watkins, OL Connor Colby, DL Clelin Ferrell, DL Kevin Givens, and CB Eli Apple inactive for Week 11 against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.headline: 49ers declared QB Brock Purdy (toe), WR Ricky Pearsall (knee), DE Bryce Huff (hamstring), C Jake Brendel (hamstring), DL Yetur Gross-Matos (hamstring), DT CJ West and RB Jordan James inactive for San Francisco’s Week 8 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.analysis: All five players with injuries were ruled out on Friday. Deommodore Lenoir (quad) and Luke Gifford (hamstring) are playing on questionable tags. James and West are healthy scratches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.headline: 49ers CB Deommodore Lenoir (hip) participated in team drills on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.analysis: It seems like Lenoir has been able to shake the hip irritation that was bothering him earlier in training camp. The veteran should be considered healthy as things stand heading into the preseason games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.headline: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters that CB Deommodore Lenoir (hip irritation) will be sidelined for at least two more practices.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.analysis: Both of the 49ers’ starting perimeter cornerbacks are now injured. Fellow starter, CB Renardo Green, is “aiming” to return for the 49ers’ second preseason game as he rehabs a hamstring strain suffered last Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.headline: 49ers CB Deommodore Lenoir was arrested on Thursday night and released on Friday morning.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.analysis: The cause for the arrest varies between sources. Members of the Los Angeles Police Department reportedly stopped a group of people, which included Lenoir, and observed a visible firearm located inside a parked car. The reason for the initial stop is unclear. Officers asked for the car keys, at which point an unidentified individual passed them to Lenoir, who passed them to another individual shortly after that, apparently rejecting the officers’ request.
