Lenoir was then arrested and booked before being released.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.headline: 49ers ruled out Nick Bosa (hip/obliques) for Week 13 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.analysis: Bosa’s dual-oblique/hip injury will sideline him again and the defensive line will also notably be without starting DT Jordan Elliott (concussion), leaving the 49ers defensive-right side of the field awfully short-staffed. Josh Allen’s blindside should be kept clean and the run game will likely be able to impose its will easily, running off of left tackle Dion Dawkins. CB Deommodore Lenoir (knee) is out though CB Charvarius Ward (personal) will return after a three-game absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.headline: 49ers G Dominick Puni (shoulder) is undergoing an MRI on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.analysis: The rookie guard played every snap in Week 12’s loss to the Packers, but apparently something popped up. He’d be a huge loss for the 49ers. Deommodore Lenoir (knee) is also getting an MRI for the 49ers after playing 93 percent of the snaps. This team just can’t buy a health-based break this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.headline: 49ers CB Deommodore Lenoir exited Week 12 against the Packers with an apparent leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deommodore.analysis: Lenoir appeared to bang knees with one of the Packers’ offensive players. Trainers tended to him for a moment on-field before eventually escorting Lenoir to the sideline. We tentatively expect Lenoir to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Travon Walker (rib) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: Walker suffered a rib injury in practice last week but played through it in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens. He starts out the week not practicing, but this may just be maintenance instead of an aggravation. Walker will need to practice in some fashion later this week, but he is not in jeopardy of missing Week 10 against the Titans just yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Travon Walker (ribs) is active for Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: The Jaguars’ No. 2 edge rusher will play through his ribs injury tonight. He apparently got hurt during Tuesday’s practice, but is good to go two days later. The Jaguars declared WR CJ Williams, CB Alijah Huzzie, S Cam’Ron Silmon-Craig and DE Wesley Williams inactive for Week 9 against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Travon Walker (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: Walker was added to the Jaguars’ injury report on Tuesday, apparently having suffered a ribs injury in practice. The Jaguars’ No. 2 edge rusher might not be needed to win an expectedly lopsided affair, but having him on the field will certainly be helpful for the Jaguars D/ST.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Jaguars signed EDGE Travon Walker to a four-year, $110 million extension through 2030.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: The deal includes $50 million at signing and $77 million in total guarantees. Walker, 25, has sacked opposing quarterbacks 29 times in regular season games over his four-year career. He banked four sacks last year, plus 42 quarterback pressures and a career-high 13.0 percent quarterback pressure rate. Fellow Jaguars EDGE Josh Hines-Allen is under contract through 2028. Today’s deal keeps the starting EDGE duo intact long-term.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: ESPN’s Michael DiRocco reports the Jaguars have had preliminary discussions about extensions for WR Parker Washington, TE Brenton Strange, and EDGE Travon Walker.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: It was pointed out by John Shipley a few days ago that Wan’Dale Robinson’s free agent contract might be a starting point for the Washington extension. Walker is entering his final season under his rookie contract’s fifth-year option. Strange and Washington are both on the final year of their rookie contracts. The Jaguars have been uncharacteristically (and probably smartly, given their success last year) quiet in free agency, so perhaps they’re just focusing on locking up their core.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes that the Jaguars could use the 2026 NFL Draft to “boost” their defensive line.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: The front office could invest heavily in the defensive line, which currently includes three projected starters who have just one year remaining on their contracts. Former No. 1 overall pick, EDGE Travon Walker, is among them and is coming off a four-sack season, matching his 2022 rookie season total. He recorded 10 in 2024 and 11 in 2023. The team could draft an EDGE to groom behind Walker just in case they don’t complete an extension before the season. The Jaguars’ projected starting DTs are Arik Armstead, 32, and DaVon Hamilton, 29. Both players are scheduled to enter free agency next offseason. Given their age, it is reasonable to assume the Jaguars draft at least one interior defender in April. The team is returning every member of their offensive line this year. Shipley believes the Jaguars will use “at least one pick on a developmental offensive lineman.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Jaguars EDGE Travon Walker (knee) is practicing in full for Week 15 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: Walker returned to practice for two limited sessions last week and played off a questionable tag on Sunday. Potentially facing the Brady Cook-led Jets, Walker should be able to return with a sack or two in Week 15.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Jaguars declared WR Parker Washington (hip) inactive for Jacksonville’s Week 14 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: As expected based on earlier reporting, Washington will be scratched. He’s droppable if you have a late move you need to get in ahead of Sunday kickoff. Also inactive for the Jaguars are: S Andrew Wingard (concussion), Yasir Abdullah, OL Walker Little (concussion), TE Johnny Mundt, DL Emmanuel Ogbah and DL Austin Johnson. DL Travon Walker (knee), S Eric Murray (neck) and Arik Armstead (hand) are playing despite questionable tags in a huge game for the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Jaguars EDGE Travon Walker (knee) is questionable for Jacksonville’s Week 14 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: Walker hasn’t played since Week 11, but was able to get in two limited sessions this week and appears to be trending towards a return in a must-win AFC South top-of-division showdown with the Colts. The pass rusher has had a somewhat disappointing year to this point with just 2.5 sacks in nine games. Arik Armstead (hand) and Eric Murray (neck) are also questionable for Jacksonville.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Jaguars EDGE Travon Walker (knee) is practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: Almost undoubtedly a limited session after missing most of the last two weeks. The Jaguars are likely checking just how much Walker can give them ahead of Sunday’s massive top-of-AFC-South showdown with the Colts. It’s his first practice since ahead of Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Dion Dawkins (rib) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: Dawkins did not practice last week due to a rib injury, missing the Bills’ Week 9 win over the Vikings. he returns to practice in a limited fashion to open Week 10, giving him a chance to return against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Bills declared WR Skyler Bell, LT Dion Dawkins, LG Alec Anderson, DL Greg Gaines, OLB Mike Danna, and S Jalon Kilgore inactive for Week 9 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: Josh Allen will be without the starting left side of his offensive line for a game against the most aggressive defense in the league, a matchup that pits two one-loss teams on Monday Night Football. Expect a more ball-out-quick game plan from Allen and the Bills, something that could benefit Dalton Kincaid and Khalil Shakir over the short-to-intermediate levels of the field. The team could also look to deploy 12-personnel at increased rates to get Dawson Knox’s blocking abilities on the field, which would be a detriment to the route participation of Shakir.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Dion Dawkins (ribs) and Alec Anderson (ankle) are questionable for Week 9 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: The Bills enter Week 9 with the entire left side of one the league’s top offensive lines questionable. Both players did not practice through Friday before drawing the questionable tag for Monday Night Football against the Vikings. We likely won’t know their respective statuses until inactives are released 90 minutes prior to first kick. Absences would be a detriment to the run game and could lead to increased emphasis on the short areas of the field through the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Dion Dawkins (ribs) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: Dawkins and starting LG Alec Anderson (ankle) have now missed two practices this week. This is concerning. The Bills face the Vikings’ elite, blitz-based defense in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game. Hopefully, the extra day off helps them return in time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Dion Dawkins (ribs) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: Dawkins, the Bills’ left tackle, and LG Alec Anderson (ankle) were both absent today. They have an extra day to rest, since the Bills face the Vikings in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game. Hopefully, the extra time allows them to suit up against Minnesota’s elite defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Bills declared DE Greg Rousseau, OT Dion Dawkins, DE Joey Bosa, WR Brandin Cooks, S Jordan Poyer, DT DaQuan Jones, and LB Terrel Bernard inactive for Week 18 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: The Bills’ game has little meaning with the team having locked up a playoff spot. They will either be the fifth or sixth seed, depending on the outcome of this game and the Texans’ game. The team might believe that they can beat the Jets without many of their starters, but we wouldn’t expect many starters to play key snaps here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Bills LT Dion Dawkins (illness) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: Players typically play through illnesses, but it would be nice to see Dawkins practice tomorrow after sitting out on Wednesday and Thursday. The Bills’ offensive line is tasked with fending off the Browns’ elite pass-rush unit this week. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Dion Dawkins cleared concussion protocol and will play in Week 14 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: Dawkins was out of the non-contact jersey on Thursday and is now on track to play on Sunday against the Bengals. While Dawkins will be back in action after one game away, head coach Sean McDermott said EDGE Joey Bosa and LB Terrel Bernard would be out in Week 14, while WR Joshua Palmer will be listed as doubtful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Dion Dawkins (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: He did, however, shed his non-contact jersey, so he may be closer to clearing concussion protocol. Dawkins and Spencer Brown (shoulder, limited for the second day in a row) are both trending towards playing on Sunday, or at least hitting the questionable line on Friday. It would do wonders for Buffalo’s offense to have their bookend tackles back on Sunday against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Bills LT Dion Dawkins (concussion) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: Bills RT Spencer Brown (shoulder) also upgraded to limited. Both players were sidelined for the entirety of Week 13. The Bills face the Bengals’ pushover pass-rush unit in Week 14. Although the offense can likely get by without their starting offensive tackles, having them on the field would give Buffalo a significant edge in the trenches. Bills LB Terrel Bernard (elbow) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Steve Avila (hamstring) did not practice in Wednesday’s walk-through.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: Avila aggravated a hamstring injury and starts out the week not practicing. Rams head coach Sean McVay said Monday that Avila will miss some time, but may not go on injured reserve as the Rams are out of return slots. Expect Avila to miss Week 10 against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Rams declared OLB Nick Hampton, QB Stetson Bennett, TE Terrance Ferguson, OT DJ Humphries and LG Steve Avila active for Week 3’s game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: Ferguson is inactive with the Rams getting Parkinson back from a shoulder injury. Braden Fiske is also active after being considered questionable with an oblique issue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said OL Steve Avila (ankle) is doubtful for Week 3’s game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: It’ll likely be Justin Decich at guard for the Rams again on Sunday against Jalen Carter and company. McVay added that Colby Parkinson (ankle) is questionable for the contest. No Rams tight ends currently qualify as major fantasy plays.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Eagles DT Jalen Carter (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: The Rams’ offensive line health is improving but LG Steve Avila remains sidelined by an ankle injury. His absence could be costly with Carter’s health improving. The Week 3 matchup between the Eagles and Rams might be a pass-heavy affair, which would bode positively for Carter’s sack productivity.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Rams LG Steve Avila (ankle) and TE Colby Parkinson (shoulder) are doubtful for Week 2’s game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: The Rams will get one of their guards back after Kevin Dotson (also ankle) was cleared off the injury report for Week 2. Beaux Limmer figures to get Avila’s snaps at guard. Parkinson’s absence doesn’t majorly impact the Rams passing tree since it mostly condensed into Davante Adams and Puka Nacua in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Rams OL Rob Havenstein (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: Havenstein sat out Wednesday’s practice, so his return is a great sign. The Rams also got back OL Kevin Dotson (ankle), who likewise practiced in a limited capacity. Fellow OL Steve Avila (ankle) remained sidelined. The Rams’ offensive line is banged up, but the unit is at least on the upswing, which bodes positively for Matthew Stafford’s ability to stay upright against the Titans in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Rams OL Kevin Dotson, Rob Havenstein, and Steve Avila did not participate in Wednesday’s practice due to ankle injuries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: Dotson, Havenstein, and Avila all popped up on the injury report with ankle issues to start Week 2. Head coach Sean McVay had said Dotson and Avila are week-to-week with their ankle injuries, but Havenstein’s status remains up in the air. Matthew Stafford’s protection will look slim should any or all of these three miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Rams activated LG Steve Avila from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: Avila landed on injured reserve after suffering an MCL sprain in Week 1 against the Lions. The second-year guard now appears set to return for Thursday night’s game against the Dolphins and should man the left side of the interior like we saw for all of last season. As a rookie, Avila played on over 1,100 offensive snaps, and earned a PFF blocking grade of 61.1. He allowed just two sacks on 32 pressures and is one of two linemen set to return for the Rams, as guard Jonah Jackson has also been activated ahead of tonight’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Rams G Jonah Jackson (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: The Rams’ offensive line is quietly trending toward a midseason turnaround after operating as one of the league’s worst units early on. Hopefully, Jackson can stack another full practice on Saturday and suit up for the first time since Week 2. Fellow OL Steve Avila (knee) likewise practiced in full on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Rams opened LG Jonah Jackson’s 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: In addition to Jackson, the Rams also opened the return window for center Steve Avila. Both players will be eligible to come off injured reserve at any time and would provide immediate boosts to an offensive line that’s ranked 31st in PFF pass-blocking grades and 15th in PFF run-blocking grades. Jackson has been on injured reserve since reaggravating a shoulder injury in Week 2 that he dealt with throughout training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.headline: Kam Curl (toe) did not practice in Wednesday’s walk-through.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.analysis: Curl played through a foot injury in Week 9 but picked up a toe injury. He starts out the week not practicing but will have a chance to play Week 10 against the Cardinals if he can get a practice in later this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) limited again on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.analysis: Garrett has a chance to face the Commanders this week, but he still belongs in the questionable column at this time. Rams CB1 Trent McDuffie (back) and S Kam Curl (foot) both missed practice for the second time this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.headline: Rams S Kamren Kinchens (hamstring) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.analysis: This is Kinchens’ second missed practice. Fellow Rams S Kam Curl (ankle) has now logged two limited sessions and should be good to go, but the team’s safety unit is ailing. They typically use three-safety looks, with DB Quentin Lake doubling as a safety and nickel coverage defender. The Rams signed S Tanner Ingle from the practice squad to the active roster. The Rams face the Giants on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.headline: Rams re-signed S Kam Curl to a three-year, $36 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.analysis: Curl first joined the Rams in 2024 and has started all 33 games he has appeared in for them while forcing two interceptions, 14 pass breakups, and three fumbles. He also posted a career high with 122 tackles last season while adding two sacks. The veteran safety is now slated to be under contract with the Rams through 2028, shoring up a secondary for the foreseeable future that recently added Trent McDuffie to the mix. Curl earned a PFF coverage grade of 66.1 last season and did not allow a touchdown on any of the 58 targets that came his way.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.headline: Rams S Kam Curl (leg) and CB Emmanuel Forbes (hamstring) left Tuesday’s practice early.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.analysis: Curl left the Rams’ practice early with a lower leg issue while Forbes exited with a hamstring injury. Head coach Sean McVay indicated there would be more clarity on the defensive backs’ injuries later this week. Curl has started 69 of 76 career games, including each of his 16 games played in his first season with the Rams last year. An absence from him would dent the Rams’ secondary on the back end. Forbes played in two games for the Rams since arriving from Washington last season and is behind Ahkello Witherspoon and Darious Williams as depth at cornerback. Derion Kendrick and Cam Lampkin would see more opportunities if Forbes missed a part of training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.headline: Lions RT Penei Sewell (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.analysis: The injury occurred when a Lions offensive lineman delivered a hit to Rams S Kamren Curl, who was attempting to clog a rushing lane. Curl impacted Sewell’s lower leg laterally, causing Sewell to briefly writhe in pain after the play. Sewell toughed it out, never leaving the field. While Friday’s injury report will be helpful, the team could opt to rest him throughout the week as a precaution, before allowing the two-time defending Pro Bowler to suit up on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.headline: Rams signed S Kamren Curl, formerly of the Commanders, to a two-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.analysis: The deal is worth “up to” $13 million. A 2020 seventh-rounder still only 25 later this month, Curl was an every-down player for the majority of his rookie contract. He has quietly developed into one of the league’s better safeties, and he could still have room to grow in a Rams defense led by Aaron Donald that is always intelligently coached.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.headline: Commanders declared S Kamren Curl, QB Sam Howell, RB Antonio Gibson, OG Chris Paul, OT Saahdiq Charles, CB Benjamin St-Juste, and DE James Smith-Williams inactive for Week 17 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.analysis: Curl has now missed two-straight games for the Commanders after popping up on the team’s injury report ahead of Week 16’s matchup against the 49ers. This leaves a glaring hole in Washington’s secondary that will be fighting for its playoff lives in Week 17 against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.headline: Commanders declared S Kamren Curl, QB Sam Howell, OG Chris Paul, OT Saahdiq Charles and DT Daniel Wise inactive for Week 16 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.analysis: In the midst of a big season, Curl is a big loss for the Commanders’ Christmas Eve road trip. Questionable today, he should have a good shot at returning on eight days rest for Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.headline: Washington S Kamren Curl (ankle) is questionable for Week 16’s game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kamren-cur.analysis: Curl popped up on the report with an ankle injury earlier this week and did not practice Thursday. We’d be a little surprised if he played based on how things are trending. Curl’s been excellent this season, notching an 80.3 PFF coverage grade. If he misses the game, the 49ers could exploit Washington safeties in coverage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.headline: Ravens signed K Riley Patterson, formerly of the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.analysis: The Ravens currently have Tyler Loop on injured reserve and lost Jake Moody to the Falcons this week. This prompted a couple of kicker workouts this week and led to the team signing Patterson to be the kicker, at least until Loop returns. Patterson made 27-of-29 field goals for the Dolphins last season and 7-of-9 field goals this season. Miami released him in October and he finds a new home in Baltimore a few weeks later. Patterson will kick for the Ravens on Monday Night Football against the Chargers, but doesn’t have much fantasy value with a Ravens offense missing Lamar Jackson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.headline: Ravens worked out K Harrison Mevis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.analysis: Riley Patterson also worked out for Baltimore. Tyler Loop is on injured reserve and Jake Moody got nabbed off their practice squad, leaving Baltimore without a kicker. One of Mevis or Patterson should get signed in the next few days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.headline: Dolphins released K Zane Gonzalez.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.analysis: Gonzalez’s release seemingly bodes well for K Riley Patterson. The two veteran kickers were competing to replace K Jason Sanders, who signed with the Jets this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.headline: Dolphins re-signed K Riley Patterson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.analysis: Zane Gonzalez is also on the roster, meaning there will be a kicking competition this summer. Gonzalez went 19-of-22 on his field goal tries with the Falcons last year. Patterson connected on 27-of-29 with Miami. We don’t expect the winner of this competition to have much fantasy relevance in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.headline: Dolphins K Jason Sanders (hip) is questionable for Week 17 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.analysis: Riley Patterson has been kicking in Sanders’ stead all year, converting 24-of-26 field goals and 31-of-32 extra points. Although the conversion rates are good, he lacks the requisite kick volume for K1 treatment. We do not know which player will be active on game day, but Sanders remained limited in practice all week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.headline: Dolphins K Jason Sanders (hip) is questionable for Miami’s Week 16 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.analysis: If you’re thinking “haven’t thought of him for a minute,” well, Sanders has missed the entire season to this point with the hip ailment. Dolphins ST coordinator Craig Aukerman was asked Thursday about whether Sanders or Riley Patterson would kick this weekend and said he didn’t want to speculate. Dolphins long-time beat Barry Jackson noted that Aukerman was asked if he views it as “A). Sanders is Dolphins kicker moving forward period or B). This is a decision above my pay grade that must be made by whoever is in charge in next 8 months,” and Aukerman politely declined to answer. So, yeah. We don’t know who will kick for the Dolphins yet against the Bengals. Someone, probably.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.headline: Riley Patterson converted 2-of-2 field goal attempts in the Dolphins’ Week 14 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.analysis: Patterson also made all four of his extra point attempts as the Dolphins trounced the Jets. He saw a lot of scoring opportunities and gave fantasy managers a productive day with two field goal kicks of 43 and 53 yards. Patterson will have fewer scoring opportunities against the Steelers in Week 15, but is productive enough for fantasy managers to keep him in lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.headline: Dolphins signed K Riley Patterson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.analysis: After elevating Patterson from the practice squad the previous three weeks, the Dolphins had no choice but to sign him if they hoped to elevate him again for Week 4 against the Jets. The veteran kicker is 2-for-2 on field goal attempts this season and has made all six of his extra point attempts. He seems like a safe bet to remain the Dolphins’ kicker as long as Jason Sanders (hip) remains sidelined. It’s worth noting that Sanders will be eligible to come off injured reserve after this week, so Patterson’s stay on the 53-man roster could be short-lived.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.headline: Dolphins elevated K Riley Patterson and RB Jeff Wilson ahead of their Week 1 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.analysis: Wilson gets the game day elevation in the wake of Jaylen Wright’s injury while the Dolphins entered Week 1 preparations without a kicker on the active roster. De’Von Achane remains the unquestioned top back while rookie Ollie Gordon appears set to step into the primary change of pace role, leaving Wilson as a likely emergency back. The team also did not elevate a tight end, meaning they will take on the Colts with only Julian Hill and Tanner Conner with Darren Waller set to miss.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.headline: Dolphins signed K Riley Patterson to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-patt.analysis: He’s expected to be elevated and kick for the Dolphins in Week 1 against the Colts. As long as Patterson doesn’t leave points off the field, he should have a chance to replace Jason Sanders throughout his entire IR stint. Sanders is expected back in 4-5 weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Carlton Davis (knee) will not play in Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: The Pats are traveling to Germany to take on the Lions. Davis was among several players who presumably didn’t make the trip overseas and were ruled out today. Davis has two pass breakups and 22 combined tackles across five appearances this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Carlton Davis (neck) is active for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: The Patriots’ No. 2 perimeter cornerback makes his return from a multi-week neck injury for this divisional showdown. The Patriots declared CB Karon Prunty, S Elliott Davison, CB Channing Canada, QB Behren Morton, RB TreVeyon Henderson and WR A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) inactive for Week 8 against the Dolphins. Prunty and Canada have also missed multiple games, dealing with hamstring injuries. They are the Patriots’ primary backups on the perimeter. Both players practiced in full this week, so their absence is a little surprising.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Carlton Davis (neck) is questionable for New England’s Week 8 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: It’s a bit of a surprise questionable because Davis got in three full practice sessions this week. Still, he is coming off a long-term neck injury that has sidelined him most of the year so we understand the Patriots being cautious here. We’d consider Davis on the optimistic side of questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Carlton Davis (neck) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Davis and both of the Patriots’ top perimeter backups, CB Channing Canada (hamstring) and CB Karon Prunty (hamstring) are practicing in full this week. This is very good news. The trio has been sidelined for some time, weakening the Patriots’ secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots ruled out Carlton Davis (neck) for Week 7 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: The Patriots will also be without their top-two backup CBs, Karon Prunty (hamstring) and Channing Canada (hamstring). The Patriots listed S Kevin Byard (chest), S Craig Woodson (shoulder) and LB Christian Elliss (chest) as questionable. This is good news for the Bears’ passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots CB Carlton Davis (neck) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: It was an upgrade from an estimated Monday DNP. Davis has missed Week 2, Week 3, Week 5 and Week 6 to the neck listing so far. Perhaps he’ll try to give it a go on Thursday night, but we’d be surprised if he did better than a questionable tag on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Gonzalez has not played since Week 3, but he returns in time to cover Garrett Wilson in a divisional showdown. Gonzalez primarily lines up on the perimeter, but he has taken 15 combined snaps in the slot and in the box. He could take a few reps on the inside this week, but perimeter CB2 Carlton Davis (neck) is out, so Gonzalez could be asked to simply stay out wide.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez will not play in New England’s Week 5 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: He has not practiced or played since Week 3. Nothing we’ve seen has suggested he’ll be a Saturday IR candidate, but it also wouldn’t necessarily be surprising if that happened. The Pats also ruled out fellow starting CB Carlton Davis (neck) for Week 5, leaving non-existent Raiders receivers with matchup upgrades. (Cody White is about to touch the end zone paint again.)

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Gonzalez and fellow starting perimeter CB Carlton Davis (neck) have missed each of the Patriots’ first two practices this week, putting them on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5 against the Raiders. Las Vegas lines up Brock Bowers as a wide receiver most of the time. Missing both starting coverage defenders would make life tough on the defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Gonzalez has been sidelined with a shoulder injury since last week, missing the Patriots’ Week 4 win over the Bills. Also not practicing were Carlton Davis (neck) and Karon Prunty (hamstring). We’ll see if any of these corners can practice enough to play for Week 5, but Raiders WR Tre Tucker is headed for a good matchup against a banged up Patriots secondary this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-brown/.headline: Ben Brown (knee) will not play in Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-brown/.analysis: Brown recently moved to left guard to fill that hole in the Pats’ lineup. He’s now out for Week 10 and Walter Rouse, his backup, is in the league’s concussion protocol. New England could be severely undermanned in the trenches for their matchup versus Detroit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-brown/.headline: Patriots ruled out Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) for Week 7 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-brown/.analysis: The Patriots will also be without RG Ben Brown (knee). The Bears’ defense is not an elite unit, but losing two starting guards is rough. Backups Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse will start instead. The Patriots listed RT Morgan Moses (foot) as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-brown/.headline: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Ben Brown (knee) are unlikely to play on Thursday night.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-brown/.analysis: Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse stepped in for the two guards towards the end of last week’s offensive line apocalypse and would likely be in line to start in Week 7. Neither Vera-Tucker nor Brown practiced on Monday or Tuesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-brown/.headline: Patriots RG Ben Brown was forced from New England’s Week 6 game against the Jets with a right leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-brown/.analysis: It’s an inconceivable development, as the Pats already lost LG Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and RT Morgan Moses (ankle) earlier on Sunday. Brown’s injury appeared to be very, very serious. Walter Rouse, the Pats’ last healthy reserve OL, will finish the game in Brown’s place.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-brown/.headline: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) will not play in New England’s Week 1 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-brown/.analysis: Henderson did not practice at any point this week and should be considered questionable heading into Week 2’s games. Rhamondre Stevenson will get the bulk of the load against Seattle and should factor into the RB2 equation despite a tough matchup on paper. The Patriots also ruled out Ben Brown (knee), who did not travel with the team to Seattle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-brown/.headline: Patriots signed OL Ben Brown to a two-year extension worth “up to” $6.6 million.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-brown/.analysis: The UDFA center will be a rotational cog along the middle of the Patriots line, probably mostly as a backup, for the two years to come. Brown has started just two games this year, but had a 10-game stretch as a starter in 2024. He qualifies as competent depth.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-brown/.headline: Patriots declared C Ben Brown, RB Terrell Jennings, QB Joe Milton, S Jabrill Peppers, G Tyrese Robinson, and G Sidy Sow inactive for Week 17 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-brown/.analysis: Peppers is out after being listed questionable for Week 17 due to a hamstring injury. Fellow safety Kyle Dugger (ankle/quad) is active. Center Ben Brown (concussion) will also miss Week 17 while Joe Milton serves as the Patriots’ emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-brown/.headline: Bengals sign Ole Miss C Ben Brown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-brown/.analysis: Brown (6’5/310) was a four-year starter in the SEC after a redshirt year, bouncing between guard and center. His 2021 season was cleaved in half with a torn left biceps tendon, an injury that prevented him from testing during the pre-draft process. He’s a broadly-built interior player with strong hands and a stout base. Bull-rushers are stymied when he drops a heavy anchor. Brown is limited athletically, struggling to hit moving targets in the second level. He’s also given issues by the counter moves of quick-twitch defensive tackles. Because of this, Brown is a better fit for a gap-running system than a zone-blocking team. If everything breaks right, Brown could have a career similar to Dan Feeney.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: The Chiefs have been limiting Kelce’s participation on Wednesdays in recent weeks. His return to full participation to begin the week is great to see. Kelce, 37, remains a locked-in TE1 at this point in his career. Treat him accordingly against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 4-of-6 targets for 72 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets, adding a rush for one yard and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce scored on a goal line tush push in the first half. It was a nice little treat for fantasy managers starting the old guy in Week 9. Kelce was second among KC pass catchers in targets, trailing Rashee Rice, who saw seven targets on the day. Kelce remains a reliable floor option in PPR formats. He’s had at least four receptions in five games this season, though his after the catch production has (predictably) cratered. Kelce should be in 12-team league lineups against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce caught 5-of-7 targets for 67 yards, playing through the ankle injury last week against the Broncos, looking slightly hobbled. Kelce was limited to begin the week, but got in two full practices over the last two days. He remains firmly in the TE1 tier for Week 9 against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: This time last week, Kelce was still a limited participant. Today’s upgraded status is a good sign for his overall health. The Chiefs’ stalwart tight end earned eight targets last week despite the ailment. He can be treated as a fantasy football TE1 against the Jets this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce looked slightly hobbled by the ankle issue in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos, but he played through it and never missed a meaningful number of snaps. A limited session today means he should be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Jets. Kelce’s numbers are down over the past month, but he’s still seeing enough work to be considered a low-end TE1, especially against a weak Jets defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 4-of-8 targets for 44 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 7 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: The Chiefs suffered their first defeat of the season as they struggled to move the football against the tenacious Seattle defense. Their offense lacked any downfield threat in the absence of their top two receivers, while Xavier Worthy drew primary coverage. Much of Kelce’s aerial work remains tethered to the short areas of the field in his age-37 season, lacking the burst and YAC ability that once defined his game. Kelce moved into sole possession of the No. 5 spot on the NFL’s all-time receptions list, and achieving such a lofty accomplishment is a testament to his standout career. That said, fantasy managers are sure to be disappointed with his early-season production, as the veteran tight end has surpassed a modest four receptions just once through six games. He gets another difficult matchup on the interior against the swarming Broncos defense in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) is not on Kansas City’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: He’ll be a reliable TE1, even in a tough matchup against Seattle’s defense, as the Chiefs simply don’t have many other Trusted Mahomes Targets healthy for this one. It’s essentially just Kelce and Xavier Worthy healthy of Kansas City’s main targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce should be good to go for the Chiefs’ Week 7 game against the Seahawks. At 37 years old, he does not need to practice fully in order to play, though it would be nice to see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow. If active, he is a locked-in TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce played through an ankle issue in Week 6, catching five passes for 53 yards. Despite not playing at full health, he was still second on the team in targets. Kelce starts out the week as a limited practice participant and it would be a surprise if he misses National Tight End Day this week against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 5-of-6 targets for 53 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce was in and out of the lineup in the first half while dealing with a lingering ankle issue. Though he clearly wasn’t 100 percent, Kelce was second on the team (behind Xavier Worthy) in targets and had a 24-yard catch and run reception in the second half. Kelce, who now has nine catches over his past three games, should see more looks from Patrick Mahomes for as long as Rashee Rice (hamstring) is sidelined. He’ll be a top-15 fantasy play in Week 7 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (knee) is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: For the first time since October 4th, the Chiefs listed Rice only with a knee issue. He had been managing a hamstring strain for more than a month, prior to today, and was typically limited early in the week. This is a great sign for his health moving forward. Rice is a WR2 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice caught 5-of-7 targets for 49 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice, as usual, led the Chiefs in targets. It was an unusually run-heavy game plan for the Chiefs against a Jets defense that showed no real interest in stopping Ken Walker. This performance comes off last week’s 56-yard, one-touchdown outing for Rice, who missed significant time with a hamstring injury. Rice profiles as a high-floor WR2/3 in most formats. He’ll face the run-funnel Falcons defense in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice posted a 7/53/1 receiving line against the Broncos last week. He got in a limited session on Wednesday before upgrading to full on Thursday. He seems to be recovering effectively from his summer knee procedure and in-season hamstring injury. Rice is a borderline WR1/2 for this weekend’s game against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice is on track to face the Jets this weekend, as expected. The Chiefs’ embattled wide receiver also reportedly filed for bankruptcy this week, theoretically adding extra incentive to play well enough for a decent contract when he enters free agency next offseason. Rice is a fantasy football WR2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice returned from a multi-game absence because of the hamstring injury last week and he’s been on the injury report with the knee issue for most of the year. It doesn’t sound like either injury will prevent him from playing in Week 9. The limited session was likely maintenance. Rice led the Chiefs with eight targets in his first game back on Sunday. He’s been the Chiefs’ only consistently productive pass-catcher when healthy. He will be in the WR1 mix when he takes on the Jets this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice caught 7-of-8 targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice was heavily involved early in the game, catching three passes for 26 yards and a score on the Chiefs’ opening drive. His role, however, took a backseat to running back targets in the second half. He caught three balls for 15 yards in the final two quarters combined. Rice briefly appeared to score the game-winning touchdown on the final play of the game, but refs had already blown the play dead because of a false start. Even without the second touchdown, fantasy managers can be confident in Rice as the team’s No. 1 receiver and a low-end WR2 for fantasy purposes going forward. He will sit just inside the WR1 ranks for his Week 9 date with the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Andy Reid said Rashee Rice (hamstring) will play in Week 8.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice will make his return to the game-day roster after missing two games due to a hamstring injury sustained in Week 4, returning as the top option through the air for an offense that has struggled with him off the field. The Chiefs scored a combined 25 points against the Chargers and Seahawks without Rice, the latter of which tied the fewest points scored in quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ career. Fantasy managers can comfortably re-insert Rice into rosters as an upside WR2 against the Broncos, against whom Rice caught both targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) was present at practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: That now marks consecutive days on the practice field for the veteran receiver whom has missed the previous two games. The Chiefs also had their bye in Week 5, giving Rice a full three weeks of recovery, which combines with his recent practice availability to make it likely he returns to face the Broncos. The Chiefs managed just 25 combined points in the two games without Rice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) will practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice, who hasn’t played since Week 4 against the Raiders, would be a big addition to the struggling Kansas City offense if he’s able to practice this week and suit up in Week 8 against the Broncos. Rice had been dominating targets in the Chiefs’ check-down offense, and would likely continue in that role if he can return this weekend. No other pass catcher in the Chiefs offense is a must-play for fantasy purposes for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Chiefs declared WR Rashee Rice, OT Jaylon Moore, QB Garrett Nussmeier, DB Jadon Canady, FB Ben VanSumeren, and DE Jack Pyburn inactive for Week 7 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: No real surprise here after Rice was ruled out on Friday, with the Chiefs once again shorthanded as they look to remain one of two remaining undefeated teams in the league following the loss by the 49ers earlier in the day. Expect Xavier Worthy and Jalen Royals to serve as the top two receivers with Rice inactive and Tyquan Thornton done for the season, with Andrew Armstrong and rookie Cyrus Allen on hand to soak up situational snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.headline: Justin Fields (neck) is practicing in full in Week 10 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.analysis: Fields may have picked up a neck injury while attempting a Tush Push last week. Backup quarterback injuries are not always relevant, but with Patrick Mahomes (elbow) nursing a small injury, this is notable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports J.J. McCarthy and Justin Fields are on the list of quarterback options for the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.analysis: If you have ever thrown a football, get an agent and have them contact the New York Giants. McCarthy and Fields join a list that, per previous reports, already included Gardner Minshew, Mac Jones, and Jimmy Garoppolo. Schefter also named Brandon Allen, who was on the Giants’ roster during training camp, as an option. Jameis Winston will get the start in Week 3, but the journeyman passer looked downright awful in relief of Jaxson Dart last week. The team will be forced to make a move at quarterback if he struggles versus the Titans today. McCarthy would be a true Hail Mary for the G-Men, but he does have a strong tie to the Harbaugh brothers via his time at Michigan.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Steelers QB Mason Rudolph and Chiefs QB Justin Fields are potential trade targets for the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.analysis: Rudolph has been discussed as a potential trade target in past seasons, and the Steelers notably kept four quarterbacks on the roster after cut-down day. Fields, we suppose, could be expendable if the Chiefs really like rookie QB Garrett Nussmeier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.headline: The Athletic’s Mike Jones writes Patrick Mahomes (knee) “has reportedly looked sharp while going through seven-on-seven drills” this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.analysis: Yes, it’s only seven-on-seven drills, but for a player coming back from a late-season ACL tear who is hoping to be ready in time for Week 1, it’s a step in the right direction. The Chiefs remain optimistic that their QB1 will be ready to go at the start of the season, and Mahomes himself has said he’s hopeful he’ll be a full participant in training camp. With nearly two months to go until training camp begins, Mahomes has plenty of time left to continue his recovery before the real work begins. In the event he isn’t ready for Week 1, Justin Fields will likely start in his absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.headline: Patrick Mahomes (knee) on Tuesday participated in Chiefs OTAs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.analysis: ESPN’s Nate Taylor reports Mahomes, recovering from a late-season knee injury, participated “in some form and fashion ... during the Chiefs’ opening OTA practice.” The team released a video of Mahomes throwing a short pass while wearing an enormous brace on his injured left leg. Mahomes, entering his age-31 season, is in a race against the clock to be ready for Week 1 against the Broncos. If Mahomes can’t suit up for the season opener, Justin Fields would likely serve as KC’s starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.headline: Chiefs acquired QB Justin Fields from the Jets in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.analysis: According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, other teams had interest in Fields, but his preference was to go to the Chiefs. It’s an interesting landing spot for the former No. 11 overall pick, who is now slated to join his third team in three seasons. With Patrick Mahomes (knee) still recovering from a torn ACL, Fields will be the presumed QB1 for the Chiefs throughout much of the offseason, and could draw the start in Week 1 if Mahomes is unable to start. Fields struggled during his lone season with the Jets, throwing for 1,259-7-1 in nine games while adding another 71-383-4 on the ground. One of the worst sack avoiders in the NFL, Fields was also sacked on 11.7 percent of his dropbacks and had an abysmal 23.3 percent pressure-to-sack rate. Going from one of the best sack avoiders in the league to one of the worst could present an interesting challenge for Andy Reid and the offense in the early portion of the season. That said, Fields’ rushing ability will also add another element to the offense that can be exploited in Mahomes’ offense. While he would be a risky short-term bit in 1QB leagues, Fields will have some later-round value in 2QB/Superflex leagues if Mahomes misses time. Jets beat writer Zack Rosenblatt reports the Jets are paying “all but $3 million of Fields’ $10 million guaranteed salary,” which saves them more money than what it would have cost to release him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.headline: Jets GM Darren Mougey said “Absolutely, we’ll talk about all those things,” when asked about possibly trading up to the No. 1 overall pick in this year’s draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.analysis: This story comes from ESPN’s Rich Cimini, who also pointed out that Mougey said, “I don’t think (a trade up is) happening.” Much like the Raiders, who currently hold the No. 1 overall pick, the Jets are in QB purgatory. While the Raiders hope Fernando Mendoza will end their years-long struggle at the position, the Jets chances to do the same look bleak at the moment. Justin Fields remains under contract, but the team is likely to move on from him at some point this offseason after a disastrous 2025, and rookie UDFA Brady Cook’s 739-2-7 line didn’t do much to help his case for earning more playing time in 2026. The Jets have some work to do to figure out the quarterback position for next season. Whatever they end up doing, it seems highly unlikely it will involve trading for the 1.01.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.headline: SNY’s Connor Hughes reports the Jets are “open to dealing & listening.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.analysis: The reports comes off the heels of New York swapping Jermaine Johnson for T’Vondre Sweat. Hughes made it clear the Jets aren’t having a fire sale, though it’s hard to see this as anything else. They sent most of their big names packing at the trade deadline last year, with Sauce Gardner, Quinnen Williams, and Michael Carter all traded. At this point, the Jets are running out of players to deal, even if they want to keep making moves. Justin Fields is expected to be released, but a team looking to sign him could guarantee his services by trading for him. Garrett Wilson was also the subject of trade rumors last year, though the Jets just inked him to a long-term deal and didn’t seem interested in moving him at the deadline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.headline: The Athletic’s Zack Rosenblatt believes the Jets could release Justin Fields.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.analysis: Fields would incur a $22 million dead cap hit and save the Jets only $1 million against the cap if released, and yet Rosenblatt still believes that is a likely scenario because the Jets are not lacking for cap space. Fields would likely find backup work somewhere if released, but the Jets runout appears likely to have been his final chance to cut it as a starter in the NFL. Rosenblatt also notes that it’s unlikely any team would trade for Fields at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jets QB Justin Fields declined an invitation to the 2025 Pro Bowl.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-fie.analysis: Fields reportedly declined the invitation to focus on his offseason training as he continues his bid to return as a franchise quarterback after a tumultuous beginning to his career. Fields enters 2026 in the final year of a two-year deal signed with the Jets prior to the 2025 regular season but appears to be on the outs with the franchise, potentially auditioning for a backup gig somewhere else. The dual threat quarterback has started 53 games during a five-year NFL career while playing for three different franchises in the three previous seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (quad) is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright missed last week with the quad issue. Kaytron Allen played through a quad issue of his own, though he only saw one carry. Allen practiced in full today as well. Wright will return to a distant RB2 role for Week 10. He is not on the fantasy radar right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Dolphins declared RB Jaylen Wright, WR Jalen Tolbert, TE Justin Joly, G Christian Haynes, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick, CB Marcellas Dial Jr., and CB Reese Taylor inactive for Week 9 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Both Wright and Kaytron Allen were questionable because of quad injuries. Allen is active and will serve as Ollie Gordon’s backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jaylen Wright (quad) will not play in Week 9 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright had been backing up Ollie Gordon before going down with the quad injury. Kaytron Allen is the next man up for RB2 duties, though he’s also dealing with a quad issue. Needless to say, we’re expecting a large workload for Gordon this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (quad) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright and Dolphins RB3 Kaytron Allen (quad) are both questionable in this one, though Allen upgraded to full participation on Friday while Wright remained limited. Wright is barely worthy of stashing in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (quad) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright is on track to be available for the Dolphins’ Week 9 game against the Lions, although he is mostly functioning as an infrequently used backup rusher while also serving as the team’s top returner. He is a mid-tier bench stash at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (quad) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Dolphins RB3 Kaytron Allen (quad) was limited. At some point, Allen might get a chance to overtake Wright for the No. 2 role, though Wright remains a capable special teams contributor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright rushed two times for five yards in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright failed to catch his lone target and returned five kicks for 142 yards. Wright is just a bench stash at this point, with Ollie Gordon operating in a featured offensive role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot/quad) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright is a mediocre bench stash at this point, with Ollie Gordon playing well in the lead role. Wright does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats, though he may be able to slightly improve his efficiency if his health continues to improve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright rushed six times for eight yards in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright managed just six touches, even with Miami running the ball 41 times today. Wright is the only running back seeing work outside of Ollie Gordon, but the latter is pushing for workhorse status, leaving Wright without much to do. He is somewhere well beyond the RB4 ranks for his Week 8 matchup with New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) will play in Week 7 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright has rushed 14 times for 28 scoreless yards this season and has yet to receive a target in the four games he has appeared in. Fellow running back Ollie Gordon has emerged as the unquestioned RB1 for the Dolphins since the team lost De’Von Achane (knee) in Week 3. Wright is well off the fantasy radar at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings missed Week 9 against the Bills with the calf issue and looks likely to sit for at least one more game. Myles Price ran ahead of Tai Felton last week, putting him in line for another round of No. 3 duties in Week 10. He is not on the fantasy radar despite the uptick in snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Vikings ruled out Jauan Jennings (calf) for Week 9 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: The fantasy implications of Jennings’ absence are negligible, with the bigger boost to the passing offense being the absence of Kyler Murray, who is looking at a multi-game absence with a Grade 2 hamstring injury. Tai Felton appears to be in line for additional run as the team’s WR3, although he is not a recommended streaming option with both Jefferson and Jordan Addison healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) was not seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings was limited yesterday, which could mean he injured his calf during the Vikings’ Thursday practice. If this is the case, he is probably unlikely to suit up for his team’s Monday Night Football game against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings has been the subject of trade rumors. Since is able to practice, even in a limited capacity, this injury is unlikely to alter a potential suitor’s interest. Regardless, Jennings is not on the FLEX radar this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams must find a way to trade for a wide receiver before the November 10th deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: The Rams’ resources are thin. They already traded away their 2027 first- and second-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. They also have just $8,000 in 2026 salary cap space, so restructuring the potential new add’s deal would be required. Atkins believes the Rams should consider Josh Downs as the top option due to his ability to beat man coverage and contribute as a returner. Other options, according to Atkins, include Calvin Ridley, Keenan Allen and Jauan Jennings, “for the likely cost of a Day 3 pick.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter named Calvin Ridley as a potential trade candidate.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Schefter threw out several names, many of whom have already been bandied about as trade candidates. Among the lesser-discussed options, he included Jerry Jeudy and Jauan Jennings in addition to Ridley. All three are veteran wideouts who have simply disappeared in the current iterations of their respective offenses. Even with new landing spots in the cards for the trio, none of them are worth holding onto in standard fantasy leagues. Ridley has five catches for 81 yards this year. He is expected to play through his hip injury today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Juan Jennings caught 2-of-3 targets for 34 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings caught a 20-yard pass, his longest reception of the season. He was targeted three times, nearly catching a long touchdown from Kyler Murray in the second quarter, but failing to haul it in. Jennings is outside of the top-three pass-catching options for the Vikings and is irrelevant for fantasy purposes in this role. Fantasy managers should keep an eye on him in case he is traded, but Jennings does not need to be in fantasy lineups heading in to Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jauan Jennings “would be a name for me to keep an eye on” for the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings has been a major disappointment in Minnesota, falling behind Tai Felton on the depth chart. A small stakes trade could make sense for the 49ers, who are down to hoping Brandin Cooks can provide for Brock Purdy in a major rash of injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Tai Felton caught 2-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jordan Addison missed this game with an ankle injury and the Vikings deployed Felton as their WR2 over Jauan Jennings. Jennings ran fewer routes and failed to catch his only target. Felton wasn’t awfully productive either, but it’s good to see the former third-round pick picking up more work in his second season. He will return to a rotational role, assuming Addison is cleared to play after the Vikings’ Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings caught 1-of-1 targets for eight yards in the Vikings’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings simply isn’t meaningfully involved in the Vikings’ game plan. That is unlikely to change in Week 5 against the Saints, especially with the Vikings’ offensive line getting banged up in Week 4. Jennings could be asked to contribute more as a run blocker next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin has missed three weeks with the rib issue. He may need to be upgraded to a full practice before being cleared to return to action. Even if he is back this week, George Pickens appears to be healthy and Ryan Flournoy is locked in as the team’s WR3, so there isn’t any fantasy value to be had here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was ruled out for Week 9 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: This will be a third-straight missed game for Turpin as he battles his rib issue. The 30-year-old has just seven targets on the season, but will again be missed by Dallas in the return game. Malachi Lawrence has also been ruled out by the Cowboys due to his ankle injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Week 8 will mark the second consecutive absence for the veteran kick returner, with little-to-no impact on the offensive pieces around him considering he has played more than 12 offensive snaps only once all season. Fantasy managers are more interested in the potential status of George Pickens, who is listed as questionable. If Pickens can’t go, Ryan Flournoy could see a slight uptick in opportunities on the perimeter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Pickens played through a minor shoulder injury last week, but the hamstring designation is new. He was still a limited practice participant, indicating neither injury should be an issue for his Week 8 status. Meanwhile, WR/KR KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was an estimated DNP in practice after not playing last week. The Cowboys may be missing Turpin again as a kick returner and gadget player on offense, but Pickens should still be the WR2 for Sunday against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: Cowboys ruled out KaVontae Turpin (ribs) for Week 7 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin’s absence will be felt most on special teams, with the team now forced to find a replacement on punt and kick returns. Otherwise, there is almost zero fantasy impact as the team’s WR4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) is questionable to return to Week 6 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin departed before the first offensive play run from scrimmage after sustaining a ribs injury on the opening kickoff. He was taken to the locker room for x-rays and is listed as questionable to return by the team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVonte Turpin failed to haul in his only target in Week 18.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin ends the season with 26 catches on 38 targets for 396 yards and two touchdowns. He also added 16 carries for 82 rushing yards, but his primary value was as a kick returner. On the season, he had 69 kick returns for 1,814 yards, which leads the league as of the end of this game. That will be his primary role in 2026 as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin caught his only target for an 86-yard touchdown in the Cowboy’s Week 17 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: It took all of one target for Turpin to make his mark felt in the win as he broke free of primary coverage and split the safeties deep down the middle for an 86-yard, catch-and-run score. Turpin continues to play behind Jalen Tolbert but his flashy touchdown demonstrates his big play ability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: Cowboys listed WR KaVontae Turpin (shoulder) as a full participant on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin played through the same shoulder injury in Week 13’s win over the Chiefs. The Cowboys’ special teams ace has posted a meager 19-260-1 receiving line this season and isn’t on the fantasy radar for Week 14 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: George Pickens (knee/calf) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 13 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: KaVontae Turpin was also cleared to play. Pickens was held out of practice on Monday but returned for a limited session on Tuesday. He was full-go today before being removed from the injury report entirely. Pickens has worked himself into a weekly WR1 ranking and is even threatening to overtake CeeDee Lamb. Both he and Lamb are elite fantasy options for Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-trav.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Jalen Travis (knee) is expected to miss 2-4 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-trav.analysis: A fourth-round pick in 2025, Travis made four starts as a rookie and took over as the team’s starting right tackle this year. He started all nine games to open the season. Luke Tenuta will take his place in the lineup for a few weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-trav.headline: Colts selected Iowa State OT Jalen Travis with the No. 127 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-trav.analysis: After four years and two second-team All-Ivy League selections at Princeton, Travis (6'7/339) transferred to Iowa State and started 11 games at left tackle in 2024. The athletic profile is very impressive. Travis has 34 7/8th-inch arms, and finished in the 97th percentile at the NFL combine with a 35-inch vertical jump. It feels almost cliche to say that the 6-foot-7 tackle had a problem getting low in his blocks, but … the 6-foot-7 tackle had a problem getting low on his blocks. Travis was a stellar pass protector for the Cyclones, allowing just one sack and nine hurries in 475 pass pro snaps per PFF. He could be a viable swing tackle prospect while Indy’s coaches take a crack at trying to help him stay anchored in the run game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports that the Rams are “hopeful” that Davante Adams (hamstring) will return for Week 13 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Over the next three weeks, the Rams face the Cardinals, go on bye and then face the Packers. While his potential return ahead of the fantasy football playoffs is helpful, we still have a long way to go before he returns, and even then, his status for Week 13 is still uncertain. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and CJ Daniels appear to be in line for 11 personnel duties at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Davante Adams (hamstring) successfully underwent surgery, and his return timeline is “probably closer” to the shorter end of the expected 6-10 week timeline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: If Adams hit the absolute soonest return date, week-wise, he theoretically could face the Chiefs in Week 13, but that game takes place on Thursday night. We suspect facing the 49ers in Week 14 is more likely, though nothing is guaranteed for a 33-year-old player. Adams should be stashed in injured reserve spots, where possible. He makes for a tough cut in leagues without them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said the team is still determining “the best time” to schedule Davante Adams’ (hamstring) “cleanup” procedure.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Surgeries are sometimes delayed to help reduce swelling. Occasionally, new information is gathered during this time and/or during the surgery. Adams is currently expected to be sidelined for 6-10 weeks. Perhaps the wide return-to-play timeline is due to the fact that the surgeon has not yet fully assessed the injury. We tentatively expect the team to share an updated recovery timeline once Adams undergoes the procedure on his ruptured hamstring tendon. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said the Rams have not had discussions about bringing in a receiver with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined for 6-10 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Earlier today, ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported that the Rams “will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver.” Obviously, McVay doesn’t want to tip off other wide receiver-needy NFL teams about their potential entrance into the trade market, and he has no reason to be honest with us. Acquiring a new wide receiver makes sense, and the Rams were aggressive players in the trade market last offseason. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports that the Rams “will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams is set to undergo a procedure after rupturing his hamstring tendon in Week 6 against the Cardinals. He will be sidelined for 6-10 weeks. The Rams were already very thin at wide receiver and Puka Nacua has spent multiple weeks on the injury report as well. Acquiring a capable wide receiver makes sense, but as Graziano mentions, the Rams have already traded away a lot of their draft capital. Thus far, GM Les Snead has already given up their 2027 first- and third-round picks, and their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. He notes that Rams QB Stetson Bennett played for Browns coach Todd Monken in college. Perhaps Monken would be interested in a reunion.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Davante Adams (hamstring) will miss 6-10 weeks with a ruptured tendon.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams had a non-contact injury at the end of Week 6’s loss to the Cardinals and unfortunately is as serious as it appeared. He’ll likely be placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 7. His absence will further focus targets on Puka Nacua and likely elevate Konata Mumpfield into a bigger role. Adams had put together a 30/480/4 line in his first six games of the season. Adams will reportedly have surgery to “clean” out the tendon, per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, in hopes he can return around the team’s bye week, which is scheduled for Week 11. It’s a major blow for a Rams team that is already reeling at 2-4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams 3-of-4 targets for 39 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams appeared to injure his left knee while running a route in the red zone on the Rams’ final possession. He cut, turned upfield and quickly began limping his way to the back of the end zone, removing himself from the play while grabbing at the inside of his left knee. He subbed himself out after that. No word on his status, but we expect an update soon. Prior to that, the Cardinals’ pass rush made life tough on the Rams’ passing attack. Adams caught his first pass a minute and a half into the second quarter. Stafford was looking his way in the end zone later on the same drive, but Josh Sweat got to him for the strip-sack.
