Adams banked 16-yard receptions on the sixth and seventh drives, impressively getting wide open via a downfield out route on the second one. If Adams escaped with a minor injury, he would be a WR2 against the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams caught 5-of-7 targets for 51 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams cashed in on a corner fade from four yards out in the second quarter and ran a beautiful route on a double move slant from five yards out for his second score in the fourth quarter, proving that he remains an elite red zone weapon for an offense that has now attempted 51 or more passes in three straight games. Adams is back to modest target rates following the Week 4 return of Puka Nacua but remains a weekly WR2 due to his red zone acumen, which remains true ahead of a much more forgiving matchup against the Cardinals in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams caught 4-of-9 targets for 32 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams was the victim of a bad Matthew Stafford ball or two in rainy Philadelphia conditions, but he sadly immediately reverted to clear No. 2 wideout status with Puka Nacua back in the lineup. Nacua went off for 9/125. Adams now has seven catches for 58 scoreless yards in two games with Nacua in the lineup compared to 15/332/2 in two games without. Hopefully that trend normalizes a bit for a potential Week 5 shootout with the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams caught 7-of-13 targets for 137 yards in the Rams’ Week 3 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams’ 137 yards combine with the 195 yards he erupted for in Week 2 to set a new high in receiving yards in consecutive games during his remarkable career. Even more stunning was the fact that he did so against one of the top corners in the league in Pat Surtain, who shadowed Adams for all but a handful of his routes, proving his ability to get open against top competition even in the later stages of his career. Puka Nacua missed both Week 2 and Week 3 and his injury timeline remains convoluted, at best. Adams will remains a top-tier WR1 should Nacua miss more time, and would be solid WR2 should Nacua return for a Week 4 meeting with the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck will start for the Cardinals in Week 10 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: With Jacoby Brissett in Baltimore and Gardner Minshew out because of a UCL injury, the Cardinals are already down to their third-string quarterback. It was almost a given that Beck would start at some point this year, though we imagine head coach Matt LaFleur didn’t think it would be this soon. Beck played well in his lone preseason appearance, throwing for 188 yards and a score. While he’s not much of a streaming option this week, he should be good enough to keep Trey McBride at the top of the TE1 ranks, especially with Michael Wilson done for the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Cardinals fear Gardner Minshew may have suffered a torn UCL in Week 9’s loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: If this proves to be the case, then Minshew played the entire second half with the injury, gutting things out for the Cardinals against a top-notch Seahawks defense. Minshew will undergo more tests to confirm the severity of his injury, but it now looks as if the Cardinals will be turning things over to rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who threw for 188 yards and one touchdown in his lone preseason game. Beck could be in for a rough few weeks, and the Cardinals’ receiving corps looks suddenly depleted with Marvin Harrison Jr. now on the Texans and Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (leg) both done for the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Gardner Minshew (elbow) could miss Week 10’s game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Minshew took a hard hit to his right elbow/arm in Sunday’s loss to the Seahawks and is now undergoing tests to determine the severity of his injury. He managed to play through the game, but if he is unable to go in Week 10 against the Rams, rookie Carson Beck would be in line to make his first career start. Minshew threw for 166 scoreless yards against a stout Seahawks defense, but led a comeback victory in just one half of play against the Cowboys the previous week. With recent reports of Michael Wilson (neck) being lost for the season, both Minshew and Beck would be best left on waivers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said he did not consider benching Gardner Minshew for Carson Beck at any point in Arizona’s Week 9 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: We don’t believe him. But it really doesn’t matter because Beck will get his chance at some point in the coming weeks. The Cardinals’ rookie looked good in the preseason Hall of Fame game, though it is unclear whether he can do enough to warrant QB2 treatment as a pure pocket passer. The Cardinals’ schedule softens after matchups against the Rams and Chiefs over the next two weeks. Beck should have a chance to play in Week 12 against the Commanders, if not sooner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck (back) will be limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: The Cardinals’ No. 3 quarterback has been dealing with back spasms in recent weeks, likely delaying his rookie season debut. Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Beck threw the ball well on Tuesday. Today, they will see how things go. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck left Thursday’s practice with back spasms and was listed as a DNP. Head coach Mike LaFleur said he was not overly concerned about the injury and that he doesn’t believe it will be anything long-term. Beck’s injury shouldn’t change his Week 7 availability, as he has been the emergency QB3 all season. He was officially listed as questionable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck appeared on the injury report last Friday, as a limited participant. He remained limited on Wednesday and was downgraded today. Beat reporters saw him at practice briefly, but he ended up going inside with a trainer. This could help preserve Jacoby Brissett’s job security. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: ArizonaCardinals.com’s Darren Urban believes Carson Beck won’t start in the “immediate future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Cardinals fans appear to be pining for the team to bench Jacoby Brissett and start the rookie in the coming weeks as another season circles the drain for Arizona. Beck so far has been the Cards’ emergency third quarterback. Urban said there remains a “chance Beck is made the backup this week or next and allow him to come on in relief if the situation presents itself. I don’t see Beck starting in the immediate future, but it does feel his time grows closer, and if the offense continues to sputter, that would be understandable.” Brissett this season ranks 15th in passing yards. He’s thrown nine touchdowns to five interceptions and ranks 30th out of 37 qualifying QBs in adjusted yards per attempt. He won’t be a viable fantasy play this week against a tough Rams coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals declared QB Carson Beck, S Dadrion Taylor-Demerson, OL Josh Fryar, DL Andrew Billings, and WR Reggie Virgil inactive for Week 3 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck continues to be the Cardinals’ third quarterback and will be a gameday inactive for Week 3 behind Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew. Dadrion “Rabbit” Taylor-Demerson (back) was scratched on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Team reporter Darren Urban reports that Cardinals QB Carson Beck (ribs) is unlikely to play in Friday’s preseason game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: This is unfortunate. Beck looked great before injuring his ribs in the Hall of Fame game. Per Urban, Beck has been a very limited participant in practice ever since, which is costing him valuable reps. Only starting QB Jacoby Brissett will take first-team practice reps once the regular season begins. Beck practiced the week after the injury, “struggling much of the time,” and has sat out since then. The Cardinals have an extremely difficult schedule, so a rough record could bring Beck back onto the field at some point this year. Ideally, he would have spent all of August refining his play, though. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team re-draft leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Quentin Nelson (knee) could play in Week 12 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Macdonald also said that Nelson is “back” with the team this week. It’s unclear whether he means Nelson has simply returned to the facility to participate in team meetings, or if he actually has a chance to practice, though we assume Nelson will not practice until after the Seahawks’ Week 11 bye. Nelson underwent a procedure to remove cartilage fragments from his knee last week. If he indeed returns in Week 12, the surgery will have only cost him two games. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that “the plan” is for Quenton Nelson to avoid injured reserve after undergoing a procedure to remove cartilage fragments from his knee.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: If the Seahawks were to place Nelson on short-term injured reserve, he would be required to miss at least four games. The Seahawks face the Cardinals this week, the Raiders next and then go on bye. Nelson could have a chance to play in Week 12 against the 49ers. His availability that week will likely just come down to how the recovery is going. His loss is unfortunate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Quenton Nelson (knee) will have a minor procedure and is week-to-week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Apparently, Nelson was dealing with this knee issue when Seattle acquired for him, and he recently “aggravated it to some degree.” FOX 59’s Mike Chappell notes that Nelson was never listed on the Colts’ injury report this season. This is a bummer for the Seahawks, who acquired Nelson as a win-now move. Nelson will not play in Week 9 against the Cardinals, and the Seahawks also ruled out LT Charles Cross (ankle), DT Leonard Williams (stinger) and LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Shaheed seems likely to miss another week, though he could technically still turn things around tomorrow. Seahawks LT Charles Cross (ankle) also remains sidelined on Thursday, and LG Quenton Nelson (knee) was downgraded to a non-participant. Hopefully, Nelson’s absence is precautionary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Seahawks acquired Quenton Nelson from the Colts in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: With the Colts’ season all but over, the team could trade away a series of key player as they look toward a total tear down/rebuild scenario following the 2026 season. That includes Nelson, an eight-time Pro Bowler who now has a chance to compete for a title now that he’s out of Indianapolis. Nelson will join a Seattle offensive line that ranks 21st in pass blocking win rate and 27th in run blocking win rate. His addition should be a boon for Sam Darnold and the Seahawks’ pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Packers, Vikings, Seahawks, and Broncos are “among the teams interested” in trading for Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: As Rap notes, the Colts view Taylor as a pillar of the franchise. Even if they are forced to rebuild the roster, they could want him there as the centerpiece of the next iteration of the offense. On the other hand, Taylor will turn 28 at the end of the season and the Colts face a lengthy teardown process without their 2027 first-round selection. Taylor will likely be past his prime by the time they are competitive again. Rapoport also named DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson as potential trade candidates if the Colts’ struggles continue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder listed QuentonNelson and DeForest Buckner as potential trade options for the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Holder writes that “trade speculation is swirling” around Buckner and notes that Nelson is in the final year of his deal, potentially providing motivation for the Colts to move him. Neither player had much to say when asked about a potential trade, but per Holder, “it is widely expected that significant organizational changes might be coming after the eventual hire of a new general manager.” Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Jonathan Taylor said he would “definitely love to be a Colt for life,” as he enters the final year of his contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Taylor, 27, has totaled more than 320 offensive touches in each of the last two seasons. His current $14 million annual salary makes him the seventh-highest-paid running back in the league. Taylor has set multiple Colts records, operating as the centerpiece of Indianapolis’ offense for years. FOX 59’s Mike Chappell writes that it is “uncertain whether there’s a mutual desire to keep Taylor in Indy beyond 2025.” Multiple Colts stars, including DTs DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart, OG Quenton Nelson and WR Josh Downs, are also entering the final year of their deal. Chappell believes owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon “might believe it’s more prudent to allow the upcoming season to run its course rather than reinvest in lucrative contracts.” Time will tell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts LG Quenton Nelson returned to Week 2 against the Broncos after suffering an apparent leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson was the downfield blocker on a delayed Tyler Warren screen pass when he was hurt. Broncos S Talanoa Hufanga went low on Nelson, which resulted in Nelson driving his quad-knee area into the diving Hufanga. Nelson immediately grabbed just above his knee as he went down. He then limped off the field under his own power and was seen talking to teammates with his helmet on, along the sideline. He returned on the following drive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts LG Quenton Nelson (ankle) is questionable for Week 17 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson was able to practice on Friday, though only in a limited capacity. He appears to be on the right side of questionable but will need to make it through pre-game warmups before being cleared. Tanor Bortolini would likely take his spot in the lineup if he is ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Michael Wilson’s prognosis is “really good for the future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson suffered a fracture in his neck on the fourth play of Week 9. He somehow finished the game but was placed on season-ending injured reserve after testing revealed the full extent of the injury. The good news is that this doesn’t sound like it will change the outlook of his career. He will be back next season as the Cardinals’ top wideout unless they make a big splash at his position in the offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Cardinals WR Michael Wilson suffered a neck injury in Week 9’s loss to the Seahawks, ending his season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: It’s a tough and unexpected loss for the Cardinals, and Wilson, who was not reported to have suffered any injury after the game. Wilson was on track for another solid season after breaking out for 76-1,006-7 last season. He was averaging a solid 9.8 targets per game this season, and never saw fewer than seven targets in any game. Wilson signed a three-year, $75 million contract extension earlier this offseason and will hopefully recover in time to be back for the start of training camp next season. Now without the top three receivers they opened the season with, the Cardinals will likely lean on the trio of Harrison Wallace III, Reggie Virgil, and Simi Fehoko for the remainder of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson caught 6-of-7 targets for 60 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 9 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: The lone Gardner Minshew incompletion directed toward Wilson was an end zone target late in the fourth quarter, a miss that would have salvaged a usable fantasy outing for the veteran receiver. Wilson was responsible for nearly one third of the total offensive output from a Cardinals offense that was held to under 200 yards by the stingy Seattle defense, finishing second on the team in targets behind the eight of tight end Trey McBride. He remains an upside WR2 ahead of another difficult test against the Rams in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson (NIR-rest/ribs) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson caught 8-of-15 targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 8 win over the Cowboys while playing through a pair of broken ribs. The Cardinals kept him limited all week. He should be good to go for WR2 duties against the Seahawks’ elite defense this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson (NIR-rest/ribs) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson will face the Seahawks this weekend, barring a setback. It’s a tough matchup, but Wilson’s target volume keeps him worth of remaining in starting lineups. Wilson showed decent chemistry with Gardner Minshew last week, which was nice to see, now that Jacoby Brissett is headed to the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson said he is playing with two broken ribs after the Cardinals’ Week 8 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson started the week off by practicing in a non-contact jersey. Now we know why. Wilson told reporters post-game that the Cardinals’ organization has changed his life, and he doesn’t believe in “taking, taking, taking,” adding that if he “can muster up the strength to go play, even at 60 percent,” he’s going to. Wilson will be in the WR3 ranks against the Seahawks next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson caught 8-of-15 targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s Week 8 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: He added a key 17-yard end around in overtime to help set up the go-ahead field goal. Wilson got off to an obscenely slow start with Jacoby Brissett, notching all but 25 of these yards as Minshew Mania took over in the second half. Wilson managed several back shoulder balls and almost caught another of his targets down to the two-yard line before a successful challenge revealed he did not hold on to the ball. It’s unclear how much better Minshew will actually make things, but the Cardinals might as well ride the hot hand. Wilson’s role should have him in the WR3 ranks even if the matchup won’t be this good again in Week 9 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Michael Wilson (ribs) is “good to go” for Arizona’s Week 8 game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: He’ll get cleared off Arizona’s injury report later today. Wilson is in a nice spot in one of the games with the highest over/under total on the slate against Dallas, but may run into Joey Porter Jr. shadow coverage. Still, even with how things have trended of late, this feels like a spot where Wilson has to be started in the majority of leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson (ribs) was limited in practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: It was the second consecutive day in which Wilson practiced with a yellow non-contact jersey after stating Wednesday that the team was simply being overly cautious. Wilson appears on track to maintain a high-volume role in the pass-heavy Cardinals offense in Week 8 against the Cowboys, where he will be a borderline WR1, if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson (ribs) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson was on the practice field wearing a non-contact jersey on Wednesday. He is dealing with a rib injury, presumably suffered in the Cardinals’ Week 7 loss to the Broncos. He will be limited as long as he wears the non-contact jersey and ideally finishes the week without it in order to play in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Kendrick Bourne suddenly becomes the WR1 if Wilson cannot go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Steelers did not open Michael Pittman’s (foot) 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: This is unfortunate, but it likely benefits Germie Bernard in the short term. Pittman told reporters that he had hoped to return following the Steelers’ Week 9 bye. The team will likely choose to ramp him up for at least one week once they open his 21-day practice window. Doing so tomorrow or Friday seems unlikely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) said he hopes to return after the Steelers’ Week 9 bye week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman has been on injured reserve since October 10th, and began running last week. While the veteran receiver said he hopes to return after the Steelers’ bye week, he also said that there’s “no time frame” for his return. Pittman’s foot injury was a reaggravation of a previous injury he had earlier in the season, so it wouldn’t be surprising if the Steelers exercised extreme caution to ensure it doesn’t flare up again when he returns. Pittman’s first season in Pittsburgh has been disappointing, to say the least. He has appeared in just three games and has totaled seven receptions for 89 scoreless yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Steelers placed WR Michael Pittman (foot) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman aggravated the foot injury that cost him Week 2 last week and will now miss four games, at minimum, while on injured reserve. Roman Wilson appears to be the primary beneficiary of Pittman’s absence and has seen six targets in each game this season while mostly playing a situational role. Wilson is a priority waiver addition over rookie Germie Bernard.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Michael Pittman re-aggravated his foot injury and will miss multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: McCarthy told reporters the team is evaluating Pittman’s roster spot, meaning they could place him on injured reserve. He would miss at least four weeks while on IR. Pittman tried to play through the foot injury but only made it two weeks before aggravating the issue. He was spotted using a scooter to support his foot in the locker room on Wednesday. We suspect the Steelers will place him on IR to give Pittman enough time to fully recover. Germie Bernard will now operate as the team’s permanent WR3, with Roman Wilson taking on more work as the clear No. 2 receiver. Both players will be decent FLEX options for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reports that Michael Pittman (foot) was in “the locker room with his left foot propped up on a scooter.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman has been playing through a foot injury this season and was seen participating in team stretches earlier today. Although the scooter use is alarming, this is likely just load management. Pittman is a boom-bust FLEX against the Colts this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Michael Pittman caught 2-of-4 targets for 15 yards in the Steelers’ Week 4 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: That makes two consecutive games with two receptions for the veteran X receiver, who continues to be handily outplayed by teammate Roman Wilson. Pittman brings his season total in receptions to seven after missing Week 2 with injury and remains largely confined to the short areas of the field. The Steelers made good on their promise to increase their 12-personnel utilization against the Browns, and it was Pittman who saw his route participation suffer the most. Pittman is quickly bordering drop candidate territory ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Michael Pittman caught 2-of-5 targets for 16 yards in the Steelers’ Week 3 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman was back in action after missing Week 2’s game with a foot injury. Despite being on the field for 28 routes, the veteran receiver struggled to make much of an impact, making two eight-yard receptions on back-to-back drives before fading into the distance. Pittman has caught 5-of-8 targets for 74 scoreless yards this season and shouldn’t be counted on for Week 4’s game against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Michael Pittman (foot) is active for Week 3 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: It was reported earlier on Sunday that Pittman was expected to suit up, so this isn’t much of a surprise. Despite being ready to go, Pittman will be hard to trust this week against a much-improved Bengals defense. He caught just three passes for 58 yards on three targets in his lone game this season and his best left on fantasy benches in most cases.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Michael Pittman (foot) is expected to play in Week 3 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman missed last week’s game with the foot issue and was limited in practice throughout this week. He was given a questionable designation on Friday. Pittman will return as the No. 2 receiver on a struggling offense, and he’s likely not back to full strength. Fantasy managers should keep him on the bench for at least one more game before getting him back into lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Michael Pittman (foot) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 3 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: He was limited in practice all three days this week with a foot injury that kept him out of Week 2. We’d say Pittman is on the optimistic side of questionable based on his participation status. If he’s out again, it would likely be Germie Bernard picking up the slack, as he did in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-gil.headline: Patriots designated Reggie Gilliam (knee) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-gil.analysis: Gilliam’s return allows the Patriots to increase their 21 and 22 personnel usage. This in turn should help out the Patriots’ run game, while also reducing target competition for the established skill position players. Gilliam is not fantasy-relevant on his own, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-gil.headline: Patriots place Mack Hollins on injured reserve with a calf injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-gil.analysis: The Patriots snuck Hollins onto the injured reserve list over the weekend. He will be eligible to return after sitting out for four games. The Patriots also placed FB Reggie Gilliam on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-gil.headline: Patriots agreed to terms with FB Reggie Gilliam, formerly of the Bills, on a three-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-gil.analysis: Per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, the deal is worth up to $12 million and includes $6 million fully guaranteed. Jack Westover, a former tight end, handled fullback duties for New England last year. Pro Football Focus graded Gilliam as their No. 1 back in pass protection last year. He also earned a top-10 mark in run-blocking. Though the fullback is a dying breed, Gilliam will be a solid upgrade for the Pats this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-gil.headline: Bills re-signed FB Reggie Gilliam to a one-year, $2 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-gil.analysis: Gilliam is a quality special teams player who sees most of his time on kick coverage rather than on offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-gil.headline: Bills signed FB Reggie Gilliam to a two-year extension worth “up to” $5.2 million.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-gil.analysis: Gilliam played 156 snaps last season, mostly as a fullback, and graded out as a positive run and pass blocker per PFF’s charting data. Gilliam, also a core special teams player for Buffalo, is now under contract through the 2024 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-gil.headline: Toledo senior TE Reggie Gilliam hopes to have an expanded role in the passing game this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-gil.analysis: Gilliam (6'1/255) has been a standout on special teams for the Rockets, blocking a total of six kicks the last two seasons (four in 2018). A second team all-MAC selection at tight end, that honor had more to do with his blocking and special teams prowess than it did his production as a pass catcher (six catches for 71 yards, 3 TDs). Gilliam could see more passes come his way this fall, as the Rockets have to account for the loss of wide receivers Cody Thompson, Diontae Johnson, and Jon’Vea Johnson. “I think my passing game will be expanded a lot this year,” Gilliam said. “A lot of our big receivers like Cody and Jon’Vea and Diontae are gone, so we need someone else to step up and I think I can fill that role.” Tight ends Drew Rosi and Jamal Turner are also in line to see an increase in opportunities this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Vikings GM Nolan Teasley said there is “always potential” for Kirk Cousins to remain in Minnesota beyond 2026, but acquiring him was about this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: It seems that the Vikings just love to move on from quarterbacks who successfully adapt to their system. It is fair to wonder how much Cousins, 38, has left in the tank, but the fact that Teasley actually said this out loud is a little perplexing. At worst, Cousins should be able to serve as a mentor for whichever young quarterback coach Kevin O’Connell decides he wants to whisper to in 2027. Cousins is currently playing on a one-year, $11.3 million contract and could likely be retained on a one- or two-year deal at a similar value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Vikings acquired QB Kirk Cousins from the Raiders for a 2027 third-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: And where did that bring you? Back to me. Cousins will likely take over as Minnesota’s starting quarterback in the near future, if not immediately. When that happens, Kyler Murray will head back to the bench for a second straight season — he’s droppable in most leagues at this point. Fernando Mendoza will take over as starting quarterback for the Raiders. Mendoza is best approached cautiously at this point in fantasy leagues. Cousins’ value likely remains stagnant — Klint Kubiak was already getting quite a bit out of him — but he provides the Vikings with a better floor at quarterback than what they were getting so it’s obvious after watching Carson Wentz play last night why this is happening.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Kirk Cousins is a “prime trade candidate” for the Vikings ahead of today’s trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: This would, of course, have multiple fantasy impacts. Fernando Mendoza would take over as Las Vegas’ starting quarterback if Cousins were traded, and Kyler Murray would likely take a backseat to Cousins sooner rather than later in Minnesota. We unfortunately must recommend that you stay tuned for the next couple of hours. Click the ads, too.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 22-of-32 attempts for 216 yards, one touchdown, and three interceptions in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: The statuesque Cousins was under duress from start to finish, often falling back as he threw the ball into tight windows. That led to three picks, which should have been four or five picks if 49ers defenders had been a little more sure handed. As usual, Cousins targeted Brock Bowers relentlessly, once again connecting with the superstar tight end for a touchdown. He nearly threw a second touchdown to Bowers in the second half. Cousins also had a touchdown to Michael Mayer called back on an offensive pass interference penalty. This was only Cousins’ second game of the year with less than two TD passes. Cousins will be a superflex option in Week 10 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 19-of-26 passes for 247 yards and three touchdowns in the Raiders’ 38-33, Week 8 win over the Jets, adding a rushing score.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: With the Fernando Mendoza chatter increasing as the Raiders were mired in a four-game losing streak, Cousins responded with his fourth three-touchdown effort through the air, albeit his first since Week 3. Cousins has now provided multiple scores in 7-of-8 starts, and is up to 20 overall on the season. This, with Tre Tucker as his No. 1 receiver. Of course, Tucker is merely Cousins’ No. 1 wideout. Brock Bowers is his No. 1 pass catcher, and the elite tight end stacked up 7/92/2 in the new Meadowlands. Cousins seemed to look Bowers’ way on all the most critical downs, and he was richly rewarded. Fantasy managers also continue to be rewarded with Cousins in streamer spots, though that will be put to the test in Week 9 against the 49ers on the road. With only two teams on bye, we would be looking elsewhere in our quarterback spots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Raiders plan to start Kirk Cousins “as long as possible.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Schefter added that the team does not feel their current four-game losing streak is the fault of Cousins. He threw for nine touchdowns in the first three games, all of which the Raiders won. Cousins has just seven touchdowns over his past four outings, though he has only thrown two interceptions and taken just five sacks during that stretch. The Raiders are probably right to lay the blame elsewhere. Still, No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is waiting in the wings. He is the future of the franchise, and his time grows closer with every Raiders loss. Vegas takes on the Jets this week. They then get a gauntlet of San Francisco, Seattle, and Denver. A 0-3 run that late in the season would likely spell the end of Cousins as their starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said “Kirk Cousins is our quarterback,” when asked about the possibility of making a change at QB ahead of Week 8.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Rather than let any speculation linger, Kubiak was quick to shut down any idea of a switch at quarterback heading into Week 8’s game against the Jets. Kubiak said, “There is no controversy” at quarterback at this time, while also adding that “Fernando [Mendoza] is going to play football” at some point this season. Kubiak said the team does not have a timeline for when Mendoza could eventually make a start, and said Cousins continues to play well despite the team’s recent struggles. Cousins will be firmly on the streaming radar this week against a Jets team that just allowed 28 points to the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Raiders’ head coach Klint Kubiak said the team is “thinking about everything” in regards to the team’s QB situation after Week 7’s loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Kubiak was asked about the possibility of switching from Kirk Cousins to rookie No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza, and said the team is considering “everything” while also making it sound like their struggles were more of a team issue. Cousins struggled in the early part of Sunday’s loss to the Rams, but managed some late touchdowns in garbage time to save his stat line. If the Raiders are considering a switch, it’s possible we’ll learn their decision by Wednesday, when they begin preparing for their Week 8 game against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 26-of-44 attempts for 295 yards and two touchdowns in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Cousins, as per usual, did next to nothing before the Raiders got down by multiple scores in the second half. He ends with a pretty solid fantasy line thanks to a couple long connections with fellow garbage time merchant Tre Tucker, who led the Raiders with 108 yards and a score. Cousins’ other score went to the Raiders’ backfield garbage time merchant Ashton Jeanty. Cousins now has multiple touchdown throws in six of his seven games in 2026. The Fernando Mendoza clock is nearing midnight as the uncompetitive Raiders flounder and Cousins looks more washed by the week. If he still has the starting job by Week 8, Cousins will be a decent streaming option against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 23-of-41 passes for 313 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Raiders’ 33-30, Week 6 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Cousins and the Raiders strung together a handful of nice drives in Sunday’s loss to the Bills, but they needed to be just about perfect to slow Buffalo’s offensive attack. With Brock Bowers bottled up for most of the evening, Cousins connected with tight end Michael Mayer seven times for 95 yards, with his lone touchdown passes coming on passes of 11 and 44 yards to Tre Tucker in the fourth quarter. The 44-yard touchdown pass to Tucker came inside of two minutes and with the Bills up by 10, but Cousins and Tucker took advantage of a struggling Bills’ defense to complete the long score and keep things interesting in the waning seconds. Now losers of three straight games, the Raiders will hope to avoid a fourth straight loss next week when they host the suddenly 2-4 Rams. Cousins continues to enjoy a career revival under Klint Kubiak and has now thrown for 1,582-14-5 in his first six games. He’ll be in the QB2 mix for next week’s game against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.headline: Cardinals activated Zach Carter’s 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.analysis: Carter has not yet played this season, but he can contribute as a run defender when healthy. The Cardinals also opened Hunter Long’s 21-day practice window, potentially bringing in blocking help for the offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.headline: Raiders waived QB Cam Miller.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.analysis: Miller was the Raiders’ sixth-round pick, and it seems very likely that the signal-caller will be back with Las Vegas on their practice squad. Tommy Mellott — a former college quarterback who is making the move to wide receiver — was also part of the cuts for the Raiders. The full list of players who won’t make the 53-man roster: aived DT Zach Carter, RB Chris Collier, DE Jahfari Harvey, WR Shedrick Jackson, LB Matt Jones, DT Treven Ma’ae, G Atonio Mafi, RB Sincere McCormick, DE Ovie Oghoufo, TE Carter Runyon, WR Justin Shorter, OL Laki Tasi, S Trey Taylor, CB Greedy Vance, T Dalton Wagner and S JT Woods, WR Alex Bachman, S Terrell Edmunds and TE Albert Okwuegbunam while Lonnie Johnson Jr. was placed on the injured list and designated for return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.headline: Florida redshirt senior DL Zachary Carter opts out of the Gasparilla Bowl against UCF.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.analysis: After a standout season for the Gators, Carter (6'4/285) will forego the bowl game and start his preparation for the NFL Draft. He announced the decision on his Twitter page on Friday. He will be a very intriguing prospect for teams come April being a versatile player on the defensive line. He can line up anything from 2i to a true edge. Carter has ample power, strength, and athleticism to succeed in whatever role you ask him to play. He currently ranks as Mel Kiper Jr’s 10th ranked defensive tackle in the upcoming draft class.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.headline: Florida redshirt senior DL Zachary Carter has been added to the Chuck Bednarik Award watch list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.analysis: Carter (6'4/285) could have entered his name into the NFL Draft this past offseason, but elected to return to school. If Carter’s plan was to return to school to boost his draft stock, it’s safe to say he’s on the right track. Through five games, Carter has seven tackles and 15 quarterback pressures. He also leads the SEC in sacks with four and has eight tackles for a loss.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.headline: Florida redshirt junior DL Zachary Carter will stay in school for the 2021 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.analysis: Carter could have made a reasonable leap to the NFL if he really wanted to. Over the past two seasons, Carter has been a top contributor for the UF front, picking up 9.5 sacks. Carter has also used his long arms to bat down four passes over that span. At 6-foot-4 and 290-pounds, Carter moves quite well for a player his size and has proven himself as a menace when allowed to just pin his ears back. Time will tell if Carter can round out his game enough to raise his draft stock in 2021.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.headline: Florida senior WR Kadarius Toney and three other players who did not report for the start of fall camp have joined their teammates and are practicing.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.analysis: Toney, fellow wideouts Jacob Copeland and Trevon Grimes, and defensive end Zachary Carter were not with the team when fall camp began a week ago for personal reasons. All have since joined the team, with Carter saying via social media that he was playing this season “in honor of all COVID-19 fighters and victims.” During his press conference ahead of the start of fall camp, HC Dan Mullen said that he would have no issue with any player that decided to opt out of playing this season. All four players are expected to be key contributors for the Gators this season, with Florida being viewed as a legitimate threat to dethrone Georgia atop the SEC East.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.headline: Florida HC Dan Mullen confirmed that multiple players missed the first day of practice on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.analysis: While Mullen did not say who decided not to attend the first day of fall camp, he did confirm that multiple players did not attend. Among those who reportedly sat out Monday’s session were wide receivers Kadarius Toney, Trevon Grimes and Jacob Copeland, and defensive end Zachary Carter. During his press conference on Monday, Mullen said that he would not be surprised if multiple players (and possibly a couple coaches) opted out of the 2020 season due to COVID-19 concerns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.headline: Four-star 2017 DE Zachary Carter is deciding between Florida and Clemson for his commitment.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.analysis: Carter once said that he would not be making a commitment until after the completion of his senior season at Hillsborough High (Florida). That plan has been adjusted and he looks much, much closer to making a decision, now, with Rivals’ Rob Cassidy relaying that the 6-foot-4, 237-pounder might commit before his aforementioned senior season has even started. Carter addressed what he likes about both of his leaders, saying, “When I go up to Clemson, I can feel the family environment. I feel it there. With Florida, it’s nice that it’s close. Being two hours away really helps them. I don’t really care about distance, but that’s a nice perk.” He ranks as Rivals’ No. 62 overall prospect for the 2017 cycle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.headline: Four-star 2017 DE Zachary Carter committed to Florida.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.analysis: Carter kicked around the idea of waiting until after his senior season at Hillsborough High to announce the commitment, but he has changed course over the last few weeks and voila, a commitment to the Gators. His choice came down to Florida and Clemson, with HC Jim McElwain winning the day. As for his role down in Gainesville, Carter explained, “They told me that I’m a rush end, but I’ll play strongside also. So that’s sorta what they’re talking about now anyway.” Rivals checks him into their master list of 2017 recruits at No. 62 overall.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.headline: ESPN’s Craig Haubert noted that Florida four-star 2017 DE Zachary Carter is a “well-built prospect with a big frame who can continue to be developed.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-carte.analysis: "[Carter] possesses the length and strength to set the edge as a run defender with the ability to quickly locate the ball and shed,” Haubert wrote. “Not a player who will just wow you athletically, but he has a quick first step.” The 6-foot-4, 237-pounder is not close to a finished product at this point and Haubert views him as something of a work in progress. Wrote the analyst, “The key for defensive line coach Chris Rumph will be maximizing Carter’s ability. He’ll need to be more consistently explosive and better utilize his excellent size and strength.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley said he does not know if he will face charges related to his altercation at the Nashville International Airport.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley told reporters that he was trying to get his keys from the valet at the airport. They were giving him a hard time, so he took the keys out of the valet’s hands. The valet claims the altercation broke his finger. Ridley was at practice today and head coach Robert Saleh called it a “very minor miscommunication.” It doesn’t sound like the incident will keep Ridley off the field for now, though he hasn’t made much of an impact this year anyway.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Calvin Ridley was involved in an “unfortunate” incident at Nashville airport.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Saleh didn’t get into the details of the matter, instead opting to say it was a “very minor miscommunication” that is “now in the hands of law enforcement.” Ridley, 31, has caught 6-of-12 targets for 91 scoreless yards this season and could find himself on the move ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. That said, he’s far from the difference-making player he was early in his career and is fourth among Titans receivers in routes run (124) this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Titans WR Calvin Ridley “could be had for a late-round pick.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: The Titans are listening on Ridley, who could be had for a late-round pick, according to Schefter. The Chiefs, Steelers and 49ers are the most likely teams to be in the market for a wide receiver ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero also reported that multiple wide receivers could be traded before the deadline and listed Ridley as a name to watch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer thinks the Titans might be willing to trade away Tony Pollard in exchange for a fourth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Breer believes a fourth-round pick “seems like a lot” to give up for an aging running back who is set to enter free agency at the end of the year. So, Pollard might end up staying in Tennessee. Breer adds that the Titans could also consider trading away Calvin Ridley for a worse Day 3 pick, but he isn’t sure if the team is eager to get rid of pass catchers while they are attempting to develop their young quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams must find a way to trade for a wide receiver before the November 10th deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: The Rams’ resources are thin. They already traded away their 2027 first- and second-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. They also have just $8,000 in 2026 salary cap space, so restructuring the potential new add’s deal would be required. Atkins believes the Rams should consider Josh Downs as the top option due to his ability to beat man coverage and contribute as a returner. Other options, according to Atkins, include Calvin Ridley, Keenan Allen and Jauan Jennings, “for the likely cost of a Day 3 pick.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley caught 1-of-3 targets for 20 yards in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley was active after dealing with a hip injury this week, seeing the fourth-most snaps among Titans wide receivers. He finished the game with a drop and one reception. The veteran is a candidate to be traded but has not been offering much by way of fantasy production. Ridley can be left on fantasy benches heading into the Titans’ Week 9 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) is active for Week 8 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley entered the week questionable due to a hip injury but will be active after getting in a full practice on Friday. The Titans declared WR Carnell Tate, RB Tyjae Spears, P Tommy Townsend, CB Jaylon Jones, OT Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, TE Kylen Granson, and DT Jackie Marshall inactive for Week 8 against the Bengals. Ridley will be one of the Titans’ top pass-catchers with Carnell Tate (shoulder) already ruled out, but is not more than a touchdown-dependent fantasy WR4 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter named Calvin Ridley as a potential trade candidate.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Schefter threw out several names, many of whom have already been bandied about as trade candidates. Among the lesser-discussed options, he included Jerry Jeudy and Jauan Jennings in addition to Ridley. All three are veteran wideouts who have simply disappeared in the current iterations of their respective offenses. Even with new landing spots in the cards for the trio, none of them are worth holding onto in standard fantasy leagues. Ridley has five catches for 81 yards this year. He is expected to play through his hip injury today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 8 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: He got in a full session on Friday and would seem to be trending towards playing. With Carnell Tate down this week, Elic Ayomanor is probably the Titans dart throw wideout for the desperate against the Bengals if you’re choosing between him or Ridley.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) returned to practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley did not practice once last week. He was listed as questionable on Friday but never appeared likely to suit up and was eventually ruled out ahead of kickoff. Elic Ayomanor popped up for 44 yards on three catches and seven targets in his absence. Ridley’s return will prevent Ayomanor from building any momentum.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said the team will stick with Harrison Butker for Week 10 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Butker has missed a field goal in every game outside of Week 1. His 63 field goal percentage is the worst mark in the league, outside of Harrison Mevis, who is not currently on a roster. Barring a sharp turnaround in Butker’s play, he’ll get benched at some point this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Harrison Butker converted 1-of-2 field goal attempts in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Butker missed a 54-yard field goal late in the fourth quarter. It would have made the game a one-point deficit instead of four for the Chiefs’ final drive. Kansas City was ultimately rebuffed at the goal line and lost the game. Having missed a field goal in all but one game this year, we suspect Andy Reid will throw in the towel on Butker after today’s performance. Justin Tucker, recently signed to the Chiefs’ practice squad, will likely get called up for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs special teams coach Dave Toub said Harrison Butker is “our kicker.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: “He went 10-for-10 yesterday, with Justin Tucker right there. ... We’re going to keep working it,” Toub continued. It sounds like despite signing Tucker, Butker will continue to kick for the Chiefs. At least this week, anyway.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs signed Justin Tucker, formerly of the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Tucker will start on the Chiefs practice squad. His signing comes a few days after Harrison Butker missed two field goal attempts against the Seahawks. On the season Butker has missed five of his 16 attempts, and over his past 11 games he’s missed seven kicks. Tucker, who recently competed for the Dolphins kicker job, hasn’t kicked since 2024 in Baltimore, when he missed eight of his 30 field goal tries. The Ravens released Tucker in 2025 after 16 massage therapists accused him of sexual misconduct.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Harrison Butker converted both of his field goal attempts in the Chiefs’ Week 15 loss against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Butker bounced back from his Week 14 miss against the Texans in a close loss. He’s missed just four of his 28 field goal attempts through Week 15. Butker’s fantasy prospects might be affected by Patrick Mahomes’ potential absence after Mahomes went down with a knee injury near the end of KC’s loss to the Bolts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Harrison Butker went 1-for-2 in field goal attempts in the Chiefs’ Week 14 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: He connected from 36 yards and made his only point after attempt, missing from 43 yards at the end of the second quarter when his kick hit off the right upright. That missed field goal contributed to the Chiefs being shut out in the first half for only the third time in quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ career, making the failed conversion slightly more meaningful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs activated K Harrison Butker from injured reserve ahead of Week 15’s matchup with the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Matthew Wright was waived in a corresponding move. The Chiefs designated Butker, who missed a month with a knee injury, to return from injured reserve earlier this week and deemed him good to go after logging three limited practices. He has plenty of time to shake off the rust before the playoffs, but may be difficult to trust in his first game back in the fantasy playoffs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Harrison Butker (knee) is questionable for Week 15 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Butker practiced in a limited capacity all week, logging his first practice repetitions since undergoing a mid-season meniscus trim in his left knee. Given the Chiefs’ Super Bowl aspirations, the team is unlikely to let him suit up this week if his re-injury risk is significant. If he plays, it stands to reason that he is good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs designated Harrison Butker (knee) for return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Butker underwent a meniscus trim on his left knee in November, as he was sent to injured reserve. The talented kicker could play as early as Week 15, however, he understandably makes for a slightly less certain K1 than fantasy managers are used to. It would be unsurprising to see him turn in an up-and-down performance in his first game back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs K Matthew Wright will start in Week 14.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: The journeyman kicker made four of his five field goal tries last week in a win against the Raiders and will get at least one more start before Harrison Butker returns from a knee injury that landed him on injured reserve. The Chiefs put K Spencer Shrader on IR this week. Wright is a solid fantasy option with the Chiefs sporting an implied Vegas total of 23.5 points against LA.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes (elbow) is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: This comes directly from Andy Reid, though we’ll have to wait until the team’s injury report officially drops to be sure it’s actually a full session. Either way, Mahomes is playing on Sunday despite suffering an ugly elbow injury in Week 9. He told reporters it’s simply a matter of pain management for now. The Chiefs may opt to lean on their ground game against the Falcons, but even that won’t knock Mahomes out of the QB1 mix after the addition of Josh Downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Patrick Mahomes (elbow) is considered “day-to-day.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: This news comes less than 24 hours after NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that an MRI “did not reveal a major injury” to Mahomes, who was able to finish out the game in Sunday’s win over the Jets. Reid said Mahomes is dealing with some soreness that he will have to rehab a bit, but it doesn’t sound like he’s at risk of missing any time. Mahomes threw for 242 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets and will be on the QB1 radar next week against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Patrick Mahomes’ (elbow) MRI “did not reveal a major injury.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Rapoport adds that Mahomes’ “elbow strain/sprain will be monitored over the next few days for pain and swelling.” Without getting too deep into the weeds, there are a few things to note. First off, Rapoport sometimes reports injury news optimistically. It would have been nice to see him actually report a “minor” injury, rather than not “major.” Secondly, “strain” typically refers to muscles and tendons, while “sprain” is often used for ligaments. Using both is a tad confusing. That said, Rapoport’s follow-up statement suggests Mahomes may have a chance to play in Week 10 against the Falcons. Updates will be provided as soon as news breaks. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 23-of-41 attempts for 242 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets, adding two rushes for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes was pulled with a few minutes to go in the fourth quarter with the Chiefs up multiple scores and the Jets not all that interested in staging a comeback. Mahomes overcame an injury to his right forearm in this one. He sustained the injury on a hard hit from a blitzing New York defender who bent Mahomes’ arm back awkwardly. After getting some treatment on the sideline, Mahomes re-entered the game and seemed fine, though he was seen grimacing and shaking his arm at times. This marked Mahomes’ sixth multi-touchdown game of the season. He should remain in starting lineups as a top-12 option in Week 10 against the pass-funnel Atlanta defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 30-of-41 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns in the Chiefs’ 28-24, Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes posted a strong box score for fantasy managers and took care of the football with zero turnovers. He also took just two sacks, but the second was one that will haunt Chiefs fans for a while. After marching the offense down to the goal line under the two-minute warning, the Chiefs found themselves on fourth-and-goal. They initially got the score via a strike to Rashee Rice, but the play was blown dead via a false start. The Broncos’ pass-rush got to him on the second try, taking Mahomes down for a game-ending sack. On the whole, it was another dink-and-dunk game plan from Mahomes, who failed to get the deep ball going once again. Luckily for him, Emmett Johnson averaged 25.6 yards per catch and turned a short toss into a 73-yard touchdown in the first half. The Chiefs get a bounce-back spot against the Jets next week in a game where Mahomes will be just inside the QB1 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 19-of-33 passes for 165 yards and one interception in the Chiefs’ 20-3, Week 7 loss to the Seahawks, adding 14 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: The three points tied the fewest scored in a start in Mahomes’ career as the Chiefs suffered their first defeat of the season. Mahomes faced consistent pressure and a shrinking pocket as the Seahawks held the Chiefs to just 213 yards of total offense. Mahomes also had an ill-advised turnover as he tried to escape pressure, over-throwing his intended receiver on the run. The Chiefs fall to 5-1 with the defeat, leaving only the Vikings as the lone unbeaten team through seven weeks. Mahomes gets little time to lick his wounds with the division rival Broncos on the horizon in Week 8, where he’ll be a low end QB1 in another difficult matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 23-of-30 attempts for 272 yards and one interception in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers, adding five rushes for 16 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes had multiple touchdown tosses in every game this season headed into Week 6. Kansas City’s offense didn’t have to do much against a sleepy Chargers offense that could barely move the ball once again on Sunday. The Chiefs leaned on Ken Walker, who went for 128 yards and two touchdowns on the day. With Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton out, Mahomes relied heavily on Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce. Until Rice is back and fully healthy, Mahomes will be more of a top-15 option. He gets the Seahawks in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 15-of-30 passes for 225 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs’ 30-27, Week 4 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes was under duress throughout this one. He took multiple hits and was sacked twice, but managed to come up with just enough plays to pull off the road win against a spry Raiders team. Mahomes threw his first touchdown of the day in the first quarter, finding Tyquan Thornton for a two-yard score, then connected with Thornton again in the fourth quarter for an eight-yard touchdown near the back of the end zone. Mahomes’ longest play of the game also went to Thornton, when the speedster broke free down the left sideline to make a 55-yard catch. Unfortunately, Thornton exited the game with a gruesome ankle injury after the play, but he did set up Kenneth Walker for a two-yard touchdown run on the ensuing play. Mahomes and the Chiefs are now 4-0 as they enter their Week 5 bye week. They’ll play host to the Chargers, who are 0-4 when they return in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 20-of-24 passes for 246 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in the Chiefs’ 24-10, Week 3 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: With the Dolphins playing ball-control offense, the Chiefs were limited to just 49 total plays, but Mahomes and company compensated with extreme efficiency. That included long catch-and-run gains to Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice, with Mahomes also finding the former for an end zone score. Mahomes has now posted multiple passing scores in each of his first three starts. It took him seven games to accomplish that feat last year. There was a scary moment when Mahomes got “body weighted” by DL Chop Robinson, but Mahomes shook it off as Robinson was flagged for roughing. Currently averaging 8.3 yards per attempt after that number was 7.1 a year ago, Mahomes is looking at home in this “new look” Chiefs attack once again coordinated by Eric Bieniemy. He has another soft Week 4 matchup in the Raiders before the Chiefs head on early-season bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 32-of-47 passes for 382 yards and three touchdowns in the Chiefs’ 33-30, Week 2 win over the Colts, adding 17 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes looked much more like himself against the Colts than he did against the Broncos in Week 1, with his typical mobility in the pocket on full display as he extended plays. He even escaped the pocket twice to pick up crucial first downs with his legs in key situations, looking closer to how he did before tearing his ACL in 2025. Mahomes managed to complete two passes greater than 30 yards, one to Tyquan Thornton and one to Rashee Rice, an area of his game that he has not excelled in over the previous two seasons. Even so, it took the Chiefs two possessions in overtime to finally sneak by the tenacious Colts, moving to a 2-0 record ahead of a road date with the Dolphins in Week 3. Mahomes has returned to weekly QB1 status, although the team could look to continue its dominance on the ground against a week opponent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cashius-ho.headline: Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Cashius Howell (wrist) is week-to-week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cashius-ho.analysis: Howell injured his wrist in Week 8 and underwent surgery shortly after the game. He was placed on injured reserve last week. Taylor declined to rule him out for the year today but didn’t offer a timeline for his return either. Howell has one tackle and three sacks this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cashius-ho.headline: Bengals selected Texas A&M EDGE Cashius Howell with the No. 41 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cashius-ho.analysis: Cashius Howell (6’2/248) emerged as Texas A&M’s premier pressure maven in 2025, pairing volume with efficiency while stacking up elite havoc totals. Across 591 snaps, he posted a strong 81.2 PFF defensive grade supported by well-rounded marks in run defense (73.6), tackling (79.6) and pass rush (90.3), the latter cementing his identity as a finisher. Howell led the Aggies with 23 total havoc plays, including 16.5 TFLs and 11.5 sacks, and his 40 total pressures on 265 rushes (15.1% pressure rate) yielded 9 sacks created and 1 strip-sack. His disruptive profile translated into backfield consistency, notching 29 hits + hurries to go with a brisk 2.68s time-to-first-pressure and a commendable 15.9% 3rd-down pressure rate that showed reliability in money downs. He ran a blistering 4.59s 40-yard dash (97th%) and recorded a solid 8.11 RAS, but his surprisingly short 30 ¼” arms could be a major problem against the mammoth NFL tackles he’ll be battling. Howell has the toolbox and motor to be a valued sub-package rusher on passing downs if he can overcome the length concerns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said he hopes Malik Willis (groin) can return this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Hafley told reporters on Wednesday that Willis would seek second opinions on the groin injury that landed him on injured reserve. It sounds like season-ending surgery is a possibility for Willis, who would end his 2026 campaign. Through Week 9, Willis ranks 26th in passing yardage and 29th in passing touchdowns. He’s dead last in EPA per pass attempt and ranks 28th out of 38 qualifying QBs in EPA per drop back. Kyle McCord will get a chance at quarterback for the Dolphins in Week 10 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins placed Malik Willis (groin) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: He had clearly been laboring since the bye week and this will give Willis some time to heal. This is not regarded as a season-ending injury and Willis will be eligible to return in Week 14. In the mean time, it appears we’re all about to see how well the roster cutdown Kyle McCord trade works out for the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 13-of-25 passes for 128 yards and an interception in the Dolphins’ 19-9, Week 9 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis only added seven yards on two carries. He was on the injury report with a groin injury this week. Despite practicing in full three times, Willis appeared to be severely limited by the issue. He turned down several opportunities to scramble, instead opting to throw the ball away when the Lions’ pass-rush got close. Without the rushing production to bail him out of tough spots, the offense collapsed despite facing one of the league’s worst defenses. His passing output was already weak, but a lack of rush attempts will pull him out of the QB2 ranks entirely. He will be downgraded to a low-end QB2 for his Week 10 matchup with the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis (groin) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis did the same during Week 8 practices and ended up running just once against the Patriots. Hopefully, the groin injury continues to improve and his rushing usage returns. Willis remains a QB2 this week against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 21-of-32 passes for 211 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in the Dolphins’ 19-24, Week 8 loss to the Patriots, adding one rush for two yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis practiced in full this week despite being listed with a groin injury. Perhaps the soft tissue issue made him play a little more restrained than we would have liked him to. The Dolphins’ quarterback continues to hold the ball too long. He took five sacks today. His interception was not totally his fault. He was hit by a pass rusher, altering the pass’s trajectory, which bounced off a defensive lineman’s helmet before flying 29 yards downfield, where a Patriots defender picked it off. Willis had another interception called back due to defensive offsides, which was lucky. The Dolphins’ young wide receivers are learning the ropes and could help him churn out usable fantasy line as the season progresses. Willis will be a high-end QB2 against the Lions in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis (groin) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: While we are happy to see Willis practicing in full, we are slightly unhappy to see that he has a new injury. The Dolphins’ quarterback has already dealt with toe and right thumb injuries this season. Willis remains a viable QB2 starter against the Patriots, but this is worth monitoring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 14-of-21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns in the Dolphins’ 28-28, Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis also added 37 yards and a touchdown on eight rush attempts. It was, by far, his best performance as a Dolphin. It was also the first win for both Willis and first-year head coach Jeff Hafley. Willis picked apart the Jets for chunk play after chunk play. His biggest play of the day was a 63-yard completion to Caleb Douglas, though nearly all of those yards came after the catch. He had already connected with Douglas earlier in the game for his first touchdown of the day. Things will be a lot tougher for Willis and the Miami offense when they take on the Patriots next week. Despite the strong showing today, Willis will remain buried in the QB2 ranks for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis (right thumb) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: ESPN’s Marcel Louis-Jacques reports that Willis received treatment for his thumb injury on his right, throwing hand, though he did not share what exactly the injury is. Hopefully, it is nothing serious. If his ball placement is impacted, the Jets’ D/ST would benefit. Willis is a volatile QB2 against them this week. Willis underwent surgery on his left thumb in August 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Malik “is our quarterback.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: “Malik needs to be better, but that’s not the headline -- we all need to be better ... everything in the pass game has to be better.. It’s the receivers, it’s the tight ends, it’s the protection,” Hafley continued. Willis is by all statistical measures one of the weakest quarterbacks in the league with his arm, but at least he’s skimping some superflex QB2 value with his legs. There’s not much reason for the Dolphins to bench him either way, as they have nobody they pressingly need to evaluate. Willis should return after the Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 15-of-27 passes for 137 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions and a fumble in the Dolphins’ 31-24, Week 5 loss to the Bengals, adding eight rushes for 74 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis had a poor passing day, finishing the first quarter completing 0-of-4 passes. He threw a pair of second quarter interceptions to Jordan Battle, the first coming off a tip and the second on a cross-body throw and poor decision. He also fumbled and recovered a snap in the two-minute drill while a potential third interception was dropped in the endzone in the second half. Willis recovered with a touchdown throw to Kevin Coleman in the fourth quarter but fumbled deep in the Dolphins’ own territory late in the game. He capped off his day with a quick goal-line rushing score at the end of the game but it was too little, too late. Between his decision-making and lack of ball security, Willis had a poor game but good fantasy production due to his rushing output. Willis is a fantasy QB2 heading into a Week 6 Dolphins bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said he wasn’t sure if Alec Pierce (heel) will play again this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce, who signed a massive new deal with the Colts last offseason, has been on injured reserve since Week 3. The Colts have little reason to rush him back in another lost season. “We’ll see. Like I said last week, he’s still in that rehab process, and I’m not going to put a timetable on return,” Steichen said Wednesday when asked about Pierce’s availability. Steichen mentioned Deion Burks and Anthony Gould as receivers who will see more playing time after the Colts traded Josh Downs and Keenan Allen this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce (heel) won’t practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce, dealing with a heel injury since mid-September, will continue rehabbing and remain on injured reserve ahead of the Colts’ Week 7 game against the Vikings. Since Week 3, Keenan Allen leads the Colts with a 24 percent target share, while Josh Downs has 17 percent of the team’s targets and 26 percent of the team’s air yards. Neither wideout is a great option in Week 7 against a marauding Minnesota defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) is still a few weeks away from a return to game action.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: No surprise here. Pierce shed his cast earlier this week, but there was also a report from the Athletic’s James Boyd that he “didn’t get the sense” Pierce was close to a return. Pelissero reports that Pierce isn’t expected to return to practice next week when he’s eligible. It’s difficult to justify holding Pierce in leagues without IR spots given the circumstances.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd reports Alec Pierce (heel) is no longer wearing a cast but is not close to a return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Boyd said he “didn’t get the sense” that Pierce is close to a return. Pierce went on injured reserve with a heel injury after Week 2 and wore a cast on his left ankle/heel while rehabbing. It’s a sign of progress for Pierce, who will have his first chance to come back in the Colts’ Week 7 game against the Vikings.
