https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts placed Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce will be sidelined for at least four weeks after suffering the injury in Week 2 against Kansas City. Pierce had seen 19 percent of the Colts’ targets and 53 percent of the team’s air yards in Week 1 against the Ravens, resuming his role as a strictly-downfield pass catcher. With Pierce out, Josh Downs should have every chance to operate as the Colts’ No. 1 wideout while Tyler Warren sees a bump in targets. Laquon Treadwell is likely to take over as the team’s lone deep threat. Treadwell can be picked up in 14-team fantasy formats ahead of the Colts’ Week 3 matchup with the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) will “attempt to rehab his injury rather than have surgery.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce will most certainly be out for numerous games after appearing to re-injure the heel that he had offseason surgery on in Week 2. Rapoport’s wording seems to indicate that additional surgery has not yet been ruled out, but Pierce will attempt to rehab the issue in the interim. It’s a disaster of a scenario for a team that extended Pierce while allowing Michael Pittman to walk in the offseason. Josh Downs appears most likely to become the focal point of the offense through the air in Pierce’s absence after amassing seven catches on nine targets in the team’s overtime loss to the Chiefs. When, or if, Pierce returns to the active roster in 2026 remains to be seen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce (heel) aggravated the injury that required surgery in March and the Colts are “still gathering information.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: X-rays came back negative last night but Pierce couldn’t put weight on it last night and left on crutches with a boot on. The fact that it was an aggravation is not promising. It sounds like Pierce could be looking at an extended absence. If true, Josh Downs will get some WR3 hype ahead of Week 3’s date against the Texans. If you were wondering why Laquon Treadwell was on the field deep in the game on Sunday night, Pierce’s injury is the reason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Colts WR Alec Pierce’s (heel) X-rays were negative.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce evidently avoided suffering a fracture. He will undergo more testing tomorrow to determine the remaining specifics and the injury’s severity. Hopefully, the Colts’ field-stretching wide receiver is not sidelined for long, if at all. Pierce underwent surgery on his ankle/heel this offseason and spent almost the entire spring and summer rehabbing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) is questionable to return to Week 2 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce came up limping on a route on the final play of the first quarter and was escorted to the medical tent by the training staff. He appeared to be unable to put any weight on the injured leg. It’s obviously not what fantasy managers want to see after he missed most of the offseason program following surgery on the ankle and heel on the same leg in late March. He remained in the medical tent for about 10 minutes before being carted to the locker room. Pierce caught his lone target for 11 yards prior to departing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce’s Thursday absence appears to have been a rest day. The Colts reportedly plan to play Pierce more in Week 2 than they did in Week 1, when he played on 59 percent of the team’s snaps. He posted a 4/61 receiving line and can be viewed as a WR3/FLEX this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Deion Burks will see an expanded role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: The rookie wideout, who has run a route on 16 percent of the Colts’ drop backs through Week 9, should see a big jump in routes with Josh Downs traded to the Chiefs. In his limited playing time this season, Burks has been targeted on a fairly strong 18 percent of his routes with a high 17.5 average depth of target. Burks and Laquon Treadwell should be the team’s primary downfield wideouts for now. Burks should only be rostered in deep leagues with multiple flex spots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd believes Ashton Dulin is the team’s third receiver “for now.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: He mentions Nick Westbrook-Ikhine and seventh-round pick Deion Burks as possible competition for the spot. We also (our speculation) wouldn’t rule out the Colts picking up one of the several as-of-yet unsigned free agents like Jauan Jennings, Deebo Samuel, or Stefon Diggs. Westbrook-Ikhine has flashed big touchdown upside in the past and would be the most fantasy-useful player in this group if he wins a role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Colts selected Oklahoma WR Deion Burks with the No. 254 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: After a 57/620/4 receiving line with Oklahama in 2025, Burks (5’10/180) showcased his athleticism at the NFL combine. His 4.30 40-yard dash and 42.5-inch vertical were both top-three at the wide receiver position. He spent his first three college years at Purdue, building up his repertoire as a quick slot receiver before transferring to Oklahoma for his final two seasons. Burks’ production doesn’t pop off the page but he showed the ability to line up both outside and in the slot with versatile usage to show off his shiftiness in space. A shorter frame limits Burks’ ability to be a physical route runner and he lacks downfield targets, seeing an average depth of target of just 8.6 yards his final season. However, speed and athleticism will allow him to be a versatile weapon in space. Burks has the tools to succeed as a shifty slot receiver at the next level.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Oklahoma WR Deion Burks ran an official 4.30 40-yard dash at the 2026 NFL Combine.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: That goes down as the fastest 40 at this year’s Combine for a wide receiver, in a year that has the fastest composite 40-yard times in NFL history. Burks profiles as a slot wide receiver capable of inflicting damage with the ball in his hands in the open field, a profile that typically results in a late day two or early day three pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Anthony Gould will play slot receiver after Josh Downs was traded to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: With Downs shipped out, the slot role will go to Gould, who has four receptions for 45 yards over three seasons with the Colts. Downs had accounted for 18 percent of the team’s targets and 24 percent of the team’s air yards through Week 9. The Colts use three wideout sets on 59 percent of their offensive plays, the 12th highest rate in the NFL. They rank 29th in EPA per pas attempt with three receivers on the field. Gould should be rostered in deeper formats based on route volume alone.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Anthony Gould (concussion) won’t play in Indianapolis’ Week 8 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: The biggest news for fantasy purposes with the Colts inactives is simply that Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs are up, but that isn’t exactly surprising. Gould practiced in full the last two days of the week before being ruled out and stands a chance at being ready for Week 8. Inactive for the Colts are: LB Bryce Boettcher (groin), TE Pharaoh Brown, DT Kevin Givens, T Charlie Heck, QB Riley Leonard (third quarterback) and CB Justin Walley (knee).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Sauce Gardner (calf) will not play in Week 7 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: Gardner was never expected to play this week after it was announced on Monday that he would be week-to-week with his calf injury. His absence could be a good sign for Vikings pass-catchers this week in what should be a plus matchup against a Colts defense that ranks 14th in fantasy points allowed to receivers this season. In addition to Gardner, the Colts also ruled out WR Anthony Gould (concussion).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Colts ruled out RT Braden Smith (concussion/neck) for Week 15 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: The Colts will be without their starting right tackle for Sunday’s road game against a stout Seahawks defense. Backup Jalen Travis is expected to draw the start in his place and will be tasked with keeping one of either Riley Leonard or Philip Rivers upright. In addition to Smith, the Colts also ruled out WR Anthony Gould (ankle) and CB Sauce Gardner (calf).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: WR Adonai Mitchell caught 1-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Colts’ preseason game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: Mitchell started in place of injured slot receiver Josh Downs (high-ankle sprain), though Mitchell was curiously subbed out for fellow rookie Anthony Gould on third downs, as noted by PFF’s Nathan Jahnke. Mitchell promisingly logged perimeter snaps opposite Alec Pierce in 12 personnel with the second-team offense. Gould averaged 22.0 yards per return on three total kickoff returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd believes Colts WR Anthony Gould could see starting snaps with Josh Downs (ankle) sidelined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: According to Boyd, Gould “has flashed more as a receiver than as a returner during camp.” The rookie fifth-rounder made a name for himself as a returner during his time at Oregon State, but with Downs sidelined for multiple weeks, there’s now a hole that needs to be filled at the slot position. Gould blazed a 4.39 40-yard dash at the combine this spring and totaled 44-711-2 in his final season of college. He played just 33.5 percent of his college snaps from the slot but had a 90.5 percent slot rate in 2021. We wouldn’t expect Gould to offer much fantasy upside, but this is worth monitoring as the team figures out a temporary replacement for Downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Colts selected Oregon State WR Anthony Gould with the No. 142 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: Gould (5’8/174) is an undersized receiver who surprisingly played 92.4 percent of his snaps out wide in his final year at Oregon State. Last season was undoubtedly Gould’s best, as the 44 receptions and 711 yards he posted were more than the he totaled in his previous four seasons combined. Despite his size, Gould’s 4.39 40-time and elite vertical and broad jumps were exactly what he needed to catch the attention of scouts. Gould ran only 601 routes during five years in college and spent most of his time in the slot before last season. He may return to the slot as a pro, but the former First-team All-Pac-12 return specialist may be better served on special teams. Gould averaged 16.3 yards per punt return and returned 14 punts for two scores in 2022.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Cleveland.com’s Mary Kay Cabot reports Deshawn Watson (concussion) will start in Week 10 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Watson was sidelined last week against the Saints with a brain injury. He’ll back in time to face his former team as the Browns push for postseason contention in the competitive NFC North. Shedeur Sanders will revert to his backup role in Week 10 after throwing for 297 yards and two touchdowns against the Saints in an overtime loss. Watson will be a borderline fantasy option against a pass-funnel Texans defense that has allowed the third most air yards per game this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Speaking Monday, Browns head coach Todd Monken declined to name a starting QB for Week 10’s game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported earlier in the day that Deshaun Watson was expected to return as the starter, but Monken didn’t rush to name a starter when questioned on Monday. Monken praised Shedeur Sanders for his performance in Sunday’s start against the Saints, but said he hasn’t really “thought through” who will start in Week 10 against the Texans. It’s hard to imagine Monken handing the job over to Sanders after a start that was mostly forgettable until the final five minutes of regulation, even if Watson hasn’t been overly impressive this season. We would still expect Watson to get the nod against Houston, but Sanders’ late-game performance won’t do anything to quiet those looking/hoping for a change.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Browns “plan to start Deshaun Watson in Week 10 vs. the Texans.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: This shouldn’t surprise anyone after Shedeur Sanders failed to make the most of his spot start in Week 9 against the Saints. Sanders and the Browns’ offense stalled through the first three quarters of Sunday’s game before a late 64-yard touchdown pass to KC Concepcion gave the Browns their first touchdown of the day. An impressive catch-and-run score by Harold Fannin in overtime gave Sanders his second touchdown pass on the day, but the 39-yard score came on a pass, in which Fannin generated 37 yards after the catch. Watson has struggled mightily at times this season, but Sanders didn’t do enough to unseat him in what was a plus matchup against a bad defense. Now out of concussion protocol, Watson will suit up in a “revenge game” against his former team next week, where he will profile as a low-end QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Browns declared QB Deshaun Watson, QB Taylen Green, C Parker Brailsford, DT Maliek Collins, LB Justin Jefferson, and CB Noah Igninoghene inactive for Week 9 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Watson cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend but was not prepared as the starter throughout the week. Shedeur Sanders will get his first start of the season and Dillon Gabriel will back him up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Deshaun Watson cleared the league’s concussion protocol but will be inactive for Week 9 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Watson returned to practice on Friday for a limited session and cleared the league’s protocol over the weekend. Still, after preparing Shedeur Sanders to start throughout the week, head coach Todd Monken decided not to throw a curveball at his own team on game day. Sanders will start and Dillon Gabriel will back him up. Watson has rebounded this year, but the lows are still staggeringly low. He took eight sacks in a blowout loss to the Steelers last week. If Sanders plays well today, Monken will at least have something to think about ahead of Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Deshaun Watson (concussion) will not start in Week 9 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Head coach Todd Monken said Watson will be questionable for Sunday’s game, but has already said Shedeur Sanders will make his first start of the season. Watson missed Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices but was upgraded to a limited participant on Friday, although he has yet to clear concussion protocol. The decision to start Sanders likely stems from him working with the first-team offense during the week and the unlikelihood of Watson clearing protocol in time for Sunday’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Deshaun Watson (concussion) is “unlikely to start” in Week 9 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Watson has not practiced this week due to concussion symptoms he has been dealing with since Week 8’s loss to the Steelers. Unless he surprisingly clears concussion protocol this week, Watson will miss Week 9, paving the way for Shedeur Sanders to make his first start of the season. We will have official word on Watson’s status in a few hours, but at this point, it would be surprising if he does start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Deshaun Watson (concussion) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Cleveland’s Mary Kay Cabot indicated yesterday that Shedeur Sanders is seemingly slated to start in Week 9 against the Saints. If that ends up being the case, and Sanders can play well enough, it might be possible for him to steal the starting job from Watson this week. Sanders would be QB2-viable against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Cleveland.com’s Mary Kay Cabot said the “vibe” is that Shedeur Sanders will start in Week 9 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Cabot said it would be a challenge for Deshaun Watson to clear the NFL’s concussion protocol by Saturday and suit up for Sunday’s game. Watson suffered a head injury in Week 8 against the Steelers and reported concussion symptoms on Tuesday, according to the Browns. Sanders in 2025 was the most inaccurate quarterback in the league and struggled to support fantasy-relevant pass catchers. Harold Fannin could see a boost with Sanders under center after Sanders targeted the tight end relentlessly during his 2025 starts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Browns placed Deshaun Watson in the NFL’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Watson took a hit to the head in the first half of the Browns’ Week 8 loss to the Steelers. He was evaluated for a brain injury and re-entered the game. He then reported concussion-like symptoms on Tuesday and entered the protocol on Wednesday. It would be somewhat surprising if Watson is able to clear the protocol in time for the Browns’ Week 9 matchup against the Saints. That would likely mean Shedeur Sanders would get the starting nod against New Orleans. Sanders should only be rostered in superflex formats for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.headline: Ravens released TE Nick Vannett.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.analysis: Vannett joined the Ravens prior to the season and operated as a blocking tight end. He appeared in five games, playing 85 offensive snaps and not seeing a target in the passing games. The Ravens now part ways with Vannett on NFL trade deadline day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.headline: Ravens signed TE Nick Vannett to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.analysis: Vannett, 33, is a journeyman veteran tight end best known for his blocking skills. Starting his career with the Seahawks, he has jumped around the league with the Steelers, Broncos, Saints, Giants, Chargers, Titans, Vikings, and Rams. He signed with the Seahawks in the offseason but was let go in final cuts. The Ravens add Vannett as blocking tight end depth on the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.headline: Seahawks signed TE Nick Vannett, formerly of the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.analysis: Seahawks general manager John Schneider drafted Vannett with a third-round pick back in 2016 before trading him to the Steelers for a 2020 fifth-round pick in September 2019. Vannett has since played for eight more teams, including the Rams in 2025. He will compete for a roster spot in Seattle this summer. The Seahawks correspondingly waived CB Tyrone Broden, who was placed on the physically unable to perform list earlier this week. He could be re-signed by Seattle if he makes it through waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.headline: Nick Vannett caught 2-of-2 targets for 26 yards in Tennessee’s Week 18 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.analysis: He managed 17 of them on a well-designed flea flicker screen that saw Vannett out in space alone with blockers. Entering his age-32 season in 2025, Vannett will continue trawling around the league in search of bad tight end depth charts. Since entering the final year of his rookie deal in 2019, he has played for the Seahawks, Steelers, Broncos, Saints, Giants, Chargers, and now the Titans. If he shows up, your team has a bad tight end depth chart. We’re sorry, we don’t make the rules here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught 5-of-7 targets for 42 yards in the Titans’ Week 17 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.analysis: Okonkwo also added an end-around carry for 17 yards. He has been Mason Rudolph’s’ favorite target since Rudolph took over as the starter, and that continued against the Jaguars. Okonkwo drew a defensive pass interference on the first Titans pass play of the game and led the team with seven targets. He was wide open on the Titans’ final drive, but Rudolph just missed him on the sideline for what would have likely been a touchdown. Instead, Nick Vannett was the tight end who had an eight-yard score earlier in the game. Okonkwo finishes with a solid 5/42 receiving line, with 17 rushing yards. He is in the back-end TE1 mix against the Texans for those still in fantasy matchups Week 18.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught 3-of-4 targets for eight yards in the Titans’ Week 14 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.analysis: Okonkwo had a quiet day, with just eight yards on four targets. He was dropped for a six-yard loss on a checkdown, bringing down his yardage total. He is the lead tight end, but that does not mean much in the inefficient Titans offense. Fellow tight end Nick Vannett caught 1-of-2 targets for four yards while Josh Whyle caught 2-of-2 targets for 31 yards. None of the Titans’ tight ends should be in fantasy lineups; Okonkwo should be the only one on the fantasy radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.headline: Nick Vannett caught 2-of-2 passes for 33 yards with a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 9 overtime win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.analysis: Vannett got open in the end zone to give the Titans an early 7-0 lead. The 31-year-old has been an afterthought in this Tennessee passing attack, and that should be the case again in Week 10 against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.headline: Titans waived TE Nick Vannett.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.analysis: Vannett appeared to make the initial 53-man roster, but he was waived with the Titans putting in a claim for Ali Gaye from the Texans. Vannett could see interest on the waiver wire, and if he goes unclaimed he could be brought back to the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.headline: TE Chig Okonkwo caught 0-of-0 targets in the Titans’ preseason game against the Saints on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.analysis: No. 2 TE Josh Whyle (concussion protocol) was inactive but Okonkwo still failed to separate from his position group. Conversely, No. 3 TE Nick Vannett caught 2-of-2 targets for 30 yards playing alongside Okonkwo in the first-team offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.headline: Titans signed veteran TE Nick Vannett.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-vanne.analysis: The two sides agreed to terms on Monday although the terms of the contract have not yet been made public. The eight-year veteran came into the league with the Seahawks in 2016, spending time with the Steelers, Broncos, Saints, Giants, and Chargers since departing Seattle. Vannett carries sparse fantasy value even though the Titans have little in the way of depth behind presumed starter Chigoziem Okonkwo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Rams signed WR Xavier Smith off the 49ers’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: With all the injuries at wide receiver, the Rams decide to bring back a familiar face in Xavier Smith in lieu of trading for a receiver. Smith was on the 49ers’ practice squad after the Rams waived him earlier this season. He caught 18 passes for 303 yards for the Rams last year, seeing the bulk of his opportunities as kick returner. Smith figures to operate as receiving depth with special teams utility once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Puka Nacua (groin) is considered a “pre-game decision” for the Rams’ Week 2 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: Nacua was added to the injury report on Friday as a DNP. He failed to get in any reps on Saturday but still received the questionable designation. Given that the game is on Monday, fantasy managers won’t have many contingency options left. With Jordan Whittington also expected to miss Week 2, the Rams’ No. 2 receiver will be either Konata Mumpfield or Xavier Smith if Nacua doesn’t suit up. Both players would be WR5/6 options in the event of a Nacua absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Rams tendered OL Justin Dedich, K Harrison Mevis, WR Xavier Smith.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: The team will maintain control of three players that surprised in 2025, including “thiccer kicker” Harrison Mevis. The tendering of exclusive rights free agents ties the three to the franchise through the 2026 season considering they are unable to negotiate with other teams. At least for now, it appears as if the Rams will continue forward with Mevis as their place kicker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Xavier Smith was not targeted in Los Angeles’ NFC Championship loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: What Smith did do was lose his footing on a punt return, letting the ball bounce off his chest and arms and right to the Seahawks. It immediately led to a touchdown in what finished as a four-point loss. Kyren Williams replaced Smith afterwards. Smith battled Tutu Atwell for a roster spot all season and eventually won out because of his work on special teams. Welp. An exclusive rights free agent in 2026, Smith was mostly a shot-play weapon and doesn’t figure to have a real fantasy role next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Xavier Smith caught 4-of-6 targets for 67 yards in the Rams’ Week 17 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: Smith operated as the WR2 with Davante Adams out of action, a role that would have likely been far less conducive to fantasy production had the Rams not been playing from behind throughout after going down 21-0 at the half. The significantly negative game script forced the Rams away from a 12 and 13-personnel base offense, allowing for more snaps for the speedy youngster. Adams is reportedly due back to the game-day roster in Week 18, meaning Smith is likely headed back to a situational role when the Rams take on the Cardinals to end their regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Xavier Smith caught both of his targets for 57 yards in the Rams’ Week 16 overtime loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: Smith was wide open for a 48-yard connection with Matt Stafford to set up a score. The 28-year-old certainly has some speed, but even with Davante Adams not available, there just aren’t enough targets to make him fantasy relevant at this stage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Xavier Smith caught 3-of-3 targets for 82 yards in the Rams’ Week 13 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: Entering the day with just 85 yards on the season, Smith unexpectedly led the Rams with 82 yards through the air in Sunday’s defeat. His longest gain on the afternoon came on a 51-yard catch thanks to a beautifully thrown deep ball by Matthew Stafford. It was a good outing for Smith, but with the low target count, we can chalk this performance up as a one-off.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Xavier Smith caught his only target for 14 yards in Los Angeles’ Week 10 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: He and Konata Mumpfield (33 snaps, zero catches) led the Rams’ WR3 platoon with Jordan Whittington only playing seven snaps. None of these players are worthwhile roster spots in this current incarnation of the Rams’ offense, though perhaps if a team thoroughly game-scripted the Rams they’d pop up. Nobody has really stepped up to fill the Tutu Atwell role to this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Rams WR Jordan Whittington (back) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: Whittington is scheduled to resume practicing, in a limited capacity today. While the return is good, he is seemingly on the wrong side of questionable for this divisional matchup. Whittington was out-targeted by rotational WR Xavier Smith 3-0 last week, and currently does not need to be rostered in re-draft formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.headline: Tutu Atwell caught his only target for four yards in the Rams’ Week 1 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-smi.analysis: Atwell and Xavier Smith (1/36 on his only target and snap) were the only non-Puka Nacua and Davante Adams receivers to have a catch in Week 1. Jordan Whittington was third on the team amongst receivers in snaps with 30, while Atwell had 25. Atwell is on pace to earn $580,000 per target on his one-year, $10 million contract. He’s not on pace to be fantasy relevant barring injuries ahead of him in the pecking order.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Cardinals placed QB Gardner Minshew (elbow) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: Officially he’ll miss at least four weeks, but Adam Schefter reports he’s not expected to play again this season, which essentially confirms that he tore his UCL without actually confirming it. There’s no current timeline for his return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Cardinals fear Gardner Minshew may have suffered a torn UCL in Week 9’s loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: If this proves to be the case, then Minshew played the entire second half with the injury, gutting things out for the Cardinals against a top-notch Seahawks defense. Minshew will undergo more tests to confirm the severity of his injury, but it now looks as if the Cardinals will be turning things over to rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who threw for 188 yards and one touchdown in his lone preseason game. Beck could be in for a rough few weeks, and the Cardinals’ receiving corps looks suddenly depleted with Marvin Harrison Jr. now on the Texans and Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (leg) both done for the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Gardner Minshew (elbow) could miss Week 10’s game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: Minshew took a hard hit to his right elbow/arm in Sunday’s loss to the Seahawks and is now undergoing tests to determine the severity of his injury. He managed to play through the game, but if he is unable to go in Week 10 against the Rams, rookie Carson Beck would be in line to make his first career start. Minshew threw for 166 scoreless yards against a stout Seahawks defense, but led a comeback victory in just one half of play against the Cowboys the previous week. With recent reports of Michael Wilson (neck) being lost for the season, both Minshew and Beck would be best left on waivers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said he did not consider benching Gardner Minshew for Carson Beck at any point in Arizona’s Week 9 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: We don’t believe him. But it really doesn’t matter because Beck will get his chance at some point in the coming weeks. The Cardinals’ rookie looked good in the preseason Hall of Fame game, though it is unclear whether he can do enough to warrant QB2 treatment as a pure pocket passer. The Cardinals’ schedule softens after matchups against the Rams and Chiefs over the next two weeks. Beck should have a chance to play in Week 12 against the Commanders, if not sooner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Gardner Minshew completed 21-of-30 passes for 166 yards in the Cardinals’ 17-3, Week 9 loss to the Seahawks, adding four yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: To be fair, the matchup in Week 9 was far different than the one Minshew erupted in last week, with the Seattle defense placing the clamps on the Cardinals from the first kick, holding them to just 198 total yards of offense on the down night. The only points mustered came on the team’s first possession, with three of their five first half possessions resulting in three-and-outs. The Cardinals saw the football only thrice following the break, getting stopped after achieving first and goal from the four on their final possession of the game. It was an outing to forget for all parties. Minshew remains likely to be the starting quarterback, at least in the immediate future, but the looking presence of rookie Carson Beck could be accelerated if the former returns more games like this one. Up next for the Cardinals are the Rams in Week 10, where Minshew will be nothing more than a streamer in two-quarterback leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Gardner Minshew will start in Week 9 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: After leading a second-half comeback against the Cowboys in which he threw for 188 yards and three touchdowns on 17-of-23 passing, the move to Minshew felt inevitable. Now, the eighth-year journeyman will have a chance to make his first start for the Cardinals in what’s sure to be a tough road matchup against the Seahawks. Minshew has long proved his value as a serviceable backup in the league and should provide enough to keep the fantasy stocks of Trey McBride and Michael Wilson up, but he could be in for a tough outing against a top-flight Seahawks defense. He shouldn’t be treated as anything more than a desperation streamer in 2QB/superflex leagues, while Wilson’s expectations should fall somewhere in the WR3 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Gardner Minshew completed 17-of-23 passes for 188 yards and three touchdowns in Arizona’s 33-30, Week 8 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: Minshew appeared to get better blocking and be more accurate and on-time with his passes than Jacoby Brissett. He also got a few major long gains from Tyler Allgeier en route to rallying the Cardinals from a 17-3 deficit. Minshew should have had a walkoff 13-yard touchdown pass to Michael Wilson with six seconds left, but kicker Chad Ryland missed the extra point. In overtime, after an initial three-and-out, Minshew completed just one pass as Wilson and Allgeier ran the Cardinals into field-goal range for the win. Hard to see how the Cardinals would bench Minshew after how this looked, though he certainly shouldn’t be considered a firm rest-of-season starter just yet. Minshew Mania will likely figure into the QB2 superflex mix in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter named Gardner Minshew and Mac Jones as potential trade candidates for the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: Jaxson Dart will miss the rest of the regular season, though there’s hope he could return for a postseason run. Schefter noted that Minshew played under Giants OC Matt Nagy in Kansas City, giving him some familiarity with the team’s scheme. He also mentioned that it will not be cheap to pry Jones away from the 49ers. Jimmy Garoppolo is out there as well. He is a free agent and is reportedly still interested in playing, “in the right situation.” For now, the Giants are going to roll with Jameis Winston. Jake Haener will back him up. They will likely add someone as an extra backup option, but Winston is an interesting QB2 for fantasy purposes until they make a bigger addition.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Cardinals ruled out QB Carson Beck (rib) for the team’s preseason Week 1 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Beck suffered a rib injury in the Cardinals’ Hall of Fame game against the Panthers. Despite feeling “soreness,” he managed to practice this week. The Cardinals “decided to keep him out tonight as a precaution and to allow more time to heal.” This pours a little cold water on Beck’s moderate hype, but the reporting suggests that the injury is not overly concerning. Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett will start, and presumably be relieved by QB Kedon Slovis at some point. No word yet on QB Gardner Minshew’s potential involvement tonight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the Cardinals and QB Jacoby Brissett “reached agreement today on a reworked contract.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: Brissett was scheduled to make up to $4.88 this year, in the final year of his old deal. His new contract increases his compensation for this season, but he is still scheduled to hit free agency next offseason. The new deal includes a $15.5 million base salary. He can make up to $21 million via incentives. Things can always change in-season, but this appears to be clear-cut starter money — and it’s good news for Cardinals pass catchers. Although the Cardinals struggled to win games with Brissett under center last year, he was a very productive passer. Theoretically, he should be able to support TE Trey McBride and likely one of WR Marvin Harrison Jr. or WR Michael Wilson reliably. Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur confirmed that the plan is for Brissett to start in Week 1 against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: Eagles waived RB Jaydon Blue.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: Not the first time this season they’ve done this, so we’re expecting a practice squad reunion here. Blue played eight offensive snaps in two weeks on the active roster and does not need to be on your fantasy team at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: Eagles signed RB Jaydon Blue from the practice squad to the active roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: Blue was called up as the replacement for Dameon Pierce, who was placed on injured reserve this week. Saquon Barkley entered Week 7 with a lingering hamstring issue. He then suffered a back injury and was in and out of the lineup for the remainder of the game. With little left to play for, the Eagles may choose to put their star running back on ice for a while. That would leave Blue and Elijah Mitchell as the next men up. Mitchell was the RB3 for Philly in Monday’s game, but he wasn’t signed to the active roster. Our money is on Blue seeing more work this week, though it’s a messy situation at best.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: Eagles placed Dameon Pierce on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: Jaydon Blue was signed from their practice squad to the active roster in a corresponding move. Pierce went down with an injury on a kickoff return in the fourth quarter of Monday’s game. The team has not announced the exact injury yet, but Pierce will now miss a minimum of four games. Blue will back up a still-very-injured Saquon Barkley. Barkley returned from his hamstring injury in Week 7, only to suffer a back injury in the process. Blue has an outside chance at starting for the Eagles this week, making him worth a look on waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: Eagles waived RB Jaydon Blue.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: They tacked on a waived/injured listing for Carson Steele, leaving the backfield with just Saquon Barkley and Dameon Pierce on the active roster. Blue did not officially get into a game with the Eagles after signing at the end of August. He’ll look to catch on elsewhere.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: Carson Steele left Week 6 against the Panthers with a shoulder injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: Steele caught a screen pass in the flats and lowered his head to try and run over the defender. He came up holding his shoulder and had to have the shoulder immobilized as he walked into the locker room with his pads off. It had the look of a dislocation, which would mean Dameon Pierce and Jaydon Blue are the only two healthy running backs for the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: Eagles ruled out RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) for Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: It was pretty clear that this was where things were headed when Barkley was unable to practice on Wednesday and Thursday. We do not yet know Barkley’s official Friday practice participation level, but he was not seen practicing during the portion of practice open to the media. Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue will likely split touches this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: Barkley is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for his team’s Week 6 game against the Panthers, potentially leaving Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue to split touches. Hopefully, reports clarify whether Pierce would handle a sizable workload as the de facto starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Tank Bigsby will have core muscle surgery and be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: Rapoport reports there are hopes that Bigsby will be back “in six weeks or shorter.” The 24-year-old back will be required to miss at least four games now that he’s headed for an IR stint. With Saquon Barkley (hamstring) also at risk of missing at least one game, third-string RB Will Shipley could be in line for a busy day in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Shipley rushed six times for 23 yards in Sunday’s loss to the Rams, but could be a sneaky option in PPR leagues given his pass-catching profile during his days at Clemson, when he caught 85 passes over three seasons. It also wouldn’t be surprising if Dameon Pierce or Jaydon Blue were promoted off the practice squad and saw early down touches while Shipley serves in more of a third-down role. There’s a lot to figure out here over the next few days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Cowboys “are bracing for an extended absence” after RB Malik Davis suffered a hip injury on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: Regarding Davis’ injury, Fowler’s source said simply, “it’s bad.” The Cowboys’ No. 2 running back is undergoing further testing, but we expect them to place him on injured reserve before long. The Cowboys waived RB Jaydon Blue and RB Phil Mafah last month. Blue has since signed with the Eagles’ practice squad. The Cowboys have RB Emari Demercado on the active roster behind RB Javonte Williams. Currently, only RB Israel Abanikanda is on the practice squad in Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.headline: Eagles signed RB Jaydon Blue to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaydon-blu.analysis: Blue was waived by the Cowboys and went unclaimed, and the 2025 fifth-round pick will remain in the NFC East. He’ll begin the campaign behind Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley as backups to Saquon Barkley, but some strong performances in practice could give the 22-year-old a chance to receive touches in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Cowboys signed RB Kendre Miller to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: Assuming all goes well, he’ll likely be elevated to be Javonte Williams’ backup this week. Dallas also has Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin as runners on the practice squad, so one of them may also get the first crack at being Williams’ backup as Tyler Goodson nurses a knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Free agent RB Kendre Miller is visiting the Cowboys on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: With Tyler Goodson dealing with a knee injury suffered late in Sunday’s game against the Colts, Miller could find himself in a backup role behind Javonte Williams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Saints released RB Kendre Miller.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: The team brought back Audric Estime to their practice squad earlier in the week, releasing Miller Saturday. The moved comes after the veteran played 137 offensive snaps for a backfield missing its top option for most of the season. Miller had a 20-carry game for the Saints three short weeks ago and now finds himself without a home. Expect him to land on a practice squad in short order.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Kendre Miller rushed 20 times for 70 yards in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: Milles led the Saints backfield in snaps and touches, adding two receptions for zero yards to his 70 scoreless rushing yards. He is the clear lead runner for the Saints and was tackled at the one-yard line on two separate drives, coming up just short of a touchdown to salvage his fantasy day. Miller’s lack of involvement in the passing game caps his fantasy ceiling but rushing volume makes him a low-end RB3 for Week 7 against a solid Steelers defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Kendre Miller rushed 10 times for 30 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: Miller led the backfield in carries, giving up three to Alvin Kamara and two to CJ Donaldson. Kamara saw the most targets at two, but Donaldson led the way in snaps. This is a true three-headed monster of a backfield, but Miller has at least settled in as the primary early-down option. With game script likely on his side versus the Giants in Week 6, Miller will be a low-end RB3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: Kamara briefly left the Saints’ Week 4 game against the Falcons to deal with a knee injury. Today, he is sidelined by a back injury. It’s perhaps unsurprising for a 31-year-old player who has clearly lost a step at this point in his career. He is backed up by Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson. Either player can be stashed in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Saints placed Travis Etienne on injured reserve with a hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: This is a tough break. The Saints’ high-priced free agent signee will be sidelined for at least four games. Their Week 8 bye makes him eligible to return in Week 9. Veteran RB Alvin Kamara is the next man up, followed by RB Kendre Miller. Both should be rostered in 12-team leagues. Kamara will likely get the first crack at the starting job, but he has struggled to play efficiently this season, and coach Kellen Moore gave RB CJ Donaldson the backfield’s first green zone touch last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) “will miss time” and that a timeline for his return has not yet been determined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: It’s unclear how much time Etienne will miss, but it wouldn’t be surprising if this became an injured reserve stint. Alvin Kamara could find himself in a more elevated role next week, perhaps with Kendre Miller joining him in a committee. Etienne exited Week 3’s loss to the Raiders with the injury after rushing for 57 yards on 13 carries. It had already been a tough scene for Etienne-reliant fantasy managers this year just based on how the results on the field were going; this won’t help.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Kendre Miller rushed four times for 14 yards in the Saints’ Week 3 loss to the Raiders, adding two receptions for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: Miller dealt with an illness this week, but today’s performance can hardly be called sick. Miller had a chance to carve out a role after Travis Etienne aggravated his hamstring injury, but he didn’t do much with the opportunity. If Etienne cannot play, Miller will be a touchdown-dependent FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Kendre Miller (illness) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 3 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: He returned to practice today and practiced in full after missing Thursday to an illness. That’s not exactly a guarantee he’ll play; he was a healthy scratch last week behind Alvin Kamara.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.headline: Vikings released WR Odell Beckham Jr.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.analysis: Beckham was not targeted in his two offensive snaps yesterday. The idea of Odell Beckham being a good wideout at 34 is really fun, and the reality is that he’s played 22 offensive snaps for two teams this year. Back to the practice squad he goes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.headline: Vikings signed WR Odell Beckham from their practice squad to the active roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.analysis: Beckham landed on the Vikings’ practice squad after being released by the Giants. He appeared in three games for New York and did not record any stats. Beckham hasn’t appeared in any games for Minnesota this year, but he’ll now be a member of their 53-man roster going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.headline: Vikings signed Odell Beckham, Jr., formerly of the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.analysis: Beckham, 33, was released by the Giants last week after getting almost no playing time in the season’s first few games. In Minnesota he will reunite with Kevin O’Connell, who worked with OBJ during his stint with the Rams. With Justin Jefferson (ankle) sidelined last week, Jordan Addison led Minnesota wideouts with 39 percent of the team’s air yards and 16 percent of the targets. Jauan Jennings, meanwhile, had one target while running 95 percent of the team’s routes. Beckham could operate as the team’s WR2 while Jefferson is sidelined. In the Vikings’ ultra run-heavy offense, that probably won’t matter for fantasy purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.headline: Giants released Odell Beckham, Jr.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.analysis: Beckham’s reuniting with his former team lasted all of three games, during which Beckham was targeted once on 11 pass routes. An afterthought in the New York offense, OBJ will look to land in an offense that might use his diminished skills. NFL insider Jordan Schultz said both the Giants and Beckham “decided a mutual parting was best for everyone.” It’s hard to imagine who would want Beckham at this point in his fading NFL career. He has nine catches since the start of the 2024 regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-4 targets for 25 yards in the Giants’ Week 1 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.analysis: The rookie wide receiver showcased a polished all-around skillset, reinforcing offseason reports that he had locked down the WR2 role opposite Malik Nabers. His 6'4, 220-pound frame was on full display as he was continually utilized as both a down-blocker and blocker in the second level on runs, something that should allow him to continue to operate as the clear-cut WR2 for the Giants throughout his rookie campaign. That said, the box scores highlights the obvious distinction that his snap rate — he led all Giants wideouts with 50 — won’t always translate to fantasy production while playing alongside Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely, the latter two of whom commanded 17 targets on 29 Jaxson Dart pass attempts. The good news is that he played well ahead of veterans Darnell Mooney and Odell Beckham Jr., with Mooney having 39 snaps and Beckham just 11. Fantasy managers are best off viewing Fields as a high-end stash at the end of benches for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports that WR Odell Beckham has officially made the Giants’ roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.analysis: Beckham’s spot on the depth chart is unclear, but he is unlikely to warrant FLEX treatment this season. Rookie WR Malachi Fields is reportedly slated for WR2 duties, and both WR Darius Slayton and WR Darnell Mooney could play ahead of Beckham. This is more of a feel-good story than an actionable fantasy-related item.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.headline: Odell Beckham caught 3-of-6 targets for 53 yards in the Giants’ preseason game against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.analysis: Darnell Mooney and Malachi Fields rested. Malik Nabers, still recovering from his 2025 ACL tear, was held out. Beckham drew the start along with the rest of the second-string offense. His stat line was impressive and it nearly went stratospheric when he burned the Jets’ secondary for a would-be 70-yard touchdown. Jameis Winston overthrew the pass and Beckham was unable to haul it in despite laying out for the catch. Per the eye test, Beckham still has something in the tank, even if that something is likely just good enough for a depth role. He isn’t a lock to make the Giants’ roster, but this preseason showing certainly helped.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.headline: Speaking on the Breaking Big Blue podcast, ESPN’s Jordan Raanan said he believes Odell Beckham Jr. is the “leader in the clubhouse” to win the final WR spot in camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.analysis: Things are just getting underway for the Giants as they open camp, so there’s a lot that could play out between now and then. Beckham, 33, signed with the Giants this offseason after pleading for one more chance with the team that originally drafted him in 2014, and got his wishes when he inked a one-year deal in June. Beckham did not suit up for a team last season and caught just nine passes for 55 scoreless yards in the nine games he appeared in for the Dolphins in 2024. We never expected him to make much of a fantasy impact even if he were higher on the depth chart, but Beckham securing the final spot in the WR room would all but cement his status as a lightly-used role player for the Giants this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.headline: Fox Sports’ Ralph Vacchiano believes Odell Beckham, Jr. will be the Giants’ third or fourth receiving option “at best.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.analysis: Beckham, who reunited with the Giants on Monday after eight years away from the team, will “likely spend camp behind veteran Darnell Mooney, rookie Malachi Fields, Calvin Austin and maybe more,” Vacchiano said. “He might have to battle for practice reps with veterans Braxton Berrios and JuJu Smith-Schuster,” journeyman who recently signed with the wideout-needy Giants. Headed into his age-34 season following a raft of injuries, Beckham “probably can’t” offer any tangible help for a New York offense in need of pass-catching upside outside of Malik Nabers, who is returning from a major knee injury. Beckham since the start of the 2022 season has 44 receptions for 610 yards. Vacchiano said OBJ’s most important contribution to the 2026 Giants could be mentoring for the team’s young wideouts. Unless you’re in a fantasy league that awards points for mentoring, OBJ likely won’t be viable this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.headline: Giants signed WR Odell Beckham Jr.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/odell-beck.analysis: How much does a 33-year-old receiver who missed all of 2025 have left in the tank? We’re about to find out. After rumors of mutual interest between the Giants and OBJ, the two sides have officially reunited on what is presumably a one-year deal. It’s been a forgettable few years for Beckham, who hasn’t had a 1,000-yard season since 2019, and managed just nine catches for 55 yards in 2024 and generated little to no interest last offseason while also being handed a six-game suspension for violating the league’s PED policy. While he’s undoubtedly the most decorated pass-catcher in the Giants’ receiver room, Beckham joins a cast of seasoned vets to go along with Malik Nabers, who is still recovering from a knee injury he suffered last season. He’ll likely face legitimate competition for snaps and seems unlikely to make much of a fantasy impact for managers in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams placed Jordan Whittington (back) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Not the Rams wideout we thought we’d be placing on injured reserve today. Whittington is, nevertheless, another hit to the depth of this wideout corps. It appears to be all systems clear for Konata Mumpfield to be the No. 1 wideout who is tasked with watching Los Angeles’ running backs in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Jordan Whittington (back) is questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Whittington has just two catches on the season, and with head coach Sean McVay suggesting he wants to get Tutu Atwell more involved, it seems unlikely Whittington will have a role as more than a returner even if he can play against Washington come Sunday. Trent McDuffie (back) is also questionable for that contest, and won’t practice Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams WR Jordan Whittington (quad) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Whittington is WR Puka Nacua’s (hip) direct backup, so he will be out there running a decent number of routes. Whittington has, however, never managed to establish himself as a reliable contributor. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues. Rams TE Colby Parkinson (knee) will be questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams WR Jordan Whittington (quad) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It is unclear whether the Rams will get their backup wide receiver back. Whittington cannot be treated as a reliable FLEX starter if he plays in place of WR Puka Nacua (hip) this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Jordan Whittington (quad) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Whittington missed Week 2 with the quad injury and doesn’t look likely to return this week. Xavier Smith and Konata Mumpfield each ran a little over half of the routes last week, though they combined for just three targets. With Tutu Atwell also in the mix for the WR2 role, there isn’t a clear fantasy winner here despite the bevy of injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams WR Puka Nacua (groin) is questionable for Week 2 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nacua did not practice for the second consecutive day Saturday, prompting the questionable designation for Monday Night Football. The issue is now being called a groin ailment and is reportedly unrelated to the psoas injury he dealt with during the offseason. Fantasy managers will want to start making alternate plans for their first-round pick considering the Rams don’t play until the final game of the week. Jordan Whittington is listed as doubtful with a quad injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams WR Jordan Whittington (quad) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Whittington is WR1 Puka Nacua’s direct backup, and Nacua appeared on the injury report today with a hip injury. Neither player practiced. This situation is worth monitoring closely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: The Athletic’s Jourdan Rodrigue believes the Rams may take a committee approach to the WR3 role this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Rodrigue listed WR Konata Mumpfield and WR Jordan Whittington as candidates for the gig, notably excluding rookie WR CJ Daniels. Daniels was viewed as the potential WR3 due to his blocking ability earlier this year. Rodrigue says it is instead Whittington who could serve as the “3B” blocker. Mumpfield reportedly “looks the part” as the “3A” receiving component. Will he return fantasy value reliably? Probably not. Earlier this month, Rodrigue’s colleague, Nate Atkins, said Mumpfield could be the next man up on the perimeter if WRs Puka Nacua or Davante Adams miss time. Rodrigue’s comments seemingly confirm this.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Jordan Whittington was not targeted in Los Angeles’ NFC Championship loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: From Weeks 1-12, the 2024 sixth-round pick was Los Angeles’ No. 3 receiver and played 52.4 percent of the Rams’ snaps. His fantasy relevancy peaked when the Rams headed to London without Puka Nacua and Whittington managed to reward managers with a 2/9 dud. Over the final five games of the season, dealing with a knee injury, he managed just 44 offensive snaps. Whittington isn’t a must-hold in dynasty leagues at this point, but it’s possible he was simply not himself while trying to play hurt. Either way, it’s hard to imagine much of a 2026 fantasy role for him here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) is questionable to play in the Wild Card Round against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Rams WR Jordan Whittington (knee) was initially listed as questionable, but later ruled out. Ferguson earned four targets in each of his last two games, catching five for 87 yards and two touchdowns. Having him on the field would be great for the Rams’ creative tight end usage. Whittington serves only as a rotational weapon at wide receiver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Falcons acquired G Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick from the Ravens for C Ryan Neuzil.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: Vorhees, in the final year of his rookie contract, appears to just be in this trade as salary ballast. He struggled in a large sample in 2025 and even with injuries to the interior line in 2026 has only received 81 snaps. The Falcons may opt to turn to Corey Levin as their starter at center rather than Vorhees.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said he is not ruling out Vega Ioane (knee) for Week 8 against the Bills yet.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: The Ravens’ mauling rookie guard suffered an MCL sprain in Week 7 against the Bengals. He is likely on the wrong side of questionable for Week 8, but Minter said he has been impressed by Ioane’s resilience and thinks he could recover quickly. In the meantime, OL Emery Jones Jr. and OT Andrew Vorhees will compete for the potential starting role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Andrew Vorhees (foot) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 6 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: The guard got in three limited sessions, he and Emery Jones Jr. (ankle) are both questionable. Ronnie Stanley, John Simpson and Roger Rosengarten were removed from the injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: Jurgens still has a chance to play, but we had hoped to see him upgrade to full participation. Ravens EDGE Mike Green (hamstring) was added to the injury report today as a limited participant. Ravens OG Andrew Vorhees (foot) joins him in the limited column. Ravens RT Roger Rosengarten (knee), LT Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) upgraded to full participation. Ravens OG John Simpson (groin) downgraded to a DNP.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: The Ravens’ new starting center is still recovering from his recent concussion, but he seemingly has a chance to face the Browns this week. Ravens EDGE Trey Hendrickson (finger) and S Kyle Hamilton (stinger) are practicing fully, while RT Roger Rosengarten (knee), OG John Simpson (groin), OG Andrew Vorhees (foot), LT Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) were limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Ravens RG Andrew Vorhees (foot) has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 4’s game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: Vorhees exited late in the first half against the Titans and was replaced by Emery Jones. Vorhees was making his first start of the season this week and played on just eight snaps in last week’s game against the Cowboys. Hopefully this isn’t anything too serious, as the Ravens’ interior offensive line has already been hit with multiple injuries this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Ravens RB Rasheen Ali (neck, IR) is questionable for Week 5 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: Ali opened the year on injured reserve after suffering a neck injury ahead of Week 1. He was a full participant in Friday’s practice, suggesting he has a good chance of suiting up this week. His return would give the Ravens another backup option behind Derrick Henry. Guard Andrew Vorhees is listed as questionable but appears likely to play versus the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Ravens OG Andrew Vorhees (ankle) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: Vorhees was listed as doubtful for Week 4 on Friday and got ruled out with inactives before kickoff. His return to practice suggests the second-year guard will be back on the field this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Ravens C Tyler Linderbaum (knee) is questionable for Week 4 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: Linderbaum was a full participant in Friday’s practice and should be good to go. Right tackle Patrick Mekari is also good to go despite dealing with a minor neck injury. Left guard Andrew Vorhees, on the other hand, is doubtful. Though losing Vorhees isn’t ideal, getting two of the three banged up linemen on the field this week is a good outcome for Lamar Jackson and the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Tyler Linderbaum (knee) returned to practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: Linderbaum and fellow lineman Patrick Mekari (neck) both returned to practice after being DNPs on Wednesday. Left guard Andrew Vorhees, however, remained sidelined. Barring any setbacks, it appears safe to say Linderbaum and Mekari will both be good to go for Sunday’s contest against the Bills. Vorhees’ availability remains TBD.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-neuzi.headline: Ravens acquired C Ryan Neuzil from the Falcons for G Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-neuzi.analysis: Neuzil, 29, was in the final year of a two-year extension signed in the 2025 offseason. He’s played reasonably well, with a 77.4 PFF blocking grade in 2025 and a 65.1 blocking grade in 2026. The Ravens, somehow always in need of a center, find a nice piece here at the deadline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-neuzi.headline: Falcons re-signed C Ryan Neuzil to a two-year, $9.5 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-neuzi.analysis: Neuzil’s contract includes $6.25 million guaranteed. The 27-year-old has spent the past three seasons with the Falcons as a former undrafted free agent. After starting eight games for Atlanta’s offensive line last season, Neuzil entered restricted free agency this offseason. He now returns to the Falcons with a two-year contract to enter the season as the team’s starting center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-neuzi.headline: Falcons signed OG Ryan Neuzil to a one-year extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-neuzi.analysis: The third-year pro has appeared in 26 games for the Falcons over the previous two seasons, four of which were starts. He’ll bring continuity to an offensive line that ranked in the top 10 in 2023.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney (chest) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: We only blurb Mooney injury reports, not Mooney game lines. There’s probably a lesson to be learned from that for fantasy managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney (chest) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: A “chest” designation accompanied the practice status Monday, which would be a new injury for the veteran wide receiver. Either way, the expectation is that Mooney will be available to face the Commanders on Thursday Night Football in a short week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney (neck) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: Mooney should be good to go this week, but he does not need to be on fantasy football rosters. Giants TE Theo Johnson (neck) was limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-8 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: Fields saw a season-high eight targets, but caught just two of those passes for 19 yards. The Giants passing game behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely isn’t productive for fantasy purposes. Darnell Mooney had a carry for 20 yards while Charlie Jones caught 2-of-3 passes for 66 yards. Fields is the best option past Nabers and Likely, but he can be left on fantasy benches for Week 7 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney (neck) is not on New York’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: Mooney turned seven targets into 14 yards last week and does not need to be trusted to do better this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney (neck) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: Mooney’s participation puts him on track to face the Saints in Week 6. He does not need to be in 12-team lineups, and his presence, unfortunately, keeps Malachi Fields from potentially playing in a full-time role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney (neck) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: He still has multiple practices left to improve his status. If Mooney were to miss time, Malachi Fields, who is tied with him for third on the team in targets, could see his role expand, though target volume could be limited behind Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney caught 2-of-3 targets for 26 yards in the Giants’ Week 3 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: Mooney has exactly two catches in each of his first three games as a Giant. He has hit on a few chunk plays in New York but isn’t seeing enough targets to be a weekly fantasy option. He is not on the FLEX radar for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney caught 2-of-3 targets for 48 yards in the Giants’ Week 2 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: Mooney played well behind Malik Nabers and rookie Malachi Fields but was able to cash in on a 33-yard reception to pad his counting stats in the loss. Fantasy managers of Nabers will want to track his status closely in the coming week after the talented youngster briefly departed with a shoulder injury. An absence could thrust Mooney into a near every-down role against the Titans in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-4 targets for 25 yards in the Giants’ Week 1 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: The rookie wide receiver showcased a polished all-around skillset, reinforcing offseason reports that he had locked down the WR2 role opposite Malik Nabers. His 6'4, 220-pound frame was on full display as he was continually utilized as both a down-blocker and blocker in the second level on runs, something that should allow him to continue to operate as the clear-cut WR2 for the Giants throughout his rookie campaign. That said, the box scores highlights the obvious distinction that his snap rate — he led all Giants wideouts with 50 — won’t always translate to fantasy production while playing alongside Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely, the latter two of whom commanded 17 targets on 29 Jaxson Dart pass attempts. The good news is that he played well ahead of veterans Darnell Mooney and Odell Beckham Jr., with Mooney having 39 snaps and Beckham just 11. Fantasy managers are best off viewing Fields as a high-end stash at the end of benches for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Kyle McCord is set to make his NFL debut against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: McCord! Daniel Jones throwing to Ashton Dulin! All the stars are here in Week 10! Even in an elevated matchup, there’s little reason to believe that McCord will be more than a bottom-five superflex option this week. And this might wind up being one of his good starts, if indeed the Dolphins commit to giving him multiple cracks while Malik Willis is on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said the team traded for Kyle McCord to be the team’s No. 2 quarterback, but that he expects recently-claimed Brady Cook to “make a push.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: Riveting situation. The main fantasy takeaway here is probably something like “if Malik Willis gets hurt this year, all Dolphins pass-catchers will take major downgrades.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Dolphins acquired QB Kyle McCord from the Packers in exchange for a sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: The news was first reported by ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The draft pick going to the Packers is a 2028 sixth-round pick. After trading Quinn Ewers to the Jaguars, the Dolphins acquired their new backup QB in McCord, who had an impressive preseason. The Dolphins new GM and HC came from Green Bay this offseason and so did both of the quarterbacks on their active roster in McCord and starter Malik Willis. McCord was a sixth-round pick by the Eagles in the 2025 NFL Draft and is yet to appear in a regular season game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Eagles signed RB Audric Estime to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: The second-year back will get a fresh start in Philadelphia, perhaps eventually pushing A.J. Dillon off the roster. Also on Philadelphia’s practice squad are: LB Chance Campbell, WR Elijah Cooks, G Kenyon Green, TE E.J. Jenkins, CB Brandon Johnson, OLB Patrick Johnson, TE Cameron Latu, WR Terrace Marshall, QB Kyle McCord, CB Parry Nickerson, T Hollin Pierce, OLB Antwaun Powell-Ryland, CB Eli Ricks and S Andre Sam.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Ohio State freshman QB Kyle McCord completed 13-of-18 for 318 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Saturday’s 59-7 win over Akron.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: McCord (6'3"/210) got the start as CJ Stroud got the night off due to a shoulder injury. There is a reason why McCord was a five-star recruit, he looked great. He got the Buckeyes on the board when he hit Chris Olave in the back of the end zone for five yards. He later hit Jaxon Smith-Njigba a little short, but he was able to reach in front of the Akron defender and grab the 34-yard touchdown. His night was over midway through the third quarter as Jack Miller came in with OSU holding a comfortable lead. Even with the great performance by McCord, Stroud is still the guy. Ohio State will travel to Rutgers next Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Ohio State freshman QB Kyle McCord will start Saturday’s game against Akron, per Big Ten Network.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: With freshman starter C.J. Stroud down due to a shoulder injury, either McCord (6'3/210) or Jack Miller was in line to start Saturday night. McCord won out in the end, but it would not come as a surprise if Miller got some reps as well. Stroud is available, but only in case of an emergency.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Ohio State freshman QB Kyle McCord will compete in practice for the start against Akron.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: Coach Ryan Day said backup QB McCord (6'3"/210) and third-string QB Jack Miller will compete in practice for the starting role against Akron on Saturday. Cj Stroud (shoulder) will be an emergency-only option. Whether it’s McCord or Miller who get the start this week for the Buckeyes, it’s a one-time deal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Ohio State HC Ryan Day has not made a decision on a backup quarterback as of now.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: CJ Stroud is obviously this team’s starter and has been mentioned several times as early as this past offseason as a player who could become one of the top prospects at his position in the future granted that he shows to be what some have projected he can be as the season goes on.
