Buckeyes HC Ryan Day has said that he has not settled on a backup QB yet, though freshman Kyle McCord has largely been the projected favorite for the No. 2 spot. Ohio State also has junior QB J.P. Andrade, senior Jagger LaRoe and freshman Jack Miller are also on the depth chart at the position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Ohio State true freshman Kyle McCord is warming up as the second-string QB ahead of the Minnesota clash.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: McCord, a highly recruited five-star QB, seems to have seized the second string job over fellow freshman Jack Miller. McCord reportedly battled close with starter CJ Stroud but ultimately fell short.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Ohio State freshman QB CJ Stroud is the early leader in the competition for the starting job, according to HC Ryan Day.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: Stroud (6'3/215) is competing with Jack Miller and Kyle McCord for the right to fill the void left by Justin Fields, and the freshman has managed to separate himself in the eyes of his head coach. “We’re not gonna name a starter today, but I do think there has been a little bit of separation,” Day said on Monday. “C.J. has separated here over the last couple of weeks. ... I don’t know how much separation there is, but every day he’s been competing, taking care of the ball, he’s been a leader, and those are all some of the traits we’re looking for.” While Stroud stands to see an increase in first-team practice reps, it’s important to keep in mind that Day said that he isn’t ready to name a starter just yet. That gives Miller and McCord the opportunity to close the gap before the Sept. 4 opener against Minnesota.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Chiefs acquired WR Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Colts for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: It was an obvious fit. Downs will slot in as Kansas City’s No. 2 wideout behind Rashee Rice and his fantasy stock receives a slight upgrade — though we felt like we’ve spent all year saying that and never seeing any actual returns for it — while Xavier Worthy moves back to the undesirable FLEX shadow zone. The Colts had to make this trade as Downs was a free agent at year’s end, but it has left them with a completely indecipherable wideout room. Ashton Dulin is perhaps the No. 1 target Daniel Jones has outside of Tyler Warren and Jonathan Taylor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder believes Josh Downs “is finding that he is best suited to play the role he has always played.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: The Colts have given Downs the opportunity to expand his offensive involvement this year, but he has struggled to capitalize on it without Alec Piece (heel) on the field to keep defenses honest. Downs reportedly asked for a trade roughly two weeks ago, and per Holder, the relationship between Downs and the Colts isn’t “the best” right now. If they can’t get adequate trade value, they may choose to keep him, while also using the lack of a substantial offer as a counterpoint to his recent disgruntlement. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs caught 3-of-6 targets for 24 yards in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Downs saw numerous snaps in coverage by his younger brother, Caleb Downs, and was unable to return a usable fantasy outing for the seventh time in nine appearances for the Colts this season. The subject of significant trade speculation ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, Downs appears likely to be headed for a change of scenery in a contract year, with the Colts reportedly already holding an offer in hand. More to come from one of fantasy’s most disappointing mid-round selections.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts have told teams they’ve received an offer of a fourth-round pick for WR Josh Downs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: The Colts’ original asking price for Downs, who has requested a trade, was a third-round pick. Indianapolis has told teams they already have an offer of a fourth-round pick for the 25-year-old receiver, who is in the last year of his rookie contract. Downs is probably one of the more likelier players to be traded ahead of the deadline. Teams have also called the Colts about Keenan Allen, though he’s unlikely to bring back a similar trade return given his age.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that Josh Downs “leads the wide receiver market” ahead of the NFL trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Downs’ 2026 season has fallen short of expectations, but perhaps he has a chance to rebound. Breer believes acquiring Downs would “probably” cost a fourth-round pick. He is “one of a number of receivers on the market” at the moment, with the Chiefs and Steelers among the teams looking for help at the position. Breer adds that the 49ers are “open” to adding a wide receiver as well, but with their positional health improving, San Francisco is “less desperate than they were a couple of weeks ago.” The Steelers’ wide receiver corps might be too muddled for Downs to meaningfully increase his productivity, but landing in Kansas City or San Francisco would likely be good for him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams must find a way to trade for a wide receiver before the November 10th deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: The Rams’ resources are thin. They already traded away their 2027 first- and second-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. They also have just $8,000 in 2026 salary cap space, so restructuring the potential new add’s deal would be required. Atkins believes the Rams should consider Josh Downs as the top option due to his ability to beat man coverage and contribute as a returner. Other options, according to Atkins, include Calvin Ridley, Keenan Allen and Jauan Jennings, “for the likely cost of a Day 3 pick.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: A to Z Sports’ Charles Goldman reports that if the Chiefs trade for a wide receiver, the team “would like to acquire a long-term fixture rather than a one-year rental.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Chiefs coach Andy Reid told reporters today that general manager Brett Veach has been constantly sharing potential trade targets with the coaching staff for about a month. According to Goldman, the Chiefs could also target additions along the offensive and defensive lines, but he believes the team would “likely have to acquire a receiver through other means” before focusing on the trenches. There aren’t many free agency options right now, though, so it is unclear how this scenario would play out. Goldman notes that Josh Downs and Brian Thomas Jr. “have surfaced in trade discussions.” He does not think the Chiefs will make a move before Sunday, though a move early next week, before the November 10th trade deadline, is still possible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs caught 4-of-5 targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 8 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Downs’ score was something of a pity touchdown in a game the Colts were trailing 35-0 at the 3:59 mark of the third quarter. Jacksonville’s defense had a rare mixup, and Downs was roaming free in the end zone. Amazingly, it was his first touchdown of the year. That speaks to just how dire things have been for Downs in an offense with an ineffective Daniel Jones and ageless Keenan Allen. Downs, who of course must be held responsible for his own mediocre play, will have no shot at a 2026 fantasy revival unless he’s subject to a change-of-scenery trade ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he “wouldn’t be surprised” if the Chiefs trade for a wide receiver.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Rapoport then named Josh Downs and Brian Thomas Jr. as players to keep an eye on. Both wideouts are in the midst of down years and their teams have already leaked that they are on the trade block. Thomas Jr. would hopefully unlock the once-vaunted Patrick Mahomes deep ball. Downs, on the other hand, would be another underneath weapon for a passing attack that his simply asking too much of Rashee Rice right now. Both players’ fantasy stock would skyrocket via a trade.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Colts want a third-round pick for Josh Downs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: The Colts are already the league’s biggest sellers ahead of the trade deadline and they’re not done yet. While they get plenty of interest in Downs, a third-round pick might be too much to ask after his slow start to the year. Downs has 26 catches for 307 yards as we approach the midway point of the season. Downs is also set to become a free agent in the spring, meaning that he might play only a handful of games for his new team. On the other hand, his disappointing season can largely be written off as the product of a failing offense. Fantasy managers should at least hold onto Downs until the trade deadline, even if he’s barely a WR3 as things stand right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.headline: Panthers released WR David Moore.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.analysis: He’ll be a candidate for a practice squad spot if he wants to stay. Moore was released to make room for the activation of Xavier Legette off injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.headline: Panthers re-signed WR David Moore.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.analysis: The financials of the deal were not immediately made available. Moore managed only four appearances for the Panthers in 2025 due to a serious elbow injury and was made a healthy inactive for the team’s Wild Card loss to the Rams. Familiarity with head coach Dave Canales and his veteran presence in the locker room were enough to warrant a new contract, although he is likely to play behind Tetairoa McMillan, Xavier Legette, and Jalen Coker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.headline: Panthers declared LB Krys Barnes, C Nick Samac, DT Jared Harrison-Hunte, WR David Moore, and DE LaBryan Ray inactive for the Wildcard Round against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.analysis: No real surprises from one of the healthier teams entering the postseason as the Panthers attempt to knock off the Rams at home as 10-point underdogs. It is the franchise’s first home playoff game since 2015.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.headline: Panthers waived WR Hunter Renfrow.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.analysis: Renfrow, who was a big part of the Carolina passing offense in the season’s first couple weeks, hasn’t been active since mid-October. He ends the season with 25 receptions for 255 yards and two touchdowns, operating mostly from the slot. Renfrow, who has 103 catches for the Raiders in 2021, will likely catch on with a receiver-needy team this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.headline: Panthers activated WR David Moore (elbow) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.analysis: The veteran wideout has been on injured reserve since the end of September with a serious elbow injury, but could return for the postseason as the Panthers prepare to take on the heavily-favored Rams this weekend. The Panthers in a corresponding move waived veteran journeyman Hunter Renfrow, who had 25 receptions for 255 yards and two touchdowns for Carolina in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.headline: The Athletic’s Joe Person reports David Moore (elbow) “likely will miss multiple weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.analysis: Rookie sixth-rounder Jimmy Horn — you may remember him as Travis Hunter’s Colorado teammate — will get a chance to ply his trade in Moore’s absence, with Dave Canales saying he wants to “make sure he’s able to go out there and give us significant reps. We’ll carve out a role because there’s certainly things he can bring to our offense with his speed and ability to carry the ball and make yards.” Horn could make an interesting pickup in deeper leagues right now with Hunter Renfrow not exactly blossoming last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.headline: Panthers WR David Moore suffered an elbow injury in Carolina’s Week 4 game against the Patriots and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.analysis: Filling in for an injured Xavier Legette (hamstring), Moore injured his elbow in gruesome fashion on the game’s opening series. It further thins the Panthers’ already nonexistent receiver depth, but it has little ripple effect in fantasy football. Moore is likely looking at a stint on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.headline: Brycen Tremayne caught 2-of-2 targets for 15 yards in the Panthers’ Week 3 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.analysis: Tremayne got some early looks in the Panthers’ offense, catching Bryce Young’s first two completions of the game. He was not seen from again as the Panthers went run-heavy with the lead later on. The 25-year-old has been consistently getting 15-20 snaps per game and could see more run if Xavier Legette remains out long-term. Veteran David Moore started in Legette’s place, but caught just one pass for five yards. Neither Moore or Tremayne are fantasy-relevant regardless of Legette’s status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.headline: Panthers re-signed WR David Moore to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.analysis: Moore had a career season in 2024, managing a 32/351/3 receiving line after last being targeted more than 40 times in 2020. The veteran enters his age-30 season as Carolina’s No. 4 receiver behind Adam Thielen, Xavier Legette, and Jalen Coker. It’s possible that the Panthers will draft a receiver and give him even more roster spot competition. Moore has the special teams chops to hang on the back of a 53-man roster if needed, so this seems like a signing without any real downside for Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.headline: David Moore caught 1-of-3 targets for nine yards in the Panthers’ Week 18 win against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-moor.analysis: Moore ends the season with 32 receptions for 353 yards over 16 games, five of which he started and had a role in the Carolina passing offense. A journeyman wideout who hadn’t been on the fantasy radar since 2020 with the Seahawks, Moore was a somewhat reliable target for Bryce Young in an offense without much in the way of pass-catching threats. Moore, 29, will be an unrestricted free agent this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Colts won’t trade Jonathan Taylor before today’s trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Multiple teams, per Pelissero, offered a second-round pick. It sounds like Indianapolis was holding out for a first. Playing out the season in Indy, Taylor will likely retain RB1 value despite a gross situation. It should be noted that Seth McGowan had begun to cut into Taylor’s playing time a bit, but with the Colts now committed to Taylor for the short-term, it’s plausible that he’ll operate at a 70-75 percent of snaps player for the remainder of the season. McGowan retains contingency value in fantasy leagues but will not stumble into a major role barring injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder believes the Colts could receive “an 11th-hour offer” for Jonathan Taylor that convinces Indianapolis to trade him.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Holder’s sources are currently telling him that there is “not a strong indication” that the Colts will be busy making deals at Tuesday’s trade deadline, but he adds that “you can’t rule this out with Taylor.” The Colts already received an offer including a second- and a fifth-round pick. Holder wonders aloud whether a second- and a third-round pick could be enough for Indianapolis to trade him away. Reading between the lines, that could be the Colts leaking an asking price to him. We’ll find out for sure in less than 48 hours. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed 13 times for 46 yards in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, adding 18 yards on five receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Taylor also lost a key fumble in the fourth quarter following the team’s second takeaway of the game, leaving fantasy managers wanting more in what could have been his final game in Indianapolis. Taylor has been the subject of significant trade speculation and rumor as we head toward Tuesday’s trade deadline, although teams will need to take on his recently-signed contract extension that ties him to the Colts through the 2028 season. Things started off rough as Taylor was subbed out on third-and-goal from the two, watching from the sideline as Seth McGowan punched it in for the team’s only rushing score of the game. It did not get better from their for Taylor’s fantasy managers as the Colts played through consistently negative game script, limiting his volume in the process. Taylor’s next opponent remains uncertain, although he currently lines up to take on the reeling Dolphins in Week 10, at least as long as he remains with the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: NFL insider Josina Anderson reports the Giants “cooled on acquiring Colts RB Jonathan Taylor because of price.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: She added that the Giants have resolved to move on from the trade talks ahead of their Week 9 date with the Eagles. Things change quickly in the NFL and this report doesn’t guarantee that Taylor won’t be a Giant. On the other hand, Anderson’s reporting doesn’t leave much room error. With the Colts’ asking price reportedly being through the roof, the Giants are content with Cam Skattebo as their top back. Devin Singletary is expected to start this week with Skattebo banged up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Colts RB Jonathan Taylor “most likely” won’t be traded.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: An earlier report from the Athletic’s Jonathan Jones listed the Vikings and Giants as the favorites to trade for Taylor while the Seahawks, Packers and Broncos are still in the mix. Pelissero threw cold water on all of that by reporting no team has come close to offering what the Colts want for Taylor. Maybe that changes after Week 9, but if Taylor is stuck in Indianapolis, that’s probably the worst-case scenario for his rest-of-season fantasy value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the Giants are serious suitors for Jonathan Taylor, while the Broncos and Vikings might be less inclined to acquire him.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: All three teams have inquired about Taylor’s trade cost. Per Breer, the Colts either want a first-round pick or a draft pick package similar to what the Panthers received for Christian McCaffrey in 2023. The 49ers handed over 2023 second-, third- and fourth-round picks, and a 2024 fifth-rounder to acquire him. None of the three suitors have met either asking price yet. That said, the Giants have reportedly offered enough for Breer to label them “a serious suitor.” Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Jonathan Taylor said he has not requested a trade.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Taylor didn’t dwell on the question for more than a word, but he did confirm that no trade request has been made. The team’s desire to trade him is ultimately about rebuilding the roster after going all in on the ill-fated “Daniel Jones era.” With several teams reportedly interested and the Colts strongly motivated to recoup draft capital for the coming years, we expected a deal to get done before Tuesday’s deadline. For now, fantasy managers can keep Taylor in their lineups, as there’s been no indication that Taylor will be put on ice to protect his trade value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Colts plan to wait until after Week 9 against the Cowboys “before revisiting the offers on the table and making the trades that make sense on Monday and Tuesday.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Long story short, the Colts are trying to wring every last ounce of draft capital out of their roster and think teams will up their offers after Sunday’s games. Schultz named Jonathan Taylor, Josh Downs, and Grover Stewart as players who could be on the move. Daniel Jones’s name has also come up, though it’s hard to imagine another team paying even a late-round pick for his services given how dreadful he has been this year. All signs point to Taylor being moved early next week, but it’s clear the Colts are going to play hardball in trade talks. We still suspect he’s playing for a new team by Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Jonathan Taylor remains on the Colts roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Steichen mostly dodged questions about why the Colts would play Taylor in Week 9 if the team was in talks with contenders who might want to acquire the star running back before the NFL’s trade deadline. “Teams call all the time,” Steichen told reports. He said the team was focused on the Cowboys, their opponents in Week 9. Taylor seems more than likely to be dealt to another team in the coming weeks. That could be the Vikings, Bengals, Seahawks, or another contending team in need of backfield help.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: DNVR Broncos’ Zac Stevens reports that the Broncos are “going to try” to trade for Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Stevens said that this trade “could happen at any moment,” telling Broncos Country that they “might not want to go to sleep.” While this could be hyperbole, it sounds like Stevens is saying the trade could go down tonight. Stevens said he’s had conversations with multiple people on the matter, and the Broncos “know that this is not the time to wait and develop” young running backs. Stevens closed by reminding viewers that the Broncos were very interested in Breece Hall at one point, and added that there are likely other backup plans that the Broncos could be considering.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Jordan Schultz reports the Chargers “immediately shut down all inquiries” for Justin Herbert at the trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Schultz reports the Vikings called on Herbert, but the Chargers had no interest in moving on. It’s hard to understand what Herbert’s market value would have been — this has been one of the most disgusting outlier seasons for a previously good quarterback in recent memory — but the Chargers appear ready to move forward with him as their franchise quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Justin Herbert may have suffered a left-hand fracture in the Chargers’ 22-44, Week 9 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Last year, when Herbert injured his left, non-throwing hand, his trainers stabilized the hand, with extra padding and tape applied to his middle finger. The exact same thing happened today. Herbert fended off a pass rusher with his left hand before bracing himself with the same hand as he fell. Fortunately, he remained in the game long enough to complete a 58-yard touchdown pass to Quentin Johnston. After a trip to the blue medical tent, Herbert was on the sideline, helmet on, with his left hand and middle finger heavily taped and padded. However, he did not return. The Chargers’ pass protection remains a huge problem, allowing eight sacks on the day. Before exiting, Herbert completed 13-of-23 passes for 193 yards, one touchdown and one interception, rushing once for seven yards. Herbert told reporters post-game that he does not expect his left middle finger to be an issue going forward. We will know more once he undergoes imaging. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert entered the blue medical tent in Week 9 against the Texans after suffering an apparent left hand injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Herbert appeared to injure his left hand, and specifically his left middle finger, while fending off a pass rusher in the fourth quarter. He fractured the same hand, and seemingly the same digit, last year and underwent surgery to stabilize it in-season. We tentatively expect him to return after getting it taped up, but he will be playing hurt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 24-of-32 attempts for 257 yards and two interceptions in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams, adding four rushes for 15 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Coming off their bye week, the Chargers looked worse than ever on offense, with Herbert apparently confused as to where to throw the ball or how to conduct OC Mike McDaniel’s complex pre-snap motion scheme. Herbert had a negative EPA per drop back. Both of his picks were of the mind blogging variety, thrown directly to Rams defenders in the open field. Frustrated and dejected, Herbert continues his worst pro season for the winless Bolts. As usual, Herbert — who ranks 33rd in fantasy points per game — won’t be a fantasy option in Week 9 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: The Athletic’s Noah Furtado reports the Chargers will try to “simplify” the team’s offense in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Justin Herbert and the flailing Chargers skill position players have appeared almost comically confused about all the pre-snap motion OC Mike McDaniel uses. That came through in the team’s embarrassing Week 6 loss to the Chiefs when players were bumping into each other during pre-snap motion calls from Herbert. Head coach Jim Harbaugh acknowledged the team is considering narrowing the offensive playbook during their bye week. “Definitely looking at volume and where you can make it to where the players can understand,” Harbaugh said when asked about how Chargers players were adjusting to McDaniel’s complex offense. The Chargers have used pre-snap motion on 74 percent of their snaps, the fourth highest rate in the NFL. Last year they used motion on 56 percent of their snaps. Hopefully these adjustments lead to some production for the NFL’s worst offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 22-of-37 attempts for 205 yards and one interception in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs, adding five rushes for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Herbert’s hellish season continued unabated on Sunday against a Kansas City defense that swamped the beleaguered Bolts quarterback on seemingly every drop back. After throwing exactly one touchdown in each of his first five outings, Herbert didn’t have any against the Chiefs. He had a negative EPA per drop back and was 10 percent below his expected pass rate in the loss. Ladd McConkey was ruled out with a head injury in the first half, further complicating OC Mike McDaniel’s efforts to stop the bleeding for the LA offense. The team’s wideout injuries and the predictability of the offense means Herbert should be dropped in most one-QB fantasy formats ahead of the Chargers’ Week 7 bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter said the Chargers would not consider trading Justin Herbert.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Schefter reached out to the team after a league source told him the Chargers could get upwards of three first-round draft picks in exchange for Herbert. The Chargers source told Schefter the team has “never” discussed the idea of dealing Herbert, even as the Chargers start the season 0-5 and rank near the bottom in almost every offensive category. It would seem unlikely that the Chargers would consider trading Herbert even if they go all in on a rebuild following the 2026 season. Herbert, 28, who ranks 33rd out of 34 qualifying quarterbacks in EPA per drop back this year, is signed through the 2029 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 14-of-24 passes for 121 yards with a touchdown and interception while rushing for 54 yards and losing a fumble in the Chargers’ 23-17, Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Herbert was without his top wideouts, his top offensive lineman, and the fact he was able to put up even this type of statline is somewhat impressive, if you squint very hard. The 28-year-old quarterback was constantly under pressure, and was at his best when he was able to escape the pocket and use his underrated wheels. That being said, he could have had more turnovers than this, and his interception was an inexcusable throw right into the hands of the Broncos defender. Even if Herbert gets his weapons back, fantasy managers should be looking elsewhere in Week 6 in standard leagues with a tough matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Rashawn Slater suffered a high ankle sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: The injury, sustained during the Bolts’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, will cost Slater between four and six weeks, Rapoport said. It’s yet another massive blow for the struggling Chargers offense. Through Week 4 the Chargers rank 30th in ESPN’s pass blocking win rate and fifth in run blocking win rate. Justin Herbert’s weekly prospects take a hit with the oft-injured Slate sidelined, as do the prospects of LA’s pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 19-of-31 passes for 189 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions in the Chargers’ 30-23, Week 4 loss to the Seahawks while adding 40 yards on the ground on six attempts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: It really wasn’t this close. Herbert and Sam Darnold became the first quarterbacks since 1991 to throw interceptions on their first throws of their game. Things didn’t get less weird, nor less shaky for the now 0-4 Chargers. He threw both his picks to linebackers, and outside of a 26-yard scramble, there just wasn’t much there from a quarterback who had (much) loftier expectations coming into the year. His only touchdown was a flip to Kimani Vidal that left Los Angeles down two scores. There’s a lot of football left, but this is ugly. Herbert will try and get going in Week 5, but the Broncos make for a tough team to get that ship righted.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Fernando Mendoza will take over as Raiders starter following the trade of Kirk Cousins to Minnesota.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: We’re sure we’ll get something more official from the team once Klint Kubiak has a press conference, but this is the obvious move. The No. 1 overall pick will face a gauntlet in his first three games, starting with the defending champion Seahawks in Week 10. It’s not an immediate re-draft add situations outside of deep leagues, but Mendoza could eventually factor into the re-draft formula this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Vikings acquired QB Kirk Cousins from the Raiders for a 2027 third-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: And where did that bring you? Back to me. Cousins will likely take over as Minnesota’s starting quarterback in the near future, if not immediately. When that happens, Kyler Murray will head back to the bench for a second straight season — he’s droppable in most leagues at this point. Fernando Mendoza will take over as starting quarterback for the Raiders. Mendoza is best approached cautiously at this point in fantasy leagues. Cousins’ value likely remains stagnant — Klint Kubiak was already getting quite a bit out of him — but he provides the Vikings with a better floor at quarterback than what they were getting so it’s obvious after watching Carson Wentz play last night why this is happening.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Raiders plan to start Kirk Cousins “as long as possible.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Schefter added that the team does not feel their current four-game losing streak is the fault of Cousins. He threw for nine touchdowns in the first three games, all of which the Raiders won. Cousins has just seven touchdowns over his past four outings, though he has only thrown two interceptions and taken just five sacks during that stretch. The Raiders are probably right to lay the blame elsewhere. Still, No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is waiting in the wings. He is the future of the franchise, and his time grows closer with every Raiders loss. Vegas takes on the Jets this week. They then get a gauntlet of San Francisco, Seattle, and Denver. A 0-3 run that late in the season would likely spell the end of Cousins as their starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said “Kirk Cousins is our quarterback,” when asked about the possibility of making a change at QB ahead of Week 8.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Rather than let any speculation linger, Kubiak was quick to shut down any idea of a switch at quarterback heading into Week 8’s game against the Jets. Kubiak said, “There is no controversy” at quarterback at this time, while also adding that “Fernando [Mendoza] is going to play football” at some point this season. Kubiak said the team does not have a timeline for when Mendoza could eventually make a start, and said Cousins continues to play well despite the team’s recent struggles. Cousins will be firmly on the streaming radar this week against a Jets team that just allowed 28 points to the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders’ head coach Klint Kubiak said the team is “thinking about everything” in regards to the team’s QB situation after Week 7’s loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kubiak was asked about the possibility of switching from Kirk Cousins to rookie No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza, and said the team is considering “everything” while also making it sound like their struggles were more of a team issue. Cousins struggled in the early part of Sunday’s loss to the Rams, but managed some late touchdowns in garbage time to save his stat line. If the Raiders are considering a switch, it’s possible we’ll learn their decision by Wednesday, when they begin preparing for their Week 8 game against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Kirk Cousins is the starter “but if Fernando [Mendoza]'s number is called we have confidence in him.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: No real surprise after Mendoza’s mop-up appearance in Week 5. It doesn’t appear that he’s taken a major step towards unseating Cousins — who has played well — just yet. But it remains a reasonable bet to happen in the near future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Fernando Mendoza completed 6-of-8 passes for 48 yards in relief of Kirk Cousins in Las Vegas’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This doesn’t necessarily mean that Mendoza is going to take the reins this week; we expect Cousins to continue starting even if Raiders coach Klint Kubiak didn’t affirmatively get ahead of the situation in Sunday’s post-game. But Mendoza looked reasonable and this will obviously be something that will bubble up eventually. No. 1 overall picks don’t typically stay on benches too long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders named Kirk Cousins as the team’s Week 1 starter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: With input from Tom Brady, head coach Klint Kubiak will put the 38-year-old Cousins under center for the season opener against the Dolphins. Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, will serve as Cousins’ backup. How long this arrangement will last is anyone’s guess. A good start to the regular season could delay Mendoza’s first NFL start for a couple months but he’s almost certain to take over as the Vegas starter at some point in 2026. Mendoza should be stashed in most superflex formats and Cousins profiles as a decent QB2 in such formats for Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said he’s talking with Tom Brady “multiple times per week” about the team’s starting quarterback situation.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: An NFL head coach consulting with an NFL announcer on who his team should start under center is a brave new world for the league. It looks like the Raiders are set on Kirk Cousins to start Week 1 against the Dolphins after Fernando Mendoza’s spotty preseason play and struggles in training camp. Look for Cousins to target his short-area pass catchers relentlessly, like he did last year in Atlanta. It won’t be long before Mendoza gets a shot at starting duties. He should be rostered in most superflex leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Raiders QB Kirk Cousins is expected to be named the starter eventually.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Appearing on NFL Live Friday afternoon, Fowler said that people inside the Raiders’ building and around the league still expect Cousins to be named the starter. Raiders HC Klint Kubiak declined to name a starting quarterback Friday morning. Following the loss of Thursday’s preseason game against the 49ers, Kubiak said rookie Fernando Mendoza needs another three preseason games before going as far as mentioning that Mendoza’s practice reps will decline once the regular season begins. While Kubiak continues to drag his feet when it comes to the official announcement, all signs still point to Cousins being named the starter at some point eventually.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.headline: Bills acquired S Amani Hooker and a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Titans for a 2027 second-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.analysis: It’s not Budda Baker, but Hooker has a respectable 81.0 PFF defensive grade in 495 snaps this season and has always helped as a run defender. The second-round pick is a steep price to pay and it’s quite a coup for the Titans to get that kind of return, even if they had to throw in another pick to get it done. This is all about solidifying Buffalo’s defense for a Super Bowl run for the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.headline: Titans activated S Amani Hooker off the active/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.analysis: He spent roughly four days there, but he passed a physical today. The 28-year-old is expected to be a veteran presence for the Titans’ secondary this year as they break in second-year player Kevin Winston Jr. alongside him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.headline: Titans placed OT JC Latham on the physically unable to perform list with an undisclosed injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.analysis: Latham and Hooker are reportedly recovering from spring injuries. We suspect these are active/PUP designations because team reporter Jim Wyatt writes, “players placed on the PUP list during training camp can come off of it at any time,” indirectly indicating that these are not season-ending placements. The Titans also signed OT Zach Thomas and waived OT Ryan Hayes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.headline: Titans agreed with S Amani Hooker on three-year, $48.6 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.analysis: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the deal includes $29 million in guaranteed money. While more details about the contract are unknown, this is already Hooker’s third contract just months after turning 27 in June. He’s started at least nine games for the Titans in four consecutive seasons, but is arguably coming off his best season with 71 tackles and a career-high five interceptions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.headline: Titans placed S Amani Hooker (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.analysis: Hooker did not practice at all this week before going on injured reserve, indicating he left Week 15 with the issue. With the Titans eliminated from the playoff hunt, Hooker’s season is over. He totaled seven pass breakups and one interception across 13 games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.headline: Titans S Amani Hooker was cleared to return to practice, but he remains in concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.analysis: Obviously, with Hooker still in protocol, there are steps remaining in his recovery, but him already being cleared to practice is a good sign for his potential availability this weekend against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.headline: Titans CB Kristian Fulton (hamstring) will not play in Week 2 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.analysis: In addition to Fulton, safety Amani Hooker (concussion) has also been ruled out. This could open the door for the Chargers to have a big day through the air against a Titans defense that allowed Derek Carr to throw for 305 yards in Week 1. Justin Herbert, Keenan Allen, and Mike Williams could all be in for big days with Fulton and Hooker both out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.headline: Titans S Amani Hooker (shoulder) was ruled out in Week 8 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.analysis: Hooker went down early in the game but wasn’t ruled out until the third quarter. When healthy, Hooker plays on every defensive snap for the Titans. He has an interception, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery in four appearances this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.headline: Titans declared DB Amani Hooker, DB Theo Jackson, DB Ugo Amadi, OL Le’Raven Clark, LB Wyatt Ray, LB Ola Adeniyi, and LB Zach Cunningham inactive for Week 4 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.analysis: The defensive injuries continue to pile up for the Titans as they look to keep their head above water in the tight AFC South. The winner of this game suddenly could find themselves atop the division a quarter of the way through the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.headline: Titans signed S Amani Hooker to a three-year, $33 million extension through 2025.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amani-hook.analysis: A fourth-round pick in 2019, Hooker was entering the final year of his rookie contract. A rotational player early in his career, Hooker shined as a 12-game starter in 2021. He and Kevin Byard will form a quality safety duo over the next several seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: 49ers acquired WR Keenan Allen from the Colts for a 2027 sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Just what the 49ers needed: To get older at the skill positions. With Christian Kirk gone, Allen figures to fill a role for the 49ers and could still be fantasy relevant depending on Mike Evans’ health. It does seem unlikely he’ll draw the same sort of targets as he had been handling for the Colts, but the targets should be more effective. The Colts signed Allen off the street in August and flipped him for something as they realized they were going nowhere, so they’ve done well for themselves here. The wideout vacuum in Indianapolis may draw players like Ashton Dulin into fantasy consideration, especially if Josh Downs also moves later today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 4-of-8 targets for 26 yards in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen wasn’t targeted until late in the second quarter but picked up two receptions on back-to-back plays to tease fantasy managers in an otherwise poor outing. Things can’t get much worse in Indianapolis, with their decisions in the coming days ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline potentially allowing Allen to step into a more featured role in the second half of the season. Stay tuned as the Colts limp into a Week 10 matchup against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts have told teams they’ve received an offer of a fourth-round pick for WR Josh Downs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: The Colts’ original asking price for Downs, who has requested a trade, was a third-round pick. Indianapolis has told teams they already have an offer of a fourth-round pick for the 25-year-old receiver, who is in the last year of his rookie contract. Downs is probably one of the more likelier players to be traded ahead of the deadline. Teams have also called the Colts about Keenan Allen, though he’s unlikely to bring back a similar trade return given his age.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams must find a way to trade for a wide receiver before the November 10th deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: The Rams’ resources are thin. They already traded away their 2027 first- and second-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. They also have just $8,000 in 2026 salary cap space, so restructuring the potential new add’s deal would be required. Atkins believes the Rams should consider Josh Downs as the top option due to his ability to beat man coverage and contribute as a returner. Other options, according to Atkins, include Calvin Ridley, Keenan Allen and Jauan Jennings, “for the likely cost of a Day 3 pick.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 7-of-7 targets for 67 yards in the Colts’ Week 8 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: As is now the case every week, Allen easily lead the Colts in most every receiving category. That did not include targets — a returning Tyler Warren commanded 10 looks — but Allen out-gained him 67-18. Now Allen and fantasy managers must sit and wait to see what kind of moves the tanking Colts make ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. That could include non-roster changes like the benching of Daniel Jones. For now a low-end WR3, Allen could be valued much differently 10 days from now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 3-of-3 targets for 31 yards in the Colts’ Week 7 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen was second on the team in targets while leading in receptions and yards against the Vikings. He saw just 30 snaps but operated as a quick release valve over the middle of the field for Daniel Jones against a blitz-happy Vikings defense. In an otherwise low-volume day, Allen had another game with a high share of the Colts’ receiving output. He will be in the WR3 ranks ahead of a Week 8 matchup against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 8-of-11 targets for 82 yards in the Colts’ Week 6 loss to the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Each of Allen’s targets, receptions and receiving yards were new personal bests for his embryonic Colts career. Allen is doing what he’s supposed to be doing in Indy, but that’s not true for many of his teammates. Then again, we don’t really care in fantasy football, as Allen’s WR3 checks are clearing all the same. Allen’s short-area looks will be in high demand in Week 7 as Daniel Jones tries to survive the Vikings’ onslaught of blitzes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 5-of-9 targets for 45 yards in the Colts’ Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen did not play a full complement of snaps in his first week back from a groin injury. He played 32 of the team’s 71 snaps and ran a route on 28 of their 47 dropbacks. That makes him leading the team with nine targets even more impressive. Of course, the Colts were forced to throw almost 50 times because the Steelers made it a priority to contain Jonathan Taylor. It’s highly unlikely Daniel Jones throws that much going forward, but Allen remains the top target in the offense. The issue is that most of his targets are in the short-yardage areas of the field, so he is more of a fringe-FLEX option unless you’re in a full PPR league. Next week against the Titans is a good matchup for the Colts, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen (groin) is active for Week 5 against the Steelers
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen got in a full practice on Friday, so he seemed to be trending towards being active, but now we know for sure. With Jamel Dean out this week and Joey Porter Jr. now in Dallas, the Colts’ passing game gets a slight bump, which is good news for Daniel Jones, who really needs to get back on track. The Colts inactives are: LB Jaylon Carlies, WR Ashton Dulin, QB Riley Leonard, WR Darius Slayton, and G Dalton Tucker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Keenan Allen (groin) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen missed Week 4 with the groin issue but returned to practice this week and even managed a full session on Friday. The team still listed him as questionable, though he appeared to be on the right side of that designation heading into the weekend. Allen will be a low-ceiling WR4 for his date with the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joey-aguilar/0.headline: Cardinals signed QB Joey Aguilar off the Jaguars’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joey-aguilar/0.analysis: With Gardner Minshew looking at a lengthy absence, Aguilar figures to be Arizona’s No. 2 behind Carson Beck for the time being. Aguilar completed 17-of-20 passes for 230 yards and a touchdown in preseason action with the Jaguars after being signed as a UDFA after this year’s draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joey-aguilar/0.headline: Jaguars waived QB Joey Aguilar.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joey-aguilar/0.analysis: The news was first reported by ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. Aguilar joined the Jaguars in April as a UDFA from Tennessee, where he played one season. Aguilar turned 25 in June and is unlikely to be claimed by another team. Fowler adds that the Jaguars hope Aguilar returns to the practice squad, which seems like the most likely scenario.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joey-aguilar/0.headline: Jaguars signed Tennessee QB Joey Aguilar
https://www.nbcsports.com/joey-aguilar/0.analysis: The latest QB prospect to come out of Tennessee, Aguilar (6’3”/229) joined the Vols in 2025 after spending two seasons at Appalachian State, and like so many QBs before him, thrived in Josh Heupel’s scheme. Also, like previous Heupel signal-callers, Aguilar faces questions about his ability to make reads at the NFL level, and his accuracy numbers, which saw a massive bump in 2025 (67.3 completion percent), may prove unsustainable. Aguilar rushed for 553 yards and nine touchdowns in his three years of FBS play, showing some ability to make plays with his feet. His career 12.0 pressure-to-sack rate suggests he knows where to go with the ball or when to take off and run to avoid a loss, but he’s also proven to be careless at times, throwing 10-plus interceptions in all three seasons as a starter. He will be 25 at the start of this season, and will likely need to battle for a spot on the 53-man roster with a chance to stick around as a practice squad member.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.headline: Falcons released K Nick Folk.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.analysis: Folk, 42 after his birthday five days ago, had hit just 13-of-18 field-goal attempts this year after being the league’s most accurate kicker in 2023, 2024, and 2025. He’ll either resurface with a new club or have a Bluesky account in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.headline: Falcons signed K Jake Moody off Baltimore’s practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.analysis: They released Nick Folk in a corresponding move, leaving the Ravens holding nothing at the position currently as Tyler Loop is on injured reserve. Workouts to come for the Ravens. Moody will be a reasonable fantasy kicker provided he can do better than his 78.3 percent career field-goal conversion rate, which, of course, is not guaranteed in any way. At least he plays half his games in a dome now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.headline: Falcons signed K Nick Folk, formerly of the Jets, to a two-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.analysis: Folk, one of the NFL’s last millennials, made 28 of his 29 field goal tries last year for the Jets and is a career 85 percent kicker over 18 NFL seasons. The Falcons have made due at kicker since Younghoe Koo flamed out and will look to Folk for some short-term stability in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports Jets K Nick Folk is planning to play the 2026 NFL season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.analysis: Folk, 41, is entering year No. 19 in the NFL. He is the NFL’s most accurate kicker since 2023 and made 28-of-29 field goals last season. The veteran is slated to be a top free agent at the kicker position this offseason; whether Folk heads back to the Jets or kicks elsewhere, he will secure a short-term contract as long as he desires to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.headline: Jets signed K Nick Folk.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.analysis: Entering his age-41 season, Folk looks to have found a comfy starting gig in New York. UDFA Harrison Mevis is his competition for the job. Folk missed just one kick last year for the Titans in 47 tries between field goals and extra-point attempts. We’d consider him the favorite to win the job.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.headline: Jets hosted free agent K Nick Folk for a tryout on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.analysis: Folk kicked for the Jets from 2010 to 2016 and could find his way back to the Meadowlands. The 40-year-old vet played for the Titans last season, converting on 21-of-22 field goal attempts while also going 25-for-25 on his PATs. Folk has led all kickers in field goal percentage in each of the last two seasons and has made 11-of-12 attempts from 50-plus yards over that span. Despite his age, Folk doesn’t appear to have lost a step and will likely find himself kicking somewhere in 2025, even if it’s not with the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.headline: Titans signed K Joey Slye, formerly of the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.analysis: It’s possible this spells the end for 40-year-old Nick Folk, who has spent the last two seasons with the Titans. Slye kicked last season for the Patriots, converting on 26-of-33 attempts while going 6-for-9 on distances of 50 or more yards. He hit a career-long 63-yard field goal in last season’s Week 4 game against the 49ers. Slye is a career 81.7 percent field goal kicker, and could have the inside edge to win whatever kicker competition comes his way once training camp starts up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.headline: Titans K Nick Folk (abdomen) will not play in Week 18 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.analysis: Matthew Wright will again kick for the Titans. Folk, now 40 years old, will be a free agent in the offseason. Coming off back-to-back seasons leading the league in field goal percentage, he will have plenty of opportunities to keep playing if he wants to.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.headline: Titans K Nick Folk (abdomen) will not play in Week 17 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.analysis: Matthew Wright was signed to the Titans practice this week and will kick for the Titans on Sunday. Fantasy managers should look elsewhere for streaming upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.headline: Titans declared K Nick Folk, LB Jerome Baker, WR Jha’Quan Jackson, CB Tre Avery, RB Joshua Kelley, CB Gabe Jeudy-Lally, and LB Luke Gifford inactive for Week 16 against the Colts
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-folk/.analysis: Folk entered the weekend questionable with an abdomen injury and will remain out for the team’s Week 16 game against the Colts. Kicker Brayden Narveson was signed off the practice squad to kick in Folk’s place. Linebacker Luke Gifford (concussion) is the other injury inactive for the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Falcons signed K Jake Moody off Baltimore’s practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: They released Nick Folk in a corresponding move, leaving the Ravens holding nothing at the position currently as Tyler Loop is on injured reserve. Workouts to come for the Ravens. Moody will be a reasonable fantasy kicker provided he can do better than his 78.3 percent career field-goal conversion rate, which, of course, is not guaranteed in any way. At least he plays half his games in a dome now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Ravens placed K Tyler Loop (groin) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: Loop will be sidelined for at least the next four weeks after suffering a right groin injury in Sunday’s loss to the Bills. The second-year kicker competed for the starting kicker job in camp and has struggled during parts of this season. He has converted on 13 of his 17 field goal attempts this year, with his four misses all coming from inside 50 yards. Veteran Jake Moody is set to take over in Loop’s absence when the Ravens face the Jaguars on Thursday night. Loop will be eligible to return in Week 14 when the Ravens play host to the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Ravens signed Jake Moody to the team’s practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: Moody could serve as competition for Tyler Loop after Loop’s early-season struggles. Loop has made 10 of his 13 field goal attempts and all 16 of his extra points through Week 6. Moody — a career 78 percent kicker — competed with Loop for starting duties ahead of the regular season. Whoever ends up kicking for Baltimore will be fantasy relevant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Ravens released K Jake Moody from their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: Moody is free to shop his services elsewhere as Tyler Loop’s 2-for-2 opening game appears to have marked him as safe for the moment. The Ravens used the practice squad spot on WR Gage Larvadain.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Ravens signed K Jake Moody to the team’s practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: It’s an interesting move after Tyler Loop, the team’s Week 1 starter, struggled in training camp and during the preseason. The journeyman Moody was most recently cut by the Commanders and would only be activated to the 53-man roster if Loop’s struggles continue into the regular season. Last year with Washington, Moody went 10-for-11 while going 2-for-2 on distances of 50-plus yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Commanders released K Jake Moody.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: NFL insider Jordan Schultz was the first to report the move. The former 49er was signed to a one-year deal earlier this offseason after a brief stint with Washington, in which he went 10-for-11 while going 2-for-2 on distances of 50-plus yards. Moody had been in a kicking competition with rookie UDFA Drew Stevens, who has outperformed Moody in camp. Moody was a third-round pick by the Niners in 2023 and has converted 78 percent of his field goals in his career and is 107-for-110 on his extra point tries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Commanders re-signed K Jake Moody to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: Just days after the team opted not to tender Moody as a restricted free agent, they have now re-signed him for next season before the start of free agency kicks off next year. Moody was 18-of-20 on field goal attempts last season for the Bears and Commanders after going 1-for-3 in Week 1 for the 49ers. The former third-round pick only attempted two field goals from 50-plus yards last season, and will likely find himself in a kicking competition later this summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Commanders did not tender restricted free agent K Jake Moody, making him a free agent.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: The 2023 third-rounder became a vagabond in 2025, playing for the 49ers, Bears, and Commanders. He’ll likely get another crack to win a starting job again in 2026 somewhere. He was 18-of-20 on field goal attempts for the Bears and Commanders after a Week 1 hail of misses had him released in San Francisco.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Jake Moody converted 1-of-2 field goal attempts in the Commanders’ Week 18 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: Moody missed a chip shot 24-yard field goal in Week 18, but subsequently made a 56-yard field goal later. He spent the 2025 season bouncing between the 49ers, Bears, and Commanders. The 49ers cut him after missing a pair of field goals in Week 1, after which he signed to the Bears’ practice squad. The Commanders signed him off the Bears’ practice squad after he made eight field goals in two games for Chicago. Moody spent the final six games of the season with the Commanders; it remains to be seen if he will return to Washington or sign elsewhere for next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Commanders signed K Jake Moody, formerly of the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: A former third-round pick of the Niners back in 2023, Moody was waived by the 49ers for missing two kicks in Week 1’s win over the 49ers. The third-year kicker missed a whopping 10 kicks last season, but has gone 8-for-9 on his attempts in two games with the Bears, although he notably hasn’t attempted a field goal from 50-plus yards this season. Moody replaces Matt Gay, whose struggles primarily came from distances of 50-plus yards. If the goal is to find a kicker with more range, it seems unlikely that Moody will prove to be the difference-maker the Commanders are looking for. For his career, Moody is 6-for-12 on attempts from 50-plus yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Bengals’ trade for Eagles EDGE Arnold Ebiketie has fallen through.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.analysis: The acquisition had not been finalized, according to Schultz, who said said the nixing of the deal “is not physical or performance related.” It could be related to the Ebiketie acquisition forcing the Bengals to forfeit a 2027 3rd round compensatory draft pick that via the team’s Trey Hendrickson trade to the Ravens. In any case, the Bengals will likely head into the second half of the season with one of the league’s worst pass rushes. Only the Bills and Chiefs have fewer sacks on the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.headline: Bengals acquired EDGE Arnold Ebiketie from the Eagles in exchange for 2027 sixth round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.analysis: The Bengals are shoring up their defense ahead of a postseason run with Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins healthy and operating at a high level. Ebiketie, who had played 48 percent of the Eagles’ defensive snaps this season, logging zero sacks, no tackles for loss, and two QB hits, will join a Bengals defense with the NFL’s tenth highest pressure rate and tenth highest quick pressure rate on the season. Only the Bills and Chiefs have fewer sacks than the Bengals through Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.headline: Eagles signed EDGE Arnold Ebiketie, formerly of the Falcons, to a one-year, $7.3 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.analysis: The contract includes $4.3 million in financial guarantees. Ebiketie spent the last four seasons with the Falcons after they drafted him in the 2022 NFL Draft’s second round. He totaled 25 quarterback pressures, two sacks, 24 solo tackles and seven TFLs last year. He now joins a talented Eagles defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.headline: Falcons EDGE Arnold Ebiketie (forearm) left Week 12’s game against the Commanders and did not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.analysis: Ebiketie came back to the sideline with a large wrap around his forearm. Asked if he’d be ready for Week 13, Ebiketie responded “That’s the goal.” This injury doesn’t appear to be a season-ender, but it’s possible that Ebiketie could miss some time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.headline: Falcons signed second-round EDGE Arnold Ebiketie to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.analysis: Ebiketie’s deal will be worth roughly $8.8 million over four years. Atlanta traded up five picks to nab Ebiketie, who broke out in his fifth collegiate season after transferring to Penn State. He tallied 62 tackles, 17.0 TFLs, 9.5 sacks, and two forced fumbles in his one year with Penn State. A speedy pass-rusher with an array of moves, Ebiketie will likely be thrust into a starting role for Week 1. The Falcons’ defense ranked dead last in sacks per game last year, so any impact from Ebiketie will go a long way.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.headline: Falcons traded up with the Giants to select Penn State EDGE Arnold Ebiketie with the No. 38 overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.analysis: The Falcons surrendered picks No. 43 and 114 for the right to move up five spots. Somewhat surprisingly, it was not for a quarterback. Born in Yaounde’, Cameroon, Ebiketie (6’2/250) grew up playing soccer before emigrating at 12 years old. He played his first four seasons at Temple, not starting until his fourth year where he racked up 42 tackles, 8.5 TFL, 4.0 sacks, and three forced fumbles in just six games. Ebiketie then transferred to PSU, leading all Big Ten edge defenders with 62 tackles in addition to 17.0 TFL, 9.5 sacks, two forced fumbles, and a pair of field-goal blocks. The second-team All-American also performed well across the board in his athletic testing, with a 4.66 40, 4.24 shuttle, and a scorching 6.95s three-cone drill that would have been the third-highest mark in this year’s wide receiver class. Though he doesn’t possess prototypical height, his long 34-inch arms, speed, and get-off allow him to get an immediate advantage on tackles, causing them to overset. That is when Ebiketie digs into his array of moves, utilizing a club/chop and hand swipe to keep his pads clean before dipping his shoulder, leading to an exceptional 90.5 PFF pass-rush grade last year. He is tireless in pursuit of ball carriers, flowing to the ball and using his speed to track them down. He can sometimes let linemen latch on and overpower him in the run game, but he has the tools to be a starting-caliber pass rusher in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.headline: The Draft Network’s Ryan Fowler mocks PSU S Jaquan Brisker and EDGE Arnold Ebiketie to the Cowboys in the first two rounds of next week’s draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.analysis: Last season, the Cowboys selected linebacker Micah Parsons with the 12th overall pick of last year’s draft. Parsons totaled 13 sacks as a rookie and was named the NFL’s Defensive Rookie of the Year and a First-team All-Pro. With the recent success of PSU players, Fowler mocks two more Lions to the Cowboys in Brisker (6'1/200) and Ebiketie. Brisker has the ability to line up at both safety and cornerback, displaying great versatility during his time at Penn State. Ebiketie wrecked the Big 10 in 2021 to the tune of 62 tackles, 18 TFLs and 9.5 sacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.headline: Penn State EDGE Arnold Ebiketie ran an impressive 6.95-second three-cone drill at his pro day on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.analysis: In a deep edge class, anything you can do to stand out will help you separate from the pack. Ebiketie (6'3/253) was able to do that with a three-cone drill in the 88th percentile at 6.95 seconds. He has the size, skill set, and production with eight sacks and 52 pressures last season per PFF. Ebiketie projects currently as a day two selection.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.headline: According to Pro Football Focus, EDGE Arnold Ebiketie receives the highest defensive grade for a Penn State player since 2019.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.analysis: This is a really good draft for pass rushers with a few players projected to go into the first round, one of those being Ebiketie (6'3/253). Penn State has always had a history of great defensive teams and this one was no different as they finished sixth in points allowed, so being a good player on this defense should get you high praise. Pro Football Focus likes Ebiketie a lot as he received the highest defensive grade for a Penn State player since Micah Parsons in 2019. Parson was one of the stars coming into the draft last year, was selected 12th overall to Cowboys, and not only was the clear-cut Defensive Rookie of the Year, but finished as the runner-up for overall Defensive Player of the Year. This could be a good sign for Ebiketie’s draft stock.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.headline: Pro Football Focus has a second-round draft grade on Penn State EDGE Arnold Ebiketie.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arnold-ebi.analysis: In an article written by PFF’s Doug Kyed, Ebiketie (6'3/253) earned a second-round draft grade, but could jump up boards after Penn State’s pro day. Kyed pointed out Ebiketie’s elite numbers at the NFL Scouting Combine, although it is worth noting that he opted out of the 40-yard dash. Penn State had two EDGE rushers drafted in the first round of the 2021 NFL Draft, with Dallas’ Micah Parsons winning Defensive Rookie of the Year. Ebiketie totaled 47 tackles, eight sacks and 52 pressures last season, per PFF.com, and finished his career with 14 sacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Dolphins DT Zach Sieler (bicep) is out for the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.analysis: Sieler, who’s played well for an underperforming Miami defense, will undergo surgery on his injured bicep and remain sidelined for the remainder of the regular season. It’s a blow to the Dolphins defense, which has allowed the league’s highest EPA per play and highest offensive success rate. This could make the Dolphins more vulnerable to the run as well. Through Week 9 they have allowed the tenth most fantasy points per game to running backs, along with the 13th highest yards per carry.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the NFL’s defensive tackle market “has been hot,” and teams “might” try to trade for Derrick Brown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.analysis: The Panthers are “not actively looking to move” Brown, but Breer says they have considered it. Other defensive tackles on other teams who have come up in trade talks include Grover Stewart, Davon Godchaux, Nathan Shepherd, Christian Barmore and Bobby Brown. The Dolphins have told teams they are not interested in trading away Zach Sieler.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.headline: Dolphins HC Mike McDaniel said ZDT Zach Sieler (unspecified) will be out “between days and weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.analysis: McDaniel said that Sieler likely would have suited up for Saturday’s preseason game against the Lions if it were a regular season game. The veteran lineman who signed a three-year extension this offseason now has 22 days to get right before the Dolphins visit the Colts in Week 1. While the timeline for Sieler’s return is murky, McDaniel said he is not concerned about his Week 1 availability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.headline: Dolphins signed DT Zach Sieler to a three-year, $67.75 million extension through 2029.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.analysis: The contract makes him the Dolphins’ highest-paid defender and includes $44 million in guarantees. Sieler remains a talented three-down player at 29 years old. His 11 sacks in 2024 tie for second among NFL defensive tackles. He has 20 over the last two seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.headline: Dolphins ruled out DL Zach Sieler (orbital bone) for Week 8 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.analysis: Sieler reportedly fractured his orbital bone in Friday’s practice and will miss at least one week. NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports Sieler will undergo further testing to determine if surgery is required. This is a significant loss for the Dolphins’ pass rusher. Sieler leads the team in quarterback pressures (18) and ties for the team lead in NFL sacks (2.0).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.headline: Dolphins signed DL Zach Sieler to a three-year, $30.8 million extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.analysis: The Dolphins gave Sieler $20 million guaranteed and he can make up to $35 million with incentives. It’s a nice raise for the 2018 seventh-rounder after he became a full-time starter for the first time last year. Sieler is now signed with Miami through 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.headline: Dolphins DE Zach Sieler’s contract is worth $8.041 million over three years.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.analysis: He also gets a $1 million signing bonus. Claimed off waivers from the Ravens last year, Sieler has eight quarterback hits and 1.5 sacks in nine appearances (three starts) this season. Sieler’s new deal keeps him in Miami through 2023.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.headline: Dolphins and DE Zach Sieler agreed to a contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.analysis: The official terms haven’t been announced, but Sieler is expected to be under contract through the 2023 season. Ozzie Newsome’s last ever draft pick with Baltimore, Sieler was claimed off waivers by the Dolphins in December and has totaled 26 tackles, eight quarterback hits and 1.5 sacks as a rotational player and special teams piece across nine appearances this year. He turned 25 in September.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.headline: Dolphins re-signed DE Zach Sieler to a one-year, $660,000 contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.analysis: Sieler was an exclusive rights free agent. A second-year seventh-rounder, Sieler made seven 2019 appearances between the Ravens and Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.headline: Ravens selected Ferris State DE Zach Sieler with the No. 238 overall pick in the 2018 NFL draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-siele.analysis: Sieler (6'6/290) was not invited to an all-star game or the NFL Combine, but he did work out at Michigan’s Pro Day and produced an athletic profile in the 32nd percentile. He posted a ridiculous 2016 season with 19.5 sacks and 29.5 tackles for loss.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Jaguars won’t trade Brian Thomas, Jr. ahead of the NFL’s trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: Fowler said the Jacksonville front office has told other teams they will not part ways with Thomas before today’s 4:00 eastern trade deadline. Thomas, 24, has been an afterthought in the Jaguars offense for much of the 2026 season after a down 2025 campaign. He’s run a route on 47 percent of the team’s drop backs while accounting for 9 percent of the team’s targets and 16 percent of the team’s air yards. Thomas has seen a target on 17 percent of his pass routes, the sixth highest rate among Jags pass catchers. Stuck in Jacksonville, Thomas will have some deep league value as a big play dependent wideout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that it “sounds like” the Jaguars are going to listen to trade offers for Brian Thomas Jr.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: The Jags have shot down all offers so far, but it’s hard to justify his current usage when the team could instead recoup some draft capital by moving him. Thomas hasn’t caught more than two passes in a game since Week 2. He has three games with zero catches this year and played just 19 snaps on Thursday versus the Ravens. The Chiefs are reportedly interested, though that would require the Jags to send BTJ to one of their biggest competitors in the AFC. The Steelers and 49ers are also reportedly interested.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the Jaguars “have been less inclined” to trade away Brian Thomas.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: Breer and NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe put out similar reports today, indicating that the Jaguars are now hesitant to trade away Thomas. Per Breer, Thomas is not the best fit for coach Liam Coen’s scheme, but he “brings a downfield element that’s really important in keeping defenses honest against the run, and opening things up underneath for Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington.” Wolfe echoed Breer’s downfield sentiment and added that when the Jaguars traded away Tyson Campbell last year, it had a negative impact on the locker room — and Jaguars brass has “learned from it.” Thomas and Travis Hunter are reportedly close friends, and Thomas is liked in the locker room. It sounds like the formerly productive wide receiver might be staying put. Breer lists the Chiefs and Steelers, and the 49ers to a lesser degree, as the teams known to be seeking wide receiver help.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: A to Z Sports’ Charles Goldman reports that if the Chiefs trade for a wide receiver, the team “would like to acquire a long-term fixture rather than a one-year rental.”
