That being said, Allen’s two rushing touchdowns give him 85 for his career, which means he’s now tied with former Bill Marshawn Lynch for 17th on the NFL’s all-time list. The Bills and Allen will look to get things straightened out against the Patriots next week, and Allen will clearly be in your lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 20-of-31 passes for 248 yards and three touchdowns in the Bills’ 41-31, Week 2 win over the Lions, adding 69 yard and two touchdowns on 14 carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Was it ever a doubt that Super Josh would make an appearance in the franchise’s first game in their new stadium? To the utter dismay of James Cook fantasy managers, Allen accounted for three touchdowns from inside the five against the Lions, two with his legs and one with his arm, extending his NFL-record for games with multiple rushing touchdowns and multiple passing touchdowns to 10 in the process. The unquestioned overall QB1 in fantasy circles continues to prove the doubters wrong as the Bills surge to 2-0 atop the AFC ahead of a home meeting with the Chargers in Week 3. Allen remains a top-tier fantasy asset until pigs fly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 20-of-29 passes for 334 yards and two touchdowns in the Bills’ 36-31, Week 1 win over the Texans, adding 23 yards and two touchdowns on the ground.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Some had suggested you might want to bench Josh Allen against the Texans defense this week. Instead, Allen absolutely decimated last year’s top defense with a game-winning stick throw to the post for Josh Palmer to take a late five-point lead. He did his typical witchcraft out of structure, the best of which was probably a floater in his own end zone with a man in his face that landed directly on Dalton Kincaid’s hands. He also owned the ground game in the red zone. It was the first Bills win in Houston since the JP Losman Era. Allen, as always, will be in the QB1 overall discussion against the Lions in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia said he would not be surprised if DJ Moore is “on the field constantly and for [Josh] Allen to default to looking his way.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Buscaglia called Moore, who was acquired from the Bears this spring, the “crown jewel of the offseason” for the Bills front office. “Moore’s contributions to the offense within training camp were immediate and obvious,” Buscaglia said. “Allen routinely pushed the ball downfield to Moore, making a concerted effort all summer to build on-field chemistry with the Bills’ new No. 1 receiver. ... The days of ‘everybody eats’ seem to be in the rearview mirror.” It’s a bullish report — one that could mean Moore is among the best values in redraft leagues this season even after being among the NFL’s most inefficient wideouts in 2025. Moore should be in all 12-team lineups for Week 1 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports Josh Allen and “most Bills starters” will sit for Saturday’s preseason game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: After a good week of joint practices against the Browns, the Bills are expected to sit most of their starters while giving their depth players a chance to show what they have. Veteran QB Kyle Allen will draw the start on Saturday, with backup Shane Buechele also expected to see work. The Bills’ decision to sit their starters should come as good news for Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson, who are still battling for the QB1 job, with Sanders in line to start with the first-team offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Cardinals signed QB Josh Johnson from the Bengals’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: In the wake of trading away Jacoby Brissett and the UCL injury to Gardner Minshew, the Cardinals spring into action to add veteran depth behind rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck, the latter of whom is expected to start for the remainder of the season in Arizona. Beck will be thrust into action without the team’s starting left tackle and alpha wide receiver in Michael Wilson but will get much needed experience as the Cardinals decide the trajectory of their franchise in the final half of the 2026 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Bengals signed QB Josh Johnson to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: It really strains the limits of credulity to have a 40-year-old practice squad player, but here we are. johnson remains QB3 in Cincinnati after being released at last cuts. Also on Cincy’s practice squad are: RB Kentrel Bullock, QB Sean Clifford, DT Howard Cross, DE Isaiah Foskey, LB Joe Giles-Harris, LB Shaka Heyward, DB Bralyn Lux, RB Kendall Milton, WR Jordan Moore, WR Noah Thomas and DB Russ Yeast.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Bengals released QB Josh Johnson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Johnson was signed before the Bengals knew they’d be getting Joe Flacco back, but with Flacco in the fold they’ve decided to move on from the 40-year-old. Johnson looked solid enough in the preseason to find a role elsewhere, hopefully on a team he hasn’t been on before for Immaculate Grid purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. believes the Bengals are “waiting on” Joe Flacco.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Flacco has been searching for an unlikely path to a starting job, but one doesn’t seem like it will materialize any time soon. The Bengals brought in Josh Johnson as a backup, but Dehner believes he’s just a hedge in case Flacco is able to find more reps elsewhere. Our nation’s great Flacco free-agency scuttlebutt will continue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Bengals agreed to terms with QB Josh Johnson on a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: The well-traveled quarterback turns 40 on Sunday and heads back to Cincinnati for his third stint with the team after agreeing to terms on a one-year contract. He’ll have a good chance to earn the backup role behind franchise quarterback Joe Burrow considering the only other quarterback on the roster is Sean Clifford. Johnson has spent time with 16 NFL franchises during his sprawling career, amassing 11 professional starts across 50 appearances, most recently starting two games for the Commanders in 2025 in relief of the injured Jayden Daniels. The financials of the contract were not yet made available.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Josh Johnson completed 14-of-22 passes for 131 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Commanders’ 24-17, Week 18 win over the Eagles, adding nine carries for 45 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Career journeyman Josh Johnson made two starts for the Commanders, both at the end of the season after Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota were ruled out due to injuries and Washington was eliminated. The 39-year-old passed for 372 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions over two starts and five games, adding 55 yards and a touchdown on the ground. A touch pass to John Bates in the fourth quarter of Week 18 against the Eagles was Johnson’s first touchdown pass since 2021. Johnson has been in the NFL for 18 seasons as a backup quarterback. He could certainly find work in a quarterback room once again for 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Commanders QB Josh Johnson will start Washington’s Week 18 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Johnson! McKee! It’s Week 18! Johnson was a checkdown artist against the Cowboys in his Week 17 start and figures to continue that role against a better defense this week. Johnson might crack the QB2 superflex ranks if you’re desperate with so many quarterbacks in tenuous situations, but he isn’t someone you’d actually want to start this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn told reporters QB Marcus Mariota (quad) is doubtful for Week 18 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Not much has changed since Quinn met with reporters Monday. Mariota still isn’t practicing and his coach called him a long-shot to play and even added that he’s “likely doubtful.” Barring a miraculous recovery, Josh Johnson will be under center for Washington in Week 18 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn told reporters that it’s “still a stretch” that Marcus Mariota (quad/Hand) plays in Week 18 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Quinn did say that “there’s still hope” that Mariota can get back on the field for the finale against Philadelphia. Assuming Mariota isn’t able to get back on the field, it’ll be Josh Johnson under center again for the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Josh Johnson completed 15-of-23 passes for 198 yards in the Commanders’ 30-23, Week 17 los to the Cowboys, adding 10 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Johnson’s final stat line is a bit misleading as over 20% of his production came on a short catch-and-run completion to Deebo Samuel, who gained 41 yards on the gadget play. The Commanders ran only 41 offensive plays, leading to the low pass volume for the veteran journeyman. Washington limps to the offseason in one of the more injury-ravaged seasons in recent memory.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: The NFL reinstated 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk from the reserve/left squad list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: According to The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero, the NFL has granted the 49ers a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk as the two sides continue to negotiate his impending release. The 49ers will have until November 23rd to make a roster move, but once released, Aiyuk will be free to sign with any team. The 28-year-old receiver last played in 2024 and hasn’t taken a snap since tearing his ACL in Week 7 of that season. While there is a chance Aiyuk could suit up for a new team at some point this season, fantasy managers hoping to stash him shouldn’t expect anything meaningful until the fantasy playoffs at the earliest, as it could take him several weeks to find a new team and get up to speed with the season more than halfway over.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Commanders “haven’t completely abandoned” the idea of acquiring WR Brandon Aiyuk.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Aiyuk was rumored to end up in Washington all offseason and there seemingly could still be a fit there with Terry McLaurin out for the season. However, this report suggests the Commanders haven’t completely ruled it out rather than this being something they’re actively pursuing. Aiyuk met with 49ers brass Friday, though a resolution proved elusive. This saga is far from over.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: Brandon Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said talks between him and the 49ers are “to be continued.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Aiyuk and Rosenhaus met with the 49ers’ “big bosses” today to discuss an amicable solution to their multi-year conflict. Aiyuk seeks reinstatement, but under league rules, he owes th e 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture. The two sides met today, but evidently, things were not resolved. The saga continues. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Brandon Aiyuk owes the 49ers “roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture,” which could delay his return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Pelissero calls this a “potential complication in [Aiyuk’s] efforts to secure his release by reporting to the facility Friday.” While it’s possible both sides reach a deal for Aiyuk to pay back that money, which would make this a non-issue, Pelissero said this could also end up going to arbitration, which may delay things. Aiyuk is scheduled to report to the 49ers’ facilities today, so we could have our answer in the next few hours about when this situation is resolved and Aiyuk has been granted his release. Aiyuk recently hired Drew Rosenhaus with the hopes of being reinstated into the league and with a new team soon. The 28-year-old last played in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: Brandon Aiyuk submitted paperwork to the NFL for his reinstatement.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, confirmed the development on Wednesday, and said Aiyuk would report to the 49ers on Friday. That could expedite his release from the team so he could seek employment with another, presumably wideout-needy NFL team. Aiyuk’s erratic behavior over the past year and questions about his conditioning could prevent some teams from pursuing him. “Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field,” Rosenhaus said. He had been closely linked to the Commanders before a series of online meltdowns in the offseason. The Rams could be in the market for Aiyuk with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined indefinitely. Aiyuk is still unlikely to have any fantasy value this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports free agent WR Brandon Aiyuk “is close to hiring new representatives in an effort to get back to the NFL and on a team.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: An entire offseason spent creating goofy Instagram videos in hopes of willing himself onto the Commanders’ roster didn’t go as Aiyuk had hoped. Instead, the 28-year-old receiver, who last played a snap in 2024, remains under contract with the 49ers after failing to apply for reinstatement, which remains the first step he would need to take if he hopes to be made available to other teams. The 49ers put a “left squad designation” on Aiyuk back in July, meaning while he remains under contract with the team, he does not count against the team’s 53-man roster. It seems unlikely he will remain with the Niners if/when he applies for reinstatement, meaning the team will either have to release him or find a trade suitor for him before this month’s deadline. It would be surprising if Aiyuk played a snap for any team in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: ESPN’s Nick Wagoner reports that 49ers WR Demarcus Robinson has been initially diagnosed with a right high-ankle sprain “that could cost him extended time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Although Robinson will apparently undergo more testing, the “initial diagnosis” aspect seems like a formality at this point. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said he is “sure” the team will have to sign a wide receiver, “whether it’s a practice squad or to the roster.” For those curious, Shanahan was asked whether there was any chance of bringing back WR Brandon Aiyuk. Per Wagoner, Shanahan responded simply, “No.” That’s that. Expect Robinson to miss time, likely increasing WR Deebo Samuel’s involvement. No. 1 WR Mike Evans suffered a hip injury, though Shanahan did not seem to think it was serious.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: ESPN’s John Keim reports Stefon Diggs “remains a player of interest” for the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Perhaps more notable is that Keim pointed out “other free agents don’t appear to be on their radar,” with Brandon Aiyuk presumably the “other” in this scenario. Diggs has long been linked to the Commanders as a potential fit, and ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported last week that “Washington is intriguing” to Diggs, so there’s a good chance some mutual interest exists. The Commanders’ receiver room is headlined by Terry McLaurin, but behind him is an unproven group in Jaylin Lane, Luke McCaffrey, Dyami Brown, and rookie Antonio Williams. It feels like only a matter of time before the Commanders eventually make a move to upgrade their receiving corps, and Diggs would provide a solid option opposite McLaurin after going for 85-1,013-4 with the Patriots last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: 49ers GM John Lynch said Brandon Aiyuk “is on a left squad designation” as the team opens training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: For those who continue to follow the Niners/Aiyuk saga, this is no surprise. Aiyuk’s designation means he does not count against the 49ers’ 90-man roster for camp, and the designation requires him to apply to the NFL for reinstatement before he can be released or traded. Aiyuk has been active on his Instagram account, and appears to be trying to manifest a move to the Commanders to play with long-time friend and former college teammate Jayden Daniels, but the ball is ultimately in his court to take the steps necessary for anything to be facilitated. It was reported earlier this month by ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler that he “doesn’t think” the Commanders would be interested in Aiyuk if he were to come available. Aiyuk last played in 2024, posting a 25-374-0 line in seven games before suffering a torn ACL in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that “he doesn’t think” the Commanders are going to bring in Brandon Aiyuk “at this stage.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Well, let’s see if we can get a few Instagram posts off that change minds, Brandon. Aiyuk and the 49ers are at an impasse and he has not posted on his social accounts that he’s not “doing business” with the 49ers at this time, and unless he reports to the 49ers they can’t actually release him anyway. This situation has turned from a fait accompli that he’d eventually join the Commanders into something that surely has them second-guessing things, as reported by Nicki Jhavala of The Athletic earlier last month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said C Erik McCoy is expected to miss some time with a bicep injury
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.analysis: McCoy missed 10 games last season due to a torn biceps. It doesn’t sound like his injury is nearly as severe this time around, as Moore said he believes McCoy will avoid surgery. That said, it sounds like the veteran center could be headed for injured reserve with hopes he will return at some point in the season. McCoy has started all eight games he has appeared in this season, earning a PFF grade of 73.2 while allowing just five pressures on 352 pass-blocking downs. He was replaced by Will Sherman in Week 9’s win over the Browns, with Sherman being the favorite to takeover in the weeks ahead while McCoy is sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Saints C Erik McCoy is believed to have suffered a torn biceps in Week 7’s loss to the Bears, ending his season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.analysis: Once the injury is confirmed, McCoy’s season will be over. The seven-year vet missed 10 games last season due to groin and shoulder injuries, but remains one of the league’s top centers when healthy. We’ll likely receive official word on his injury in the coming days, but for now, it sounds like the team already fears the worst. Backup Luke Fortner would be next in line to draw the start in place of McCoy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.headline: Beat reporter Nick Underhill reports “Erik McCoy is restructuring his contract” as the Saints work “to get under the cap.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.analysis: Per OverTheCap, the Saints are still more than $46 million over the cap but the team’s star center is willing to do his part, presumably in exchange for a nice bonus. McCoy is coming off an injury-dampened season, having dealt with both groin and shoulder issues. However, he should be good to go for 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.headline: Saints interim head coach Darren Rizzi said he “doesn’t know” if Erik McCoy (shoulder) will return this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.analysis: The good news, Rizzi offered, is that McCoy avoided major injury and won’t need surgery. McCoy started just seven games this year while dealing with a recurring groin injury, but he was wildly successful when he did play, notching a 94.2 PFF grade in 293 snaps. He left Week 16’s game after just seven plays and did not return. McCoy enters his age-28 season in 2025 as the likely starter for the Saints at center, carrying a $16.38 million cap figure that could be adjusted if the Saints want to continue to push money into future years.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.headline: Saints coach Darren Rizzi said C Erik McCoy (groin) should “be ready to roll this week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.analysis: McCoy did not play off the questionable line in Week 13 and has been hampered by the groin injury all season, as he aggravated the initial groin injury that sent him to injured reserve upon his return to the lineup. It would be a big boost for the Saints if they could get him back for Week 14. The Saints should run all over the Giants regardless of who their starting center is, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.headline: Saints RB Jamaal Williams (groin) is active for Week 13 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.analysis: Williams entered the weekend questionable but is expected to play. He is the clear backup running back and should remain off fantasy radars. Saints declared QB Spencer Rattler, RB Jordan Mims, LB Jaylan Ford, OL Lucas Patrick, C Erik McCoy, WR Mason Tipton, and DT Khristian Boyd inactive for Week 13 against the Rams. Patrick and McCoy are out due to ankle and groin injuries, respectively. Their absences leave the Saints offensive line weaker against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.headline: Saints C Erik McCoy (groin) is questionable for Week 13 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.analysis: McCoy initially suffered the groin injury in Week 3. He spent two months on the sidelines before returning in Week 11, only to immediately aggravate the issue. Interim head coach Darren Rizzi said he was going to be okay but didn’t put a timeline on the injury. McCoy didn’t practice at all this week before being listed as questionable. The Saints are giving him the weekend to test things out, though three straight DNPs puts him on the wrong side of questionable for now. Fellow interior offensive lineman Lucas Patrick has already been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.headline: Saints interim HC Darren Rizzi said Erik McCoy (groin) is “going to be OK.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.analysis: “Went through a lot of tests last night and this morning,” Rizzi told reporters. McCoy re-aggravated the injury in the first half of Week 11’s game against the Browns after missing two months with it. The Saints are on bye this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.headline: NewOrleans.Football’s Nick Underhill reports Saints C Erik McCoy (groin) will be active for Week 11 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.analysis: McCoy has been sidelined since Week 3 because of the groin injury. He underwent surgery and was placed on injured reserve shortly after going down with the injury. McCoy returned to practice last week but was listed as doubtful. The Saints listed him as questionable this time around after the veteran lineman got in a full practice on Friday. He is good to go for Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Saints C Erik McCoy (groin) is out for 6-8 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/erik-mccoy.analysis: McCoy went down in Week 3 against the Eagles with a groin injury that will require surgery in the coming days. McCoy, a key piece of an already-struggling New Orleans offensive line, will be sidelined until at least early November, maybe longer. The Saints struggled to protect Derek Carr last week against a tough Eagles pass rush. Carr was pressured on 44 percent of his Week 3 drop backs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said he expects Jacoby Brissett to start in Week 10 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: The Ravens wasted little time in trading for Brissett after he lost his starting job with the Cardinals. The 33-year-old journeyman is familiar with Ravens QB coach Israel Woolfork and was acquired in part because the team believed he could quickly become the starter. Brissett threw for 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns, and seven interceptions in his eight games with the Cardinals this season, and will now look to save the Ravens’ season after they fell to 4-5 last week. With Lamar Jackson (finger) hoping to come back in the next six to nine weeks, if Baltimore can string together a few wins, it’s possible he will be back in time for the playoffs should they make the postseason. Brissett being under center should also provide some stability to Zay Flowers’ and Derrick Henry’s fantasy stocks after a rough few weeks sans Lamar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: The Ravens and Cardinals finalized a trade on Friday that sends Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: We already knew this deal would be done, but the two sides made things official on Friday. The Ravens will receive Brissett, along with a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Cardinals in exchange for a 2027 4th-round pick and a 2028 7th-round pick. Brissett will immediately step into a starting role for the Ravens when they face the Chargers in Week 10 and should provide an immediate upgrade over Joe Fagnano, who struggled mightily in his first career start against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the Ravens are acquiring Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals in a deal that is expected to be completed this weekend.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Schefter adds that this trade will not be completed in time for Brissett to play in Week 9’s Thursday Night Football game for the Ravens, but he will make his debut in Week 10 against the Chargers. Brissett’s impending arrival in Baltimore immediately stabilizes the pass-catching corps’ fantasy value. The trade compensation has not yet been revealed, but we expect to know more soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett will serve as the Cardinals’ emergency QB3 in Week 9 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: After holding out part of the offseason for a new deal that was fitting for a starting QB in the league, Brissett now finds himself as the QB3 of the Cardinals entering Week 9. There’s a good chance this is the end of the road for Brissett as far as his time with the Cardinals is concerned, as a handful of dire QB situations around the league could warrant a trade to a contender who is looking to upgrade at QB before the trade deadline. Brissett was solid last season for a three-win Cardinals team, throwing for 3,366 yards, 23 touchdowns, and eight interceptions in 12 starts. He currently sports a 1,719-10-7 line this season but has struggled in his last three starts, throwing just one touchdown to two interceptions. With Brissett being demoted to QB3, rookie Carson Beck will be elevated to QB2 on game days, and draws ever closer to making his first career start at some point in the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 10-of-23 passes for 119 yards and an interception before being benched for Gardner Minshew in the third quarter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: He took four sacks, including back-to-back sacks to kill a third-quarter drive, before being replaced. Brissett hasn’t necessarily played this poorly all season, but we’d been getting plenty of questions at press conferences about if he’d remain the starter so we’re ultimately unsurprised by this move. Minshew took over and we assume Carson Beck will also be mentioned ahead of Week 9. Full Mike LaFleur press conference coverage to come, naturally.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 27-of-48 passes for 272 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals’ 30-16, Week 7 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett struggled to get the deep ball going in this game and was largely stuck dinking and dunking his way down the field. He averaged a measly 5.7 yards per attempt while completing 56.3 percent of his passes. Brissett hasn’t averaged seven yards per attempt in a game since Week 1. Even worse is the fact that he’s taking bone-crushing hits more than ever. Brissett injured his non-throwing hand while taking a sack late in the second quarter but never missed any time with the issue. We expect him to make an appearance on the injury report this week. Head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters after the game that Brissett remains the starter, meaning he’ll take on a terrible Dallas defense next week. He will be a priority streamer for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 24-of-35 passes for 218 yards and one touchdown in the Cardinals’ 18-16, Week 6 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett threw an interception to Rams S Quentin Lake while targeting Trey McBride on the Cardinals’ third play from scrimmage but managed to play mistake-free and touchdown-free football from there on out. Brissett took zero sacks for the first time this season and linked up with four different players for explosive gains. That said, the box score results obviously disappoint. Brissett nearly linked up with Michael Wilson for a 36-yard touchdown on the Cardinals’ seventh drive, but the ball glanced off Wilson’s fingertips as he dove for it in the end zone. The drive ultimately resulted in a field goal, as did five others. Brissett will be a high-end QB2 against the Broncos in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: ArizonaCardinals.com’s Darren Urban believes Carson Beck won’t start in the “immediate future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Cardinals fans appear to be pining for the team to bench Jacoby Brissett and start the rookie in the coming weeks as another season circles the drain for Arizona. Beck so far has been the Cards’ emergency third quarterback. Urban said there remains a “chance Beck is made the backup this week or next and allow him to come on in relief if the situation presents itself. I don’t see Beck starting in the immediate future, but it does feel his time grows closer, and if the offense continues to sputter, that would be understandable.” Brissett this season ranks 15th in passing yards. He’s thrown nine touchdowns to five interceptions and ranks 30th out of 37 qualifying QBs in adjusted yards per attempt. He won’t be a viable fantasy play this week against a tough Rams coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 29-of-47 passes for 292 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in the Cardinals’ 21-45, Week 5 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett also rushed twice for 19 yards and nearly scored on a trick play via a seven-yard reception. He was stopped at the Lions’ two-yard line. Brissett guided the Cardinals to a 14-play scoring drive on their first possession, which he capped off with a two-yard touchdown strike to backup TE Teagan Quitoriano. The bottom dropped out after that. The Cardinals racked up five straight drives ending a punt, with Brissett only managing to break the dreary streak by throwing an interception. Brissett managed to salvage his box score with another Quitoriano score, and a juggling touchdown catch secured by Trey McBride. Brissett also coaxed a few big plays out of fellow backup TE Elijah Higgins. Apparently, the veteran quarterback is ready to target more towering pass catchers with Marvin Harrison Jr. now a Texan. Brissett is a borderline QB1/2 with a shaky floor in Week 6 against the Rams. Coach Mike LaFleur said post-game that he is not considering a quarterback change.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 21-of-35 passes for 166 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions in the Cardinals’ 36-24, Week 4 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett added four carries for 18 yards. Entering the proceedings with just one pick through three starts, Brissett tossed two in the first half before “adding” a walk-off pick-six on the game’s final play. Trailing 30-24, the Cardinals had a 4th-and-goal from the Giants’ four-yard line. Then a pressured Brissett threw it right to Deonte Banks after Michael Wilson cut off his route in the end zone. It was a brutal end to a brutal game, one where Brissett took a pair of sacks in addition to his giveaways. He did find the beleaguered Marvin Harrison Jr. for a 12-yard score against man-to-man coverage on the game’s opening drive, but that opening drive score went down as MHJ’s only reception. The duo did draw a late DPI to set up their ill-faded goal-line series. Averaging a miserable 4.7 yards per attempt on 115 throws over his past three starts, Brissett could get the Carson Beck chatter going in the desert sooner rather than later. That being said, the Lions are a plus Week 5 matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Kyle Hamilton “looks fairly good” after suffering a hip injury in Week 9’s loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: Hamilton exited Thursday’s game and did not return to the field. Despite the scare, it doesn’t sound like Hamilton is at risk of missing much, if any, time. The two-time All-Pro has totaled 60 tackles, nine TFLs, and one interception this season while also breaking up five passes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Kyle Hamilton (knee) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: Hamilton managed a full session to clear the report after a Wednesday DNP. While the Ravens are missing some key players on defense, having their star safety ready to deal with Josh Allen is a big get for them in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Kyle Hamilton (knee) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: Hamilton was seen in full pads, participating in practice the day after being held out due to a knee injury. The All Pro safety-linebacker hybrid is arguably the most important piece of the Baltimore defense considering his absurd flexibility to play multiple positions on the field. While the official status of his return has not been provided by the team, it’s a step in the right direction ahead of a divisional showdown against the Bills in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Kyle Hamilton (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: Neither did fellow Ravens safety Jaylinn Hawkins, who is also dealing with a knee injury. Ravens coach Jesse Minter said a few of his players were dealing with “after game type things” when asked about Hamilton, so it doesn’t sound like this is a major issue. Still, with multiple members of the secondary banged up, this is a situation to monitor throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: The Ravens’ new starting center is still recovering from his recent concussion, but he seemingly has a chance to face the Browns this week. Ravens EDGE Trey Hendrickson (finger) and S Kyle Hamilton (stinger) are practicing fully, while RT Roger Rosengarten (knee), OG John Simpson (groin), OG Andrew Vorhees (foot), LT Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) were limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ravens S Kyle Hamilton is “more likely to play than not” for Week 16 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: Hamilton was a surprise addition to the injury report on Friday, being listed as a limited participant because of the ankle issue. Per Rapoport, Hamilton will still need to go through a pre-game workout before the team makes a final call on his status. The standout defensive back has 87 tackles, seven pass breakups, and one sack this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Ravens S Kyle Hamilton (ankle) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 16 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: It’s a surprise listing and comes with a Friday limited session. Hamilton would be a huge absence for the Ravens defense if he can’t push through this listing and play on Sunday night. We’d tentatively tag him as a true game-time decision.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Ravens WR Rashod Bateman (ankle) and S Kyle Hamilton (shoulder) were limited in Tuesday’s practice after initially announced to be full participants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: Head coach John Harbaugh had announced both Bateman and Hamilton to be full participants on Tuesday, but the team’s official injury report has them listed as limited participants. It’s not the first time Harbaugh and the Ravens have had discrepancies in practice reporting, but we’ll take the official limited listing as the truth for now. Bateman opens the week with back-to-back limited practices and has a shot to return to his starting role on Thanksgiving against the Bengals. Meanwhile, Hamilton has played through injuries before and we would not rule out the same happening again this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Ravens coach John Harbaugh said Kyle Hamilton (shoulder) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: Hamilton looks on track to play Thursday despite being pulled from Baltimore’s Week 12 game against the Jets multiple times. The star safety is the straw that stirs Baltimore’s drink on defense and they’ll badly need him as they try to keep control of the AFC North with another win on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.headline: Ravens HC John Harbaugh said Kyle Hamilton (ankle) will “have a chance” to play in Week 13 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-hamil.analysis: Hamilton was already playing through a shoulder injury entering Week 12, and was knocked from Sunday’s win over the Jets with an ankle injury that he suffered after slipping on the turf. Hamilton is one of the premier defenders in the league and would make for a massive loss if the Ravens are without him against Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Bucky Irving’s touches could decrease in the second half of the season to preserve his health.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: As Bucs beat writer Greg Auman points out, Irving is on pace for 315 carries this season, which would have been the second most in the league last year. Irving has not missed a game yet this season, but after injuries limited him to 10 games in 2025, it’s not surprising to learn Bowles may want to dial things back a bit. The efficient play of Kenneth Gainwell in recent weeks has also earned him an expanded look, and it should instill a bit of confidence in OC Zac Robinson when asking him to spell Irving in certain situations. With the Bucs now entering their bye week, we will get our first look at how the team plans to deploy its backfield in Week 11 when they visit the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving rushed 20 times for 97 yards and two scores in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears, adding four catches for 28 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Irving was held in check for the first three quarters outside of a short rushing touchdown, but broke several tackles to open the fourth quarter on a 25-yard gain. He scored again in the fourth quarter to tie the game at 24-24 and now has six rushing scores in 2026. It wasn’t quite the monster effort he produced against the Falcons (27/170/1) the week prior, but still a very strong fantasy day for the 24-year-old tailback. Irving should be considered as an RB1 against the Lions in Week 11 after a bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving rushed 27 times for 170 yards and a touchdown in the Bucs’ Week 8 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: The Bucs became the first team in over 50 years to not complete a pass for an entire game. In turn, Irving was able to rack up a career high in rush attempts. He then turned that into a career high in yards by averaging over six yards per carry. He could have posted even better numbers, but the Bucs put him on ice after his third-quarter touchdown. With the exception of one attempt from Irving, Gainwell saw 18 consecutive rush attempts to close the game. Gainwell wound up running for 140 yards on 25 attempts. To the Bucs’ credit, Gainwell was picking up chunk gain after chunk gain and Irving had already earned a massive workload. Irving failed to hit 100 yards on the ground in any of his first three games. He has since reached triple digits three times in his past four outings. Playing some of the best football of his career, Irving is pushing for an RB1 rank headed into Week 9 versus the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving (rest) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Irving was absent from Thursday’s sessions with an official “rest” designation, allowing fantasy managers to breath a collective sigh of relief after the veteran back has morphed into a borderline workhorse in recent games. Managers can likely continue forward with Irving in their starting lineups as an upside RB2 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Gainwell missed Wednesday’s session with the hip issue. He will likely be listed as limited today, but that still puts him on track to play in Week 8 against the Falcons. Gainwell racked up 14 carries in a blowout win over the Panthers last week, but that hasn’t been the norm for him. Gainwell is averaging 6.4 touches per game and has topped out at three receptions in a week. He is buried in the RB4 ranks for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Gainwell suffered the hip injury while logging a season-high 14 rush attempts in Week 7. The Bucs blew out the Panthers and racked up 49 carries as a team. Bucky Irving would be in line for more work on passing downs if Gainwell is out for Week 8. Sean Tucker could also see an uptick in snaps, though his normal role has very little overlap with what Gainwell does. Per usual, Irving looks like a high-end RB2 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving rushed 24 times for 106 yards and two touchdowns in the Bucs’ Week 7 win over the Panthers, adding a four-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: The two-score day on the ground was somehow the first of Irving’s career. He led the way as the Bucs rolled up a ridiculous 258 yards rushing in a stunning road clobbering of the Panthers. That means Irving ceded plenty of work to Kenneth Gainwell and a little to Sean Tucker, but everyone got home as the Bucs simply dominated on the ground. Irving’s scores came from four and one yards out, meaning he had the goal-line advantage on Tucker while the game was still in doubt. It was a really strong performance, and a nice bounce-back effort after a rough Week 6. This figures to remain an up and down offense and rushing attack, but Irving has proven to be a high-end RB2 more weeks than not. That will include for Week 8 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving (illness) is not on the Buccaneers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: As is typically the case with ill players, Irving is good to go for this week’s game. He upgraded to full participation today after getting a limited session in on Thursday. The Buccaneers’ No. 1 running back has been a volatile producer this season, yet even with last week’s flop, he still totaled 21 touches. That type of workload keeps him firmly in the RB2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving (illness) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: The Buccaneers’ No. 1 running back is on track to play in Week 7 against the Panthers. The offense is expected to be led by Baker Mayfield (thumb), who will play with a protective plate on his hand to prevent re-injury. Irving should be good to go this week and can be treated as a high-end RB2, as usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving (illness) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Players missing time because of an illness this early in the weekend almost always get cleared to play by Sunday. We expect no difference from Irving. Coming off his third 20-touch game of the year, Irving remains a high-end RB2 for his Week 7 date with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.headline: Jets traded S Andre Cisco to the Lions in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.analysis: Cisco has started four of the nine games he has appeared in for the Jets this season, racking up 23 tackles, one sack, and one pass breakup while also forcing a fumble. The sixth-year safety has 59 games of starting experience and should provide some help on the back end to a secondary that has allowed the most passing yards this season. He has graded out well as a run stopper in each of his last two seasons, per PFF, and can also line up in the slot when needed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.headline: Jets re-signed S Andre Cisco.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.analysis: Cisco suffered a season-ending torn pectoral injury in Week 8. PFF credits him with one forced incompletion. He regularly grades out well as a run defender, most recently earning a 75.6 PFF run-defense grade. The veteran safety turns 26 later this month. He should start in the Jets’ secondary again this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.headline: Jets HC Aaron Glenn said S Andre Cisco (pectoral) will miss the remainder of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.analysis: Cisco suffered a torn pectoral in Week 8’s win over the Bengals. Returning from the team’s Week 9 bye, Glenn confirmed that the fifth-year safety will now miss the remainder of the season. Cisco signed a one-year deal with the Jets this offseason and started all eight games he appeared in while totaling 41 tackles, one TFL, and one pass breakup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Jets S Andre Cisco suffered a pectoral tear in Week 8.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.analysis: Cisco reportedly tore his pectoral muscle in the Jets’ Week 8 win over the Bengals. The 25-year-old signed with the Jets in the offseason and started all eight games, tallying 41 combined tackles on the season. Cisco’s pectoral tear needs repair and he will be sidelined for some period of time, leaving the Jets to turn to Isaiah Oliver and Tony Adams for help at the safety spot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.headline: Jets agreed to terms with S Andre Cisco, formerly of the Jaguars, on a one-year, $10 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.analysis: The deal marks Cisco’s first season away from the Jaguars, who drafted him in the third round in 2021. The 24-year-old safety has forced incompletions at a 20.0 percent rate or better in 3-of-4 seasons. He can be expected to compete for one of the two starting roles alongside incumbent S Tony Adams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.headline: Jaguars agreed to terms with S Eric Murray, formerly of the Texans, to a three-year, $22.5 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.analysis: This courtesy of former Jaguars back Maurice Jones-Drew, who added that Murray will get $12 million in guarantees. Murray has spent the last five years in Houston — he was playing on the team when Bill O’Brien was still the head coach. Entering his age-31 season, this is a strong contract for a player who spent two of the last three years as a reserve. Murray saw more playing time last year as the Texans moved Jalen Pitre to nickelback, and had a playoff pick-six of Justin Herbert. Signing him seems like an admission that the Jags will move on from Andre Cisco.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.headline: Doug Pederson and Jaguars S Andre Cisco differed as to whether Jaguars players are quitting in-game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.analysis: Talking with reporters about the state of his team, Pederson told reporters, “I feel like the guys are -- they don’t quit. They keep fighting.” Shortly after that, Cisco told reporters, " I feel like it was... a lot of quit... It felt very early in the game, maybe at halftime, that we weren’t playing as one.” Pederson likely has one last shot to turn things around, against the Patriots in Week 7. For fantasy purposes, a potential buy-low window for Jaguars players may currently be underway. An interim head coach could provide fantasy-friendly, schematic upgrades for the rest of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.headline: Jaguars selected Syracuse S Andre Cisco with the No. 65 overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.analysis: Cisco (6'0/209), a three-year starter at Syracuse, snagged 13 interceptions throughout his career, which is made more impressive by the fact he was only able to play two games in 2020 due to an ACL injury. He was voted as the only true freshman to the Walter Camp All-America team in 2018, then earned himself second-team All-ACC honors in 2019. On film, Cisco is a dream for Cover 3 teams, which bodes well for Jags DC Joe Cullen. He can hold up when playing a deep centerfielder role, showing off some ability to maintain proper spacing and trigger on the QB, even if he can be too overzealous at times. Moreover, Cisco can roll down to play hook/curl assignments as a pseudo-box player because of how quickly he reacts to and drives on plays in front of him. Long speed is a question mark for Cisco, which means playing man coverage from the slot is going to be tough, but he offers enough elsewhere that he can still be a decent starter along the lines of Ha Ha Clinton-Dix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.headline: Syracuse DB Andre Cisco’s one elite trait is his explosiveness, according to Pro Football Network draft analyst Oliver Hodgkinson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.analysis: Cisco (6'1"/209) saw his 2020 season come to a premature end, as he suffered a torn ACL after colliding with a teammate during pregame warmups ahead of the Orange’s September matchup with Georgia Tech. But the standout safety had done enough in the two seasons prior to merit serious interest as an NFL prospect, with some draft analysts believing that Cisco could be a Day 2 selection this spring. One reason why is his explosiveness, in Hodgkinson’s opinion. “Cisco is an impressive athlete,” Hodgkinson wrote. “I don’t think he’s quite an elite athlete overall, but he does have one elite trait in his explosiveness. The Syracuse safety can easily generate immense amounts of momentum out of his breaks, and his closing speed shows up at all ranges.” The knee injury may complicate things when it comes to where Cisco is ultimately picked, but the safety could wind up being a steal if he slips far enough down the board.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.headline: Syracuse junior S Andre Cisco will opt out of the remainder of the 2020 season and enter the 2021 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-cisc.analysis: Opting out of the 2020 season was a formality -- Cisco is out for the season after suffering a freak lower-body injury in pregame warmups ahead of the Georgia Tech game a few weeks ago when he collided with a teammate. He’s been inactive the past few games. Cisco, a preseason AP first-team All-American, intercepted 13 passes in college, the highest active total in the FBS. In August, The Athletic’s Dane Brugler ranked Cisco (6'0/205) as the No. 2 draft-eligible safety in college football. At the time, Brugler wrote that Cisco was considered a top-60 prospect by multiple NFL scouts. Cisco is a ballhawk in coverage but needs to get better at tackling in space.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.headline: Jaguars acquired DT Davon Godchaux from the Saints in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.analysis: Godchaux becomes the second defensive player the Jaguars have added ahead of the deadline. Early Monday morning, they went out and acquired safety Jessie Bates from the Falcons to improve their secondary, and now they’ve added Godchaux to bolster a defensive line that has been dealt a few injuries in recent weeks. Godchaux, like Bates, is also on an expiring contract, but should provide a small upgrade to what is already a top-10 defense. The 31-year-old lineman has totaled 15 tackles and one TFL this season while appearing on 163 snaps, with most of his contributions coming in run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the NFL’s defensive tackle market “has been hot,” and teams “might” try to trade for Derrick Brown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.analysis: The Panthers are “not actively looking to move” Brown, but Breer says they have considered it. Other defensive tackles on other teams who have come up in trade talks include Grover Stewart, Davon Godchaux, Nathan Shepherd, Christian Barmore and Bobby Brown. The Dolphins have told teams they are not interested in trading away Zach Sieler.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.headline: Saints acquired DT Davon Godchaux from the Patriots in exchange for a seventh-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.analysis: Godchaux has appeared in every regular season game for the Patriots since 2021 — his first season with the team. He has started all but one of those games. The veteran defensive tackle is a prototypical run-stopper, who has racked up 123 tackles over the last two seasons with just three TFLs and zero sacks. Last year’s Saints ranked 31st in rush yards allowed and yards per carry (4.9) allowed, and Gochaux will be called on to help rectify that problem. Godchaux is under contract for the next two seasons but can be released next offseason for a cap savings of $8.5 million if the Saints don’t want to pay him beyond 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Patriots have given DT Davon Godchaux permission to seek a trade.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.analysis: Godchaux was reportedly available at the trade deadline last year but nothing materialized. The Pats have since fired their head coach and hired Mike Vrabel as the team’s next boss. As Rapoport notes, the shift in defensive scheme is a reason for both Godchaux and the Pats to find a trade partner this time around. Godchaux logged six pressures and one TFL last year in his age-30 season. Given his age and lack of production, the Pats aren’t likely to get much in return for him in a trade.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.headline: Patriots DT Davon Godchaux is available ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, according to Dianna Russini of the Athletic.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.analysis: Russini notes that the 49ers are looking to add help on defense and the team is aware of Godchaux’s availability via trade. While it’s unclear if anything will materialize before Tuesday’s trade deadline, San Francisco certainly fits the mold as a team that wouldn’t mind taking on Godchaux’s salary and parting with draft picks given where the 49ers are in their contention window. Russini also notes that New England is open to trading receivers Tyquan Thornton and Kendrick Bourne as well as safety Kyle Dugger.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.headline: Patriots signed DT Davon Godchaux to a two-year $21 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.analysis: Per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, the deal is worth “up to” $21 million and features $16.5 million in guarantees. Godchaux signed with the Patriots as a free agent in 2021 and has appeared in all 51 regular season games and the team’s lone playoff appearance. He has been a rotational lineman who sees the majority of his reps in run defense. Godchaux totaled 56 tackles, two TFLs, and one fumble recovery in 2023.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.headline: Patriots signed DT Davon Godchaux to a two-year, $20.8 million extension through 2024.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.analysis: Godchaux joined the Patriots last offseason on a two-year deal after spending his first four years with the Dolphins, and the team obviously liked what they saw. This deal makes Godchaux one of the highest-paid run stuffers in the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.headline: Patriots signed DT Davon Godchaux, formerly of the Dolphins, to a two-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.analysis: The deal is worth “up to” $16 million, and includes $9 million guaranteed. The Pats are reversing the New England-to-Miami pipeline as they look to shore up their run defense. Godchaux is a load in the middle of the line, though he was limited to five games last season after tearing his biceps in October. Stout in the run game, 26-year-old Godchaux can also create some pressure up the middle. It could prove to be a shrewd early signing in what is going to be a more confusing market than usual because of the declining salary cap.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.headline: Dolphins placed DT Davon Godchaux (torn biceps) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.analysis: As expected. Godchaux sought a second opinion but was eventually moved to injured reserve to undergo season-ending surgery. He finishes 2020 with 16 tackles and two quarterback hits. Expect coach Brian Flores to replace him with both Zach Sieler and rookie Raekwan Davis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Dolphins DT Davon Godchaux suffered a torn biceps in Week 5 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-godc.analysis: He’ll get a second opinion on his injury before inevitably being moved to season-ending injured reserve. Godchaux has been impactful this year, totaling 16 tackles and two quarterback hits in Miami’s front-seven, but Zach Sieler’s emergence lightens the blow. Expect coach Brian Flores to demand more from rookie Raekwan Davis, too.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold (quad) will not play in Week 10 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Macdonald said Darnold will need at least one more week to recover from the quad injury that sidelined him in Week 9. While Drew Lock (oblique) is dealing with his own injury, Macdonald said he believes the team can manage it and expects him to start next week against the Raiders. The Seahawks will have their bye in Week 11, so hopefully three straight weeks off will give him enough time to recover before Week 12’s game against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock suffered an oblique injury today, and his status for Week 10 against the Raiders is “up in the air.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Macdonald also said that he does not know whether Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) will be healthy enough to play. Lock has also been dealing with tendinitis in his throwing-arm elbow. If both Lock and Darnold are ruled out, it will be Jalen Milroe who leads the Seahawks’ offense against the Raiders next week. Milroe would warrant starting consideration in two-quarterback leagues thanks to his rushing abilities.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks declared QB Sam Darnold, WR Rashid Shaheed, T Charles Cross, G Quenton Nelson, LB Uchenna Nwosu, DT Brandon Pili, and DT Leonard Williams inactive for Week 9 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold was ruled out earlier in the week while Shaheed misses his second consecutive game with a knee injury. Drew Lock gets the start under center for the second time this season while veteran receiver Cooper Kupp could see a slight uptick in usage with Shaheed sidelined. Injury trouble along the offensive line could lead to a more ball-out-quick offensive game plan as the Seahawks look to keep pace in the NFC West.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Sam Darnold (quad) could “potentially” miss Week 10 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Garafolo added that Darnold is dealing with a cracked rib, though it sounds like the quad issue is what’s preventing him from playing. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald called Darnold “week to week” on Wednesday. They get their bye in Week 11, so holding him out for one more game to get an extended break makes the most sense. Fantasy managers should plan on Darnold missing Week 10 in addition to today’s game against Arizona. Drew Lock will start today. As long as his elbow issue doesn’t flare up, he will be in line to start next week as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold (quad) will not play in Week 9 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Per Macdonald, Darnold also suffered a rib injury early in the team’s Week 8 loss to the Bears, though that doesn’t appear to be the reason he’s out this week. Darnold is considered week-to-week. Per Macdonald, he won’t go on injured reserve. It’s possible this quad issue is related to the glute issue that sidelined Darnold earlier in the season. Either way, Darnold’s health concerns are now becoming an issue for a Seahawks team that was already struggling to live up to the hype. Drew Lock will draw the start versus Arizona this week. He’ll likely start in Week 10 as well. With two successful appearances under his belt this year, Lock is a somewhat safe QB2 bet for Superflex managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold completed 17-of-34 passes for 188 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Seahawks’ 34-17, Week 8 loss to the Bears, adding 20 yards on two rushes.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold really struggled through consistent pressure from Dennis Allen’s aggressive defensive front as the Seahawks gained just 252 yards of total offense. Things looked manageable in the first half while Darnold leaned heavily on alpha wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, feeding his top option for 92 yards before the break. Allen’s second half adjustments all but removed JSN from the offense, holding him to just 26 yards after the break. Week 8 went down as only the third game of the 2026 season in which Darnold threw multiple touchdowns, leaving him outside QB2 range and on waiver wires ahead of a Week 9 meeting with the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold completed 20-of-28 passes for 257 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Seahawks’ 20-3, Week 7 win over the Chiefs, adding 17 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold continued to flaunt his connection with wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba with zero regard to the naysayers, feeding his alpha 12 targets on 28 pass attempts, the latter of whom accounted for 150 of the 257 pass yards for Darnold. As you probably guessed, Smith-Njigba was also the recipient of Darnold’s lone touchdown throw, which was a dime down the left sideline on a corner route that the veteran signal caller dropped into the bread basket. The two would connect on another similar play later in the same quarter in which Smith-Njigba was forced out at the two, with the result of that drive Darnold’s interception in the end zone. Darnold continues to do just enough for his team and not enough for fantasy managers that thought they could grab cheap production late in drafts. He’s better sent back to the waiver wire than inserted into starting lineups. The Seahawks next face the Bears on the second half of back-to-back Monday Night Football games, where Darnold remains a shaky fantasy option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold’s starting quarterback job is not in jeopardy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: The Seahawks’ head coach stood by his quarterback today, saying Darnold is “definitely part of the solution” to the offense’s recent struggles. Darnold returned somewhat quickly from a glute tendon strain a couple of weeks ago. One wonders if he is still rounding back into form following the early-season ailment. Backup Drew Lock played well in his stead, but the Seahawks believe their Super Bowl-winning quarterback should keep his job. That makes sense to us. He’s a QB2 next week against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold completed 27-of-51 passes for 278 yards and two interceptions in the Seahawks’ 17-14, Week 6 loss to the Broncos, adding 19 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: The Seahawks struggled to move the football throughout against the tenacious situational play calling from Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph, scoring only three points until just over five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. A late-game surge saw them punch on in and a successful two-point conversion drew the team within three points. They would stop the Broncos on the subsequent possession but an interception in Denver territory put the game in jeopardy. The defense would do their job and force a three-and-out that took only 15 seconds off the clock, giving the ball back to Darnold to lead a two-minute drill to send the game to overtime through a chip shot field goal. Darnold would throw his second interception in overtime, watching from the sideline as the Broncos walked it off with a 53-yard Will Lutz field goal. The loss sends the Seahawks to 3-3, matching the total number of losses from a season ago through only six weeks of the 2026 season. The Seahawks have work to do to make up ground in the NFC West, now 2.5 games behind the undefeated 49ers through the first third of the regular season. Darnold and the Seahawks now have a long week to prepare for the now-undefeated Chiefs at home in Week 7, where Darnold will be a fringe QB2 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold completed 18-of-29 passes for 195 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Seahawks’ 32-29, Week 5 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: It was a rough outing for Darnold, who was picked off on his first pass attempt of the day and absorbed a season-high five sacks. His lone touchdown pass came on a 16-yard pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Darnold completed a short two-yard pass to JSN, who turned it upfield for the score to give the Seahawks the 23-21 lead with just over five minutes left in the third quarter. On the Seahawks’ final drive of the game, Darnold found JSN for a 35-yard completion, but three straight incompletions, including an uncharacteristic drop by JSN, put the Seahawks in a fourth-and-10 situation that they were unable to convert after Cooper Kupp came up a yard short on his second reception of the night. Darnold has now thrown seven touchdowns and six interceptions in his last three games since returning from injury, and now faces a short week to get ready for the Broncos on Thursday night. He profiles as a mid-to-low-end QB2 in what could be a tough road matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Panthers “have received calls” on DT Derrick Brown’s availability via trade.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: The Panthers have said that they are “not actively looking to move Brown,” but it Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reported last week that they have considered it. One of the premier DTs in the league, Brown could fetch a decent pick haul if the Panthers were willing to move him. With the NFL trade deadline set to pass on Tuesday, we will soon know the fate of several players who are rumored to be on the move, but it sounds like it will take a lot for the Panthers to give up Brown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the NFL’s defensive tackle market “has been hot,” and teams “might” try to trade for Derrick Brown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: The Panthers are “not actively looking to move” Brown, but Breer says they have considered it. Other defensive tackles on other teams who have come up in trade talks include Grover Stewart, Davon Godchaux, Nathan Shepherd, Christian Barmore and Bobby Brown. The Dolphins have told teams they are not interested in trading away Zach Sieler.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: Panthers DE Derrick Brown (elbow) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: Brown appeared on Thursday’s injury report as a limited participant on Thursday, but successfully practiced in full on Friday. The Panthers’ star defender should have a fruitful outing against an injury-depleted Saints offensive line missing OT Taliese Fuaga (ankle) and C/OG Erik McCoy, who is on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: Panthers DE Derrick Brown (elbow) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: Mid-week additions to the injury report are concerning, particularly for a team’s lynchpin defender. Brown is a difference-maker as both a pass rusher and run defender, boasting 16 quarterback pressures, four sacks and 20 tackles. Whether the Saints can exploit his potential absence on Sunday is up for debate, but having him on the field is certainly ideal for Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: Panthers DT Derrick Brown left Carolina’s Week 8 against the Bills with a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: Brown limped off the field late in the fourth quarter with a knee injury and was in the blue medical tent for a while. He seemed to be in good spirits on the sideline afterward, but he was listed as questionable to return. The Panthers are down 40-9, so they likely just wanted to hold their best defender out with the Packers on deck next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: Panthers DE Derrick Brown “has continued to impress this summer and should be a force” in his return from last year’s season-ending knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: Brown was sidelined for the entirety of the 2024 season after undergoing surgery to repair a meniscus tear that he suffered in Week 1. Brown has been a “high-impact player” for years, notably setting the defensive linemen record for tackles in a single season (103) in 2023. The Athletic’s Jeff Howe reports, “judging by conversations with those around him this season, it doesn’t sound like there’s any dropoff in sight.” Brown was held out of preseason play due to a separate rib/oblique issue, but there are no indications that Brown’s Week 1 availability is in question. The Panthers’ defensive leader will have a busy day, attempting to contain the Jaguars’ three-deep rushing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: Panthers GM Dan Morgan said Derrick Brown (knee) is “cleared for all activity.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: Of course, the caveat is that the Panthers “will be smart” with the Pro Bowl defensive lineman. Brown’s status for the season doesn’t look to be in any doubt after his season-ending meniscus injury in Week 1 last year, but he’ll likely have plenty of off-days in training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: Panthers HC Dave Canales said the team is taking it “week to week” with Derrick Brown’s (knee) recovery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: Brown suffered a season-ending meniscus injury in Week 1 of last season and said earlier this offseason that his goal is to be ready for Week 1. How that plays out is anybody’s guess, but it’s clear the Panthers are in no rush to put their star defensive tackle back on the field until he’s at 100 percent. Brown racked up a career-high 103 tackles in 2023 and received a lucrative four-year, $96 million contract last offseason for his efforts. His return, coupled with the additions of top-100 draft picks Nic Scourton and Princely Umanmielen, should go a long way in bolstering a Panthers defense that finished dead last in points and yards allowed last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports that the Panthers will be “seeking big-name players in free agency,” particularly on defense.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: Graziano suggests the Panthers “might be one of the teams willing to spend big to lure defensive tackle Milton Williams away from the Super Bowl champion Eagles.” The Panthers will also attempt to bolster their edge rush and Graziano lists Saints defensive end Chase Young as an “intriguing option.” Adding Williams and Young to a defensive line featuring Derrick Brown and Jadeveon Clowney could help turn around Carolina’s dire 2024 defense. Safeties Jevon Holland and Camryn Bynum are also reportedly on the Panthers’ short list of preferred defenders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports Panthers DL Derrick Brown (knee) could miss the remainder of the regular season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: Brown in Week 1 against the Saints sustained an injury to his meniscus. He’ll require surgery and could be out for much of the season. It’s a brutal blow to a Carolina defense that was shredded by Derek Carr and the Saints on opening day. Without Brown, the Panthers almost certainly have the NFL’s worst pass rush.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jets DE Will McDonald has requested a trade.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: McDonald has been lightly used this season by the Jets. The former first-rounder has appeared in all nine games this season, totaling three sacks and 15 tackles while appearing on just 278 defensive snaps, per PFF. According to Rapoport, the Jets have not engaged in trade talks for McDonald despite receiving calls, and “they have no plans to.” With a 2-7 record, the Jets should be sellers, but have maintained for over a week that they would prefer not to move many players, if any.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: Jets EDGE Will McDonald (calf) is active for New York’s Week 5 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: He popped up on the Friday injury report with a calf, but will try to play through it. Inactive for the Jets are RB Breece Hall (quad), LB Kiko Mauigoa (quad), OL Dylan Parham (knee), WR Adonai Mitchell (finger), EDGE Nate Lynn and CB Nahshon Wright. The four with injury statuses were ruled out on Friday, the other two are healthy scratches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: Will McDonald (calf) is questionable for New York’s Week 5 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: He popped up on the injury report on Friday, never a great sign. McDonald has a 68.4 PFF pass rush grade on 69 pass rushes and the Jets would lose something on defense without him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: Jets declared CB D’Angelo Ponds, S Minkah Fitzpatrick, RB Kene Nwangwu, ED Joseph Ossai, LB Trevin Wallace, and K Blake Grupe inactive for Week 2 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: We knew Fitzpatrick had already been ruled out with a groin injury. D’Angelo Pounds had practiced all week, and Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that he was healthy enough to play, but apparently there is no room for him in the secondary at the moment. The good news for the Jets is that Will McDonald (ankle) is active and will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: Jets HC Aaron Glenn said Will McDonald will play in Week 2 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: McDonald popped up on Thursday’s injury report with an ankle injury, but speaking with the media on Friday, Glenn said the fourth-year pass rusher will be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Packers. Rookie CB D’Angelo Ponds, who missed last week with an ankle injury, is also expected to make his NFL debut this week, giving the Jets additional help in the secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: Jets EDGE Will McDonald (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: The midweek downgrade is never a promising sign, and the Jets were definitely hoping to have a full complement of pass-rushers against a beleaguered Packers offensive line in Week 2. Assuming this wasn’t a practice injury that spirals into an extended absence, we’d expect McDonald to be listed as questionable tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: SNY’s Connor Hughes said “there is a lot of smoke” to the Jets drafting Ohio State LB Arvell Reese with the 2026 NFL Draft’s No. 2 overall pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: There is “an internal debate” in the Jets’ organization between drafting Reese or Texas Tech EDGE David Bailey.
