Bailey, 22, is generally regarded as the draft’s top pass rusher and is knocked for his run defense. Reese is a complete player and is currently just 20 years old. Hughes notes that current Jets EDGE Will McDonald is a great pass rusher, but can be a liability in run defense. McDonald and Bailey would form a potent pass rush duo, but could be a suboptimal tandem against the run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: Jets general manager Darren Mougey said the team plans to exercise EDGE Will McDonald’s fifth-year option.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: McDonald was taken No. 15 overall in the 2023 draft and is now eligible to have his fifth-year option picked up. In three seasons, McDonald has tallied 21.5 sacks, including back-to-back seasons of at least eight sacks. His option is expected to be around $14 million, making his contract for 2027 relatively light for a productive edge rusher. McDonald will head into year four with the Jets likely exploring extension talks to keep him long-term.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: Jets placed EDGE Will McDonald IV (knee) on season-ending injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: McDonald marked eight sacks in 15 games this year and continues to look like a solid building block pass rusher. The Jets will face a decision on whether they want to pick up his fifth-year option this offseason. With the season over in all but name, the Jets also sent LB Kiko Mauigoa (neck) and DL Jay Tufele (foot) to the injured reserve list.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: Jets ruled out TE Mason Taylor (neck) for Week 17 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: Taylor has now missed three straight games as a result of his neck injury. The rookie tight end, who has caught 44 passes for 369 yards and one touchdown this season, will have one more chance to suit up for Week 18’s season finale against the Bills, but after missing three-straight weeks of practice, he could be a long shot for next week. In addition to Taylor the Jets also ruled out EDGE Will McDonald (knee), DL Jay Tufele (foot), and LB Kiko Mauigoa (neck) for Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.headline: Falcons traded S Jessie Bates to the Jaguars in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.analysis: The Jaguars also sent a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Falcons in exchange for Bates, who is in the final year of his contract. Bates provides an immediate upgrade to a defensive unit that already ranks top-10 in points and yards allowed per game but has been more susceptible to being hurt through the air. Bates is a three-time Second-Team All-Pro and among the top safeties in the league. It stands to reason that the Jaguars will look to extend him at some point next offseason, but for now, he will join a 6-2 team that is clearly willing to go all in on what could be a deep run in the postseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.headline: Falcons S Jessie Bates said he hasn’t had any extension talks with the Falcons yet but would like to.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.analysis: “I want to retire as a Falcon. My family loves it here,” Bates told local media. Bates had the worst season of his prime, per PFF grading, last season, finishing with a 59.6 PFF coverage grade. Entering his age-29 season, he’ll likely have to have a strong 2026 campaign to remain in Atlanta’s plans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.headline: Falcons HC Raheem Morris said Michael Penix (knee) will be day-to-day.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.analysis: Penix practiced in the days leading up to Week 8’s game against the Dolphins but was ultimately ruled out in favor of Kirk Cousins. The second-year quarterback is one of several Falcons players who are day-to-day to start the week, as Morris also said S Jessie Bates (ankle), DL Zach Harrison (knee), CB Billy Bowman (hamstring), and EDGE Jalon Walker (groin) would also be day-to-day to open the week. Penix appears to be trending in the right direction but if he’s unable to go, Cousins would again draw the start on the road against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.headline: Falcons S Jessie Bates (ankle) will not return in Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.analysis: Bates suffered an ankle injury versus Miami and was ruled out in the fourth quarter. Bates has appeared in six games this year and has 39 tackles. Losing Bates is a big blow to an Atlanta defense that had looked like one of the league’s best units before today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.headline: Falcons signed S Jessie Bates, formerly of the Bengals, to a four-year, $64.02 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.analysis: Bates was considered “as good as gone” from the Bengals by The Athletic’s Jay Morrison back in February. Now, that speculation has been confirmed, as Bates inks a four-year deal with the Falcons, who will give him $23 million in the first year of his deal. Bates reluctantly played under the franchise tag last season but was due a big payday after performing at a high level for his first five years in the league. Bates was named a Second-team All-Pro in 2020 and has totaled 14 interceptions and 479 tackles in his career. He will immediately improve a Falcons pass defense that allowed the eighth-most passing yards (231.9) last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.headline: The Athletic’s Jay Morrison writes S Jessie Bates is “as good as gone” from the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.analysis: Bates was a good solider and played last year on the franchise tag, he’ll likely be one of the NFL’s biggest free agents this offseason with a number of teams pursuing safety help. The Bengals drafted Dax Hill last offseason to take Bates’ spot and though Bates has said he’d love to return to Cincinnati, the actions are speaking louder than the words on Cincinnati’s desire (or lack thereof) to give him a long-term deal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.headline: Bengals S Jessie Bates said he’d “love to” return to the Bengals in 2023.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.analysis: Bates was franchise tagged by the Bengals for the 2022 season, and is once again set to hit free agency. The former second-round pick has spent his first fives seasons with the Bengals, starting 79 games while totaling 14 interceptions, 43 passes defensed, and three forced fumbles. A Second-team All-Pro in 2020, Bates will be one of the more coveted safeties on the market when free agency officially opens. He held out for the majority of last summer in hopes of signing a new contract, but ultimately signed his franchise tag on August 23rd and reported to training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.headline: Bengals S Jessie Bates (contract) returned to training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.analysis: Bates reportedly signed the franchise tag Tuesday. It appears he will suit up this season as the Bengals defend their AFC title crown. The team had reportedly offered Bates a five-year deal without sufficient guaranteed money. Bates, who has 13 interceptions and 35 passes defended in four NFL seasons, was a key piece of a Bengals secondary that stepped it up late in the 2021 season and into the postseason. Pro Football Focus graded Cincinnati’s defense as the 11th best coverage unit in 2021.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Bengals unsigned franchise S Jessie Bates will not report to training camp Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.analysis: This was expected, and it will be an official start to a holdout. The deadline for a long-term deal has already passed, so it’s unclear what type of resolution Bates is wanting from the Bengals. We can only imagine he desires a trade, as he’s already stated he won’t play on the franchise tag. We’ll see how long this thing drags out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.headline: CBS Sports’ Josina Anderson reports Bengals unsigned franchise player S Jessie Bates has “no intentions” of reporting to training camp or playing on the tag this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jessie-bat.analysis: Considering the deadline for the two sides to reach a long-term deal is in mere hours, this could be a final push by Bates’ side to get the Bengals to better their offer. According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, the Bengals are offering Bates a five-year deal, but it includes minimal guaranteed money over what he’d get on the franchise tag. This isn’t the first time it’s been reported that Bates has no plans to play on the tag.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught 2-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: The only positive to take from this is every Tampa Bay receiver who caught a pass clobbered their production from the week before. Godwin did have a 12-yard rush, but it’s another clunker for the wideout in a year where Godwin has yet to reach 50 yards. It’s a mistake to bet that mark will be reached in Week 11 against the Lions after their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin failed to catch his only target in the Bucs’ Week 8 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin has fallen off the map this year, but forces beyond his control caused this goose egg. The Bucs did not complete a pass and only attempted three in total. With their defense terrorizing Michael Penix, Tampa Bay leaned on their ground game to an absurd degree. Emeka Egbuka is working through a foot injury and didn’t play today. Godwin will return to the WR4/5 border if he’s back for Week 9. Godwin would have some FLEX appeal if the Bucs are without their No. 1 receiver versus the Bears next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught 4-of-5 targets for 27 yards in the Bucs’ Week 7 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: That might not look like much, especially with Emeka Egbuka on the shelf, but it was actually a 45 percent target share in a game where the Bucs attempted just 11 passes in a 43-13 victory. Godwin also had a score called back by a Bucky Irving illegal shift. Promising in theory, we suppose, though Godwin has not cracked 40 yards receiving since Week 2. He has not reached 50 all year. It feels like he will have to get more involved at some point, but then again, this team has a lot of young receiving talent. Godwin’s WR4 prospects are hanging on by a thread heading into Week 8 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught 4-of-8 targets for 37 yards in the Bucs’ Week 6 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin’s eight targets today go down as a season-high, but he failed to make much of his opportunities, per usual. The veteran wideout hasn’t hit 50 receiving yards in a game this year and is still looking for his first touchdown of the season. With Emeka Egbuka pulling away as the team’s WR1, there isn’t much volume headed Godwin’s way. With Jalon Daniels likely to make another start next week, Godwin is tumbling down the WR4 ranks ahead of Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught all three targets for 37 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 5 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin’s three targets finished tied for fourth on the team behind Emeka Egbuka, Cade Otton, and Kenny Gainwell on a night backup quarterback Jalon Daniels attempted only 25 passes. Week 5 now marks the fourth game in five tries in which Godwin was held to four targets or fewer, leaving the veteran wide receiver completely unusable in a fantasy setting, for the time being. He can safely be stashed on benches ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught 6-of-7 targets for 31 yards in the Bucs’ Week 4 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: UDFA rookie Jalon Daniels made his first career start and leaned on Godwin for some easy completions. Godwin led the team in catches and targets, though Cade Otton surprisingly led the way in yards with 37. Godwin set new season highs in targets and catches. The Bucs are operating an incredibly low-wattage offense without Baker Mayfield, but Godwin could continue to see enough work to return WR4 numbers in PPR leagues. He will put that to the test versus the Cowboys in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin (ankle) is not on Tampa Bay’s final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin was a full participant for two straight days after a Wednesday DNP. The insertion of Jalon Daniels makes him (well, makes every Buccaneers player) hard to trust for Week 4, but Godwin is probably still in the FLEX conversation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin should be expected to play in Week 4 against the Packers at this point, although he has mostly underperformed thus far. Buccaneers OC Zac Robinson said earlier that Godwin Jr. “is a stud and will continue to do his thing. The ball will find him.” That might be harder than one imagines with an undrafted free agent rookie at quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin (ankle) returned to practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: It will likely go down as a limited session for the veteran wideout, but Godwin should be on track to play in Week 4. The bad news is that he will do so with UDFA rookie Jalon Daniels as his quarterback. Godwin was already off to a slow start, and things aren’t likely to improve with a backup quarterback under center. He is low-wattage FLEX play for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin’s history of lower-leg injuries makes this a little bit concerning. The veteran wide receiver is already set to catch passes from a backup quarterback. If active, he may be playing on an injured ankle. He can only be viewed as a boom-bust FLEX at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 4-of-6 targets for 25 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Otton was targeted a couple of times in the end zone, but Baker Mayfield wasn’t able to connect with the tight end on either attempt. The 25 yards are his most since Week 5, but it’s still a middling — at best — effort for the 27-year-old. Fantasy managers should look elsewhere in Week 11 against the Lions after Tampa Bay’s bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton was not targeted in the Bucs’ Week 8 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Otton has one catch over his past three appearances and hasn’t hit 40 yards since Week 3. The Bucs, who only attempted three passes today, will increase the pass volume in Week 9, but that alone won’t be enough to get Otton back into fantasy lineups. He is not even in the TE2 mix for Week 9 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton was held without a catch in the Bucs’ Week 7 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: What seemed like it could maybe be a pop-up performance for Otton in Emeka Egbuka’s (concussion, foot) absence instead turned into a one-target day as the Bucs rode their rushing attack and Panthers turnovers to a dominant road W. Otton typically comes with a 3-4 catch floor, but the same has been true of his “ceiling” this season. He will continue to struggle to get into the mix ahead of Week 8 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 1-of-2 targets for four yards in the Bucs’ Week 6 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Otton had caught between three and five passes in every game this year until today, so this goes down as his first true bust of the season. On the other hand, he has peaked at five catches and 56 yards with zero touchdowns thus far, so the ceiling has been nonexistent. Otton could increase his production once Baker Mayfield is back in the lineup, but it doesn’t look like that will happen next week. He is barely in the TE2 conversation as long as Jalon Daniels remains under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 4-of-6 targets for 37 yards in the Bucs’ Week 4 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Otton’s 37 yards were somehow enough to lead Tampa Bay, though that largely speaks to the ineffective nature of the team’s passing attack. With Jalon Daniels under center, there simply wasn’t much production to go around. He was intercepted twice and threw for just 148 yards. With Daniels likely to make his second start of the year on Week 5, Otton is a low-end TE2 for his upcoming matchup with Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 3-of-6 targets for 56 yards in the Bucs’ Week 3 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: As usual, Otton led the Bucs in pass routes and was second on the team in targets behind Emeka Egbuka. Most of Otton’s production came on a 37-yard catch in the first half. Baker Mayfield narrowly missed the tight end for another long gain later in the contest. Otton’s route involvement should keep him in deep league lineups next week against the Packers, unless Mayfield (hand) is sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 5-of-6 targets for 38 yards in the Bucs’ Week 2 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Otton led the Bucs in targets while running nearly every route. This has been Otton’s role for quite some time. You know what you’re getting if you use Otton in fantasy lineups: He’s something of a PPR cheat code when the Bucs hit a negative game script. He’ll be a deep league option in Week 3 against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 3-of-5 targets for 26 yards in the Bucs’ Week 1 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: This is about a standard Otton statline, though this one came on a day where Baker Mayfield attempted fewer than 30 passes. With Jalen McMillan sidelined, Otton probably would have exceeded five catches had the Bucs not kept killing drives with sacks and turnovers, alas. Otton is always good for a few PPR points on the back end of the TE2 ranks, but that appears to be his ceiling heading in to his age-27 campaign.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Buccaneers TE Cade Otton said there is “a lot of play action” in new OC Zac Robinson’s scheme.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: This is the kind of thing we like to hear for QB Baker Mayfield and his pass catchers. Robinson did not feature play action during his two seasons as the Falcons’ offensive coordinator, nor did former Buccaneers OC Josh Grizzard, so Otton’s comments are reassuring. Per PFF, NFL offenses averaged 7.76 yards per pass play with play action and just 6.72 without it. Upping the play action rate should help the Buccaneers run a more efficient offense in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Bucs and Chargers are hosting Georgia TE Oscar Delp for top-30 pre-draft visits.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Delp last week made pre-draft visits with the Vikings, Patriots, and Ravens. Delp at Georgia was a little-used tight end who totaled 65 receptions for 793 yards and seven touchdowns over his final three collegiate seasons. He was targeted on a meager 13 percent of his pass routes over those three years. Delp, 23, profiles as a rotational tight end to start his NFL career, though he has some upside if he lands in the right spot. In LA he would compete with Oronde Gadsden II for tight end snaps and routes, and in Tampa he would compete with Cade Otton, who recently re-signed with the Bucs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka caught 3-of-5 targets for 38 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: It was Egbuka’s first game since Week 6 because of his foot injury, and it was pretty similar to his previous efforts in 2026. He was able to get lose for a 21-yard catch from the arm of Baker Mayfield, but once again, he was unable to eclipse 50 yards; a mark he hasn’t bested since Week 3. Egbuka is a high-floor, low-ceiling WR3 going forward, and the next chance will come after a bye in Week 11 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) is active for Week 9 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: As expected, Egbuka is back after missing two games with his foot injury. The wideout has been heavily targeted when healthy, but hasn’t been particularly effective with those opportunities with zero games over 65 yards in 2026. The Bucs’ inactives for Week 9 will be OLB Yaya Diaby, G Trevor Keegan, G Billy Schrauth, CB Ayden Garnes and DL DeMonte Capehart.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Emeka Egbuka (foot) will play in Week 9 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Egbuka missed two games with the foot injury, though a concussion also kept him out for one of them. He practiced in full on Friday, so we’re not expecting much of a pitch count for the second-year wideout. Without anyone emerging as a viable replacement for Egbuka over the past two weeks, he should reclaim the No. 1 receiver role in Tampa Bay without much of a fight. Egbuka will be on the WR2/3 border for his first game back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) is listed as questionable for Week 9 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Egbuka was able to get in another full practice Friday after getting the same Thursday, so it seems like he’s on the right side of the questionable tag, even with coach Todd Bowles suggesting he’ll be a game-time decision. The 24-year-old wideout is on the WR2/WR3 range for the Sunday Night Football showdown against Chicago if he is able to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) was a full participant in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: After only participating in drills on the side and being listed as a non-participant Wednesday, Egbuka was a full-go for Thursday’s session. The 24-year-old will likely need to get in one more full session before fantasy managers can fully trust the wideout for Week 9 against the Bears, but this is obviously a significant step in the right direction.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Egbuka missed Week 7 with a concussion and a foot injury. He cleared the league’s concussion protocol last week, but the foot issue kept him on ice. A DNP today suggests he will miss another week. However, head coach Todd Bowles told reporters Egbuka worked off to the side today. The team will see how he feels tomorrow. That leaves the door open for him to play, but fantasy managers should at least have backup options in place. If he does suit up, Egbuka would be a high-risk WR3 versus Chicago.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Emeka Egbuka (foot) will not play in Week 8 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Bowles said Egbuka did clear concussion protocol, but the foot injury he has been dealing with for the last two weeks will officially sideline him for this week’s game against the Falcons. Hopefully this isn’t any kind of a major setback for Egbuka, who shed his non-contact jersey in Thursday’s practice and was limited in the first two practices to start the week. Ted Hurst will again operate as the Buccaneers’ primary outside target but shouldn’t be trusted as anything more than a risky WR4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: After being limited in back-to-back practices to start the week, and shedding his non-contact jersey on Thursday, Egbuka being a DNP on Friday is a notable setback. Buccaneers beat writer Greg Auman speculated that Egbuka will “be ruled out again” for Week 8’s game against the Falcons, but we’ll wait for official word from the team before drawing conclusions. That said, the Bucs could again have Ted Hurst operating as their primary outside threat.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: The Tampa Bay Times’ Rick Stroud reports Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) shed his non-contact jersey for Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: There’s a good chance Egbuka has been upgraded to a full participant in practice, meaning he is making his way through the league’s concussion protocol. He remains on track to play this week after missing Week 7. With Baker Mayfield back under center, Egbuka may be able to turn around his season after a rather quiet start to the year. He is in the WR2 mix for Week 8 versus the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Egbuka logged one limited practice on Friday last week but was ruled out shortly after. It looks like he is trending in the right direction for Week 8, but the Bucs’ next two injury reports will be more revealing. Assuming all goes well, Egbuka should be back in the WR2 ranks with Baker Mayfield under center and playing well in Tampa Bay’s Week 7 demolition of the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.headline: Tez Johnson caught 2-of-5 targets for 76 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.analysis: Johnson’s 58-yard connection with Baker Mayfield set up a rushing score from Bucky Irving. He also had two big drops on third down that would have kept drives going for the Bucs, and on the first he was seen taking out his frustration on his helmet. Johnson ended up leading the Bucs in receiving yards and tied for the lead in targets, but that’s not quite the compliment it should be. Johnson and Tampa Bay get a bye before a showdown with the Lions in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.headline: Tez Johnson caught 2-of-2 targets for 33 yards and a touchdown in the Bucs’ Week 7 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.analysis: Johnson actually led the Bucs in receiving on an afternoon where they attempted just 11 passes in a 43-13 blowout victory. The limited volume was the result of four Panthers turnovers and a dominant Tampa rushing attack. Johnson’s 14-yard score put the Bucs up 33-6 just before halftime. He worked himself free in the end zone as a besieged Baker Mayfield bought time with his legs. Good stuff for a player who had yet to score this season, but probably not the harbinger of things to come with Emeka Egbuka likely returning for Week 8 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.headline: Tez Johnson caught his only target for 64 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 5 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.analysis: Two of Johnson’s five receptions this season have accounted for 113 yards in what has become a situational role for the Buccaneers behind Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin, and rookie Ted Hurst. That big play ability remains unlikely to translate into consistent fantasy production while running a route on less than a third of the team’s dropbacks, meaning Johnson is likely best left on the waiver wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.headline: Tez Johnson caught 1-of-4 targets for 49 yards in the Bucs’ Week 2 loss against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.analysis: Johnson was targeted a few times downfield in the second half and nearly came down with a long catch that would have put the Bucs in position to beat Cleveland. Johnson, who ran a route on 16 of the Bucs’ 41 drop backs, won’t be fantasy relevant unless the team struggles with wideout injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.headline: Buccaneers WR Tez Johnson left Tuesday’s practice early with a groin injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.analysis: Johnson left practice early Tuesday to get treatment for an apparent strain. Bucs head coach Todd Bowles said the 24-year-old wideout is dealing with a groin injury. The severity of the injury is unclear as Bowles said it’s too early to tell if any of the team’s top four wide receivers would miss next week’s joint practices with the Jets. Chris Godwin, Emeka Egbuka, and Jalen McMillan also missed practice out of maintenance and precaution. With Johnson and David Sills also exiting practice, rookie Ted Hurst saw a boost in practice reps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.headline: ESPN’s Jenna Laine reports that Buccaneers WR Tez Johnson stood out at organized team activities and mandatory minicamp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.analysis: Laine compliments Johnson for standing out among the Buccaneers’ wide receivers, competing in “arguably the most competitive room on the team.” The second-year wide receiver posted a 28/322/5 receiving line as a rookie and should turn in another usable, if volatile FLEX season while stretching the field for Tampa Bay in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.headline: Tez Johnson caught his only target for 17 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 18 win over the Panthers, adding a five-yard rush.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.analysis: The Buccaneers didn’t throw the ball much due to Baker Mayfield’s shoulder issues on top of rainy conditions in Tampa Bay. But Johnson wasn’t likely to get many targets anyway. The rookie wideout showed some real promise at times while Tampa dealt with wideout injuries, and could be in line for more targets in 2026 depending on what the Bucs do with their crowded wideout room. He likely won’t be a factor in the playoffs if the Buccaneers are able to clinch the division with a Saints win over the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.headline: Tez Johnson was not targeted in the Bucs’ Week 14 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.analysis: At least not officially. Johnson did draw a 28-yard DPI early in the third quarter. Fair enough, but today’s doughnut comes as Mike Evans is probably on the right side of questionable to return for Thursday’s game against the Falcons. Even if he doesn’t, rookie Johnson has proven to be a safe 12-team league drop with bye weeks over and the fantasy playoffs beginning in Week 15.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.headline: Tez Johnson caught 1-of-2 targets for five yards in the Bucs’ Week 13 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.analysis: With Bucky Irving finally back in action and Chris Godwin getting more involved, Johnson’s usage cratered. The only time he made a noticeable impact in the game was when his second quarter OPI penalty took a Rachaad White touchdown off the board. Johnson should continue to soak up snaps and run routes in this short-handed offense, at least until Mike Evans returns. It’s just not providing WR4 numbers in fantasy with the playoffs almost here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.headline: Tez Johnson caught 1-of-3 passes for six yards in a Week 11 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tez-johnson/00.analysis: He also rushed three times for zero yards. Johnson has been a nice story as a seventh-round rookie, but he has never topped 60 yards receiving in a game, so his fantasy value is excessively tied to touchdown value. That makes him really difficult to trust, especially next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 4-of-7 targets for 32 yards in the Bears’ Week 9 win over the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond had a quiet day, but made a huge 13-yard catch on the final drive that ended with a Cairo Santos’ game-winning field goal. Luther Burden exited the game with a head injury late, and if Burden can’t go in Week 11 after the bye, Raymond will be an intriguing dart throw for that contest. If Burden can go, he’s tough to trust in redraft formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 2-of-3 targets for 14 yards in the Bears’ Week 8 win over the Seahawks, adding 39 yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond’s lone “carry” came on a third-and-long in the fourth quarter in a three-point game, with the play ruled a rush attempt following a slightly backwards toss on a quick swing pass to the perimeter. Raymond did the rest as he turned on the jets for a 39-yard gain to the five, which D’Andre Swift would punch in for the second of his three rushing scores on the evening. Raymond remains unlikely to match his early-season exploits but can be stashed in case of injury to Luther Burden, Rome Odunze, or Colston Loveland.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught both of his targets for 18 yards in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond ran a pass route on 18 of the Bears’ 45 drop backs and didn’t see a target until the second half. He has been mostly phased out of the team’s passing offense since profiling as Chicago’s de facto WR1 over the first couple games of the season. Raymond, who has just 30 receiving yards over his past three games, can be left on the waiver wire ahead of Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 3-of-4 targets for six yards in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond’s fast start to the season has now been erased to the tune of just five catches for 12 yards over the past two weeks. Even with Caleb Williams (hamstring) looking likely to return for Week 6 against the Falcons, Raymond’s brief moment in the 2026 fantasy sun has come and gone.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 6-of-7 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 3 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond has now led the Bears in receiving in two of the team’s first three games, with Week 3 his best performance yet on the back of a 41-yard touchdown through busted coverage. It isn’t likely the career role player will lead the team in receiving throughout the season, but the early returns on investment must have fantasy managers ecstatic for those that either drafted him in the final round or scooped him off the wire following Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 5-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Bears’ Week 2 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: For whatever reason, Raymond again lead the Bears’ receiver corps in production, though Luther Burden did out-target him on fewer snaps. Cold comfort. Although Raymond out-snapped Burden, he was on the field 16 fewer plays than Rome Odunze. Pro Football Focus’ Nathan Jahnke charted Raymond as seeing more time in “12" personnel than his sophomore teammate. We would like to say this is bound to change going forward, but coach Ben Johnson had no problem featuring veteran Olamide Zaccheaus in 2025. Raymond is struggling to create WR4 value of his own, but he is certainly hampering Burden and Odunze’s production ahead of Week 3 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 8-of-9 targets for 89 yards in the Bears’ Week 1 win against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond, who ran a route on 23 of 40 Caleb Williams drop backs, led the Bears in targets, catches, and receiving yards, while Colston Loveland went catchless and Luther Burden was an afterthought. Raymond’s route participation suggests he’ll be a rotational player in the run-first Chicago offense. That should make him a risky option in any sort of fantasy league. Even so, it’s clear Raymond has taken something similar to the D.J. Moore role and could be useful in fantasy this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: The Chicago Tribune’s Sean Hammond reports that Bears WR Rome Odunze exited practice early on Thursday after suffering an apparent leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Per Hammond, Odunze “came up hobbling during an install period at the start of practice,” with what appeared to be a right leg injury. Apparently, Odunze “wasn’t overly concerned” and tried to continue practicing, but Bears trainers removed him from the field. That last bit is encouraging. Hopefully, Odunze’s Week 1 availability has not been jeopardized. Bears TE Colston Loveland and WR Luther Burden would benefit if Odunze cannot play. Odunze is backed up by WR Kalif Raymond.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: The Athletic’s Kevin Fishbain believes the “expectation” is that Kalif Raymond will be the team’s No. 3 receiver.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Jahdae Walker could position himself as the No. 3 with a second-year jump, and third-round pick Zavion Thomas is also in the mix. This room will probably split the snaps enough to make them unappealing from a fantasy perspective, but it’s possible someone emerges as a WR4-type.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Bears signed WR Kalif Raymond, formerly of the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond was mostly a role player and a special teams standout during his five years in Detroit. Last season Raymond had 24 receptions for 289 yards and a touchdown while drawing three starts for the run-heavy Lions. In Chicago, Raymond — entering his age-32 season — will likely function as a role player in Ben Johnson’s run-centric offense. He could see starter’s snaps if the Bears struggle with receiver injuries in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 4-of-7 targets for 60 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 9 win over the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Odunze couldn’t quite haul in a touchdown throw from Caleb Williams on the first drive of the game, but on the next play, he was able to reach the end zone for his first touchdown of the 2026 season. He could have had another, but a perfect throw from Williams bounced off his hands with nothing but green grass in front of him. Still, it’s another competent game for the former first-round pick, and he’s reached 60 yards in each of his last three contests. Odunze belongs in the WR3 range for Week 11 against the Saints after a Week 10 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 4-of-6 targets for 87 yards in the Bears’ Week 8 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Odunze was almost nonexistent in the first half, catching his first pass, an 18-yard reception over the middle of the field, with just under five minutes remaining in the second quarter. The Bears exploited the attention paid to Luther Burden and Colston Loveland after the half, with Odunze catching three passes for chunk gains in the third quarter to help position the team for their sixth victory. Odunze remains unlikely to challenge for the team lead in targets on a weekly basis while playing alongside Burden and Loveland, but his big play ability keeps him in the FLEX discussion, for the time being. That could change in a more favorable matchup through the air in Week 9 against the Buccaneers, where Odunze will be a WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 4-of-5 targets for 69 yards in the Bears’ Week 7 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The yardage total goes down as Odunze’s second highest mark of the season as the third-year receiver was held out of the end zone for the seventh straight game to start the 2026 season. He did make three massive catches on third downs to help extend drives, making his mark felt more with quality than quantity. That doesn’t necessarily benefit fantasy managers that chased his big-play abilities this offseason as Odunze has largely been a fantasy dud outside of the Week 4 win over the Jets in which he returned 15.4 PPR points. He remains best left on fantasy benches ahead of another difficult test against the Seahawks in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 3-of-4 targets for 39 yards in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Odunze, who led the Bears in pass routes on the day, was third in targets while Luther Burden and Colston Loveland had big days with Caleb Williams back under center. Odunze was seeing more targets and air yards with the Bears’ backups QBs under center, though he should remain a high-variance flex in Week 7 against the Patriots. Odunze leads the Chicago offense with a 35 percent air yards share this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 3-of-9 targets for 40 yards in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers, also losing a fumble.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Although the Bears were already losing 31-7, Odunze’s fourth quarter giveaway was an ill-advised decision on a fourth down catch-and-run where he had already secured a new set of downs. Odunze seemed to be extending the ball forward. Unnecessary. Like every Bears pass catcher, Odunze is treading fantasy water waiting for the return of Caleb Williams (hamstring). It appears that will be Week 6 against the Falcons, but Odunze’s returns have been uneven enough that not even Williams’ re-insertion under center will be enough to get Odunze above the mid-range WR3 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 6-of-7 targets for 94 yards in the Bears’ Week 4 win against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Tyson Bagent, making his first NFL start, locked on to his boundary wideout in the first half, hitting Odunze for a couple long gains, including a nicely-placed 37 yarder. Odunze was second on the team in targets behind Colston Loveland, who saw nine looks on the day. Odunze is leading the Bears offense in air yards and profiles as a high-variance weekly fantasy option in an offense that leans toward the run. Odunze will be a solid flex option in Week 5 against a Green Bay secondary that struggles against boundary receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 3-of-6 targets for 44 yards in the Bears’ Week 3 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Odunze continues to function as the deep threat in Ben Johnson’s offense, which spells trouble for his fantasy value in the immediate future considering the absence of Caleb Williams. Case Keenum got the start under center against the Eagles, and while he kept the offense on track through veteran savvy, his general lack of arm strength limited the offense to hefty rates of attacking the short-to-intermediate areas of the field. It is unclear whether Keenum or Tyson Bagent will draw the start in Week 4, but the decision could dictate whether Odunze can be inserted into fantasy rosters against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 3-of-4 targets for 43 yards in the Bears’ Week 2 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It was Odunze’s second quiet statline in as many weeks to begin the season. The difference this time, of course, was the Bears scored only three points after dropping 59 on the Panthers in Week 1. They did attempt 35 passes, 26 of which came from Caleb Williams before he injured his hamstring midway through the fourth quarter. If Williams misses Week 3 against the Eagles as is currently looking likely, it would be difficult to jam Odunze into the WR3 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 2-of-3 targets for 52 yards in the Bears’ Week 1 win against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Odunze came down with an impressive 47-yard contested catch near the end zone in the first half. He was quiet from there on out. Running a route on about 60 percent of the Bears’ drop backs, Odunze may have been limited by the calf injury that kept him out of practice for much of last week. Odunze will continue as a high-variance downfield option in a run-first Chicago offense next week against the Vikings. He should be treated as nothing more than a WR3 option in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze (calf) is active for Week 1 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Odunze missed some practice time this week with the calf issue and was considered questionable headed into the weekend. He could see his snaps and routes limited if the calf is still bothering him. Odunze should be considered a high-variance flex option with a frightening floor against the Panthers. Bears declared QB Tyson Bagent, QB Miller Moss, S Xavier Woods, OT Ozzy Trapilo, DE Jamree Kromah, and OL Jordan McFadden inactive for the team’s season opener.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift rushed 12 times for 31 yards in the Bears’ Week 9 win over the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Swift didn’t catch his lone target in a bust of a contest for the veteran tailback. He had a long gain of just six yards, and was nearly outrun by Salvon Ahmed who finished with 25 yards on the ground. Yes, that Salvon Ahmed. It’s a disappointing — but not terribly surprising — follow-up to the three touchdowns he had Monday night in Week 8, but this is what Swift has done throughout his career. He’ll be a RB2 for Week 11 against the Saints after the Bears’ enjoy their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift rushed 27 times for 69 yards and three touchdowns in the Bears’ Week 8 win over the Seahawks, adding 10 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Swift managers were sweating early as he alternated drives with Roschon Johnson. Those worries were swiftly erased as the veteran lead back played almost the entirety of the second half, scoring all three of his short yardage touchdowns after the break. The three trips to paint marked his second game with three touchdowns through the first eight weeks, now the only player in the league with multiple three-touchdown games. Swift will be a matchup-based RB2 when the Bears host the Buccaneers in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift rushed 22 times for 78 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 7 win over the Patriots, adding 12 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Swift shook off an early injury scare when he took a helmet directly to his knee to earn a season-high 26 opportunities in the absence of Kyle Monangai. This game had an entirely different feel than the previous game played without Monangai, during which Roschon Johnson was much more involved in a game the Bears held a 31-7 lead in the fourth quarter. The back-and-forth nature of Week 7 kept Swift on the field for more of the game, allowing him to return a legitimate RB1 performance on the backs of elite volume. Monangai could return as early as Week 8 considering the Bears now have 10 days until they play the Seahawks on Monday Night Football, potentially sending Swift back into the RB2 range in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: Bears ruled out Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) for Week 7 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Monangai will miss his third game in a row this week. Exactly two weeks ago, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that Monangai’s turf toe injury would be an issue for 1-2 weeks. Technically, his statement remains accurate. This week’s Thursday Night Football game complicates things. If the Bears thought Monangai would miss four games, they likely would have put him on injured reserve, so he should, theoretically, be able to play in Week 8 against the Seahawks. Of course, nothing is guaranteed, and for those wondering, the Bears go on bye in Week 10. D’Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson have been splitting touches with Monangai sidelined. We do not yet know if Johnson will be punished for last week’s fumble though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift had 16 rushes for 44 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons, adding four catches for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Swift again dominated backfield touches for Chicago with Kyle Monangai sidelined with injuries to his toe and hand. Roschon Johnson had 13 carries, with most of those coming after the Bears had raced out to a big lead (before that lead dwindled in the fourth quarter). Both of Swift’s touchdowns came inside the ten yard line. Swift should be locked in for at least 15 touches in Week 7 against the Patriots if Monangai remains sidelined. His involvement in the pass game provides a nice weekly PPR floor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: Bears ruled out Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) for Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Monangai is “trending in the right direction,” but remains week-to-week. D’Andre Swift should handle a sizable workload with Monangai sidelined. Roschon Johnson may be able to catch a few passes, but he makes for a shaky FLEX bet. Monangai should be stashed safely on fantasy football benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift rushed nine times for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers, adding four receptions for 30 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Swift was the only Bear to find the end zone in a throwaway performance where Tyson Bagent was benched for the fourth quarter. It was still a disappointing statline with Kyle Monangai (toe) on the shelf, but there just wasn’t much Swift could do with Bagent failing to threaten the Packers’ defense and the Bears’ D struggling mightily. Swift also lost a ton of passing-game work and targets to fill-in No. 2 RB Roschon Johnson. That’s a potentially disturbing development heading into Week 6 against the Falcons, with or without Monangai in the lineup. Thankfully, Caleb Williams (hamstring) should be back, shoring up Swift’s value in the RB10-14 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift (hip/knee) is not on Chicago’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Despite an early-week DNP, Swift heads into the week in arguably a better position than he started it. We’re not sure how much workload he’ll handle with Kyle Monangai (foot) out, but it will certainly be a large majority of what the Bears do. Roschon Johnson figures to handle whatever Swift can’t, but isn’t a priority free agency pickup so much as a stash at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the “belief is that D’Andre Swift (hip/knee) should be able to go” in Week 5 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: We will get a better sense of Swift’s availability soon when the Bears release their final injury report of the week. After being a DNP in Wednesday’s practice, Swift was able to log a limited session on Thursday, which is a good sign for his availability with one practice left to go. Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), who has yet to practice this week, could be at risk of missing Week 5, which could lead to a busy day for Swift, while Roschon Johnson would serve as the Bears’ RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift (hip/knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: It’s an upgrade from Wednesday’s DNP. Swift has been a constant presence on the midweek injury reports, but hasn’t seemed at any real risk of missing a game yet. We’d imagine he’s more likely than not to avoid a questionable tag again on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenny Gainwell rushed five times for 16 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears, adding three catches for 60 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Most of Gainwell’s yardage came on a 44-yard busted coverage that set up the Bucs’ first score of the game. He found little room in the run game after gashing the Falcons for 140 yards. The 1A/1B talk that head coach Todd Bowles mentioned with Gainwell and Bucky Irving never really came to fruition, as Irving was much more effective with 97 yards on the ground and a pair of scores. Gainwell remains a RB3 going forward, with his next chance to contribute coming in Week 11 against the Lions after their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenny Gainwell (hip) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Gainwell has been a little more involved in recent weeks, and coach Todd Bowles recently told reporters that they are getting closer to the 1A/1B usage that they envisioned when they signed him. Gainwell will again play sidekick to Bucky Irving this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenny Gainwell was a full participant in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Gainwell never seemed in danger of missing Week 9 against the Bears, but the 27-year-old should be just fine for the Week 9 bout against the Bears. He’s coming off a monster 140-yard performance against Atlanta, but keep in mind that Tampa Bay was basically a service academy school for that game with zero completions. He’s closer to FLEX than RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Gainwell played through the hip injury last week to the tune of 25 carries. He starts out the week limited, but fantasy managers should expect to see the 27-year-old to play in Week 9 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said RB Kenneth Gainwell’s usage is getting closer to the “1A, 1B” usage the team envisioned when signing him.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Gainwell saw 25 carries in a run-heavy game against the Falcons in Week 8. Bowles said, “I think we finally got to where we’re utilizing Kenny more and more, and that’s kind of the 1A, 1B we were talking about when we first signed him.” Gainwell saw 50-percent of the snaps for the first time all season last week and now has back-to-back weeks of at least 14 carries. He is still seeing low utilization in the passing game and game script has certainly played a role in his recent role, but it is notable that Bowles mentions the Bucs envisioned a 1A/1B backfield pairing between Bucky Irving and Gainwell. Despite Bowles’ comments, fantasy managers should anticipate Irving operating with the majority of backfield touches, like he did from Weeks 1-6. We will still have to see Gainwell’s usage in a more neutral game script to feel confident about him as a fantasy option moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenneth Gainwell rushed 25 times for 140 yards in the Bucs’ Week 8 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Bucky Irving gave the Bucs a 16-0 lead entering the fourth quarter and passed the baton to Gainwell, who racked up 18 carries in the final frame. Irving only touched the ball once over the final 15 minutes. Gainwell’s late-game dominance got him up to career-highs in carries and yards. He also managed a season-high 14 attempts under similar circumstances last week. Unfortunately for Gainwell, the Bucs aren’t likely to be playing with a big lead in Week 9 against the Bears. Gainwell will return to the RB3/4 border next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) is active for Week 8 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Right tackle Luke Goedeke is also active. Gainwell will continue mixing in behind Bucky Irving this week. He has yet to hit a dozen fantasy points in a game this year and there’s no reason to expect that to change anytime soon. Gainwell is a low-end RB4 for Week 8. Inactive for the Bucs are DL DeMonte Capehart, WR Emeka Egbuka, CB Ayden Garnes, OT Luke Haggard, and OG Billy Schrauth.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Kenneth Gainwell (hip) is “good to go” for Week 8 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Week 7 was Gainwell’s first game with more than seven touches all year. He handled 14 opportunities, all of which were carries, and they came in a 30-point blowout win over the Panthers. Unless the Bucs stay hot and roll over the Falcons, expect Gainwell’s touch total to return to the single digits. He is barely in the RB4 mix for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenny Gainwell (hip) is questionable for Tampa’s Week 8 game against Atlanta.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: His absence would free up more work for Bucky Irving and Sean Tucker. Presumably Gainwell will play after logging a full practice on Friday. Either way, with an injury also nipping at him, he’s an unenviable FLEX option at best against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Gainwell missed Wednesday’s session with the hip issue. He will likely be listed as limited today, but that still puts him on track to play in Week 8 against the Falcons. Gainwell racked up 14 carries in a blowout win over the Panthers last week, but that hasn’t been the norm for him. Gainwell is averaging 6.4 touches per game and has topped out at three receptions in a week. He is buried in the RB4 ranks for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden left Week 9’s game against the Buccaneers with an apparent injury. He finished with 7 catches for 97 yards and a touchdown before exiting.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: Burden fumbled and set up Tampa Bay’s tying score in the fourth quarter after a shot that could have easily been a helmet-to-helmet penalty. The 22-year-old did most of his damage on a 58-yard score that gave Chicago a 14-0 lead. Burden will assuredly undergo concussion testing, but it’s worth noting the Bears don’t play again until Week 11 against the Lions because of a bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden caught 7-of-9 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 8 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: Burden’s opening drive score was the first touchdown surrendered by the Seahawks on an opening possession in the previous 26 games, finishing tied with tight end Colston Loveland for the team lead in targets while catching the only passing score from quarterback Caleb Williams. He continues to operate as the team’s top option through the air in a role that is most malleable, which can either be concentrated on the short areas against zone or extended in the vertical against man. Burden is a WR2 in a pass-funnel matchup against the Buccaneers in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden caught all four targets for 130 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 7 win over the Patriots, adding seven yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: Burden erupted on the scene with a 58-yard, catch-and-run reception on a crosser in the first quarter to set up a four-yard score for D’Andre Swift. He would tack on another 24 yards and his touchdown late in the second quarter to push him over the century mark in yards on an improbable touchdown reception, taking a quick screen to the house on third-and-17 with only 14 seconds remaining before the break. Burden would largely fall victim to a more reserved offensive stance after the Bears pushed their lead to 13 points on their first possession of the second half, adding just one additional reception in the final 30 minutes of play. That matters not to fantasy managers that had been waiting for a marquee performance from a player they chased up draft boards this summer. Burden appears to be heating up now further removed from the offseason injury he carried into the start of the regular season and can continue to be started as an upside WR2 ahead of a difficult matchup against the Seahawks in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden III caught all eight of his targets for 95 yards in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: With Caleb Williams back from a hamstring injury, Burden led the Bears with eight targets and a season-high 95 yards, mostly on short over-the-middle passes from Williams. Burden’s long play was a 25-yard catch and run. That he ran a route on just 19 of the Bears’ 45 drop backs is something of a concern going forward. With that little route involvement, Burden will have to be hyper efficient if he’s going to be a WR2/3 in fantasy formats. He should remain in lineups next week against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden III caught 4-of-6 targets for 47 yards in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: Burden “led” the Bears in receiving, but the fact that 47 yards was the team’s high-water mark tells you all you need to know about their offensive effectiveness this afternoon. Today was actually the first time in three games without Caleb Williams that Burden finished under 60 yards receiving, but he is still in dire need of his starting quarterback’s return. It appears that will be Week 6 against the Falcons, keeping Burden in the low-end WR2 mix despite his lack of spiked weeks through the season’s first five contests.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden III caught 4-of-6 targets for 63 yards in the Bears’ Week 4 win against the Jets, adding one rush for 11 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: It was a fine outing for Burden after he showed signs of life in Week 3’s win over the Eagles. Burden was second on the team in targets, trailing Rome Odunze’s seven looks from Tyson Bagent. He ran a few more pass routes than Kalif Raymond, who had two grabs for six yards. Chicago operating as a run-first team is going to necessarily limit Burden’s opportunities, but he should suffice as a WR3/4 in the coming weeks. That includes next week against a middling Green Bay secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden caught 7-of-11 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 3 win over the Eagles, adding seven yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: Burden got the scoring started with a shovel-pass touchdown on the first possession of the game and continued to be the primary engine of the offense on a night the team was led by veteran journeyman Case Keenum. Head coach Ben Johnson handily outmatched his counterpart in Sean Mannion, keeping the offense in rhythm and unpredictable throughout. Burden should continue to improve upon his early-season returns for fantasy managers that chased him up draft boards this offseason, particularly once Caleb Williams returns to the starting roster in a few weeks. In the meantime, treat Burden as an upside WR2 ahead of a Week 4 meeting with the Jets in Chicago.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden caught 3-of-7 targets for 32 yards in the Bears’ Week 2 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: For the second straight week, Burden was out-produced by Kalif Raymond, who again led the receiver corps in production. D’Andre Swift “led” the entire team in receiving with five receptions for 54 scoreless yards. Burden is now sitting on eight catches for 95 yards through two weeks. It’s not the worst start anyone has ever seen, but fantasy managers were expecting better. It might not be coming in Week 3 if Caleb Williams’ hamstring injury costs him time against the Eagles, which seems highly likely. We are trying not to overreact to small-sample sizes, but Burden is definitely now more of a WR3 than WR2 heading into next Monday’s contest. That, of course, should still have him in most fantasy lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden caught all five of his targets for 63 yards in the Bears’ Week 1 win against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: Burden overcame a first quarter fumble on a bubble screen to finish second on the team in targets behind Kalif Raymond, who saw nine looks from Caleb Williams, just as everyone had predicted. While Burden’s 17 percent targets per route run was well below his 2025 rate, he should be more involved going forward in a Bears offense that might be trying to break the NFL’s single season scoring record, as head coach Ben Johnson mentioned in an August interview. Burden will be a top-30 PPR option next week against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Bears elevated WR Kaden Davis for Week 1 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: This wouldn’t be news under normal circumstances but takes on additional meaning with Rome Odunze listed questionable for Week 1. It is of particular note that the Bears already have five wide receivers on the active roster and still chose to elevate another. While recent reports seemed to indicate a sense of optimism regarding Odunze’s potential availability, he could be on the wrong side of questionable given the recent transaction. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status when the team releases its inactives 90 minutes prior to first kick. Luther Burden and Colston Loveland would be in line to benefit greatly should Odunze be unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield completed 18-of-32 passes for 243 yards with two interceptions in the Buccaneers’ 27-24, Week 9 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Well, it was infinitely better than last week. Mayfield made two long connections; a 44-yarder to Kenny Gainwell to set up a field goal, and a beautiful 58-yard lob to Tez Johnson that was followed by Bucky Irving score. Unfortunately, his only scoring pass went the wrong way as it was a 67-yard pick-six from Jaylon Johnson that made it a two-score game. He did at least run in a two-point conversion that tied the game at 24-24, but the Bears were able to pull out the win on a last-second field goal. Mayfield also looked to be uncomfortable on the sidelines, as the Bears generated pressure throughout the contest. The Bucs get a needed bye next week, and Mayfield will be a QB2 for Week 11 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield completed 0-of-3 passes for zero yards in the Bucs’ 16-0, Week 8 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: You read that correctly. Mayfield did not complete a pass and the Bucs handily defeated Atlanta. Playing in a torrential downpour, Tampa Bay’s defense eviscerated Michael Penix and the Bucs simply took the air out of the ball for four quarters. Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell combined for 310 yards on 52 carries. There was simply no need for Mayfield to handle the football outside of transferring it from the center to a running back. Mayfield did have a long touchdown to Ted Hurst that was knocked out of the rookie’s hand. This is just the second time a team has completed zero passes in the Super Bowl era and the first such game in over 50 years. Needless to say, Mayfield’s numbers will rebound in Week 9 when he takes on the Bears. He will be in the QB2 mix for that contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield was seen without his protective glove during Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield wore the protective glove during last week’s game to avoid further damage to the thumb he injured in Week 3. Mayfield attempted only 11 passes in his return against the Panthers last week, but that was all he needed in a game where the Buccaneers totaled over 250 yards on the ground. Hopefully the shedding of his protective glove is a sign that he’s no longer at risk of re-injury heading into Week 8’s game against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield completed 7-of-11 passes for 64 yards and a touchdown in the Bucs’ 43-13, Week 7 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Making his first start since Week 3 but missing Emeka Egbuka, Mayfield got his first “quarterback win” of the season in a game where he had to attempt only 11 passes. Go figure. The Bucs road paved the Panthers on the ground — 49 carries for 258 yards — and continually took advantage of short fields set up by Panthers turnovers. This, in a game where Mayfield committed zero giveaways. It was the exact kind of day this offense needed, though there aren’t many going-forward takeaways for Mayfield seeing how little he had to throw. Mayfield will presumably be called on for more against the Falcons in Week 8, hopefully with Egbuka back in the fold. Mayfield is just a mid-range QB2 for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) is active for Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: When last we left Mayfield, he was struggling mightily in Weeks 1-3. Predictably, UDFA Jalon Daniels was not any better in his stead. Mayfield returns to an undermanned skill corps, as Emeka Egbuka (foot, concussion) is out for Week 7. Mayfield is a shaky option in the QB16-18 range. Joining Egbuka on the shelf are OT Luke Goedeke, S Antoine Winfield, OG Billy Schrauth, DL DeMonte Capehart and CB Ayden Garnes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles told reporters earlier today that Mayfield “looks like he’s ready to go” for this week’s game. Mayfield seemingly has solid odds of suiting up this week, but we must wait for an official ruling. Hopefully, that arrives tomorrow. If active, Mayfield will play with a protective plate on the back of his glove to help keep his recently dislocated thumb in place. He is a QB2 for the occasion, if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Baker Mayfield (thumb) “looks like he’s ready to go” for Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield was a full participant in practice all week and should be removed from the team’s final injury report when it’s released later in the day. Mayfield is expected to wear a protective glove on his throwing hand, which should prevent injury to the thumb he dislocated in Week 3, and will be on the QB2 radar in what is a must-win game for the 1-5 Buccaneers. Hopefully he can improve on a rough start to the season in which he threw for 615-2-2 in his first three games while completing 63.5 percent of his passes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield said his injured thumb has “gotten to a place where it’s strong enough to play” in Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield has played through injuries regularly over the years. We expect him to be out there for the Buccaneers’ Week 7 game against the division rival Panthers. He is a QB2 for his first game back. A run-heavy game plan could be in the works as they ease him in. If his thumb really is good to go, though, this game could turn into a shootout. He practiced in full for the second time this week on Thursday, and told reporters that he will play with a protective plate on the back of his glove to help prevent re-injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) practiced in full on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield going down as a full participant is a bit of a surprise given that it’s his first time practicing in any capacity since Week 3. Todd Bowles told reporters earlier this week that the team was preparing for Jalon Daniels to start. Now it looks like Mayfield may be the favorite to draw the start versus Carolina. This is ultimately a rather ambiguous situation, likely by Bowles’ design. Fantasy managers should have a backup plan in place if they are counting on either of the Bucs’ quarterbacks this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield hasn’t played since dislocating his thumb in Week 3. As of late last week, he hadn’t even thrown a football since suffering the injury. Todd Bowles told reporters on Monday that he’s preparing for Jalon Daniels to start, but Mayfield’s return to practice puts things up in the air. His practice statuses over the next few days will be telling. For now, fantasy managers should still plan on seeing Daniels under center, but this is a situation to monitor throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams completed 22-of-37 passes for 279 yards with two touchdowns and four interceptions in the Bears’ 27-24, Week 9 win over the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: An absolutely bizarre football game. Williams was brilliant on the first two drives with two touchdowns. After that, things got weird at best and disastrous at worst. He threw interceptions on back-to-back throws in the second quarter, and threw two more picks for his first career four-INT game. Kudos to the Bucs for generating the pressure necessary to create those picks — this is back-to-back four interception games for the Tampa Bay defense — but three of the four interceptions were egregious throws. He was able to get the job done at the end of the night, hitting Colson Loveland on a blown coverage for a 38-yard gain that set up the game-winning field goal. He’ll get a week to review the tape on bye before taking on the Saints in Week 11

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams completed 24-of-34 passes for 247 yards and one touchdown in the Bears’ 34-17, Week 8 win over the Seahawks, adding one yard on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams marched the Bears down the field for a 17-play opening possession touchdown, snapping a 26-game streak in which the Seahawks kept opponents out of the end zone on first possessions in the process. The two teams traded defensive stops for much of the remainder of the first half before the Bears opened the flood gates after the break, vaulting to a 6-2 record and now just half a game behind the Vikings for the lead in the NFC North. Williams’ ball placement was impeccable in this one, the most notable of which came just after the half on three absolute dimes to Rome Odunze for chunk gains. Two surging teams meet in Week 9 when the Bears host the pass-funnel Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football, where Williams will remain a back end QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams completed 22-of-33 passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears’ 30-24, Week 7 win over the Patriots, adding 18 yards on five carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The enigmatic signal caller also took three sacks, the last of which almost placed the Bears in position to hand the keys to victory to the Patriots. Ben Johnson called a pass play on third-and-five with under two minutes to play in Patriots territory, placing another nod of support toward his franchise quarterback. Things turned dire when Williams took a sack that appeared to take the Bears out of field goal range in a six-point game, with veteran kicker Cairo Santos hitting a career-long 58-yard field goal to dispel the worries. That sequence of two plays displayed Johnson’s unrelenting trust in his players considering the 58-yard field goal was not only the longest of Santos’ 12-year career, but the third longest field goal in Soldier Field history. Either way, Williams and the Bears escaped with the victory and move to 5-2, now 1.5-games behind the Vikings for the division lead in the most competitive division in football. The Bears get a mini-bye ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Seahawks on Monday Night Football, where Williams will remain a back-end QB1 in fantasy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams completed 30-of-36 attempts for 305 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons, adding four rushes for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams was all the way back in this one, returning to action after three weeks on the sideline recovering from a hamstring injury. His only real miss of the day came on a ten yard throw to Colston Loveland that should have been an easy touchdown. Williams tormented the pass-funnel Atlanta defense with middle-of-the-field throws, along with typical out-of-structure passes to the sideline. It was an impressive outing against a Falcons defense giving up the league’s fifth lowest drop back success rate. Williams should remain in lineups in Week 7 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is active for Week 6 against the Falcons.
