https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams will make his return to the starting lineup after being sidelined for a few weeks with a hamstring injury while the Bears declared RB Kyle Monangai, CB Tyrique Stevenson, LB T.J. Edwards, LB Keyshaun Elliott, OL Jordan McFadden, DL Jayden Loving, and QB Case Keenum inactive against Atlanta. Monongai’s absence should translate into another big workload for D’Andre Swift, facing a tough Falcons rush defense. Meanwhile, Tyson Bagent will serve as Williams’ backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) will start in Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This was expected to be the case but is now confirmed by sources close to the team. Williams returns after missing the previous three games as the Bears look to claw their way back into contention in a crowded NFC North division. Consider it a sizable boost for all Chicago pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) posted a video to social media indicating he will play in Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Normally, social media posts don’t count for much. However, earlier today, Bears coach Ben Johnson said that the Bears should have more clarity on Williams’ status by the end of the day, after the medical team put Williams through “the final stress tests” in his return-to-play program. We are inferring that Williams’ social media post suggests he passed the final medical testing, though we have not officially received word that this is indeed the case. For now, we tentatively expect Williams to play on Sunday. He can be treated as a mid-to-low QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Bears are smartly taking a conservative approach with their franchise quarterback. Williams had a limited practice session last week and practiced fully this week. Bears coach Ben Johnson told reporters that the team should have more clarity by the end of the day on whether Williams has passed his return-to-play plan’s final stress tests. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Bears’ QB1 is seemingly on track to make his return this week, when his team takes on the Falcons. When speaking to reporters after practice, though, Williams said he does not know if he is going to play yet, adding that he still has a number of tests and protocols to go through before he’s cleared. If active, Williams could end up running a little less frequently than he did early in the year, perhaps playing cautiously in his first game back. Regardless, Williams is a low-end QB1 if he is indeed active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) practiced in full Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Technically, Williams was estimated as a full participant ahead of the Bears’ Week 6 game against the Falcons. We’ll see if Williams, who has missed the past three games, practices in full on Thursday. Either way he’s likely to be under center against the pass-funnel Atlanta defense in Week 6. He should be in all lineups if he’s active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Audric Estime rushed 15 times for 72 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Estime was waived by the Browns on Monday. The Saints claimed him on Tuesday and he was their starting back by Sunday. Life comes at you fast. Kellen Moore made it a point to get Estime going early with three carries for him on their first three plays of the game. He gashed the Browns 32 yards on those three attempts alone. He would later punch in a goal line touchdown to give the Saints the lead in the fourth quarter. Estime will be the Saints’ lead runner until Travis Etienne is activated from injured reserve. That could happen as soon as Week 10, so fantasy managers shouldn’t count on another usable week from Estime anytime soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Audric Estime rushed nine times for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Browns’ Week 6 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It wasn’t an overly impressive day for Estime, who was on the Vikings’ practice squad earlier in the week. But in the fourth quarter, with the Browns trailing 10-3, Estime took back-to-back carries for six yards, with his second resulting in a two-yard touchdown that would tie the game with just over eight minutes left in regulation. Estime could see a similar role in next week’s game against the Titans if Quinshon Judkins (ankle) misses another game, but he’ll be hard to trust as far as fantasy is concerned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Browns signed RB Audric Estime from the Vikings’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Estime’s signing comes as Quinshon Judkins is dealing with an ankle injury he suffered in Week 5. Estime, who is only 23 years old, already feels like an NFL journeyman as he now heads to his fifth team in three seasons after brief stints with the Broncos, Eagles, Saints, and Vikings. The former fifth-round pick has rushed for 508 yards and three touchdowns in his career and rushed for 76-310-2 as a rookie with the Broncos. Estime could see snaps in Week 6 against the Ravens if Judkins is unable to play, but we wouldn’t expect to see anything close to a meaningful workload at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints placed Kelvin Banks (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The team signed long snapper Cal Adomitis and reached an injury settlement with running back Audric Estime in corresponding moves. Banks is undergoing surgery for a severe high-ankle sprain. He could return later this year, but the team will be without their starting left tackle for at least four games, and likely much longer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Alvin Kamara (knee) is questionable to play in Week 1 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kamara logged two limited sessions to begin the week, and New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill said he thinks Kamara will play, barring a setback. We do not yet know Kamara’s practice participation level on Friday, but he is traveling with the team, which is a good sign. Kamara would be a PPR FLEX if active. He is expected to play on passing downs while starting RB Travis Etienne leads the team in carries. Etienne is the best bet to handle the primary red zone role, but Kamara has been a prolific touchdown scorer over his career and could factor in. The Saints ruled out RB Audric Estime (thigh).

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Kendre Miller (back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Saints’ backup running back statuses continue to change. Veteran No. 2 RB Alvin Kamara (knee) is expected to be sidelined for at least one month, and RB Audric Estime is now sidelined with an undisclosed injury. Miller and RB Devin Neal (hamstring) both returned this week, though. Beat reporter Jeff Nowak notes that Miller, Neal and RB Ty Chandler were all allowed to rotate in for first-team reps today, as coach Kellen Moore presumably seeks out a viable primary backup for starting RB Travis Etienne. Per Nowak, Miller “looks sharp despite the time missed.” This is worth tracking for short-term bench stash purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Kendre Miller (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The good news is that Miller was not listed with a knee injury after suffering a season-ending ACL tear in Week 7 last year. The bad news is that he evidently has a new injury, and the Saints have a fairly deep running back room right now. RBs Devin Neal, Audric Estime, Ty Chandler and CJ Donaldson are all vying for roster spots. Per Underhill, Neal is taking advantage of the extra reps. He could have the inside track to the RB3 role right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Audric Estime rushed 21 times for 63 yards in the Saints’ Week 18 loss to the Falcons, adding five receptions for 43 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Playing out the string for the Saints’ injury-ruined backfield, Estime reached 100 yards from scrimmage for the first time in his career after posting 98 the week before. Not a bad end to the year for a player who spent the first half of the season on practice squads. Still only 22 years old, Estime is buying himself time to get established in the NFL, but he still probably mostly profiles as a special teamer if he’s going to make a 53-man roster out of camp. Considering the Saints’ issues at running back, it could very well be in New Orleans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Alvin Kamara (knee/ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The team opted not to place Kamara on injured reserve, though he has been sidelined since Week 12. Unless something drastic occurs, Saints RB Audric Estime will start in Kamara’s stead against the Falcons on Sunday. Both teams have been eliminated from the playoffs, but it still gives coaches a chance to evaluate key players one last time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Alvin Kamara (knee/ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kamara has neither practiced nor played since spraining his MCL in Week 12. He was already dealing with an ankle injury at that time. We expect him to remain sidelined in Week 18 against the Falcons. Saints RB Audric Estime will again operate as the team’s starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Brandin Cooks caught both of his targets for 25 yards in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders. Cooks ran about 30 percent of the team’s routes and was fourth in targets among Niners pass catchers. With Jordan Watkins and Demarcus Robinson in the fold, Cooks should remain on waiver wires ahead of Week 10.
Brandin Cooks caught 1-of-3 passes for 13 yards in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Cooks was out-targeted and outplayed by both Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing. Cooks did run the most routes of any receiver on the team, but he didn’t command targets or look like a key piece of the receiving game. With Mike Evans likely back in Week 9, it’s hard to hold onto Cooks through the Week 8 bye in fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: 49ers declared DE Nick Bosa, WR Mike Evans, WR Deebo Samuel, LB Luke Gifford, LB Garret Wallow, S Marques Sigle, and QB Kurtis Rourke inactive for Week 7 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: None of these comes as a surprise. All of Bosa, Evans, and Samuel were already ruled out earlier in the week, and Sigle has missed multiple weeks with an ankle injury. Brandin Cooks and Christian Kirk are likely to lead the 49ers’ pass catchers against the Falcons this week, and both are worth adding in deeper formats in case either emerges as a legit weapon while Evans (Achilles) and Samuel (hamstring) are sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Jordan Watkins caught his only target for 22 yards in the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Watkins drew the start in place of the injured Deebo Samuel but was unable to take advantage of the opportunity, with 23 of Brock Purdy’s 29 targets going to the team’s top three options in Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, and George Kittle. Evans departed at the end of the second quarter with an aggravation of his Achilles injury, something that appears likely to cost the veteran a Week 7 game against the Falcons. That could leave Watkins in line for a second consecutive start, although the upside remains modest. Fantasy managers are likely best leaving both Watkins and veteran Brandin Cooks on the waiver wire, the latter of whom caught 1-of-2 targets for 13 yards against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows believes Brandin Cooks is the “next man up” in the 49ers receivers room.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: With Deebo Samuel sustaining a serious hamstring injury in Week 5 against Seattle, Cooks stepped in and functioned as San Francisco’s No. 2 receiver behind Mike Evans. Cooks was targeted on 17 percent of his pass routes against the Seahawks and caught a touchdown on his only reception. Though Jacob Cowing could mix in with Samuel sidelined, Cooks should be in line for a few targets a game. The well-traveled veteran can be picked up in deeper fantasy formats this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: 49ers signed WR Brandin Cooks, formerly of the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Cooks is signing with the 49ers’ practice squad initially “to get up to speed for games.” Cooks, 32, posted a 24/279/0 receiving line in the regular season last year, before chipping in five catches for 78 yards in two playoff games. He is perhaps unlikely to be fantasy-relevant right away, but there is a real chance he could work his way into the 49ers’ wide receiver rotation, given their influx of injuries at the position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Free agent WR Brandin Cooks worked out for the Ravens on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: This is probably a bad sign regarding WR Zay Flowers’ (hamstring) Week 2 availability, though the Ravens also placed rookie WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) on short-term injured reserve this week. A signing seems likely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Bills GM Brandon Beane said he’s had conversations with Brandin Cooks and his agent.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Cooks is probably a fallback plan for the Bills if they don’t draft someone. Even if he’s signed, the pecking order in targets in Buffalo has radically changed with DJ Moore in town and fantasy managers shouldn’t be expecting more than a WR5 role for Cooks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Brandin Cooks caught 2-of-6 targets for 20 yards in the Bills’ Divisional Round loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Cooks made two spectacular almost catches. On one of them, he caught the ball while twisting on the sideline, and his knee came down in bounds, but his wrist landed a fraction of a second earlier and landed out of bounds. The other play was far more controversial. It seemed like Cooks had hauled in a 44-yard pass to set the Bills up for a game-winning field goal in overtime, but the ball was stripped away by a Broncos defender. The Bills believed Cooks was down by contact before the ball was stripped loose, but the call was not reviewed, and the Broncos would then drive for a game-winning field goal of their own. The 32-year-old came on down the stretch for the Bills, showing that he still has enough deep speed to make big plays. He finished the season with 24 catches on 36 targets for 279 yards and no touchdowns in 15 games with the Bills and Saints. Some team will sign him in free agency and give him a role as a deep threat.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Brandin Cooks caught 3-of-5 targets for 58 yards in the Bills’ Wild Card Round win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Cooks came down with a 36-yard bomb from Josh Allen late in the fourth quarter that eventually set up a go-ahead score. He finished the day second on the team in catches, targets, and yards. With Josh Palmer on IR, there was already plenty of volume up for grabs in the receiver room. The Bills then lost Gabe Davis to a knee injury late in this game. His status for the Divisional Round is up in the air. Cooks will likely operate as the team’s No. 2 receiver next week, putting him squarely on the DFS radar as a salary relief option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-szmy.headline: Andre Szmyt converted 3-of-3 field goal attempts in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-szmy.analysis: Szmyt nailed his third attempt, a 51-yarder to send the game into overtime. He has attempted at least three field goals in three of his past four games. Both of his misses, however, have come in the past month. Cleveland’s hit-or-miss offense makes Szmyt a risky fantasy option, but he’s hanging around the top-12 halfway through the 2026 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-szmy.headline: Browns tendered exclusive rights free agent K Andre Szmyt.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-szmy.analysis: Cleveland also tendered LB Winston Reid and LS Rex Sunahara. Szmyt went 24-of-27 on his field goal attempts in 2026. He missed one of his 26 PATs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-szmy.headline: Browns K Andre Szmyt (calf) is questionable for Week 3’s game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-szmy.analysis: He popped up on the injury report for the first time this week and will undergo an MRI per head coach Kevin Stefanski. It’s possible the Browns replace Szmyt ahead of kickoff if the injury is serious. Please do not start either Browns kicker against the Packers defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-szmy.headline: Browns released K Dustin Hopkins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-szmy.analysis: Hopkins was vying for the kicking job with Andre Szmyt, and it appears Szmyt has won that battle. Hopkins could get a tryout with another club, but it’s also possible he’s kicked his last field goal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-szmy.headline: Browns released EDGE Ogbo Okoronkwo.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-szmy.analysis: The team signed K Andre Szmyt in a corresponding move. Okoronkwo was reportedly available via trade ahead of the draft but nothing came of it. He played a pass-rush specialist role in Cleveland last year and tallied three sacks. He should be able to find a similar gig before training camp, but a starting role is likely out of the picture.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-szmy.headline: Browns signed K Andre Szmyt.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-szmy.analysis: With Dustin Hopkins struggling mightily, the Browns could turn to Szmyt as early as Week 17 against the Dophins. Hopkins, who missed an extra point last week in a loss to the Bengals, has made just 16 of his 25 field goal attempts in 2024. Szmyt would not be a fantasy option in Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-szmy.headline: Free agent K Matt Ammendola worked out for the Lions on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-szmy.analysis: Per ESPN’s Field Yates, the Lions also worked out Lucas Havrisik, Matthew McCrane and Andre Szmyt following Michael Badgley’s season-ending injury. Ammendola (67.0 percent) and Havrisik (75.0 percent) are coming off shaky field-goal conversion rates in 2023. McCrane (80.0 percent) and Szmyt (87.0 percent) fared better in their recent UFL stints, though none of the four inspire confidence. The Lions’ fantasy-friendly kicker role may underwhelm in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-szmy.headline: Syracuse redshirt freshman K Andre Szmyt won the Lou Groza Award.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andre-szmy.analysis: Szmyt is a former walk-on, and was a big reason why the Orange were able to win nine games this year. He went 28-for-32 on his kicks this year -- 57-for-57 on his PATs -- and he was 3-for-3 from 50-plus yards out. LSU’s Cole Tracy and Wyoming’s Cooper Rothe were the other finalists for the award.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey had 18 rushes for 68 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders, adding two catches for 19 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey didn’t have much trouble against a Vegas run defense that has been one of the league’s worst over the past month. His rushing score was his ninth of the season, while his receiving score was his first of 2026. CMC logged 28 routes on the day while Kaelon Black had just five routes and did not see a target from Brock Purdy. McCaffrey, with at least 15 carries in five games this year, has a spectacular Week 10 matchup against a miserable Dallas defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Kaelon Black had 11 rushes for 70 yards in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Christian McCaffrey, meanwhile, had 18 rushes on the day and scored two touchdowns. Black had just five pass routes against the Raiders while CMC ran 28 routes. Black’s 70 rushing yards marks a season high and shows he can be a fantasy factor when the Niners have game script in their favor. It didn’t help that he faced an abysmal Raiders front seven. Black should have some flex viability in deeper leagues next week against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) will have a “full workload” in Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey went down with the hamstring injury in Week 7, but then got a well-timed bye week to recover. He was a full participant in Friday’s practice before being removed from the injury report entirely. Per usual, he will be near the top of the RB1 ranks for his date with the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey injured his hamstring in Week 7. The 49ers were on bye in Week 8, giving him extra time to rest. McCaffrey then sat out on Wednesday before practicing in a limited capacity on Thursday. He should be in fantasy football lineups this week, facing a soft Raiders run defense, but Kaelon Black could mix in for 8-10 touches, potentially warranting FLEX consideration.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) was able to participate in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: A rare bit of good news on the injury front for the 49ers. McCaffrey was given the day off Wednesday. Even though today’s activity only resulted in a limited session, it’s a good start for what could be a Week 9 date against the Raiders that sees the tailback get a smorgasbord of touches due to the issues involving several injured receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said more than a week ago that McCaffrey has a “mild” hamstring strain. Hamstring strains can be finicky. If Kaelon Black is available, add him immediately. McCaffrey still has a chance to play in Week 9 against the Raiders’ soft run defense, but he is ever so slightly in the questionable column at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Kyle Shanahan said Christian McCaffrey has a “mild” hamstring strain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: That explains McCaffrey’s brief departure in the team’s Week 7 loss to the Falcons, when the veteran alpha missed most of the second quarter but returned for the second half. 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan added that he believes McCaffrey will be fine when the team comes out of their Week 8 bye. “We’re pretty optimistic,” he said Monday. Fantasy managers appear to have dodged a bullet with the first-round fantasy powerhouse but will want to continue to monitor reports from the team through their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey rushed seven times for 39 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons, adding 61 receiving yards on six catches.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey scored a touchdown on the first drive of the game and had six touches, which seemed to set the tone for a massive workload. However, he also picked up a thigh injury on that drive and didn’t return again until the third quarter. The 49ers seemed to give him a few extra breaks in the second half, but McCaffrey didn’t look any less explosive. He was also half a yard away from catching a touchdown pass in the fourth quarter, but he was ruled down short of the end zone, and then Brock Purdy threw a touchdown pass to Kyle Juszczyk on the next play. The 49ers have a bye next week, so we doubt McCaffrey’s thigh injury will be an issue when we see them next in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey (thigh) returned to the game in Week 7 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey was injured on the first drive of the game when the 49ers scored a touchdown. The training staff was working on his thigh before he jogged into the locker room in the second quarter and was listed as questionable to return. It was a 14-3 49ers lead when McCaffrey went into the locker room, and it’s 19-14 in favor of the Falcons now, so the team is going to see if their star running back can get them back in front.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey is questionable to return to Week 7 against the Falcons with a thigh injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey was used heavily on the first drive with the 49ers down so many offensive players, and he came out of that drive with a touchdown but also a thigh injury. The trainers worked on him on the sideline for two drives before finally bringing him into the medical tent. The 49ers do have a bye next week, so they could try to get him back into the game, but they are also up 14-3 at this point, so the Falcons will likely need to get the game closer. Kaelon Black will continue to see a workhorse role while CMC is sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 21-of-35 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ 23-22, Week 9 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough got off to a dreadfully slow start, throwing for a measly 156 scoreless yards over the first three quarters. The Browns weren’t pushing the Saints to play fast or pass often, resulting in a noticeable lack of volume for Shough. A 64-yard touchdown for the Browns in the middle of the fourth quarter finally forced the Saints to pick up the pace. Shough responded with a 55-yard touchdown drive two series later, though Audric Estime found the end zone on the ground. Shough eventually closed out the game with a 15-yard touchdown strike to Juwan Johnson in overtime. Shough’s fantasy output is tied directly to his passing volume. He’ll remain at the top of the QB2 ranks as long as his defense keeps giving up points, which should happen versus the Panthers in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 30-of-38 passes for 273 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the Saints’ 16-10, Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough’s seven rushing yards led the team, which isn’t ideal. The 27-year-old was mostly accurate and on-time with his throws, but he should have had three turnovers in the first half — one dropped interception, one strip-sack that was overturned and one fumble that luckily went out of bounds — in addition to the one costly red-zone interception that actually made the stat sheet. It wasn’t Shough at his best, but there were some flashes of brilliance in the loss. Shough will get a bye week before he faces the Browns in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 16-of-30 passes for 144 yards and three touchdowns in the Saints’ 34-27, Week 6 win over the Giants, adding five carries for 32 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Saints had their usual slow start on offense, going scoreless in the first quarter. Shough then did what he does best and led an effective offensive effort the rest of the way. He is dealing with broken bones in his non-throwing hand and it arguably impacted some of his throws, missing open receivers and struggling to push the ball downfield. Though he averaged 4.8 yards per attempt, he totaled three touchdowns on the day. Shough was also impactful as a runner, totaling 32 yards and a tush push touchdown on the day while also getting tackled inside the five-yard line on another rush. Two straight games have been impacted by Shough’s hand injury but the post-first quarter volume continues to elevate his fantasy floor. Shough is a high-end QB2 for Week 7 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Tyler Shough has two broken bones in his non-throwing hand.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Both Shough and Kellen Moore have given non-answers when asked about the quarterback’s left hand. Per Schefter, the injury could take a couple of months to heal, but it will not cost him any playing time. Shough injured his hand versus the Falcons in Week 4 and wore a protective glove in Week 5. He is coming off his two worst games of the year, though we don’t suspect the hand is to blame. Things get much easier this week with the Giants on tap. Shough will get another shot at a QB1 finish in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore, asked directly if Tyler Shough’s non-throwing hand is broken, said “it got banged two weeks ago and he’s just wearing some protective layers there.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: So, probably, then. The hand hasn’t really been a contributing factor to New Orleans’ decline so much as the Saints offensive line has just been in the blender for two weeks against Atlanta and Minnesota’s fronts, but it sure looks like Shough is managing through something and we should probably break ties against him in the rankings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 16-of-25 passes for 96 yards and two interceptions in the Saints’ 23-13, Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough had been coasting on extreme play volume over the first month of the fantasy season. Brian Flores and the Vikings’ hyper-aggressive defense had no issues shutting down that approach. The Saints had five drives in the first half. Only one lasted longer than three plays. Of their four second-half drives, two ended with interceptions. A fumbled kickoff coming out of the break didn’t help the team’s play volume either. Shough has ultimately been a better fantasy quarterback than a real-life passer this year and the Vikings’ defense exposed that truth for the better part of four quarters. He will look to rebound against a far worse Giants unit in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough (hand) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As expected, he’ll start and be on the QB1/QB2 borderline against an extremely pesky and attacking Vikings defense that has held down quarterback scoring quite well so far this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough (hand) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As a right-handed quarterback, Shough should be fine despite his surprise appearance on the injury report. Even in a blowout loss on Monday, the second-year passer racked up 286 yards and a touchdown on 48 attempts. As long as the volume is there, Shough is good for low-end QB1 numbers. He will remain inside the top 12 at his position for Week 5 against Minnesota.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 30-of-48 passes for 286 yards and one touchdown in the Saints’ 45-24, Week 4 loss to the Falcons, adding five yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough and the Saints stayed true to recent form as they quickly fell into a 14-point hole in the first quarter, with the team now averaging an almost eight point deficit at the half since head coach Kellen Moore took over to start the 2025 season. The team was unable to reproduce the second half magic they so frequently muster behind an overmatched offensive line. Shough needed a late touchdown toss to Devaughn Vele with less than two minutes to play to give fantasy managers something of value. Moore and Shough have their work cut out for them with Brian Flores’ relentless defense coming to town in Week 5, where Shough will be on the QB1/2 border in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 29-of-42 passes for 255 yards, four touchdowns and one interception in the Saints’ 27-35, Week 3 loss to the Raiders, adding one rush for 36 yards and two lost fumbles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough funneled four touchdown passes to Saints TEs Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant, bringing the game’s total to six tight end touchdowns, which tied a league record. The Saints’ quarterback played well overall, though his interception was due to a poor throw. Both fumbles were caused by Raiders pass rushers, and Shough had a third fumble reversed by an illegal contact penalty on the Raiders. Regardless, he can be trusted to throw the ball voluminously while adding a little extra with his legs. He warrants low-end QB1 treatment against the Falcons next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.headline: Demarcus Robinson caught 3-of-4 targets for 22 yards in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.analysis: Robinson was back from his ankle injury, though the CBS broadcast mentioned Robinson was only about 50 percent back from the ankle issue. He logged a pass route on 21 of the team’s 36 drop backs and was tied for second in targets. Jordan Watkins — who had a 37-yard score against Vegas — appears to be the Niners’ No. 1 wideout for now (with Mike Evans sidelined). Robinson can be rostered in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.headline: 49ers activated WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.analysis: The veteran receiver returns to a decimated receiving corps, potentially in line to serve as the top receiver against the Raiders in Week 9. Fantasy managers in a bind could do much worse than taking a swing on Robinson considering the elite matchup and lack of viable depth, for a 49ers team with one of the week’s highest Vegas implied team totals on the board.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.headline: Demarcus Robinson (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.analysis: If Robinson can make his return from injured reserve with Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Christian Kirk (knee) sidelined, Robinson could end up returning WR3 value against the Raiders this week. Wide receiver-needy fantasy managers should add him now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.headline: Demarcus Robinson (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.analysis: Robinson may still need more time before taking the field on game day, but his continued practice participation, albeit limited, is a good sign overall. Given the state of the 49ers’ wide receiver corps, if active, Robinson could handle a decent workload.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.headline: 49ers opened Demarcus Robinson’s (ankle) 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.analysis: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Robinson will be limited at today’s practice. This gives him a chance to play in Week 9 against the Raiders. Wide receiver-needy fantasy managers can consider adding him, though his place in the target pecking order is uncertain with Mike Evans (Achilles) recovering.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Demarcus Robinson (ankle) has an “outside chance” to return in Week 7 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.analysis: The 49ers go on bye in Week 8. Shanahan says that Robinson is more likely to return after that, in time to face the Raiders in Week 9. Robinson can be stashed in injured reserve spots, if need be, but he is not a must-stash type of player. Depending on how the 49ers’ wide receiver corps looks, Robinson can likely be snagged off waivers during the bye week for those in need at the wide receiver position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said they’re going to hold off on placing Deebo Samuel (hamstring) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.analysis: The 49ers have a Week 8 bye and thus Samuel would stay on injured reserve an extra week. Reading between the lines, it sounds like Samuel has a chance to play in Week 9 if things go well. Shanahan added that Demarcus Robinson (ankle) could return for Week 9 as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.headline: 49ers placed WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.analysis: The high-ankle injury will now cost the veteran receiver a minimum of four games, thinning an already reeling group of pass-catchers in San Francisco. Jacob Cowing is technically the next man up, although the offense appears more likely to concentrate on the remaining veterans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.headline: 49ers ruled out WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) for Week 3 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.analysis: This was the expected outcome for Week 3. Reports on Robinson’s injury indicate this could be a multi-week issue. With WR1 Mike Evans (hip) questionable, WR Deebo Samuel and TE George Kittle could take on sizable workloads, though the team will likely still try to limit Kittle’s snap count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.headline: 49ers WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.analysis: Robinson suffered an ankle injury in the 49ers’ Week 2 win over the Dolphins. The initial diagnosis was that the veteran would miss some time and his DNP designation Wednesday indicates just that. With Mike Evans (hip) also not practicing, the 49ers’ receiving corps is getting thinner than it already was.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: Kaelon Black had 11 rushes for 70 yards in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: Christian McCaffrey, meanwhile, had 18 rushes on the day and scored two touchdowns. Black had just five pass routes against the Raiders while CMC ran 28 routes. Black’s 70 rushing yards marks a season high and shows he can be a fantasy factor when the Niners have game script in their favor. It didn’t help that he faced an abysmal Raiders front seven. Black should have some flex viability in deeper leagues next week against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: McCaffrey injured his hamstring in Week 7. The 49ers were on bye in Week 8, giving him extra time to rest. McCaffrey then sat out on Wednesday before practicing in a limited capacity on Thursday. He should be in fantasy football lineups this week, facing a soft Raiders run defense, but Kaelon Black could mix in for 8-10 touches, potentially warranting FLEX consideration.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said more than a week ago that McCaffrey has a “mild” hamstring strain. Hamstring strains can be finicky. If Kaelon Black is available, add him immediately. McCaffrey still has a chance to play in Week 9 against the Raiders’ soft run defense, but he is ever so slightly in the questionable column at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: Kaelon Black rushed 12 times for 63 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: Black’s day did not start great as he was stuffed on three straight plays inside the three-yard line on the first drive. Then he watched as Christian McCaffrey scored a touchdown on fourth down. However, McCaffrey also picked up a thigh injury on that drive and missed the remainder of the first half, which allowed Black the opportunity to rip off some nice chunk runs and a long touchdown. McCaffrey did return in the second half, and Black also lost a fumble in the second quarter, so there were some moments of inconsistency. That being said, Black looks like one of the best bench stash running backs in fantasy football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: Christian McCaffrey is questionable to return to Week 7 against the Falcons with a thigh injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: McCaffrey was used heavily on the first drive with the 49ers down so many offensive players, and he came out of that drive with a touchdown but also a thigh injury. The trainers worked on him on the sideline for two drives before finally bringing him into the medical tent. The 49ers do have a bye next week, so they could try to get him back into the game, but they are also up 14-3 at this point, so the Falcons will likely need to get the game closer. Kaelon Black will continue to see a workhorse role while CMC is sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: 49ers RB Kaelon Black (illness) is not on the final injury report for Week 5 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: Black was limited on Wednesday, but upgraded to full participation on Thursday and Friday. There are no concerns about his ability to handle backup duties against the Seahawks this week. That said, he has just 10 carries over the last two weeks and cannot be started in 12-team FLEX spots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: Kaelon Black (illness) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: This should be a non-issue for Black by the time Sunday comes around. Black cut into Christian McCaffrey’s role again last week with six carries, though he only turned that into 13 yards. He doesn’t have much standalone fantasy value but remains one of the better contingency options headed into Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: Kaelon Black had six rushes for 13 yards in the 49ers’ Week 4 win against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: After seeing 14 carries in Week 1 against the Rams, Black now has 17 rushing attempts over his past three games as the Niners’ No. 2 back behind Christian McCaffrey. Black should be rostered in most leagues as one of the best contingency options in the game. As long as CMC is healthy, Black should remain on benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: Kaelon Black rushed four times for 17 yards in the 49ers’ Week 3 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: Black has seen his role decrease with Christian McCaffrey returning to bell cow usage. The rookie saw four carries and one target, totaling eight offensive snaps. He saw a red zone touch but otherwise did not get close to scoring opportunities. Black is one of the most valuable handcuffs in fantasy football moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.headline: Kaelon Black rushed seven times for 25 yards in a Week 2 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaelon-bla.analysis: After splitting work fairly evenly with Christian McCaffrey in Week 1, Black took a clearer backup role here. He had some snaps on the first drive of the game, but then Black mixed in sporadically until the game was decided early in the fourth quarter. At the end of the day, the rookie played on 16 of the team’s 45 snaps and is unlikely to have any standalone value; yet, he remains one of the better bench stashes in fantasy football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer was second on the team in pass routes behind Brock Bowers. He nearly had not one, but two touchdown catches on the day. Mayer had the ball knocked out of his hand as he reached for the goal line in the first half, and was called for pass interference on a short touchdown reception in the fourth quarter. It was a tough luck day for the Raiders’ TE2. With 15 receptions over the past three games coming into Week 9, Mayer is usable in deeper formats going forward. He gets the Seahawks in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 5-of-6 targets for 53 yards in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: This was Mayer’s fourth five-catch outing of the season. Only Brock Bowers caught more passes this afternoon. It could have been a bigger day in fantasy, but Mayer’s unconverted look was an inaccurate goal-line pass he short-armed. Mayer has a reasonable enough PPR TE2 floor, but his spiked week potential remains limited enough that he is not a very exciting streamer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught all three of his targets for 32 yards in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer benefited from a pass-heavy second half for the Raiders as they once again faced a big deficit. He ran a pass route on 38 of the Raiders’ 49 drop backs. With four games of at least five targets, Mayer profiles as a desperation play in tight end premium games and a 12-team option if Brock Bowers misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 7-of-9 targets for 95 yards in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: This is the second time in three weeks that Mayer has popped up for a big performance. With Brock Bowers blanketed for much of the first half, Mayer stepped up to catch five passes for 52 yards in the first half, and he ripped off an impressive 28-yard reception in the second half on a drive that ended with a Matt Gay field goal. Playing behind Bowers continues to make Mayer a risky fantasy bet, but he’s averaging 6.7 targets in his last three games, which is buoyed by this week’s nine-target game and a 10-target outing in Week 4 against the Chiefs. With a few reliable tight ends on bye in Week 7, Mayer could have some viability as a dart throw next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught his lone target for two yards in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer and the rest of the Vegas pass catchers took a backseat to Brock Bowers, who had a team-leading ten targets for 110 yards and a touchdown before the Raiders pulled their starters in the fourth quarter of this blowout loss. Mayer was fresh off an 82-yard outing (on ten targets) against Kansas City. He should remain on waivers ahead of Week 6’s game against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 8-of-10 targets for 82 yards in the Raiders’ Week 4 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer’s 10 targets were just one fewer than what Brock Bowers (11) saw on the day. Mayer made the most of his opportunities, racking up 82 yards—the second most in his career and saw four of his receptions come on the Raiders’ first four drives of the game. On the Raiders’ fourth drive, Mayer hauled in passes of two, seven, and 17 yards, with his longest catch setting up a 48-yard field goal just before halftime to put them up 13-10. We shouldn’t expect this level of production from Mayer on a weekly basis, but the Raiders’ underwhelming WR corps could pave the way for more opportunities for Mayer going forward after this solid outing. There’s a lot to like here, but Mayer will be a boom-or-bust TE2 next week against the Patriots until we see reliable target totals on a more consistent basis, while he shares the field with Brock Bowers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 3-of-3 targets for 32 yards and one touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 3 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer scored with just under six minutes left in the first half. Coach Klint Kubiak sent Brock Bowers in motion, back and forth across the formation, behind the line of scrimmage, before Kirk Cousins executed the play-action fake. Mayer ran an out route from the slot and shook Saints defender Justin Reid on the cut before quickly hauling in the pass. Mayer’s other two catches both went for double-digit yardage gains. He will be a viable TE2 moving forward, with defenses focused on stopping Bowers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 3-of-4 targets for 23 yards in the Raiders’ Week 2 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Brock Bowers missed his second game of the year while recovering from a mensicus trim procedure, giving Mayer another opportunity to start. He led the Raiders in routes but failed to make a big impact in the box score, logging a measly 14 percent target share. Mayer is generally in the TE2 mix when Bowers is out, but even then he isn’t a particularly high-upside option. With Bowers expected to return next week, Mayer can be sent back to the waiver wire on the upcoming waivers run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 6-of-7 targets for 32 yards in the Raiders’ Week 1 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer was seemingly set for a sizable workload, going 3-of-3 for 21 yards on the Raiders’ first drive. He caught his fourth pass on the second drive, which was punched out and recovered by the Dolphins, but the play was overturned. For his part, Mayer looked good on short in-breakers and out routes, and his six receptions tie for a team-high. The Raiders simply got up to a 10-0 lead early in the second quarter and controlled the game thereafter, leaving the passing offense to take a backseat role to the Raiders’ ground game. Mayer can be started as a TE1 again next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Raiders signed TE Michael Mayer to a three-year, $45 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: The deal was first reported by NFL Insider Ian Rapoport. Mayer’s deal includes $30 million guaranteed and his $15 million average annual value is third among tight ends. The Raiders selected Mayer in the second-round (35th overall) of the 2023 NFL Draft. He had 300 yards as a rookie and the Raiders drafted Brock Bowers 13th overall the following year. Mayer is firmly on the fantasy radar for Week 1 against the Dolphins with Bowers (knee) sidelined, but his value is unstable as the Raiders’ second tight end.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 7-of-12 targets for 98 yards in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: It was business as usual for Olave, who has seen at least 10 targets in 6-of-8 games this year. He earned an astounding 38 percent target share today, and his 229 air yards are the second-most of the week, pending the two remaining games. The return of No. 8 overall pick Jorydn Tyson had no impact on his role, though Tyson was limited to 16 routes in his NFL debut. Tyson should see more work next week, but that will primarily come at the expense of Devaughn Vele. Olave will remain in the WR1 mix when he takes on the Panthers in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 6-of-10 targets for 57 yards in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave was once again a shorter-yardage target with a long gain of just 14 yards in the contest. Tyler Shough missed the 26-year-old on what would have been a walk-in touchdown from deep on a disappointing day for the top target in the Saints’ passing attack, at least based on expectations. He’ll remain one of the top fantasy receiving options in his next game, but that won’t come for two weeks as the Saints get a bye before facing the Browns in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Saints general manager Mickey Loomis said Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) won’t practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Loomis said Tyson is “improving” in his long rehab from a major preseason hamstring injury. Tyson, who traveled with the Saints to France for their Week 7 game against the Steelers, could still be a couple weeks away as the team takes a cautious approach to his recovery. In the meantime, Bryce Lance will operate as the Saints’ No. 2 wideout behind Chris Olave. Lance over the past two weeks has a 13 percent target share and a 20 percent air yards share in the pass-first New Orleans offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 4-of-7 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave finished as the Saints’ leading receiver after coming into the weekend questionable with an illness. He was able to salvage his fantasy day with an 18-yard score at the beginning of the fourth quarter. Despite a season-low 43 yards receiving, Olave is still averaging just under 100 yards receiving per game this season. There is no question he belongs in the fantasy WR1 ranks heading into a Week 7 showdown against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Chris Olave (illness) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: There was reportedly a bug going around the Saints’ locker room last weekend, and Olave seems to have caught the tail end of it. He missed the first two practices of the week but was back on the field for Friday’s session. The team listed him as questionable for Week 6. Barring any further updates, we’re expecting business as usual for the star wideout. He remains entrenched in the WR1 mix for his date with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (illness) is questionable for New Orleans’ Week 6 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave missed the first two days of practice this week with the illness, but we’d ultimately still expect him to play. He should be regarded as on the optimistic side of questionable. He’ll be an easy WR1, assuming he plays, against the Giants in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (illness) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Unless we get word that it’s an exceptionally rough illness, we’d expect no worse than a questionable listing on Friday despite the two missed practices. Olave should remain a smash WR1 against the Giants in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (illness) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: We expect Olave to be fine for the Saints’ Week 6 game against the Giants. There is currently no cause for concern, but this is worth keeping an eye on. Olave experienced blood clots in his lung last season, and spent much of the offseason recovering. We are not doctors and cannot opine on the matter. For now, expect him to play, but keep an eye out for his hopeful return to practice tomorrow or Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 4-of-6 targets for 46 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave was averaging over 120 yards per game before today’s contest. The Saints’ extreme play volume and tilt to toward passing the ball turned his great role into elite fantasy production. That finally came to a halt with Brian Flore’s defense shutting down Tyler Shough. The second-year passer completed just 16 throws for 96 yards. Shough and the entire passing attack should improve drastically versus the Giants next week. Fantasy managers can keep treating Olave as a WR1 despite this speed bump.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (foot) is not on the final injury report for Week 5 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: The Saints gave Olave a rest day on Wednesday. He then logged a limited practice on Thursday, listed with a new foot injury, and was reportedly seen sporting a walking boot after practice. ESPN’s Kat Terrell notes, however, that “walking boots are often a precautionary measure.” The fact that the team cleared him right away is reassuring. He can be treated as a low-end WR1, as usual. Olave later told Terrell that his “foot got a little bruised in Thursday’s practice, but he’s good.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught both of his targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson split reps with Noah Fant and Oscar Delp once again. He had one catch headed into overtime but made the most of the extra drive with a game-winning touchdown grab. It was his first touchdown since Week 3. This was also his first multi-catch game since Week 5. With Jordyn Tyson set to take on a larger role in the coming weeks, Johnson’s days as a high-end TE2 appear to be over. Fantasy managers can do better off the waiver wire in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports Saints WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) “should be good to go” against the Browns in Week 9.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: The oft-injured Tyson hurt his hamstring in training camp and is yet to make his NFL debut. According to Schultz, he should be good to go Sunday against the Browns. A limited participant in practice throughout the week, it’s unclear how much Tyson might play in his first game. Eventually, though, he should settle in as the Saints’ WR2 behind Chris Olave. Tyson’s return also puts a damper on the fantasy prospects of Devaughn Vele and Juwan Johnson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 1-of-3 targets for seven yards in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson was solid over the first four weeks of the season, but this was another clunker for the 30-year-old tight end. After going over 50 yards in his first four games and bringing in three touchdowns, Johnson has just 23 total yards without a score in the next three. Because of positional value Johnson can’t be completely ignored, but the Saints haven’t paid much attention to him lately, so it’s time to look for alternatives, at least.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson failed to catch either of his two targets in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson was silent in a low-efficiency passing day for the Saints offense. The tight end position in general was a non-factor as a pass-catching group on the day. As Tyler Shough deals with broken bones in his non-throwing hand, the Saints’ passing game is tightening up and has less room for Johnson. He is a fantasy TE2 for Week 7 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 4-of-5 targets for 16 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson had hovered around 50 yards in every game before today’s loss, but a shutdown Minnesota defense was more than enough to mute the production of every New Orleans pass-catcher. Things should improve for everyone when the Saints take on the Giants next week. Johnson will be a volume-based TE2 for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 6-of-8 targets for 59 yards in the Saints’ Week 4 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson saw a slight uptick in snaps and routes after Noah Fant was inactive with an abdominal injury but returned a modest receiving line while being kept out of the end zone. The towering veteran finished third on the team in targets behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele, the latter of whom scored the only receiving touchdown in a game that saw the two teams combine for seven rushing scores. Johnson remains a back-end TE1 for as long as rookie Jordyn Tyson remains sidelined, which appears likely to persist for another few weeks, at minimum. That holds true ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the vaunted Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 8-of-8 targets for 53 yards, two touchdowns and one lost fumble in the Saints’ Week 3 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson was getting open at will on out routes and shallow crossers. He and Noah Fant, along with the two Raiders tight ends, combined for six touchdowns, tying an NFL positional record. Johnson fumbled while trying to make a big play for his team late in the game. He attempted to stiff-arm Nakobe Dean, who cleanly punched the ball out for Eric Stokes to recover. Tyler Shough threw a bad pass to Johnson earlier on, which CB Hezekiah Masses easily picked off and returned downfield. Johnson raced after him and successfully punched the ball out with a diving hammer-fist, but the Raiders ultimately recovered that fumble, leading to a turnover for the Saints. Johnson remains a reliable TE1 against the Falcons next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 4-of-4 targets for 66 yards in the Saints’ Week 2 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson was on the receiving end of two big plays in Sunday’s win over the Ravens. Johnson hauled in a short pass on a third-and-13 in the third quarter and turned it upfield for a 25-yard gain. In the fourth quarter, Johnson again picked up 25 yards on a short pass on third-and-eight, taking it to the Ravens’ five-yard line and setting the Saints up for a touchdown a few plays later. Johnson has caught seven passes in his first two games and is averaging an impressive 17.1 YPR on said catches. He’ll be on the TE2 radar for next week’s game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Saints TE Juwan Johnson (illness) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson posted a 3/54/1 receiving line last week and can be treated as a TE1 again in Week 2. Saints WR1 Chris Olave is nursing a hamstring strain, though the team is telling reporters that the injury is not concerning. Johnson could take on a slightly larger workload if Olave is at all limited, though we won’t know if that is the case until the dust settles and the game ends.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Saints TE Juwan Johnson (illness) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson is firmly on track to play. Illness-related absences are very rare, and the Saints’ No. 1 tight end is already back at it. The Saints face the Ravens this weekend, in what should be a high-scoring game environment. Johnson is a locked-in TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Gracen Halton suffered a season-ending ankle fracture.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The fourth-round rookie finishes the year with 10 tackles, eight quarterback pressures and two sacks. Shanahan also told reporters that starting cornerbacks Renardo Green (back) and Deommodore Lenoir (foot) picked up injuries in today’s game against the Raiders. The defense has been hit hard by injuries this season. Hopefully, the cornerbacks are back before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers selected Oklahoma DT Gracen Halton with the No. 107 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Halton (6’2/293) is a twitchy, penetration-based interior disruptor whose elite testing profile (8.44 RAS with 97th percentile speed and 93rd percentile jumps) translates directly to his first-step quickness and backfield production. Halton posted 40 tackles, 10.5 TFL, 3.5 sacks and 16 run stops in 2025, pairing that with 26 pressures on 233 pass-rush snaps (11.2 percent pressure rate), strong efficiency for an undersized interior defender. He wins early in reps with explosive get-off and lateral burst, consistently crossing faces and creating immediate stress on protection schemes before blockers can anchor. Halton’s 92.3 percent run-tackle rate and 90.9 percent tackle efficiency highlight his ability to finish once he penetrates, though his lighter 293-pound frame can get overwhelmed when forced to play through contact or absorb double teams. His pass-rush plan is still developing, relying heavily on quickness and effort rather than counters, which leads to streaky down-to-down impact. Halton projects as a high-energy interior penetrator with sub-package upside, whose explosiveness and pressure production give him a clear path to a rotational role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Oklahoma has signed 2022 four-star DL Gracen Halton.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Halten (6'3/270) is the 34th ranked defensive lineman of in the 2022 class, and is the 257th ranked player nationally. Halten is a native of San Diego, California and had previously been committed to Oregon up until last week when he opted to re-open his commitment before ultimately signing with Oklahoma. Halton joins a Sooners class that currently ranked ninth nationally and second in the Big 12, despite multiple players de-committing from the program following the departure of former head coach Lincoln Riley. Halten will be a welcomed addition to the Sooners, who allowed 25.8 points per game to opposing teams and 391.2 yards per game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Former Oregon 2022 four-star commit DE Gracen Halton has re-opened his recruitment.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: According to his 247Sports.com player profile, Halton (6'3/270) de-committed from the Ducks on Wednesday, less than a month after receiving an offer from Oklahoma and making an official visit to Miami. A native of San Diego, California, Halton has not announced where he plans on signing ahead of the 2022 season, but as of now, it would appear that Oregon is off the table. Halton has also received offers from Arizona State, Cal, Fresno State, Miami, Michigan, Nebraska and Penn State, among several other programs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Oregon received a verbal commitment from four-star 2021 DE Gracen Halton.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Halton (6'3/270) is a big late commit for the Ducks, as the four-star prospect is considered the 12th best weak side defensive end and 15th overall player in the state of California from the 2021 high school class. They’ve made significant inroads by signing a large chunk of the high-end California recruiting market over the past few seasons. Oregon managed to fight off challenges from USC, Tennessee, Texas, Washington, Penn State, Cal and Michigan in order to reel in the promising defensive end.

Vidal was more effective than Omarion Hampton (33 yards on 14 carries) and Keaton Mitchell (11 on six) but still seems likely to be behind both for Week 6 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Kimani Vidal caught two passes for 11 yards and a touchdown while rushing four times for 16 yards in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Chargers RB Kimani Vidal rushed five times for eight yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Texans.
