Mitchell did not play, nor did starting RB Omarion Hampton. Vidal is a proven, capable fill-in starter, but he should only be drafted as the Chargers’ RB3 at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Speaking on NFL Daily about his backfield rotation, Chargers OC Mike McDaniel said, “if a player is playing really well, I’m not going to take them out.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Earlier this week, McDaniel said he plans to employ a hot-hand approach at the running back position and plans to “use all three of those guys probably every game.” NFL Daily co-hosts Gregg Rosenthal and Jourdan Rodrigue helpfully followed up on those comments, specifically regarding their fantasy football implications. McDaniel encouragingly prefaced his response by saying, “no one has to worry,” adding that benching productive players is “bad business.” If you were already bullish on one or more of Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal, these comments can be taken positively. Reading between the lines, if Hampton, the starter, proves his value as the team’s RB1, he should receive a fantasy-friendly workload.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Chargers OC Mike McDaniel said “I’ll use all three of those guys probably every game” when asked about the backfield.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Speaking to reporters Monday, Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said that all three of Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell, and Kimani Vidal will be featured in the backfield this season. “Good news is I see all three of those guys performing at a very high level,” McDaniel said. “Kinda play hot hand once you’re into games.” While that’s not the best news for fantasy managers that invested second round picks into Hampton, the opportunity for the Chargers to turn heads on the scoreboard could result in a case of “a rising tide raises all ships.” McDaniel famously, and recently, made two backs top-six producers in fantasy points per game in the same season, with both Raheem Mostert and De’Von Achane finishing 2023 in that range. Whether a similar situation transpires in Los Angeles remains to be seen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Chargers OC Mike McDaniel said he could use all three RBs in a game and that usage may depend on who has the “hot hand.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: It’s the kind of thing fantasy managers hate to hear. When speaking about his running backs on Monday, McDaniel said, “I see all three producing at a very high level,” while saying the workload for each back could depend on the opponent and who has the “hot hand.” While it’s certainly concerning on the surface, we feel pretty confident in Omarion Hampton having the safest role as far as fantasy is concerned, while Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal could prove a bit more volatile. Their volatility has been baked into their ADP all offseason, as Mitchell is often going in the 12th or 13th round of drafts while Vidal often goes undrafted. It may take some time to get a good sense of McDaniel’s plans for the backfield, but we would expect a clear-cut RB1 and RB2 to emerge this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 13 times for 60 yards in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters last Thursday that Omarion Hampton would get more touches. Surprise. The Chargers continued their three-player backfield rotation for much of the day, though Kimani Vidal was somewhat phased out in the second half. That said, Hampton at least totaled double-digit rushing attempts for the first time since Week 5. He clearly looked like the most powerful, explosive Chargers running back on a 32-yard run late in the game, jump-cutting his way into an open hole before exploding down the right side of the field. Hampton is a FLEX option against the Ravens in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh indicated that Omarion Hampton will get more touches.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Harbaugh reportedly made comments to this effect earlier in the week. When asked for his thoughts on the matter, OC Mike McDaniel said he is “excited about someone dictating the rotation” and added that Hampton has “had a really great week of prep.” Hampton hasn’t scored double-digit half-PPR points since Week 4. Whether the potential usage increase can get him back to 10.0-plus points remains to be seen, but this week’s comments are at least somewhat encouraging.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton had nine rushes for 20 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams, adding two catches for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: It was business as usual for the plodding Hampton, who breaks no tackles and does nothing beyond what is blocked for him. Hampton, who now has less than 50 rushing yards in five games this season, was third in pass routes among LA running backs on the day and tied with Keaton Mitchell with three targets. Hampton’s role doesn’t offer much: Coming into Week 8, he ranked 31st among running backs in expected fantasy points per game (and 37th in actual fantasy points per game). With no ceiling of which to speak, Hampton should stay on benches in Week 9 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: The Athletic’s Noah Furtado reports the Chargers will try to “simplify” the team’s offense in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Justin Herbert and the flailing Chargers skill position players have appeared almost comically confused about all the pre-snap motion OC Mike McDaniel uses. That came through in the team’s embarrassing Week 6 loss to the Chiefs when players were bumping into each other during pre-snap motion calls from Herbert. Head coach Jim Harbaugh acknowledged the team is considering narrowing the offensive playbook during their bye week. “Definitely looking at volume and where you can make it to where the players can understand,” Harbaugh said when asked about how Chargers players were adjusting to McDaniel’s complex offense. The Chargers have used pre-snap motion on 74 percent of their snaps, the fourth highest rate in the NFL. Last year they used motion on 56 percent of their snaps. Hopefully these adjustments lead to some production for the NFL’s worst offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton had seven rushes for 18 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs, adding four catches for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Hampton was his usual plodding self in this one, with a long rush of four yards in another depressing outing for the LA offense. Kimani Vidal, meanwhile had seven rushes for 21 yards and got much of his work in the first quarter. Keaton Mitchell had just two carries and did not catch his lone target. Hampton led the backfield in routes and targets on the day. His diminishing role and his lack of efficiency has made Hampton nothing more than a touchdown-dependent desperation flex option this year. The Chargers have a bye in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 14 times for 33 yards in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Webster’s defines plodding as whatever this was. Hampton picked up a literal third of his yards on one 11-yard carry, and while much of the blame goes to the sheer lack of bodies on the offensive line, it was still mightily unimpressive. Hampton is at best a dart-throw FLEX for Week 6 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said he has not lost “any faith” in Omarion Hampton.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: “I don’t see any change in terms of the depth chart at all. I felt I was underutilizing a strength,” McDaniel said about the increased usage of Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal. McDaniel’s statement is good for Hampton in the sense that we know Hampton will retain a reasonable role. And it’s bad because McDaniel is all but confirming the pecking order will remain the same. Expect more low-end RB2/FLEX nonsense from Hampton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed nine times for 45 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Hampton’s late touchdown that still left the Chargers down by 10 in the middle of the fourth quarter is the only positive of the day. Los Angeles clearly isn’t enamored with the second-year tailback — or at the very best, is concerned about keeping him healthy — right now, and he was clearly in a timeshare again with Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal. He’s at best a FLEX play for Week 5 against the tough Denver defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 15 times for 56 yards in a Week 3 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: The Chargers were missing two starting interior linemen and decided that running up the gut was not going to work for them. Understandably so. Hampton was held to just 3.7 yards per carry and didn’t seem to break any tackles in the interior of the Bills’ defensive line. Mike McDaniel decided to use Keaton Mitchell on the perimeter at the start of the game, but the Bills adjusted to take that away. At the end of the day, Hampton had 15 carries to Mitchell’s eight, but Hampton played 29 snaps, while Mitchell played 26 and ran a route on double the amount of dropbacks that Hampton did. This is a problematic timeshare in an offense that doesn’t look very good right now. Hampton remains a low-end RB2 who is touchdown dependent, which means he’s probably an RB3 next week against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 23 times for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 2 loss to the Raiders, adding two catches for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Hampton was a workhorse in this game, picking up what was blocked but not much more. He had a solid outing going until late in the fourth quarter when Nakobe Dean knocked the football out of his hands and into the waiting arms of Jeremy Chinn. A lengthy return put the Raiders in scoring position and all but ended the game. Fantasy managers won’t be too bothered by the blunder today, but it could result in the team giving more work to Keaton Mitchell, who only touched the ball six times. Hampton will be near the top of the RB2 ranks for Week 3 versus the Bills despite seeing an RB1 workload today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/dj-uiagalelei/.headline: DJ Uiagalelei completed 2-of-7 targets for 24 yards and one touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans.

Uiagalelei will be a QB3 against the Ravens if he gets the start next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/dj-uiagalelei/.analysis: The rarely-seen doubtful tag. Only the Chargers could discover a way for their backup quarterback to get it. DJ Uiagalelei could backup Justin Herbert this week.

He had a 67.0 PFF grade in 69 offensive preseason snaps this past offseason and could eventually become Los Angeles’ backup quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/dj-uiagalelei/.headline: Chargers elevated QB DJ Uiagalelei from the pracice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/dj-uiagalelei/.analysis: It will be Uiagalelei who backs up Trey Lance for the Week 18 finale against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/dj-uiagalelei/.headline: Clemson junior QB DJ Uiagalelei is reportedly “stronger and faster” heading into his second season as the team’s starter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/dj-uiagalelei/.analysis: Uiagalelei (6'4/250) struggled mightily in 2021, throwing for 2,246 yards, nine touchdowns and 10 interceptions. The junior quarterback is in need of a bounce-back season in 2022, especially with incoming freshman Cade Klubnik waiting in the wings. According to head coach Dabo Swinney, Uiagalelei is not the same quarterback we saw last season and is entering the season fully healthy. Uiagalelei reportedly also dealt with several injuries to his hand, including a strained PCL and a fractured finger on his throwing hand. It will be interesting to see how long a leash Uiagalelei has if he struggles early.

https://www.nbcsports.com/dj-uiagalelei/.headline: Clemson junior QB DJ Uiagalelei completed 17-of-36 passes for 175 yards and one interception in Saturday’s spring game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/dj-uiagalelei/.analysis: Uiagalelei (6'4/250) is in competition with freshman QB Cade Klubnik for this year’s starting role, and didn’t help himself in the spring game. The veteran QB once viewed as a Heisman Trophy contender failed to throw a touchdown, while completing just 47.2% of his passes. Klubnik appeared a little more polished, completing 15-of-23 passes for 106 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. Uiagalelei had nine touchdown passes for 10 interceptions last season in 13 games, and has just 14 career touchdowns in 22 games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/dj-uiagalelei/.headline: Clemson sophomore QB DJ Uiagalelei completed 21-of-32 passes for 187 yards and an interception in a 20-13 win over Iowa State on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/dj-uiagalelei/.analysis: Over the course of the season, you could tell that Uiagalelei (6'4/250) didn’t feel comfortable with the offense and what he was seeing. That continued in this game. While he was missing multiple receivers via injury and the transfer portal, Uiagalelei struggled finding receivers downfield, even with ample protection. His struggles were epitomized in the third quarter. He dropped back, escaped the pocket to the left avoiding pressure and threw a touch pass across his body. It was tipped and intercepted easily. The throw was ill-advised and likely would have been intercepted even if it wasn’t tipped. While he struggled all season, Uiagalelei led the Tigers to 10 wins on the season, but threw one more interception (10) than touchdowns (9).

https://www.nbcsports.com/dj-uiagalelei/.headline: Clemson sophomore QB D.J. Uiagalelei threw for 208 yards, including 137 to former high school teammate Beau Collins, as the Tigers cruised to a 48-27 win over Wake Forest.
https://www.nbcsports.com/dj-uiagalelei/.analysis: This was the type of Clemson performance most pundits expected throughout the year, as Uiagalelei (6'4/250) connected on 11 of 19 passes including a touchdown and an interception. While a big part of the story was the Clemson defense limiting an explosive Demon Deacon offense, Uiagalelei did enough to help a balanced Tigers attack approach the 50-point mark. Four of those completions went to Collins, including a 58-yard touchdown that made the score 31-13. Clemson (8-3) has now completed ACC play and will need some help to make a seventh straight conference title game, including a loss by Wake Forest to Boston College and a loss from North Carolina in one of their final two games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: Jordan Watkins caught all four of his targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: Watkins’ big day was capped off by a second half 37-yard touchdown grab on a perfectly placed ball from Brock Purdy. Watkins, who had 56 yards on three receptions in Week 7, functioned as the Niners’ top wideout with Mike Evans (Achilles) out. Watkins led the Niners in pass routes against a lousy Raiders secondary. He’ll be in play as a WR3 option in Week 10 against the Cowboys if Evans remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: Jordan Watkins caught 3-of-6 targets for 56 yards in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: Watkins was second among receivers in routes, running a route on 30 of the team’s 43 dropbacks, and was also third on the team overall in targets. He made a few nice catches over the middle of the field, and his day could have been much better as he caught a 20-yard touchdown pass from Brock Purdy in the second half. Unfortunately, while his feet were in bounds, the ball shifted a couple of inches when his back slammed into the ground, and replay review overturned the call of touchdown on the field. Depending on the status of the 49ers’ wide receivers coming out of next week’s bye, Watkins could be an interesting fantasy option, but it’s hard to know that for sure until we know who will be healthy for the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: Jordan Watkins caught his only target for 22 yards in the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: Watkins drew the start in place of the injured Deebo Samuel but was unable to take advantage of the opportunity, with 23 of Brock Purdy’s 29 targets going to the team’s top three options in Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, and George Kittle. Evans departed at the end of the second quarter with an aggravation of his Achilles injury, something that appears likely to cost the veteran a Week 7 game against the Falcons. That could leave Watkins in line for a second consecutive start, although the upside remains modest. Fantasy managers are likely best leaving both Watkins and veteran Brandin Cooks on the waiver wire, the latter of whom caught 1-of-2 targets for 13 yards against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: KhaDarel Hodge (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: This is a low blow, even for the subsation. Hodge began the year on San Francisco’s practice squad but was promoted to the active roster when De’Zhaun Stribling went down with an ankle injury. He wound up running 45 percent of the routes in Week 3 but was not targeted once. With Mike Evans also banged up, Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins could be in line for more work this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: Jordan Watkins caught both of his targets for 60 yards in the 49ers’ Week 3 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: Watkins saw increased opportunity with Mike Evans (rib) exiting in the second quarter. He caught a pair of long targets from Purdy despite KhaDarel Hodge and Jacob Cowing beating the 24-year-old in snaps. Watkins could certainly be on the fantasy radar if Evans misses an extended period of time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers declared RB Jordan James inactive for Week 1 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: James has officially lost the backup job to rookie RB Kaelon Black, who should be safely stashed on fantasy benches before kickoff. The 49ers also declared QB Kurtis Rourke, CB Ephesians Prysock, WR Jordan Watkins, LB Tatum Bethune and OT Enrique Cruz inactive for Week 1 against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers WR Deebo Samuel will take over “a portion” of the Z-receiver role, while also contributing as a “wide back.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows notes that at 30 years old, Samuel is “not going to be close to an every-down player.” 49ers WRs Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing are competing to be Samuel’s backup, though neither player will be reliable in fantasy. Samuel may also struggle to return FLEX value at this point in his career.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said he is excited by the work WR Jordan Watkins and WR Jacob Cowing have been putting in this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: Watkins drew positive reviews as a rookie last summer, but September ankle and calf injuries stunted his development, pushing him to the bottom of the depth chart. Cowing’s second NFL season was derailed by a recurring hamstring strain. The Athletic’s Matt Barrows listed him as a standout at Thursday’s practice, but he caught just four passes as a 2024 rookie. Expectations for him must be tempered. Watkins is worth monitoring for deep-league managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers WR Jauan Jennings (ankle/ribs/shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: Jennings is very difficult to trust after last week’s meltdown. He was limited twice to begin the week, and we do not yet know his Friday participation level. At this point, the big-bodied wide receiver can only be viewed as a boom-bust WR4/FLEX option. If and when he resumes practicing in full consistently, we will be able to upgrade him to WR3 status. 49ers rookie WR Jordan Watkins (calf) is also expected to play this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Jordan Watkins (calf) is expected to resume practicing this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: We were just thinking the 49ers wideout projections needed another variable to deal with. Watkins briefly wowed in training camp before dealing with a high-ankle sprain and later this calf issue. It’s possible he cuts into some veteran playing time if the 49ers wideout room remains unsettled, but he’s not someone to rush and pick up in re-draft leagues without seeing some real signs of fantasy life.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden caught 2-of-3 targets for 17 yards in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Justin Herbert gave Gadsden a chance to get going downfield early on, but the pass clanged off his hands. The incompletion may ultimately have been erased by a penalty. Herbert looked his way again later, on the Chargers’ late two-point conversion attempt, but it failed. Charlie Kolar, meanwhile, caught 3-of-3 targets for 31 yards and rushed once for three yards. Neither player needs to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden II caught all five of his targets for 52 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden led LA tight ends in targets and trailed only Ladd McConkey in receiving yards on the day. Operating as a big slot receiver, Gadsden could have some fantasy value if he were to get more snaps and routes in the Chargers offense. In Week 9 against the Texans he’ll be a decent streaming option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden II caught 3-of-5 targets for 17 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Both Gadsden and Charlie Kolar had five targets on the day. (Kolar caught three of those targets for 20 yards.) Gadsden logged 28 pass routes to 24 for Kolar. The split-up tight end role will make it next to impossible for either player to be fantasy relevant without catching a touchdown. The Chargers are on bye next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden failed to haul in his only target in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden had another disappointing outing for the Chargers and his fantasy managers on Sunday. He’s now been held without a catch in two of his last three games and has yet to exceed 36 receiving yards in any game this season. Playing in one of the worst offenses in the league certainly doesn’t help things, but Gadsden can’t be trusted by fantasy managers at this point and won’t be on the fantasy radar in Week 6 when the Chargers visit the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden II caught 5-of-8 targets for 36 yards in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden did make a spectacular catch on fourth down to set up a touchdown, but oustide of that, the tight end — while finishing tied for the most catches on the day with Keaton Mitchell — was unable to find any room against the Seahawks’ defense. The 23-year-old was more involved than he has been in previous weeks, but that’s less compliment to this effort than insult to the first few. He’ll be back at it in Week 5 against another tough defense in the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Chargers TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Week 4 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: He did rejoin practice today, making it plausible he’ll be up for the Chargers’ Week 5 game against the Broncos. Second-year receiving TE Oronde Gadsden was unable to seize the moment with Kolar and TE David Njoku (knee) sidelined last week, catching 0-of-3 targets. The once-promising youngster must do something on Sunday if he wishes to remain re-draft-relevant in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden didn’t catch any of his three targets in a Week 3 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden’s first target of the day was on a third-down pass that hit off his hands and landed on the grass. Neither of his other two targets was particularly close to being caught. He did play on 39 of the team’s 69 snaps, more than any other tight end, and ran a route on 31 of their 43 dropbacks, which was the third-most of any player on the Chargers. We guess you can talk yourself into his role based on those numbers, but the results weren’t there, and the Chargers look discombobulated on offense. It’s hard to trust Gadsden in fantasy going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: ESPN’s Kris Rhim reports that Chargers TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) will not be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Kolar’s surgery earlier this week reportedly changed his prognosis. Kolar was expected to land on short-term injured reserve and miss at least four games. Apparently, the team expects him back sooner than that. Backup TE Oronde Gadsden is still set to start, given Kolar and TE David Njoku’s (knee) injuries, but Gadsden’s audition window has evidently shrunk. He remains a worthwhile add and can be started by TE-needy fantasy managers in what should be a productive game environment against the Bills this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden caught both of his targets for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 2 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: David Njoku left the game early with a knee injury and Charlie Kolar followed him to the locker room much later because of a forearm injury. As a result, Gadsden’s route rate jumped from 14 percent in Week 1 to 48 percent today. He still managed just two catches, but Gadsden at least found the end zone for the first time this year. The Chargers offense has looked defunct through two weeks, so even a full-time role for Gadsden could result in middling fantasy numbers. Still, he is worth a look off the waiver wire for teams in need of tight end production.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Chargers OC Mike McDaniel said the team plans on utilizing TE Oronde Gadsden’s skillset.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: McDaniel was asked why Gadsden only played eight snaps in Week 1. The Chargers’ offensive coordinator said he expected Gadsden to get more involved last week, but the game “didn’t play out” that way. McDaniel closed by saying he expects Gadsden “to be more involved outside of an unforeseen situation where the game and the parameters with which you’re playing change — and therein lies the problem. Gadsden is not a full-time player. Projecting his weekly usage will be challenging. He is currently not worth starting in 12-team leagues, though that could change if McDaniel decides to feature him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 4-of-7 targets for 58 yards in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: It was a fairly low volume day for Brock Purdy and the Niners passing offense. The team had 25 pass attempts to 34 designed rushes against a miserable Vegas defense. Kittle ran a route on 28 of the team’s 32 drop backs and led the Niners with seven targets. His biggest play came on a patented catch and run through the Vegas secondary — one of a few long YAC plays for the San Francisco offense. Kittle should remain in all lineups next week against a porous Dallas coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 8-of-10 passes for 88 yards in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Unfortunately, Kittle also lost a fumble on the team’s final drive of the game as he was trying to earn extra yardage and set the team up for a better shot at the end zone. Even with that mistake, Kittle was tremendous on the day and the clear top option in the passing attack. The 49ers will be on a bye in Week 8, and then some of their injured receiving corps should return in Week 9, which might impact Kittle’s usage a bit. He will remain a rock-solid TE1 in fantasy leagues though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 5-of-8 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle got the scoring started with an 11-yard touchdown on a dime from Brock Purdy to the corner of the end zone, contributing to the offense steadily through a dominant first half before pushing his yardage totals with a 35-yard reception to start the third quarter. It was a tale of two halves for the San Francisco offense, which managed a staggering 303 yards of total offense in the first half and only 72 yards of total offense after the break, likely heavily influenced by the departure of Mike Evans at the end of the second quarter. Evans is expected to miss the team’s Week 7 contest against the Falcons, where Kittle could step into additional volume in his already-solid TE1 profile.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 5-of-6 targets for 24 yards in the 49ers’ Week 5 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: After three straight big weeks, Kittle finally came back down to earth in Sunday’s win over the Seahawks. His longest reception came on a 13-yard gain in the third quarter, but proved inconsequential after Deebo Samuel lost a fumble on the following play to end the drive. Kittle has been targeted 19 times over the last three weeks and has gone for 70-plus yards in three of his last four games. He should be primed for a bounce-back next week when the Niners play host to the Commanders on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle (illness) is active for Week 5 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: It was reported earlier on Sunday that Kittle was dealing with an illness, but that he was still expecting to play. Kittle was not listed with the 49ers’ inactives when the team announced them 90 minutes before kickoff, meaning he is good to go and can be treated as a TE1 as usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 4-of-6 targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 4 win against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: It was a quiet day for Kittle before a fourth quarter screen pass went for a 58-yard score that sealed the game for the Niners. Displaying explosiveness less than a year after tearing his Achilles tendon, Kittle outran the Broncos secondary for his second touchdown in as many weeks. His six looks from Brock Purdy was second most among Niners pass catcher, trailing only Mike Evans (eight targets). Kittle’s big play upside and his role in the red zone make him a potential matchup flipper in fantasy. He gets the Seahawks in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 6-of-7 targets for 82 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 3 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle saw a season-high seven targets in the 49ers’ win, becoming the team’s No. 1 pass-catcher after Mike Evans (rib) left the game. He caught a 10-yard touchdown at the start of the fourth quarter and later sealed the win with a 20-yard score with under two minutes left. Kittle seems to be all the way back from his Achilles tear, leading all 49ers offensive skill players in snaps, only trailing Brock Purdy and the offensive line. With Evans’ status in the air, Kittle is the team’s top receiver and is squarely in the fantasy TE1 conversation for Week 4 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: 49ers ruled out WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) for Week 3 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: This was the expected outcome for Week 3. Reports on Robinson’s injury indicate this could be a multi-week issue. With WR1 Mike Evans (hip) questionable, WR Deebo Samuel and TE George Kittle could take on sizable workloads, though the team will likely still try to limit Kittle’s snap count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught all four of his targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in a Week 2 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle looked good in this one, finding space over the middle of the field and showing good burst after the catch. That’s important considering he’s still working his way back from last year’s Achilles injury. The veteran played just three fewer snaps than Mike Evans and was fourth on the team in routes run, just one behind Christian McCaffrey. His playing time will continue to increase as the year goes on, but he looks pretty close to the George Kittle we’ve gotten used to.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: 49ers TE George Kittle (Achilles) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle will likely remain on a snap count in Week 2, though his usage should continue steadily ticking upward. He can be started as a TE1 against the Dolphins’ fantasy-friendly defense this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-4 targets for 58 yards and one touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans, adding one rush for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: If you didn’t start Johnston, we can’t blame you. It’s been a rough go. Johnston deserves credit for his long score. He caught a pass on a slant route and took off downfield via a post pattern, churning his legs through a shoestring tackle attempt. It’s the type of play we expected Johnston to be featured on in OC Mike McDaniel’s offense, rather than the deep routes he is frequently stuck running. Johnston also earned an end zone target, but was unable to secure it. With Justin Herbert (left hand) ailing, Johnston is tough to trust as a FLEX against the Ravens next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught all four of his targets for 37 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: It was yet another down game for Johnston, who did his work underneath in this one. He now has one game this season with more than two receptions in a Chargers offense that can be described as utterly dysfunctional on every level. Johnston should not be rostered in most fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-3 targets for 57 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston’s lone catch was a fantastic grab over tight coverage in the fourth quarter. He nearly scored on the play. Even with Ladd McConkey out with a head injury, Johnston did not function as the Chargers’ top wideout, as DeAndre Lambert-Smith led the team with ten targets. Johnston will be nothing more than a deep league flex option going forward. He should not be rostered in most 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Stark difference from last week’s limited-limited-rule out. Jim Harbaugh would not commit to putting it on the record that Johnston would be on a snap count. Playing through the injury with Los Angeles’ sad sack offensive line would seem to have Johnston as more of a sketchy FLEX play than a WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston is on track to play, but this wide receiver corps is very banged up. KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) and Brenen Thompson (quad) remained limited as well. Marquez Valdes-Scantling (ribs) upgraded to full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston, KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring), Brenen Thompson (quad), and Marquez Valdes-Scantling (rib) were all limited Wednesday. Lambert-Smith currently has his practice window for return from IR open while the others are dealing with a varying level of ailments. Johnston is the best fantasy option out of this group, but he is only worth FLEX consideration in the deepest of leagues. With Ladd McConkey (foot) also limited, the Chargers have several “maybes” ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Quentin Johnston (chest) will “probably be limited this week like last for the practice.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: “We’ll see where he’s at the end of the week,” Harbaugh added. Johnston practiced on both Thursday and Friday so he likely has the best chance of being active among Los Angeles’ main three wideouts. Unfortunately this passing game is in rough shape, and even a higher volume, healthy load probably wouldn’t get Johnston above the FLEX line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Week 5 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston got in limited sessions on Thursday and Friday, so it was surprising to see him sent straight to “not playing.” Tre’ Harris figures to step in as Los Angeles’ top outside receiver by snaps this week and is a worthwhile FLEX play, even against a formidable Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston and TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) both remained limited today, though WR Brenen Thompson (quad) downgraded. He did not practice, nor did Ladd McConkey (foot). Tre’ Harris could end up being the Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver, but he would only be a FLEX against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Chargers WR Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: In addition to Johnston, TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) and WR Brenen Thompson (quad) were also limited. Johnston has played in every game this season, but pops up on the practice report with a chest issue on Wednesday. He is not yet in danger of missing Week 5, barring setbacks later in the week. Neither Thompson nor Kolar have played since Week 2 but both have a chance to return this week against the Broncos. With Ladd McConkey (foot) not practicing, Johnston may have fantasy value as the Chargers’ No. 1 wideout this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 2-of-4 targets for 42 yards in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Schultz’s box score is a tad inflated by two throwaway targets. CJ Stroud aimed passes Schultz his way while pressured, in order to avoid intentional grounding penalties. Schultz did make a great toe-tapping catch along the right sideline on the Texans’ seventh drive, and later hauled in a 28-yard pass downfield against busted coverage. Schultz is a borderline TE1/2 against the Browns next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 5-of-6 targets for 45 yards in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Nothing groundbreaking here, though this was more like reasonable low-end TE1 work than reasonable low-end TE2 work. Schultz heads into the Week 8 bye with 137 yards in six games against non-Bengals defenses this year and unless you’re in a TE-premium league likely does not need to be on the roster while on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) is not on Houston’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: He’ll be good to go, but given how much Houston’s wideout usage has expanded of late, Schultz is probably just a passable TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Correcting a previous item, Schultz ended up practicing today. He was limited, as was Brevin Jordan (foot), who evidently picked up a new injury. Schultz’s return gives him a chance to face the Giants this week. Ideally, he will upgrade to full participation tomorrow, though it is possible he gets hit with the questionable tag if he remains limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Schultz is unlikely to play in Week 7 against the Giants, and now Texans TE4 Brevin Jordan (foot) appears to have suffered an injury. Jordan was added to the injury report today as a limited participant. The injuries elevate TE2 Foster Moreau to the streaming ranks for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Schultz never left the Texans’ Week 6 game against Jacksonville, but he was spotted with a limp after taking a knee to the leg. It’s possible the injury was worse than initially expected. If he were to miss Week 7, Foster Moreau, who scored twice last week, would be the next man up. Given that Schultz was barely putting up TE2 numbers as the starter, our hopes for Moreau as a streaming option would not be high.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 3-of-4 targets for 30 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: If you’re thinking all Dalton Schultz lines have started to blur together, you’re not wrong. He’s had eight catches for 69 yards since his Week 2 explosion against the Bengals. There’s not much upside here, but at least he’s providing a safe TE2 floor for those of you who get five points per TE reception.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 2-of-2 targets for nine yards in Houston’s Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Not the most inspiring entry of #RevengeGame lore. Schultz was outgained by Cade Stover and Brevin Jordan. He’s trending towards TE2 usage with Nico Collins back in the lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 3-of-3 targets for 30 yards in Houston’s Week 3 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Schultz told the CBS booth before the game that he “hopes to not have stat lines” like he had in Week 2, an anecdote they related as he had just one catch in the fourth quarter. Sounds like news that fantasy managers wish they had heard yesterday. He didn’t have a catch in the first half and yielded a red zone touchdown to spoiler Foster Moreau. Schultz has low-end TE1 status in a classic #RevengeGame against the Cowboys in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Texans ruled out WR Nico Collins (hamstring) for Week 3 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Collins will miss his second consecutive game with yet another hamstring strain. Last week, the passing offense ran through TE Dalton Schultz, who earned 13 targets. Fellow Texans WR Xavier Hutchinson was next with eight targets, but he caught just three, making for a shaky FLEX option this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-5 targets for 29 yards and one touchdown in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: The Texans’ run-blocking specialist isn’t going anywhere. He capped off the Texans’ opening drive with an 18-yard touchdown on third down, and came up clutch with a tough catch to pick up a first down on the ensuing drive. He later let a pass go off his fingertips 38 yards downfield, near the Texans’ 25-yard line. Had he caught it and landed on his feet, he probably could have scored. He had the secondary beat. Hutchinson cannot be trusted to return FLEX value against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-6 targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants, adding two carries for 12 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: One of the carries came on Houston’s last goal-to-go sequence of the game, where they wound up setting up what looked like a Hutchinson pass only to see him tuck the ball and run. We got nothing. With Tank Dell back and Marvin Harrison Jr. looking for work as well, it would seem that Hutchinson’s days as a FLEX option are over. But we would have said that before this game as well, and Hutchinson wound up with more wideout snaps than anyone but Nico Collins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 4-of-5 targets for 65 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: He led the team in receiving and didn’t have any contested drops today, so that’s a step up from where he’s been most of the year. Still, he played just 27-of-65 snaps. Kayshon Boutte (39-of-65) would be our main target as Houston’s third receiver if we thought the offense was good enough to warrant that kind of respect; they aren’t.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Kayshon Boutte caught 3-of-4 targets for 36 yards in Houston’s Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: He managed to get his finger underneath a sideline ball for a 21-yarder, and the replay booth upheld the ruling of catch on the field. He also managed fewer targets than Xavier Hutchinson (five), as well as 10 fewer yards, despite Hutchinson playing 16 snaps to Boutte’s 32. The Nick Caley WR platoon will continue until morale improves, making nobody much of a FLEX play against the Titans in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-6 targets for 51 yards in Houston’s Week 3 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: Hutchinson left the game after catching a 28-yarder in the fourth quarter and visited the blue medical tent. The Texans never announced a status for him, so it’s something to monitor. He lead the team in targets and yards. We guess that’s just where things are for the Texans now. If Hutchinson is healthy and Nico Collins is not in Week 4, he’ll have fringe FLEX/WR4 value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Texans ruled out WR Nico Collins (hamstring) for Week 3 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: Collins will miss his second consecutive game with yet another hamstring strain. Last week, the passing offense ran through TE Dalton Schultz, who earned 13 targets. Fellow Texans WR Xavier Hutchinson was next with eight targets, but he caught just three, making for a shaky FLEX option this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-9 targets for 37 yards in Houston’s Week 2 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: Through two games, Hutchinson has 15 targets and 69 yards. If you’re going to be this bad, you at least want the meme number. Hutchinson let a (admittedly hard to reel in) C.J. Stroud ball hit him in the hands in the end zone before dropping it and repeatedly struggled to finish contested catches, as he did in Week 1. Hutchinson is a fine depth receiver who has been pushed into a role he simply can’t do at the NFL level.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he “would not be surprised” if Texans WR Jaylin Noel is more involved in Week 2 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: Rapoport adds that Noel is “really talented.” We agree, but the Texans have consistently played WR Xavier Hutchinson ahead of him. Noel, 24, is an explosive player, and the Texans will be looking for playmakers to contribute with WR Nico Collins (hamstring) sidelined this week. Noel is officially on the boom-bust FLEX radar in Week 2 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-6 targets for 32 yards in Houston’s Week 1 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: He let two of the other three non-catches glance off his hands. Marie Kondo loves mess, so she’d love this Texans WR2 situation. Hutchinson led the four non-Collins receivers with 44 snaps. This should not be confused with him being a desirable fantasy football play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.headline: Texans WR Xavier Hutchinson caught1-of-2 targets for minus-one yard in Thursday’s preseason game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-hut.analysis: Hutchinson also failed to execute his blocking assignment on a run play that resulted in no gain for RB Woody Marks. Playing only with the first-team offense, Hutchinson nearly hauled in a tough sideline catch that would have picked up a first down, but the pass glanced off his fingertips. It wasn’t a great outing for him, but the Texans need him all the same, with their receiving corps awfully banged up at the moment. He should not be drafted in 12-team fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-8 targets for 55 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker occupied his usual role as the team’s de facto No. 1 wideout, almost connecting with Kirk Cousins in the second half for what likely would have been a long touchdown. Tucker was tied for the team lead in targets with Brock Bowers. His air yards domination gives Tucker a fairly high weekly ceiling in a Vegas offense usually chasing points in the second half. Tucker will be an iffy option next week against Seattle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker was held without a catch in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Coming off 10/200/3 over the past two weeks, Tucker somehow commanded only one target in a game where the Raiders scored 38 points. It was the first time since the opener he caught fewer than four passes. Tucker has definitely benefitted from some garbage time production, but he is not typically going to be a zero waiting to happen. He can still be trotted out there as a low-end WR3 for a Week 9 matchup where the Raiders are going to have to pass to compete with the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-12 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: It was a quiet day for Tucker until the Raiders once again found themselves down by three scores in the fourth quarter. Kirk Cousins — as he did last week against Buffalo — let it rip and peppered Tucker with late downfield targets, one of them resulting in an impressive 37-yard touchdown. Tucker led all Vegas pass catchers with a dozen targets and dominated air yards as usual. Last week against the Bills, Tucker went for 97 yards and two scores on five receptions. The miserable Raiders defense should lead to plenty of runaway negative game script for the team’s offense in the coming weeks, and Tucker’s role as the team’s lone deep ball option gives him weekly upside. He’ll be a WR3 option in Week 8 against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-7 targets for 97 yards and two touchdowns in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker found the end zone on an 11-yard touchdown pass from Kirk Cousins in the fourth quarter to tie the game at 23-23. Later in the game, with the Raiders down by 10, Tucker found himself on the receiving end of a Kirk Cousins moon ball in the end zone, which he hauled in for a 44-yard touchdown to cut the Bills’ lead to 33-30 with just over a minute left in the game. Tucker is the closest thing the Raiders have to a fantasy-viable wide receiver, and he has proven to be a volatile player throughout his four-year career. Fantasy managers shouldn’t view him as anything more than a boom-or-bust WR4 in next week’s game against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-5 targets for 41 yards in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots, adding two rushes for -7 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker’s two rushing attempts were blown up in the backfield. He was third on the team in targets, trailing Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty. Tucker, who usually operates as the team’s primary downfield option, should have some appeal in Week 6 against Buffalo in what could be a high-scoring game. He has at least four receptions in four of five games this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-8 targets for 44 yards in the Raiders’ Week 4 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker’s longest catch came on a 23-yard reception late in the fourth quarter as the Raiders looked to drive and tie up the game. Had the replay officials called for a review of the play in time, the catch likely would have been overturned, but the play was upheld, much to the disappointment of the Chiefs and head coach Andy Reid. The eight targets Tucker saw in this one set a new season high. He’s totaled 44 or fewer yards in three of four games this season and will be hard to trust as anything more than a dart-throw WR4 in Week 5 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-4 targets for 43 yards in the Raiders’ Week 3 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker had a bigger impact in real life than he did in fantasy. On the plus side, he helped set up a field goal and a touchdown, first by finding the soft spot in the Saints’ zone coverage in the two-minute drill. Later, his 15-yard gain on a deep crossing route helped set up the Raiders. He also committed a holding penalty, which erased a short gain for RB Ashton Jeanty. Tucker is a WR4/FLEX against the Chiefs next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-7 targets for 119 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 2 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Kirk Cousins got the deep ball going in this game after settling for mostly check-downs in Week 1. Tucker caught two passes of 40+ yards, the first of which was a second-quarter touchdown. He also tied Ashton Jeanty with a team-high seven targets, so it wasn’t just a one-off deep shot for the veteran wideout. Brock Bowers is expected to return next week, meaning Tucker’s target share should take a hit the next time we see him. Even if he is relegated to field-stretching duties in Week 3, Tucker will remain a high-ceiling FLEX bet versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 2-of-4 targets for 27 yards in the Raiders’ Week 1 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Despite receiving clear-cut No. 1 wide receiver treatment late in the preseason, Tucker was not the clear-cut No. 1 wide receiver in Week 1. He nabbed a nice 21-yard gain and had another downfield pass broken up by DPI, but Raiders coach Klint Kubiak didn’t have a focal target here. Treat Tucker as a boom-bust FLEX against the Chargers next week, in what should be a back-and-forth game environment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said the team is still trying to find a wide receiver who is “accountable and can help us on Sunday.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: He punctuated his point by saying only, “still looking.” Kubiak’s ambiguous phrasing could suggest that the Raiders are seeking a wide receiver via trade, but it can also be read simply as an indictment of players like Jalen Nailor, Jack Bech and Malik Benson. None of the three turned in a great game last night, while Tre Tucker was given the night off. Tucker makes for a boom-bust FLEX option in an underwhelming position group.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington, Jr. had six rushes for -3 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: A week after getting 25 rushes, Washington was relegated to six carries in this one, as the Niners raced out to a big lead and never relented. Washington tied Ashton Jeanty for the team lead in rushing attempts. Neither back got it going against a tough 49ers front seven. Washington, who ran five routes against San Francisco, will continue to be a prototypical early-down bruiser who is sensitive to weekly game script. He should be benched in almost every format next week against the brutal Seahawks defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Ashton Jeanty had six rushes for 25 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers, adding five catches for -5 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Jeanty and Mike Washington were scripted out in the second half, with the Raiders — as usual — falling behind by multiple scores. Jeanty was swallowed up by Niners defenders almost every time he caught the ball in the backfield. The plodding Jeanty couldn’t get anything going against a swarming 49ers defense. This was Jenaty’s sixth game of the season with at least four catches. It’s a role that has made him playable in 12-team leagues this season. Washington, meanwhile, had six carries for -3 yards. Jeanty might have some flex value in Week 10 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said the team’s backfield touch distribution will be a “moving target.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Mike Washington, Jr. in Week 8 against the Jets took over as the team’s lead rusher, logging 25 carries to just two carries for Ashton Jeanty. While Kubiak said after the game that Jeanty would remain a part of the offense, it’s clear the Raiders are willing to experiment with backfield touches. “You see where your team is at and who’s playing the best ball at the time. It’s a 17-game regular season where things change every week. They’ve been changing at guard, they change up front defensively, they change at corner,” Kubiak said. “That’s the NFL. We have a young roster and we’re going to give guys opportunities and see what fits us best. But your 11, whether you’re playing really well or not playing well at all, it’s always going to change a little bit.” The Raiders through Week 8 rank dead last in EPA per rush and second to last in rushing success rate. Jeanty should remain viable as long as he’s the team’s primary pass catcher out of the backfield. Jeanty ranks fifth among all RBs in expected fantasy points per game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington rushed 25 times for 83 yards in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: At least for one week, the Raiders formalized Washington’s early-down takeover, as the rookie out-carried a doghoused Ashton Jeanty 25-2. However, Washington got routinely stood up on his ample goal-line opportunities, and only out-gained Jeanty 83-73 thanks to Jeanty’s involvement in the passing game. A 45-yard reception where Jeanty literally fell down to catch an inaccurate Kirk Cousins pass only to get up and rumble nearly half the length of the field was by far the biggest play by a Raiders running back in this one. Although Washington now has to be considered the favorite for early-down work, he was uninspiring enough this afternoon that it’s not going to be an open-and-shut case against the 49ers. We would still rather start Jeanty in fantasy because of his pass catching.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington, Jr. had six rushes for 27 yards in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As usual, Washington was far more efficient than lead back Ashton Jeanty, who had 15 yards on eight carries while catching eight passes for 61 yards and a touchdown. Washington can be stashed for now in case Jeanty misses time in the second half of the season. Washington likely won’t get the pass-catching work if Jeanty misses time, however.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) is active for Week 7 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Whether Washington plays all that much remains to be seen. He is not a recommended FLEX starter. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak has misdirected at times with injury-related comments. The Raiders declared DT Thomas Booker IV, DE Cian Slone, S Dalton Johnson, DT Jonah Laulu, G Bryan Cabeldue, S Tristin McCollum and QB Aidan O’Connell inactive for Week 7 against the Rams. O’Connell will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Mike Washington (foot/back) is a game-time decision for Week 7 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Washington Jr. didn’t practice on Thursday or Friday but still received a questionable designation for Week 7. Fowler added that there is “some optimism” that he plays this week, but the pre-game workout will be the determining factor. Washington saw an uptick in carries last week with nine totes for 43 yards. We don’t expect as much work to go this way given the injury situation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 7 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Washington didn’t practice on Thursday and was not spotted at practice on Friday. It would seem that he’s a very tenuous questionable at this point. Dylan Laube would be next up for backup duties behind Ashton Jeanty if Washington were ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Dang. This suggests Washington suffered one or both injuries yesterday in practice. He is firmly in the questionable camp and may have only a long shot at suiting up in Week 7 against the Rams. Without him, Ashton Jeanty should handle a solid workload. Dylan Laube could end up serving as the No. 2 running back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington Jr. (foot/back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: In a semi-surprising twist of fate, the Raiders running back on the practice report with injuries is Washington, who was limited with foot and back injuries on Wednesday. Ashton Jeanty was not listed on the practice report. A limited practice indicates Washington is still trending to play Week 7, but with him appearing on the injury report and Jeanty off, any hopes for Washington achieving standalone fantasy value will have to wait.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 5-of-9 targets for 102 yards in the Patriots’ Week 9 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: The Patriots trailed throughout this one, which resulted in Drake Maye airing it out a season-high 38 times. The nine targets Douglas saw in this one also set a new season-high for the 25-year-old receiver, who reeled in two passes for 30-plus yards. Douglas has had a productive few games as of late, topping 60 receiving yards in four of his last five outings while also finding the end zone four times. He’ll be in the WR4/Flex range in Week 10 in what could be a high-scoring game against the Lions in Munich.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Mack Hollins (calf) will return to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Hollins has been on injured reserve for a month with a calf injury. With a full practice today he’ll have a good chance of suiting up in Week 9 against the Packers. Hollins will likely function as Drake Maye’s primary downfield option if A.J. Brown remains sidelined. Hollins’ return dings the fantasy prospects of DeMario Douglas, who has an 18 percent target share and a 19 percent air yards share over the team’s past three games. Hollins will be flex viable in deeper formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 3-of-3 targets for 76 yards and one touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: The Patriots rolled with 12 personnel on their first play from scrimmage, so Douglas began his day on the sideline. Hunter Henry suffered an apparent foot injury early on, which likely afforded Douglas extra snaps via 11 personnel. He made his opportunities count. Douglas critically picked up a first down, powering through contact on 4th-and-2 on the Patriots’ eighth drive. He showed up again on the Patriots’ ninth drive, securing a play-action pass along the right sideline before juking a Dolphins safety and slipping a shoestring tackle attempt from JuJu Brents before racing into the end zone for a 48-yard touchdown. Douglas is a FLEX option against the Patriots next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 3-of-4 targets for 23 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: The magic of the previous two games quickly evaporated for the diminutive slot receiver as Hunter Henry and Rhamondre Stevenson stepped into the primary security blanket role for Drake Maye, the latter of whom faced consistent pressure from the aggressive Dennis Allen Bears defense. Starting Douglas on a weekly basis is akin to reaching your hand into a brown paper bag found on the side of the road. It feels exhilarating at the time but you never know what you’re going to get.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 7-of-8 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets, also losing a fumble.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Douglas followed up his best game of the season with another best game of the season, as well as the third most receiving yards of his career. His touchdown was a nine-yarder in the second quarter where the Jets’ defense simply afforded Drake Maye too much time. Things could not have been going better for “Pop” until his fourth quarter fumble at the end of a 39-yard catch-and-run. He was the victim of a classic “Peanut punch” from behind. Rather ominously, he was not targeted thereafter, though the Patriots were also in ball-control mode as they worked on draining the clock. That today’s effort came as A.J. Brown was returning from a five-week absence was promising, but the reality is that Douglas’ big box scores are likely to remain pop-up efforts rather predictable and/or weekly occurrences. He’s a shaky WR4 even with byes and injuries in full swing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 4-of-5 targets for 65 yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Douglas had his first two touchdown grabs of the season as Drake Maye sliced and diced a lifeless Vegas defense from start to finish. Douglas was wide open standing in the end zone by himself for his first score, and broke out of a bunch formation inside the ten yard line for his second score. Douglas has run significant routes in the New England offense since A.J. Brown (ankle) went down to injury. When Brown returns — perhaps this week — Douglas will take on a smaller role in the Pats pass game. He should remain on waiver wires in most formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 1-of-5 targets for 38 yards in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Douglas was second on the team in targets behind only Mack Hollins, who saw nine looks from Drake Maye. Douglas got open and made a nice grab for his 38-yard gain — one of the only big plays for the struggling New England offense on Sunday. Though Douglas is playing a decent snap share, he should remain on waivers in most formats ahead of the Patriots’ Week 4 game against Buffalo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to miss 6-8 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Schefter and other reporters previously called it a 4-6 week injury, which now seems unlikely. Schefter did add that Brown is moving “pretty well” and could come back on the faster side of his updated timeline. Still, it looks like Brown will miss at least half of the regular season. Romeo Doubs will operate as the team’s No. 1 receiver until he returns, though it will likely be a group effort to replace Browns’ production. Mack Hollins and Demario Douglas will also be more involved.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Patriots’ Week 2 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Douglas made the first catch of the game for the Patriots, but was silent the rest of the day. The 25-year-old is a low-yardage slot receiver who tends to get schemed targets when he is on the field. Douglas tallied the third-most snaps of all Patriots wide receivers on the day but will find it hard to achieve fantasy relevancy in an offense that utilizes multiple receivers in several different ways. Second-year receiver Kyle Williams also saw a pair of targets, catching one for 10 yards. Neither Williams or Douglas are anything more than deep league dart throws for Week 3 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the “preliminary diagnosis” for A.J. Brown is a high-ankle sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Garafolo added, “MRI today after X-rays were negative.” That’s a good sign, but there is currently no timeline for Brown’s return. It will ultimately be a multi-week injury that could linger well into the season. Demario Douglas led the Pats with seven targets last night, though his looks are generally low-value check-downs. Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs will serve as the team’s primary outside receivers until Brown is healthy. Hollins led the Pats in receiving yards at a modest 51. Hollins is worth adding in deeper leagues, but it’s hard to imagine him putting up anything more than WR4 numbers while Brown is sidelined. Doubs should improve in Week 2 after failing to catch any of his three targets versus the Seahawks. He will get another shot at WR3 numbers against Pittsburgh next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner rushed eight times for 55 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 9 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Patriots lost Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) late in this one, but it’s still worth noting that nearly all of Kiner’s production came when the backups were on the field. Kiner punched in a nine-yard touchdown late in the fourth quarter with the game well out of reach, and broke off a 20-yard run on the second-to-last play in regulation. While it’s possible Kiner finds himself in a lead role when the Patriots take on the Lions next week, fantasy managers will want to temper expectations for Week 10 if either Stevenson (knee) or TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It seemed pretty obvious that Henderson wasn’t going to play Sunday after it was announced the second-year runner was dealing with “neurological symptoms” but it’s now official. There are much bigger things than football going on in his life. While he gets better, Corey Kiner should be the backup running back behind Rhamondre Stevenson going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner rushed seven times for 38 yards in the Patriots’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kiner’s most notable usage note is that he was trusted with a carry on 3rd-and-1 during the Patriots’ eighth drive. He was unable to convert it for a first down. Kiner was involved today because TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was inactive. Kiner does not need to be stashed on fantasy football benches in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner rushed 11 times for 57 yards in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Even with Rhamondre Stevenson active and TreVeyon Henderson surprisingly playing through his ankle injury, Kiner was called on as the Patriots’ “closer,” with all 11 of his handles coming in the final 16:30 of the contest. The Patriots were winning, but the game was still in doubt. Kiner responded by continually turning his short-yardage opportunities into first downs, while he ended up leading the team in rushing. It wasn’t easy to see that one coming, but it might be difficult for coach Mike Vrabel to un-see it as neither Stevenson nor Henderson impress in their No. 1 or 2 jobs. Kiner is worth an end-of-bench stash in 14-team leagues but is not yet 12-team league relevant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) will miss multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Henderson suffered his latest ankle injury in Week 5 against the Raiders. Schefter said Henderson is “regarded as a quick healer, so the Patriots are hoping his return is sooner rather than later.” Still, he could be sidelined for the next few weeks, leaving Rhamondre Stevenson as the team’s clear lead back. Corey Kiner, meanwhile, appears to be in line as the Patriots’ RB2 after seeing seven touches last week against the Raiders. Kiner should be stashed in most 12-team fantasy leagues for now. Stevenson profiles as a top-12 play until Henderson returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner had six rushes for 52 yards in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders, adding one catch for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kiner’s seven touches came after TreVeyon Henderson went down with what could be a serious ankle injury in the second quarter. While much of his work came in garbage time, Kiner could work as the Patriots’ No. 2 back behind Rhamondre Stevenson if Henderson is sidelined in Week 6. Kiner is worth a look on waiver wires this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner rushed six times for 11 yards in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kiner served as Rhamondre Stevenson’s backup with TreVeyon Henderson out this week. He was the only other Pats running back to see a carry in this game, though practice squad call-up Lan Larison was targeted twice, both of which he caught. Kiner did not see a look through the air. As a backup running back without any pass-catching value, Kiner is not on the fantasy radar heading into Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss reports that Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is not present for the media-access portion of practice on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The injury has sidelined Henderson since August 24. The Patriots face the Seahawks on Wednesday. At this point, Henderson must be considered questionable to play. Even if he were active, he would be slated for No. 2 duties behind starting RB Rhamondre Stevenson, and it is fair to wonder if the team would keep Henderson on a snap count. Reiss reported this morning that RB Lan Larison and/or RB Hassan Haskins would likely be elevated from the practice squad if Henderson cannot play, joining Stevenson and backup RB Corey Kiner on game day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots acquired RB Corey Kiner from the Cardinals in exchange for a seventh-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The trade was first reported by ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The draft pick going to the Cardinals is a seventh-round pick in 2028. Kiner was buried on the depth in Arizona, but should immediately step in as the RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson with the Patriots. A former UDFA who appeared in four games with the Cardinals last year, Kiner is only worth a stash in deeper formats and has no standalone fantasy value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Emari Demercado rushed five times for 30 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 16 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Demercado failed to snag his only target and he was out-touched 6-to-5 by fellow backup RB Corey Kiner. Cardinals RB Michael Carter is the clear-cut starter and Kiner’s presence reduces Demercado’s bench-stash value. This looks like a three-player committee with one FLEX-viable player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins caught 3-of-6 targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 9 loss to the Packers.
