https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Playing in his first game since Week 4, Hollins ran a season-high 34 routes and tied Eli Rairdon for the second-most targets among Patriots pass-catchers on the day. Hollins found the end zone on a 22-yard score in the third quarter with the Packers already well ahead, which gave Hollins his first touchdown of the season. Hollins has been targeted five or more times in three of his five games this season and could be a deep league streaming option next week against the Lions if A.J. Brown (knee) misses next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Patriots activated WR Mack Hollins (calf) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins misses the minimum four games with a calf injury and returns to a pass catching corps without A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson, while tight end Hunter Henry is also listed as questionable for Week 9. There is opportunity for him to lead the team in receiving with the bulk of the remaining healthy players largely operating in the short-to-intermediate areas of the field. Fantasy managers in a bid could do worse as a FLEX option against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins (calf) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins is firmly in the questionable column with one practice left in Week 9. If active, he would be a boom-bust FLEX. The Patriots’ healthy wide receivers have played well in Hollins’ absence, though the team would probably like to get their field-stretcher back in action before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Mack Hollins (calf) will return to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins has been on injured reserve for a month with a calf injury. With a full practice today he’ll have a good chance of suiting up in Week 9 against the Packers. Hollins will likely function as Drake Maye’s primary downfield option if A.J. Brown remains sidelined. Hollins’ return dings the fantasy prospects of DeMario Douglas, who has an 18 percent target share and a 19 percent air yards share over the team’s past three games. Hollins will be flex viable in deeper formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Patriots place Mack Hollins on injured reserve with a calf injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: The Patriots snuck Hollins onto the injured reserve list over the weekend. He will be eligible to return after sitting out for four games. The Patriots also placed FB Reggie Gilliam on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins (calf) will not play in New England’s Week 5 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: It sounds like Efton Chism, Kyle Williams, and Demario Douglas will all work more than usual next to Romeo Doubs in Week 5. Chism might be the most interesting FLEX play of the three after putting up 2/42/1 in relief of Hollins against the Patriots, though all of them have cases.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins (calf) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Normally a wind-sprinter and a blocking specialist, Hollins became shockingly important at work after A.J. Brown went on IR with an ankle injury. He currently leads the team in targets, tied with Romeo Doubs at 20 apiece. Hollins holds the lead outright in catches (15) and yards (209). His absence would free up downfield opportunities for Kyle Williams. Efton Chism and Demario Douglas would likely see an uptick in routes as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins injured his calf in Week 4 and was listed as questionable to return. He immediately went to the locker room and did not return. Hollins is unlikely to play in Week 5. Romeo Doubs finally broke out last week with six catches for 58 yards and two scores. He will be in line for another sizable role once Hollins is ruled out. Kyle Williams will take on a starting role, though he is only worth a stash in deeper fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Speaking Monday, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel did not have an update on Mack Hollins’ calf injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Vrabel said he’ll have more information on Hollins shortly, but added that Hollins may miss a few days of practice. Hollins exited Week 4’s game against the Bills with a non-contact injury, leaving the field with a 3-53-0 line on four targerts. Hollins has seen 13 targets over the last two weeks while running the third-most routes (45) of any receiver. We’ll likely know more about the severity of his injury soon, but he could be at risk of missing Week 5’s game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins is questionable to return with a calf injury
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins went down when he cut to the sideline on an out route. He had to hobble off the field and was immediately taken into the locker room. The Patriots have not ruled him out yet, but we’d be surprised if he returned today. Romeo Doubs should continue to see the vast majority of targets. Hollins had 53 yards receiving on 3-of-4 targets before getting hurt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 4-of-4 targets for 55 yards and one touchdown in the Texans’ Week 9 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: Collins delivered a 19-yard catch-and-run on the Texans’ opening drive. He played particularly well running curl route today. His one-handed touchdown has to be seen to be believed. He and his coverage defender went vertical in the end zone and Collins somehow underhanded the pass around the other player’s body, briefly pinning it to the defender’s torso to secure it. Collins is a locked-in WR1 against the Browns next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 2-of-5 targets for six yards in Houston’s Week 7 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He did draw a defensive pass interference and a defensive holding, so at least he helped in points per penalty leagues. The Giants had defenders draped all over Collins for the majority of the game, and he was punished when he did catch the ball. It was Collins’ worst box score return since his rookie season, and one of only four games in his career where he was targeted and did not return at least 13 yards. The Texans wideout situation is complicated, but we’d still bet on Collins returning from the bye as a low-end WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 3-of-5 targets for 76 yards in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He added a long defensive pass interference penalty drawn on Travis Hunter to set up Houston’s second third-quarter touchdown. Collins also took an end around in the red zone for five rushing yards. Close, but ultimately not the line that fantasy managers were hoping for. Collins will remain in the low-end WR1 region against the Giants in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He went for 3/45 in the first half and was mostly managed down with the Texans not really threatened in a major way after he sealed a block for their first touchdown in the third quarter. Collins took a hard fall after a leaping grab and did look a little worse for the wear on the sideline. We wouldn’t be surprised if he saw injury report time this week. That said, he looked good and the Texans simply didn’t need to throw the ball much late in this one. It’s back to the low-end WR1 line next week against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 7-of-8 targets for 118 yards and two touchdowns in Houston’s Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He immediately busted out of the gates with a 45-yarder, caught a touchdown to end that drive, then found the end zone a second time in the second half when he worked to the other side of zone coverage and C.J. Stroud was able to find him on an improvised throw. Pretty good player. Collins handled 36-of-53 snaps, highest on the team. He’ll be a low-end WR1 against the Titans in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins (hamstring) is not on Houston’s final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He got in a full session and will escape the line. Collins doesn’t play the same amount of snaps that most of the league’s top wideouts play anyway, so even if he is managed a bit, he can be trusted as a low-end WR1 in what looks to be a smash spot against a bad Cowboys pass defense, though one that is integrating new trade acquisition Joey Porter Jr. against Collins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins (hamstring) was seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: We’re still waiting for the final injury report to drop, but Collins appears set to return in Week 4 after missing the last two games with a hamstring injury. Collins was listed as limited in Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices and has been trending in the right direction all week. We’ll check back in when the Texans officially confirm Collins’ status ahead of the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: The Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan M. Alexander reports that Nico Collins (hamstring) was “optimistic” about playing in Week 4 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: Alexander caught up with Collins after the Texans’ star player logged his second consecutive limited practice. Collins should probably still be treated as sitting somewhere in the questionable-to-probable range, but this is great to hear. Collins is a WR1, as usual, if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: Another limited session keeps Collins in the questionable column as he attempts to return from a multi-week hamstring strain. The Texans would surely like to have their star wide receiver back for what could be a back-and-forth game environment against the Cowboys this week, but balancing short-term and long-term needs is critical. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins (hamstring) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported over the weekend that Collins had a “decent chance” to return in Week 4. Even a limited practice today is a big step in the right direction. The winless Texans desperately need a playmaker on offense and Collins is their only option. While he could be on a pitch count in his first game back, Collins has to be in fantasy lineups the moment he is cleared to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 2-of-4 targets for 17 yards in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: As expected, the return of Jordyn Tyson brought about the end of Vele’s time as a WR3 fantasy option. Though Vele got his normal complement of routes, Tyson out-targeted him 5-4. He also went for more yards on two extra catches. Tyson’s role is only going to grow as he gets more practice reps under his belt. Fantasy managers can thank Vele for the good times and send him to the waiver wire on this week’s run. He will be buried in the WR5/6 range for Week 10 versus the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports Saints WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) “should be good to go” against the Browns in Week 9.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: The oft-injured Tyson hurt his hamstring in training camp and is yet to make his NFL debut. According to Schultz, he should be good to go Sunday against the Browns. A limited participant in practice throughout the week, it’s unclear how much Tyson might play in his first game. Eventually, though, he should settle in as the Saints’ WR2 behind Chris Olave. Tyson’s return also puts a damper on the fantasy prospects of Devaughn Vele and Juwan Johnson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 5-of-5 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Vele brought in a one-yard touchdown on fourth-and-goal late in the second quarter to tie the game at 10-10. It would be the last points the Saints would score. Vele has hovered around these numbers through the first half of 2026, and while he provides Shough with a nice safety valve, it’s not exactly what fantasy managers should be chasing. He’ll be a WR4 in Week 9 against the Browns after the Saints “enjoy” their bye in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 3-of-6 targets for 42 yards in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: The Saints offense has not pushed the ball downfield over the past two weeks, leading to low-scoring outputs for Vele. He caught three passes on the day, and nearly reeled in a fourth catch on a Tyler Shough sideline overthrow in the second quarter. When the Saints aren’t in a pass-happy game script, Vele is relegated to touchdown-dependent FLEX value. He will be in the WR4 ranks against the Steelers for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 4-of-6 targets for 26 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Tyler Shough managed a dismal 96 passing yards in this game, so there simply wasn’t enough production for any New Orleans wideout to post usable fantasy numbers. Vele still tied Chris Olave for a team-high in targets. He has at least four catches and six targets in every game this year. Even after a quiet Week 5, Vele remains a solid WR4 option headed into a Week 6 date with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 6-of-9 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 4 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Vele’s nine targets ranked behind only alpha Chris Olave, although he was headed for another modest fantasy outing before a garbage time touchdown with less than two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter of the blowout loss. Vele has yet to eclipse 69 yards through the first month of play as he continues to operate in an intermediate role for a Saints team struggling to attack downfield. Fantasy managers could consider sitting Vele against the ferocious Vikings defense in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards in the Saints’ loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Vele nearly added a decent first-down pickup to his box score, but he was unable to secure the pass as he was diving to the ground. Aside from that, he had a nice 17-yard gain in which he ripped his leg away from a would-be tackler and scampered away for a few extra yards. Vele is a boom-bust FLEX against the Falcons next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Saints WR Barion Brown (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: It seems like Brown is very unlikely to play at this point. His agility and long speed define his game as a gadget player and return specialist. His absence could benefit WR2 Devaughn Vele and WR Bryce Lance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 5-of-7 targets for 64 yards in the Saints’ Week 2 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: It was another solid outing for Vele, who has now caught 12 passes for 133 yards and one touchdown in his first two games this season. Vele’s biggest play came on a third-and-eight when he hauled in a 29-yard reception to extend a drive that ended with a Daniel Carlson field goal. Vele is the clear-cut WR2 for the Saints at this point and could be worth a dart throw in deeper leagues next week as a WR3/WR4 in Week 3 against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill reports that Saints WR Chris Olave (hamstring) “left practice as a precautionary measure” on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Underhill adds that Olave’s hamstring issue is not expected to be a “problem.” If this really is a non-issue, perhaps Olave just experienced cramping today and will be back out there on Friday, practicing in full. That said, soft tissue issues that pop up mid-week are typically not good. Saints No. 2 WR Devaughn Vele is worth adding if he is a free agent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 21-of-35 passes for 384 yards, five touchdowns and one interception in the Texans’ 44-22, Week 9 win over the Chargers, adding two rushes for 20 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: Stroud was nonchalantly excellent today, linking up with four different pass catchers for five touchdowns. He capped off the opening drive with a 17-yard, third-down touchdown strike to Xavier Hutchinson. Tank Dell hauled in Stroud’s second touchdown in stride, beating his coverage defender and racing into the end zone for a 63-yard score. Kayshoun Boutte bagged two, including one against Chargers CB Duke Shelley, who Stroud picked on for much of the Texans’ seventh drive. He hit Nico Collins for an improbable one-handed score, in which Collins briefly pinned the football against his coverage defender’s torso to secure the catch. Stroud’s lone mistake was an off-target interception that one Chargers defender tipped to another. Stroud should remain in fantasy football lineups as a QB1 next week against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: Texans GM Nick Caserio said he expects to eventually reach a deal on a contract extension with C.J. Stroud.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: Speaking on Monday with the media, Caserio said that “nobody is discouraged” with how negotiations with Stroud and his agent have gone thus far, saying that the two sides just “couldn’t quite come to an agreement” yet. Stroud is in the fourth year of his rookie contract and had his fifth-year option picked up by the team earlier this offseason. He will be under contract through the 2027 regardless of how negotiations go, but we would expect him to sign a long-term extension at some point next offseason to avoid this becoming an issue come training camp. Despite the Texans’ 2-5 start to the season, Stroud has been mostly solid, throwing for 1,867 yards, 11 touchdowns, and one interception while completing 64.8 percent of his passes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 17-of-28 passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in Houston’s 27-21, Week 7 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: The Texans seemed to always be playing from well behind the sticks today with 10 penalties and Stroud was let down by a ghastly drop from Marvin Harrison Jr. with someone in his face in the fourth quarter. The Giants did a better job than other teams had at getting interior pressure on Stroud. Still, it wasn’t a bad game outside of an immediate overtime three-and-out, one that was punctuated by a dropped pick by Kayvon Thibodeaux. Stroud heads into the bye as a reasonable high-end QB2 with a Week 9 matchup against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 24-of-34 passes for 312 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in Houston’s 34-31, Week 6 win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: The Texans running game was mostly abandoned until the fourth quarter, leaving Stroud to wail on an overmatched Jaguars secondary. His best throw was probably on Houston’s final possession of the first half, as he dotted a 50-yard throw with a defender in his face to Jaylin Noel, eventually setting up (checking notes) Foster Moreau’s second touchdown of the day. Stroud has now thrown for six touchdowns and gone over 260 yards in each of his last three games; he’s suddenly in the high-end QB2 competition with bye weeks hitting as the Texans host the Giants in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 26-of-34 passes for 261 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s 26-3, Week 5 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: He added a rushing touchdown on a goal-to-go red zone keeper. The Texans offense continues to bog down with penalties and bad runs — they went into half with four field goals — but Stroud was able to pilot the ship well enough to keep things reasonable until the Titans defense broke in the second half. He’ll head to London next week to face the Jaguars, yet another team that should keep him throwing given how good their run defense is, so he’ll be a mid-range QB2 for that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 21-of-31 passes for 347 yards and two touchdowns in Houston’s 34-30, Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: Well, hard to blame much of this on him. Stroud was turnover-free for the third time in four games and peppered the returning Nico Collins with targets while also finding a 52-yarder to Jaylin Noel and several chunk gains to the tertiary receivers. The Texans had a 30-27 lead at the two-minute warning. For once, the defense gets to pick up the slack. The Texans have the mother of all get-right games in an 0-4 bowl against the Titans next week. Given how poorly the run offense is going, Stroud may continue to let it rip here and could be on the high-end QB2 line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said he is open to leaning more into the passing game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: “The thing for me about offensive football is you have to make sure you move the ball and try to score as many points as possible,” Ryans is quoted as saying by the Houston Chronicle. “How that looks to me, it really doesn’t matter. You can think or want to be a certain thing. But if you’re shown that that’s not the case and it’s not getting done, then you have to adjust. That’s where we are.” The Texans already abandoned the run against the Bengals in Week 2, throwing the ball 55 times. Perhaps Nico Collins’ return this week will raise all ships, but if it was as simple as the Texans needing to throw more, they probably would have scored more than six points against the Bengals. C.J. Stroud has a streamable matchup against the Cowboys this week if it all comes together.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 16-of-27 passes for 167 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s 19-17, Week 3 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: It was turnover-free football despite three sacks. Simply put: The Texans just don’t look like an NFL offense right now. Two of Stroud’s three deep balls in this game could have been intended for any of four different receivers, one of them hit off Jaylin Noel’s hands. Nobody has taken the reins. Texans OC Nick Caley deserves to be on the hot seat. Stroud passes the eye test when you watch these games, but the design of this offense — especially the run offense — is brutal. Stroud is near the bottom of the superflex QB2 ranks against the Cowboys next week, though the potential return of Nico Collins merits some consideration that better things could happen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 30-of-55 passes for 353 scoreless yards in Houston’s 20-6, Week 2 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: Stroud looked pretty good in this game, but he had no one to throw to, the Texans had no running game (Stroud lead the team in rushing with 29 yards), and they scored six points. Other than that, Mrs. Lincoln... Xavier Hutchinson failed to reel in several passes that hit him in the hands, including a would-be touchdown in the waning moments. It’s clear that without Nico Collins there’s just not enough talent on the field here to support a dead running game, and that’s what happened today. The Texans will look to rebound against the Colts in Week 3, a game where Stroud is probably on the QB2 radar for in superflex leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 26-of-38 passes for 274 yards and two touchdowns in Houston’s 36-31, Week 1 loss against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: The buried news from the traditional stat line is that Stroud fumbled twice and the Texans recovered neither of them, including a back-breaker inside the Buffalo 20 on Houston’s final drive. The hard truth is that this offensive line is still not good. But, overall, it’s hard to fault the Texans offense for this one — if the 2025 Texans defense showed up, they win the game. Stroud looked competent-if-not-stellar in leading a touchdown drive in the two-minute drill of the first quarter. This is a good result for his superflex QB2 prospects — the Texans defense being as bad as they were in this one would also be welcomed news for fantasy managers. Stroud will get an (on-paper) easier roll against the Bengals in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Jerry Jeudy caught 2-of-4 targets for 37 yards in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Jeudy reeled in a game-changing 30-yard pass on the Browns’ final drive of regulation. The grab eventually set up a tying field goal from Andre Szmyt. While the Browns would go on to lose in overtime, Jeudy’s catch at least gave them a shot at the win. He’s not on the fantasy radar right now, but his occasional big play should be enough to keep the Browns from trading him ahead of Tuesday’s deadline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter named Calvin Ridley as a potential trade candidate.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Schefter threw out several names, many of whom have already been bandied about as trade candidates. Among the lesser-discussed options, he included Jerry Jeudy and Jauan Jennings in addition to Ridley. All three are veteran wideouts who have simply disappeared in the current iterations of their respective offenses. Even with new landing spots in the cards for the trio, none of them are worth holding onto in standard fantasy leagues. Ridley has five catches for 81 yards this year. He is expected to play through his hip injury today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Jerry Jeudy caught all four of his targets for 21 yards in the Browns’ Week 7 win against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Jeudy was second on the team in pass routes — behind Denzel Boston — and fourth on the team in targets. This comes after Jeudy’s Week 6 performance against the Ravens in which he went for a season-high 69 yards on four receptions. Jeudy is well behind Boston and KC Concepcion in the pass-catching pecking order and should only be rostered in the deepest leagues for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Jerry Jeudy caught 4-of-4 targets for 69 yards in the Browns’ Week 6 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Jeudy made the most of his limited volume in this one, with his longest play coming on a 33-yard reception on the final drive of the game as the Browns were driving down the field to complete the comeback victory. This was easily the best game of the season for Jeudy, who hadn’t gone for more than 36 yards in any other game this season. He’s seen four or fewer targets in four of his five games played and won’t be on the fantasy radar heading into Week 7 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Jordan Schultz reports the Browns would like a third or fourth-round pick for WR Jerry Jeudy but he’s not sure they’ll be able to get it.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: We, too, would like to simply be given valuable things for no reason. Jeudy has fallen off the fantasy map enough that we’re now simply blurbing trade possibilities for him. The 27-year-old’s only real fantasy value at this point is hoping he gets traded somewhere where he can get involved again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jerry Jeudy “could be had” before the trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: With Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion earning large roles right away, Jeudy has all but vanished from the box scores. He went two games without catching a single pass before bringing down three balls for 36 yards on Thursday night. Jeudy got pushed out of the Browns’ long-term plans on draft night and isn’t even part of the week-to-week game plan at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: KC Concepcion caught 5-of-8 targets for 64 yards in the Browns’ Week 4 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Concepcion continues to operate as the primary slot receiver for a Browns team clearly looking to their youth while phasing out veteran Jerry Jeudy, the latter of whom managed three receptions on three targets for 36 yards. Concepcion has yet to lead the team in receiving while working in a short area role, with this the first game thus far which he has gained more then 43 yards. He’ll be a difficult start in fantasy circles when the Browns take on the Jets in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Jerry Jeudy did not catch his lone target in the Browns’ Week 2 win against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: After his two-catch performance in Week 1, Jeudy is off to a roaring start. Denzel Boston has established himself as Cleveland’s de facto No. 1 wideout while KC Concepcion is being force fed the ball on gadget plays near the line of scrimmage. With almost no avenue to fantasy relevance, Jeudy should remain on waiver wires.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Browns WR Jerry Jeudy (wrist) is practicing in full for Week 2 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Jeudy is on track to play, but he is seemingly being phased out of the offense. Browns rookie WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion are establishing themselves as impactful starters, and their roles should only grow in the coming weeks. Jeudy should be left on waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Jerry Jeudy caught 2-of-4 targets for 26 yards in the Browns’ Week 1 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Jeudy felt like an afterthought behind the two rookie wideouts in the Browns’ passing game. He tied for second in targets and was a distant third in yards behind Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion. The veteran is still involved as a starter on the outside, but Todd Monken made it a point to make Boston the deep target and Concepcion the primary offensive weapon. In a fantasy-unfriendly offense, Jeudy is best left off the fantasy radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 1-of-3 targets for one yard in the Packers’ Week 9 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Interestingly, Kraft had a more productive day on the ground (2-8-0) in what was a quiet day for the 26-year-old tight end. His quiet day can be partly blamed on a hyper-efficient passing attack that saw Matthew Golden and Christian Watson combine for 335 of the 372 receiving yards the Packers managed on the day. The three targets Kraft saw tied a season low, and he averaged 6.7 targets per game over his last six games. He will look to bounce back next week at home against the Vikings and will profile as a low-end TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 6-of-6 targets for 53 yards with a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft was able to bring in a score between a pair of defenders to give the Pack a 6-0 lead in the first quarter. That’s back-to-back games for the tight end with a score, and three in the first half of 2026. Kraft has seen a similar amount of involvement throughout the campaign, and he’ll likely put up a similar statline — hopefully with a touchdown for fantasy managers who roster him — in Week 9 versus the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 4-of-6 targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 7 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft found the end zone on a 14-yard touchdown near the end of the second quarter, giving him his second touchdown of the season and his first since Week 4 against the Buccaneers. Kraft has seen six or more targets in four of his last five games and has posted double-digit PPR points in three of his last four. Even when he isn’t finding the end zone, his volume, coupled with his big-play ability, is enough to keep him in the TE1 conversation. Kraft gets a nice matchup next week against the Panthers on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 5-of-8 targets for 37 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft was forced from the game in the second quarter after taking a scary hit to his thigh area that generated torsion on his knee while his foot was still planted. It was the opposite knee to the one he injured a season ago and the veteran tight end would miss only one drive before returning to the game after the half, providing a collective sigh of relief for fantasy managers that have tasted the despair of a major knee injury already. Kraft could be busy in Week 7 against the defense allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends when the Packers face off against the division rival Lions in a potential shootout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 5-of-5 targets for 64 yards in the Packers’ Week 5 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: The five-catch effort was Kraft’s second straight after previously having zero. His 54 yards were also his most since Week 1. His 46-yard reception in the third quarter was his longest of the season. All of that is good, though it was still somewhat disappointing amidst a 367-yard Jordan Love outburst where Christian Watson and Matthew Golden both eased by 100 yards. Kraft is averaging a pedestrian six targets. He’s going to need both more looks and big plays to remain a higher-end TE1. It will nevertheless be impossible to bench him for Week 6 against the Cowboys’ shaky defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 6-of-7 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 4 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Jordan Love made it a point to get Kraft going in this game, peppering him with easy-button targets throughout the contest. Kraft led the team with a 23 percent target share. His six grabs also led the team and are a new season high. He found the end zone with an impressive toe-dragging catch at the goal line. Kraft is still looking for the explosive play, but the team is getting him more involved every week. He is back in the TE1 ranks after a slow couple of weeks to start the season. Kraft will look to stay hot versus the Bears next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 4-of-8 targets for 26 yards in the Packers’ Week 3 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft has not yet looked himself after recovering from a torn ACL suffered in 2025, this time committing two drops for the first time in his career. To add additional context, Kraft has never had more than three drops in an entire season entering his fourth year in the league. The game plan clearly consisted of getting Kraft involved early to circumvent the offensive line struggles, but the connection with Jordan Love was off throughout. Kraft appears likely to need time to get back to full speed for the Packers, although his snaps and route participation rate were back to normal for the second consecutive week. Fantasy managers are likely forced to ride through the turbulence considering the state of the tight end position throughout the league, but he is a shaky start ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 2-of-3 targets for 15 yards in the Packers’ Week 2 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: The good news is that Kraft played 52 of the team’s 53 snaps and ran a route on 32 of their 34 dropbacks. The bad news is that he wasn’t commanding targets, and he also fumbled one of his catches, but the replay review couldn’t determine for sure who recovered it, so the Packers were able to maintain possession. Perhaps we should have been a little less aggressive in expecting Kraft to return from tearing his ACL less than a year ago and go right back to being himself at the start of the season. His role remains elite, but it may take another couple of weeks before he’s physically able to play like we’re used to seeing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 3-of-6 targets for 65 yards in the Packers’ Week 1 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft, who tore his ACL in Week 9 last year, told reporters he would not be on a snap count in Week 1. He was. Kraft ran 20 routes to Jonnu Smith’s 18. The good news is that Kraft looked as explosive as ever, racking up gains of 30, 23, and 12 yards. Even with the weak route rate, this goes down as a win for a player whose game is built around big plays. His route rate should climb in the coming weeks, keeping him in the TE1 mix versus the Jets next Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Packers signed TE Tucker Kraft to a four-year, $75 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: The news was first reported by ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Kraft’s deal, which runs through the 2030 season, has a maximum value of $92 million and includes a $26.5 million signing bonus. He’s now the NFL’s highest-paid tight end. Kraft had 32 receptions, 489 yards and six touchdowns before tearing his ACL in Week 9 last year. Not on the injury report for Week 1, Kraft is a surefire TE1 even in a tough matchup against the Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: AJ Barner caught 2-of-4 targets for seven yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 9 win over the Cardinals, adding three yards and a touchdown on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: Barner kicked off the scoring in the second quarter with a tight end sneak from one yard out, adding a second score on the following possession on a beautiful, fingertip grab in the flat from seven yards out. Quarterback Drew Lock delivered the football late and behind the veteran tight end, the latter of whom adjusted in the face of suffocating pressure to pluck the football from the air and hold on through the ground for the touchdown. Barner remains highly unlikely to see consistent weekly volume in this Seattle offense, but fantasy managers can benefit from high variance touchdowns every so often.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: AJ Barner caught 2-of-5 targets for 23 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: Barner is far from fantasy consideration having only one game through eight appearances with more than a modest five targets while failing to notch a single receiving touchdown. Fantasy managers can safely return him to the waiver wire in all formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: AJ Barner caught 4-of-5 targets for 42 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 7 win over the Chiefs, adding four yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: All three carries for Barner were tush push plays that resulted in first downs in key situations, while his five targets tied his second most of the young season. Even so, that was not enough to return a usable fantasy week outside of tight end premium leagues, keeping Barner best left on the bench or returned to the waiver wire, regardless of the severity of Rashid Shaheed’s injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: AJ Barner caught 3-of-5 targets for 20 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 5 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: Barner continues to be a non-factor in the Seahawks’ passing game. Outside of a Week 3 game against the Commanders in which he went for 5-69-0 on nine targets, Barner has totaled 53 yards in his other four games combined and has yet to find the end zone this season. Barner won’t be on the streaming radar in Week 6, even with four teams on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: AJ Barner caught 1-of-3 targets for 12 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 4 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: After a solid effort against the the Commanders where he caught five passes for 69 yards, Barner was once again a non-factor in this one. The 24-year-old is clearly the top tight end in the passing attack, but outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the rest of the options just haven’t done much. He’ll be a boom or bust TE1 for Week 5 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: AJ Barner caught 5-of-9 targets for 69 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 3 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: It was easily Barner’s best receiving day of the year, although he was unable to find the end zone. His nine targets were second on the team behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s 14, and it’s clear he and Sam Darnold have more of a connection than he did with Drew Lock. Barner will be on the TE1 precipice for Week 4 against the Chargers, but this was encouraging.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: AJ Barner caught 1-of-1 targets for eight yards in the Seahawks’ Week 2 win over the Cardinals, adding one rush for one yard and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: Up 24-7 on 4th-and-goal with just over three minutes left in the game, the Seahawks started a fresh set of downs from the Cardinals’ three-yard line. Both RB George Holani and RB Emanuel Wilson were given chances to punch it in before Seahawks OC Brian Fleury dialed up a Tush Push play for Barner on 4th-and-goal. Barner jumped up and across the line, bringing his fantasy stat line from something unusable to something we can live with. He remains a boom-bust TE1 against the Commanders next week. Seahawks TE2 Elijah Arroyo nabbed a 17-yard pass on a post route, but that was it for him. So far, the Seahawks’ reported uptick in usage for the tight end position has not panned out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: A.J. Barner caught both of his targets for 13 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 1 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: Barner also had a tush push attempt that was called back by a penalty. With Jaxon Smith-Njigba soaking up 11 targets on just 24 team pass attempts, there wasn’t much volume to go around for the rest of the Seattle pass-catchers. Barner only topped four catches in 20 combined regular and postseason appearances last year. If Week 1 is any indication, he won’t be putting up big box scores very often this season either. He will barely crack the TE2 ranks when Seattle takes on Arizona next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: Seahawks TE AJ Barner (oblique) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: The Seahawks’ starting tight end is firmly on track to play in the 2026 season opener on Wednesday night. Barner is reportedly set to handle a bigger role than he did last year, when he finished as the PPR TE14. He can only be viewed as a borderline TE1/2 early on, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: The Athletic’s Andrew Destin believes Seahawks TE AJ Barner “will likely see an uptick in production, as should backup TE Elijah Arroyo” this year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: Destin notes that new Seahawks OC Brian Fleury served as the 49ers’ TE coach for four seasons “and is expected to feature the position prominently.” Aside from that, and an increase in shifts and motion, he thinks the offense is “going to look very similar” to last year. Barner underwent two offseason surgeries, one of which was to address a nagging ankle injury that Barner said he initially suffered during the 2024 Senior Bowl before the Seahawks drafted him. After turning in the PPR TE14 performance last season, Barner might have a shot to crack the position’s top 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Cooper Kupp caught 3-of-4 targets for 32 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 9 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Backup quarterback Drew Lock attempted only 28 passes on a night their defense held the Cardinals to under 200 yards of total offense, leaving little more than scraps for Kupp, despite the absence of Rashid Shaheed. Further uncertainty persists given the multi-game injury to starting quarterback Sam Darnold and the oblique injury sustained by Lock, with the offense potentially helmed by Jalen Milroe when they face the Raiders in Week 10. Kupp remains far from the fantasy radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Cooper Kupp caught 1-of-3 targets for seven yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp was unable to take advantage of the absence of fellow receiver Rashid Shaheed but did cash in for his second touchdown of the season. Kupp’s days of consistent fantasy production are long behind him as the Seahawks head into a Week 9 divisional meeting against the Cardinals approaching must-win territory.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Cooper Kupp caught both targets for 20 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 7 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp saw sparse usage as Jaxon Smith-Njigba went off in the first half and the team transitioned to a run-heavy approach while playing with a lead after the break. Fellow receiver Rashid Shaheed departed with a knee injury following a collision with Smith-Njigba in the end zone at the end of the second quarter, which is something managers will will want to monitor ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Bears on Monday Night Football. Kupp could work his way into the FLEX discussion if Shaheed misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Cooper Kupp caught 5-of-10 targets for 50 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp’s 10 targets finished second on the team behind alpha Jaxon Smith-Njigba but were largely a product of 51 Sam Darnold pass attempts in game that had all the ingredients for increased pass volume, including an inability to run the football, negative game script, and overtime. It continues to appear as if Kupp’s fantasy-relevant days are far behind him, with the veteran best left on the waiver wire ahead of a Week 7 showdown against the Chiefs on deck.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Cooper Kupp caught 4-of-5 targets for 46 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 3 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp took advantage of the Commanders double-teaming Jaxon Smith-Njigba and walked into the end zone on the fourth touchdown throw from Sam Darnold. It’s his first score of the season, and it’s a season high in receiving yards for the former star. Kupp will try and build on this in Week 4 in a matchup against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp will be available for QB Sam Darnold (glute), who makes his return from his Week 1 injury. Kupp is a mild FLEX option, facing a soft Commanders’ coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp will not be fantasy-relevant in 12-team managed leagues this week, but he could be an option in single-game DFS tournaments. If QB Sam Darnold (glute) can play, he will appreciate having Kupp on the field with him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp also opened last week with a limited practice due to the back injury before getting in two full practices and playing in Week 2. His limited designation Wednesday is likely a continuation of veteran workload management for his back; fantasy managers should not be surprised to see the 33-year-old limited on Wednesdays this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Cooper Kupp caught 2-of-2 targets for 20 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 2 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp got involved on the Seahawks’ fifth and sixth drives, but was quiet outside of that. The 33-year-old wide receiver entered the game with a back injury, though he logged two full practice sessions, so it is unlikely to have meaningfully impacted him. He nabbed his second reception during the Seahawks’ two-minute drill at the end of the first half, but he was unable to get out of bounds, allowing precious seconds to tick away. Kupp is a WR5/FLEX against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) is not on the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp, 33, is good to go against the Cardinals. He was limited on Wednesday, but upgraded to full on Thursday and Friday. With QB Drew Lock under center, Kupp’s outlook is a little more volatile. He should be viewed as just a boom-bust FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 7-of-10 targets for 51 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 9 win over he Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: The fact that 54 yards is something to talk about says enough about the year Smith-Njigba is having, still handily leading the league in receiving despite the down performance. He remained the clear top dog through the air, receiving 10 targets on only 28 Lock pass attempts, largely confined to short area work as the Seahawks struggled to decipher the zone-heavy and two-high-heavy Arizona defense. Lock suffered an oblique injury in the third quarter that could place his Week 10 status in doubt, despite not missing an offensive snap, meaning fantasy managers of Smith-Njigba will want to monitor the situation ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Raiders considering Sam Darnold remains unlikely to play with a multi-week injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 6-of-11 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba was the entire offense in the first half, accumulating 92 yards through the air while the rest of the offense managed only two, including his receiving touchdown. Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen made adjustments after the break that confined JSN to only 26 additional yards the rest of the way. Smith-Njigba now has seven 100-yard receiving games in eight appearances as he extended his league-leading yardage totals, far and away the top overall wide receiver in fantasy circles. That position will not change ahead of a Week 9 meeting with the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 9-of-12 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 7 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Is there anyone in the league doing it better than Smith-Njigba at the moment? The reigning receiving leader put on an absolute show in this one, making two nearly identical bread basket catches down the left sideline in the second quarter, the first of which he snuck inside the pylon for his touchdown. He was forced out at the two on the second, resulting in an end zone interception from Sam Darnold two plays later. Those two long receptions before the break helped push Smith-Njigba to 126 yards and a touchdown before halftime, and he added an additional 24 yards on three more receptions in the final two frames as the Seahawks transitioned to a more ground-heavy attack while playing with the lead. Fantasy’s early-season cheat code has now gone over 100 yards in six of seven games while notching a league-leading eight receiving touchdowns. It goes without saying, but Smith-Njigba remains the overall WR1 in a solid matchup against the Bears in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 12-of-16 targets for 134 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba overcame a sluggish first half to extend his stranglehold on the overall WR1 in fantasy circles with a dominant second half and overtime period. While the 51 pass attempts from Sam Darnold were highly uncharacteristic of this Seattle offense, a complete inability to run the football paired with a negative script to form the perfect environment for Smith-Njigba to set a season high in targets and receptions. Smith-Njigba has now gone over 100 yards in five of six appearances to start the 2026 regular season and is in a good spot to continue that dominance when the Seahawks host the Chiefs in Week 7, where he remains a top-tier WR1 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) has no injury designation ahead of the Seahawks’ Week 6 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba played through an ankle injury in Week 5 and was limited in practice this week before getting a full designation on Wednesday. Despite the short week ahead of a Thursday matchup against the Broncos, he is off the injury report and good to go. Smith-Njigba is once again a top-three wide receiver option for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) was listed as a limited practice participant on Tuesday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba gets a second-straight “limited” practice designation. The Seahawks have technically not practiced yet this week but it is notably the 24-year-old receiver gets back-to-back limited designations. With a Thursday matchup against the Broncos on the horizon for Week 6, the Seahawks are leaving the door open for Smith-Njigba to play; he battled the ankle injury in Week 5 and the short week makes this a tougher evaluation. For now, we still expect Smith-Njigba to play against the Broncos on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Seahawks listed Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: With the Seahawks preparing to face the Broncos on a short week, it would be a bit more concerning if JSN were listed as a DNP. The team listing him as limited on the first day of the week is encouraging after he clearly battled through an ankle injury in Week 5’s loss to the 49ers. Smith-Njigba still topped 100 receiving yards for the fourth time this season and made several big plays despite being in visible pain. We’ll continue to update his practice status throughout the week, but as long as he’s active come Thursday, JSN should be in your fantasy lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 5-of-8 targets for 102 yards and one touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 5 loss to the 49ers, adding one rush for 16 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: JSN appeared to be playing through a bit of an ankle injury in this one, but he looked perfectly fine when he turned what would have been a short two-yard reception upfield for a 16-yard touchdown in the third quarter. In the fourth quarter, as the Seahawks were attempting a comeback, JSN hauled in a 35-yard reception, evading multiple defenders to get the Seahawks to the 50-yard line. A few plays later, he would drop a wide-open pass that may have set the Seahawks up for a game-winning field goal opportunity, but JSN did his part to keep the Seahawks in what proved to be a sloppy game for the offense as a whole. He’s gone for 100-plus yards in four of his first five games of the season and will look for his fifth 100-yard game on Thursday night when the Seahawks visit the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 5-of-6 targets for 78 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 4 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: For the first time this year, Smith-Njigba was held out of the end zone. It was a quiet day fore the star wideout, but if 78 yards is your worst day (so far), well, you’ve had a pretty good season. JSN and fantasy managers will hope for a return to the end zone and a little more volume against the 49ers in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 10-of-14 targets for 128 yards and two touchdowns in the Seahawks’ Week 3 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Goodness gracious. Smith-Njigba did have a drop, but it was yet another dominant effort for the 24-year-old. His first touchdown saw him fake a fade route only to comeback to the pylon for an easy six, and then he and Sam Darnold connected for a second time on a pass over the middle in the end zone. That’s already six touchdowns in three games for the 24-year-old, and he’s reached the century mark in all three contests. On top of that, he also completed a 14-yard pass. Asking for this kind of red-zone production every week is tough, but he’s more than capable of these kind of fireworks. Obviously. JSN will be a WR1 and then some for Week 4 against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Jadarian Price rushed nine times for 24 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 9 win over the Cardinals, adding 54 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price’s 13 opportunities lagged the 18 of Zach Charbonnet in what is developing into a true 60-40 split between him and the veteran, and while the 54 yards through the air were impressive, Price appears to need consistent aerial production to sustain his fantasy value moving forward while playing on the wrong side of a timeshare. Hopefully he can improve upon the modest 2.7 yards per carry he notched against the Cardinals when the Seahawks take on the sliding Raiders in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Jadarian Price rushed 10 times for 29 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears, adding eight yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: It was Zach Charbonnet that drew the start for the Seahawks in his first game since tearing his ACL last year, but it was the talented rookie that led the team in opportunities. Price was making his first appearance since going on the injured reserve with a chest injury suffered in Week 2, and while he led the team in yardage and carries, George Holani remained involved in clear passing situations and Charbonnet is liable to see his role continue to grow with each healthy game. Price will be a shaky FLEX option in a better matchup against the Cardinals in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Seahawks plan to activate Jadarian Price from injured reserve and that he will play in Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price and Zach Charbonnet will both make their returns from injured reserve tonight, putting the Seahawks’ backfield at full strength heading into a pivotal NFC matchup. It’s hard to know how the touches will be spread out in this one, which makes both backs hard to trust on Monday night against the Bears. Price averaged 11.5 carries per game in his two full games played this season, but Charbonnet should eat into that somewhat. Fantasy managers looking to play either Seattle running back in this one should temper expectations until we have more data to go on in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Seahawks removed Jadarian Price (chest) from the injury report Saturday and he is expected to play in Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: The team has yet to activate him from injured reserve, a procedural move that is expected to come before they take the field in Week 8 against the Bears on Monday Night Football. Zach Charbonnet is also expected to be activated from injured reserve, giving the team their top two backs for the first time this season. No word yet on an expected snap count for either, although Price would seem to be in line to serve as the top option in the backfield considering it will be Charbonnet’s season debut.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Jadarian Price (chest) was upgraded to “full” for Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price was upgraded to full while Zach Charbonnet (knee) was downgraded to limited. That is probably part of a pre-planned process with Charbonnet, but as of Friday evening, we suppose Price is now technically closer to returning than his veteran backfield mate. As it is, both players now seem more likely than not to suit up, which would make for an extremely chaotic fantasy situation with Emanuel Wilson still in the fold. With the Seahawks playing on Monday evening, we will receive official game designations Saturday afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Jadarian Price (chest) was a limited participant during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price gets in the limited session after coach Mike Macdonald said that it was realistic that the tailback could be back Monday night against the Bears in Week 8. Zach Charbonnet was a full participant Thursday, so the Seattle backfield could finally be at full strength — or close to it, anyway — for the stretch. That’s nice for the Seahawks, but creates a lot of confusion from a fantasy perspective.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said it’s “realistic” that Jadarian Price (chest/IR) could return in Week 8.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: With Zach Charbonnet’s status also in some doubt, Seattle’s backfield situation likely won’t be sorted out until Saturday (or MNF inactives), but if Price is back that’s probably the end of Emmanuel Wilson’s short-term RB2 ride. We’ll keep an eye on the situation. Wilson-reliant managers might want to consider alternative arrangements for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Seahawks coach Mike MacDonald said the team would designate Jadarian Price (chest) to return from injured reserve this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price has missed the minimum four games and being immediately designated to return should have him making his debut sooner rather than later. Of course, with Zach Charbonnet also returning to the fold soon, this could be a split backfield rather than the RB2 zone that Price looked to be opening the year in. Price probably will only reach the FLEX ranks when active until we see what the touch counts look like; perhaps he could have a Blake Corum-ish role if all goes well for the Seahawks offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Seahawks placed RB Jadarian Price (chest) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price reportedly aggravated a chest injury during the team’s Wednesday practice and will now miss the next four games, at minimum, as he tends to the injury. The backfield will be left in the hands of Emanuel Wilson and George Holani in Week 4 against the Chargers but should get reinforcements in short order with Zach Charbonnet set to resume practicing. Price’s season continues to trend poorly for fantasy managers that invested a mid-round pick in his services this summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Seahawks rule out Jadarian Price (chest) for Week 4 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price reportedly aggravated his chest injury on Wednesday. That is unfortunate. With Price out of the picture against the Chargers, and Zach Charbonnet (knee) still rehabbing, burly RB Emanuel Wilson and receiving specialist RB George Holani will split backfield reps. Wilson can be started as a volume-based RB2/FLEX while Holani is FLEX-viable in PPR formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet rushed 16 times for 77 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 9 win over the Cardinals, adding nine yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet served as the clear lead back against an inferior Cardinals team, handling 16 carries and two targets to the nine carries and four targets of rookie Jadarian Price. The roughly 60-40 split between the two is likely closer to what to expect for the remainder of the season now that Charbonnet has another game under his belt coming off the 2025 torn ACL. The fantasy returns could be much greater against arguably the worst defense in the league at present, with Charbonnet inching closer to weekly FLEX status ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet rushed six times for 23 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears, adding six yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet drew the start but saw four fewer opportunities than rookie Jadarian Price, the latter of whom led the team in rush yards and touches. Expect the two to continue operating in a near-even timeshare moving forward, leaving Charbonnet in shaky FLEX territory ahead of a Week 9 meeting with the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) and Jadarian Price (chest) are active for Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet makes his season debut after a suffering a torn ACL late in the 2025 season while Price returns from short-term injure reserve due to a chest injury. Emmanuel Wilson and George Holani had held down the backfield in the absence of the two top backs, leaving an uncertain situation regarding expected backfield utilization when the Seahawks take on the Bears in a marquee matchup. Inactive for the Seahawks are QB Drew Lock, LB Uchenna Nwosu, WR Rashid Shaheed, RB Velus Jones Jr., OT Charles Cross, G Beau Stephens, and NT Brandon Pili.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Seahawks plan to activate Jadarian Price from injured reserve and that he will play in Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Price and Zach Charbonnet will both make their returns from injured reserve tonight, putting the Seahawks’ backfield at full strength heading into a pivotal NFC matchup. It’s hard to know how the touches will be spread out in this one, which makes both backs hard to trust on Monday night against the Bears. Price averaged 11.5 carries per game in his two full games played this season, but Charbonnet should eat into that somewhat. Fantasy managers looking to play either Seattle running back in this one should temper expectations until we have more data to go on in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) is expected to be active for Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: The team has yet to activate Charbonnet from injured reserve but removed him from the injury report Saturday, leaving only the procedural step in the way of his season debut. He likely returns to a limited role as the team manages his reps in his first game since tearing his ACL in 2025. Rookie Jadarian price is also expected to play after being removed from the injury report. He, too, will need to be activated from injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) was downgraded to “limited” for Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: It’s not particularly concerning — this is probably part of a pre-established practice plan as Charbonnet completes his injury comeback — but Jadarian Price’s Friday return to full practice certainly has our attention. Now even if Charbonnet does manage to make his 2026 debut on Monday evening against the Bears, he could have even more company in Seattle’s crowded backfield. Both backs returning would make all three of Charbonnet, Price and Emanuel Wilson shaky FLEX plays. We will receive official game designations on Saturday afternoon. Until then, hang tight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) was a full participant during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: It’s obviously a positive development for Charbonnet, who appears to be on track for his season debut against the Bears in Week 8. Fantasy managers just have to keep in mind that the rug was pulled from underneath last week when the Seahawks ruled the tailback out late in the week. Jadarian Price (chest) was a limited participant, but fantasy managers who want to use a Seattle tailback on Monday night won’t have clarity until Saturday at the earliest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald declined to say whether or not Zach Charbonnet (knee) would play in Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Macdonald said the team will continue to stick to their plan regarding Charbonnet’s return. The 25-year-old running back was activated from the PUP list last week, only to be ruled out before the weekend as the Seahawks were preparing to face the Chiefs. It’s worth noting that Charbonnet was a full participant in practice last week, so we would assume he will log another full week of practices this week. Should the Seahawks opt to sideline Charbonnet next week, Emanuel Wilson would again assume the role as lead back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks declared RB Zach Charbonnet, QB Drew Lock, LB Drake Thomas, RB Robert Henry Jr., LB Chazz Surratt, LB Connor O’Toole, and G Beau Stevens inactive for Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Lock will serve as the emergency quarterback while the team will have to wait another week for the season debut of Zach Charbonnet. The Seahawks look to make up ground in the NFC West following the loss from the 49ers against one of two remaining undefeated teams in the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks ruled out Zach Charbonnet (knee) for Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that Charbonnet has not suffered a setback. He just isn’t ready yet. Many teams might rush a player of his caliber back, now that he is practicing in full, but the Seahawks are smartly taking the long view with Charbonnet’s health. Emanuel Wilson will function as the team’s leading rusher while George Holani plays on passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson rushed eight times for 21 yards in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints, adding three catches for 27 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Per usual, Sampson did the bulk of his damage through the air, especially in PPR leagues. He saw six targets compared to just one for Quinshon Judkins. Sampson’s role is good for a few weekly PPR points, but his lack of rushing production makes a ceiling outcome almost impossible. He’ll be a viable RB4 fantasy option when the Browns take on the Texans next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson caught six passes for 62 yards in the Browns’ Week 8 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Sampson only had one carry in this game, gaining seven yards, but he was third on the team in targets and second on the team in receiving yards. Early reports show that he played 11 more snaps than Quinson Judkins and ran a route on 29 of the team’s 49 dropbacks, compared to seven for Judkins. Sampson is very clearly the pass-catching back in Cleveland, and a good one too. If this team is going to be trailing often, he’ll have PPR value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Sampson got in two full sessions to close out the week and should be a low-end RB3/FLEX play in limited snaps against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: He played last week just fine, so it seems like he was just given a bit of a breather on Wednesday during a limited session. Sampson should handle 5-10 touches for the Browns on Sunday against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: The Browns’ No. 2 running back played through his knee injury effectively last week, totaling 79 scrimmage yards and three receptions against the Titans. He should be expected to continue playing productively on his limited workload moving forward. He is not a must-start player in Week 8 against the Steelers, but he belongs in the FLEX conversation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson had six rushes for 45 yards in the Browns’ Week 7 win against the Titans, adding three catches for 34 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: In his first action of 2026, Sampson looked spry and explosive as the Browns’ No. 2 back behind Quinshon Judkins, who totaled over 100 yards and scored two touchdowns on the day. Sampson, meanwhile, logged more pass routes and targets than Judkins. It would appear Sampson is the next guy up in the Cleveland backfield if Judkins misses time in the coming weeks. He should be rostered in most 12-team leagues as a bench stash.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Browns activated RB Dylan Sampson (knee) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Sampson was limited in practice throughout the week and listed as questionable for Week 7 against the Titans. Now that he’s officially been activated from injured reserve, he’s likely to be Cleveland’s change-of-pace back behind Quinshon Judkins this week. Sampson is worth stashing on fantasy benches, but is truly just a desperation FLEX play coming off a knee injury that’s sidelined him since Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee/IR) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 7 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: If active, he will be a change-up back for Quinshon Judkins, who is not carrying a status this week. Coming off a long-term injury, it would be a real leap of faith to put Sampson in a FLEX role this week, even against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: The Browns could get their receiving specialist back in the lineup this week, though it would be nice to see him practice fully tomorrow. Sampson injured his knee while returning a kickoff in Week 1 against the Jaguars and has been sidelined ever since.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Browns coach Todd Monken indicated earlier today that Sampson has a chance to return from injured reserve in time to face the Titans on Sunday. The Browns’ skill position corps is banged up and could use an explosive player. Sampson might end up warranting FLEX treatment right off the bat, if he is active this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports that the Colts informed Daniel Jones that they are not trading him by Tuesday’s deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones successfully returned from last year’s season-ending Achilles tendon rupture, but his play has been negatively impacted by it. With two young quarterbacks on the roster, it would seemingly make sense to trade Jones to get an extended look at either Riley Leonard and/or Anthony Richardson. Apparently, the Colts disagree. We have no way of knowing whether Pelissero’s report is a hardball negotiation tactic by the Colts’ front office, but we will have an answer to that question in the next couple of days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 20-of-34 passes for 180 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Colts’ 27-23, Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, adding 11 yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: The final score would have been much more lopsided if not for 14 accepted penalties from an undisciplined Cowboys team, something that allowed the Colts to surge back in the second half and take the lead with under two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter.
