The efforts would prove fruitless as they immediately let Dak Prescott connect with Ryan Flournoy on a 46-yard gain on the first play of the following possession, resulting in a Javonte Williams touchdown. A Jones pick on the next possession sealed the game and sent the Colts to a 2-7 record ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, with questions abound regarding the future of the franchise. Jones has been a name linked to numerous teams this week, the most of which is the Vikings following the hamstring injury sustained by Kyler Murray. More to come as the Colts enter a tear-it-down rebuild.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport believes the Vikings are “a team to watch” for Daniel Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Per Rapoport, the Ravens called Indy about Jones after Lamar Jackson went down with a potentially season-ending thumb injury. They eventually traded for Jacoby Brissett. With Kyler Murray hurt and playing poorly even when healthy, the Vikings are at least going to explore some outside options at quarterback. Jones was on the team’s practice squad in 2024 before joining the Colts last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Colts have told teams they aren’t trading QB Daniel Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Despite ESPN’s Adam Schefter trying to will a Jones trade into existence by recreating Brian Windhorst memes, Pelissero reports the Colts have informed teams they aren’t trading the 29-year-old quarterback. Jones is set to start against the Cowboys in Week 9, but could find himself on the bench once the Colts are eliminated from playoff contention given the injury guarantees for next season in his contract.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts have received calls from multiple teams about trading for QB Daniel Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Schefter passes along that the Ravens called the Colts about Jones before they acquired Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals. Otherwise, this report lacked specifics. According to league sources, multiple teams have called the Colts about trading for Jones, but he couldn’t name a team other than the Ravens. Schefter mentions the Vikings as a possibility, but while that suggestion makes sense given Minnesota’s need at quarterback and Jones’ history with the organization, it’s still purely speculation at this point. Jones is set to start against the Cowboys in Week 9, but isn’t on the fantasy radar outside of 2QB/superflex leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Daniel Jones “maybe wants to” be traded away from the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Fowler says that multiple sources around the league, including multiple sources inside the Colts’ organization, believe Jones “should be trying to get out of Indy, or maybe wants to.” The Colts are entering a rebuild, with trade rumors swirling around multiple star players. Fowler closed the segment by hinting at the Vikings as a possible landing spot. Jones’ fantasy-scoring outlook might tick up a little bit were he to head back to Minnesota.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Daniel Jones will start in Week 9 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: After taking some time to evaluate his quarterback room, Steichen has decided to stick with Jones, saying he believes Jones gives the Colts “the best chance to win right now.” Jones has struggled mightily in his second season with the Colts and is now sitting on a 1,542-5-9 passing line this season, and he tossed two picks in Week 8’s 42-7 blowout loss to the Jaguars. He was pulled in favor of Anthony Richardson late in the game, but he will get at least one more start against a woeful Cowboys defense that is fresh off blowing a 14-point fourth-quarter lead to the Cardinals in a comeback that was orchestrated by Gardner Minshew. With only two teams on bye this week, Jones is nothing more than a desperation streamer in 2QB/superflex leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Colts Shane Steichen said he is “going to evaluate everything, every position going forward.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: This is the first time this season that Steichen has left open the possibility of replacing Daniel Jones as the team’s official starter. Anthony Richardson replaced him in-game today, with just under 12 minutes remaining. It seems as though Richardson, or even fellow backup Riley Leonard, could end up playing next week against the Cowboys’ fantasy-friendly defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 19-of-28 passes for 144 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Colts’ 42-7, Week 8 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Distressingly, this has become something of a standard statline for Jones, who is now sitting on a 5:9 TD:INT ratio through eight starts. That being said, Jones would have piled up more garbage time yards had he not been benched for most of the fourth quarter with the Colts getting annihilated. Jones’ first interception was a 92-yard pick-six, though the “interception” was really more of a Tyler Warren drop. The same was not true of Jones’ second pick, which was simply an awful third quarter throw where he never saw LB Branson Combs in coverage. There is nothing left to see of Jones under center for the tanking/rebuilding Colts, but the problem is, the same is true of backups Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard. This is just a team that’s going to have to play out the string with things getting worse before they get better. That does not mean Jones will keep his starting job. It’s likely only a matter of time before Richardson gets one final look under center. That could come as early as Week 9 against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Colts haven’t discussed benching QB Daniel Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones received a vote of confidence from Colts HC Shane Steichen earlier this week and now there’s a report from prominent NFL Insider Pelissero that the organization hasn’t discussed benching him. While that’s all well and good, the Colts still seem like they’re in the early stages of a process that will likely end with benching Jones at some point this year. The fact that Pelissero mentioned Jones’ contract includes a $10.51 million injury guarantee for 2027 is an ominous sign. Once the 2-5 Colts are officially eliminated from playoff contention, Indianapolis won’t have much incentive to risk injury with the oft-injured Jones.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 10-of-10 targets for 164 yards and one touchdown in the Packers’ Week 9 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden appeared to be on pace for a historic performance after the first quarter. The second-year receiver hauled in two receptions of 40-plus yards, along with a five-yard touchdown, and ended the quarter with a 6-126-1 receiving line on six targets. Golden obviously didn’t sustain that pace for the remaining three quarters, but fantasy managers won’t be mad with the one highly productive quarter he offered up. Golden continues to dazzle in his second season and has now gone for 100-plus yards in four different games this season. He’s both a target hog and an air-yards king, which makes for a deadly combination as far as fantasy football is concerned. He will be a fringe WR1/WR2 next week against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 7-of-13 targets for 79 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden is rarely boring, that’s for sure. He dropped two passes, and one of those was a wide-open touchdown in the second quarter. The good news for Golden, Jordan Love and fantasy managers was that he was wide open again on the next play, and he was able to bring that pass in. Golden’s athleticism and ability to get down field is unquestionable, but to say the efficiency isn’t there is an understatement. He’ll be back at it in Week 9 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) is active for Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden got in a lone limited session in preparation for the team’s Week 8 meeting with the Panthers on a short week, ultimately able to go as he looks to continue his recent hot stretch in fantasy production. No limitation in expected role has been passed by the team, meaning Golden should be good to go for a normal workload against the Panthers. Fantasy managers can confidently insert him into Week 8 rosters as an upside WR2. Inactive for the Packers are TE Jonnu Smith, RB Kaleb Johnson, LB Zaire Franklin, G Donovan Jennings, C Sean Rhyan, and G Travis Glover.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) is “trending toward playing” in Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden was estimated as a DNP for two walkthroughs this week before being limited in the Packers’ only real session. The short turnaround to Thursday Night Football likely forced the Packers to take an extra cautious approach with him in practice. While he almost certainly isn’t at 100 percent, Golden looks like a good bet to play in a sneaky shootout with the Panthers tonight. He will be on the WR1/2 border if he gets the green light.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) is questionable for Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: The Packers held two walkthrough practices to start the week. Golden was estimated as a DNP for both. He was limited in the team’s final practice before being hit with the questionable tag. Fantasy managers should treat him as a true game-time decision for tomorrow’s game. Savion Williams has been operating as the team’s No. 3 receiver over the past two weeks. He would presumably be the next man up if Golden can’t go, though Williams would still be a high-risk FLEX bet for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said the team is “still working through it” when asked if WR Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) will play Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: ESPN’s Rob Demovsky relayed LaFleur’s noncommittal response to questions on Golden’s status. LaFleur said the team hopes Golden plays, but the 23-year-old has been an estimated DNP for the first two practices of the week due to shoulder and foot injuries. With the Packers playing on a short week against the Panthers, Golden’s status will likely rely on the final practice report before a Week 8 Thursday showdown against Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: This does not have us optimistic that Golden will play on Thursday night. If he’s sidelined, Savion Williams will be a candidate for more work on offense and perhaps a worthwhile FLEX streamer, while Tucker Kraft will likely ascend to the No. 2 role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Packers listed Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) as a DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden has been dealing with the shoulder injury since last week, but the foot injury is a new one. While this is only an estimated injury report, the DNP is still mildly concerning for Golden, with the Packers playing on a short week. His status will be one to monitor in the coming days, but hopefully this is a minor issue. Golden played the entirety of the game in Week 7’s loss to the Lions and didn’t appear to be hampered by any nagging issues. We’ll see if he get upgraded to a limited participant on Tuesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 6-of-12 targets for 39 yards in the Packers’ Week 7 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden’s 12 targets led all Packers receivers, but the speedster was unable to convert them into anything meaningful. Of the 12 targets Golden saw, four came on passes of 20-plus air yards. He managed to secure one of those passes for a 22-yard gain, but that was all he could manage in what ended up being a relatively low-scoring game despite the two teams combining for over 700 offensive yards. The 39 yards Golden posted on Sunday were good for his second-lowest total of the season, but he’s an air-yards king who is seeing the kind of volume we expect of a true WR1. He’s primed for a bounce-back in next week’s game against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: A few Packers got a little banged up against the Cowboys last week, including Golden, but the breakout second-year wide receiver is good to go. This game profiles as a fantasy-friendly shootout. Golden should be started as a high-end WR2 with solid upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 7-of-8 targets for 171 yards and one touchdown in the Packers’ Week 9 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson and fellow receiver Matthew Golden combined to catch 14 passes for 335 yards and two touchdowns, as both receivers attacked downfield at will against an overmatched Patriots secondary. Watson saw four of his seven receptions go for 20-plus yards, and found the end zone on a 39-yard touchdown in the third quarter, one play after the Packers’ defense forced a turnover. Watson has now gone for 100-plus yards in back-to-back weeks and has four games of 100-plus-yard performances on his resumé this season. He draws a tough Week 10 matchup against the Vikings and will be in the mix as a high-end WR2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson is off the injury report for Week 9 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson got in a pair of limited practices after leaving in Week 8 against the Panthers with a rib injury that required a trip to the hospital. The 6-foot-4 wideout is a WR1 for the upcoming battle against New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (rib) was limited during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: It’s back-to-back limited sessions for Watson. It’ll likely be a pain-tolerance issue for the wideout, but assuming he doesn’t suffer a setback in practice, he appears to be good for Week 9 against the Patriots and deserves WR1 consideration.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (rib) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson famously left for the hospital in the middle of Week 8’s win over the Panthers, only to return after halftime like a WWE performer. The fact that they’re letting him practice in any capacity today means he should be able to play through the issue in Week 9. We’d expect him to wear a flak jacket for at least a few weeks. Barring a setback in practice, Watson will be a high-variance WR1 for his matchup with the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 8-of-10 targets for 113 yards in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The fact that Watson was able to even play in the second half was incredible, as the 27-year-old was forced to be examined at the hospital following a chest injury. He didn’t do much after putting up 100 yards in the first half, but again, that’s not really the story here. Watson told reporters after the game that he was coughing up blood and suffered a fractured rib before returning. Assuming no setbacks, he’s a WR1 candidate for Week 9 against the Patriots, but keep in mind Christian Gonzalez — on top of this injury — can make things difficult.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (chest) returned to action in Week 8 against the Panthers in the third quarter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson went to the hospital to have his chest injury examined, but obviously checked out well if the Packers were willing to reinsert him into a game where they were leading by two scores. It’s a sigh of relief for fantasy managers, as Watson has been sensational Thursday night with six catches for 100 yards in just one half thus far.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson is questionable to return in Week 8 against the Panthers with a chest injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson was hurt on a deep pass in the middle of the second quarter, and went to the locker room to be evaluated and will head to the hospital to be further examined. The 27-year-old was playing well prior to the injury with six catches for 100 yards on his seven targets. Matthew Golden will be the primary wideout target for Jordan Love if Watson can’t return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (ankle) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson remained limited through the first two practices this week. We do not yet know his Friday participation level, but he seems to be ready for action. Watson belongs in the WR1 tier against a Lions’ pass defense that has freely surrendered big plays this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson appears to just be being managed at this point as Matt LaFleur said there are no concerns on him playing in Week 7. Two limited sessions are often a starting point for a questionable listing, but we’d be surprised if it got that far with Watson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Matt LaFleur said he has no concerns about Christian Watson’s ankle injury ahead of the Packers’ Week 7 game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The same is true of Matthew Golden, who is dealing with a shoulder issue. Both players were estimated as limited participants for Wednesday’s walkthrough. It doesn’t look like either wideout is at risk of missing the Packers’ upcoming shootout with Detroit. Watson is currently fifth in the league in receiving yards at 538. Golden is sixth at 501. Both players hold a spot in the WR1 ranks heading into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins rushed 15 times for 43 yards in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Judkins was hit at or behind the line of scrimmage constantly, resulting in a dreadful yards per carry of 2.9. This was particularly painful for fantasy managers when he got near the end zone. Judkins was stuffed from the one- and three-yard line on separate drives. He also ceded receiving work to Dylan Sampson. Judkins was targeted once while Sampson saw six opportunities through the air. Without receiving work to buoy his poor rushing days, Judkins is tumbling down the RB2 ranks. He’ll be on the RB2/3 border for his Week 10 matchup with the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins rushed 11 times for 25 yards in the Browns’ Week 8 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Judkins added two catches on just two targets for 24 yards. The Browns’ offense could get nothing going against the Steelers’ defense, and the Browns’ offensive line was pushed around all day. Judkins also had two carries from inside the five-yard line, including a carry from the one-yard line with 22 seconds left, but he couldn’t convert on either. The Browns should have a bit of an easier time moving the ball against the Saints next week, but if Judkins has a good day, that might be the chance to trade him away. Judkins actually played 11 fewer snaps than Dylan Sampson in this one with the Browns trailing all game, so that gives Judkins a low fantasy floor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins had 17 rushes for 96 yards and two touchdowns in the Browns’ Week 7 win against the Titans, adding one catch for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Judkins took full advantage of a Titans defense that has struggled to stop the run in recent weeks. He broke tackles on a couple of his longest runs and made decisive cuts in the open field on well-designed rushing attempts. It was Judkins’ second career 100-yard day and his second and third touchdowns of the season. Dylan Sampson, in his first action of the 2026 season, saw six carries for 45 yards and ran 19 routes to 13 routes for Judkins. As long as game script remains neutral or positive, Judkins should be a viable flex play in Week 8 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: He should carry his usual load in a good matchup against the Titans. That will put Judkins in the mid-to-low RB2 range this week, even with Dylan Sampson getting a chance to come back off injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Yesterday, Browns coach Todd Monken said he was “optimistic” about Judkins’ Week 7 availability. He has a chance to face the Titans this week, after sitting out in Week 6 against the Ravens, but it would be great to resume practicing in full tomorrow. If active, Judkins could be limited to a run-centric role, with Sampson also technically being on track to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Earlier today, Browns coach Todd Monken said he was “optimistic” about Judkins’ availability for Week 7 against the Titans. Today’s limited session puts him on track to play, though it would be nice to see him practice in full. If active, he would be a FLEX starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said he’s “optimistic” Quinshon Judkins (ankle) will play in Week 7 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Monken sounded like Judkins and Dylan Sampson will be active and ready to go against Tennessee. Judkins had been the locked-in lead back for Cleveland before his Week 5 ankle injury, seeing 71 percent of the team’s designed rushing attempts. The potential return of Sampson, a good pass catcher, could complicate things for Judkins’ involvement in the pass game going forward. Judkins will be a touchdown-dependent flex play against a Titans defense allowing the NFL’s ninth lowest rushing success rate in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) will not play in Week 6 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Judkins tested out his ankle in pregame warmups, with the team deciding afterward that he would not play in this AFC North battle with the Ravens. With backup Dylan Sampson still sidelined and Raheim Sanders (hip) on injured reserve, the Browns will look to Jaleel McLaughlin and the recently signed Audric Estime to lead their backfield in Week 6. This is looking like a backfield to avoid for this week, but McLaughlin could have some value in deeper leagues. The Browns also ruled QB Taylen Green, CB Noah Igbinoghene, DT Mike Hall Jr., C Parker Brailsford, OG Teven Jenkins, and DT Mason Graham inactive for this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Quinshon Judkins (ankle) will work out pregame to determine his status for Week 6 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Per Rapoport, there is optimism that linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle) will be able to play this week. Judkins logged a single limited practice on Friday before being listed as questionable. The fact that the Browns are even letting him test the groin injury in warmups suggests he will miss at most one game. If he doesn’t suit up, the Browns would be down to Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime as their remaining options at running back. McLaughlin would be the better choice for fantasy managers, though this is largely a situation to avoid if possible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 6 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: He only got in a limited session on Friday, leaving us to conclude this is likely a true questionable situation. The viability of Jaleel McLaughlin as a FLEX play will probably be determined by if Judkins is active or not. It’s also possible Judkins plays on a pitch count. He’ll be a shaky low-end RB2 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 21-of-38 passes for 299 yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions in the Patriots’ 45-27, Week 9 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye’s three first-half interceptions but the Patriots in the hole early, but the defenses’ inability to limit explosive plays also didn’t do them any favors. The Patriots saw three of their first six drives end in interceptions, but Maye did what he could to keep the game within reach. He completed his first touchdown pass of the day to Rhamondre Stevenson, who broke free down field for the 30-yard score in the second quarter. and on the following drive, Maye would complete passes of 19 and 28 yards to set up Efton Chism for an eight-yard touchdown with less than three minutes to go in the half. His third and final touchdown would come on a 22-yard pass to Mack Hollins, but Maye and the Patriots were under duress all afternoon and struggled to keep up with a Packers offense that didn’t slow down until it pulled it’s starters late in the fourth quarter. Maye also took four sacks in this one and has now been sacked nine times in his last three games. He’ll look to bounce back next week against the Lions in Munich.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 16-of-20 passes for 199 yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots’ 24-19, Week 8 win over the Dolphins, adding eight rushes for five yards and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye’s two-yard touchdown run was a thing of beauty. The Patriots quarterback took off to the right side of the field, faking a pitch to Rhamondre Stevenson, which caused a Dolphins defender to fully bite on it, running right past Maye while the Patriots’ quarterback darted into the end zone. Maye’s first touchdown pass was thrown to Kyle Williams on a post route. It was well-placed, allowing Williams to secure the ball in stride just before entering the end zone. Maye later linked up with DeMario Douglas via play action for his second score. The Patriots’ quarterback is a QB1 against the Packers next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 24-of-31 passes for 321 yards, two touchdown, and one interception in the Patriots’ 30-24, Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 26 yards and a touchdown on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye and the Patriots struggled to tame an unrelenting Chicago pass rush and were unable to move the football on the ground effectively, two cariables that led to an early deficit against the Bears. Their first half possessions went turnover on downs, three-and-out, three-and-out, touchdown, interception before a wild series to end the second quarter. Caleb Williams led a touchdown drive that left only 14 seconds on the clock. After an 18-yard completion to A.J. Brown, just three seconds remained with the ball near midfield. That’s when Maye dumped the ball off to Rhamondre Stevenson in the flat underneath deep prevent coverage, and Stevenson did the rest on a touchdown that never should have happened to bring the game to a one-possession game. Maye’s other touchdown toss was a beautiful bread-basket throw to rookie tight end Eli Raridon up the seam, adding a score on a grit-play rushing touchdown early in the second quarter. It goes down as Maye’s fourth consecutive QB1 fantasy performance after starting the season leading the league in turnovers through three weeks. The 4-3 Patriots get a mini-bye ahead of a divisional meeting against the Dolphins in Week 8, where Maye will remain an upside QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 18-of-32 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns in the Patriots’ 26-19, Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye added four carries for 24 yards rushing. The three-score passing effort was his third in as many weeks, while he is now up to 11 total touchdowns during his three-game hot streak. Good stuff, though it could have been much better. Maye lost No. 2 receiver Romeo Doubs to an early shoulder injury after he housed a 42-yard touchdown, while returning “No. 1" A.J. Brown had a nightmarish day with 4-5 drops, including several long gains and a potential score or two. Pop Douglas also lost a fumble at the end of a long catch-and-run. Unfortunate, but Maye is at least playing well enough again that those miscues merely held back his final box score instead of ruining it. He now has a likely short-week shootout in Thursday’s Bears road tilt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 26-of-34 attempts for 374 yards and four touchdowns in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders, adding seven rushes for 25 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye had all day to operate in the pocket against a Raiders front seven that entered Week 5 with the league’s ninth highest pressure rate and fourth highest quick pressure rate. He attacked the Vegas secondary downfield from start to finish, hitting Kyle Williams and Pop Douglas for long touchdowns, and Williams for another long gain that put the Pats inside the five yard line. Maye’s rushing score came on a green scramble in the third quarter. Fully emerged from his early-season struggles, Maye is once again carving up opposing coverage units and causing fits with his scrambling ability. Maye, with eight total touchdowns over his past two outings, should be locked into lineups next week against a middling Jets secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 22-of-37 passes for 269 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in a 29-26, Week 4 win over the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye also added 53 yards rushing on eight carries. This was easily the best game of Maye’s season. The Bills had pressure in his face often, but Maye was frequently able to evade pass rushers and pick up chunk gains with his legs. When he did have time to throw, he ripped off big passes downfield and could have even had a bigger day after a potential 40+ yard pass slipped through Romeo Doubs’ hands in the fourth quarter. Maye did wince and grab his right shoulder on one hit, so that will be something to watch during practice this week, but we don’t expect him to miss any time. The bad news is that Maye figures to be without Mack Hollins (calf) in Week 5, and A.J. Brown (ankle) is not yet ready to return, so Maye will play with limited options next week against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Bills declared CB Christian Benford, WR Skyler Bell, OL Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL T.J. Sanders, OLB Mike Danna, and S Jalon Kilgore inactive for Week 4 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: No real surprises here. Benford was listed as questionable heading into the day, but he didn’t practice at all this week so he was never likely to play. Rookie Davison Igbinosun is likely to step into his spot opposite Maxwell Hairston, which makes the Bills young and inexperienced on the boundary. Perhaps Drake Maye could finally take advantage of that on the way to his first truly good fantasy game of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye (right shoulder) is practicing in full for Week 4 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: We are happy to see that the Patriots’ quarterback is practicing fully, but this is a new injury for Maye. He notably dealt with a throwing shoulder injury during the Patriots’ playoff run last season. His listing raises questions as to whether there might be a lingering issue. We expect a follow-up report on this in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: The Athletic’s Chad Graff believes Drake Maye’s confidence is “shot.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye, after another meltdown in Week 3 against the Jaguars, has now posted a negative drop back EPA in six dtraight outings dating back to last season. Against Jacksonville on Sunday he posted a meager 40 percent drop back success rate, the fifth lowest of the week. “What’s fallen apart with Maye looks like it’s between the ears as much as anything physical,” Graff said. “He looks like a quarterback whose confidence is shot.” Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said this week that Maye needs to calm down if things are going to turn around. “We need to stop trying to choke the life out of every single play,” Vrabel said during his Monday radio appearance. “We need to relax.” Maye through Week 3 ranks 32nd in fantasy points per drop back, below the likes of Daniel Jones and Cam Ward. It will be tough to start Maye in Week 4 against Buffalo if there are other viable QB options on the waiver wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 14-of-29 attempts for 199 yards and two interceptions in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars, adding four rushes for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: He fumbled twice, losing one to the Jags defense. Maye was under duress and missing routine throws for most of this game. He also had a long touchdown throw and a rushing touchdown called back on penalties. Without A.J. Brown (ankle) in the lineup the Patriots have no one to threaten secondaries, allowing opposing defenses to stack the box, shut down the run game, and leave the Pats a one-dimensional offense. Though Maye’s rushing could keep him afloat as a top-12 quarterback in Week 4 against the Bills, he should be considered a shaky option for now. New England’s offensive line might be able to hold up against a Buffalo front seven that has struggled to pressure the passer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 14-of-22 passes for 208 yards and an interception in the Patriots’ 20-3, Week 2 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: It was a defensive slugfest for the Patriots and Steelers in Week 2, with neither team passing for a touchdown on the day. Maye added 17 rushing yards on four carries but took three sacks, including one in the red zone in the second quarter. His interception was a floater in Steelers territory in the third quarter, tossed right to Patrick Queen to end a drive. He ends the day with 44-percent of his passing yards coming on two third-quarter chunk plays to Romeo Doubs. Maye has had a rough start to the season, following up a three-interception Week 1 with a scoreless, one-interception Week 2. He faces another solid defense in the Jaguars for Week 3; Maye’s rushing upside keeps him in the low-end QB1 territory for next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 23-of-29 passes for 372 yards and three touchdowns in the Packers’ 45-27, Week 9 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: As has been the case for much of the season, big plays were the name of the game for Love. Love aired the ball out at will against a helpless Patriots defense, going 6-for-9 on passes of 20-plus air yards for 235 yards and a touchdown. Love connected with Matthew Golden on multiple long plays in the first quarter, completing passes of 43 and 49 yards, and found him in the end zone for a five-yard score. Love’s longest touchdown pass of the day came in the third quarter when he connected with Christian Watson for a 39-yard-score immediately after the Packers recovered a fumble by Rhamondre Stevenson. Love and the Packers boast arguably the most explosive passing attack in the league, and both Watson and Golden continue to look like premier threats while also being versatile in other areas of the field. Love and the Vikings will have their work cut out for them next week at home against the Vikings, but he will remain in the QB1 mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 30-of-41 passes for 288 yards with three touchdowns and an interception in the Packers’ 27-19, Week 8 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love completed 17 of his first 20 passes, and two of those incompletions were drops. He threw a seed to Tucker Kraft for his first touchdown between defenders, found Matthew Golden wide open in the end zone for his second score — one play after Golden dropped a touchdown — and connected with Josh Jacobs for his third score of the day. The interception was a heinous decision where he didn’t see the safety, but outside of that, it was an impressive evening for the 27-year-old. Love gets zero, well, love from the run game and doesn’t have a quality offensive line, but he’s still putting up respectable numbers. He’ll look to add to those numbers in Week 9 against the Patriots in what should be a fun matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 27-of-45 passes for 274 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Packers’ 20-17, Week 7 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Even with Josh Jacobs back in the mix, the Packers still struggled to get the ground game going. As a result, Love aired it out early and often, throwing a ridiculous 10 passes for 20-plus yards, but only three were completed. Love’s first touchdown pass came on a third-and-nine when he connected with Tucker Kraft for a 14-yard score, and in the third quarter, a short pass to Jacobs was turned upfield for a 25-yard touchdown after Jacobs tight-roped along the sideline to find pay dirt. Love nearly connected with Jacobs for another score late in the fourth quarter, but Jacobs was unable to complete the diving catch in the end zone for the go-ahead score. On the next play, Trey Smack had a 35-yard field goal blocked, which ultimately set the Lions up for the game-winning field goal on the ensuing drive. Love continues to play an aggressive style of football, airing it out to his speedsters in Matthew Golden and Christian Watson. He and the Packers now have a short turnaround to prepare for the Panthers in Week 8, where he will be on the QB1 radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love (back) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love was limited on Wednesday before upgrading to full on Thursday. Packers coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that his starting quarterback was “pretty beat up” after the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys. Hopefully, he is feeling much better by now. This divisional showdown looks like one of the most fantasy-friendly game environments in Week 7. He’s a QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: It’s an upgrade from Wednesday’s limited session. Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Love was “pretty beat up” after Sunday night, but Love doesn’t appear to be in any danger of missing the game. He’ll likely be cleared off the injury report Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Jordan Love (back) was “pretty beat up” after the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love got checked out by the team’s chiropractor after the game and was listed as limited for yesterday’s practice. LaFleur told reporters they haven’t determined whether he will be limited for today’s session. Either way, he said yesterday that there is no chance Love misses Week 7, so the practice reports are a moot point. Love is a top-half QB1 for his date with Detroit this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Wednesday’s session was a walkthrough, so this is just an estimate from the team. We don’t believe it will be much of an issue for Love in Week 7. Barring a setback, Love will remain in the QB1 mix for a likely shootout with the Lions on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 23-of-41 passes for 276 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Packers’ 23-13, Week 6 win over the Cowboys, adding 12 yards and a touchdown on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love isn’t typically a threat to punch in a touchdown with his legs, but the state of the backfield and flow of the game gave him that opportunity late in the second quarter, which he would cash in for his first rushing score since Week 11 of 2024. Fantasy managers shouldn’t get too excited about the touchdown on the ground considering running back Josh Jacobs is expected to be activated from the commissioner’s exempt list Monday. Even so, Love has now accounted for two touchdowns in all six games played through the first third of the season and has gone over 300 yards through the air in half his appearances to start the 2026 season, leaving plenty of meat on the bone for continued fantasy production as the Packers enter their most difficult stretch of the schedule. Love remains a locked-in QB1 ahead of a potential shootout against the division rival Lions in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 25-of-31 passes for 367 yards and two touchdowns in the Packers’ 31-7, Week 5 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: With the Packers’ backs against the wall in a rivalry grudge match, Love had one of the best starts of his NFL life by simply cutting it loose. His 367 yards passing were the third most of his career, and accompanied by zero turnovers. He found each of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft for at least one 46-yard gain, including a 53-yard touchdown to Watson. That does not include an earlier 42-yard scoring strike to Watson. Each score had serious air underneath them. This really was Love airing it out, something less competent quarterbacks had been struggling to do vs. the Bears’ vulnerable defense. We have seen this Love and Packers movie before — a step forward not followed by another move in the right direction — but neither Packers fans nor fantasy managers could have asked for more this afternoon. Love will have a good shot at keeping the good vibes going vs. the Cowboys’ struggling defense in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 22-of-30 passes for 197 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Packers’ 17-14, Week 4 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Green Bay entered this game in desperate need of a win. They got it, though it was not pretty. Kneel downs aside, the Packers had five drives that gained fewer than 10 yards. Love nearly threw the game away with an interception straight into the hands of Jacob Parris in the red zone with less than four minutes left on the clock. The Bucs could not score on the ensuing drive and Love got to kneel out the clock. The Packers’ offense still looked disjointed today. They simply found an opponent that wasn’t a threat to put more than a handful of points on the board. Love is slipping further back in the QB2 ranks as he prepares to take on the Bears in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: Trey McBride caught 7-of-8 targets for 54 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 9 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: The lone incompletion directed toward McBride came on the team’s final play of the game when the veteran tight end was unable to corral an end zone target that was thrown slightly behind him on fourth and goal. McBride combined with alpha wide receiver Michael Wilson to account for 15 targets on 30 Minshew pass attempts, something we’d expect to continue forward give the current state of the team. The Cardinals get another difficult matchup against the Rams in Week 10, where McBride will remain a surefire TE1 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Broncos checked on Trey McBride.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: To no one’s surprise, the Cardinals hung up the phone in record time. Even as a perennially rebuilding franchise, Arizona was never going to trade arguably the league’s best tight end in the middle of his prime. Schefter added that the Cardinals have “checked in around the league on tight ends.” Evan Engram has a measly 13 catches for 136 yards this year and Denver’s passing attack has taken a step back despite acquiring Jaylen Waddle in the offseason. Dallas Goedert is the biggest name believed to be available at tight end ahead of Tuesday’s deadline. On an expiring contract, he wouldn’t cost the Broncos much. Carolina tight end Ja’Tavion Sanders is likely on the trade block as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: Trey McBride caught 7-of-8 targets for 72 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s Week 8 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: McBride’s touchdown with 2:11 left seemed like it would be a bit of a fantasy afterthought, but it quickly proved important as the Cowboys fizzled out after a failed onside kick by Arizona. The veteran tight end caught four passes and 44 yards of this production, as well as the touchdown, once Jacoby Brissett left the game. He’ll remain a don’t-have-to-think-about-it TE1 even in a tough matchup against Seattle in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: Trey McBride caught 10-of-13 targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 7 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: The Cardinals couldn’t get much going on offense, but that’s not a problem for McBride. He accounted for 27 percent of the team’s targets and was the only Cardinal to find the end zone on the day. McBride did so on a seven-yard strike from Brissett in the third quarter. Despite posting weekly TE1 numbers, this is McBride’s first 100-yard outing of the season. Facing a laughable Dallas defense next week, McBride will likely clock in as the TE1 overall in the weekly rankings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: Trey McBride caught 7-of-9 targets for 53 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 6 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: McBride’s first target ended up being a Quentin Lake interception, but Jacoby Brissett went right back to his star tight end on the following drive. McBride made a contested catch on a quick in route, spun off contact and took off downfield for a 26-yard gain. McBride’s day largely consisted of out routes and catches in the flats after that, but he was given two opportunities to score a touchdown from inside the Rams’ 25-yard line on the Cardinals’ seventh drive. On 2nd-and-1 from the Rams’ 21-yard line, McBride caught a pass in the flats and rumbled through contact for a short first-down gain. Three plays later, on 3rd-and-goal from the Rams’ seven-yard line, Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur dialed up a screen pass for him, but the Rams blew it up, resulting in a yardage loss. It wasn’t McBride biggest outing, but a 7/53 is hardly unusable. McBride remains an elite TE1 against the Broncos next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: ArizonaCardinals.com’s Darren Urban believes Carson Beck won’t start in the “immediate future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: Cardinals fans appear to be pining for the team to bench Jacoby Brissett and start the rookie in the coming weeks as another season circles the drain for Arizona. Beck so far has been the Cards’ emergency third quarterback. Urban said there remains a “chance Beck is made the backup this week or next and allow him to come on in relief if the situation presents itself. I don’t see Beck starting in the immediate future, but it does feel his time grows closer, and if the offense continues to sputter, that would be understandable.” Brissett this season ranks 15th in passing yards. He’s thrown nine touchdowns to five interceptions and ranks 30th out of 37 qualifying QBs in adjusted yards per attempt. He won’t be a viable fantasy play this week against a tough Rams coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: Trey McBride caught 9-of-10 targets for 66 yards and one touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 5 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: McBride looked like his normal, dominant self, carving up defenders on out routes and in-breakers. Unfortunately, hearts were also broken when Jacoby Brissett fired a touchdown pass right past McBride, running wide open inside the Lions’ five-yard line, to backup TE Teagan Quitoriano, also running wide open in the back of the end zone. Fortunately, McBride was able to haul in a juggling, falling and contested touchdown catch late in the fourth quarter to boost his final stat line. McBride is an elite TE1 against the Rams next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: Trey McBride caught 7-of-12 targets for 31 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 4 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: It was another compiling-based statistical performance for the Cardinals’ dominant seam stretcher, but the PPR check clears all the same. Amazingly, seven catches were actually a new season low. McBride is going to keep stacking volume efforts, but he has now been out-targeted 30-23 by Michael Wilson over the past two weeks, not that a single soul is concerned about 23 targets in two games. Potentially more concerning is the negative chatter arising around Jacoby Brissett’s play. Either way, McBride has a Week 5 smash spot in the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: Trey McBride caught 9-of-11 targets for 75 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 3 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: McBride had a big receiving day, though penalties prevented it from being more productive. His first reception was called back due to offensive pass interference while he drew defensive pass interference in the endzone on a 4th-and-1 play. He continues to be the Cardinals’ most effective target on immediate routes, slashing through the 49ers defense for 75 yards. Not much more nuance is needed here, McBride is a fantasy TE1 for Week 4 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: Trey McBride caught 8-of-10 targets for 41 yards and one touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 2 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: McBride is unbelievably good at getting open on short-to-intermediate crossers and out routes. Even the Seahawks’ elite defense had trouble capping his receptions total, although they did prevent him from producing a double-digit gain. McBride’s second-quarter touchdown pulled the Cardinals even with the Seahawks, 7-7. It was a daring, smart call by coach Mike LaFleur, who called McBride’s number via a short out route on 4th-and-goal from the Seahawks’ three-yard line. McBride remains an elite TE1 against the 49ers next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Tyler Allgeier rushed 17 times for 46 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 9 loss to the Seahawks, gaining zero additional yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: In what was the first game as the clear starter for the Cardinals in the absence of both Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight, Allgeier was contained to only 2.7 yards per carry as the offense managed under 200 yards of total offense against the stingy Seattle defense. Fantasy managers that were quick to scoop Allgeier off of waivers heading into Week 9 are surely to be disappointed with the returns, particularly considering Knight had largely outperformed the former prior to missing Week 9 with a concussion. Expect a near-even split backfield once Knight returns, which appears likely to be in Week 10 when the Cardinals face another difficult test in the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Tyler Allgeier rushed 11 times for 147 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s Week 8 win over the Cowboys, adding five catches for 44 yards and an additional touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Allgeier was given reign of the backfield in the second half after Bam Knight (concussion) was ruled out and Jeremiyah Love (ankle) left early in the first half. He decided to take advantage of it with runs of 63 yards (for a score) and 52 yards to set up a very nice sideline tightrope touchdown on a reception. Allgeier was the only healthy back for the Cardinals at this point in the game and this isn’t the kind of performance we’ll see repeated, but he definitely could step in to an expanded role in Week 9 given the injuries around him. If he was dropped in your league, he’s a worthwhile waiver wire consideration.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Tyler Allgeier (toe) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 8 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Allgeier saw a steady progression in practice throughout the week, starting off with a “DNP” before upgrading in each subsequent session, culminating in a full practice Friday. He will be available to form a likely three-headed timeshare with Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight against the Cowboys and likely does not warrant fantasy consideration.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Tyler Allgeier (toe) was a limited participant during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Allgeier was able to get a bump up after a DNP for Wednesday. It appears to just be a case of rest for the 26-year-old, but fantasy managers who will consider Allgeier for Week 8 against the Cowboys if Jeremiyah Love (ankle) can’t go — Love was also limited Thursday — should keep an eye on Friday’s designation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Tyler Allgeier (toe) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Allgeier popped up on the injury report with a toe issue as rookie Jeremiyah Love (ankle) returned to practice in a limited fashion. Though we don’t know the severity of Allgeier’s injury, it may be worth keeping Bam Knight rostered despite Love’s return. If Allgeier cannot play in Week 8 against the Cowboys, Knight will get another week of fantasy viability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will be limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: We were hoping to see Love practice in full after taking two weeks off. While today’s limited session puts him on track to play in Week 8 against the Cowboys, Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier are still worth stashing on benches, just in case. The Cardinals are finally handling Love’s recovery patiently, after giving him far too many touches early in the preseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Tyler Allgeier rushed eight times for 19 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 7 loss to the Broncos, adding three catches for 30 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Allgeier only saw one more carry than Bam Knight. Both backs caught three passes, but Knight was the recipient of five targets. Through two Jeremiyah Love absences, Allgeier has 26 carries for 57 yards. He’s barely playing ahead of Knight and has been the far less efficient member of the backfield. Knight has 128 yards on four fewer attempts. Even if Love is out again next week, Allgeier will barely crack the RB3 ranks versus Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Tyler Allgeier is “always” going to serve as a complementary running back.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: LaFleur really laid it all out there at today’s press conference, saying Allgeier “is always going to complement that next guy” when the starter is out. He adds that Allgeier is “extremely smart” and can be trusted in pass protection and short-yardage situations on third down. While Allgeier “can” do what the Cardinals need him to do on first and second down, LaFleur said Bam Knight will take “a lot” of that work with Jeremiyah Love (ankle) sidelined. LaFleur closed by saying he does not think any of these running backs can hold up in a full-time role over the course of the season. Allgeier handled a hefty 19 touches in this complementary role last week. He can be started as a high-volume FLEX with touchdown-based upside against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Things have been trending in this direction all week, but LaFleur officially confirmed on Friday that Love will miss a second straight game. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will likely split duties again in Week 7 after seeing a near 50/50 split in the touch distribution last week, with Allgeier’s 19 touches narrowly edging out Knight’s 17. Both Allgeier and Knight are fringe RB2/RB3 plays against a stout Broncos defense. In addition to Love the Cardinals also ruled out DT Walter Nolen III (ankle), S Andrew Wiggins (ankle), and OG Jo Gaines II (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is not expected to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Love didn’t practice on Wednesday and Thursday after missing Week 6. It doesn’t sound like he will practice at all this week. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will split the backfield again this week. Allgeier out-carried Knight 18-15 last week, but Knight was far more effective, running for 80 yards in total. Allgeier posted just 38 yards. He still figures to be the lead runner this week, but Allgeier shine as a plug-and-play RB2 is waning headed into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 2-of-4 targets for 14 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Despite the quiet fantasy outing, Dulcich finished second on the team in catches and yards. If you couldn’t tell, it was not a productive day for Miami’s passing attack. Dulcich had stacked a few usable weeks over the past month, but Week 9 was his breakout spot against a dreadful Detroit defense. Having missed his big opportunity, he’ll return to the back of the TE2 ranks for Week 10 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 4-of-6 targets for 43 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Three of Dulcich’s catches occurred on the final two drives, and his first catch occurred in the two-minute drill at the end of the first half. Malik Willis seemingly only looks his way when playing quickly. Maybe the coaching staff should address that, because Dulcich played effectively in those situations. The Dolphins face the Lions’ fantasy-friendly pass defense next week, potentially elevating Dulcich to high-end TE2 status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich is not on Miami’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: The fringe TE2 life awaits Dulcich against the Patriots on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich (ankle) remained limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Still, back-to-back practices are a good sign that Dulcich will be ready to go for Week 8’s game against the Patriots. That isn’t necessarily an endorsement of using him in fantasy football — even after last week’s surprise 5/86 against the Jets — but hey, the Dolphins will be glad he’s around.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: The Dolphins’ tight end finally had a decent game, only to tweak an ankle along the way. He should be fine for Week 8 against the Patriots, but he is barely in the TE2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught all five of his targets for 86 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Dulcich made the most of National Tight Ends Day with a 32-yard catch on the Dolphins’ opening drive and two more gains of 15+ yards throughout the contest. He led the team in catches and targets. Dulcich now has at least four receptions in three of his past four games. Miami’s run-first approach is preventing him from finding spike weeks, but Dulcich has worked himself into the TE2 conversation ahead of Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 4-of-5 targets for 37 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Dulcich also added a two-point conversion to his total. It was a low-efficiency passing offense for the Dolphins once again, leading to Dulcich averaging under 10 yards per reception. The 26-year-old tight end is a fantasy TE3 as the Dolphins head into a Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 5-of-7 targets for 55 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 3 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Held under 20 yards in each of the Dolphins’ first two games, Dulcich finally had something of a pop-up effort as the ‘Fins tried in vain to match points with the Chiefs. It was nice to get some proof of TE2 concept, but it is going to be exceptionally difficult for Dulcich to carve out streamer value in a low-volume passing attack focused on seeing what it has in its intriguing rookie receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 2-of-2 targets for 18 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 1 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Both of Dulcich’s targets occurred on the third drive. One was a six-yarder via play action. The other was a delayed screen pass, which Dulcich admirably ran for 12 yards, picking up a first down along the way. The fact that he was barely involved in a pass-heavy game script bodes poorly for his TE1 viability. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues heading into Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: The South Florida Sun Sentinel’s David Furones believes Jalen Tolbert “appeared to be” one of Malik Willis’ top targets in OTAs and minicamp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Furones also lists Greg Dulcich as a player that was a primary receiver for Willis, but we’ve done plenty of offseason hype on Dulcich. Tolbert appears to be a potential “someone has to catch a ball here” deep league pick, as he’s well off the fantasy radar at this point. He’s not off the board among the top-100 wideouts in ADP. The ceiling is likely low, but if he can emerge as the top option amongst Miami’s wideouts, Tolbert could be a viable WR3/WR4 at points this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty had six rushes for 25 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers, adding five catches for -5 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty and Mike Washington were scripted out in the second half, with the Raiders — as usual — falling behind by multiple scores. Jeanty was swallowed up by Niners defenders almost every time he caught the ball in the backfield. The plodding Jeanty couldn’t get anything going against a swarming 49ers defense. This was Jenaty’s sixth game of the season with at least four catches. It’s a role that has made him playable in 12-team leagues this season. Washington, meanwhile, had six carries for -3 yards. Jeanty might have some flex value in Week 10 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said the team’s backfield touch distribution will be a “moving target.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Mike Washington, Jr. in Week 8 against the Jets took over as the team’s lead rusher, logging 25 carries to just two carries for Ashton Jeanty. While Kubiak said after the game that Jeanty would remain a part of the offense, it’s clear the Raiders are willing to experiment with backfield touches. “You see where your team is at and who’s playing the best ball at the time. It’s a 17-game regular season where things change every week. They’ve been changing at guard, they change up front defensively, they change at corner,” Kubiak said. “That’s the NFL. We have a young roster and we’re going to give guys opportunities and see what fits us best. But your 11, whether you’re playing really well or not playing well at all, it’s always going to change a little bit.” The Raiders through Week 8 rank dead last in EPA per rush and second to last in rushing success rate. Jeanty should remain viable as long as he’s the team’s primary pass catcher out of the backfield. Jeanty ranks fifth among all RBs in expected fantasy points per game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty rushed two times for nine yards in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets, adding three receptions for 64 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty was benched as the Raiders’ early-down back, getting out-carried 25-2 by Mike Washington Jr. For his part, Washington was not effective, churning up just 3.3 yards per carry and getting stoned on a bevy of goal-line handles. Speaking afterward, coach Klint Kubiak said the move was his call but that "(Jeanty) is still going to be a big part of our team.” Jeanty made waves during the week when he said the Jets could not tackle. Rather than let the struggling second-year back prove his theory on the field, the Raiders made the takedown themselves for the Jets. While it’s clear Jeanty is now in a true timeshare, we do also take Kubiak at his word that Jeanty will remain a “big part” of the team, almost certainly with double-digit carries more weeks than not. The question is if he can keep catching enough passes to hold RB2 status. Washington is now the preferred short-yardage back, but his failures in Sunday’s highest-leverage spots could keep the door ajar for Jeanty.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty had eight rushes for 15 yards in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss to the Rams, adding eight catches for 61 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Among the least efficient rushers in the game, Jeanty again struggled to get anything going on the ground behind a middling Vegas offensive line. He did almost all of his damage through the air, turning eight targets into 61 yards and a late score in garbage time. He ran a route on 20 of the team’s 35 drop backs against the Rams and ranked second among Raiders pass catchers in targets. Mike Washington had six carries on the day. Jeanty, with at least six targets in six of his seven games this season, can maintain RB2 status as long as he’s catching passes out of the backfield. He gets the Jets in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Dang. This suggests Washington suffered one or both injuries yesterday in practice. He is firmly in the questionable camp and may have only a long shot at suiting up in Week 7 against the Rams. Without him, Ashton Jeanty should handle a solid workload. Dylan Laube could end up serving as the No. 2 running back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty rushed 10 times for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills, adding four receptions for 36 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty, who is dealing with a foot/ankle injury, wasn’t effective on the ground, but that didn’t stop him from scoring his first rushing touchdown of the season. Jeanty punched in a one-yard score in the first quarter of Sunday’s game to give the Raiders an early 7-3 lead, but averaged a disappointing 2.2 YPC overall. He did manage a solid 4-36-0 receiving line on six targets, with two of his four receptions coming on the Raiders’ third drive of the game. Jeanty appeared on 15 more snaps than Mike Washington and out-touched him 14 to 10. While he continues to struggle from an efficiency standpoint, Jeanty’s volume will make him a low-end RB1 next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (foot) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: The Raiders’ starting running back is good to go for what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment. The Raiders encouragingly stopped listing Jeanty with an ankle injury this week. Hopefully, his remaining plantar fasciitis issue subsides before long as well. Jeanty is a low-end RB1 in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (foot) said he is feeling “great” and “ready to go” for Week 6 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: The quotes read a tad bit more enthusiastically than Jeanty did while speaking to media members at his locker, but this is still good to hear. Jeanty has been dealing with an ankle injury for a long time, but the team took that injury off the weekly practice report this week. He is now listed only with the foot injury after experiencing “a flare-up of plantar fasciitis” last Friday. Jeanty is a low-end RB1 against the Bills this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (foot) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty’s previous ankle designation was removed from the injury report and he was a full practice participant on Wednesday. His practice participation lines up with Raiders coach Klint Kubiak saying the 22-year-old running back was starting to “feel a lot better.” Though there were rumors of the Raiders resting Jeanty for a week, he is trending to play in Week 6 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Ashton Jeanty (foot/ankle) is starting to “feel a lot better.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Kubiak also shot down the idea of the Raiders resting Jeanty for a week, despite it being reported earlier today that the Raiders were considering giving him a week off to recover at some point. Jeanty has been dreadfully inefficient this year, averaging a meager 3.3 yards per carry, though the team’s subpar offensive line also deserves some of the blame. For fantasy purposes, his workload has been the big draw. He is averaging 22 touches per game through five weeks. Even if the foot and ankle injuries continue to bother him, Jeanty has to be treated as a mid-range RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eli Stowers was held without a catch in the Eagles’ Week 9 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers was targeted once. He’s now drawn five looks in three games since making his NFL debut in Week 7. With the Eagles now headed on bye, an adjustment upon their return could be more looks for their rookie seam man, especially/obviously if Dallas Goedert is traded ahead of Tuesday’s deadline. It is something to file away, but Stowers is still not a strong 12-team league stash ahead of the open date.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eagles activated Eli Stowers (quad) off injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers probably won’t have a fantasy-relevant role right away this week, but with Dallas Goedert an impending free agent and the Eagles struggling, it wouldn’t be stunning if Goedert were traded away to open up snaps at tight end. Stowers has yet to hit redraft league relevance but it could eventually come. The Eagles also activated Grant Calcaterra (back) from injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eli Stowers (quad) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers is only notable because of his draft capital. The second-round rookie has not carved out a role for himself and would not be fantasy-relevant if the Eagles activate him from injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eli Stowers (quad) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers had his 21-day practice window opened after he started the season on the injured reserve due to hamstring and quad injury. The Eagles also opened fellow TE Grant Calcaterra’s practice window; Calcaterra was also limited due to a back injury. Both have a chance to return Week 6 against the Panthers or Week 7 against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eagles placed TE Eli Stowers (hamstring, quad) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers entered his rookie season unlikely to contribute in a meaningful way but will now be forced to miss the next four games, at minimum, while on injured reserve, something that could stunt his growth at the professional level further. Dallas Goedert remains a locked-in TE1 in fantasy circles moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eagles TE Eli Stowers (hamstring) is questionable for Week 1 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers is listed as the Eagles’ co-TE3, so even if he is absent, that will not be a huge deal. The team is undoubtedly hoping he develops over the course of the season, so tracking his recovery is worthwhile. For now, though, TE Dallas Goedert is the clear-cut tight end to roster in Philadelphia.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eagles TE Eli Stowers (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers had a rough training camp and has been sidelined since late August by the hamstring injury. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eagles TE Eli Stowers (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers has been dealing with a hamstring injury he suffered in the preseason and he opens Week 1 with a limited practice. The 23-year-old rookie was already in line for a limited role this season after a subpar training camp but now may be limited even further with a soft tissue injury. Stowers is off fantasy radars in redraft leagues but his absence propels Dallas Goedert into borderline top-10 tight end territory.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eagles TE Eli Stowers (hamstring) missed his second straight practice Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers missed his second straight practice Tuesday as he deals with a hamstring issue. There is no indication this is a major injury yet, but something to keep an eye on as the Eagles prepare for preseason Week 3. The rookie second-round pick has struggled in camp and comes into the NFL as a raw tight end prospect. Don’t expect the Eagles’ tight end rotation to change drastically should Stowers miss time in the 2026 regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eli Stowers caught all three targets for 12 yards in Saturday’s preseason game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers was somewhat involved in the first half but the rookie tight end had a long gain of just six yards in the first exhibition game of the season. The 23-year-old has significant long-term upside because of his athleticism, but it’s very clear — at least early on — that Stowers has work to do before he’s a fantasy option in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble caught 4-of-6 targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: The Panthers liked something in their middle of the field matchups with the Broncos’ defense, targeting Tremble and Darren Waller 16 combined times. Both seam stretchers scored, with Tremble’s TD his first since Week 6. Tremble’s name has come up in the box score more than expected this year, but he has yet to have a 50-yard day and has three total touchdowns. He remains waiver-wire fodder in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble caught all four of his targets for 46 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: The Panthers seemed a little concerned about the Eagles’ pass rush since Tremble played on 54 of the team’s 79 snaps. He also was on the field for more than half of their dropbacks, but a large chunk of those were in pass-blocking situations. Still, he was schemed wide open on both touchdown passes, which led to a great fantasy day. It’s just not something we would recommend chasing next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: The Athletic’s Joseph Person believes the Panthers could target TE Kenyon Sadiq in the 2026 NFL Draft.
