https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Person said the Panthers, who hold the 19th pick in the 2026 draft, could target two Oregon players: Sadiq, who had 51 receptions for 560 yards and eight touchdowns in his final collegiate season, and safety Dillon Thieneman, one of the most sought-after secondary options in this year’s draft. The team would likely have to trade up to make sure they have a shot at Sadiq, who would join Tommy Tremble and Ja’Tavion Sanders in the Carolina tight end room if he lands with the Panthers. The Panthers in 2025 targeted the tight end position at a 21 percent clip, the seventh lowest mark in the NFL. “Could that change with Brad Idzik taking over the play calling and the addition of offensive specialist Darrell Bevell, who was in Seattle with Canales when the Seahawks traded for All-Pro tight end Jimmy Graham?” Person said. “Possibly.” Sadiq, who ranks 11th in yards per route run among tight ends in the 2026 draft class, would probably be a rotational player in Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble caught 3-of-3 targets for 22 yards in Carolina’s Wild Card Round loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: The Panthers failed to establish a full-time TE1 for most of this year, with Tremble only going over 75.4 percent of the snaps in the final two games of the regular season. He played 54-of-67 snaps versus the Rams. Tremble caught more than one ball in six of his 18 games played this season. He’s low-end TE2 fodder at best entering the final year of his contract.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble caught 3-of-4 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 18 loss to the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Tremble caught a touchdown pass early from Bryce Young to get the Panthers within a score at 10-7. The former Notre Dame tight end finished with just two touchdowns in 2025, and remains much more effective as a blocker than as a receiver. The Panthers didn’t really showcase any of their tight ends this year, making it hard to trust any of them in fantasy leagues. Ostensibly they’d like Ja’Tavion Sanders to be their main receiving tight end, but he just can’t stay healthy. Tremble could get a playoff game next week if the Falcons beat the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble caught his lone target for zero yards in the Panthers’ Week 7 win against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Tremble logged 12 routes on the day while Ja’Tavion Sanders ran 14 routes and did not catch either of his targets. Neither Tremble nor Sanders are fantasy relevant unless one of the tight ends misses time. Tremble had been a viable streaming option while Sanders was sidelined with an ankle injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble caught 4-of-4 targets for 39 yards in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: He added one Liu Kang flying kick against a Cowboys defender in the open field, though nothing was called. Tremble appears and disappears from the Panthers passing game depending on the matchups, and when Ja’Tavion Sanders comes back he’ll likely lose most of his pure passing-game snaps. He can be left on waiver wires heading into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble caught 5-of-8 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Tremble entered the game with only six targets all year but was needed for more with Ja’Tavion Sanders sidelined and provided some volume. His score was a seven-yarder to cap the Panthers’ opening drive. The Panthers would then give up 42 unanswered points before Tremble took a massive hit to bring them to the one-yard line with 2:20 remaining. He was shaken up but said afterward he was fine. The Panthers are so low on quality targets that Tremble could stick in the top 24 for however long Sanders is sidelined, but it is difficult to recommend anyone in this awful overall offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Ja’Tavion Sanders caught 2-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Panthers’ Week 3 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Sanders’ usage came back down to earth after a nine-target Week 2 put him on fantasy radars. The 22-year-old didn’t get his first target until the second half, when he caught a Bryce Young pass and hurdled a defender for a seven-yard gain. The Panthers offense is a difficult one to project for consistent fantasy points, but he will have better days in a more pass-heavy game script. Fellow tight end Tommy Tremble caught both of his targets for 16 yards on the day. Sanders is a deep league streamer option at tight end for Week 4 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Panthers TE Tommy Tremble (back) is not on the injury report and will play in Week 1 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Tremble underwent back surgery in May and opened training camp on the PUP list. He returned to practice and was activated from PUP last week. J’Tavion Sanders should slot in as the Panthers’ starting tight end heading into his second season, but Tremble will pitch in for blocking reps and some work in 12-personnel looks. Tremble’s return to the lineup will keep Sanders off the tight end streaming radar for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers caught 7-of-8 targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers led the Raiders in routes and tied Tre Tucker for the team lead with eight targets. Though Bowers had the ball punched out on a first half reception, he played well against a stingy San Francisco coverage unit that regularly shifted coverage his way. This marked the fifth time in 2026 Bowers has exceeded 80 receiving yards, and the sixth time he’s had at least six receptions in the game. It’s incredible production for a tight end — exactly what Bowers drafters expected when they took him in August drafts. He’ll take on the Seahawks in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers caught 7-of-10 targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: The multi-score start was Bowers’ first of the season but third of his career. He won a first quarter end zone hand fight for a 12-yarder before later contributing a two-yarder where he broke some tackles. He is now up to five touchdowns in six games and has yet to finish below 70 yards. That is league-winning type stuff out of the tight end position. The 49ers are on deck as a tough matchup up the seam for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers caught 6-of-8 targets for 73 yards in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers seemed to be battling some sort of minor injury for most of the game, missing a few high leverage plays while staying loose on the sideline. Bowers was second on the team in targets behind Tre Tucker (12), who did most of his damage in garbage time. Bowers, who has at least nine targets in every game this season, has as high a weekly floor as any tight end in recent memory. Hopefully he’ll be able to explore some of his upside in Week 8 against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf) is not on Las Vegas’ final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: A Friday afternoon tradition unlike any other, Bowers was cleared after getting in two full sessions on Thursday and Friday. He can be played as an elite TE1, as usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf) practiced in full on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Phew. Seeing Bowers return to full participation today is heartening. The star tight end appeared on the injury report as a limited participant yesterday, leaving some questions as to when the injuries occured, and how severe they are. Ideall, he remains full tomorrow and can be started as an elite TE1 as usual against the Rams this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers is usually a limited practice participant due to his knee injury, before upgrading to full and eventually playing. However, this week is notable as he was listed with hamstring and calf injuries instead of a knee injury. He was still limited as usual on Wednesday but the new designations are something to keep an eye on throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers caught 4-of-9 targets for 70 yards in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.i
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: After being held without so much as a target in the first half of Sunday’s loss, Bowers still managed to finish the day with 70 receiving yards on a team-high nine targets. The Bills effectively shadowed Bowers with cornerback Christian Benford for much of the game but Bowers took advantage of a few holes in the Bills’ zone defense to make a few plays, which included back-to-back catches of 18 and 29 yards in the fourth quarter. Bowers did in one half what most tight ends need a full game to do, which speaks to his ability as one of the top play-making tight ends in the league. He’ll remain on the TE1 radar next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: One of these days, Bowers will be removed from the injury report for good. For now, we will continue to let you know that the Raiders’ star player gets a half day on Wednesday before practicing in full for the rest of the week. Bowers is the overall TE1 in fantasy football each week. Start him accordingly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (knee) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: The Raiders continue managing Bowers’ practice reps early in the week, though he plays unrestrictedly on game day. The Raiders face the Bills in Week 6, likely facilitating a fantasy-friendly game environment. Bowers should be treated as the overall TE1 as usual this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers continues his trend of practicing limited to open the week before upgrading to a full practice later in the week and getting cleared off the injury report. Fantasy managers can again expect to see Bowers return top-five fantasy tight end value in Week 6 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: Darius Cooper caught 2-of-8 targets for 25 yards in the Eagles’ Week 9 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: One of Cooper’s missed connections in an inefficient performance was a drop on a potentially long score. So it goes with backup-level pass catchers are playing with No. 3 quarterbacks. Cooper has provided the Eagles with some desperately needed snaps and down-field ability, but there is extremely little chance his real life “value” translates to fantasy points in the second half of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: Darius Cooper caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: With DeVonta Smith back, Cooper played just 39 of 64 snaps and ran a route on 26 of the team’s 52 dropbacks. Those were both fourth among wide receivers on the team. Cooper’s fantasy value is likely limited until there is another injury in the receiving room.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: Darius Cooper caught 2-of-3 passes for 71 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: Cooper has been a touchdown magnet this year, scoring three times on five catches before today’s explosion. He broke loose against the Jags in the second quarter with a 62-yard grab. Cooper beat his man deep and his adjustment to the throw, which was thrown back toward the center of the field, put him in open space with a full head of steam. He ran untouched into the end zone. Cooper’s absurd touchdown efficiency can’t be sustained, but he is developing into a meaningful deep threat for a struggling Philly passing attack. He will at least warrant some FLEX consideration if DeVonta Smith remains out for Week 6 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: Darius Cooper caught 3-of-7 targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: Doing his best Isaac TesLaa impression, Cooper is now up to three touchdowns on only five catches this season. His first score today was a fluke 18-yarder where he turned a Jalen Hurts end zone interception into six after he wrestled the ball away from Quentin Lake. His second was a 10-yarder where the Rams somewhat understandably simply stopped covering him in the painted area. Cooper is one of the only Birds stepping up right now, but his paltry targets total through four appearances — 10 — means he’s not about to push for WR4 status even with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) on the shelf.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: The Philly Voice’s Jimmy Kempski reports that Eagles WR Johnny Wilson had a “better” spring than WR Darius Cooper and could challenge for a roster spot.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: Wilson’s first two years in the NFL were riddled with injuries. A summer concussion and in-season hamstring injury slowed his rookie season development, and he was robbed of his second season after being rolled up on in an August practice. He underwent season-ending ankle and knee injuries and was replaced in the lineup by Cooper, who uninspiringly caught nine passes for 92 yards all year. Wilson, an oversized slot receiver, is unlikely to be fantasy-relevant, but it sounds like he has a chance to at least contribute this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: The Athletic’s Zach Berman reports Darius Cooper “raised eyebrows” and “even pushed Jahan Dotson last year to be the No. 3 receiver.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: In trying to figure out how the Eagles could look if A.J. Brown gets traded, it’s possible Cooper pushes for a role in a three-wide set with Johnny Wilson also in the conversation. Cooper did manage a five-target, 33-yard game in meaningless Week 18 action with Tanner McKee starting. He’s on the deep dynasty radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: Darius Cooper caught 3-of-5 targets for 33 yards in the Eagles’ Week 18 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: Cooper, an undrafted free agent rookie from Tarleton State, had six targets on the season heading into Week 18. He made a few chunk plays running the most routes he had all season with the Eagles resting starters. Also splitting WR4 looks for the Eagles was Britain Covey, who caught 2-of-4 targets for 20 yards. Neither Cooper nor Covey are relevant on offense when the Eagles are playing starters, which they will be doing in the Wild Card round against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: Eagles placed OLB Nolan Smith on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: Smith reportedly re-injured the triceps muscle that he tore during Super Bowl LIX. He underwent surgery to repair the torn tissue this offseason. The Eagles believe Smith will not require surgery and hope to have him back “around” their Week 9 bye. Players placed on injured reserve are eligible to return after missing four games. The Eagles also placed CB Jakorian Bennett and WR Darius Cooper on injured reserve with undisclosed injuries. Both players are likewise expected to avoid surgery and are expected to return around Week 9. The Eagles signed S Marcus Epps, TE Cameron Latu, and CB Parry Nickerson to the active roster, and LB Lance Dixon, DB Eli Ricks, and WR Quez Watkins to the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 5-of-6 targets for 50 yards in the Eagles’ Week 9 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: With No. 3 QB Joe Milton making his starting debut, Goedert padded the box score with some empty PPR production. Excellent, though there figures to be distressingly little difference between Goedert’s floor and ceiling for the time being. With the Eagles headed on bye for Week 10, how Goedert is valued upon the team’s return will depend on whether DeVonta Smith or Dontayvion Wicks finally get back in the lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 3-of-4 targets for 30 yards in the Eagles’ Week 8 loss to the Commanders, adding two yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert also committed a drop that was intercepted in the down performance, although the play in question was overturned through penalty. The veteran tight end continues to be limited by an ineffective offense with Tanner McKee under center in what has quickly become a lost season after the team’s sixth consecutive loss. Fantasy managers are likely better off looking for viable alternatives ahead of a Week 9 divisional clash with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 5-of-7 targets for 48 yards in the Eagles’ Week 7 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert has now returned consecutive games of middling production with Tanner McKee under center, which is a somewhat troubling realization considering DeVonta Smith missed both games and Dontayvion Wicks departed Week 6 with an injury before missing Week 7. Goedert’s fantasy value appears strictly tied to the state of a sinking Philadelphia ball club, now fighting through declining quarterback play in addition to poor offensive structure and shoddy play calling. Fantasy managers are likely forced to endure the middling production for lack of better options.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) was removed from the injury report Saturday and will play against the Cowboys in Week 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert reportedly aggravated his previous knee injury but got back on the practice field for a full session Saturday before being removed from the injury report. He could be stepping into a massive target share with both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks ruled out. Fantasy managers can start him as an upside TE1 in a great matchup against the Cowboys in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert is on the wrong side of questionable for the Eagles’ Week 7 Monday Night Football game against the Cowboys. The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane reports that as of Thursday, there was “optimism” about Goedert’s Week 7 availability. Hopefully, he resumes practicing tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert missed time with a knee injury earlier this year, but he was not on the injury report last week. This could just be a maintenance day, but it is worth keeping an eye on in the lead up to the Eagles’ Monday Night Football game against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 6-of-8 targets for 61 yards in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Early in the game, when Tanner McKee was struggling to get anything going, he seemed locked onto Goedert. When the Panthers were up by multiple scores and the defense seemed to allow some more space in the secondary, McKee felt more confident in taking shots down the field to his receivers, which meant Goedert was quiet in the second half. Still, he was second on the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards and will be a low-end TE1 against the Cowboys next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 6-of-9 targets for 38 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert returned to the lineup after missing three games with a knee injury. Already without Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith, Goedert was immediately thrust into a high-usage role. He led the team in targets and catches, though much of his looks were simply check-downs. Even if that’s his role going forward, Goedert should catch enough passes to sustain borderline TE1 numbers until DeVonta Smith returns. He gets a date with the Panthers in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) is not on Philadelphia’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert got in a full session on Friday and is cleared. With DeVonta Smith down, he has some TE1 potential against the Jaguars on volume. He’s always been one of Jalen Hurts’ favorite red zone targets, and Saquon Barkley being down may lead the Eagles to throw more once the field condenses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert’s return cannot come soon enough. DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Hollywood Brown (ankle) remain sidelined, and Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) got hurt in today’s practice. If Goedert can play this week, he will vault right back into the TE1 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 17-of-25 attempts for 232 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders, adding seven rushes for 40 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy made quick work of a Raiders defense that has ranked as one of the NFL’s worst over the past month. The Niners tormented the Vegas defense with well-timed screens and quick hits to the middle of the field. Purdy used his legs in a couple high leverage situations in the first half and scored his second rushing touchdown of the season. He connected with Christian McCaffrey and Jordan Watkins for his throwing scores. The ultra-efficient Purdy will take on the generationally bad Dallas defense in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 27-of-40 passes for 288 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the 49ers’ 29-20, Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: After losing seemingly every wide receiver to injury, it was only a matter of time before we finally had a down Purdy game. The truth is, he didn’t even play poorly. His first interception was on a pass that he was trying to throw away when safety Jesse Bates made an incredible toe-drag interception. The second pick was on a really nice play by linebacker Kendal Daniels over the middle. Purdy looked good and gave his team a chance to win despite a depleted offense. The 49ers will have a bye next week and then hopefully get back at least one of their primary receivers before a Week 9 game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 21-of-29 passes for 264 yards and one touchdown in the 49ers’ 23-17, Week 6 win over the Commanders, adding 28 yards on five carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy and the 49ers absolutely dominated the first two quarters, gaining 303 yards of total offense on 41 plays before the break. The situation would alter course in a hurry after Purdy lost his top option through the air in the final minute of the second quarter as Mike Evans departed with an aggravation of the Achilles injury that had him listed as questionable entering the game. The team would go on to gain only 72 additional yards after the intermission, allowing the Commanders the ability to claw their way back into the game in the fourth quarter. Even so, Purdy now holds the NFL record for highest career passer rating after qualifying for the statistic with his 1,500th pass attempt in the win, which pushes the 49ers to a perfect 6-0 record ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Falcons before their bye the following week. Purdy remains a surefire QB1 against the pass-funnel Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 19-of-29 passes for 189 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the 49ers’ 32-29, Week 5 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy and the 49ers made the most of several short fields in this one. After an interception by Sam Darnold on the Seahawks’ first drive of the game, Purdy led a short 18-yard drive that he capped with a two-yard touchdown pass to Mike Evans to give the Niners an early lead. Purdy would orchestrate a long scoring drive in the fourth quarter, completing seven passes for 89 yards, with his final completion resulting in a seven-yard touchdown to Brandin Cooks. The Seahawks became the first team to sack Purdy this season, bringing him down three times in the backfield in the second half, but Purdy was able to evade pressure for the entire second half. Purdy and the Niners get a juicy Week 6 matchup next Monday against the Commanders, where he will profile as a solid QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 19-of-30 attempts for 218 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 4 win against the Broncos, adding ten rushes for 29 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy’s ten rushing attempts were a season high, and the product of Denver’s secondary blanketing Niners pass catchers for much of the game. Injuries to both starting Broncos corners eventually loosened things up for Purdy and the 49ers. He connected with George Kittle on a fourth quarter screen pass that went for a 58-yard score — the biggest play of the game. Purdy, who now has 11 touchdown passes through four games, is a weekly top-10 fantasy play even on his less-than-efficient days. He gets a tough matchup against Seattle in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 15-of-27 passes for 297 yards and four touchdowns in the 49ers’ 36-30, Week 3 win over the Cardinals, adding two carries for 34 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: The 49ers offense had another fruitful fantasy day despite injuries haunting the team once again. Purdy showcased his mobility and athleticism, often making throws on the run and scrambling out of pressure. His first score was a completion to Mike Evans, who lateraled it to Deebo Samuel for the score. Purdy then threw a more traditional touchdown to Evans later in the first half, then threw two scores to George Kittle to seal the game in the second half. Despite losing Evans and LT Trent Williams by the third quarter, Purdy was still able to gash the Cardinals defense and surpass 300 total yards. Though the offense keeps losing pieces, Purdy in Kyle Shanahan’s scheme is a fantasy QB1 until further notice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 20-of-22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns in a 35-13, Week 2 win over the Cardinals, adding 30 yards rushing and a touchdown on the ground.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: The Dolphins’ defense didn’t put up much of a fight, but Purdy was tremendous in this one. He bought extra time in the pocket when he needed to, made plays with his legs if the opportunities were there, and found open receivers over the middle of the field all game long. He may find the going a little bit tougher next week against the Cardinals, but probably not much. The bigger question will be who else can step up in the receiver room with Demarcus Robinson leaving this game with an ankle injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 25-of-34 passes for 205 yards with three touchdowns and one interception in the 49ers’ 27-7, Week 1 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy also added 29 yards on his five attempts. The veteran signal-caller did throw a terrible interception, but outside of that pick he played exceptionally well; even if most of his completions were for short yardage. All three passing scores came to different players, with his best throw being a perfectly placed touchdown to Deebo Samuel between two Rams’ defenders to cement the blowout. Purdy will look to keep it going in Week 2, and gets a friendly matchup against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that 49ers QB Brock Purdy said he is “prepared to use his mobility more this year if needed.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: The 49ers’ quarterback is not a straight-line burner, but he is more agile than he is given credit for. Purdy adds that he won’t constantly be looking for opportunities to run, however, he believes he can help the offense by scrambling for 10-12 yards from time to time. Purdy has racked up 113 carries over the past two NFL seasons, including the playoffs, proving himself an efficient scrambler with a 47.8 percent conversion rate that ranks first among quarterbacks with at least 50 attempts. He’s a borderline QB1/2. Scrambling more often could get him into the weekly low-end QB1 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: 49ers added $300,000 in incentives to Mac Jones’ contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Jones, who could have started elsewhere this season if the Niners had found a trading partner, will now make $3.55 million in 2026, with another $2.25 million available in incentives. Jones will be a free agent after the 2026 season. The Niners reportedly wanted a first-round draft pick in exchange for Jones. The veteran threw for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns, and six interceptions last season over eight games as the Niners’ starter. Jones in 2025 was tenth in EPA per drop back, just behind Sam Darnold and Patrick Mahomes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 6-of-9 targets for 61 yards in the Eagles’ Week 9 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon again led this limited offense in receiving as Joe Milton made his first start under center, but he hurt the cause with a handful of drops, including a particularly brutal one with the Eagles desperately trying to tie the game late. Lemon now has at least six catches in three straight games but has not reached 70 yards in the process. In other words, he is posting empty PPR volume. That will remain the “thesis of the play” when the Eagles come off bye in Week 11, though the return of either DeVonta Smith or Dontayvion Wicks would take a major bite out of Lemon’s WR3 appeal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 6-of-9 targets for 57 yards in the Eagles’ Week 8 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon led the team in receiving for the second consecutive game without both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, although the returns were nothing to write home about in Week 8. Largely confined to a short area role, Lemon’s nine targets were mostly the product of the offense’s inability to attack downfield and carry weak per-target upside, a trend likely to continue for as long as Tanner McKee remains under center. That leaves fantasy managers in a precarious position heading into a Week 9 showdown against the Giants, where better options likely exist.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 7-of-8 targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 7 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon showed out with the best game of his career in the absence of both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, operating as the top option through the air throughout the game against the Cowboys. He started his night off with a 21-yard reception on the team’s first possession before adding a fourth quarter touchdown on a quick slant from four yards out. The uncertainty surrounding Smith’s injury could leave Lemon as the de facto lead receiver for a Week 8 divisional tilt against the Commanders, where his fantasy value will be strictly tied to the availability of the other receivers on the roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-6 targets for 19 yards in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Despite not lighting up the box score, Lemon was third on the team in targets and finished fourth in receptions. Initial reports had him playing on 52 of the team’s 64 snaps and running a route on 47 of their 52 dropbacks. That was the most routes of any receiver on the team. Some of this was because the team seemed to be easing DeVonta Smith back from injury, and Dontayvsion Wicks briefly left the game with an injury scare, but we also wouldn’t be surprised to see Lemon get more work in what is looking like a bit of a lost season in Philadelphia.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 5-of-7 targets for 43 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: The good news is that Lemon set new season highs in targets, catches, and yards. The bad news: All of that resulted in a measly 9.3 PPR points. Lemon will hopefully continue to earn more opportunities as the season progresses, but DeVonta Smith’s return could just as easily stall the rookie’s progress. Lemon will be a WR4/5 if Smith remains out for Week 6 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Wicks was listed as a limited participant today, indicating that he strained his hamstring during Thursday’s practice. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) still sidelined, rookie WR Makai Lemon could be the de facto top receiver, though the team has struggled to use him effectively thus far. Hollywood Brown (ankle) also remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-6 targets for 27 yards in the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon moved up a spot in the targets pecking order with DeVonta Smith sidelined, but it resulted in the same quiet box score he posted the first three weeks of his career. The No. 20 overall pick is now sitting on 10 receptions for a scoreless 65 yards through his first four NFL appearances. There has yet to be any light at the tunnel with regards to either his usage or the Eagles’ overall offensive environment. Even with byes beginning and injuries mounting, Lemon is not a recommended WR4 heading into Week 5 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-4 targets for 29 yards in the Eagles’ Week 3 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon was the target on the team’s first play from scrimmage, gaining a first down on a first down play for the Eagles for the first time all season. The offense would sputter throughout the game on their way to only 47 offensive plays run from scrimmage, capping the fantasy upside of all involved in the process. Lemon has yet to live up to his lofty draft capital through the first three games of his professional career, but he could be called on for heavier work with tight end Dallas Goedert nursing an MCL sprain. Things don’t get any easier with a matchup against the Rams on deck for Week 4, where Lemon can safely be left on fantasy benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught a 14-yard pass in the Eagles’ Week 2 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon also “added” a -5 yard rush. Lemon’s first quarter catch ended up going down as his only target of the afternoon. He’s now stuck on four catches for nine yards through his first two NFL contests, and is getting soundly out-targeted by Dontayvion Wicks. That’s with Darius Cooper mixing in. The Eagles are calling plays like Lemon has to be manufactured his touches. Two games is not a large sample size, but it is enough to know we can’t rely on Lemon as a WR4 for Week 3 in Chicago.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-4 targets for negative -5 yards in the Eagles’ Week 1 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: It’s possible things could’ve gone worse for Lemon in his debut, but not much worse. The rookie first-rounder saw two of his four targets come at/behind the line of scrimmage, with his longest target coming eight yards downfield. Lemon’s 28 routes run were good for third-most among Eagles receivers in this one, but we would expect him to see a little more work downfield going forward. Lemon remains a bench stash heading into Week 2’s game against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught 2-of-3 targets for 21 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington wasn’t awfully involved in this game, even if you account for the Dolphins’ low-volume passing approach. He earned a 12 percent target share and added one carry for zero yards. Caleb Douglas, on the other hand, was the runaway WR1 for Miami. He earned eight targets and led the team with six grabs for 70 yards. Already completely out of the playoff race, the Dolphins are in evaluation mode with their young receiver corps. That could mean increasing workloads for Douglas, Chris Bell, and Kevin Coleman. Washington will get another week in the WR4 ranks, but he could be waiver wire fodder if he posts another quiet game against the Colts next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught 5-of-6 targets for 40 yards and one touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington continues to play well as a short-area pass catcher, though he did haul in a 23-yarder downfield. He got leveled on the Dolphins’ fifth drive, and Patriots LB Christian Ellis received an unnecessary roughness penalty for the act. It briefly seemed like Washington’s day might be over, but he returned a few plays later to score a one-yard touchdown via a quick out route after going in motion pre-snap. Today’s stat line allowed Washington to clear the century mark in career catches (103). Among NFL wide receivers with at least 100 receptions from 2021-26, Washington’s 8.4 yards per reception ranks dead last. He is a WR4/FLEX against the Lions in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington (knee) is not on Miami’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington’s WR4 status will continue aplomb against the Patriots in Week 8, though Caleb Douglas’ return probably has capped his ceiling case for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Back-to-back limited sessions probably leave Washington in a good spot for Week 8. He’s more likely than not to be cleared off the injury report on Friday as long as there’s not a sudden downgrade.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington has cooled off in recent weeks. Although his knee injury is unlikely to keep him out of the Dolphins’ Week 8 matchup against the Patriots, he is barely a WR5 in fantasy football. Washington does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets, adding two carries for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington’s previous season-low in targets was five. He had also reached at least 43 receiving yards in every game before today. It shouldn’t come as a surprise that his worst box score of the season came in Caleb Douglas’s first game back from a month-long absence. With more competition for targets on a team that doesn’t want to pass the football, Washington is trending in the wrong direction headed into Week 8. He will be a low-end WR4 versus the Patriots next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught 6-of-8 targets for 43 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals, adding one carry for 19 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington was the most involved Dolphins receiver, leading the team in targets and receiving yards. He started things off with an 18-yard rush and saw a steady peppering of low-depth targets. Though he led all Dolphins skill-position players in snaps, Washington doesn’t see many scoring opportunities in the Miami offense. After a Week 6 bye, The 25-year-old is a volume-based FLEX play Week 7 against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught 5-of-5 targets for 67 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 4 loss to the Vikings, adding two rushes for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington remains one of the Dolphins’ primary returners despite his increased receiving involvement. His day began with a muffed punt that he successfully recovered in the end zone for a touchback. Things improved from there. Washington delivered multiple double-digit gains, functioning effectively as a weapon behind the line of scrimmage and in the flats. He also turned in a 17-yarder via a corner route on play action. Rookie WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) may return for next week’s game against the Saints. If he remains sidelined, Washington should be FLEX-viable, though his ceiling is questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: We expect to see Douglas listed with a second DNP next to his name today, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 4 against the Vikings. Were he indeed to miss this week’s game, WRs Chris Bell (knee) and Malik Washington would benefit. Washington’s target volume is somewhat intriguing, but Bell looks like the far more talented player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Douglas, who has shown flashes in limited action so far this season, did not suit up in Week 3 against the Chiefs and looks like a long shot for Week 4 against the Vikings. Douglas’ absence would be a potential boost for Malik Washington, who leads the Dolphins in targets and air yards through Week 3. Minnesota’s defense, while elite, has allowed the fourth most air yards this season and profiles as a pass-funnel.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 5-of-9 targets for 45 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 9 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Even with Pat Bryant (ankle) returning, Sutton posted new season highs for receptions and targets as Jaylen Waddle departed early with a concussion. He did get out-gained by Bryant, who also found the end zone. Sutton is a perfectly fine role player, but it is the bitter truth that he is no longer a featured option. With Waddle now having the Broncos’ bye week to get healthy, Sutton could be returning as the team’s No. 3 option. He’s a borderline WR4/5 hold in leagues with shallower benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught all four of his targets for 53 yards in the Broncos’ Week 8 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton’s 53 yards today are now a season-high, as are his four receptions. That, however, largely speaks to how unproductive he has been this year. Sutton has more games under 20 yards than over 40. He also has just one touchdown through eight games. His signs of life versus the Chiefs will keep him in the WR5 ranks for Week 9, but the ceiling remains nonexistent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Jaylen Waddle suffered a chest injury and his Week 8 status has not been determined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Waddle left Sunday’s game against the Cardinals with the chest injury. It was, according to Rapoport, an “aggravation of his previous chest injury.” Waddle could try to practice later this week, but would appear to be iffy unless he can log a practice session by Friday. If Waddle is sidelined this week against the Chiefs, Courtland Sutton would likely see more targets and become an interesting flex option against a tough KC secondary. Sutton over the past four weeks leads Denver in air yards and has the second most targets behind Waddle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 3-of-5 targets for 45 yards in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton’s 45 yards today were one shy of his season-high, which mostly speaks to how quiet the veteran wideout has been this year. He has only topped 25 yards twice and has just one touchdown to his name. Jaylen Waddle injured his chest late in this contest and could be out for Week 8. That would funnel a few more targets Sutton’s way, but it’s not like Waddle was putting up loads of counting stats that now shift to Sutton. Even if Waddle is out for Week 8 versus the Chiefs, Sutton would have a hard time pushing past the WR4 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-3 targets for 19 yards in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Nix’s only incompletion when targeting Sutton resulted in the veteran receiver getting rocked over the middle of the field on a ball Nix led him directly into oncoming contact. Sutton vented his frustration by repeatedly pounding the ground following the hit, with it unclear whether it was due to the hit or the incompletion on third down on a night the Broncos struggled to move the football to the tune of only 168 yards of total offense. Fantasy managers likely aren’t utilizing Sutton as a weekly option, but will want to track his practice status ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Cardinals if bye week fill-ins are required.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-3 targets for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: It’s the first touchdown for Sutton on the season, and it tied the game at 17-17. The 31-year-old was unable to find room versus the Chargers’ secondary, and for the fifth-straight week, Sutton was held under 50 yards. His size could give the smaller Seahawks’ defensive backs trouble, but he’s essentially a touchdown-dependent FLEX for Week 6 against Seattle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 1-of-6 targets for four yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton was the recipient of a couple off-target intermediate looks from Bo Nix, who struggled to place the ball against the 49ers secondary. Sutton could see an expanded role in the Denver offense if Pat Bryant is out long term following his leg injury in Week 4. Sutton has been targeted on 16 percent of his pass routes this season; he has nine receptions through four games. Sutton should only be rostered in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 3-of-7 targets for 46 yards in the Broncos’ Week 3 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton tied for the team lead in targets while pacing the offense in yards, which highlights the struggles that persist in Davis Webb’s offense through three games. He will be off the FLEX radar ahead of a Week 4 showdown against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 3-of-4 targets for 25 yards in the Broncos’ Week 2 win against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton’s lone end zone target was intercepted on a poor throw from Bo Nix. Last week Sutton had just 11 yards on five targets in the Broncos’ season-opening loss to the Chiefs. Jaylen Waddle, with 148 yards in Week 2, has established himself as the clear-cut WR1 in the Denver offense. Sutton will be a touchdown-dependent WR3/4 option in Week 3 against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Bo Nix called the Broncos’ Week 1 offensive performance “pretty pitiful.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Nix during his postgame presser defended offensive play caller Davis Webb, who took over for head coach Sean Payton this offseason. “The players did not make it easy on [Webb] today,” said Nix, who completed 17-of-28 passes for 131 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Monday night’s loss to Kansas City. “Pretty pitiful, actually.” Denver had the league’s second lowest drop back EPA of Week 1; only the Falcons were worse. Nix, meanwhile, ranked 28th out of 32 qualifying QBs in Week 1 accuracy. “We called exactly what we prepared for and what we wanted to get to and we just didn’t execute,” Nix said. “Then we were behind.” Webb and the Broncos will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a tough Jaguars defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Pat Bryant caught 4-of-5 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 9 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Active for the first time since Week 4, a returning Bryant (ankle) ended up leading the Broncos in receiving. Jaylen Waddle was forced to depart after only one target with a concussion. Bryant’s score, his second of the season, was a 26-yarder against broken coverage. Although his snaps were somewhat rationed following his month-long layoff, Bryant avoided setbacks and continues to look like a dark horse contender for No. 1 receiver duties in Denver. He’s a solid bench option heading into the Broncos’ Week 10 bye before their Week 11 return against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Broncos activated WR Pat Bryant (ankle) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: The young receiver will make his return to the active game-day roster after missing the minimum four games after injuring his ankle in Week 4. He returns to a passing attack with no clear direction or upside, with no receiver other than Courtland Sutton playing in a near every-down role of late. Perhaps he can carve out a featured role, but it is more likely this team simply doesn’t have viable weekly fantasy assets through the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Pat Bryant (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant is expected to be activated from injured reserve by Saturday, but the team has officially listed him as questionable. He makes for a boom-bust FLEX in his first game back. The Broncos’ passing offense has struggled this season. Perhaps Bryant’s return lifts it up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Pat Bryant (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant’s 21-day practice window has been opened, and it begins with a full session, putting him on track to play in Week 9 against the Panthers. The Broncos’ passing game has severely underperformed expectations. Bryant does not necessarily need to be added in 12-team formats, though he could ultimately compete for No. 2 wide receiver duties.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: The Denver Gazette’s Chris Tomasson said “indications point to Broncos WR Pat Bryant returning to practice this week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant has missed the Broncos’ last four games after being placed on injured reserve with an ankle injury. The 23-year-old receiver is eligible to return whenever the Broncos deem him ready to do so, and his practicing this week would mean the team has opened his 21-day return window. Bryant has caught nine passes for 133 yards and one touchdown and was third among Broncos receivers in routes run (91) through the first four weeks of the season. He could make for an interesting stash in deeper leagues, but fantasy managers shouldn’t rush to put him in their lineups whenever he does return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Broncos placed Pat Bryant on injured reserve with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant will be eligible to return from injured reserve in Week 9, when the Broncos face the Panthers. The Broncos go on bye in Week 10, though, so if he isn’t feeling ready to play, they could hold him out until they face the division-rival Raiders in Week 11. Bryant’s absence could create more opportunities for Courtland Sutton and Marvin Mims, but Jaylen Waddle may end up hogging targets instead.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Broncos WR Pat Bryant will miss “a few weeks” after suffering a sprained ankle in Week 4’s loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant was carted from the field in the second half of Sunday’s game after taking a big hit over the middle. The 23-year-old receiver currently ranks third among Broncos receivers with 91 routes run and has played 55 percent of his snaps out wide. Troy Franklin or Marvin Mims could be in line to see more snaps while Bryant is sidelined, but it’s hard to imagine either player becoming valuable fantasy assets at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Pat Bryant was carted off with an apparent leg injury in Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: He’s questionable to return. Bryant took a big hit over the middle on a second half reception against the Niners and was down on the turf for some time before being helped onto the cart. Looking dejected, Bryant was taken to the locker room. The oft-injured Bryant could be facing yet another extended absence. That would likely boost playing time and targets for Courtland Sutton and possibly Marvin Mims.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Pat Bryant caught both targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 3 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant also added a successful two-point reception in the third quarter to give him a usable fantasy week for the first time in 2026. He continues to play well behind Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle in an offense that has yet to find its footing with a new offensive play caller. He’ll be a difficult start in Week 4 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Pat Bryant caught 4-of-6 targets for 42 yards in the Broncos’ Week 1 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: The good news for fantasy managers is that Bryant played well ahead of both Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin, rewarding those who took a late-round dart through on the talented second-year receiver. That’s about where the good news ended on this night considering the Broncos managed only 176 yards of total offense. While better days are likely ahead for Bryant, there is likely to be mounting pressure from the outside for offensive coordinator Davis Webb to relinquish play calling duties back to head coach Sean Payton. Until, or unless, that happens, Bryant appears likely to remain an upside WR4. That begins in Week 2 when the Broncos face the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed 16 times for 55 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Gordon caught his only target for nine yards. Jaylen Wright was out this week. Kaytron Allen was active but entered the weekend with a quad injury. He saw one touch. Gordon earned another bell-cow workload but failed to do much with it for the second week in a row. Things should turn around for him when Miami takes on the equally down-bad Colts in Week 10. Gordon will remain in the RB2 mix despite the consecutive bust weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed 19 times for 69 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Gordon continues to look like a powerful, capable interior runner, deserving of the Dolphins’ starting role. He, frustratingly, had a 15-yard run erased by a holding penalty and failed to catch his lone target. Gordon celebrated a bit too enthusiastically after a five-yard run on the Dolphins’ seventh drive and was flagged for a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. The young player was extremely upset about the call and required one-on-one conversations with coach Jeff Haffley, another unidentifiable coaching staff member and Malik Willis before regaining composure. Gordon will likely end up in the mid-to-high RB2 ranks against the Lions next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed 25 times for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: The Dolphins took an early lead and never looked back, allowing them to lean on their ground game for the better part of four quarters. Gordon, in turn, set new career highs in rushes and yards. In four starts sans De’Von Achane, Gordon has 69 carries for 332 yards and four touchdowns. He has finished as a top-20 fantasy option at his position in all four starts. Gordon’s role on one of the most run-heavy offenses in the league is too good to ignore. He will be in the RB2 mix when the Dolphins take on the Patriots next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed 18 times for 88 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Gordon continued to operate as the Dolphins’ No. 1 running back, scoring a touchdown for the second straight week. He took all of Miami’s red zone backfield touches and was tackled at the one yard line in the third quarter, coming close to his second touchdown of the day. He lost two yards the next play and the Dolphins did not convert. Gordon saw 42 snaps on the day and will be a low-end fantasy RB2 for Week 7 against the Jets after a Week 6 bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed nine times for 100 yards and one touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Gordon entered the game on the Dolphins’ second drive, generating one yard and two receptions on three touches during that possession. Things improved from there. After letting nominal starting RB Jaylen Wright and Gordon each play their own drives, the Dolphins eventually began rotating them in and out until Gordon separated on the first drive after halftime. Gordon notched three carries in a row, breaking off a 53-yarder on the second one by navigating traffic and making his way to the left sideline, shedding a jersey grab along the way. On the seventh drive, he had what could have been a breakaway touchdown run blown dead by officials, who thought Gordon was down by contact as he stumbled through the box. It was a close call. He then touched the ball on two-of-four plays on the ensuing drive, including a touchdown run up the middle from 12 yards out, in which Gordon acrobatically vaulted over a downed lineman. Tentatively expect Gordon to be the Dolphins’ starter in Week 5 against the Bengals and treat him as an RB2/FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: The South Florida Sun Sentinel’s David Furones reports that Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright is lining up with the first-team offense during pre-game warmups.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Dolphins RB Ollie Gordon is rotating in behind Wright, confirming Wright is the team’s current starter. That said, the Dolphins could still split the backfield workload almost evenly. We won’t know what the plan is until the game is underway. For now, Wright should be viewed as the slightly safer FLEX, though both running backs could get bottled up by the Vikings’ defense today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Wright sits atop the Dolphins’ depth chart with De’Von Achane (knee) done for the year. He will likely split touches with new No. 2 running back Ollie Gordon in a very difficult matchup against the Vikings this week. Both players are worth rostering, but they are shaky FLEX starters this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said Jaylen Wright (foot) should be good to go for Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Wright was a full participant in Thursday’s and Friday’s practices, which is a good sign for his Week 4 availability. If he doesn’t draw a questionable tag later in the day, we’ll go ahead and assume that the third-year back will be on the field when the Dolphins visit the Vikings. Wright should be in line for a decent day as far as volume is concerned, but it’s hard to invest much hope in him or Ollie Gordon, who will split work with De’Von Achane (knee) out for the remainder of the season. It’s hard to know how the touches could be distributed here, but fantasy managers shouldn’t be rushing to put either back in their lineups against a stout Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Wright should be rostered in 12-team leagues. He is now on track to play in Week 4 against the Vikings and is still listed ahead of RB Ollie Gordon on the Dolphins’ depth chart. The Vikings’ defense could bottle up this running back, but things might get a tad easier in Week 5 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) said he was “very close” to playing in Week 3 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Wright and RB Ollie Gordon are expected to split backfield touches moving forward, though this could be a fluid situation if one running back simply outplays the other. Gordon profiles as a burly grinder, while Wright may offer more big-play potential. It sounds like Wright has a strong chance of playing in Week 4 against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Bears declared QB Case Keenum, CB Malik Muhammad, RB Kyle Monangai, LB Keyshaun Elliott and DT Jayden Loving inactive for Week 9 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Monangai will miss one more week with the expectation being that the 24-year-old tailback will be good to go after the bye in Week 10. Keenum will be the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) will not play in Week 9 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Per Rapoport, Monangai is expected to return after Chicago’s Week 10 bye. Monangai has been out since Week 4. He finally returned to practice earlier this week, but it was for a single, limited session on Friday. He should be back in a 1B role when the Bears take on the Saints in two weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) returned to practice Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: The Bears are calling the tailback questionable for Week 9 against the Buccaneers. It’s the first time that Monangai has been able to practice picking up the injury a month ago against the Jets. It seems extremely unlikely that the 24-year-old will be able to play against Tampa Bay on Sunday night, but he appears to be on track to return after the Week 10 bye for the final stretch. Malik Muhammed and Tyrique Stevenson are also questionable for the Sunday Night showdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not participate in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: It’s back-to-back missed practices for the 24-year-old ahead of Week 9’s contest against the Buccaneers. It seems more than likely that Monangai comes back for Week 10 after the bye, but if he can get a full session in, there’s a chance he rolls against Tampa Bay come Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Monangai was an estimated DNP on Wednesday, still not practicing in any capacity since Week 4. He has missed four consecutive games and is trending to miss a fifth one in Week 9 against the Buccaneers. In any injury taking this long for a return, a full practice is the best indicator of a return but the Bears may just wait until after their Week 10 bye to bring Monangai back. D’Andre Swift is in line for a workhorse game once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Bears declared RB Kyle Monangai, QB Case Keenum, DB Malik Muhammad, OL Jordan McFadden, DL Jayden Loving, and OL Jordan van den Berg inactive for Week 8 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: No real surprises here after Monangai was ruled out for Week 8 on Saturday, leaving D’Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson to handle backfield duties in a difficult matchup against the Seahawks. The two had operated in a loosely split backfield before Week 7, during which Swift saw workhorse usage in a tight game against the Patriots. It would appear likely that Swift will once again see the bulk of the work considering the opponent, making him a surefire RB2 with RB1 upside to cap the Week 8 festivities.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Bears RB Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) is out for Week 8 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: No surprise here as Monangai hasn’t practiced since Week 4. He’s set to miss his fourth consecutive game against the Seahawks in Week 8. Roschon Johnson figures to continue to serve as the Bears’ RB2 with Monangai sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: We’d be floored if Monangai got on the questionable line on Saturday. He hasn’t played or practiced since Week 4. We’re still waiting for some kind of positive movement here. Roschon Johnson will likely be Chicago’s second-string back again in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Monangai has yet to practice after sustaining thumb and toe injuries in Week 4, with the potential that he misses his fourth consecutive game a very real possibility. The Bears held a walkthrough Thursday ahead of a Monday Night Football showdown against the Seahawks, meaning Monangai will have two more opportunities to get on the practice field ahead of Week 8. Fantasy managers are likely best making alternate arrangements considering the timing of the team’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) was not spotted at Chicago’s Tuesday practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: The Bears elected to have a practice Tuesday, as they prepare for a MNF matchup with the Seahawks, so they won’t have an injury report until Thursday. This isn’t exactly a strong sign that Monangai won’t make it back this week, but it also isn’t good news for managers that would like to see him active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker caught 4-of-5 targets for 29 yards in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker is now really going through it over his past three games, managing just seven total catches for 74 yards and a touchdown. If there’s “good” news, it’s that it has been an offensive-wide slump in Carolina, not just Coker. He and everyone else has a premium Week 10 get-right spot in the Saints, though Coker is starting to look more like a WR3 than the WR2 he was showing out as earlier in the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker caught 2-of-5 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers while also losing a fumble.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker’s fumble came on the last play of the game as the Panthers played pitchy woo woo in their attempt to tie the game. The 24-year-old didn’t have a catch in the first half, but salvaged his fantasy day — to a point, anyway — with a 26-yard touchdown from Bryce Young. The 24-year-old has just three catches over the last two games, and he’ll try and get things going against the Broncos in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 8 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker was at little risk of missing tomorrow’s game after getting in a full practice on Tuesday. He was listed as a full participant again today before being cleared for action. Despite the quiet Week 7 showing, which saw Coker catch just one pass, fantasy managers should still treat him as a WR2 for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker (shoulder) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Seems there’s little doubt that Coker will play on Thursday night. He’ll likely be removed from the injury report on Wednesday. Even after last week’s fiasco he likely belongs in the WR2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Panthers listed Jalen Coker (shoulder) as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: The Panthers won’t have their first official practice until Tuesday, but Coker would have been limited on Monday had the team been on the field. Coker caught one pass for nine yards in Week 7’s loss to the Buccaneers. His struggles came on a day when the entire Panthers offense was stymied for much of the day, so hopefully he’ll be in line to bounce back against the Packers on Thursday if he is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker caught 1-of-4 targets for nine yards in the Panthers’ Week 7 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker was also the intended target on the first of Bryce Young’s two interceptions. The wideout fell down, leading to the miscue. It was simply a nightmarish day for the Panthers’ offense, who also watched Young cough up a fumble-six. With the Panthers trailing 33-6 at halftime and 43-6 at the 10:21 mark of the fourth, the first-team offense sat for the game’s final 10 minutes. A disaster for fantasy managers, but likely a short-lived one with the Panthers heading to Green Bay for a short-week Thursday night matchup with the Pack. Coker must still be fired up as a WR2 for that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker caught 6-of-13 passes for 97 yards in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker missed Week 4 with a quad injury but was able to heal up over the bye week and play a full complement of snaps in Week 6. Initial reports had him playing 59 of the team’s 79 snaps and running a route on 39 of 46 dropbacks, which was second most on the team. He also led the team in targets, catches, and receiving yards. He’s a rock-solid WR2 against the Bucs next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker (quad) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Panthers coach Dave Canales told reporters earlier this week that Coker was returning from both quad and ankle injuries, though the team is only listing the quad issue. We take this as a good sign for his overall health. Coker can be treated as a WR2 in his first game back, facing an Eagles defense that struggles to cover opposing slot receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Jalen Coker (quad) is “on track” to play in Carolina’s Week 6 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker was spotted practicing on Tuesday (there will be no injury report for this one) and seems like he’s well on track to return. He’ll be a fringe WR2/WR3 against the Eagles in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Panthers WR Jalen Coker (quadricep) is inactive for Week 4 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: This was though to be the most likely scenario after head coach Dave Canales told reporters Friday that the team would elevate Ja’Seem Reed if the belief was that Coker could not go on Sunday Night Football. Reed was, in fact, elevated Saturday and Coker was declared inactive. Brycen Tremaine appears to be in line for a featured role after playing 81 percent of the team’s offensive snaps a week ago. Expect John Metchie to also see additional snaps and opportunities, while David Moore could see package usage on the perimeter. Also inactive for the Panthers are TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, QB Haynes King, G Damien Lewis, OT Albert Reese, and DT Cam Jackson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 4-of-6 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan’s four-yard touchdown with the Panthers attempting to complete a fourth quarter comeback was his first since Week 4 and only his third of the season. He has also now been held below 60 yards receiving in three straight games as Bryce Young has been mired in a slump. If there’s good news, it’s that McMillan has maintained a decent floor, and we know the next spiked week can’t be far away. It could come as early as Week 10 against the Saints’ soft defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-11 targets for 58 yards in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan had a long gain of just 14 yards, as Bryce Young just didn’t have time to get the ball down the field and wasn’t particularly accurate on the rare times he did. The wideout was targeted early and often, but it was an inefficient effort for the 23-year-old, at best. Even as the clear top option in this passing attack — all due respect to Jalen Coker — there’s a ton of volatility in McMillan’s fantasy profile, and that won’t change for Week 9 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 4-of-6 targets for 40 yards in the Panthers’ Week 7 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: Feel lucky McMillan even reached those marks, as the Panthers simply did not compete in a game where they committed four turnovers and trailed 33-6 at halftime. The first-team offense sat for the game’s final 10 minutes. McMillan had a better go of it than Jalen Coker, who caught one pass and fell down to create an interception. A shambles, though one the Panthers have to move on from quickly, as they are headed to Green Bay for a potential short-week shootout on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-9 passes for 86 yards in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan saw a lot of Quinyon Mitchell in tight coverage on Sunday, but he had a solid day that could have been much better after a fourth-quarter pass went off his hands in the end zone. It would have been a difficult catch with Mitchell draped all over him, but it was a catchable pass. More importantly, it shows that McMillan remains a key piece of this passing game, and he did run the most routes of any receiver on the team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 14-of-16 targets for 192 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 4 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan set career highs in both receptions and yardage in the first half with nine catches for 147 yards before the break. He operated as the clear alpha in a pass attack without both Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette, routinely dusting everyone the Lions had at their disposal in an injury-ravaged secondary. While the receiving line surely turns heads, fantasy managers were left even more ecstatic about the way in which he was utilized, with the second-year receiver catching six passes for 94 yards and both touchdowns while aligned in the slot. Offensive coordinator Brad Idzik is providing structure, sequencing, and situational tendencies unlike anything fans had grown accustomed to when head coach Dave Canales was helming the offense, resulting in quarterback Bryce Young leading the league in passing while averaging more than 30 points per game through the first month of play. McMillan’s ceiling remains sky-high as a legitimate WR1 when the Panthers square off against the Eagles fin Week 6 following their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 2-of-5 targets for 17 yards in the Panthers’ Week 3 loss to the Browns.
