https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: By far McMillan’s quietest outing of the young season came with Jalen Coker departing midway through with a quad injury. No. 3 Xavier Legette didn’t even suit up as he battled a knee issue. That allowed the Browns’ defense to key in on T-Mac, and key they did. Fill-in No. 2 Brycen Tremayne took advantage with four receptions for a team-leading 83 yards. Heinous stuff for McMillan managers, but he has an immediate Week 4 bounce-back spot in the defense-less Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 5-of-10 targets for 101 yards in the Panthers’ Week 2 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan took a backseat to Jalen Coker last week. The opportunities were distributed more evenly this time around. McMillan led the team with 10 targets and a 28 percent target share. Coker wasn’t far behind with nine targets. McMillan easily led the team in yards, though Coker caught eight balls and Darren Waller popped up for a two-score game. This offense may ultimately be too spread out for McMillan to reach his full potential, but Week 2 reaffirmed his status as the team’s top dog. He will be in the WR2 mix when the Panthers take on the Browns next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 5-of-8 targets for 75 yards in the Panthers’ Week 1 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan played distant second fiddle to Jalen Coker, who cooked the Chicago secondary for 138 yards and two touchdowns, leading the Panthers in air yards and targets. A bulked-up McMillan appeared a little slower than he was as a rookie in 2025, and had trouble separating for most of the game. Coker’s involvement and Bryce Young’s trust in his WR2 might be a problem for McMillan’s upside this season. He should, however, remains a decent weekly floor option, including next week against a gettable Atlanta defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports that the Panthers will “likely” decide whether to offer QB Bryce Young an extension in the 2027 offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: Young has two years remaining on his contract, but is currently eligible for an extension. According to Wolfe, Young needs to improve in three areas. First, Young must check down when it’s the responsible thing to do, in turn elevating his completion rate to the “high 60s, low 70s” range. Second, Young must be comfortable playing with tempo and diverse personnel formations, including WR Tetairoa McMillan lining up in the slot more often. Third, Young must play quickly and decisively. Whether he can accomplish these feats is up in the air. He’s a mid-to-low QB2 for fantasy purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: The Athletic’s Joe Person reports that Panthers WR Chris Brazzell will undergo season-ending knee surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: Brazzell was initially expected to avoid surgery and instead rehab the “moderate LCL tear in his left knee.” After getting a second opinion, the player and team decided surgery was the “best option” for the rookie’s long-term health. According to Person, Brazzell was expected to challenge WR Xavier Legette for the No. 3 role, while also potentially allowing WR Tetairoa McMillan to line up in the slot more often. The latter storyline is worth tracking. Hopefully, the plan remains in place and Brazzell makes a full recovery ahead of the 2027 season. We expect him to be placed on injured reserve soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmett Johnson had six rushes for 34 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson, fresh off a big receiving day in Week 8 against the Broncos, didn’t see much involvement until the Chiefs were up multiple scores in the fourth quarter. He ran in his first NFL touchdown on a goal line carry after Ken Walker — who had three touchdowns on the day — was resting on the sideline. Johnson remains one of the game’s most important and upside backup running backs and should be rostered in every league in case Walker misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmett Johnson caught all five of his targets for 128 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: He added one carry for 15 yards. Johnson racked up the bulk of his production on a 73-yard touchdown grab in the first half. The Broncos sent pressure and Patrick Mahomes perfectly lofted the ball to Johnson, who saw nothing but green grass ahead of him. The turf monster nearly took him down at the 10-yard line, but Johnson stayed upright enough and lost one final defender on his way into the end zone. He also picked up a 38-yard catch just before halftime to set up a last-second field goal. Johnson had more than two touches in just one of his previous three games headed into Week 8. Though he’s not going to challenge Kenneth Walker for RB1 duties anytime soon, this breakout performance should earn him a few more touches in Week 9. He will be have some value as a boom/bust FLEX play versus the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmett Johnson had three rushes for six yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: It was another Ken Walker explosion game (128 yards, two touchdowns on the ground) with Johnson serving as the breather back. Johnson should be rostered as a high-upside contingency option in case Walker misses any time in the coming weeks or months.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmett Johnson rushed six times for 17 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson was not targeted in the passing game. His six carries were nothing to sneeze at on an afternoon where the Chiefs were limited to 49 total plays, but that was compared to 20 Kenneth Walker touches. Johnson will have some pop-up standalone value behind workhorse Walker, but he is primarily a contingency option heading into the meat of the fantasy campaign.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said RB Emmett Johnson “will continue to get more snaps.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson has turned 14 touches into 103 scrimmage yards thus far. Evidently pleased with his fifth-round rookie, Reid wants to keep “allowing Emmett to grow,” in turn taking “a little bit of load off” starting RB Kenneth Walker. Reid notes that Walker wants the ball on every play and is not asking for a lighter workload, but Reid is seeking “a nice balance with those two in there,” which “keeps them even more fresh as the season goes on.” Walker, of course, remains an elite RB1. Johnson, however, should be rostered in all 12-team leagues as a high-upside bench stash that could return standalone value before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Chiefs waived RB Emari Demercado.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Demercado’s departure leaves rookie RB Emmett Johnson and second-year RB Brashard Smith to back up starting RB Kenneth Walker. The Chiefs also waived DE Vincent Anthony, LB Kam Arnold, WR Andrew Armstrong, WR Wesley Bissainthe, DT Cole Brevard, WR Jason Brownlee, WR Jacob De Jesus, OT Ethan Driskell, WR Omari Evans, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick, LB Cam Jones, WR Xavier Loyd, S Tanner McCalister, DT Amari McNeill, C Pete Nygra, RB Jaydn Ott, DT Damon Payne, CB D’Arco Perkins-McAllister, TE Mason Pline, S DeShon Singleton, CB Melvin Smith, EDGE Tyreke Smith, OG Josh Thompson, CB Zelmar Vedder, TE Tre Watson and WR Jeff Weimer. The Chiefs released LB Cole Christiansen, CB Kaiir Elam, CB Kader Kohou and EDGE Emmanuel Ogbah. The Chiefs placed DT Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) on the reserve/physically unable to play list and WR Jimmy Holiday on injured reserve. The Chiefs also waived OG C.J. Hanson, QB Chris Oladokun and RB EJ Smith with injury designations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmet Johnson rushed seven times for 39 yards in the Chiefs’ preseason game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson added two catches for 15 yards and had another chunk gain through the air called back because of a penalty. Kenneth Walker didn’t play in this contest, allowing Johnson to draw the start with some of KC’s first-team offense on the field. Johnson split reps with Emari Demercado over the team’s first three drives, then left the game for good. He looks like the team’s No. 2 back, though all three backs have been the next man up behind Walker at some point during the preseason. Johnson isn’t guaranteed the backup job, but he’s now the favorite, putting him in the mix as a late-round flyer in deeper fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Emmett Johnson was “one of the positives coming out of” their first preseason game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson had 12 carries for 59 yards and three catches for 10 yards against the Rams. While we’ve seen a little camp buzz about Johnson, The Athletic’s Jesse Newell presents this as a step forward for Johnson who “has been running with the fourth-string offense most of training camp.” He’s still probably the best back to have rostered in the event of a Kenneth Walker injury, but this isn’t such an important role that the backup necessarily needs to be rostered in standard redraft leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that Chiefs RB Emmett Johnson “is swiftly earning a role as an explosive, decisive runner.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Breer refers to RB Kenneth Walker as an “every-down” player, says RB Brashard Smith “has already shown he can be a weapon in space,” and notes RB Emari Demercado adds depth. Perhaps taking on a change-of-pace rushing role is in play for Johnson this season. The rookie back has pass-catching experience as well, but Smith and Demercado could offer more in that department at the moment. Johnson could be the next player up if Walker were to miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano believes Emmett Johnson “has a shot” to be Kansas City’s No. 2 back.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: The currently-murky situation behind Kenneth Walker includes the rookie Johnson, veteran receiving back Emari Demercado, and Player Who Is Nominally A Running Back Brashard Smith. The fifth-round pick sure seems like the best play here over the long-term, but if Johnson can win the No. 2 role out of camp, he’d hold some stash fantasy value behind Walker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 1-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor ran a route on 22 of the team’s 39 drop backs while Kenyon Sadiq has 21 routes and caught all four of his targets. Splitting the TE1 role with Sadiq, Taylor won’t be fantasy viable in most formats next week against the Bills. He has four receptions over his past two games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Sadiq logged 21 pass routes on the day to Mason Taylor’s 22 routes. The two tight ends have largely split the TE1 role in the New York offense in recent weeks. Taylor had just one catch on two targets against Kansas City, while Sadiq got open down the seam a couple times and found himself wide open for Geno Smith. Sadiq, who had five receptions over his previous four outings, won’t be usable in most fantasy formats next week against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (back) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor’s contributions are far too volatile for him to be trusted in 12-team formats, but his presence hurts rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq’s fantasy-scoring outlook. Taylor does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor is firmly on track to play in Week 9 against the Chiefs. He will operate as the team’s top tight end, keeping intriguing rookie Kenyon Sadiq in the TE2 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: It’s likely a maintenance day for Taylor, who tallied three catches on five targets in Week 8. He has been running ahead of rookie Kenyon Sadiq in recent weeks, though his own fantasy has been hit or miss. Taylor has been held under 40 yards in three of his past four appearances. He erupted for 62 yards and two scores in the fourth. Barring a setback in practice, Taylor will be a low-end TE2 for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 3-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor’s five targets were third on the team behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, while fellow seam stretcher Kenyon Sadiq mustered only two looks. Taylor has become a weekly volume presence in an offense that attempts a lot of passes, but he has not established a particularly high floor while his spiked week odds remain practically nonexistent. He’s a TE2 by the letter of the law but not one we would be looking to start in Week 9 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 5-of-6 targets for 62 yards and two touchdowns in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor got off to a hot start on National Tight Ends Day by mossing Dolphins cornerback Jason Marshall Jr in the end zone. Not content with just one score, Taylor double-dipped with a leaping touchdown catch late in the fourth quarter. He also scored the two-point conversion after the play. Taylor is running well ahead of first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq right now and there’s no reason to expect anything different in Week 8 versus the Raiders. Taylor will be in the TE2 mix next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 4-of-6 targets for 33 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor is now up to 7/57 in two games since returning from his thumb injury. First-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq, who missed most of Week 5 with a concussion, is 3/15 during the same timespan. This Jets tight end targets battle figures to oscillate back and forth, but Taylor is the preferred option for the time being. It’s still not resulting in more than desperation TE2 value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Kenyon Sadiq remains in the league’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: The good news is that Sadiq was able to practice in a limited capacity on Wednesday. Sadiq suffered the head injury in Week 5 against Cleveland and did not return to action. Mason Taylor led the team’s tight ends with a 59 percent route rate against the Browns, catching all three of his targets for 23 yards. If Sadiq remains in the protocol tomorrow, he would be a long shot to play in Week 6. Taylor in that case would be a desperation streaming option in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 3-of-3 targets for 24 yards in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Active for the first time since Week 2, Taylor caught the second most balls on the team as Kenyon Sadiq departed with a third quarter concussion. Those are awful developments for Sadiq managers, but almost certainly not enough to create TE2 value for Taylor, even if Sadiq misses Week 6 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 4-of-5 targets for 32 yards in the Lions’ Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta was the only Lion outside of Amon-Ra St. Brown to catch more than two passes. He accounted for a fifth of Jared Goff’s targets, but the team’s low-volume passing approach meant there wasn’t much volume to go around. LaPorta has gone cold in recent weeks with three straight games under 40 yards. He’ll look to get back on track as a mid-range TE1 versus the Patriots next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 3-of-5 targets for 33 yards in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta had a quiet day against a Minnesota defense that has shut down opposing tight ends for much of the season. He had at least 80 receiving yards in each of that past two Detroit games. LaPorta had been a serviceable starting tight end headed into Week 8, and should have a better outlook in Week 9 against the Bills. He’s been targeted on 18 percent of his routes on the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 1-of-2 targets for 18 yards in the Lions’ Week 7 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: While Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams combined for 244 yards and two touchdowns, LaPorta was an afterthought in the Lions’ offense on Sunday. LaPorta’s first target didn’t come until late in the fourth quarter, and his first catch came in the fourth quarter on an 18-yard play. It was an uncharacteristically underwhelming game by LaPorta, who entered the day coming off two-straight games in which he topped 80 yards and found the end zone. Despite the dud performance, LaPorta will be in the TE1 ranks next week at home against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports “it’s more likely than not” that the Lions work out an extension with TE Sam LaPorta before free agency.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: According to one of Jones’ sources, Lions GM Brad Holmes “does not like losing his draft picks, especially high ones.” A second-rounder in 2023, LaPorta made waves earlier this week when he expressed frustration with his lack of a contract extension on the Pardon My Take podcast. While those frustrations persist, the 25-year-old tight end clarified some of his comments to local Detroit media Friday, reiterating his desire to stay with the Lions long-term. Jones notes that other extensions the Lions have handed out have taken some time to get done. He also cautions that the team shouldn’t wait too long to sign LaPorta as the Raiders are unlikely to waste time making Brock Bowers the highest-paid tight end in football when he becomes extension-eligible after the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta said he wants to continue playing for the Lions long-term.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: Earlier this week, LaPorta expressed frustration in an interview about his contract negotiations stalling in-season. The Athletic’s Colton Pouncy asked him a few follow-up questions today on the matter today, and LaPorta made clear that he hopes to remain a Lion long-term and is excited about the prospect of raising a family in Detroit. LaPorta seemed extremely earnest, saying he felt bad about his comments potentially causing a distraction for his team, but he knows his teammates care for him and want him to be happy and compensated. He handled the issue well and appears to be ready to play hard for a lucrative contract extension, which is good news for fantasy managers. LaPorta is a locked-in TE1 against the Packers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 5-of-5 targets for 88 yards and one touchdown in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta got involved on the Lions’ third drive, making a clutch 12-yard grab on 4th-and-3 while suffering what the officials deemed an unnecessarily rough hit by LB Mack Wilson at the end of the play. He chipped in two catch-and-run plays on the following drive. The first being an 11-yard play that was controversially ruled down in front of the sticks. Coach Dan Campbell called his number on the next play, resulting in an effortless 38-yard touchdown down the right side of the field. LaPorta tacked on an eight-yard catch and a 19-yard catch in the second half as the Lions cruised to a blowout win. He goes on bye next week but returns to the TE1 ranks in Week 7 against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 8-of-13 targets for 84 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 4 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta was the primary beneficiary against the single-high-heavy Panthers, which was interesting considering both of Carolina’s top two corners were absent from this game. The 13 targets were easily a season high for the veteran tight end, primarily the result of 52 Jared Goff pass attempts in what would become a negative game script. LaPorta routinely found space behind the linebackers as the primary outlet through pressure for Goff, and while it remains unlikely he repeats the lofty target totals, LaPorta’s red zone acumen keeps him a fantasy TE1 ahead of a very different matchup in the two-high-heavy Cardinals in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sam LaPorta and the Lions “have broken off contract talks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: Rapoport did note that the Lions could make another push to sign LaPorta later this year, so the door isn’t entirely closed. LaPorta is set to become a free agent next offseason. The team could, however, place the franchise tag on him. He has gotten off to a quiet start with 14 catches for 144 yards and one score. LaPorta is currently on pace for a career-low in yards per game. He would still have plenty of suitors in free agency, even if the counting stats don’t improve this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 3-of-4 targets for 44 yards in the Lions’ Week 3 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta was a secondary piece of the passing attack in this game, taking a backseat to Jhamyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown. The two superstars combined for 16 targets while LaPorta and Jameson Williams were held to a combined eight looks. LaPorta has at least 44 yards in every game this year but no more than 52. With a solid floor established, all that’s left is for LaPorta to hit on a ceiling game. He remains a mid-range TE1 for Week 4 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 6-of-7 targets for 52 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 2 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta combined with Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs to be the primary targets for quarterback Jared Goff on a night where relentless pressure from the Bills forced the offense to primarily attack the intermediate areas of the field. That could be the norm for this offense moving forward considering the mounting injuries along their offensive line, which are likely to be felt the most against opponents with a legitimate pass rush. That may not be the case in Week 3 when the Lions host the Jets, a team that is likely to also utilize elevated rates of zone coverage. LaPorta has had stark man-zone splits throughout his career and could see less volume due to matchup. He’ll be a low-end TE1 against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Mason Taylor caught 1-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Taylor ran a route on 22 of the team’s 39 drop backs while Kenyon Sadiq has 21 routes and caught all four of his targets. Splitting the TE1 role with Sadiq, Taylor won’t be fantasy viable in most formats next week against the Bills. He has four receptions over his past two games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq logged 21 pass routes on the day to Mason Taylor’s 22 routes. The two tight ends have largely split the TE1 role in the New York offense in recent weeks. Taylor had just one catch on two targets against Kansas City, while Sadiq got open down the seam a couple times and found himself wide open for Geno Smith. Sadiq, who had five receptions over his previous four outings, won’t be usable in most fantasy formats next week against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Mason Taylor (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Taylor is firmly on track to play in Week 9 against the Chiefs. He will operate as the team’s top tight end, keeping intriguing rookie Kenyon Sadiq in the TE2 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught a 22-yard pass in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq’s third quarter reception went down as one of just two targets for the rookie tight end. He was once again out-caught by Mason Taylor, though Taylor provided just 19 yards across his three grabs. Sadiq’s reception was an impressive, leaping catch against single coverage, but therein lies part of the problem: It’s taking spectacular acts for Sadiq to create fantasy value. He is sadly off the radar for the time being in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught his only target for six yards in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: The first-round rookie was held to one catch for the second week in a row. He has four catches over his past four games. It wouldn’t be surprising for his role to expand as the season wears on, but there were no signs of that happening this week. He isn’t worth holding onto in most fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught 1-of-3 targets for 12 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Although there was an injury-shortened appearance mixed in, Sadiq now has just three catches for 15 yards over his past three games. This, as Mason Taylor has caught nine balls for 57 yards over the past two weeks. Sadiq’s big-play ability is going to come back into play sooner rather than later, but he is unsurprisingly maxing out as a zero-floor TE2 in fantasy for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is active for Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq made quick work of the league’s concussion protocol, for better or worse. With Omar Cooper Jr. also active vs. the Pats, Sadiq isn’t much more than a low-end TE2 prayer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq left Week 5 with a concussion. He was upgraded to a full practice on Friday and seemingly cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend. With Mason Taylor and Omar Cooper Jr. back for Week 6, there will likely be fewer targets to go around in a Jets offense that has regressed heavily over the past two weeks. Sadiq is a low-end TE2 for his date with New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is questionable for New York’s Week 6 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: He did upgrade to a full practice and Aaron Glenn told reporters he expects Sadiq to play. Sadiq’s fantasy upside is well-known, but with Mason Taylor back and Omar Cooper Jr. also pushing to play, his target volume has shrunk quite a bit from some of the early-season scenarios we’ve seen. He’s likely a TE2 at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: He has been limited twice and doesn’t look close to clearing concussion protocol. It’s become rarer for players to launch a Friday comeback to get off protocol, but it’s not unprecedented. Sadiq looks like he’s on the doubtful side of questionable heading into Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley rushed 13 times for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 9 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: It was a horribly inefficient day for the Eagles’ superstar back, but there was not a whole lot he could do with the Giants understandably not respecting the “threat” presented by No. 3 Philly quarterback Joe Milton. Barkley at least saved face with his three-yard scoring plunge in the first quarter. Having his snaps and touches rationed for this injury-ruined and tanking team, Barkley will probably have a hard time getting back into the RB1 ranks when Philly comes off bye in Week 11 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley will again play through his hamstring and back injuries. Touchdowns have helped offset Barkley’s moderate yardage totals, and the offense will now be led by Joe Milton. Barkley’s role and talent keep him in the high-end RB2 tier, though an apex outcome is perhaps unlikely, given the state of the Eagles’ offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley is again on track to play through his injuries on game day. The Eagles’ offensive centerpiece totaled 54 scrimmage yards, one catch and one touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 8 loss to the Commanders. He may have trouble solidifying a spot in the RB1 tier, given the state of the Eagles’ offense, but he remains a high-end RB2 at worst, based on talent and usage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) was not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley played through the pair of injuries last week, turning 13 carries into 30 yards and a score. While this could just be maintenance for a banged-up veteran, the Eagles are waving the white flag on 2026 by starting Joe Milton at quarterback. If they’re worried about making Barkley’s injuries worse, the team may simply shut him down for the year at some point. Elijah Mitchell is the next man up for Philly if Barkley doesn’t play in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley said the Eagles informed him that they don’t intend to trade him ahead of the NFL trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Speaking with the media early Monday morning, Barkley said he was informed that the team would not be trading him despite falling to 2-6 on the season after Sunday night’s loss to Washington. Barkley rushed 13 times for 30 yards and a touchdown in the loss while catching one pass for another 24 yards. The soon-to-be 30-year-old back could have decent trade value for the Eagles in what is shaping up to be a lost season, but it sounds like he’s in the team’s future plans heading into 2027. Barkley is playing through injuries and has just 56 carries for 274 yards and two touchdowns this season, and has caught seven passes for another 41 yards. Assuming he can get in another week of practice this week, he’ll be a fringe RB1/RB2 in Week 9 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley rushed 13 times for 30 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 8 loss to the Commanders, adding 24 yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley showed clear limitations as he played through hamstring and back injuries, routinely spotted on the sideline riding the stationary bike and getting stretched out by trainers as he rotated with Elijah Mitchell. The Philadelphia offense remained largely ineffective as they gained only 268 yards of total offense, while Barkley’s longest carry of the game went for only five yards against a solid Washington run defense. Fantasy managers will want to consider their alternatives when the Eagles face the Giants in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Saquon Barkley “will not be traded before next week’s trade deadline.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Though teams can change their minds in very short periods of time, Rapoport’s wording on this matter is rather definitive. Sitting at 2-5 with Jalen Hurts out for the year, it makes sense for the Eagles to be sellers at the trade deadline. Players including Dallas Goedert, Riq Woolen, and Hollywood Brown have also been the subject of trade rumors. All three are more likely than Barkley to land with new teams over the next week. Barring a change of heart from GM Howie Roseman, Barkley will continue to be the focal point of a failing offense for the remainder of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring, back) was removed from the injury report Friday and will play in Week 8 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley gave a cryptic response when asked if he would play earlier in the day, ultimately ready to gut out multiple injuries as the Eagles continue to trudge forward in an injury-decimated season. The veteran back added that the injuries are both something he will need to manage throughout the game but that he feels as if he can play through them. That leaves fantasy managers in a sticky situation, likely forced to start Barkley if he’s on the roster. Barkley is a middling RB2 in a difficult matchup on the ground against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) was spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: After being a DNP in each of the Eagles’ first two practices of the week, it’s far too early to be confident that Barkley will suit up on Sunday night against the Commanders. That said, his return to the field is still an encouraging sign for the Eagles, whose backfield is suddenly among the most banged up in the league. We will check back in when the Eagles announce Barkley’s Week 8 status, but it wouldn’t be surprising if this ends up being a game-time decision, which could prove frustrating for fantasy managers. We should know more on his availability in the next few hours.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) was not spotted at Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: This doesn’t look ideal. Barkley practiced all week leading up to his return, and at this point he doesn’t even have a limited session ahead of Sunday’s game with the Commanders. There’s probably not a zero percent chance that Barkley is playing, but at this point the best Barkley-reliant managers can likely hope for is a questionable tag on Friday. Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue would be in line to form some sort of committee if Barkley can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 1-of-2 targets for 31 yards in the Lions’ Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: We’re not sure if a player can be due for a catastrophic bust of a fantasy week, but “Jamo” was probably due for a catastrophic bust. He came into this game red hot, with 208 yards and five touchdowns over his past three games. Given Williams boom/bust nature, a flop was always right around the corner. He also dropped one of his two targets, which didn’t help his cause. The Lions get a potential shootout with the Patriots next week, meaning fantasy managers can safely keep Williams in their lineups as a WR3 despite today’s quiet outing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 4-of-6 targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Williams scored the Lions’ lone passing touchdown on a short corner-of-the-end-zone grab in the first half. Williams was second behind Amon-Ra St. Brown in targets, functioning as the primary downfield threat with a nice 46-yard catch on a Jared Goff shot down the middle. Williams, who came into Week 8 with the 16th most air yards among wide receivers this season, should remain in lineups next week against a vulnerable Buffalo secondary that has struggled against boundary wideouts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 5-of-9 targets for 91 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 7 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Williams wasted little time getting involved early in this one. On the Lions’ fifth play of the game, he ripped off a 24-yard gain to the Packers’ 16-yard line. On the next play, Williams came in motion and snuck out of the Lions’ backfield to turn a short pass into a 16-yard score, giving the Lions their first points of the day. Williams would find the end zone again in the third quarter on a 10-yard touchdown, and on the following drive, he nearly scored again. Were it not for a Packers defender knocking him out of the back of the end zone on a catch, we would have seen a hat trick. Williams’ big-play ability was on display all night, as three of his five receptions went for 15-plus yards. Williams now has back-to-back two-touchdown performances to his name and has gone for 90-plus yards in two of his last three games. His volume continues to be inconsistent, but Williams is capable of breaking any game open at a moment’s notice. He will be a fringe WR2 in what could be a tough Week 8 matchup against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 2-of-4 targets for 47 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: The Lions’ speedster only caught two passes today, but he made them count. Williams’ first catch was a nine-yard, fourth-down touchdown on the Lions’ fifth drive. He nearly hauled in a 25-yarder via a play-action target on the sixth drive, but Cardinals CB Max Melton batted it away. He was open for an explosive gain on the next drive, but Jared Goff checked down to Sam LaPorta about 10 yards beneath Williams. A few plays later, Williams dusted his coverage defender for a 39-yard score from bunch formation, hauling in the touchdown pass in stride in the end zone. Goff later gave him another touchdown chance on a downfield throw targeted inside the Cardinals’ five-yard line, but Williams couldn’t secure it. He’ll now take a week off with the Lions’ Week 6 bye, but return as a WR2 against the Packers in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 6-of-8 targets for 102 yards in the Lions’ Week 4 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Fantasy managers had suffered through three down games with the middle-round pick before Williams was able to take advantage of a Carolina secondary missing its top two corners. He was kept out of the end zone for the fourth consecutive contest to start the 2026 season but returned his first fantasy-viable outing on the backs of 52 Jared Goff pass attempts. While that level of volume is unlikely to be the norm for the Lions, a Week 5 meeting with the Cardinals provides another opportunity for Williams to return value in a potential shootout. Williams will be an upside WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: The Detroit Free Press’s Dave Birkett reports Jameson Williams will not face assault charges stemming from an incident with a woman on August 6th.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: The incident was reported to the police earlier this month. Jeff Wattrick, spokesman for the Oakland County Prosecutor, told Birkett, “Based on the facts presented to us at this time, the Novi Police and our office jointly concluded that there is no cause to file charges against Mr. Williams.” Williams has been an off-field headache for the Lions since entering the league, but it doesn’t sound like this latest incident will be an issue. He will be on the field for the team’s Week 4 date with Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in the Lions’ Week 3 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Drew Petzing schemed up a few short and intermediate looks for Williams, but he still finished with a measly 12.5 percent target share. Both Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown saw eight targets. Williams has topped out at four catches through three weeks. His 49 yards today are a season-high. Williams closed the 2025 season as an every-week WR2, maybe even more. That usage has all but disappeared to start the 2026 season. He is tumbling back into the WR3 ranks heading into the Lions’ Week 4 game against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 2-of-4 targets for 33 yards in the Lions’ Week 2 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Williams continues to be primarily utilized as a deep threat in the Detroit offense, which is not the development fantasy managers were expecting following offseason reports that his route tree would be expanded in the new year. The mounting injuries along the offensive line have limited Goff’s time in the pocket to the point where Williams rarely has enough time for his routes to develop, leading to the down production through two weeks. Whether either of those two variables changes in the immediate future remains to be seen, leaving us to treat Williams as nothing more than an upside WR3 in the interim. He will be a difficult start in Week 3 when the Lions host the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Lions head coach Dan Campbell said he’s “not concerned” with Jameson Williams’ drops.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: At least a couple times a year Campbell has to tell reporters that he’s not worried about Williams’ sometimes-egregious drops, and that his playing time won’t suffer as a result. “I mean, look, nobody’s more frustrated than he is about it, but what I love is this just shows his growth,” Campbell said. “He bounced back, he gets back in the huddle. He’s not sulking, he’s not pouting about it, he’s not letting it go in the tank.” Williams in Week 1 against the Saints had two drops, one of which could have gone for a long score. He led the Lions with 128 air yards (a 56 percent share) and was second on the team with a 23 percent target share. Williams ran a route on 37 of Detroit’s 40 drop backs. He should be locked into lineups for Thursday night’s matchup against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 4-of-9 targets for 45 yards in the Lions’ Week 1 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Williams posted a semi-usable fantasy score, but the film was hard to watch. He dropped a perfectly thrown deep shot from Jared Goff early in the game and bungled a pitch later, resulting in a loss. Williams has had these types of games in the past and he generally rebounds well. Fantasy managers can keep him in their lineups for a likely shootout with the Bills next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed 16 times for 79 yards in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos, adding four receptions for 17 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: Hubbard’s 16 totes were his second fewest since Week 2, though fantasy managers will at least take the 96 yards from scrimmage. Handling huge workloads and snap counts, Hubbard hasn’t always maintained his efficiency under such voluminous usage, though we have yet to see any red flags in 2026. He will remain a strong option on the RB1/2 borderline for Week 10 against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed 22 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers, adding seven receptions for 38 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: Hubbard was easily the most effective offensive player for the Panthers, but that’s at least partially an insult to everyone else as much as it was compliment to him. The tailback was able to make the most of the limited rushing room, and with Bryce Young having zero time to throw the football, he was a frequent target of Young’s checkdowns. Trevor Etienne received just one carry for one yard, meanwhile. Hubbard’s usage makes him a high-end RB2 for Week 9 against the Broncos, even if it’s more floor than ceiling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed seven times for 33 yards in the Panthers’ 43-13, Week 7 loss to the Bucs, adding four receptions for 27 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: With Bryce Young committing three turnovers — killing drives and setting up Bucs short fields that took the Panthers out of run-friendly game script — Hubbard had little shot at providing fantasy-friendly returns this afternoon unless he found the end zone late. He did not, with those honors going to “Anthony Tyus III” in garbage time. It was just one of those days in Charlotte. Thankfully the Panthers don’t have long to stew, as they must now get ready for a short-week Thursday evening road date with the Packers. With most Pack — and Panthers — games projecting as shootouts these days, Hubbard will remain safely ensconced in the high-end RB2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed 28 times for 120 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: It wasn’t easy for Hubbard, who didn’t have many runs over 10 yards, but he ran hard, broke tackles, and was able to find the end zone in the fourth quarter for a short touchdown run. Still, the Panthers did have some issues running the ball up the gut against the Eagles and continued to do it, rather than try to get Hubbard going on the edge. Trevor Etienne was the only other running back to have a carry in this game, and he had just one rush, so this backfield belongs entirely to Hubbard, which is tremendous for his fantasy value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed 20 times for 122 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 4 win over the Lions, adding seven yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: Hubbard’s successes on the ground allowed the Panthers to remain balanced on a night they were without two of their top three wide receivers due to the absences of Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette, cashing in on two scores from 15 and two yards out. Hubbard appears to be locked into an RB1 workload in the absence of Jonathan Brooks, who will be out for 6-8 weeks after undergoing core muscle surgery. His 26 opportunities dwarfed the six of current backup AJ Dillon, the latter of whom gained just seven total yards on six touches. Fantasy managers can start Hubbard with confidence when the team returns from their bye to face the Eagles in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed 19 times for 82 yards in the Panthers’ Week 3 loss to the Browns, adding four receptions for 28 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: With Jonathon Brooks on injured reserve, Hubbard’s 23 touches were nine more than he handled in Week 2, and 10 more than Week 1. Although he ceded a smattering of snaps to new backup AJ Dillon, he was a near every-down player in this road loss. Hubbard lacks high-end fantasy upside, but his floor right now is very much that of a locked-in RB2. That will be especially true for matchups like next week’s date with the defensively-challenged Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Panthers will host a workout for Austin Ekeler, formerly of the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: Carolina is in need of some backfield reinforcements after losing Jonathon Brooks to a core injury that will leave him sidelined for at least six weeks. AJ Dillon is set to fill in for Brooks while Chub Hubbard presumably continues as the team’s lead back. Ekeler, 31, who hasn’t played since injuring his Achilles last September, could be an emergency running back if Hubbard or Dillon go down with injuries in the coming weeks. First he’ll need to make the squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed 12 times for 53 yards in the Panthers’ Week 2 win over the Falcons, adding two catches for 11 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: Hubbard operated as the Panthers’ unquestioned RB1, out-carrying Jonathon Brooks 12-5. He got on the board early with a touchdown catch near the goal line. It was his second touchdown grab of the year and his third time finding the end zone in total. Brooks also left the game early with a groin injury and his status for Week 3 is up in the air. Hubbard was already going to project for RB2 numbers with Brooks in the middle. He will push to the middle of the RB2 pack if Brooks is out versus the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Chuba Hubbard had ten rushes for 49 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 1 loss to the Bears, adding three catches for 38 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: Hubbard was the clearcut lead back for the run-heavy Carolina offense. Jonathon Brooks saw five touches on the day, and ran six pass routes for 29 routes for Hubbard, who was the Panthers’ primary red zone back throughout the game. For now Hubbard’s role in the run-first Panthers offense seems secure while the team eases Brooks into action. That could change at some point this season. Hubbard will be a locked-in RB2 option next week against a middling Falcons defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.headline: Jonathon Brooks had four rushes for 14 yards in the Panthers’ Week 1 loss to the Bears, adding one catch for 48 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chuba-hubb.analysis: In his first regular season action, Brooks played well behind lead back Chuba Hubbard, who finished the day with ten carries and three receptions. The highlight of Brooks’ day came on a sideline throw from Bryce Young that went for 48 yards. Brooks, coming off multiple major knee injuries, showed impressive burst and speed on the catch and run. That Hubbard was the team’s primary option inside the ten yard line is bad news for Brooks’ touchdown upside in the Carolina offense. For now he profiles as a bench stash in case Hubbard misses time this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed four times for 18 yards in the Broncos’ Week 9 win over the Panthers, adding a four-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins operated as a pure breather back for this one, getting out-touched 21-5 by Jonah Coleman and out-snapped 58-11. Dobbins did receive two touches inside the Panthers’ 20-yard line — one of which was nullified by penalty — but none inside the 10. It sure looks as if the Broncos are ready to ride rookie Coleman, making Dobbins a shaky 12-team league hold since the Broncos are now headed on bye. They return in Week 11 against the Raiders. The odds are strong Dobbins will not be in your starting lineup for that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed seven times for 13 yards in the Broncos’ Week 8 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins got the Bronocs’ first touch on offense and immediately took a backseat to Jonah Coleman. The rookie tallied 11 carries and five targets. He also became the first Bronocs running back to hit 100 yards from scrimmage in a game this year. Dobbins was not targeted and was not on the field at the goal line, where Coleman was heavily involved. Coleman ultimately punched in a goal line touchdown for the game-winning score after setting himself up with a 51-yard catch. The short-yardage role used to belong to Dobbins, but the rookie appears to have taken that as well. Without any high-value touches to work with, Dobbins is a between-the-20s grinder averaging a little over three yards per carry this season. He is falling back into the RB4 ranks for his Week 9 date with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed six times for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins was the team’s preferred option at the goal line, allowing him to save a bust of a fantasy day with a one-yard score in the second half. He was initially stood up at the goal line but made it in the paint by driving his legs through the contact for six. Dobbins was held under 10 points even with the touchdown. Jonah Coleman returned this week and led the team in carries with nine. Harvey ran the ball just three times. This backfield is a messy, three-man committee and Dobbins doesn’t get to pad the stats with PPR-friendly targets. He will shuffle to the back of the RB3 ranks for his Week 8 date with the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: Broncos designated Jonah Coleman (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Coleman can return to practice this week and the team now has 21 days to bring him off injured reserve. He could be back on the field as soon as Sunday. With the Broncos’ offense struggling and two backs already seeing work in the backfield, it’s hard to imagine Coleman having much fantasy value in his first game back. He’s worth stashing in deeper leagues, but it might be a while before fantasy managers want him in their lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed 17 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins found little room to run on a night the Broncos gained only 168 yards of total offense but handily led the backfield in opportunities in what was a consistently positive game script due to the dominance of their defense. Dobbins has now failed to eclipse a modest 50 yards on the ground in four of five appearances but might be useful as a bye week fill-in when the Broncos travel to Arizona to face the Cardinals in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed 18 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins was the most effective offensive player for both teams, which isn’t quite the compliment you’d think it is. The 27-year-old was the bellcow for the Broncos, however, and he was able to keep the chains moving enough to give Denver the victory over the winless Chargers. Dobbins will likely find the sledding tougher in Week 6 when the Broncos face the Seahawks on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: JK Dobbins had 11 rushes for 40 yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers, adding two catches for 12 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins, as usual, led the Denver backfield in carries but lost out to RJ Harvey on pass routes and targets. In fact, Harvey led the Broncos with ten catches on ten targets in a check-down heavy game plan for Bo Nix and OC Davis Webb. Dobbins has been touchdown-reliant as the Broncos’ lead back, and sensitive to game script, as we saw in Week 4. Dobbins can be used as a flex next week against a vulnerable Chargers run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins (hip) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins practiced in full this week, so he should be ready to handle his typical workload against the 49ers this week. The Broncos’ lead rusher has played very unproductively this season, failing to hit 7.0 PPR points each week. The Broncos’ defensive line has been hit hard by injuries. Perhaps Dobbins can steady himself in the RB2/FLEX ranks against them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins (hip) is practicing in full for Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: RJ Harvey was checked for a concussion in Week 3 and is not on the injury report today, meaning both backs are good to go for Week 4. Dobbins saw 17 carries versus the Rams compared to just two for Harvey, though the latter caught six passes. Dobbins caught one pass. The rushing advantage will keep Dobbins in the RB3 mix for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed 17 times for 49 yards in the Broncos’ Week 3 win over the Rams, adding four yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins and the rest of the Denver offense have been subject to poor situational tendencies from first-time play caller Davis Webb’s offense through three weeks. Dobbins is the player arguably hit the hardest with poor play sequencing as the bulk of his work comes on early downs. Even so, Dobbins now has a higher share of the backfield opportunities following the placement of Jonah Coleman on IR Saturday. Dobbins is a shaky RB3 ahead of a Week 4 showdown with the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman rushed 17 times for 57 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 9 win over the Panthers, adding four receptions for 31 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman also put the ball on the ground near his own goal line on a Bo Nix pitch, but the Broncos were thankfully able to recover. Also thankfully for fantasy managers, coach Sean Payton continued to look Coleman’s way late after the miscue, including the very next play. Coleman experienced really strong usage in Charlotte, playing 58-of-75 snaps per PFF’s initial count while easily setting a new career high with his 21 touches. He has also now cleared 80 yards from scrimmage in back-to-back contests. It must be noted that today’s score was not a goal-line carry — it came from nine yards out — but he did receive a first quarter carry from the Panthers’ four-yard line. Coleman’s role continues to grow, thus far without setback. Hopefully that does not change when the Broncos come off bye in Week 11 against the Raiders’ soft defense. We will be ranking Coleman as a strong RB2 for that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman rushed 11 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 8 win over the Chiefs, adding four catches for 63 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman out-carried Dobbins 11-7 and was the only Broncos running back to earn a target, of which he saw five. Most importantly, Coleman was on the field for goal line duties, and he cashed in with a touchdown late in the fourth quarter. Though he only averaged 3.7 yards per carry, Coleman was a handful for Chiefs defenders to bring down, routinely creating missed tackles while racking up yards after contact. Coleman’s best rep of the day was a 51-yard catch-and-run to set up his touchdown on the next play. Coleman saw all of the high-value touches in the backfield while leading the way in carries and targets. The takeover is all but complete, putting Coleman in the RB2 ranks for Week 9 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: RJ Harvey (knee) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Harvey was added to the injury report Thursday with a knee injury before being unable to practice Friday, ultimately ruled out for the team’s divisional clash against the Chiefs. Expect Jonah Coleman to serve as the primary rusher in addition to the possibility he sees his pass game involvement tick up in the absences of both Harvey and Tyler Badie, the latter of whom is on injured reserve. The increase in opportunity is enough to vault Coleman into viable FLEX territory for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Broncos coach Sean Payton, asked about Jonah Coleman, said touches were “something you earn and he’s done a good job of that.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: He also noted that Coleman’s touches were explosive. It’s hard to sit here with much certainty about what looks to be a three-headed Broncos running back room where every back has their niche, but Coleman probably enters Week 8 as the favorite of the three to crack 10 touches. Payton added, for the 17th time since he became Broncos coach, that he needed to get more touches for Marvin Mims on offense. We’ll believe that when we see it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman rushed nine times for 54 yards in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals, adding two catches for 15 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman returned to action after missing a month because of an ankle injury. He was immediately in the mix for touches and saw three opportunities before RJ Harvey got his first look. Coleman went on to lead the Broncos in carries. Both he and Harvey earned two targets apiece. Unfortunately for Coleman, he was the only Denver back who didn’t find the end zone in Week 7. Coleman has made a mess of a backfield that had just begun to stabilize. Now all three Denver backs will be low-end FLEX options for Week 8 versus the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman (ankle) is active for Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper is also active. Coleman hasn’t played since Week 2, when he turned 10 carries into 39 yards and a score. The Broncos were banged up at running back that week. They have since established a stable two-man rotation with JK Dobbins operating between the tackles and RJ Harvey handling passing downs. Coleman will likely take a backseat to those two this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Broncos activated Jonah Coleman (ankle) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman missed the minimum four games as he tended to an ankle injury suffered in Week 2. He led the team in snaps in that contest and could return to the primary rushing role considering the inefficient play of J.K. Dobbins in his absence, making him worthy of a start in fantasy circles in a plus matchup against the Cardinals in his first game back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman practiced in full all week, but the Broncos could technically give him another week to rehab the ankle. If active, there are too many unknowns regarding Coleman’s potential workload to start him in the FLEX, but he must be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman is trending toward returning for the Broncos’ Week 7 game against the Cardinals. His teammate, RB Tyler Badie (thumb), remains sidelined. Coleman makes for a risky start if active, but the Broncos’ coaching staff likes him. He should be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Broncos designated Jonah Coleman (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman can return to practice this week and the team now has 21 days to bring him off injured reserve. He could be back on the field as soon as Sunday. With the Broncos’ offense struggling and two backs already seeing work in the backfield, it’s hard to imagine Coleman having much fantasy value in his first game back. He’s worth stashing in deeper leagues, but it might be a while before fantasy managers want him in their lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gregory-de.headline: Greg Desrosiers rushed three times for 20 yards in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gregory-de.analysis: The Giants’ “No. 2 running back” with Cam Skattebo (hamstring) on the shelf, Desrosiers was charted as playing only five snaps, but his 20 yards on three touches were just 19 fewer than Devin Singletary generated on 23 handles. Translation, if Skattebo can’t go for Thursday evening’s short-week date with the Commanders, UDFA Desrosiers might be in line for more work following Singletary’s stink bomb against the Eagles. That’s a 14-team league waivers dart calling your name.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gregory-de.headline: Giants signed RB Gregory Desrosiers off the Chargers’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gregory-de.analysis: The first-year UDFA rushed for 166 yards on 23 carries in the preseason for the Chargers, adding one touchdown and one eight-yard reception. We’d be surprised if he got real run in this backfield but at least he has the bye week to acclimate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin caught 1-of-2 targets for 55 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: Dulin’s lone reception went for a 55-yard touchdown on a simple screen late in the third quarter to bring the Colts within three, but it likely came with the veteran journeyman sitting on waiver wires. Dulin is a name to keep an eye on ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline as his role could be growing, pending what the team does with Josh Downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is not on Indianapolis’ final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: With Tyler Warren down, Dulin probably figures to join Keenan Allen and Josh Downs as one of Indianapolis’ three main receivers. He has some desperation play viability in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin (hamstring) won’t play in Indianapolis’ Week 5 game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: After dealing with an ankle injury that sidelined him most of the first three weeks, Dulin picked up a hamstring injury and did not practice all week before being ruled out ahead of this game. Laquon Treadwell prayer starts remain on the fantasy football menu.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: Dulin made his 2026 debut in Week 4 after missing the first three games of the year with an ankle injury. He’s now at risk of returning to the bench because of this hamstring injury. With Keenan Allen back at practice, Dulin’s role was going to decline either way. Laquon Treadwell would be the team’s No. 3 receiver if he is ruled out for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin caught 3-of-6 targets for 29 yards in the Colts’ Week 4
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: Dulin was active for the first time this year. His return could not have come at a better time with Keenan Allen ruled out over the weekend. Dulin took on a starting role and wound up leading the team in targets, tied with Laquon Treadwell. The Colts couldn’t get much going through the air and settled for spreading the ball around instead of peppering their top pass-catchers with targets. It’s hard to imagine them taking that approach again in Week 5. Even if they do, Dulin is more of a thorn in the sides of Tyler Warren and Josh Downs than a FLEX option in his own right.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin (ankle) will play in Week 4 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: With Keenan Allen ruled out and Alec Pierce on IR, Dulin is now in line to be the Colts’ No. 2 receiver in his season debut. The passing attack will run through Josh Downs, putting him comfortably inside the WR2 ranks. Inactive for the Colts are WR Keenan Allen, WR Darius Slayton, RB DJ Giddens, QB Riley Leonard, EDGE George Gumbs, and OG Dalton Tucker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Colts WR Ashton Dulin (ankle) will not play in Indianapolis’ Week 3 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: Laquon Treadwell prayer starts are officially on the menu for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Colts declared WR Ashton Dulin, LB Austin Ajiake, RB DJ Giddens, DE George Gumbs, QB Riley Leonard, and G Dalton Tucker inactive for Week 2 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: No real surprises here as the Colts look to snap the longest active losing streak in the league, having lost their previous eight games dating back to last season. Alec Pierce could see an increase in snaps and utilization after week of healthy practices.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Alec Pierce (heel) is practicing in full for Week 2 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: The Athletic’s James Boyd noted that Pierce also had his wrist X-rayed after the game, though neither that nor the heel injury is a concern for him going forward. Ashton Dulin missed practice with a hamstring injury. Pierce was targeted six times in Week 1 despite having his snaps limited. He caught four passes for 61 yards. He will be a boom/bust WR3 for his Week 3 matchup with Kansas City.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd believes Ashton Dulin is the team’s third receiver “for now.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: He mentions Nick Westbrook-Ikhine and seventh-round pick Deion Burks as possible competition for the spot. We also (our speculation) wouldn’t rule out the Colts picking up one of the several as-of-yet unsigned free agents like Jauan Jennings, Deebo Samuel, or Stefon Diggs. Westbrook-Ikhine has flashed big touchdown upside in the past and would be the most fantasy-useful player in this group if he wins a role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Devin Singletary rushed 21 times for 31 yards in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles, adding two receptions for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Charted by Pro Football Focus as playing 62-of-67 snaps with Cam Skattebo (hamstring) on the shelf, Singletary was an every-down player, but a predictably ineffective one. In fact, his performance was just the third time this decade a player generated fewer than 40 yards from scrimmage on 20-plus touches. The 29-year-old lost what little remained of his explosiveness several years ago, and should never end up in a position where he is “forced” to be an every-down back. With Skattebo supposedly “pushing to play” this afternoon, hopefully he will be ready for Thursday evening’s short-week date with the Commanders. If not, Singletary will be a low-upside FLEX who might cede more snaps and touches to rookie UDFA Greg Desrosiers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is “pushing to play” in Week 9 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Skattebo was listed as doubtful for Week 9 after getting in a single limited practice this week. Players rarely suit up after getting the doubtful tag, but it’s not out of the question. Even if he is ruled out with inactives, the fact that Skattebo is pushing to play means he should be good to go for Week 10. Devin Singletary will handle the bulk of the backfield touches if he can’t go this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: At this point, Devin Singletary should be considered the tentative starter for the Giants’ Week 9 game against the Eagles. Singletary could handle a sizable workload, though he was buried on the depth chart as the No. 3 running back for a reason. Singletary warrants volume-based FLEX status if Skattebo cannot play this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said Cam Skattebo (hamstring) remains day-to-day.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports that Skattebo once again worked with trainers off to the side at today’s practice. He will be listed as a non-participant. With Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) on injured reserve, Devin Singletary is tentatively in line to start in Week 9 against the Eagles. He would likely be an RB3/FLEX if Skattebo cannot play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Giants GM Joe Schoen said the Giants will place Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Well that sorts out the Giants backfield for the short term. Devin Singletary will take over as the primary passing down back behind Cam Skattebo and should be a usable FLEX play going forward. Tracy will miss the next four weeks after going down with the hamstring injury in the second quarter of New York’s win over the Texans in Week 7. Schoen indicated this isn’t a season-ender for Tracy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Devin Singletary rushed five times for 41 yards and a touchdown in New York’s Week 7 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: He didn’t get much usage in this one, managing just 19 snaps despite Tyrone Tracy leaving in the second quarter, but Singletary made the most of his final opportunity with a 30-yard touchdown run in overtime to walk off the Texans. With Tracy and (apparently) Skattebo both managing injuries throughout the bye, Singletary could wind up with a reasonable Week 9 role. You probably don’t need to chase it on waivers this week unless you’re in a very deep league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan believes Cam Skattebo “will be back in the mix” in Week 7 against the Texans, likely in “some sort of timeshare with Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Sigh. Three-player backfields are generally fantasy-unfriendly situations, and this one is no different. Skattebo is a capable dual-threat player who has seemingly been limited by the significant ankle injury he suffered last year. The Giants could get him more involved in the passing game, but Tracy can contribute there as well, muddying that opportunity. Singletary would not be a contributor for many NFL teams, but lucky him, he’s a New York Giant. Skattebo and Tracy are viable FLEX options, though both are likely touchdown-dependent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Giants released Najee Harris.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: The move comes a couple days after Harris criticized the New York coaching staff for its handling of the backfield touch distribution. “It’s hard to get into a rhythm with one or two plays...if you’re getting a play here and then get taken out for a series, there’s nothing you could do,” Harris said after the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints. “I’ve never been through none of this before.” Harris had 31 rushes for 99 scoreless yards before getting the boot. With Harris gone, Cam Skattebo could get another chance to see increased playing time after being all but benched last week. Tyrone Tracy, who led the team in rushing attempts against New Orleans, could be the de facto lead back for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Devin Singletary rushed four times for 14 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints, adding one reception for 19 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Singletary saw 31 snaps on the day, leading Giants running backs in a pass-happy game script. It’s unclear what the Giants backfield will look like moving forward, but it’s a messy committee for now. Singletary and Tyrone Tracy seem to be the preferred options for passing down snaps, though Tracy is the preferred choice for more high leverage situations. Singletary is worth a waiver claim but fantasy managers should stay tuned to wade through the coach-speak and see what this Giants backfield looks like for Week 7 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Giants declared S Jason Pinnock, RB Devin Singletary, CB Nikko Reed, DT Bobby Jamison-Travis, OT J.C. Davis, and QB Jake Haener inactive for Week 5 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Singletary is once again a healthy scratch as the Giants will roll with Cam Skattebo, Najee Harris, and Tyrone Tracy as their top three backs. J.J. McCarthy will serve as the QB2 behind Jameis Winston in what figures to be a messy game in the elements in Washington this afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 18-of-32 attempts for 162 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs, adding one rush for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: The 36-year-old Smith was as immobile as ever, taking five sacks on the day and narrowly avoiding a half dozen others. Some of that was the Jets offensive line being overwhelmed against an elite KC pass rush; some of it was Smith refusing to get rid of the ball as the pocket collapsed. Smith playing without Garrett Wilson (concussion) was irate on the sideline in the fourth quarter with the Jets down multiple scores, barking at coaches and teammates alike. He had a negative EPA per drop back on the day. Smith should be seen as a matchup-dependent fantasy play. He will be streamable in Week 10 against a vulnerable Buffalo secondary.
