Lamb and the Cowboys now have over a week to rest up before facing the Packers on Sunday Night Football in Week 6. Barring an unexpected development, we would expect Lamb to be good to go for next week’s game against the Packers at Lambeau Field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb (quad) is questionable to return to Week 5 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb departed in the fourth quarter with a quad injury. He tried to return but managed one snap before making his way back to the sideline, coming back on the field later in the drive for a two-point attempt. He was shown on the sideline in visible discomfort following the additional two snaps. Lamb managed to catch just 2-of-5 targets for nine yards prior to departing. Fantasy managers will want to track his status in the coming week, although the additional recovery time could allow him to avoid any missed games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 17-of-21 targets for 189 yards and a touchdown in Dallas’ Week 3 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: He simply could not be stopped the way the Texans were playing defense. Lamb feasted on the sideline and against zone coverages — his longest catch went just 30 yards — and he had the go-ahead touchdown with less than 30 seconds left that had FOX’s Greg Olsen wondering why any defense would play him that way when he’d been that productive over the course of the game. He’d never managed more than 17 targets in a game before today. Obviously he won’t do this again, but Lamb has delivered for those who lucked into him in the late first-round mix and will again be a plug-and-play alpha WR1 against the Bucs on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 7-of-8 targets for 112 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 3 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: That makes it back-to-back games of 100-plus yards for Lamb. Lamb didn’t officially find the end zone on this one, but he did come up with a catch on a two-point reception in the third quarter to cut the Ravens’ lead to 24-21. He came up with a few big plays in the fourth quarter, with his biggest being a 49-yard reception on a drive that ended with a KaVontae Turpin rushing touchdown to briefly give the Cowboys the lead. Despite being out-targeted 11 to 8 by George Pickens in this one, Lamb has looked like the unquestioned WR1 for the Cowboys through the first three weeks. He’s totaled 15 receptions for 265 yards and two touchdowns over the last two weeks and is a high-end WR1 in next week’s game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 8-of-9 targets for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 2 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb caught three passes on the Cowboys’ opening drive, picking up gains of 15 and 23 yards before connecting with Dak Prescott on a three-yard score. Lamb gave the Commanders fits all day, but strung together another massive drive late in the fourth quarter when he hauled in a 35-yard pass from Prescott, who went right back to him five plays later for a 24-yard touchdown on a pass Lamb had to fight to come down with. Lamb has now scored in each of his first two games this season and will be firmly on the WR1 radar in next week’s game against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: Shedeur Sanders completed 19-of-31 passes for 297 yards and two touchdowns in the Browns’ 23-22, Week 9 overtime loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: Sanders added 10 carries for 28 yards. He struggled to get much of anything going for three quarters before finding the big one in the fourth. Sanders threw a bomb to KC Concepcion, who tracked the ball well and then outran two defenders for a 64-yard score. Sanders’ second touchdown came in overtime on a grown-man catch-and-run from Harold Fannin. Cleveland opted for a two-point conversion to go for the win, but Sanders couldn’t connect with Denzel Boston after being flushed out of the pocket. It took a while, but Sanders at least looked like a viable backup in this contest, which wasn’t the case at any point last year. He’ll return to his QB2 gig in Week 10, keeping him off the fantasy radar for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Deshaun Watson cleared the league’s concussion protocol but will be inactive for Week 9 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: Watson returned to practice on Friday for a limited session and cleared the league’s protocol over the weekend. Still, after preparing Shedeur Sanders to start throughout the week, head coach Todd Monken decided not to throw a curveball at his own team on game day. Sanders will start and Dillon Gabriel will back him up. Watson has rebounded this year, but the lows are still staggeringly low. He took eight sacks in a blowout loss to the Steelers last week. If Sanders plays well today, Monken will at least have something to think about ahead of Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said Shedeur Sanders will start in Week 9 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: Sanders will draw the start as Deshaun Watson (concussion) has yet to clear protocol in time to be ready for Sunday’s game. Interestingly, Watson is still expected to be listed as questionable, per Monken, but Sanders will draw the start. We are assuming this decision is based on Sanders taking first-team reps after Watson missed each of the first two days of practice, but this is a nice opportunity for Sanders to show whatever growth he has made since a tough rookie season in which he threw for 1,440 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions in eight games played. He’ll be on the low-end QB2 radar on the road against the Saints, who rank 16th in fantasy points allowed to opposing QBs this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: Deshaun Watson (concussion) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: Cleveland’s Mary Kay Cabot indicated yesterday that Shedeur Sanders is seemingly slated to start in Week 9 against the Saints. If that ends up being the case, and Sanders can play well enough, it might be possible for him to steal the starting job from Watson this week. Sanders would be QB2-viable against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: Cleveland.com’s Mary Kay Cabot said the “vibe” is that Shedeur Sanders will start in Week 9 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: Cabot said it would be a challenge for Deshaun Watson to clear the NFL’s concussion protocol by Saturday and suit up for Sunday’s game. Watson suffered a head injury in Week 8 against the Steelers and reported concussion symptoms on Tuesday, according to the Browns. Sanders in 2025 was the most inaccurate quarterback in the league and struggled to support fantasy-relevant pass catchers. Harold Fannin could see a boost with Sanders under center after Sanders targeted the tight end relentlessly during his 2025 starts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: Browns placed Deshaun Watson in the NFL’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: Watson took a hit to the head in the first half of the Browns’ Week 8 loss to the Steelers. He was evaluated for a brain injury and re-entered the game. He then reported concussion-like symptoms on Tuesday and entered the protocol on Wednesday. It would be somewhat surprising if Watson is able to clear the protocol in time for the Browns’ Week 9 matchup against the Saints. That would likely mean Shedeur Sanders would get the starting nod against New Orleans. Sanders should only be rostered in superflex formats for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter said Shedeur Sanders could start in Week 3 if Deshaun Watson plays poorly in Week 2.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: Schefter said it “feels like Shedeur’s time is coming” if Watson bombs in the Browns’ Week 2 matchup with the Bucs following his Week 1 collapse against Jacksonville. Sanders, in that scenario, would be under center for the Browns’ home opener against the Panthers in Week 3. Sanders, who is slightly more accurate than Watson in the short and intermediate areas, would be an upgrade for Harold Fannin and KC Concepcion. He would likely be a downgrade for downfield air yards eater Denzel Boston.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports “the belief is that the first two games would serve as a natural evaluation point” for Deshaun Watson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: The Browns open the year with a two-game road trip before returning to Cleveland for their home opener next week. Watson was a disaster in Week 1, turning the ball over twice while throwing for 205 yards and one score. Another showing like that versus the Bucs this week and he could be sent to the bench. Shedeur Sanders would then draw the start against Carolina in Week 3. It’s unlikely the Browns offense turns things around under Sanders, but things truly cannot get worse than they are right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said he’s confident in Deshaun Watson’s downfield passing ability.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: Monken has stressed explosive plays as an important part of the Cleveland offense headed into the 2026 regular season. “Obviously having explosive players helps that,” Monken said. “Being able to scheme it up against certain looks and then being able to execute because your protection has to hold up when you get those opportunities. I’m confident in Deshaun and our ability to push the ball down the field, otherwise we wouldn’t be starting him.” That confidence might be misplaced considering Watson completed just 1-of-6 attempts for 20 yards and an interception on downfield passes in the preseason and was among the league’s worst deep ball passers in 2024, when he threw downfield on a career-low 27 percent of his attempts. Once an elite deep ball thrower, Watson will look to regain form coming off two torn Achilles, entering his age-30 season. Perhaps rookie WR Denzel Boston will be a boon for Watson’s downfield game in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: Browns HC Todd Monken said it’s possible QB Taylen Green will be active for Week 1 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: When speaking with the media on Monday, Monken said, “There could be a package where we have (Green)” on the field. Monken also suggested he would prefer to not have three QBs active on game day , which could mean Shedeur Sanders would be a healthy scratch. Even if this were to happen, we shouldn’t assume this means Sanders is behind Green on the depth chart. As long as Deshaun Watson is in the QB1 seat, the Browns’ weekly game plan won’t include Sanders, while Green’s explosiveness on the ground could add another element to the offense in select packages, making him a more valuable option on game days. If Watson were to miss time due to injury or lose the starting job, we would still expect Sanders to be the next man up, with Green continuing to serve in select packages.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 20 times for 101 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 9 win over the Colts, adding 23 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Williams notched his second 100-yard game of the season, tacking on a fourth quarter score with less than two minutes remaining to push his fantasy production into RB1 territory. Week 9 also marks the third straight week in which the Cowboys utilized a new-look, run-heavy game plan, this time utilizing Tyler Goodson to soak up carries behind Williams. Williams has now seen 20 or more carries in three straight and will remain a volume-based RB1 in a difficult matchup against the 49ers at home in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 24 times for 56 yards in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Woof. The Cardinals simply overwhelmed the line of scrimmage with run blitzes and dared the Cowboys to do something about it; they often didn’t. Williams also fumbled away a goal-line tote only for it to wind up as a Cowboys touchdown by landing in the hands of journeyman tight end James Mitchell. Things should be easier next week against the Colts, where Williams will remain a reasonable RB1/high-end RB2 tweener.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 25 times for 155 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 7 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Williams churned out consistently positive gains against the injury-riddled Eagles but took off in the fourth quarter, gaining over 60 yards in the final frame. He cashed in for fantasy managers with a touchdown with just over two minutes remaining on the clock to push his line into elite territory, despite failing to notch any receptions. The career high in yardage on the ground comes after the Cowboys averaged the fewest rush attempts per game during the first six weeks of the new season. Williams gets a sparkling matchup against the Cardinals at home in Week 8, where he’ll return to RB1 status in fantasy circles following the eruption against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 11 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers, adding nine yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Williams has now been held to 3.8 yards per carry or fewer in five of six games and 45 yards on the ground or fewer in four of six games, with seven combined touchdowns keeping his fantasy value afloat through the first third of the regular season. Williams has now seen 12 or fewer carries in four of six contests to start the year. The good news is that the Cowboys have no choice but to keep riding Williams until the wheels fall off considering the general lack of depth in the backfield, meaning there are likely to be better days ahead for the veteran back. He gets another middling matchup on the ground against the division rival Eagles in Week 7, where he will be a volume-driven RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 12 times for 45 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 5 loss to the Buccaneers, adding 17 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Williams has now averaged 3.8 yards per carry or fewer in four of five games, keeping his fantasy value afloat via six combined touchdowns through five weeks. While the touchdown equity is solid in one of the league’s most potent offenses, we’re liable to see more down weeks like the one he put forth against the Buccaneers unless, or until, the Cowboys can fix their woes on the ground. Williams did see all but one running back opportunity in this one, keeping him in the top six in backfield opportunity rate through Week 5. Consider Williams a volume-aided and touchdown-aided RB2 ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the reeling Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 19 times for 62 yards and three touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 4 win over the Texans, adding five catches for 21 yards on his only five targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Williams had a very easy rushing score — his first one where he only had to beat one defender to the outside after a pair of pulls. He also had a very hard one, where he dragged several Texans defenders into the red zone. The Cowboys didn’t run the ball much, but when they did it was effective. Williams was averaging 5.1 yards per tote before the second half, where he simply lived in the goal-to-go set. He’ll be on the low-end RB1 line in Week 5 against a Jalon Daniels-led Bucs outfit on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 19 times for 98 yards and one touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 3 loss to the Ravens, adding two receptions for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: The Cowboys drew up a lot of carries for Williams early in this one. The 26-year-old back totaled seven carries for 45 yards on his team’s first two possessions, and punched in a two-yard score late in the fourth quarter to put the Cowboys up 10-0. Williams would mostly be bottled up by the Ravens after his score, but he did break free for a 22-yard run in the third quarter that helped set up a Brandon Aubrey field goal — which was blocked. This is undoubtedly the best game of the season for Williams, who hadn’t gone for more than 41 yards in either of his first two games. That said, he still struggled at times to get going on the ground, as seven of his carries went for two or fewer yards. His volume remains reliable enough to keep him in the RB2 conversation for next week’s game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 12 times for 30 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 2 win over the Commanders, adding three receptions for 20 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: The Cowboys dominated through the air on Sunday, but the same can’t be said of their efforts on the ground. Washington bottled up Williams all afternoon, with his biggest play coming on a nine-yard run on the Cowboys’ final drive. Williams has just 71 rushing yards on 24 attempts (3.0 YPC), but has also seen nine targets in his first two games. He remains the unquestioned leader of the Cowboys’ backfield and will be a volume-based RB2 in next week’s game against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 12 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 1 loss to the Giants, adding five receptions for 31 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Williams understandably operated as a clear workhorse for a Cowboys team with little depth at the position following Malik Davis’ season-ending injury earlier in the week. His two second half scores and five receptions masked poor rushing efficiency on a night the Cowboys ran only 52 offensive plays, although a robust 32.7 percent total opportunity share foreshadows the potential for continued elite counting stats for the remainder of the regular season. Fantasy managers can continue to start Williams as a volume-driven RB1 as the team prepares to host the Commanders in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said RB Jaydon Blue and RB Phil Mafah “are going to get a bunch of work” in the preseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Per Schottenheimer, Blue and Mafah “are in a tight battle for the backup running back spot.” Blue has received positive reports for some time now. His speed and receiving ability make him an ideal complement to starting RB Javonte Williams, who “probably won’t get a whole lot of run” in the preseason. If Blue can secure the role, he could warrant FLEX treatment on a weekly basis. Mafah (6'/234) is a burly rusher. Were he to win the RB2 job, he may be ill-suited to playing on passing downs, which could benefit Williams. We’ll see how things shake out in the preseason. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: The Athletic’s Jon Machota believes Jaydon Blue is “the ideal fit” to be a complementary option to Javonte Williams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Machota noted Blue’s pass-catching ability as the biggest reason for him to potentially see some work behind Williams. Blue caught 42 passes for 368 yards and six scores during his final season at Texas. He then flopped as a rookie, seeing just one catch and 38 carries in total. The bulk of his opportunities came in a meaningless Week 18 game. Still, Dallas did nothing to address their backfield depth this offseason and head coach Brian Schottenheimer has talked up Blue’s work ethic this time around. With a strong training camp, Blue could cement himself as a change-of-pace option for the Cowboys, putting him on the menu for fantasy drafters in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 21-of-34 passes for 335 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys’ 27-23, Week 9 win over the Colts, adding one yard on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: The two teams played to a maddening field position battle through the first three quarters in what was one of the least disciplined games in recent memory, including a multitude of penalties on key downs, two turnovers, and a missed field goal from the Cowboys. A poor fourth quarter saw the Colts snatch the lead with a late field goal, but a 46-yard deep connection with Ryan Flournoy on the the play of the subsequent possession allowed the Cowboys to take the lead with just over a minute remaining in the fourth quarter. A Caleb Down interception ended the game, allowing Prescott and the Cowboys to escape with a win to send them to 4-5 as they chase the Giants in the NFC East. Up next is a home test against the 49ers in Week 10, where Prescott will remain a back end QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 19-of-29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown in Dallas’ 33-30, Week 8 loss to the Cardinals, adding seven carries for 20 yards and a touchdown on the ground.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: If you’re wondering, it was Prescott’s first rushing touchdown since Week 12 of the 2025 season against the Eagles, and his first game with seven carries since Week 5 of the 2025 season. The gist of it is: The Cardinals big blitzed a lot and vacated several underneath zones to allow Prescott to run. Dallas often tried to solve things pre-snap, and they often did — but not often enough to win. Dallas was either throwing haymakers or quickly finding themselves going three-and-out, as they did in overtime. Prescott will get to rebound quickly in Week 9 against a Colts outfit that barely qualifies as a serious football team amid what has the look of a fire sale.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 15-of-27 passes for 212 yards and three touchdowns in the Cowboys’ 38-21, Week 7 win over the Eagles, adding eight yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: Prescott made the throws when they counted while connecting on three touchdowns to his two alpha receivers, two to CeeDee Lamb and one to George Pickens. After averaging the fewest rush attempts per game through the first six weeks of the regular season, the Cowboys leaned heavily on Javonte Williams against a battered Eagles team; Williams set a career high with 155 yards on the ground. Even so, Prescott did not look his best, nor did the pass offense. Lamb committed two drops and the team benefited from multiple first downs due to penalty. Prescott gets another sparkling matchup against the Cardinals at home in Week 8, where he remains a fantasy QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 34-of-54 passes for 258 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Cowboys’ 23-13, Week 6 loss to the Packers, adding seven yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: Prescott and the Cowboys were completely unable to get anything going prior to the half, managing just 92 yards of total offense while taking a 17-point deficit into the break. They would force a three-and-out to start the third quarter and follow it up with a touchdown drive to get on the board, but a punt and two turnovers on downs left them trailing by 16 until a late score inside of two minutes remaining in the final frame. Prescott’s two interceptions occurred deep in Green Bay territory in the second quarter, removing much needed points from the scoreboard in what was then a tight game. The loss drops the Cowboys to 2-4 and looking up at the Giants for the division lead through a third of the regular season. Prescott will be a back-end QB1 on the road against the division rival Eagles in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 24-of-42 passes for 316 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Cowboys’ 24-16, Week 5 loss to the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: The two interceptions on Dak’s ledger were both in-and-out of his receivers’ hands, the second of which hit tight end Jake Ferguson in the face mask to allow the Buccaneers to ice the game in the fourth quarter. The first “pick” bounced off the hands of Ryan Flournoy to allow the Buccaneers to establish an 11-point lead at the beginning of the third quarter, a deficit the Cowboys would be unable to overcome. That said, Prescott wasn’t at all at his sharpest, missing numerous throws wide in addition to a few badly under-thrown balls in the second half. To make matters worse, alpha wide receiver CeeDee Lamb departed the game in the fourth quarter with a quad injury. The Cowboys fall to 2-3 and find themselves looking up at both the Giants and Eagles ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Packers at Lambeau. Prescott returns to QB1 status in what has become a soft matchup, pending the health of Lamb.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 32-of-45 passes for 335 yards and one touchdown in the Cowboys’ 34-30, Week 4 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: He had just 87 passing yards at halftime, but the Cowboys turned up in a major way in the second half by peppering CeeDee Lamb with targets and getting George Pickens matched on Kamari Lassiter to their benefit. Prescott was surgical against the blitz and led a game-winning drive after C.J. Stroud briefly put the Texans up 30-27, leading the Cowboys 74 yards in 1:43 by brutalizing the Texans’ zone coverage. Dak should remain in the QB1 ranks next week against the woeful Buccaneers on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 25-of-40 passes for 276 yards and one touchdown in the Cowboys’ 34-31, Week 3 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: Dak and the Cowboys came out with a run-heavy approach early, but Prescott was efficient through the air when given the chance. He was able to get both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens involved in this one, with the two receivers combining for 14 receptions for 194 yards on the day. Prescott’s lone touchdown pass came on a 19-yard strike to Jake Ferguson in the third quarter to cut the Ravens’ lead to 24-21, but on the Cowboys’ final drive in the fourth quarter, he would go 3-of-6 passing for 36 yards while adding another nine yards on the ground to help set up a game-tying field goal by Brandon Aubrey. A literal last-second field goal moments later would give the Ravens the win, but Prescott and the Cowboys have now gone for 30-plus points in back-to-back weeks. He’ll be a fringe QB1/QB2 in next week’s game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 26-of-31 passes for 279 yards and four touchdowns in the Cowboys’ 37-20, Week 2 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: Dak and the Cowboys faced little resistance from the Commanders’ defense in this one. The Cowboys came out firing from the start, as Prescott orchestrated a 10-play, 66-yard opening drive that ended with a three-yard touchdown pass to CeeDee Lamb, who had three receptions on the drive. Prescott threw his second touchdown of the game to Jake Ferguson, who broke free in the end zone for a 10-yard score, and in the third quarter, the two connected again for a 12-yard score. Dak found Lamb for a 24-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter to set the Cowboys’ franchise record for career touchdown passes (249), putting the finishing touches on what was an impressive day. Prescott will be a fringe QB1/QB2 in next week’s game against the Ravens in Rio De Janeiro.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 22-of-34 passes for 175 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Cowboys’ 28-20, Week 1 loss to the Giants, adding 14 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: A first half in which Prescott was victimized by drops and penalties from his supporting cast was completely overshadowed by a defensive performance that saw the Giants go 9-of-10 on third down and amass 394 yards of total offense. The Cowboys saw the ball only twice in the second half, scoring touchdowns on both drives, but it was ultimately not enough as they fell to 0-1 for the second consecutive season. Prescott’s lone interception came on a prayer ball down the sideline on third down at the end of the first half, eventually leading to a go-ahead touchdown for the Giants as they took a 14-7 deficit into the break, one they would not overcome. The Cowboys now turn the page to Week 2 as they prepare to host another division opponent in the Commanders in what has quickly become a near must-win game for both teams. Prescott will look to return to the QB1 ranks in a plus matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports that the Cowboys “had high interest” in former Texas Tech QB Brendan Sorsby when he shared plans to enter the NFL Supplemental Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: Archer cites multiple sources on this one. Sorsby’s gambling issues were reportedly not enough to dissuade the Cowboys from considering him as a potential long-term replacement for QB Dak Prescott, who turns 33 next week and is signed through 2028. In the end, the NFL declined to hold a supplemental draft this year, preventing the Cowboys from potentially drafting him at “a lower-than-expected price.” Perhaps they will revisit the idea next offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas caught 6-of-8 targets for 70 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas made several big plays, including a highlight-reel grab in the first quarter that saw him high-point the ball for a 20-yard gain. He also had his fair share of rookie blunders. Douglas dropped a pass on fourth down late in the fourth quarter. Detroit was able to run out the clock after getting the ball back. Douglas was also the intended target on Malik Willis’s lone interception of the day. Willis told reporters after the game that it was the result of a miscommunication between the two. The good news for Douglas is that the Dolphins are in development mode. Growing pains are part of the process and Douglas’s errors shouldn’t cost him playing time going forward. He will be in the WR3 mix when Miami takes on the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas caught 4-of-6 targets for 43 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Malik Willis did not throw a pass to Douglas until just over a minute left in the first half. The talented rookie came down with both two-minute drill targets for a total of 24 yards. He caught two more passes in the second half, seemingly injuring his right ankle while being tackled on the first. He managed to return for the next drive and helped set up Kevin Coleman’s 35-yard touchdown with a 12-yard reception. Douglas should be rostered in most 12-team leagues. He is a WR4/FLEX against the Lions next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas caught 2-of-3 targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas was active for the first time since suffering an ankle injury in Week 2. Though he logged a measly 14 percent target share, Douglas was involved early, turning a first-quarter red zone target into his first NFL touchdown. Douglas turned his second catch of the day, a short out route, into a 63-yard touchdown by toe-tapping his way along the sideline for a game-sealing score. His role is only going in one direction after the breakout performance. He will be in the WR3 mix when the Dolphins take on the Pats next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Dolphins WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) will play in Week 7 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas hasn’t played since Week 2 against the 49ers, but the rookie caught five passes for 94 yards in his pro debut against the Raiders and has been targeted on 16.4 percent of his routes. Stuck in a Dolphins offense that currently ranks 31st in scoring and passing yards, Douglas will be hard to trust as anything more than a fringe WR3/WR4 this week against a top-five Jets pass defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) remained limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: That’s back-to-back limited sessions from Douglas as he attempts to come back from an injury suffered in Week 2. We’d bet on him getting to the questionable line at this point given the significant layoff, but he does have a real chance to play against the Jets in Week 7 and be a WR4/FLEX candidate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas told reporters that he has finally progressed to being “day-to-day,” giving him a real chance to suit up in Week 7 against the Jets. Douglas should be added in 12-team formats. He played very well early on and will likely warrant FLEX consideration upon his return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) won’t play in Miami’s Week 5 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas has not practiced or played since Week 2. If only there were some sort of “injured reserve list” he could be placed on. Ah well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Dolphins coach Jeff Halfey said Douglas is “doing better” but is not ready to practice yet. It sounds like the rookie will miss another week. Malik Washington will continue to operate as the Dolphins’ No. 1 receiver, putting him in the WR3 mix for Week 5. Fellow rookie Chris Bell has seen his role grow every week, but the fantasy numbers aren’t there to match. He was held without a catch on three targets in Week 4. Bell is a solid long-term stash but barely cracks the WR5 ranks for Miami’s matchup with the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said the team is taking it “one day at a time” with Caleb Douglas’ ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: It’s hard to know what to make of this, but Douglas has missed back-to-back games with his injury and could be at risk of missing a third straight game if he can’t get on the practice field ahead of Week 5’s game against the Bengals. Douglas did not practice at all last week, so even getting on the field in a limited capacity would be an improvement. His name will be one to keep an eye on when the Dolphins release their first injury report on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Dolphins declared WR Caleb Douglas, QB Brady Cook, CB Marcellas Dial, EDGE Rob Beal, OG DJ Campbell, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick and TE Justin Joly inactive for Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: The Dolphins will be without Douglas, one of their two talented rookie wide receivers, against the Vikings’ top-tier defense today. He is sidelined by an ankle injury. Joly, the Dolphins’ rookie tight end, is inactive after making his debut last week. Cook wil serve as the team’s emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall had 15 rushes for 61 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs, adding three catches for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Finally returning from his multi-month quad injury, Hall took over as the Jets’ lead back even after Braelon Allen had a nice run as the team’s RB1. Allen ended up with 10 touches on the day, including eight carries. Hall looked spry, dodging would-be tacklers and creating yards after first contact on a handful of his touches. It seems Jets coaches were serious when they said Hall would resume lead back duties upon his return. Hall’s role in the Jets offense should make him a locked-in top-24 option, including next week against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports the Jets have no desire or intention to trade RB Breece Hall.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: While the Jets traded young players for draft picks last season, don’t expect New York to do that again this year. A team source told Jones the Jets moving Hall is “very unlikely to happen.” Hall appears ready to return from a quad injury in Week 9 against the Chiefs, but is difficult to trust in fantasy with Braelon Allen potentially cutting into his workload after a strong showing in Hall’s absence in recent weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) will play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: This comes a day after Hall said he expects to play, so this news isn’t all too surprising. Hall’s return could somewhat complicate the Jets’ backfield situation on Sunday, however, as Braelon Allen has played well in Hall’s absence, making a strong case for more touches even when Hall is healthy. Glenn declined to get into how he plans to divvy up his running backs’ touches next week, saying “both guys will play,” when asked about his plans. This was already shaping up to be a tough fantasy matchup on the road against the Chiefs, but a potential backfield split would only further complicate matters. Until we see how things shake out, both Hall and Allen should be viewed as mid-to-low-end RB2s.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) said he is ready to go for Week 9 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: We expect to see Hall listed as a full participant on today’s injury report. An update will be provided if that is not the case. Earlier today, Jets OC Frank Reich discussed Hall and Braelon Allen’s expected usage, saying having the two players is “a great problem to have,” referring to the duo as “two No. 1 backs.” That said, Reich added that Hall “is obviously the bell cow,” but the backfield usage will be a “mix” of both players. Jets coach Aaron Glenn will reportedly share his ideal backfield split with Reich, who will work with the position coaches to make it happen. Hall likely belongs in the high-end RB2 tier while Allen remains FLEX-viable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Hall is expected to return this week, but a full practice might be required before the team gives him the go-ahead. Hall logged three limited practices last week before being ruled out on Sunday. Barring a setback, we’re still expecting Hall to ramp up to a full session over the next two days. Assuming he does, Hall will likely split work with Braelon Allen, who has been extremely effective as the Jets’ workhorse running back in his absence. Both backs will sit in the RB3 ranks for their Week 9 date with the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) is “trending in the right direction.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Hall, barring setbacks in practice, should be OK for Week 9 against the Chiefs. What his workload will look like is another question entirely. Braelon Allen has established himself as an efficient, tough runner over the past few weeks, and could remain the Jets’ lead rusher while Hall takes on most pass-catching opportunities. Though Hall should have some kind of floor in Week 9, he probably doesn’t have much of a ceiling unless the Jets decided to phase out Allen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich said he “assumes” Breece Hall will remain the team’s lead back when he returns from injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn has knocked down suggestions that the Jets would trade Hall before the league’s trade deadline, as Braelon Allen continues as one of the NFL’s most productive rushers. When asked about how the backfield might look when Hall returns from his quad injury, Reich seemed to say Hall would remain the de facto lead runner. “Well, that’s obviously coach’s decision, but they’re both the guy … I mean, that’s a good problem to have,” Reich said. “That’s coach’s decision, but to me … Breece is our guy. I’m assuming Breece is our guy, you know what I mean? He’s one of the best in the NFL, but I think what’s been so excited is like, oh my gosh, we’ve got two of them. I mean, we’ve got two. This Braelon guy, he’s a beast as well.” Allen this season ranks third among running backs in rushing success rate; 11th in rush yards over expected per attempt; eighth in yards after contact per rush; and over the past three weeks he ranks eighth among RBs in expected fantasy points per game, proving the haters wrong along the way. Hall is expected to return to action this week against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Breece Hall (quad) is “now good to go and should play next week” against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: It was reported on Sunday that Hall was “hoping for next week,” which is now here, as the Jets prepare to take on the Chiefs in Kansas City. After logging a week of limited practices and entering last weekend as questionable, Hall was still scratched from Week 8’s game against the Raiders, leading some to believe he had suffered a setback in his recovery. Hopefully that was more of a case of the Jets exercising caution with their RB1, especially with Braelon Allen playing well in his absence. Hall’s status will still be one to monitor, but this is a very optimistic report on him to start the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said “we’re in the business of keeping good players” when asked if the team would consider trading Breece Hall before the deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: The Jets are 2-6 and Braelon Allen has put together a solid few weeks in Hall’s absence. As a result, there has been some speculation as to whether or not the Jets would consider moving Hall, who has missed the last five games with a quad injury. In addition to saying the Jets are “in the business of keeping good players,” Glenn also was sure to remind the media that Hall is “one of our better players,” suggesting there are no plans to move the 25-year-old back at this year’s deadline. If he’s able to play next week against the Chiefs, Hall would fall somewhere in the RB2 ranks in his return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: DNVR Broncos’ Zac Stevens reports that the Broncos are “going to try” to trade for Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Stevens said that this trade “could happen at any moment,” telling Broncos Country that they “might not want to go to sleep.” While this could be hyperbole, it sounds like Stevens is saying the trade could go down tonight. Stevens said he’s had conversations with multiple people on the matter, and the Broncos “know that this is not the time to wait and develop” young running backs. Stevens closed by reminding viewers that the Broncos were very interested in Breece Hall at one point, and added that there are likely other backup plans that the Broncos could be considering.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.headline: Van Jefferson caught 5-of-7 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams.
Commanders signed WR Van Jefferson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.analysis: Jefferson spent all offseason with the Commanders but found himself on the outside looking in when camp cuts came around. The 30-year-old receiver caught 29 passes for 350 yards and one touchdown last season with the Titans and has bounced around the league over the last four seasons. He could be an injury away from being promoted to the 53-man roster, but we wouldn’t expect him to offer much fantasy production even if he is active on game day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.headline: Commanders released Van Jefferson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.analysis: Jefferson was in the running for a rotational role this summer, but a handful of younger players ultimately passed him on the depth chart. Treylon Burks appears to be the team’s WR3 for Week 1 while Jaylin Lane, Luke McCaffrey, and Antonio Williams are all vying for the WR4 gig.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said RB Rachaad White stood out throughout the offseason program.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.analysis: Reporters asked Quinn to name players who stood out and stepped up throughout the offseason. White, WR Van Jefferson and rookie WR Jaden Bradley were the three offensive players. The latter two could have a tough time achieving fantasy relevance, but White has a wide range of outcomes. The Commanders are hoping RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt can return from his soft tissue injury and prove his three-down viability. They also drafted RB Kaytron Allen. White, 27, has struggled to perform well as a rusher, but is a proven passing game contributor. Depending on how things shake out in training camp, White could have a reliable role this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.headline: Commanders signed WR Van Jefferson, formerly of the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.analysis: Jefferson caught 29-of-51 targets for 350 yards and one touchdown last season. Somehow, his 59.6 percent catch rate is only the third-worst of his career. Jefferson is likely due for a backup role, perhaps as a field stretcher. He should not be a target in fantasy drafts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.headline: Titans WR Van Jefferson (forearm) will not play in Tennessee’s Week 18 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.analysis: Jefferson finishes the 2025 season with a 29/350/1 line — this is the standard, as Jefferson has finished between 209 yards and 369 yards in five of his six NFL seasons. The sacrificial X will be a free agent this offseason and tuns 30 in July. Zero fantasy upside, but he could find a real role again in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.headline: Van Jeffferson (forearm) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.analysis: Jefferson hasn’t caught more than three passes in a game since Week 7 but still runs plenty of routes every week. With nothing left to play for in week 18, the Titans could give him the week off. His absence would free up a few extra looks for Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.headline: Gunnar Helm (toe) is active for Week 16 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.analysis: As is Van Jefferson (back). It means this undermanned Titans skill corps is at least at full strength as it tries to steal a victory vs. the dazed and confused Chiefs. Inactive for the Titans are OL Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, OL Garrett Dellinger, OL Drew Moss, DL Cam Horsley, LB Cedric Gray and S Erick Hallett.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.headline: Titans WR Van Jefferson (back) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 16 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.analysis: He got in two limited sessions and is probably on the optimistic side of questionable. Playing Jefferson in fantasy football during Week 16 feels like a punishment you would get for finishing in last in a league, but we can’t legally stop you from doing it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.headline: Titans WR Van Jefferson (back) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/van-jeffer.analysis: It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday DNP. We doubt you’re seriously considering starting Van Jefferson in Week 16, but hey, there are sickos out there. He looks to be on track to play on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 26-of-43 passes for 228 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Rams’ 20-13, Week 9 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: It was an uneven day for Stafford and the Rams, who managed just six points in the first half of this one. Stafford threw 19 of his 43 targets to Puka Nacua, who was unsurprisingly his most reliable receiver of the day, as the two connected 14 times for 150 yards and a touchdown. Stafford’s lone touchdown pass of the day came on a seven-yard pass to Nacua in the back of the end zone, which gave the Rams a 20-13 lead early in the fourth quarter. This marks back-to-back pedestrian outings for Stafford, who has thrown for 385 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions in his last two games. Stafford will be a fringe QB1/QB2 next week on the road against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford (right elbow) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford has downplayed inquiries regarding his throwing-arm injury, saying he’s been icing his elbow post-game and post-practice for a while now — and he called out the beat reporters for missing it. Lingering elbow soreness isn’t exactly reassuring, but at least he is practicing fully. Stafford should be good to go for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders, but this is obviously worth monitoring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 17-of-25 attempts for 157 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford wasn’t asked to do much against the Chargers, as the Rams once again went ultra run-heavy with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined. Averaging a meager 6.3 yards per attempt, Stafford mostly checked down to his short-area targets. His touchdown came on a well-designed screen pass to Puka Nacua. Stafford will have some fantasy appeal in Week 9 against the pass-funnel Washington defense. Coming into Week 8, Stafford ranked 13th in expected fantasy points per game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 23-of-29 attempts for 195 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: It was a fairly clean game for Stafford against a Raiders defense that rarely pressures the passer and has proven vulnerable in the intermediate and deep areas of the field. Stafford picked apart the Vegas secondary in the first half, with heavy three tight end-set usage and a more run-heavy game plan than usual with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined. The Rams had 35 rushing attempts to 29 passes on the day. Stafford connected with Puka Nacua for one score and Davis Allen for two others. Though Stafford’s ceiling is going to be lower with Adams out, he profiles as a safe option in Week 8 against the Chargers. He now has six multi-touchdown games this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 25-of-33 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ 16-18, Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: The Cardinals’ pass rush was disruptive, hitting Stafford seven times and sacking him twice. Stafford lost a fumble on a two-point conversion, but the box score only shows a failed two-point try, evidently saving fantasy managers two fantasy points. Stafford later fumbled after getting spooked by a pass-rushing ghost. A Rams lineman recovered it, but it derailed an otherwise effective, tempo-based drive. Stafford engineered a touchdown drive at the tail end of the game, connecting with Puka Nacua on a 42-yarder and a 16-yarder, before Colby Parkinson barreled into the end zone for the score. Stafford should return to the QB1 tier against the Raiders in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 40-of-54 passes for 383 yards and three touchdowns in the Rams’ 37-34, Week 5 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: It was the third consecutive game in which Stafford attempted 51 passes or more in what has become the most voluminous passing offense in the league. The two powerhouses felt each other out throughout the first half as only 20 combined points per scored before the break. Things would get aggressive for the final 30 minutes as seven combined touchdowns were scored on nine second half possessions, four of which were accounted for by the Rams. Stafford directed a whopping 24 targets toward alpha wide receiver Puka Nacua, who set a career high with 17 receptions in a short-area role. The reigning MVP returned an instant classic performance against the 2024 MVP, ultimately coming up short in overtime following a blocked field goal attempt from Harrison Mevis. The Rams fall to 2-3 ahead of a home matchup against the more forgiving Cardinals in Week 6. Stafford is once again a fantasy QB1 in that matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 32-of-51 passes for 316 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions in the Rams’ 24-20, Week 4 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford put the Rams behind the eight ball with a pair of first half interceptions but was better after the break as the Rams slowly erased a 20-10 deficit. Not that he was amazing, but with the Eagles finishing an inconceivable 0-12 on third down, Stafford needed to make just enough plays, and that’s what he did despite leaving some meat on the bone. It was forgivable on a rainy day in Philly, though Stafford now has at least one interception in all four of his starts. In fact, he has as many scores (six) as picks. Hopefully that trend reverses with Puka Nacua back in the lineup, though the schedule is not lightening up with the Rams hosting the Bills for Monday Night Football in Week 5. That should nevertheless be a fantasy football bonanza.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 30-of-55 passes for 390 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Rams’ 30-26, Week 3 loss to the Broncos, adding 13 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: The Rams stormed out to a 16-0 lead they would take into the break but two unanswered scores and two-point conversions from the Broncos saw the game knotted at 16 heading into the fourth quarter, which is where the scoring really took off. Stafford and the Rams appeared to be in control of the game until a Talanoa Hufanga pick-six off Stafford, making 33 career pick-sixes thrown to give him a record he would otherwise not like to have on his ledger. Stafford answered on the following possession on a 48-yard strike to Konata Mumpfield, only for the Broncos to answer back with a Bo Nix rushing score with 47 seconds left to play. Stafford worked more magic to get the team into the red zone, marching the field with only one timeout with a chance to win on the final play of the game. Hufanga ultimately won the play with his second interception off Stafford, sending the Rams to a 1-2 record. Stafford also became the first quarterback in NFL history to throw for 20,000 yards for two different franchises in the loss. Stafford remains a locked-in QB1 in fantasy circles ahead of a Week 4 showdown with the Eagles on the road.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said he’s “not sure” if Puka Nacua (groin) will play in Week 3.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: McVay said he’s “hopeful” Nacua, who missed Monday night’s game against the Giants, will be able to suit up against Denver next week. The Rams offense was fine without Nacua on Monday against an injury-ravaged Giants team. LA had the week’s fourth highest EPA per play on the way to a 28-6 win. Another game with Nacua sidelined will mean more target domination for Davante Adams and more involvement for Terrance Ferguson, who caught 6-of-9 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown against New York.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 22-of-31 passes for 327 yards, four touchdowns, and one interception in the Rams’ 28-6, Week 2 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: It was an inspiring effort from the 38-year-old quarterback while playing without his top option through the air in Puka Nacua. Stafford locked onto Davante Adams, the latter of whom turned 10 targets into eight receptions for 195 yards and two touchdowns, on his way to a 22nd career game with four touchdown passes. He also moved into sixth on the all-time passing touchdown leaderboard, overtaking Philip Rivers with the four-touchdown performance. The Rams shook off their travel woes in convincing fashion to move to 1-1 ahead of road meeting with the Broncos in Week 3, where Stafford will remain a locked-in QB1 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 20 times for 74 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: This was easily Gibbs’ worst fantasy outing of the year, though that largely speaks to just how incredible he has been in 2026. The big difference today was a lack of receiving usage. Gibbs was only targeted once and failed to catch a pass for the first time since Week 4 of the 2024 season. Jared Goff only attempted 25 passes, but that would still result in more than one target for Gibbs on a normal day. We’re willing to write this off as the product of a low-scoring rock fight with the Dolphins. Gibbs will be back at the top of the RB1 ranks for his Week 10 date game against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Sione Vaki had 11 rushes for 65 yards in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings, adding one catch for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: It was the first time this year Vaki has seen more than six carries. The Lions went ultra run-heavy in this one to combat the Vikings’ vexing blitz scheme, which led to 35 carries on the day. Vaki should be stashed in most formats in cae Jahmyr Gibbs misses any time in the coming weeks. Vaki would be a potential 20-touch weekly option in such a scenario.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs had 23 rushes for 153 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings, adding two catches for 15 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Like all Minnesota opponents this season, the Lions got nothing going through the air. They resorted to a run-heavy game plan and shredded the Vikings defense on the ground for 228 yards. The rushing attack was led by Gibbs, who popped a handful of chunk runs in the second half after the Lions had mostly given up on attacking the Vikings through the air. This is Gibbs’ third 100-yard rushing effort of the 2026 season. His centrality in the Detroit offense makes Gibbs an elite play every week. He’ll take on the Dolphins in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) will play in Week 8 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Like teammate Amon-Ra St. Brown, Gibbs started the week off with a missed practice before upgrading to a full participant in both sessions to end the week. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will be ready for a normal workload against the division rival Vikings Sunday. Fantasy managers are clearly starting Gibbs, regardless of matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) practiced in full Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: The return to practice comes on the heels of a missed practice Wednesday for the veteran workhorse, immediately putting fantasy managers at ease for Week 8. Managers will want to confirm his practice status Friday before making final preparations for the weekend, but it certainly appears as if Gibbs will be good to go for a normal, and massive, workload when the Lions take the field against the division rival Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: A DNP to open the week would normally be concerning, but Dan Campbell told reporters earlier today that he was going to get a lot of players “off their feet” during today’s practice. Gibbs appeared to injure his leg while awkwardly sliding to the ground on his final carry of Week 7. The fact that he isn’t listed with a leg injury on today’s report is also a good sign. Sione Vaki is the next man up if Gibbs can’t play this week, but we aren’t overly concerned quite yet. Tomorrow’s injury report will be more telling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 29 times for 116 yards in the Lions’ Week 7 win over the Packers, adding five receptions for 27 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Fantasy managers won’t balk at what was an overall solid performance, but they probably would have liked to see Gibbs rush in a touchdown; the Packers were more than willing to give him one late in the fourth quarter. Gibbs intentionally fell short of the end zone twice on the Lions’ final drive to ensure Jake Bates’ game-winning field goal attempt would be the final play in regulation, which worked to the Lions’ advantage in the 20-17 win. Gibbs ripped off multiple chunk gains in this one, with 13 of his 29 carries going for five or more yards. He did lose a fumble deep inside Packers territory near the end of the second quarter, which likely cost his team at least three points, but as usual, Gibbs was a big reason why the Lions constantly found themselves in position to win. It’s worth noting that on his final play of the game, Gibbs appeared to suffer a knee injury when his left leg bent awkwardly as he attempted to stop and fall to the turf to keep the clock running, but he was able to jog off under his own power. We would ultimately expect him to be fine, but his practice status will be one to monitor this week as the Lions prepare to take on the Vikings. Assuming he is good to go, Gibbs will be an obvious RB1 candidate next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 25 times for 151 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals, adding five receptions for 56 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Gibbs scored twice today, bringing his career touchdown total up to 57, breaking the NFL record set by former Lions RB Barry Sanders for the most touchdowns scored by a player under 25 years old. The exceptionally talented player gets a boost from his sharp coaching staff, who continue to maximize Gibbs’ strengths. OC Drew Petzing dialed up a trick-play screen pass for Gibbs after the two-minute warning, in which Gibbs took the handoff, pitched it to Amon-Ra St. Brown, who pitched it back to Jared Goff, who then chucked it back to Gibbs with three offensive linemen in front of him on the left side of the field. An 18-yard gain ensued. Gibbs later produced a season-long 22-yard run. Although he scored two touchdowns today, he could have had a third. On the Lions’ ninth drive, Gibbs got two chances from the one-yard line on the ninth drive before the coaching staff greenlit a successful QB sneak for Goff. The Lions are on bye in Week 6, but he returns to the top of the running back ranks against the Packers in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 15 times for 46 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 4 loss to the Panthers, adding 31 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Gibbs had eclipsed 100 combined yards against all three opponents to start the season before the Panthers held him largely in check, with fantasy’s top asset cashing in on a one-yard touchdown in the second quarter to avoid a disastrous outing. The two teams were knotted at 16 entering the half but it was the Panthers that dictated terms following the break, winning the time of possession battle by over six minutes. Gibbs maintained an elite workload by seeing all but two backfield opportunities and every available carry on the evening, keeping his fantasy value sky-high ahead of a potential shootout against the Cardinals in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 20 times for 99 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 3 win over the Jets, adding seven catches for 65 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahmyr-gib.analysis: Per usual, Gibbs was dynamic with the ball in his hands, making defenders miss at will while racking up 27 touches. He put an exclamation point on the game with an 11-yard touchdown grab that eventually gave Detroit the win. He’s already up to six touchdowns this year and has no fewer than five catches and 113 yards from scrimmage in his three appearances. With the ability to crush on the ground and through the air, Gibbs is an unstoppable fantasy force. He remains the RB1 overall heading into his Week 4 date with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/thomas-boo.headline: Raiders declared DT Thomas Booker, WR Malik Benson, WR Dont’e Thornton, G Bryce Cabeldue, SAF Dalton Johnson, and QB Aidan O’Connell inactive for Week 9 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/thomas-boo.analysis: The struggling Vegas defense will be without Booker against the ultra-efficient 49ers offense. The Raiders since Week 4 has allowed the NFL’s third highest EPA per rush and the fifth highest rushing success rate. That should be good news for both Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/thomas-boo.headline: Raiders tendered DT Thomas Booker.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/thomas-boo.analysis: Booker received an original round tender, meaning the team would be entitled to a pick in the round he was originally drafted in if he were to join another team. That would result in a fifth-round pick being returned to the team if Booker signed elsewhere. The fourth-year tackle had his best season as a pro in 2025, starting 13 of the 17 games he appeared in while tallying 44 tackles, five pass breakups, and one forced fumble. If he does not sell elsewhere, Booker will remain under contract with the Raiders for next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/thomas-boo.headline: Raiders traded CB Jakorian Bennett to the Eagles for DT Thomas Booker.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/thomas-boo.analysis: The move should be considered a depth move for both franchises as neither player were expected to open the 2025 season as starters. That said, the move makes sense for both teams as it addresses relative weaknesses. We should see more trades go down as teams work through their respective depth charts as we inch closer to the start of the regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/thomas-boo.headline: Stanford DE Thomas Booker has met with multiple NFL teams throughout the pre-draft process.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/thomas-boo.analysis: After putting up his best season in terms of total tackles with the Stanford Cardinal and spending four seasons with the team, Booker (6'4/310) is taking his talents to the NFL. According to Justin Melo of The Draft Network, Booker had a Top 30 visit with the Houston Texans, attended Baltimore Ravens local day and has met virtually with the likes of the Tennessee Titans, San Francisco 49ers, Indianapolis Colts and New England Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/thomas-boo.headline: Stanford signed four-star 2018 DE Thomas Booker.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/thomas-boo.analysis: Booker (6'5/290) committed to play at Stanford in October in what essentially was a head-to-head battle with Notre Dame. 247 Sports lists him as the 12th best defensive end in the class, while ESPN has him a few spots lower at 24. Either way, Booker is a talented end who has also could play at tight end with soft hands and surprising speed. Whatever side of the ball Booker is on, he should help.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Broncos CB Riley Moss suffered a concussion in Denver’s Week 9 game against the Panthers and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: Attempting to help out in run defense, Moss took a second quarter knee to the hit and went down in extremely concerning fashion. He was ruled out after the break. The Broncos’ thinned out pass defense has been struggling since Moss’ departure.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Riley Moss (ribs) is active for Week 6 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: Moss, one of the Broncos’ starting cornerbacks, returns from a one-game absence. He injured his ribs in Week 4 against the 49ers. The Broncos declared QB Sam Ehlinger, OL Kage Casey, TE Dallen Bentley, DL Jordan Jackson and DL Tyler Onyedim inactive for Week 6 against the Seahawks. Ehlinger will serve as the team’s emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Riley Moss (ribs) is questionable for the Broncos’ Week 6 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: Moss missed Week 5 due to a rib injury but has a chance to return Thursday against the Seahawks after three straight limited practices this week. CB Patrick Surtain (ankle) and S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) did not practice all week and were ruled out, as expected.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Broncos CB Riley Moss (ribs) was listed as a limited practice participant on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: Moss was ruled out of Week 5 against the Chargers but has a chance to play Week 6 against the Seahawks with back-to-back limited practice listings. Meanwhile, S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) was a DNP for the second straight day. With Patrick Surtain (ankle) still out in the short term, the Broncos’ banged-up secondary may have a tough time against Jaxon Smith-Njigba and company on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) did not practice on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: It was an estimated session, but one that probably bodes pretty prescient since Hufanga left Week 5’s game with the ankle injury and was ruled out. Riley Moss (ribs) was listed as limited and would appear to have a chance to come back after being ruled out for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Broncos CB Patrick Surtain (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: Neither Surtain or Riley Moss (ribs) practiced on Wednesday. Head coach Sean Payton said the Broncos don’t anticipate placing Surtain on injured reserve. The injuries to both corners look to be shorter-term; Surtain is week-to-week while Moss’ return timeline is not disclosed yet. Both are on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5 against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Patrick Surtain’s ankle injury is not believed to be season-ending.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: According to Rapoport, there are no longer any concerns that this is an Achilles injury for Surtain, who left Week 4’s game against the 49ers with a non-contact injury. Surtain could be looking at a multi-week absence and will undergo an MRI soon to confirm the severity of his injury, but it sounds like he avoided anything too serious. In addition to Surtain, the Broncos are also evaluating the status of CB Riley Moss, who is dealing with a rib injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Broncos HC Sean Payton said the injury Riley Moss suffered in Friday’s preseason game is not considered serious.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: Moss exited Friday’s game with an apparent rib injury, but Payton said the team is choosing to make the smart decision by not practicing him. Moss totaled 57 tackles and one interception last season and has started all 31 games he has appeared in since 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Broncos CB Riley Moss exited Friday’s preseason game against the Packers after suffering an apparent ribs injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: Broncos CB Pat Surtain appeared to force a fumble from Packers WR Christian Watson moments after Watson hauled in the pass. Moss dove on it, injuring himself in the process, but Watson was eventually ruled down by contact. Bummer. Moss was grabbing at the right side of his rib cage as he entered the blue medical tent. If Moss misses time, the Broncos have CB Jahdae Barron waiting in the wings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.headline: Broncos CB Ja’Quan McMillian signed his one-year restricted free-agent tender.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/riley-moss.analysis: The Broncos brought McMillian, 25, aboard as an undrafted free agent in 2022. He impressively won the starting slot cornerback role in 2023 and has manned that spot for the Broncos ever since. The front office retained McMillian via a one-year contract last year, and appears set to do so again, though McMillian’s agent said the cornerback is hoping to sign a long-term deal. That may not happen. General manager George Patton made his top-tier cornerback unit even deeper by spending a first-round pick on former Texas CB Jahdae Barron in 2025. While No. 1 CB Patrick Surtain II will assuredly retain his starting role, the Broncos could end up hosting a competition between McMillian, Barron and No. 2 perimeter CB Riley Moss this year. Last year, Barron logged 155 snaps in the slot, 95 in the box and 90 on the perimeter and could have the talent to compete for either role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle suffered a concussion in the Broncos’ Week 9 game against the Panthers and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle was listed as questionable in the first half but then ruled out to begin the third. It’s another nightmare development for Waddle in his first Broncos season, as he has struggled for both 100 percent health and productive box scores. Today’s injury came as Waddle skied for a target over the middle of the field and got high/lowed. He had just one grab for 22 yards before departing. The only good news is the Broncos are on bye for Week 10, meaning Waddle might not miss any game time beyond this afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle played through a questionable tag with this injury last week, catching 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards and one touchdown against the Chiefs. He apparently made it through the contest without re-injuring himself and can be started as a WR3 this week against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle caught 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 8 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Starting with the positive, Waddle found the end zone for the second time this year and got going over the middle of the field with a 35-yard missile from Nix early in the second quarter. It’s his longest catch since Week 2, when he erupted for 138 yards on eight receptions, including a 49-yarder. On the downside, Waddle managed a pedestrian 19 percent target share and finished third on the team in receiving. He found the end zone and still scored a grand total of 12.9 PPR points. The Broncos’ offense is still a work in progress, even if today was a step in the right direction. Waddle will get another week in the WR3 mix when the Broncos take on the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (shoulder) is active for Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Left tackle Garrett Boles and EDGE Zach Allen are also active. All Broncos players who were questionable for Week 8 are active. After a disappointing two months to start the year, Waddle is at the back of the WR3 ranks for Week 8. Inactive for the Broncos are S Talana Hufanga, QB Sam Ehlinger, OL Gavin Ortega, DL Jordan Jackson, DL Tyler Oneydim, OL Kage Casey, and TE Dallen Bentley.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jaylen Waddle (chest) is “trending toward playing” in Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle suffered the chest injury late in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals and a doomed trick play. He was leveled by Josh Sweat several yards behind the line of scrimmage. The Broncos held him out of Wednesday’s practice before giving him two limited sessions and a questionable tag. Though we suspect he is on some form of a snap count, it looks like Waddle is giving it a go. Already struggling to put up WR3 fantasy numbers, we’re regarding him as a high-risk FLEX play versus Kansas City.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is questionable for Denver’s Week 8 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle got in two limited sessions after missing practice on Wednesday. It feels like he’s on the optimistic side of questionable given the trend line, though of course you would have preferred to see a full session somewhere in here. It’s also possible he winds up on a snap count, so we’ll see if any insiders dig up anything on that this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
