https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle aggravated an existing chest injury on a trick play late in the fourth quarter of Week 7. A return to the practice field, in any capacity, Thursday keeps the door open for him to be available to play the Chiefs in Week 8, although fantasy managers are likely looking for an excuse to bench the over-hyped receiver. It would be prudent to look at other viable options in a difficult matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Earlier today, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Waddle’s status for Week 8 against the Chiefs has not been determined. The Broncos’ No. 1 wide receiver aggravated his preexisting chest injury in Week 7 against the Cardinals. Backup plans should be made at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Jaylen Waddle suffered a chest injury and his Week 8 status has not been determined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle left Sunday’s game against the Cardinals with the chest injury. It was, according to Rapoport, an “aggravation of his previous chest injury.” Waddle could try to practice later this week, but would appear to be iffy unless he can log a practice session by Friday. If Waddle is sidelined this week against the Chiefs, Courtland Sutton would likely see more targets and become an interesting flex option against a tough KC secondary. Sutton over the past four weeks leads Denver in air yards and has the second most targets behind Waddle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle left Week 7’s game against the Cardinals with an apparent chest injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Up by 14, Sean Payton dialed up a trick play for Waddle, giving him a pitch as Waddle came across the formation. Waddle bobbled the ball and was clobbered by Josh Sweat. He writhed in pain while holding his left shoulder. Trainers came onto the field and eventually walked him into the locker room. With less than four minutes on the clock at the time of his departure, we don’t expect to see him again today. Waddle’s day ends with four catches for 48 yards on seven targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 2-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Bengals’ Week 9 victory over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki had caught a touchdown in each of his last six games, but was essentially a non-factor in the win over the Falcons in Madrid. The Bengals scored three times in the red zone, but those touchdowns went to Tee Higgins (twice) and Joe Burrow. Gesicki needs those scores to be fantasy-relevant. He’ll be a touchdown-dependent TE2 heading into Week 10’s matchup with the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 4-of-6 targets for 76 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki has been a high-value red zone target for the Bengals all season long. His score against the Titans came from outside of the red zone, catching a 25-yard pass for the score in the fourth quarter. It’s Gesicki’s sixth-straight game with a touchdown and seventh score of the season. Pass-heavy game scripts will lift all boats in the Bengals offense but Gesicki remains a high-end fantasy TE2 due to his high amount of touchdown opportunities.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught his lone target for six yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki’s lone target came on an end zone target from Joe Burrow that resulted in a six-yard touchdown. The 31-year-old tight end has now scored in all five games he has appeared in this season, but has managed just 10 yards on two receptions in his last two games. Fellow tight ends Erick All and Drew Sample combined to catch five passes for 45 yards and one touchdown on five targets. Gesicki has run 15 routes in each of his last two games and is purely a touchdown-dependent option in Week 8 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 1-of-2 targets for 4 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: The Bengals utilized all of their tight ends against the Dolphins, with Gesicki catching just one pass on the day. His sole reception was a touchdown on the Bengals’ opening drive, totaling four on the season and salvaging some fantasy value for those who streamed him at tight end this week. Gesicki’s value is lowered when Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are active; his red zone utilization makes Gesicki a low-end fantasy TE2 heading into the Bengals’ Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Bengals’ Week 4 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki caught a third quarter touchdown against the Jaguars, his third score of the year. He saw just five targets on a day where Joe Burrow threw 54 passes and Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) exited early. However, Gesicki has a clear red zone role and he led all Bengals tight ends in snaps on the day. If Chase and Tee Higgins (adductor) miss any time, Gesicki is a tight end streaming option for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 3-of-3 targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 3 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: After going without a target last week, Gesicki made the most of his three targets in this one. His most notable reception came in the fourth quarter on a fourth-and-two when he broke free across the middle of the field for a wide-open 25-yard touchdown to put the Bengals up 27-24. Gesicki has now scored in two of his first three games this season, but is averaging just 3.3 targets per game. Fantasy managers should be rushing to add him to their lineups for next week’s game against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki was not targeted in Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: The rollercoaster ride that is “tertiary target in a Tee Higgins/Ja’Marr Chase-centric offense.” Erick All (2/5 on three targets) lead Bengals tight ends in receptions. Drew Sample (36 of 60) led Bengals tight ends in snaps. Starting Gesicki will pay off at times, but this wasn’t one of them. He’s a TE2 in Week 3 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 5-of-7 targets for 78 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 1 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki led the Bengals in catches, targets and yards and was the only pass catcher to score on an afternoon where the Bucs’ defense was funneling Joe Burrow to the middle of the field. Gesicki’s score was a two-yarder where he rolled in to the end zone in the first quarter. Gesicki’s yardage total would have been his second highest of 2025. He’s a valuable real-life contributor, but he is going to have trouble cracking the top 18 tight ends on a regular basis with Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown all usage monsters for the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: ESPN’s Ben Baby reports that Bengals rookie WR Colbie Young is competing for OC Dan Pitcher’s “passing target No. 3" role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Baby’s practice notes indicate that incumbent No. 3 WR Andrei Iosivas and No. 1 TE Mike Gesicki are the other two competitors for the role, and both players “had productive springs.” Pitcher also said RB Chase Brown “can sometimes be viewed as a slot receiver,” but those types of comments are common in the summer and rarely pan out in the fall. Iosivas and Gesicki have been helpful contributors, but the fact that the team is searching for an answer at the No. 3 receiving role is indicative of their ceilings. Pitcher believes Young is “going to fight and battle” this summer, and thinks there are things Young “can do quickly and help us.” If he can actually become the team’s third-most voluminous target earner, he could pay off as a late-round best ball pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught both of his targets for 13 yards in the Bengals’ Week 18 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Hot off a rebound 2024 season, Gesicki inked a three-year, $25.5 million contract to stay in Cincinnati in the offseason. It became apparent early in the year that Gesicki would not be giving Bengals fans an encore in 2025. He was held under 20 receiving yards in each of his first six games before a pec injury sent him to injured reserve. Gesicki started to turn things around after coming off IR, totaling 35 yards on four grabs in Week 12. At the time, it was his best game of the year. He eventually popped for a few other meaningful games, though he ultimately topped 50 yards just once on the year. He posted a 28/307/2 receiving line in total. The Bengals could save $3.3 million in cap space with a $4.3 million dead cap hit if they move on from him after the year. Either way, we don’t expect him to be on the fantasy radar in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-2 targets for 16 yards in the Falcons’ Week 9 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: The Falcons passing attack was a mess against the Bengals in Week 9. Michael Penix threw 31 times, but for just 162 yards. Dotson was a non-factor by product, totaling just 16 yards on two receptions. He’s Atlanta’s WR2, but is merely a WR5/6 heading into Week 10 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-5 targets for 95 yards in the Falcons’ Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: The bulk of Dotson’s production came on a single, 76-yard gain in the fourth quarter. Michael Penix lobbed him a ball on the boundary and two Bucs defensive backs collided, leaving Dotson uncovered with room to run. He bolted down the sideline but didn’t have the speed to take it to the house. That play alone accounted for over half of Penix’s passing output. Dotson has made the occasional splash play while running as Atlanta’s WR2, but his fantasy prospects are not that intriguing headed into Week 9. He will be in the WR5/6 range when the Falcons take on the Bengals next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 1-of-3 targets for six yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson was also targeted on three different deep passes that resulted in San Francisco penalties. That doesn’t help your fantasy team, but it is indicative of his role in this offense. Dotson did run the second-most routes of any receiver on the Falcons; however, he is really only targeted on deep shots down the field, which will make his production inconsistent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 3-of-5 targets for 87 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson, whose season-high yardage coming into the week was 54 — his total in both of the past two weeks — got loose a couple times in this one, mostly when the Falcons ditched their usual run-heavy offense in favor of a fast-pace pass-heavy approach while facing a multiple touchdown second half deficit. Running a route on 32 of the Falcons’ 38 drop backs, Dotson led the team in receiving yards thanks largely to a 41-yard grab. Dotson could be a deep league play in Week 7 against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-4 targets for 54 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson’s 54 yards finished second on the team behind alpha Drake London but his four targets finished behind London, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson. His status as the starting wide receiver opposite London likely means little in the wake of modest volume games that continue to stack up. He can safely be left on, or returned to, the waiver wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-3 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson continues to operate as the team’s WR2 opposite Drake London but remains unlikely to return consistent fantasy production in an offense heavily concentrated on its top two options in London and Bijan Robinson. Dotson’s touchdown came in the fourth quarter with the team cruising, pushing the lead to 21 points with under 10 minutes to play. Fantasy managers can safely keep Dotson on the bench ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Ravens in Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-4 targets for 11 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson saw four targets for the second week in a row. He went for 19 yards on one catch last week and didn’t look any different this time around. Dotson is the team’s No. 2 receiver by routes, but there aren’t enough targets to go around after Drake London, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson all get theirs. Dotson is not on the fantasy radar for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 1-of-3 targets for 19 yards in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson actually operated as the second receiver for the Falcons in this one, running a route on 20 of the team’s 29 dropbacks. He also played 38 snaps, while Olamide Zaccheaus played just 18. That didn’t amount to much, but it’s something for fantasy managers in deeper leagues to keep in mind when Michael Penix eventually gets back onto the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi believes Falcons WR Zachariah Branch could start the season as a “gadget guy,” before later earning a starting role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Branch was a screen game dominator in college, with speed to spare. Raimondi thinks the Falcons will attempt to replicate his Georgia game early on, but Branch has a chance to become “the No. 3 guy, maybe even the No. 2 guy at some point.” Falcons WRs Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus sit in those two spots. Branch is unlikely to contribute meaningfully in fantasy early in the year, but he is worth keeping an eye on in-season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall believes that if the Falcons make a “random offseason move,” it might come at wide receiver.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: The Atlanta depth chart at wideout is sparse even after we account for third-round pick Zachariah Branch in the draft. The No. 2 receiver right now might be Jahan Dotson. Olamide Zaccheaus is also in the picture. The Falcons still have $27 million in cap space but we’ve rarely heard them mentioned by national reporters as interested in the Stefon Diggs/Deebo Samuel/Keenan Allen best veteran free agent wideout tier. Those guys aren’t mentioned in this report either, but they do make plenty of sense from a roster standpoint.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 3-of-5 targets for 23 yards in the Falcons’ Week 9 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Three receptions for 23 yards is a disappointing line and unfortunately it represents the most receiving yards Pitts has had in his last three games. Pitts has four touchdowns on the season, but is unusable in fantasy unless he finds the end zone. The definition of touchdown-dependent, Pitts is a low-end TE2 in Week 10 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 2-of-5 targets for six yards in the Falcons’ Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts’ 20 percent target share would have been good for at least TE2 fantasy numbers on a normal day. This game was anything but normal. Pitts and Jahan Dotson were the only Falcons pass-catchers with multiple receptions. Michael Penix only completed eight passes, so there simply wasn’t enough production to go around. He was intercepted four times and the Falcons were shut out. Pitts’ role as a PPR merchant should tick back up in Week 9 versus the Bengals. He will be back in the TE2 mix for that contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught all five of his targets for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: The touchdown is nice to see, and Pitts finished tied for second on the team in both catches and targets. However, preliminary snap counts say he played on 37 of the team’s 67 snaps and ran a route on 20 of their 37 dropbacks. Charlie Woerner ran a route on 11 dropbacks and Austin Hooper ran a route on 10 dropbacks, so the Falcons continue to get tons of tight ends on the field. That makes Pitts more of a high-end TE2 option, really solely because of good touchdown equity.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 5-of-7 targets for 60 yards and two touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts was one of the beneficiaries of a pass-heavy second half for a Falcons offense that was forced to abandon the run game facing a multi-touchdown deficit. Pitts took advantage of single coverage a couple times, including on his first touchdown grab. He now has three touchdowns over his past two games as Michael Penix brings some stability to the Atlanta offense. Pitts, who ran a route on 26 of the team’s 38 drop backs against Chicago, will be a viable play in Week 7 against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 5-of-6 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts remained largely confined to short area work with his game-long reception going for only 13 yards. A second quarter touchdown from five yards out gave the veteran tight end his first trip to paint through five games and his five receptions doubled that of his previous four appearances. Pitts remains a difficult weekly start for as long as Drake London and Bijan Robinson remain healthy. A Week 6 meeting with the Bears in Atlanta should see him remain in the TE2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught all three targets for 47 yards in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts played just one snap on the team’s first two possessions before seeing modest usage the rest of the game. His counting stats were padded in the second half with a 28-yard, catch-and-run reception on a play action pass out of the flat. Pitts isn’t getting the snaps or route participation to return consistent fantasy production and is best left on fantasy benches for as long as Drake London remains healthy. That won’t change ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 1-of-2 targets for five yards in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts was the recipient of Michael Penix’s first completion of the 2026 season, with the latter making his season debut following ACL surgery. The return of his starting quarterback was not enough to give Pitts his first fantasy-relevant performance of the season as he watched blocking tight end Austin Hooper score the lone receiving touchdown of the evening from five yards out in the second quarter. Fantasy managers are stuck in the constant hype cycle with Pitts with very little to show for it through three games, making Pitts a difficult start on the road against the Saints in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 1-of-3 targets for 15 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Cooper Rush was a disaster once again, tanking the fantasy prospects of every Falcon. Pitts narrowly avoided his second straight bagel with a lone catch late in the second quarter. He failed to catch his only target last week. There’s not much to say about Pitts and the entire offense when Rush simply shuts down all production from the jump. Pitts will reclaim a spot in the TE1 ranks if Michael Penix is back for Week 3. He is not on the fantasy radar if Rush is under center once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowlers reports Michael Penix (knee) is “not yet ready for live game action.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Fowler said Penix, still recovering from his 2025 ACL injury, “wants to be fully confident before stepping onto the field. And my understanding is the Falcons are leaving the comfort level part of his recovery up to him.” “Penix is coming off his third ACL reconstruction, which is a lot of ACL reconstructions,” ESPN’s Dan Graziano added. “I believe it takes a lot of mental work to convince yourself it’s OK to go back out there and play. If Penix needs more time, I’m sure the Falcons will give it to him, though I believe we will see him on the field at some point this season.” That would leave Tua Tagovailoa as the team’s presumed starter if Tua can play through the oblique strain that sidelined him in Week 1 against the Steelers. If Tua can’t go, the Falcons could be forced to start Cooper Rush for another game or two. Rush, who had the lowest drop back EPA of any QB in Week 1, makes Drake London and Kyle Pitts iffy starts in 12-team fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts Sr. had no catches on one target in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts owes most of this to a poor performance by Cooper Rush under center. Pitts played on 39 of the team’s 61 snaps and ran a route on 22 of their 29 dropbacks. He simply wasn’t a factor with Rush struggling to move the ball down the field. We should note that the Falcons were very run-heavy with Rush at quarterback, and Charlie Woerner played 38 snaps and was on the field for 22 run-blocking snaps to just 16 for Pitts. If the Falcons are going to continue to be so focused on rushing the ball, that could cut into some of Pitts’ snaps and usage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 5-of-5 targets for 68 yards in the Falcons’ Week 9 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London bounced back after being held to one reception and eight yards in the loss to the Buccaneers in Week 8. He caught all five of his targets for 68 yards, but still has only one touchdown on the year after being held scoreless again. After dominating with Michael Penix in the lineup last season, London has just been okay with Penix under center this year. Likely facing a pass-heavy game script in Week 10 against the Chiefs, London will be a low-end WR1 again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 1-of-6 targets for eight yards in the Falcons’ Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: Bucs defenders caught more passes on London’s six targets than he did. It was that bad of a day. Michael Penix was intercepted four times and only completed eight attempts. He managed just 125 yards, over half of which came on a 76-yard throw to Jahan Dotson that was the result of a coverage miscue. There’s simply not much to take away from a game where London’s quarterback plays this poorly. London had gone for at least 60 yards on four catches in every previous Penix start. We fully expect him to get back on track as a WR1 versus the Bengals next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 7-of-10 targets for 66 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London fought through a tackle on a 21-yard catch in the fourth quarter for his first touchdown catch of the season. He was also open for a touchdown earlier in the game, but Michael Penix Jr. sailed the pass over his head. London had twice as many targets as any other pass catcher in Atlanta and should continue to get elite usage in this offense. He did leave the game to be evaluated for a concussion, and while he was able to return to the field, it’s a situation to monitor for early practice reports next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 4-of-10 targets for 62 yards in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London couldn’t get much going against Chicago’s middling secondary outside a 39-yard grab in the second half, with the Falcons abandoning the run game as they faced a three-touchdown deficit. Michael Penix missed London in the first half on what could have been a fairly easy 30-yard score with a better-placed throw from Penix. London almost came down with an end zone target too. No other Atlanta pass catcher had more than seven targets on the day. London will remain a top-10 option in Week 7 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 7-of-11 targets for 118 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London started slow along with the rest of an Atlanta offense that gained just 37 total yards on their first three possessions before a 78-yard scoring drive to end the half. He would add six receptions after the break to push his season average to 127 yards per game in games started by Michael Penix. Penix departed late in the fourth quarter with a ribs injury, suddenly making London’s fantasy managers skittish after the veteran receiver managed a meager 80 total yards in two games without Penix to begin the season. Fantasy managers will want to monitor Atlanta’s starting quarterback’s status in the coming days ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Bears, where London will be a WR1 with Penix or an upside WR3 in his absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 5-of-6 targets for 96 yards in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London turned in his second consecutive usable fantasy week with Michael Penix under center. The low volume can primarily be attributed to just 20 Penix pass attempts in a game Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson combined for 207 yards and five touchdowns on the ground on 33 carries. London could be tasked with more volume when the Falcons host the Ravens in Week 5, for which he will remain an unquestioned WR1 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 9-of-10 targets for 194 yards in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: To make the stat line more impressive, London didn’t catch his first pass until three minutes into the second quarter following a 1-of-5 start from Michael Penix. He would catch his final nine targets on his way to a massive fantasy day, combining with Bijan Robinson to set the NFL record for a wide receiver and running back duo to both go over 150 yards in the same game with three such occurrences. London continues to excel with Penix under center and returns to the WR1 ranks in fantasy circles ahead of a Week 4 meeting with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 4-of-5 targets for 51 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London also had a 25-yard grab called back by penalty. As expected, the Falcons simply rolled out a dead-on-arrival offense with Cooper Rush under center. Rush turned the ball over three times before being benched in the third quarter. Things didn’t get any better with Jack Strand under center. He threw an immediate pick-six and the Falcons promptly pulled the bulk of their starters from the game. With Michael Penix expected to play next week, London should return to the WR2 ranks next time we see him. If Penix isn’t available once again, London will barely register as a WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowlers reports Michael Penix (knee) is “not yet ready for live game action.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: Fowler said Penix, still recovering from his 2025 ACL injury, “wants to be fully confident before stepping onto the field. And my understanding is the Falcons are leaving the comfort level part of his recovery up to him.” “Penix is coming off his third ACL reconstruction, which is a lot of ACL reconstructions,” ESPN’s Dan Graziano added. “I believe it takes a lot of mental work to convince yourself it’s OK to go back out there and play. If Penix needs more time, I’m sure the Falcons will give it to him, though I believe we will see him on the field at some point this season.” That would leave Tua Tagovailoa as the team’s presumed starter if Tua can play through the oblique strain that sidelined him in Week 1 against the Steelers. If Tua can’t go, the Falcons could be forced to start Cooper Rush for another game or two. Rush, who had the lowest drop back EPA of any QB in Week 1, makes Drake London and Kyle Pitts iffy starts in 12-team fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 2-of-4 targets for 29 yards in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London also added six yards on one rush as the Falcons looked to do anything to get the ball in the hands of their best receiver. The 25-year-old was an absolute non-factor in this one, largely because Cooper Rush was highly inefficient and ineffective under center. The role is not in question though. London played 60 of the team’s 61 snaps and ran a route on 28 of their 29 dropbacks. However, he will be tough to trust with Cooper Rush (and probably even Tua Tagovailoa) under center. London has a much better matchup next week against the Panthers, but there is some fear that he’s more of a WR2 option until Michael Penix (knee) returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 19 times for 100 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 9 loss to the Bengals, adding six receptions for 47 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson bounced back nicely after posting 76 scoreless yards in the loss to the Buccaneers in Week 8. The 24-year-old running back had 100 rushing yards and score while adding six catches for 47 yards through the air. Robinson’s touchdown gives him six in nine games this year after scoring 11 times in 17 games last season. Still an elite fantasy option despite the offense around him, Robinson is a locked in RB1 against the Chiefs in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 19 times for 76 yards in the Falcons’ Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson dropped his only target of the day. He has quietly been held under 100 rushing yards in four straight games. Robinson normally papers over that with strong receiver numbers, but that disappeared today as well. Michael Penix only completed eight passes and threw four interceptions. Robinson should have better luck in Week 9 against the Bengals, but the odds of him repeating as the RB1 overall are shrinking by the week. He will sit just outside the top tier of fantasy options in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Bijan Robinson handled 20 carries and five targets with his backup, Brian Robinson, sidelined in Week 7. The backup should be considered questionable to play at this time, though he could make a late-week return. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 20 times for 63 yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson did add 59 yards receiving on five catches to help salvage his fantasy day, but this is the third straight week he has delivered a modest fantasy return after explosive performances in Weeks 3 and 4. In fact, this is now five of seven games this season that Robinson has been held under 90 yards rushing. He’s contributing as a pass-catcher, and he looks elusive when he can get beyond the line of scrimmage, but the Falcons may need to make an adjustment on offense with defenses clearly keying on stopping Robinson. We’d expect them to focus on getting him going next week against the Bucs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: The Falcons’ No. 2 running back was limited yesterday. This series of events suggests Robinson strained his hamstring on Wednesday, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for the Falcons’ Week 6 game against the 49ers. Bijan Robinson would handle a few extra touches in Robinson’s absence. The team does not have a third running back on the active roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson had nine rushes for 61 yards in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears, adding two catches for -8 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson couldn’t get anything going against a Chicago defense allowing the fifth highest rate of yards before contact. The Bears were intent on snuffing out the Atlanta rushing attack and forcing Michael Penix to move the ball through the air. It worked for much of the game. Robinson, who had 425 rushing yards in his previous three games, remains the engine of the run-heavy Falcons offense and should get back on track in Week 7 against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 17 times for 86 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens, adding 32 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson suffered through poor offensive efficiency in the first half, finally breaking loose for a 38-yard carry on the team’s first possession of the third quarter. Although the receiving production and yardage total were enough to salvage a usable fantasy week, it was only the second time in five games in which Robinson failed to find the end zone. Robinson remains an elite fantasy RB1 ahead of a Week 6 showdown against the Bears in Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 19 times for 145 yards and two touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints, adding two yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Week 4 marked Robinson’s second consecutive game going over 100 yards with two touchdowns on the ground, this time aided by a 59-yard touchdown run on his first touch of the game. The Falcons tied a franchise record with five rushing scores, with backfield mate Brian Robinson adding three to the two of Bijan. The return of quarterback Michael Penix has given the Falcons the threat of passing after dropping their first two games of the season behind suboptimal play from the position, and nobody has benefited more from reduced numbers in the box than Robinson. He’ll look to keep the momentum going as a top-tier RB1 when the Falcons host the Ravens in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 29 times for 194 yards and two touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers, adding 19 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson single-handedly out-gained the Packers in the first half after clearing the century mark on the ground early in the second quarter. His patience and burst through the gap were on full display, routinely gaining chunk yardage on first down while making the Green Bay defensive front look like Swiss cheese. A 55-yard scamper on a wide zone carry in the first quarter got the All Pro back off to a blazing start, adding his first of two touchdowns to cap the drive. He would take on a second score late in the fourth quarter to send the Packers to their first home opener loss in 14 years. Robinson remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the division rival Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 16 times for 72 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers, adding three catches for nine yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson did what he could in the midst of a Cooper Rush meltdown, but it’s hard to expect much when his team puts up a grand total of three points. Atlanta also pulled their starters early, allowing Brian Robinson Jr. to rack up 13 touches of his own. Robinson is a volume-based RB1 even when Rush is under center, and he’ll move back into the top three once Michael Penix takes over. That could happen next week versus the Packers on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix completed 20-of-31 passes for 162 yards, one touchdown and one interception in the Falcons’ 34-17, Week 9 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix has now gone back-to-back weeks without eclipsing 200 yards. He found Charlie Woerner for a one-yard touchdown in the first quarter, but couldn’t get much going for the rest of the game. Wide receiver Drake London dominated in a small sample with Penix healthy last year, but he’s had just two games with at least 100 yards and only one touchdown this season. Penix is a low-end QB2 heading into Week 10’s home matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix completed 8-of-24 passes for 125 yards and four interceptions in the Falcons’ 16-0, Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix got off to a poor start and his play spiraled from there. He threw a pass directly at Bucs linebacker Alex Anzalone’s chest on the first play of Atlanta’s second drive for an easy interception. Anzalone then took the ball away two Penix throws later by, again, simply standing in the throwing lane. Penix wasn’t seeing the field and nothing changed as the game went on. He threw two more interceptions and had several other passes that could have been caught by the Bucs. Even his best play, a 76-yard toss to Jahan Dotson, was a throw into double coverage where two Bucs defensive backs collided, leaving Dotson wide open at the last second. This looked like an homage to Cooper Rush’s two catastrophic starts to open the season. Penix should rebound in Week 9 versus the Bengals, but his fantasy stock is undoubtedly on the decline. He is shuffling to the back of the QB2 ranks for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix Jr. completed 25-of-34 passes for 213 yards and three touchdowns in the Falcons’ 29-20, Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The stats may make it seem like Penix had his way with the 49ers, but it didn’t seem like a seamless performance in reality. He missed some deep passes and overthrew Drake London on a clear touchdown in the second half. He really wasn’t able to get much going down the field, but the Falcons’ defense forced four turnovers, which set up some short fields that Penix was able to take advantage of. He gets a good matchup against the Bucs next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix completed 19-of-33 for 225 yards and three touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix was a mess in the first half, missing Drake London on what should have been an walk-in 30-yard touchdown. The Falcons abandoned the run game in the second half, facing a three touchdown deficit, and Penix threw three touchdowns in hurry-up mode. Taking five sacks on the day, Penix targeted London and Jahan Dotson heavily, connecting with Dotson on a nicely thrown 41-yard gain in the second half. This was the first multiple-TD game of Penix’s season. He’ll be a low-ceiling superflex play in Week 7 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix (ribs) is active for Week 6 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix was able to practice this week and will start for Atlanta in a potentially high scoring game against the Bears. Penix should be considered a streaming option in most formats. Falcons declared QB Cooper Rush, QB Jack Strand, CB C.J. Henderson, DB Malcolm DeWalt IV, LB Christian Harris, OL Ethan Onianwa, and DE Drake Jackson inactive against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix has been removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It was reported the day after the Falcons’ overtime loss to the Ravens that there was “optimism” that Penix would start in Week 6. After being upgraded to a full participant on Thursday’s practice, he seemed like a lock to be ready to go by Sunday, so Friday’s news isn’t all that unexpected. Penix has thrown for 719 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception this season, throwing one touchdown in each of his first three games. He’ll be on the fantasy radar in 2QB/Superflex leagues against a Bears defense that has allowed just two top-12 fantasy finishes to opposing QBs this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix (ribs) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This is great news for the Falcons’ offense, which can barely function with Tua Tagovailoa at the helm. Penix is firmly on track to play in Week 6 against the Bears, as long as he gets through the week setback-free. Penix can be viewed as a high-end QB2 with four teams on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix (ribs) will practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: “We’ll see how he’s feeling,” head coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters Wednesday morning, adding that Penix should be able to play through the injury. Even if it’s a limited practice session for Penix, it’s good news for his Week 6 availability following his Sunday night rib injury against the Ravens. Penix, operating under center at a much higher rate than last season, is among the most efficient quarterbacks in the league through Week 5. If Penix is out, Tua Tagovailoa would represent a major downgrade for all Atlanta pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports there’s “optimism” that Michael Penix (ribs) will be able to play in Week 6 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix said after Sunday’s loss that he didn’t believe his injury would be long-term. He was replaced by Tua Tagovailoa in overtime because of his injury, but he also added that he likely would have gone back on the field had the Falcons received the ball to start the extra quarter. Instead, Penix said his pain worsened the longer he sat, which was why he ultimately didn’t go back in. Penix’s status will be one to monitor throughout the week. If he can’t start in Week 6, Tagovailoa would be in line to start his first game of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix (ribs) said he doesn’t believe his injury will be a long-term issue.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix will undergo an MRI on Monday to confirm the severity of his injury, but it doesn’t sound like he’s at risk of missing much time. Penix exited in the fourth quarter of Sunday night’s game against the Ravens and was forced to stay on the sideline in overtime to watch Tua Tagovailoa throw the game-losing interception shortly after the Ravens scored the go-ahead touchdown. Penix threw for 240 yards and a touchdown and has been solid in his three games since returning from injury. If he’s not able to start in Week 6, Tagovailoa would presumably draw the start at home against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed 11 times for 43 yards in the Bengals’ Week 9 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine had 43 yards on 11 carries, which was notable because he had two more rushing attempts than starter Chase Brown. While Brown continues to underwhelm, Perine is cutting into Brown’s ceiling (or lack thereof) more than he’s carving out a legitimate role for himself. Perine is one of the better handcuffs to stash, but he shouldn’t be in starting lineups in Week 10 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed 4 times for 10 yards in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans, adding one reception for nine yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine took a backseat to Chase Brown against the Titans, seeing 26 snaps to Brown’s 50. He was still involved in the red zone, but was not utilized as much as Brown as a pass-catcher. Perine’s path to fantasy production will be touchdown opportunities. He is a fantasy handcuff with some desperation RB4 value in Week 9 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed four times for 16 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine saw only four carries in this one, but he turned his lone goal-line touch into a one-yard touchdown to barely salvage what was still a relatively disappointing day. Perine was out-snapped by Chase Brown 38-12, with Brown also leading the way with 11 rush attempts. Perine will be hard to trust as anything more than a desperation RB4 play next week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Bengals OC Dan Pitcher said the team will “continually assess how that touch share between [Perine] and Chase Brown should play out.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Pitcher suggested that when they run the ball more from shotgun — as they did last week against the Dolphins — Perine’s a better fit for those kinds of plays. The Bengals spent a lot of time this offseason working on an under center run game to get Brown more explosives, but that has gone for naught early on in the season. We may indeed see more Perine in Cincinnati’s running game after they return from the bye week, lowering Brown into the RB2 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed 14 times for 68 yards in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins, adding 2 receptions for 10 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine was involved heavily against the Dolphins, a surprising development given his lack of touches to open the season. He trailed Chase Brown by just five snaps on the day, getting involved in short-yardage situations and seeing an increase in red zone snaps after Brown’s red zone fumble in the second quarter. He caught a touchdown running a route out of the backfield and finished with 78 total yards. We don’t expect Perine to consistently see this kind of usage, but he is back on the radar as a deep-league FLEX value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed three times for seven yards in the Bengals’ Week 4 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine only saw three touches on the day, though he had a rushing touchdown called back for holding in the second quarter. He has generally held a pass-catching role throughout his career but ceded all the backfield pass-catching opportunities to Chase Brown on the day. Perine remains a handcuff in the event of a Brown injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed two times for six yards in Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: He added 16 yards on his only catch, making him the third-leading receiver for the game. Perine has 42 snaps in the first two games of the season and looks like a decent stash in case of a Chase Brown injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed eight times for 42 yards in the Bengals’ Week 18 loss to the Browns, adding three catches for 10 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine returned to Cincinnati on a two-year deal in the offseason. He easily took the RB2 gig over rookie Tahj Brooks and eventually parlayed that into a committee role. Perine didn’t log a single carry over the first two weeks but was stacking 10-touch games by November. He finished the year with 84 carries for 382 yards and three scores while adding 17 grabs for 87 yards. Perine was a staple of the RB4 ranks over the final two months of the year. He will likely keep his No. 2 role with the Bengals into the 2026 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed seven times for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 16 win over the Dolphins, adding two receptions for 16 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine got the Bengals’ backfield scoring started with a four-yard touchdown run in the second quarter, but then Chase Brown got the next three. Wild. Brown ended up out-touching his veteran backfield mate 16-9. Perine has been much more involved of late, but it’s not creating standalone fantasy value, and it’s somehow not affecting Brown’s. Brown has a plus Week 17 matchup in the Cardinals while Perine remains off the radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed 14 times for 42 yards in the Bengals’ Week 15 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine saw one more carry than Chase Brown, but averaged just three yards per carry on the day with his longest gain coming on an eight-yard pickup. Perine briefly left the game in the fourth quarter due to a knee injury, and was carted to the locker room at one point. Despite all of this, he returned to finish out the day and should be good to go for Week 16 against the Dolphins. Even if he is active, fantasy managers can avoid him next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed nine times for 57 yards in the Bengals’ Week 9 win over the Falcons, adding three receptions for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: While Brown struggled in Week 8, the silver lining was that he out-touched Samaje Perine 20-to-5. After fumbling against the Titans last week, Perine actually had more carries than Brown (11-to-9) in Madrid. Brown saw all three targets that went to running backs against the Falcons, but there’s no way to spin this positively for the 26-year-old who had a preseason ADP in the teens. Brown still hasn’t scored since Week 1 and he’ll be an RB2 at best against the Steelers in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 12 times for 55 yards and a fumble in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans, adding eight receptions for 46 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Brown saw most of his fantasy production come from the passing game, seeing nine targets in a pass-heavy game script. He fumbled on a handoff from Joe Burrow and also had a receiving touchdown called back for holding in the first half. Despite the dampened fantasy production, Brown saw most of the backfield opportunities for the Bengals, out-touching Samaje Perine 20-to-5. Brown’s production has been underwhelming the first half of the season but fantasy managers should hold tight given his large share of opportunities in pass-heavy game scripts. Brown’s production should regress to see more touchdowns the second half of the season. He is in the RB2 ranks for Week 9 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 11 times for 39 yards in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens, adding four receptions for 19 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: The Ravens held Brown in check both on the ground and through the air, with his longest play coming on an eight-yard reception. Even with the Bengals scoring 35 unanswered points in the second half alone, Brown was unable to find the end zone, and watched from the sidelines as Samaje Perine vultured a one-yard touchdown run from him down near the goal-line. Brown out-snapped Perine 7-to-3 in the red zone, but that won’t help fantasy managers much. This continues to be a tough season for Brown, who has just one touchdown on the year and has yet to surpass 82 yards from scrimmage in any game this season. He shouldn’t be considered as anything more than an RB2 next week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Bengals OC Dan Pitcher said the team will “continually assess how that touch share between [Perine] and Chase Brown should play out.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Pitcher suggested that when they run the ball more from shotgun — as they did last week against the Dolphins — Perine’s a better fit for those kinds of plays. The Bengals spent a lot of time this offseason working on an under center run game to get Brown more explosives, but that has gone for naught early on in the season. We may indeed see more Perine in Cincinnati’s running game after they return from the bye week, lowering Brown into the RB2 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 13 times for 39 yards and a fumble in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins, adding 3 receptions for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Brown took a surprising backseat to Samaje Perine in the Bengals’ win over the Dolphins. He still out-snapped Perine 38-to-33, but a red zone fumble hurt his fantasy production while splitting backfield touches 50/50. There were a few snaps where Brown lined up as a receiver with Perine in the backfield; the Bengals used both backs heavily. Brown previously dominated all sorts of touches for the Bengals backfield, so this is a new development. Game script certainly played a factor but Brown’s ceiling as an RB1 may be considerably lessened if Perine’s usage sticks. He is a fantasy RB2 with a Week 7 matchup against the Ravens on the horizon after a Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed nine times for 10 yards in the Bengals’ Week 4 loss to the Jaguars, adding 11 receptions for 71 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: It was a big pass-catching day for Brown, who saw 11-of-54 total Bengals targets on the day. After Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) exited, Brown and Tee Higgins saw massive upticks in usage. Brown saw 57 backfield snaps, catching a series of checkdowns and wheel routes despite just 10 rushing yards on the day. He worked ahead of Samaje Perine on passing downs, a good sign for his fantasy production moving forward. We don’t expect Brown to consistently see this many targets but a high backfield share gives him a consistent fantasy floor. Brown is a fringe RB1 for Week 5 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 13 times for 61 yards in the Bengals’ Week 3 loss to the Steelers, and two receptions for eight additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Brown was effective with the opportunities he received, but the Bengals did all of their damage through the air in this one, as Joe Burrow and the company aimed to keep pace with a surprisingly explosive Steelers offense. As far as the Bengals’ backfield is concerned, Brown continues to be the only game in town. He handled 71.4 percent of the Bengals’ running back opportunities in this one but has only one touchdown to show for his efforts this season. He’ll be a fringe RB1/RB2 in next week’s game against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 20 times for 80 yards in Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: He “added” three catches for two yards on five targets, getting absolutely exploded by Kamari Lassiter on one of them. He also had a 20-ish yard run called back for holding. Brown looked quick and able, but the Bengals ran just two plays inside the Texans red zone all game. He played on 42-of-60 snaps per PFF. Brown will be in the low-end RB1 ranks against the Steelers in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 16 times for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 1 win over the Bucs, adding five receptions for 22 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: It was neither an efficient nor prolific outing for the Bengals’ lead back, but he found the end zone and out-touched No. 2 Samaje Perine 21-8. It was a full “as expected” day in the Bengals’ backfield. Brown will remain in the RB10-14 range for Week 2 against the Texans. That’s a tough defensive matchup, albeit one the similarly offensive-minded Bills just handled with ease.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. said he “wouldn’t be surprised if the Bengals double last year’s” number of runs from under center on early downs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Dehner has been covering the Bengals’ intent to increase the number of plays run from under center all summer. Last season, “the Bengals ran from under center 120 times on early downs. The league average was 210.” Per Dehner, it has become clear “over the weeks that the under-center offense would not be going away.” The Bengals are committed to changing their ways in pursuit of more explosive gains. Starting RB Chase Brown is a locked-in RB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 5-of-6 targets for 32 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals’ Week 9 victory over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins had recorded at least 148 receiving yards in three of his last four games. His 32 yards were a far cry from those gaudy totals, but he was able to save the day from a fantasy perspective by catching a four-yard touchdown and an eight-yard touchdown. Higgins still has 758 receiving yards on the season to Ja’Marr Chase’s 647, so he has that going for him. Higgins is technically the WR2 on the Bengals, but he’s a top-10 WR in fantasy heading into a matchup with the Steelers in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 10-of-11 targets for 155 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins led the team in receiving yards while trailing Ja’Marr Chase in receptions and targets. He was Joe Burrow’s primary target over the middle of the field in the intermediate and deep areas. Higgins caught a pair of second half touchdowns, catching an 18-yard score to tie the game towards the end of regulation. Pass-heavy game scripts will lead to a high amount of fantasy production for Higgins and Chase, who saw a combined 56-percent target share from Joe Burrow. Higgins is a high-end WR2 for Week 9 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 6-of-7 targets for 148 yards and one touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins came up big multiple times for the Bengals in the second half after they were shut out 13-0 in the first half. He hauled in passes of 10 and 19 yards on the Bengals’ opening drive in the second half to help set up an eventual six-yard touchdown pass to Mike Gesicki, and hauled in a 13-yard touchdown of his own on the following drive. He would also make two catches of 40-plus yards, and came up six yards short of a second touchdown on an impressive 44-yard grab — his longest play of the day. Higgins has gone for 140-plus yards in two of his last three games and has topped 90 yards in four of six games this season. He profiles as a high-end WR2 in next week’s game against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 2-of-4 targets for 22 yards in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins saw just four targets against the Dolphins after seeing 16 targets in Week 4. The adductor/neck injuries didn’t limit his playing time as much, seeing 45 snaps on the day, No. 2 among Bengals receivers. With Ja’Marr Chase back on the field, Higgins’ target volume decreased considerably and he totaled just 22 yards in a more run-favorable game script. Despite the dud, Higgins still belongs in the WR2 ranks and gets a mediocre Ravens defense in Week 7 after a Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Bengals WR Tee Higgins is active for Week 5 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins suffered an adductor injury in Week 4 against the Jaguars and was a full practice participant Friday after DNPs the two days before. Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) both declared active. Though NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports he will play mostly “meaningful plays”, Higgins is in the WR2 ranks while Chase is back in the WR1 ranks this week. The Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, TE Jack Endries, WR Colbie Young, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 5 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Tee Higgins (groin/neck) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) will also play. Higgins is likely suiting up at less than full strength, but fantasy managers have to keep him in their lineups versus a Miami defense that is giving up explosive passing plays at the second-highest rate in the league this year. He will be a boom/bust WR2 for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said Tee Higgins (groin/neck) is questionable for Week 5 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins missed the first two practices of the week but practiced in full on Friday. We would consider him to be truly questionable given his one day of practice, meaning fantasy managers will want to check his official game status when the team announces inactives 90 minutes before kickoff. If he can’t go, Dohnte Meyers, who saw nine targets last week, could be on the fantasy radar as a WR4 in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) was seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Chase still needs to clear concussion protocol if he hopes to suit up for Week 5’s game against the Dolphins. That said, he appears to be trending toward being able to play after logging back-to-back practices to close out the week. Tee Higgins (groin/neck), who was a DNP on Wednesday and Thursday was also seen sprinting and running routes on Friday, which suggests he could also be good to go for Sunday’s game. We will check back in with official game day statuses in the coming hours when the team releases its final injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins (adductor/neck) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins is sporting a T-shirt and shorts at today’s practice. We expect to see him listed as a non-participant at the end of the day. Consecutive absences put him on the wrong side of questionable for the Bengals’ Week 5 game against the Dolphins, though he still has at least a small chance of turning things around tomorrow. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins (adductor/neck) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Head coach Zac Taylor told reporters before practice that Higgins would be listed as limited. Not only did he not practice, but the team listed him with a neck injury on top of his adductor issue. He went down with the adductor injury late in Cincy’s Week 4 loss to the Jags. It’s unclear when the neck issue cropped up. With multiple injuries holding him out of practice, Higgins looks unlikely to play in Week 5. With Ja’Marr Chase potentially out as well, Dohnte Meyers could be Joe Burrow No. 1 receiver this week. He should be added in all fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 10-of-12 targets for 155 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 9 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase hadn’t had a game with 100 yards receiving until two weeks ago. Since then, he’s had at least 10 receptions, at least 141 yards and a touchdown in back-to-back games. Ho-hum. Chase absolutely toasted Falcons cornerback AJ Terrell for a 47-yard touchdown in the first quarter on a play that looked eerily similar to a touchdown he had against Terrell when the two were in college. Chase is up to 647 yards and seven touchdowns on the season. He’s a WR1 heading into Week 10’s matchup against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 11-of-16 targets for 141 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase was heavily involved in a pass-heavy game script, seeing 16-of-48 Joe Burrow pass attempts. He was targeted downfield several times, catching a 30-yard touchdown but being the intended target on a pair of interceptions. It was Chase’s first 100-yard receiving day as he led the team in targets and receptions. The Bengals have a pass funnel to Chase and Tee Higgins, leading to extremely productive fantasy days in high scoring games. Chase is once again squarely in the fantasy WR1 ranks for Week 9 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase is not on Cincinnati’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: He will play and be on the overall WR1 line against the Titans. Zac Taylor spoke earlier today and said he had no concerns about Chase. Everyone has downplayed concerns about Chase’s ankle for the majority of the week. He will be a smash play against a Jeffrey Simmons-less Titans defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase quickly puts his fantasy managers’ worries to rest, returning to a full session Thursday after being limited Wednesday. The Bengals will be playing without two tight ends and their WR3 in Andre Iosivas, but their primary contributors remain one of the healthier units as we approach the half way point in the regular season. Chase can be started as a top tier WR1 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ja’Marr Chase’s ankle injury “is not considered a major deal.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Rap isn’t breaking much news here. Chase didn’t practice on Wednesday, but the Bengals listed him as getting a rest day on top of the ankle issue. It was just a maintenance day for one of the league’s best wideouts. Chase remains in the WR1 overall mix for his Week 8 game against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (NIR-rest/ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: The rest aspect suggests Chase’s ankle injury can effectively be treated as a non-issue, but NFL teams have played games with the injury report at times this season, so we are cataloguing it here to be safe. Assuming Chase resumes practicing tomorrow, he can be started as an elite WR1, as usual, in Week 8 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 5-of-7 targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase caught just two passes for 23 yards in the first half, but he popped up for a 30-yard gain in the fourth quarter on a drive that he capped with a two-yard touchdown to save the day for his fantasy managers. His seven targets tied Tee Higgins for the team-high this week, but Higgins had the far more productive day. He’s still in search of his first 100-yard performance of the year, but Chase has now found the end zone five times and has gone for 60-plus yards in four of six games this season. He’ll be on the WR1 radar next week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 6-of-10 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase returned from a concussion he suffered last week, seeing 10 targets in a productive fantasy day. He saw a goal-line fade target on the Bengals’ first drive and was later tackled at the one-yard line towards the end of the first half. Joe Burrow missed Chase for a 70-yard touchdown in the second half but Chase made a miraculous catch with his right arm for a 45-yard touchdown later in the half. He finishes with a successful fantasy day and is squarely in the WR1 ranks heading into the Bengals’ Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) will play in Week 5 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend. With Tee Higgins (neck/groin) also expected to play, it’s business as usual for the Bengals this week. Higgins could be on a pitch count, while Chase won’t have any restrictions. Facing a pitiful Miami defense, Chase is in the running for WR1 overall this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) is questionable for Cincinnati’s Week 5 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: He did fully practice today — it feels like this is trending in the right direction, but it’s hard to know without detailed reporting of where he is in the protocol how likely he is to sit. We’re sure there will be many more report on Chase over the next 24-36 hours. He enters the weekend a true question mark.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) was seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase still needs to clear concussion protocol if he hopes to suit up for Week 5’s game against the Dolphins. That said, he appears to be trending toward being able to play after logging back-to-back practices to close out the week. Tee Higgins (groin/neck), who was a DNP on Wednesday and Thursday was also seen sprinting and running routes on Friday, which suggests he could also be good to go for Sunday’s game. We will check back in with official game day statuses in the coming hours when the team releases its final injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 24-of-29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in the Bengals’ 34-17 Week 9 win over the Falcons, adding three carries for seven yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow’s excellent run of play continued against the Falcons defense in Madrid in Week 9. The 29-year-old signal caller has amassed 16 passing touchdowns in the last four weeks and added two more touchdowns on the ground. Burrow’s production is unsurprisingly coming from playing through his top wide receivers as Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins combined for 187 yards receiving and all three receiving touchdowns against Atlanta. Burrow is likely to find himself on the shortlist for the MVP award the way things are going. He’s a locked in QB1 heading into a Week 10 matchup with the Steelers on Sunday Night Football, which airs on NBC and Peacock.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 38-of-48 passes for 462 yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions in the Bengals’ 43-36 win over the Titans, adding three carries for 10 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow and the Bengals passing offense started off slow, ending the first quarter scoreless. A first quarter interception from Burrow in Titans territory led to a Tennessee score the other way. He finished the half on a better note, tossing a 30-yard touchdown to Ja’Marr Chase and a one-yard score to Jack Endries. The second half saw many more possessions between both teams, with Burrow throwing two more interceptions to give the Titans increased opportunities. He was able to lead several scoring drives regardless, tossing three touchdowns in the second half and scrambling for the go-ahead touchdown in overtime. A high-scoring game script leads to very productive days for Burrow and the Bengals offense. Burrow profiles as a fantasy QB1 once again for Week 9 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 22-of-30 passes for 292 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals’ 35-13, Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: After throwing for just 55 scoreless yards in the first half, Burrow and the Bengals came out firing on all cylinders in the second half. Trailing 13-0 at halftime, Burrow immediately orchestrated a nine-play, 66-yard drive that ended with a six-yard touchdown pass to Mike Gesicki, and followed that up with four more touchdown drives on his team’s next four possessions to jump out to a 35-13 lead. Burrow was as sharp as could be in the second half, completing 16-of-18 attempts while also completing two passes of 20-plus air yards. Burrow has now thrown four touchdowns in back-to-back games and has four multi-touchdown games this season. He’ll be on the QB1 radar next week when the Bengals play host to the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 23-of-32 passes for 190 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals’ 31-24, Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: The Bengals offense mostly had a smooth-sailing day against the lackadaisical Dolphins defense. After a high-volume Week 4, Burrow threw 32 passes, tossing touchdowns to Mike Gesicki, Samaje Perine, and Tanner Hudson in the first half. He just missed Ja’Marr Chase for a 70-yard score in the second half, but later connected with Chase for a 45-yard score in the third quarter. Burrow was hardly under pressure and had plenty of time to make accurate throws and take deep shots against Miami. He is a fantasy QB1 heading into the Bengals’ bye and gets a middling defense in the Ravens for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 39-of-54 passes for 428 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Bengals’ 22-17, Week 4 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: The Bengals offense struggled to finish drives for much of this game, with Burrow throwing his first touchdown to Mike Gesicki in the third quarter. He also added a rushing touchdown on a fourth-quarter quarterback sneak. Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) leaving early didn’t help as Burrow threw two interceptions and nearly had a third. He threw one to Travis Hunter in the first quarter, though it was nullified by a roughing the passer penalty. He later threw one with under two minutes left in the first half, leading to a Jaguars score the other way. The final interception came in the fourth quarter in the red zone, ending a promising drive. Burrow made great plays under pressure, often finding Tee Higgins downfield. However, the interceptions proved to be back-breaking and the Bengals’ comeback attempt ultimately fell short. Burrow is a low-end fantasy QB1 for Week 5 against a soft Dolphins defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 28-of-37 passes for 281 yards and three touchdowns in the Bengals’ 30-27, Week 3 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow came out hot in this one, completing his first 14 passes while throwing a three-yard touchdown to Ja’Marr Chase on the Bengals’ opening drive. Burrow would throw his second touchdown of the day late in the second half when he connected with Tee Higgins for a 28-yard score and found Mike Gesicki 25 yards downfield on a fourth-and-two for his third touchdown of the day. Burrow led his offense on multiple long drives in this one, but with his team trailing 30-27 and driving late in the fourth quarter, he would cough up the ball on a strip-sack, which was recovered by Pittsburgh to seal the win for the Steelers. Burrow has attempted 30-plus passes in every game this season while throwing for six touchdowns to just one interception. He’ll be on the QB1 radar for next week’s game against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 20-of-31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns in Cincinnati’s 20-6, Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow was under pressure quite a bit in this one, as he took five sacks, but the Bengals were able to establish enough of a lead on a few incredible out-of-structure plays by Burrow that they took the air out of the ball in the middle of the third quarter. Both touchdown passes were to Ja’Marr Chase, the second as Burrow drifted out of his pocket to the right. It’s full-steam ahead in the QB1 tiers as Burrow heads to Pittsburgh in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow (back) is active for Cincinnati’s Week 2 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: It never seemed like there was a real chance Burrow would miss this game, even after Josh Johnson was elevated from the practice squad yesterday. Burrow will be on the QB1 line against a Texans defense looking to rebound. Inactive for the Bengals are: Johnson, WR Ke’Shawn Williams, CB Josh Newton, C Connor Lew, OL Myles Hinton, DT B.J. Hill (Achilles), and DT Landon Robinson.
